title: feat: rig init front door + auto-mode harness provisioning
body:
Makes `rig` the single front door into agent-tools and provisions agent autonomy through the reconciler (#3634).

## `rig init` — THE front door
A thin synonym of `rig setup`, dispatched through the **same handler** (one engine, two names — it can never drift from setup/apply). Commands table + quick-start updated in README and AGENTS.md so `rig init` is the documented entry; `rig setup` is its synonym and keeps working.

## Auto-mode provisioning via the reconciler/config
New `harness:` config section + reconcile target:

```yaml
harness:
  enabled: true
  kind: claude-code      # implemented; opencode documented-but-reserved (fails closed)
  auto_mode: true        # RECOMMENDED default
```

On `rig apply` this merges **only** `permissions.defaultMode` into `.claude/settings.json` (`bypassPermissions` when auto_mode, else `default`) — every other setting preserved — idempotent and backup-on-conflict, with two-way drift surfaced by `rig status`. `auto_mode: true` is recommended in the scaffold + `rig export` output, with the explicit rationale "safe because the agent-hook guards are installed" (including the new `block-raw-pr-merge` guard, pulled in by `agent_hooks.all: true` in the same apply).

The opencode equivalent (a `permission` block in `opencode.json`) is documented in `docs/config-schema.md` even though only claude-code is implemented.

## Architecture (follows house rules)
- stdlib-only at import; pure planning in `riglib/plan.py` (`_build_harness`), effectful merge in `riglib/actions/runner.py` (`_do_apply_harness`), drift in `riglib/drift.py` (`_check_harness`).
- Fail-closed validation: unknown/reserved `harness.kind`, non-bool `auto_mode`.

## Verification
- pytest: **101 → 117**, all green. New tests: `rig init` dispatch + scaffold-includes-auto-mode; harness parse/plan/apply (write, idempotent re-apply, conflict-backup, key-preservation, missing→modified→converged drift); validation fail-closed cases.

- `docs/config-schema.md` updated with the full `harness` schema + opencode note.

title: feat(rig): provision the model-freshness checker as a daily cron (#3685)
body:
## What & why (#3685)

On `rig init` AND `rig apply`, **check whether the daily model-freshness checker schedule is installed and install it if missing** (idempotent — the CTO's "проверять есть ли крон и устанавливать"). The schedule runs the agent-tools checker (`lib/checker/model_freshness.py`, see the agent-tools PR). Default: **daily at 12:00 (noon)**.

## Cross-platform "cron"

- **macOS → launchd**: a `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hyperide.model-freshness.plist` (daily `StartCalendarInterval`), loaded via `launchctl`.
- **Linux → crontab**: a sentinel-fenced managed line (`# rig-managed: <label>` + the cron line), position-preserving, idempotent, removable, `%`-escaped.

## How it flows (the one-engine reconciler)

`models:` block in rig.yaml → `config.validate` (fail-closed) → `plan._build_models` (a pure `provision_schedule` action, skipped with a note if the checker file isn't on disk) → `actions/runner` install-if-missing (present-and-current = no-op `skipped`, backup-noted, honors `RIG_SCHEDULE_DRY_RUN`). `schedule.py` is the pure artifact planner. `rig status` reports installed/drifted/not-configured; `drift` surfaces it both ways (position-preserving); `rig doctor` flags a missing `launchctl`/`crontab`. The default scaffold provisions it (enabled, noon).

## rig.yaml

```yaml
models:
  enabled: true
  schedule: { time: "12:00" }    # daily at noon (default)
```

## Multi-model review applied (review-cli, pool=4)

Real findings fixed: the test-isolation gap (drift's by-name bindings weren't stubbed + the default scaffold could write a real plist) — conftest now neutralizes the scheduler suite-wide; position-preserving crontab (a user's lines after rig's block no longer spuriously drift); `%` crontab-escaping; the missing-checker guard.

## Tests

157 tests pass (schema parse, plan both platforms, install idempotency, drift, dry-run, position-preserving crontab, `%` escaping, missing-checker skip). Smoke green. ruff clean. No test touches the real launchd/crontab.

title: feat(skills): wire installed skills into the harness discovery dir
body:
## Problem

A skill copied into `skills_target` (default `~/.agents/skills`) is **invisible to the agent harness**. claude-code lists/loads Skill-tool skills from `~/.claude/skills` (its userSettings skill dir; symlinks there resolve to the real skill). So `rig apply` installed skills that the harness never listed — they only worked if some other tool's own `install-skill` had separately symlinked them.

## Fix (the durable mechanism)

`rig apply` now maintains an idempotent symlink `<harness_skill_dir>/<skill> -> <skills_target>/<skill>` for every enabled skill, making each one actually discoverable by the harness.

- new `link_skill_harness` action (plan + runner + drift), emitted per enabled skill alongside `copy_skill`. Harness-keyed: claude-code → `~/.claude/skills` (default; follows `harness.kind` when a harness block pins one; other harnesses documented for when implemented).
- config knobs: `skills.harness_link` (default **true**) + `skills.harness_skill_dir` (override the per-harness default). Fail-closed validation.
- **idempotent**: a correct symlink is a no-op; a wrong/broken one is re-pointed; a **real (non-symlink) dir/file** already at the path is **left untouched** — never clobber hand-authored skills like `h-reason`, `debate-swarm`, `moshi-best-practices`. `on_conflict` is not consulted for a symlink (no content to back up); this is documented as the one carve-out from the conflict contract.
- `rig status` reports a missing/wrong link as drift; a real dir is not flagged (rig won't touch it).
- self-link guard compares **resolved** paths (no link when harness dir == skills dir, even via HOME symlink / `..`).
- `install-skill` (rig's own bootstrap path, run by `install.sh`) now links `rig` into the harness dir too — it previously wrote only `~/.agents/skills/rig` and was itself undiscoverable.
- suite-wide HOME isolation (autouse fixture) so no test can ever touch the real `~/.claude/skills`.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest -q` → **179 passed** (was 158; +21 new tests).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` against the real agent-tools checkout: harness skill links installed + resolve, second apply idempotent (`Summary: skipped=91`), `rig status: in sync`. (The smoke's trailing pytest `✗` is a pre-existing `RIG_SCHEDULE_DRY_RUN` env-leak in the smoke harness, identical on main — unrelated to this change.)
- multi-model `review` run before commit (Opus + Codex); all actionable findings addressed (bare `skills:` guard, `install-skill` link, broken-symlink re-point, unknown-kind no-link, resolved-path self-link guard, on_conflict carve-out doc, HOME isolation).

Tests cover: plan/runner/drift link behavior, idempotency, re-point (stale + broken), real-dir-left-alone, disabled, default-dir-under-HOME, no-self-link, unknown-kind, `harness.kind` follow; config validation; `install-skill`; smoke harness-link assertion.

title: feat(harness): provision the agents-hooks/v1 → CC hook-bridge dispatcher
body:
## Why

rig installs agent-hook descriptors into `~/.claude/hooks`, but Claude Code never runs them — it only runs hooks declared in `settings.json`. So the guards rig installs (`block-raw-pr-merge`, `block-secrets-write`, …) were **inert in CC**, and the README's "auto-mode is safe because the guards intercept" claim was false (agent-tools#18).

The dispatcher that makes them fire ships in **agent-tools PR alex-mextner/agent-tools#20** (`lib/cc_hook_bridge`). This PR is the rig side: it wires that dispatcher into `settings.json` on `rig apply`.

## What it provisions

A new `register_hook_bridge` action. When a `claude-code` `harness:` block is present and `agent_hooks` is enabled, `rig apply` merges into the same `settings.json` the harness block writes:

```jsonc
"hooks": {
  "PreToolUse": [
    { "matcher": "Bash",                              "hooks": [{ "type": "command",
      "command": "PYTHONPATH=<agent-tools>/lib python3 -m cc_hook_bridge PreToolUse" }] },
    { "matcher": "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit", "hooks": [{ "type": "command",
      "command": "PYTHONPATH=<agent-tools>/lib python3 -m cc_hook_bridge PreToolUse" }] }
  ],
  "Stop": [ { "hooks": [{ "type": "command",
      "command": "PYTHONPATH=<agent-tools>/lib python3 -m cc_hook_bridge Stop" }] } ]
}
```

Opt out with `harness.hook_bridge: { enabled: false }`; override the interpreter with `hook_bridge.python`.

## Properties

- **Additive + idempotent.** Your other hooks (rtk-rewrite, tg-ctl, …) are preserved; a re-apply is a no-op. A drifted managed command (moved checkout / changed `python`) is rewritten in place — UNLESS `on_conflict=skip`, which leaves it (file-level skip parity).
- **Fail-CLOSED at plan time.** If the agent-tools checkout lacks `lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`, the action is skipped with an actionable note rather than wiring a command that errors at runtime.
- **Shell-safe.** Both the lib path and the configured `python` are `shlex.quote`d (spaces / injection).
- **Drift-aware.** `rig status` reports the bridge `missing` when a managed hook is absent and `modified` when its command is stale. Drift and apply share `find_managed_bridge_hook` + `hook_bridge_entries`, so they never diverge.
- **Validated.** `harness.hook_bridge` is type-checked (mapping; `enabled` bool; `python` str).

Also corrects the README harness section: the guards only fire because of this bridge.

## Tests (198 pass)

Plan emission (+ skipped when the dispatcher module is absent / `agent_hooks` off / explicitly disabled / `settings_path` + `python` honored); apply (wires Bash + write-tools + Stop, idempotent re-apply, preserves unrelated hooks, repoints drifted command, `skip` leaves stale untouched, malformed-JSON `skip` untouched, quotes a spaced python); drift (missing→synced, stale-command→modified→synced); config validation.

## End-to-end

Smoke against the REAL agent-tools checkout: rig plans `register_hook_bridge` and writes the dispatcher command at the real `lib/` path; piping a blocking event through that exact command yields `permissionDecision: "deny"`, a benign one passes.

Depends on agent-tools#20 (the dispatcher). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(rig): provision a GitHub branch ruleset via gh api (github.ruleset)
body:
Add a new top-level `github` config block that declaratively provisions a
GitHub repository branch ruleset (the modern branch-protection replacement) on
the repo's default branch, reconciled like skills/hooks/CI. Structurally
mirrors the agents_md feature: a fail-closed config validator, a plan builder,
an idempotent Action handler, a drift check sharing one classification with
apply, dedicated tests, and a docs section.

The sensible default keeps merges WORKING: require a PR (zero reviews), block
force-push + branch deletion, and add the repo Admin role as a bypass actor so
admins are never locked out. The merge-lockout guard is structural, not a knob:
rig NEVER emits the `update` ("Restrict updates") rule (it blocks every merge to
a protected default branch) nor a `required_deployments` rule with an empty
environment list — neither is expressible in the rule assembly.

- config: `github` top key + fail-closed `_validate_github` (unknown keys,
  non-bool knobs, required_reviews int>=0, required_status_checks list[str]).
- plan: `_build_github_ruleset` (default ON; opt out via ruleset.enabled:false),
  merging a sparse config onto the canonical defaults and dropping explicit
  nulls so they fall back to the default (no int(None) crash, no disabled guard).
- action: `provision_github_ruleset` — resolve owner/repo from the origin remote
  (anchored github.com-only parser), list the repo's OWN rulesets
  (includes_parents=false + --paginate, match repo branch ruleset by name +
  target), then POST/PUT only on create/drift. No github remote => skipped
  (never error). RIG_GH_DRY_RUN + a single `_gh_api` seam keep tests/CI off the
  network and off any real repo.
- drift: `_check_github_ruleset` reports missing/modified via the SAME
  github_ruleset_state apply uses; a gh/auth failure surfaces a visible
  "could not verify" item rather than a false "in sync".
- The pure desired-body/rule/normalize/match core lives in a new
  riglib/github_ruleset.py (no Action dependency), so plan/state import it
  without a cycle and every consumer reads one definition. Normalization
  compares every managed rule parameter, sorts rules/contexts/actors, and is
  order-independent on conditions — so a semantic match reads as in sync.

Suite: 305 passing (was 229), all deterministic; smoke green.

title: feat(cli): add `rig config get|set <dot.path>` — read/edit one key, then reconcile
body:
The recommended way to change a single setting without hand-editing YAML.

get <dot.path> [--global] [--json]
  Reads one nested key from the single target file (./rig.yaml, or
  ~/.config/rig/config.yaml with --global) — NOT the cascade. A missing file or
  absent path exits non-zero; a mapping/list subtree prints as YAML; --json emits
  the JSON value (default=str, fail-soft). Diagnostics go to stderr so
  `get --json | jq` keeps a clean stdout. `--global` get works outside a git repo.

set <dot.path> <value> [--global] [--no-apply]
  Coerces the value conservatively (true/false/int/float/null; leading-zero,
  nan/inf/1e3/underscore, and Unicode digits stay strings; quote-wrap forces a
  literal string), creates intermediate mappings, then guards the write with two
  pre-apply gates: schema validation, then a catalog-backed plan build over the
  full cascade (the same engine `rig apply` runs). On either failure — or a write
  IO error — the file is rolled back to its prior contents (a freshly-created file,
  and the immediate dir set created for it, are removed; a failed restore warns
  honestly). On success it reconciles immediately; --no-apply writes + prints the
  plan only. A repo-local set refuses when ./rig.yaml is absent (run `rig init`
  first) so built-in defaults never reconcile onto disk with no committed source.
  Setting the removed `scope` key is refused.

Dot-path engine (split_path/get_path/set_path/coerce_scalar) and a public
read_yaml_file live in riglib.config next to the loader/validator; version
validation now rejects a bool (True == 1). install-skill's SKILL.md, install.sh,
the dispatch SVG, README, and docs/config-schema.md document the command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat(stats): rig stats show — tool-adoption analytics across agent harnesses
body:
## What

`rig stats show` — measures whether the **rig + agent-tools ecosystem is actually being adopted** vs the built-in baseline, by parsing the on-disk session logs of every agent harness on the machine and reporting tool-invocation frequency bucketed into `baseline / ours / external-advertised / other`, with breakdowns by repo + harness and since-vs-prior trend.

## Architecture (`riglib/stats/`)

- **`sources/`** — one pluggable parser per harness (`@register`, auto-discovered) → normalized `ToolInvocation` stream. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, opencode implemented (file-based, stdlib-only). Adding a harness = one file.
- **`aggregate`** — pure reductions → counts/frequencies by category/tool/repo/harness + day/week buckets + period comparison.
- **`render/`** — `json` (canonical) / `tui` (rich, lazy, degrades to plain text) / `web` (self-contained local HTML, inline SVG, no CDN/JS).

Taxonomy is data-driven (`taxonomy.py`): our CLIs (rig/review/tg/draw/3d/task) detected **inside** shell commands via a quote-aware tokenizer that sees through transparent wrappers (`timeout`/`env`/`sudo`) and interpreter runners (`python3 bin/rig`, `uv run bin/rig`); skills + review MCP are *ours*; third-party MCP/skills are *external-advertised*; non-CC native tool names fold onto the canonical baseline so the adoption ratio is comparable across harnesses.

## CLI

```
rig stats show [--harness ...] [--repo ...] [--since ...] [--until ...] [--format json|tui|web] [--web-port N] [--baseline]
```

Wired into `cli.py` as a `stats` subparser with a `show` action (room for future `rig stats <other>`). `doctor` now tracks `rich` as an optional dep. Engine is stdlib-only at import; `rich`/http are lazy.

## Tests

`tests/test_stats.py` — synthetic, HOME-isolated, deterministic fixtures for all four parsers, the aggregator, renderers, trends, filters, and taxonomy edge cases. **44 passed.** Multi-model reviewed (review3–6); HIGH taxonomy-tokenizer finding (quoted shell operators falsely counting as "ours") fixed.

title: feat(tmux): rig-managed tmux configuration — generate + migrate ~/.tmux.conf
body:
## What

Adds a `tmux:` config block so rig provisions tmux configuration declaratively (ROADMAP §5b) — the same way it provisions skills/hooks/CI/models. rig **generates** the tmux config (so it can **guarantee** plugin-init ordering) and **migrates** an existing hand-written `~/.tmux.conf` instead of clobbering it.

## Why — the root-cause bug

On the dev machine, a hand-written `~/.tmux.conf` ran `if-shell '[ -n "$MOSHI_CLIENT" ]' { set -g status-right '' }` **after** `run-shell …/continuum.tmux`. tmux-continuum installs its autosave timer **into `status-right`** (it *prepends* its hook), so the later Moshi wipe erased it → continuum silently stopped saving → a reboot restored a weeks-stale session. Generating the region lets rig pin the order (Moshi wipe **before** continuum's init, continuum init **last**), so the hook survives.

## The `tmux:` schema

```yaml
tmux:
  enabled: true                 # opt-in (a block with enabled not false)
  apply: import                 # import (preferred) | block (managed-block fallback)
  conf_path: ~/.tmux.conf
  generated_dir: ~/.config/rig/tmux
  resurrect:
    processes: [claude, ssh, psql, mysql, sqlite3]   # claude required for cc restore
    capture_pane_contents: true
  continuum:
    restore: true
    save_interval: 15
    boot: true
  moshi:        { enabled: false }   # opt-in; emitted BEFORE continuum init (root-cause fix)
  cc_restore:   { enabled: true }    # per-window `claude --resume <id>` after a reboot
  anti_sprawl:  { enabled: true, session: main }   # attach-or-create one canonical session
  boot:         { enabled: true, label: ai.hyperide.tmux-boot }
```

Fail-closed validation (unknown keys, bad `apply` enum, non-list `resurrect.processes`, `save_interval` < 1, non-bool/str knobs).

## What rig generates + where

- `~/.config/rig/tmux/rig.tmux.conf` — the rig-owned config (wholesale rewrite; the ordering guarantee).
- `~/.config/rig/tmux/cc-save.sh` + `cc-restore.sh` — managed scripts wired via `@resurrect-hook-post-save-all` / `@resurrect-hook-post-restore-all`. cc-save records each `claude` pane's cwd → newest session id under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/` (**encoding `/` and `.` → `-`, verified against real on-disk dirs**); cc-restore relaunches `claude --resume <id>` only into a fresh shell pane (shell-quoting cwd/id), `--continue` fallback on a stale id.
- `~/.config/rig/tmux/tmux-attach.sh` — anti-sprawl attach-or-create (wire from login shell; rig never edits shell rc).
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hyperide.tmux-boot.plist` (macOS) — written but **never `launchctl load`ed** (the user reboots).
- `~/.tmux.conf` — in import mode, a single `source-file` line; in block mode, a sentinel-fenced managed block.

## Migration (conservative)

When `~/.tmux.conf` has rig-owned settings inline, rig backs the original up to `~/.tmux.conf.rig-bak` (never overwriting an existing backup) and **neutralizes only the inline Moshi `status-left`/`status-right` wipe** — the one harmful line — leaving every other user line live (incl. options rig doesn't model, e.g. `@resurrect-strategy-vim`, `@continuum-boot-options`). `rig status` reports drift on the **managed region only**.

## Architecture

Pure rendering in `riglib/tmux.py` (stdlib-only, effect-free, mirrors `riglib/schedule.py`); `plan._build_tmux` emits one `provision_tmux` action; `runner._do_provision_tmux` writes the artifacts; `drift._check_tmux` diffs the managed region (generated file + scripts + boot plist + import line/block). One source of truth across plan/apply/drift.

## Safety

rig prepares on-disk artifacts only — it never runs `tmux source-file` against the live server and never `launchctl load`s the boot plist, so an active session is never disrupted.

## Tests

- **73 new unit tests** (pure rendering + ordering guarantee, config validation, plan, runner install/migration/idempotency, drift incl. block-mode content + boot plist + multi-region accumulation, the cc encoding, shell-quoting, Moshi on/off).
- **Clean-room integration**: `rig apply` against a throwaway `$HOME`, asserting generated files + import line + backup + narrow-neutralize, idempotent re-apply, clean drift, and a **`tmux -f <generated> start-server` parse-check on a private socket** (rc=0, killed after).
- Full suite: **424 passed**. `cc-save.sh`/`cc-restore.sh`/`tmux-attach.sh` pass `bash -n` + shellcheck.

## Not fully verifiable here

The **boot launchd agent** and **cc-restore-after-reboot** can only be proven by an actual machine reboot — stated for the reviewer.

title: fix(tmux): timestamped backups so a re-apply never loses hand-edits
body:
Follow-up to #24 (CTO catch). The tmux migration backup was written to a fixed `~/.tmux.conf.rig-bak` only when none existed (`not exists()`) — so a second apply after the user hand-edited `~/.tmux.conf` back into a migrating state would neutralize those edits WITHOUT a backup, losing the in-between state.

## Fix
Each migrating apply now snapshots the conf under a UNIQUE timestamped `~/.tmux.conf.rig-bak-<UTC>` (microsecond precision + collision guard) — every apply keeps its OWN restore point, earlier backups stay intact. Matches rig's existing `CLAUDE.md.rig-bak-*` timestamped pattern. Docs + contract comments updated.

## Verified
460 tests pass, incl. a new test: a second apply after a hand-edit creates a second backup while an earlier precious backup is preserved.

title: feat(errors): structured what/why/fix errors + stable exit codes (error-system v2)
body:
## error-system v2 — structured what/why/fix errors + stable exit codes

Born from two same-day prod failures whose errors were thin and undiagnosable:
`unknown mcp item(s): review (known: none)` (no hint it was a **removed** slot) and a
dead hook path surfacing only as a generic harness "PreToolUse error". This makes every
rig error a consistent **WHAT / WHY / HOW-to-fix** block with a **stable per-class exit
code** (a public contract, documented in `rig --help`).

### What's in
- **`riglib/errors.py`** — `RigError(what/why/fix/exit_code)` + per-class codes
  (`2` config, `3` drift, `4` unknown-item, `5` missing-target, `6` not-a-repo,
  `127` missing-dep), a single top-level `guard()` renderer, did-you-mean
  (Levenshtein-nearest), and a **removed-slot registry** (`mcp.items.review` → names
  agent-tools #32 + the exact fix instead of "known: none").
- **`riglib/layers.py`** — GLOBAL vs REPO classification, single source of truth so
  `rig status` groups drift by layer and names **which** config file declares each item.
- **`riglib/missing_target.py`** — proactively scans the harness `settings.json` for
  hook commands pointing at a script gone from disk (the dead-rtk-hook case). Resolves
  the invoked **script** (skips bare/absolute interpreters like `/usr/bin/env`,
  `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`; honors `-c` only as an interpreter flag), checks only that
  token so a runtime output arg never false-flags.
- **`cli.py`** — 3-part error rendering + layer-grouped `rig status`; a **non-git dir**
  shows `not a git repository — repo layer N/A` (never the "should be committed" nag) and
  degrades gracefully when the agent-tools catalog can't be resolved. `rig doctor` honors
  the documented `127` missing-dependency exit code.
- **`plan.py`** raises the structured `UnknownItemError`; **`config.py`** adds
  `primary_config_path` for error provenance.

### Verification
- **`uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/` → 504 passed.**
- **`bash tests/smoke.sh` → fully green** (incl. the non-git, clean-sample, removed-slot,
  and dead-hook legs). Fixed a latent smoke bug: the non-git test dir was nested under the
  smoke's own `git init`-ed `$TMP`, so it wasn't actually non-git.
- Reviewed across models with `review --staged` (Opus / Codex); their findings on the new
  modules were addressed (HOME-isolated the new status tests; tightened the missing-target
  script resolution for absolute interpreters and `-c`).

### Known follow-ups (out of scope for this PR; CTO to triage)
- Per-key config **provenance**: `primary_config_path` names the repo file even when the
  bad key came from the global layer.
- Exit-code **class precedence**: when `rig status` has both drift and a dead target, it
  returns `3` (drift) and the `5` (missing-target) signal is masked.
- The new structured `errors.ConfigError` exists but `config.ConfigError` is still what's
  raised for malformed config (so YAML errors still render the old one-line form).
- The non-git **CatalogError fallback** skips the missing-target scan (a dead `~/.claude`
  hook is surfaced in normal status but not in the non-git + no-catalog path).

title: fix(tmux): real reboot-cycle — clean-machine rig init sets up working tmux persistence (tmux v2)
body:
## What

A clean-machine `rig init` now sets up FULLY-WORKING tmux persistence. Fixes all 6 reboot-cycle
defects a real reboot exposed (the #24/#26 provisioning was unit-only — never run through an actual
apply→save→reboot→restore on a live machine).

Spec: agent-tools ROADMAP "rig tmux v2 — REAL reboot cycle broke".

## The 6 defects, fixed

1. **Boot launchd ran an EMPTY server.** The agent ran `tmux start-server` (no conf, no plugins →
   continuum-restore never fired). Now it runs a generated **boot script** doing `tmux new-session
   -d` (loads `~/.tmux.conf` → sourced `rig.tmux.conf` → continuum → restore), and `rig apply`
   **`launchctl load -w`**s the agent so it actually fires at login.
2. **cc-save detected cc by `pane_current_command`** — but cc shows up as its VERSION (e.g.
   `2.1.178`); the real `claude` is a CHILD of the pane shell. cc-save now walks the pane's
   **process tree** (`pane_pid` descendants) and matches a `claude` process → the map is non-empty.
3. **`default-command ''`** restored NON-login shells (no `~/.zprofile`/PATH). Now sets a
   **login-shell** `default-command` (shell path baked at generation — NOT a tmux `${SHELL}` ref,
   which tmux rejects and would abort the whole config). A non-empty override must be absolute.
4. **`~/.tmux/resurrect/` was absent** → no snapshot ever written. apply creates it.
5. **Old continuum boot competed** (`osx_*_start_tmux.sh` Login Items + a stale `Tmux.Start`
   launchd agent). apply runs continuum's `osx_disable.sh` + `launchctl bootout`/removes the old
   plist; keeps `@continuum-boot off`.
6. **Clean machine had no plugins / no first save.** apply clones tpm + resurrect + continuum into
   `~/.tmux/plugins` and takes a first `resurrect save`. `PLUGINS` is now
   `{dir: (url, real_entrypoint)}` — ONE source so activation / completeness / drift agree
   (resurrect ships `resurrect.tmux`, NOT `tmux-resurrect.tmux` — the old check re-cloned a real
   checkout every apply).

Live activation is idempotent + non-fatal (offline degrades, never aborts) and gated behind
`RIG_TMUX_DRY_RUN` (unit suite + CI set it). `drift`/`status` honors the same flag so apply ↔ status
stay consistent. The first-save probe uses `tmux list-sessions` (a bare `has-session` without `-t`
resolves the current session and fails outside tmux, silently skipping the save).

## Tests

- **Unit + a REAL e2e** (`tests/test_tmux_e2e.py`): drives a real tmux server on a private `-L`
  socket — apply -> EXECUTE the boot script (no reboot) -> assert a server comes up WITH config + a
  session; a fake `claude` child under a pane -> NON-EMPTY cc-map; login-shell `default-command`; a
  real `resurrect save` writes a `.txt` snapshot; old-boot cleanup. The e2e is **opt-in**
  (`RIG_TMUX_E2E=1`, needs network for the real plugin clones) so the default `pytest -q` stays
  hermetic; a dedicated CI job (`tmux-e2e`) runs it.
- **smoke** exercises the tmux catalog through the real CLI (asserts `new-session -d` + a non-comment
  `set -g default-command`) and **drops the dead `mcp.items.review` slot** (removed upstream — it
  made smoke fail `unknown mcp item`).

Local: `bash tests/smoke.sh` -> green (500 unit passed, smoke OK); `RIG_TMUX_E2E=1 pytest
tests/test_tmux_e2e.py` -> 5 passed.

## Needs a real reboot

The cold-boot proof (power-cycle -> tmux comes up restored by the launchd agent) needs an actual user
reboot — the e2e simulates everything up to that by executing the boot script directly.

title: feat(rig): provision .claude/worktrees ignore via global core.excludesfile (supersedes #23)
body:
## What & why

Rebuilds #23's gitignore feature under the CTO-chosen **GLOBAL** design.

#23 wrote a managed block into **each repo's committed `.gitignore`** (per-repo, needs a `rig apply` per repo). The CTO rejected that and chose a **global git excludesfile**: rig manages **ONE** marker block in git's global `core.excludesfile`, so `**/.claude/worktrees/` is ignored in **every repo on the machine** — **zero per-repo commits**, no per-repo `rig apply`.

This reuses #23's tested marker-reconcile machine (`create`/`update`/`ok`/`conflict`/`io_error`, the offset-based splice, drift parity, the `gitignore:` schema), retargeted to the global file.

## Design

**Global config, wired like the git-hooks `dispatcher`** — a `git config --global` setting plus a managed file, living in the GLOBAL rig layer. Default **ON** at plan level (an *absent* `gitignore` key still provisions), so the global block is **not** scaffolded into committed repo `rig.yaml`.

**Target resolution (at apply time):**
- `core.excludesfile` **already set** (this machine: `~/.gitignore`) → manage the block **in that file**, leave git config alone (respect the user's choice).
- `core.excludesfile` **unset** → set it to the XDG default `~/.config/git/ignore` **and** write the block there. So on a **clean machine `rig init` does everything itself** (set the config if absent + write the block).
- `gitignore.excludesfile:` override → force a specific file.

**Managed block** — fenced by `# >>> rig-managed (do not edit) >>>` / `# <<< … <<<`, a fixed explanatory comment, then the entries (default `["**/.claude/worktrees/"]`, configurable). Only the bytes between the markers are ever touched; everything else (CRLF, trailing blanks, no-final-newline) is preserved verbatim.

**Strict idempotency** — a re-apply is a **byte-identical no-op**. If a prior non-idempotent tool appended the block **more than once**, rig **collapses the managed region to one correct block**, preserving any user line that sits **between** duplicated blocks (splice per marker-pair, not first-begin..last-end). `.serena/` is deliberately **not** ignored (committed shared memory).

**Drift** — `rig status` flags a missing/divergent/duplicated block, and an unset `core.excludesfile` rig would set, in the **global** section. `rig apply` reconciles.

## Tests / smoke

- `uv run pytest tests/` → **509 passed**.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` → **exit 0** (HOME-isolated leg asserts `core.excludesfile` set to the XDG default, the block written, and **markers=2** byte-stable across re-apply; pytest leg green).
- No test or smoke ever runs real `git config --global` or writes the real `~/.gitignore`: the git-config read/write seams are stubbed suite-wide and HOME/XDG are isolated.
- **Zero-churn no-op confirmed** against this machine's existing `~/.gitignore` block: `resolve_global_excludes(...)` → `ok` (no rewrite).
- Ran multi-model `review` on the diff; addressed findings (interleaved-user-line preservation, XDG test isolation, removed the global block from the committed repo scaffold, doctor→status doc fix, CRLF create-path test, SYNC note on the duplicated path-expander).

## Supersedes #23

#23 should be closed as **superseded** — leaving that to the CTO (not closing it here).

## Notes
- Rebased clean: `origin/main` has not moved since branch-off (error-system #27 and the tmux-v2 PR have **not** landed yet, so **no rebase conflicts**). Will re-run tests+smoke after those land if they touch these files.

title: feat(rig): provision tg-ctl inbound daemon as a boot LaunchAgent
body:
## What

`rig init` / `rig apply` now provision the **tg-ctl inbound control daemon** (tg-cli's
long-poll / inject-into-tmux / voice→text daemon, run as `tg-ctl run`) as a **macOS boot
LaunchAgent** so it auto-starts at login/boot — exactly like rig already does for the tmux
boot service. On a clean machine, `rig init` alone sets it up (the block is **default-ON**).

## Design — mirrors tmux-boot

The whole pipeline follows the existing `tmux` pattern (one source of truth shared by plan,
apply, drift):

- **`riglib/tg_ctl.py`** — a pure, stdlib-only, effect-free `TgCtlPlan` (analog of
  `riglib.tmux`) that renders `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hyperide.tg-ctl.plist`. It uses
  `plistlib.dumps(..., sort_keys=False)` so the key order matches the hand-created, **working**
  live plist **byte-for-byte** — `rig apply` against the live file is a true no-op (`skipped`),
  never a spurious rewrite. Paths are derived from `$HOME`; bun is discovered (`which bun` →
  `~/.bun/bin/bun` fallback); config dir honors `$TG_CTL_CONFIG_DIR` (default `~/.config/tg-cli`).
- **`runner._do_provision_tg_ctl`** — render → back up a differing prior (timestamped) → write →
  (re)load. Unlike tmux-boot (which only writes the plist), this agent **is** (re)loaded via
  `launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap` in the per-user `gui/<uid>` domain, so a clean `rig init`
  starts the daemon without a reboot. Reuses `_timestamped_backup_path` and the `fsutil`
  conflict engine.
- **`drift._check_tg_ctl`** — flags missing / divergent / written-but-not-loaded, a leftover
  plist when `boot:false`, and the stale predecessor (extra). `rig status` surfaces it in the
  **GLOBAL** section (installed / drifted / disabled / unsupported-off-darwin).

## Config block (GLOBAL layer)

Per-machine concern → belongs in `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` (like `harness`/`tmux`/`git_hooks`),
NOT a committed repo `rig.yaml`. Default ON; `enabled`/`boot` default true. Follows the `tmux:`
schema style (fail-closed validation). See `docs/config-schema.md#tg_ctl`.

## Stale-predecessor removal

If `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.ultra.codex-tg-bot.plist` (the dead predecessor) exists,
`rig apply` boots it out, backs it up (timestamped), and removes it.

## Idempotency — proven against the live plist

A **real** `rig apply` (no dry-run) against this machine's live, loaded `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl.plist`
is a `skipped` no-op: the plist sha is unchanged and no `bootstrap`/`bootout` fires (the
byte-identical-AND-loaded early-return). Verified directly.

## Tests / smoke

- **pytest: `510 passed`** (`uv run --extra test pytest tests/`).
- **smoke: exit `0`** (`bash tests/smoke.sh`), including a new focused, HOME-isolated,
  `RIG_TG_CTL_DRY_RUN` tg-ctl leg.
- **Hard isolation:** no test/smoke ever touches the real `~/Library/LaunchAgents` or runs real
  `launchctl` — conftest neutralizes the default-on provisioner + drift check and stubs the
  gui-domain launchctl seams suite-wide; dedicated tests restore the real ones with their own
  temp HOME + a `RIG_TG_CTL_DRY_RUN`-style dry-run seam. The real tg-ctl plist sha was unchanged
  by the entire test run.

## Review

Ran multi-model `review` on the diff; addressed its findings — fixed a dry-run disk-mutation
leak in the stale teardown, `boot:null`/`label:null` defaulting, off-darwin status wording,
collapsed the launchctl bootout/bootstrap helpers, and added regression tests for each.

**Do NOT merge — draft.**

title: fix(test): unlink private tmux socket in e2e teardown (stop leaking rigtest-* sockets)
body:
## Problem

The real-tmux e2e fixture `tmux_env` (tests/test_tmux_e2e.py) runs each test against a private `-L rigtest-<uuid>` server and tears it down with `tmux ... kill-server`. **On macOS, `kill-server` ends the server *process* but does NOT unlink the socket file** under `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/`. Every opt-in e2e run (`RIG_TMUX_E2E=1`) therefore leaked one `rigtest-*` socket inode.

These accumulated: forensics on the dev machine found ~185 leftover `rigtest-*`/`ccdbg-*`/`tgctl-test-*` sockets in `/private/tmp/tmux-501/` (157 of them `rigtest-*`), and the pile-up once starved/killed the live tmux server.

Reproduced directly: boot a server on a throwaway `-L` socket, `kill-server`, and the socket file lingers on disk.

## Fix

- Teardown now **kills the server AND unlinks its socket file**, via a shared `_teardown_tmux_server(real_tmux, label, env)`.
- The socket path is resolved by `_socket_path_for(label, env)` under the **same env the server was launched with** (the fixture scrubs `TMUX_TMPDIR`), so the unlink can't target the wrong path. Matches tmux's `server_create_socket`: `TMUX_TMPDIR` honored only when absolute, else `/tmp`.
- The `kill-server` call is wrapped so a timeout/OSError can't skip the unlink.

## Test

Adds `test_teardown_unlinks_the_private_socket_file`: boots a real server, asserts the socket file exists, runs the production teardown, asserts the file is gone. Confirmed catching the bug (kill-only leaks; kill+unlink does not).

Verified: full e2e module (6 pass) + 660-test hermetic unit suite (pass), and the e2e run leaves **zero** `rigtest-*` sockets behind (before: several per run), including with `TMUX_TMPDIR` set.

## Known limitation

The leak regression inherits the module-level `RIG_TMUX_E2E=1` + git + GitHub-reachability skip, so it only runs under the opt-in e2e flag. Decoupling it into a tmux-only (no-network) check is a sensible follow-up.

title: feat(status): area-coverage summary — every reconciled area, not "mostly skills"
body:
## What

`rig status` rendered only the items that **were drifting**, as one flat dump dominated by skill rows (one per skill + a harness-link row each). Every other area — agent-hooks, the git-hook dispatcher, CI gates, the ship gate, MCP, AGENTS/CLAUDE symlinks, repo settings, harness, tmux, the model-freshness cron, the tg-ctl daemon — was buried under the skill lines or, when in sync, **invisible**. A user could not see the full picture of what rig manages and where it's out of sync.

ROADMAP: *"rig status must cover ALL reconciled areas, not mostly skills"* — group by area + the GLOBAL/REPO layer split; each area shows in-sync vs drift.

> Note: the sibling ROADMAP items in the same heading cluster — the non-git handling (*"non-git dir must NOT claim 'no rig.yaml, should be committed'"*) and the loud *"extras are left for you to decide"* reassurance in `status` + `apply --help` — **already landed in #27** (error-system v2). This PR closes the remaining, biggest gap: the area-coverage summary. I left the already-done work untouched.

## How

Add an **AREA SUMMARY** headline at the top of `rig status`: every reconciled area, grouped by the GLOBAL/REPO layer, each with its state — `not configured` / `in sync` / `drift (N declared-but-missing/modified[, M on-disk-not-declared])`. The detailed per-item drift dump still follows as the detail.

- **`riglib/areas.py`** — the single source of truth for the area list (an `Area` registry + layer split), mirroring `layers.py`. The `ci` category splits into two user-facing areas — **CI gates** and **ship / `gh ship`** — by action slot / drift item, **direction-aware** so a disk→config extra workflow (even a rogue `ship.yml`) routes to CI gates, never the `~/bin` ship merge gate.
- Counts are the **unit-stable DRIFT counts**; no fragile `declared − missing` arithmetic (a plan action and a drift item are not 1:1 across areas — gitignore is one action but two checks, a skill is a copy + a harness-link).
- `tg_ctl` off Darwin renders `unsupported` (not a false `in sync`) — only when configured **and** genuinely no drift, so a real off-Darwin drift can never be masked.
- **`layers.py`** — add `gitignore` + `tg_ctl` to `_CATEGORY_LAYER` (the registry was meant to be exhaustive; both previously fell through to the GLOBAL default).
- `_LAYER_HEADERS` lifted to a module constant, shared with the per-item drift dump (one source of wording).

## Acceptance evidence

`rig status` against a real agent-tools checkout — all 13 areas visible at a glance, grouped by layer, each with its honest state:

```

  stack: unknown  type: unknown
  config layers: repo:/private/var/folders/1c/d4v7_mrs4b9085f6w7w9p35c0000gn/T/tmp4y_pjvqk/repo/rig.yaml

  areas rig manages:
    GLOBAL — machine-wide (from ~/.config/rig/config.yaml)
      skills: drift (76 declared-but-missing/modified)
      agent-hooks (v1 descriptors): drift (9 declared-but-missing/modified)
      git-hooks dispatcher: not configured
      global gitignore excludes: drift (2 declared-but-missing/modified)
      MCP servers: not configured
      harness auto-mode + hook bridge: not configured
      tmux config: not configured
      model-freshness cron: not configured
      tg-ctl inbound daemon: drift (1 declared-but-missing/modified)
    REPO — this repository (from ./rig.yaml)
      CI gates: drift (1 declared-but-missing/modified)

title: fix(tmux): cc-save detects the versioned-binary claude install (resume after reboot)
body:
## What

The 2026-06-17 tmux incident's headline defect: after a reboot, Claude Code panes were **not resumed** because the cc-session map was empty. Root cause: Claude Code installs as a symlink

```
~/.local/bin/claude -> ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>
```

so the real executable FILE is named by its **version** (`2.1.179`). When cc is launched by the *resolved path* (not the `claude` symlink), the process's name is the version string, **not** `claude`. `cc-save.sh`'s process-tree walk matched only `claude`/`*/claude`, so it missed that process — exactly as the original `pane_current_command == claude` filter did — and the `cc-sessions.map` stayed empty → cc never resumed.

This finishes the cc-save detection that tmux v2 (#28) started: detect cc by the pane PID-tree, now robust to the versioned-binary install.

> Scope note: the 5 INCIDENT fixes — (1) PID-tree detection, (2) login-shell panes, (3) boot `new-session -d`, (4) legacy `Tmux.Start.plist` cleanup, (5) single attach-or-create — were largely landed by #28. This PR closes the one remaining real gap in (1): the versioned-binary case the INCIDENT explicitly calls out (`2.1.179`).

## Fix

`pane_has_claude` now reads `ps -eo args` (the full command line) instead of `ps -eo comm`:

- **Portability:** macOS `comm` is the full executable PATH, but Linux `comm` is the 15-char-**truncated basename with no path** — so the `…/claude/versions/` segment is invisible to a `comm` match on Linux. `args` carries the full path on **both** platforms.
- Takes **argv[0]** (executable = the line up to the first space) and matches it against `claude` / `*/claude` (symlink launch) **OR** a path under `…/claude/versions/` (direct-path launch of the versioned binary).
- **Keys on argv[0] ONLY**, not the whole args line — so a `claude` / `claude/versions/` token appearing in an **argument** (`grep -r x …/claude/versions/`, `cp /opt/claude /tmp`, `vim claude.md`) never false-matches and writes a bogus map entry. (A pre-commit review with two models caught a whole-line-match false-positive bug in an earlier revision; this is the corrected approach.)

### Accepted, pinned limitations
- An install path containing a **space** truncates argv[0] (isolating a spaced argv[0] from `ps args` is impossible; the whole-line match that would cover it reintroduces the argument false-positives).
- A **wrapper** launch that rewrites argv[0] (`npx claude`, `node …/cli.js`) puts the real claude in argv[1+].

Both are absent from the canonical direct-exec install this targets, and both are pinned by tests that assert the non-match so the trade-off can't silently change.

## Acceptance evidence

**Hermetic unit (`tests/test_tmux.py`)** — BFS run against synthetic `ps` snapshots:
- versioned binary detected: bare, with args, deep in the tree
- argument false-positive guards (`grep`/`ls`/`tar`/`cp`/`find` over claude paths → no match)
- `…/notclaude/versions/…` → no match
- spaced-install / wrapper-launch limitations pinned as no-match

**Real-tmux e2e (`tests/test_tmux_e2e.py`, `RIG_TMUX_E2E=1`)** — `test_cc_save_detects_the_versioned_binary_install`: runs a `…/claude/versions/<v>` symlink by its **resolved path** as a real pane-shell descendant, runs the **unmodified generated** `cc-save.sh`, and asserts the map is non-empty with the right cwd+session-id. **Verified it FAILS on the old basename-only match** (map EMPTY — the exact incident) and passes with the fix.

```
673 passed, 7 skipped        # full hermetic suite (pytest -q), zero warnings
7 passed                     # real-tmux e2e (RIG_TMUX_E2E=1)
smoke OK                     # bash tests/smoke.sh
All checks passed!           # ruff on changed files
```

CI runs the same: hermetic `pytest -q`, `smoke.sh`, and the opt-in tmux-e2e job (`RIG_TMUX_E2E=1`) on Linux.

## Not done (out of scope, ship=HOLD)
Nothing applied to the live machine / running tmux / launchd — this PR only changes the rig TEMPLATE that *generates* `cc-save.sh`. The live machine picks it up on the next `rig apply`.

title: feat(setup): rig setup interactive config wizard + rig config get|set
body:
## What

Implements the ROADMAP item **"rig setup — interactive config wizard"** (CTO 2026-06-17).

`rig setup` is now the **INTERACTIVE configuration wizard** — no longer an alias for `init`/`apply` (this REVERSES the earlier "delete the setup alias" item, exactly as the roadmap specifies). 

**Interactive (a TTY):**
1. SHOWS what is enabled across **all reconciled areas** — the same areas `rig status` covers (skills, agent-hooks, git-hooks, CI, MCP, harness/auto-mode, model-freshness schedule, AGENTS.md, GitHub ruleset, tmux, global git-excludes block, tg-ctl daemon) — read from the cascaded (global+repo) config.
2. Lets you CHANGE any option in **both** the local `rig.yaml` AND the global `~/.config/rig/config.yaml`, each option carrying an inline **HINT** (how it works + why — the "why next to the toggle, not buried in docs").
3. APPLIES (`rig apply`) on the spot, reusing the **same engine** (`plan.build` + `run_plan`, never forked).

**Non-interactive (piped / no TTY):** prints USAGE for `init` / `apply` / `config get|set` — NOT a half-wizard.

The option list + hints live in a new in-code registry **`riglib/schema.py`** — the single source of truth, from which a JSON schema is **emitted** (`schema.json_schema()`), generated not consumed (the roadmap's "reads the schema" — the schema is derived from this registry since no JSON-schema file exists yet).

`rig config get|set <key>` is the **headless counterpart** (what non-interactive `rig setup` points at).

## Layer routing (the documented footgun guard)

Each option is routed to its **owning layer**: REPO options → `./rig.yaml`; GLOBAL-only blocks (`gitignore`, `tg_ctl`, `tmux`) → the global config, **never** written into a committed repo `rig.yaml`. `--global` forces the global layer.

## Acceptance evidence

**Non-interactive `rig setup` → USAGE (no half-wizard):**
```
rig setup — interactive configuration wizard
  ... (this is a non-interactive run) ...
    rig init / rig apply / rig config get <key> / rig config set <key> <v>
```

**`rig config get|set` + layer routing:**
```
$ rig config get harness.auto_mode          → true
$ rig config set harness.auto_mode no        → set ... (REPO → ./rig.yaml)
$ rig config set gitignore.enabled no        → set ... (GLOBAL → ~/.config/rig/config.yaml)
# repo rig.yaml gets harness only; gitignore lands in the GLOBAL config, never the repo file
```

The interactive wizard was visually proof-cycled through a real PTY (shows all 12 areas with enabled-state + hints + writable-layer tags, edits route to the correct file, apply runs).

## Fail-closed

Every write path is fail-closed BEFORE touching disk: a malformed / non-mapping existing layer file (`ConfigError`), a non-mapping intermediate (`ValueError` — won't clobber a user's scalar), an invalid value, or a schema violation is reported and nothing lands on disk; a brand-new layer file gets the canonical `version: 1`. A Ctrl-C mid-prompt exits cleanly; a Ctrl-C during the real apply propagates (apply runs outside the interrupt guard).

## Tests

- **50 new tests** in `tests/test_setup_wizard.py`: the registry (keys/hints/json-schema/coerce/layer routing incl. a reverse footgun-guard vs the scaffold), the interactive wizard (scripted input + the real engine via the parser-built apply namespace), non-interactive USAGE, every fail-closed path (malformed YAML, non-dict shape, non-mapping intermediate, invalid value), and the cascade (global override of a repo key).
- **Full suite: 710 passed, 6 skipped.** ruff + mypy clean on new code. Smoke gains a `rig setup` no-TTY check.
- Docs updated: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`.

## Review

Pre-commit multi-model review across several rounds (kimi/glm/gemini/qwen/deepseek — some seats hit shared-backend server errors). All actionable correctness/consistency findings addressed; remaining items are deliberate design choices consistent with the codebase (non-atomic writes, no ruamel comment-preservation — the whole repo writes directly).

title: feat(github): provision repo MERGE-button policy via gh api (github.merge)
body:
## What & why

ROADMAP [§5](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) — *"rig provisions REPOSITORY SETTINGS at init/apply"* — names the **merge-button policy** (squash-only, auto-delete head branch, allow-auto-merge) as one of the API-exposed settings the `gh api` backend must reconcile, alongside the branch ruleset that #19 already landed.

This adds the **`github.merge`** block beside the existing `github.ruleset`, following that module's architecture 1:1 (a pure stdlib-only desired-state core; one `*_state` classifier shared by apply + drift; default-ON with `enabled: false` opt-out; fail-closed validation; `RIG_GH_DRY_RUN` no-mutation seam).

## The settings rig reconciles (secure defaults)

| knob | API field | default | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `squash_merge` | `allow_squash_merge` | `true` | squash is the ONLY merge model… |
| `merge_commit` | `allow_merge_commit` | `false` | …so history stays linear, one commit per PR |
| `rebase_merge` | `allow_rebase_merge` | `false` | (same) |
| `delete_branch_on_merge` | `delete_branch_on_merge` | `true` | clean branch list |
| `allow_auto_merge` | `allow_auto_merge` | `true` | a PR lands the moment its gate goes green |
| `allow_update_branch` | `allow_update_branch` | `true` | "Update branch" button available |

Reconciled via `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` — the body carries **only** the managed merge fields, never a repo name/visibility key, so a PATCH can't rename or expose the repo.

## Capability detection / degrade

- **no github remote** → `skipped` (never an error) — a non-github repo is a no-op.
- **gh missing / not authed / no admin (HTTP 403) / API error** → a **visible** error on `apply` and a **"could not verify"** drift item on `status` — never a silent green, never a crash. (`_gh_api` already returns rc=127 for a missing binary and catches OSError/SubprocessError → rc=1, so the state classifier's `rc != 0` branch covers every failure mode.)
- These are repo **settings**, not a ruleset, so a mis-set value at worst disables a button — it can never lock anyone out of merging (unlike the ruleset's `update`-rule footgun).

## Acceptance evidence

**Tests** — `tests/test_github_merge.py` (31 tests): body assembly + squash-only secure default, managed-fields-only (no repo-identity key) guard, hard-bool coercion, update/skip apply, drift parity (apply & drift switch on the same `github_merge_state`), no-remote no-op, **403/401 degrade-loud**, gh_error detail fallback chain, **dry-run no-mutation**, scaffold round-trip, fail-closed validation (unknown key / non-bool knob / non-mapping).

```
$ uv run --extra test pytest -q
802 passed, 8 skipped
$ uv run --with ruff ruff check riglib/github_merge.py tests/test_github_merge.py
All checks passed!
$ uv run --with mypy mypy riglib/github_merge.py
Success: no issues found in 1 source file

desired: {'allow_squash_merge': True, 'allow_merge_commit': False, 'allow_rebase_merge': False,

APPLY RESULT: updated -> github-merge: RIG_GH_DRY_RUN — would UPDATE merge policy on

title: feat(agents-md): rig status flags a broken/dangling AGENTS.md↔CLAUDE.md link
body:
## What

ROADMAP §5 — "rig always provisions `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` as symlinks … `rig init`/`rig apply` create/**repair** the symlink (never clobber a real file without backup); `rig status` flags a missing or **broken** link."

The create/converge/conflict provisioning landed in #17. This PR closes the remaining gap: a **dangling rig-shaped link** — rig provisioned the pair, then the real canonical was deleted, leaving the symlink pointing at a now-missing target — was lumped into one generic `conflict` ("neither is a real file"), so `rig status` could not tell it apart from a directory collision or a stray foreign symlink.

## Behavior

`resolve_agents_md` now classifies the dangling shapes precisely (still a **non-mutating `conflict`** — apply never touches the link):

- **Rig-shaped dangling** (a symlink whose target is the OTHER managed name, that name missing, the other slot empty): named precisely — *"its canonical target AGENTS.md does not exist (deleted out from under a provisioned pair, or never created). Restore it from version control (e.g. git checkout) or remove the dangling link."* rig **never recreates** the missing canonical: an empty placeholder would silently mask the loss of possibly-curated content, turning a visible, git-recoverable failure into an invisible one. (This conservative "surface, don't resurrect" call was the contested design point — vetted across multiple multi-model review rounds; `apply` must not silently reverse a deletion.)
- **Other dangling shapes** (foreign/unresolved target, peer-link loop, dangling link beside a competing occupant): a generic broken/dangling-link message *without* the (here-inaccurate) "canonical deleted" narrative.
- A self-referential / peer loop no longer **crashes** `rig status`/`rig apply`: `symlink_points_to`'s resolve-guard now catches `RuntimeError` (pathlib raises it for a symlink loop), not just `OSError`. Previously `AGENTS.md → AGENTS.md` propagated a `RuntimeError` out of `resolve_agents_md`. (Crash-regression caught during review.)

## Acceptance evidence

Real `rig status` CLI (exit 3 = drift flagged; `rig apply` leaves every case untouched):

```
CASE A — canonical deleted (CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md gone):
  agents_md/symlink: CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md (missing) is a broken symlink — its
  canonical target AGENTS.md does not exist (deleted out from under a provisioned
  pair, or never created). Restore it from version control (e.g. git checkout) or
  remove the dangling link, then re-run; rig will not recreate it, to avoid
  masking lost content

CASE B — peer loop (AGENTS↔CLAUDE):
  agents_md/symlink: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are broken/dangling symlinks (their
  targets do not resolve) — reconcile the pair to one real file plus a symlink to
  it (remove the dangling link(s); create or restore the canonical), then re-run

CASE C — self loop (AGENTS.md → AGENTS.md) [previously a CRASH]:
  agents_md/symlink: AGENTS.md is a broken/dangling symlink (its target does not
  resolve) — reconcile the pair to one real file plus a symlink to it …
```

## Tests

+13 cases in `tests/test_agents_md.py`: rig-shaped deletion (both directions, relative + absolute targets), foreign/plural dangling, peer loop, self-loop (crash regression), directory-beside-dangling, mixed rig-shaped+foreign pairs (both loop iterations), drift parity, and the `_is_broken_symlink` predicate directly.

- Full suite: **784 passed, 8 skipped** (baseline was 771 → +13)
- `tests/smoke.sh`: **green**
- ruff: clean on touched code (one pre-existing unused-import on `runner.py:16` left untouched — out of scope)
- mypy: clean on `runner.py`

Smallest correct change: two files, additive; no unrelated refactors. apply/drift still switch on the same `resolve_agents_md` state, so status and apply can never disagree.

title: fix(config): restore #20's `rig config get|set <dot.path>` CLI (dropped by #34's wizard rebase)
body:
## What & why

PR #34 (the `rig setup` wizard, merged as `f054910`) rebased over main's PR #20 (`rig config get|set`, `635eaf5`) and kept the wizard's **schema-key** config CLI while **deleting #20's dot-path CLI** (`cmd_config` + helpers + the argparse parser + the whole `tests/test_config_getset.py`). Only one `config` command can register, so the user-facing single-key editor silently regressed from the dot-path design to a schema-key one. This restores #20's dot-path CLI as the **user-facing** `rig config get|set`, coexisting with the wizard.

## `rig config get|set` (restored — #20's design)

- **`get <dot.path> [--global] [--json]`** — reads ONE nested key from the single target file (`./rig.yaml`, or `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` with `--global`) — **not** the cascade. Missing file / absent path exits non-zero; a mapping/list subtree prints as YAML; `--json` emits the JSON value; diagnostics go to stderr so `get --json | jq` keeps a clean stdout.
- **`set <dot.path> <value> [--global] [--no-apply]`** — conservative coercion (`true`/`false`/int/float/null; leading-zero, `1e3`, `nan`/`inf`, underscored, and Unicode digits stay strings; quote-wrap forces a literal string), creates intermediate mappings, guards the write with two pre-apply gates (`schema.validate`, then a catalog-backed plan build over the cascade), rolls the file back on **any** failure, and reconciles via the same engine as `rig apply` on success. `--no-apply` writes + prints the plan only. A repo-local `set` refuses when `./rig.yaml` is absent. Setting the removed `scope` key is refused.

## Reconciliation (what was kept / removed, and why)

- The dot-path engine (`split_path`/`get_path`/`set_path`/`coerce_scalar`/`read_yaml_file`) was **never deleted** — #34 left it in `riglib/config.py` as an orphaned util — so this PR restores only the **CLI front-end** (`cmd_config`, `_cmd_config_get`, `_cmd_config_set`, `_config_target`, `_read_target_yaml`, the parser) + `tests/test_config_getset.py`. The shared helpers (`_load_plan`/`_print_plan`/`_print_results`/`_validate_layer_in_isolation`/`_fmt_scalar`) already existed identically in main.
- **The wizard stays as `rig setup`.** Its schema-key engine (owning-layer routing, `effective_value`, `coerce`, version-seeding) is **internal** to the wizard (`setup_wizard.py`/`schema.py`) — it is NOT the `config get|set` command. The wizard reads/writes config via its own helpers, so dropping main's schema-based `cmd_config` breaks nothing.
- Removed the now-orphaned `_fmt_config_value` (its sole caller was the replaced `cmd_config`; #20 uses the identical `_fmt_scalar`).
- `schema.option_for_key` is now unreferenced in production but **kept** — it is a public registry API, still tested, orphaned-by-this-deliberate-replacement (dead-code rule: investigate, don't delete).
- Removed the schema-key `config get|set` CLI tests from `tests/test_setup_wizard.py` (their CLI surface is replaced). The schema engine they exercised stays covered by the surviving `test_coerce_*`/`test_effective_value_*`/`test_writable_layer_*` and the wizard-interactive tests.
- Docs reconciled (README, AGENTS.md, docs/config-schema.md); the wizard's `NON_INTERACTIVE_USAGE` updated to the dot-path + reconcile framing.

## Verification

- Full suite **800 passed, 8 skipped**; `tests/smoke.sh` OK; gitleaks clean.
- Live-verified: `get` / `--json` / subtree-as-YAML / `--global` / `--no-apply`, the conservative-coercion edge cases (`09`/`1e3`/`nan`/`1_000`/Unicode-digit all stay strings), and the no-file + `scope` guards.
- Reviewed via `review --staged` (multi-model) + an in-harness multi-angle review.

## Deferred follow-ups (pre-existing #20 behavior, not regressions of this restore — see linked issues)

- `rig config set --global` from a repo with **no `./rig.yaml`** is not gated by the no-committed-source guard (only the non-global path is), so a `--global` set there reconciles built-in default repo actions. This is #20's behavior; the docs over-promise the guard for `--global`.
- The post-write rollback's `except Exception` collapses structured `RigError` exit codes (e.g. unknown-item `4`) to a flat `2` during a `set` reconcile.

These are #20's design choices, deliberately left faithful to the restore rather than redesigned in a restoration PR.

title: feat(permissions): provision per-harness command allowlist (pre-allow ecosystem CLIs + safe dev tools)
body:
## What

A new default-ON `permissions` reconciled area: `rig init`/`apply`/`status` provisions each harness's **command allowlist** so our ecosystem CLIs and the safe-to-allow external dev tools are pre-allowed — the agent never stops to ask permission for a known-safe command.

**Default tool set** (config-driven via `permissions.tools`/`extra`/`disable`):
- Ecosystem CLIs: `tg`, `review`, `draw`, `3d`, `rig`, `task` (alex-mextner/task-cli)
- External dev tools: `gh`, `git`, `rg`, `uv`, `bun`, `jq`, `gitleaks`

Nothing inherently-destructive (`rm`/`sudo`/`dd`) is in the default set. The grant is at the command-prefix level (`Bash(<tool>:*)` covers a tool's subcommands), so the restraint is in *which* tools are listed — docs are honest about this.

## Per-harness mechanism (researched; keyed off `harness.kind` / `permissions.kind`)

| Harness | File | Allowlist | Entry shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **claude-code** | `~/.claude/settings.json` | `permissions.allow` (array) | `Bash(<tool>:*)` |
| **opencode** | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `permission.bash` (object) | `"<tool> *": "allow"` |
| **codex** | `~/.codex/config.toml` | **N/A** | no config allowlist (approval/sandbox + Starlark execpolicy `.rules` is a separate mechanism) |
| **gemini / pi** | — | **N/A** | `tools.core`/`coreTools` *restricts* the toolset — writing it would disable every unlisted tool and break the harness |

## Invariants (tested)

- **Additive, never clobbers**: every existing allowlist entry (auto-mode, the user's accumulated list) is preserved; desired entries are merged in + deduped; a re-apply is a no-op.
- `disable` drops a tool from rig's *desired* set (so rig won't ADD it) — it never deletes an entry already on disk.
- Backup-on-conflict; fail-closed validation (tool-name shape, `.json` settings_path, N/A-kind guards).
- `rig status` reports an absent desired entry as `missing`, a wrong-shape file as `modified` (matching the error `apply` raises) — status and apply agree.

## Wiring

New `riglib/permissions.py` (the registry + renderers) + a `provision_permissions` action wired into plan / runner / drift / areas / layers / schema / config-validation — same pattern as the existing `harness` / `tg_ctl` provisioning. GLOBAL-only (the allowlist file is per-machine). Stayed entirely in new/own files + the registries (no churn in `cli.py`).

## Tests

- `tests/test_permissions.py` — 38 tests: resolve/render, additive-merge invariant, idempotency, opencode object form, drift (missing/modified/shape), malformed-JSON, error paths, `disable` safety, dual-target, validation.
- `tests/smoke.sh` — asserts the full default set lands in `permissions.allow` on a clean `rig init`.
- Full suite green (800 passed); smoke green. Multi-model review (`review --staged`) across several rounds; findings addressed.

title: feat(config): real, ENFORCED JSON Schema for rig.yaml + config docs in sync
body:
## What & why (ROADMAP §5)

Ships a **real, ENFORCED JSON Schema** for `rig.yaml` + the global config and actually VALIDATES against it — a malformed config now fails **loudly**, not silently. (`rig config get|set` from #40 is untouched; this is the schema + docs layer on top.)

## Changes

- **`riglib/config_schema.py`** — the single source of truth for the COMPLETE schema (every block + key, `additionalProperties: false`, open `items`/`fragments` maps for catalog item names). `schema.json_schema()` delegates here, so there is one emitter.
- **`schema/rig.schema.json`** — the committed, editor-facing Draft-07 document, generated from the registry. `rig.yaml` and the scaffold header carry a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=…` modeline so editors get **live completion + validation** (the same rules `rig apply` enforces).
- **`config.validate()`** now rejects an unknown key in **every** block (previously only `models`/`agents_md` were strict; `git_hooks` + `mcp` had no validator at all) and attaches a **schema path** to every error. Type/enum checks added where the schema and runtime had drifted (`ci`/`mcp`/`skills`/`agent_hooks` fixed knobs, `agent_hooks.target_kind` enum).
- **`ConfigError` is now a 3-part error** (what / why + schema path / fix) rendered on `apply` / `config set` / `status` / `init`. The JSON pointer resolves in the published file (stops at the open-map boundary instead of dangling on item names).
- **`rig schema`** — print / `--check` (CI-usable drift gate, exit 2) / `--write`.
- **`docs/config-schema.md`** documents the schema layer, every key, and the strictness change; a sync test keeps the file, the registry, and the validator in lockstep.

`tests/test_config_schema.py` (new) + extensions to `test_config.py` / `test_config_getset.py` / `test_cli.py`: valid configs pass; unknown-key / bad-value / bad-enum reject with the right error + exit 2 + schema path; the published schema is valid Draft-07 and equals the generator output; a real `jsonschema` validator flags the same things the runtime does; docs cover every key. **920 passed, 8 skipped.**

title: feat(config-web): web UI to view/edit rig config via shared agenttools-service
body:
## What

`rig config-web` — a local browser UI to view and edit the reconciled rig config, built as a THIRD front-end onto the same config engine the wizard and `rig config get|set` already drive (no parallel config logic).

- Renders every reconciled area from the option registry (`riglib/schema.py`) over the cascade (global `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` + repo `./rig.yaml`), tagged with the layer an edit lands in, each option with its inline hint and a live-typed control.
- An edit routes to the **owning layer** and is written by the **same `SetupState` serializer** `config set` uses (byte-identical; legacy `scope` dropped), with two fail-closed gates — schema validation, then a catalog-backed plan build (+ per-layer isolation for GLOBAL edits) with full rollback. The UI never persists a config `rig apply` would reject. It does NOT run apply. A rejected edit reverts the control in the browser.

## Lifecycle via the shared lib

`run`/`start`/`stop`/`status`/`enable`/`disable` + launchd/systemd autostart are delegated to the merged **`agenttools_service`** lib (PR #54) — not hand-rolled. The seam lazy-imports it (the parser never imports it, keeping `rig --help` clean) and fails closed with a `MissingDepError` otherwise. A bare `rig config-web` prints HELP and never launches. The daemon argv uses a `-c` bootstrap (works for symlink installs from any cwd); `-C` resolves the git root; the service identity carries a per-repo hash (no cross-repo pidfile collision); a busy port surfaces a structured error (exit 2).

## Security / robustness

Binds `127.0.0.1` only, plus: a same-origin **CSRF** guard (`Sec-Fetch-Site` + exact scheme+host+port `Origin`, fail-closed when port unknown), an `application/json` content-type requirement, a **Host-header (DNS-rebinding)** guard on every request, a 64 KiB body cap with safe `Content-Length` parsing, a per-request socket timeout, and a 1..65535 `--port` validator. Malformed config on GET, a write `OSError`, and a busy bind port all map to clean errors instead of a leaked traceback.

## Proof

Visual-proof-cycle done (screenshots in the CTO's Telegram): the config overview (all reconciled areas with layer badges + live values) and an edit interaction (toggle → success toast showing `key = value → file`), read back and verified. Live daemon smoke (start → GET 200 → stop), CSRF/Host guards (cross-port/foreign-host → 403), and busy-port clean error all verified end-to-end.

## Tests

903 passed / 10 skipped. Covers the view model, owning-layer routing, both write gates + isolation + rollback, HTML/XSS escaping, the real HTTP handler over a live socket (path whitelist, CSRF, cross-port Origin, Host rebinding, 415/413/500), the daemon argv booting a server as a subprocess, the lib-present lifecycle dispatch, and the CLI surface (bare→HELP, arg precedence, invalid-port + busy-port errors, lib-absent `MissingDepError`). ruff + mypy clean on the new files; gitleaks + leftover-grep pass. Five multi-model review rounds (glm/codex/gemini) — all High/Medium findings addressed.

title: feat(rig): provision per-repo gh-ship delegator as a reconciled area
body:
## What

Implements the ROADMAP "OWED" item: **`gh ship` must work in every repo via provisioning, not a runtime alias hack.**

`gh ship` is a gh alias → `<repo>/.claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh`, which until now existed **only in agent-tools**. In every other managed repo (rig-cli/review-cli/tg-cli) the delegator was missing, so `gh ship` failed there — papered over by a runtime alias fallback to the canonical `ship.sh`.

**Durable fix:** rig now provisions `.claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh` into every managed repo at init/apply, wired as a new reconciled REPO-layer area **`ship_delegator`** (init/apply/status), default ON (opt out with `ship_delegator: { enabled: false }`). Once this is everywhere, the agent-tools alias fallback can be dropped (follow-up below).

## How

- **Delegator** (`riglib/actions/runner.py::ship_delegator_content`): a thin shim that execs the canonical generalized ship — repo-local `ci/ship/ship.sh` first (so agent-tools self-hosts), else the rig-baked canonical path resolved from the agent-tools checkout at plan time (deterministic content → re-apply / drift compare is a byte-for-byte no-op).
- **Worktree hygiene** — ship refuses a dirty tree, so an un-ignored provisioned file would break the very command it enables. rig adds the delegator to the repo's `.git/info/exclude` (per-repo, never-committed), worktree-aware via `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` (in a worktree `info/exclude` is per-worktree). The entry is a rig-marker block reconciled idempotently and **atomically** (temp file + `os.replace`, so a hand-edited exclude is never half-clobbered).
- **Reconciled area** — `_build_ship_delegator` (plan), `_do_provision_ship_delegator` (runner), `_check_ship_delegator` (drift), `Area("ship_delegator", …)` (areas/layers), config block + validator + JSON Schema + `docs/config-schema.md`. apply and drift switch on one `resolve_ship_delegator` state, so status never misreports.

## Hardening (driven by multi-round review)

- **Shell-injection safe** — the canonical path derives from user-controlled `agent_tools_source`; it's `shlex.quote`'d before baking in, so a `$()`/backtick/quote/space can't break the script or execute on `gh ship`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` correctness** — the `git rev-parse` probe runs with `|| true`; without it, a non-git cwd aborted the whole script (exit 128) before the canonical fallback. Caught by an end-to-end execution test.
- **Fail-closed** — no `ci/ship/ship.sh` in the checkout → no delegator (a note); a malformed action with no `canonical_ship` → error, not a broken `canonical=` file. An un-writable `.git/info/exclude` → the action reports an **error** (a delegator written-but-not-ignored is the exact failure this prevents).
- **CRLF** — drift and reconcile both read RAW, so a CRLF exclude file doesn't make them disagree.

## Tests

`tests/test_ship_delegator.py` — 44 real tests (tmp HOME / git repos): content + shell-injection safety, **end-to-end delegation execution** (incl. repo-local shadowing, a path with spaces, the non-git fallback), file provisioned + git-ignored, worktree stays clean (proven via real `git check-ignore`), idempotency, stale/io_error/skip/overwrite, duplicate/unbalanced/misordered/mixed-duplicate exclude handling, surrounding-content + whitespace preservation, atomic-write-failure, both-degraded drift, default-on validation. Full suite + `tests/smoke.sh` green; schema + docs in sync.

## Follow-up (not this PR)

Drop the gh-alias fallback in agent-tools now that the delegator is provisioned everywhere.

## What & why

ROADMAP §5b ("rig manages tmux configuration") **and all 5 INCIDENT 2026-06-17 restore fixes are already implemented and merged** on `main`:

| INCIDENT fix | Where it landed |
|---|---|
| (1) cc-save detects cc by walking the pane PID-tree (handles the versioned binary e.g. `2.1.179`, not `pane_current_command == claude`) | `riglib/tmux.py` `render_cc_save` / `pane_has_claude` — PRs #28, #33 |
| (2) panes are LOGIN shells (`set -g default-command "$SHELL -l"`) | `riglib/tmux.py` `render_rig_conf` — #28 |
| (3) launchd boot runs a script that does `new-session -d` (loads conf+plugins+continuum-restore), not bare `start-server` | `render_boot_script` / `render_boot_plist` — #28 |
| (4) detect + remove the duplicate legacy `~/Library/LaunchAgents/Tmux.Start.plist` boot agent | `riglib/actions/runner.py` `_clean_stale_continuum_boot` — #28 |
| (5) single canonical attach-or-create | `render_attach_script` / `render_boot_script` — #24, #28 |

Import-preferred apply (rig owns `~/.config/rig/tmux/rig.tmux.conf`, `~/.tmux.conf` sources it) with managed-block fallback, conf migration + timestamped backup, and `rig status` drift on the managed region are all in place (#24/#26). The socket-leak teardown (kill **and** unlink the `-L` socket) shipped in #31.

**The one genuinely-open item is INCIDENT follow-up (a):** the tmux socket-leak **regression** — the test guarding the exact leak that killed the dev's tmux server (~185 stale `rigtest-*` sockets) — was hidden behind the e2e module's blanket `pytestmark` (`RIG_TMUX_E2E=1` + tmux + git + GitHub-reachable). So it **never ran in default hermetic CI or offline**, exactly when it matters. This PR closes that gap.

## Changes (test-only — no production code, no live-machine effect)

- Replace the blanket module-level `pytestmark` with two per-test gates:
  - `@_requires_tmux_e2e` (full opt-in + tmux + git + network) on the 5 plugin-cloning tests.
  - `@_requires_tmux` (tmux-present only, **no network, no opt-in flag**) on the socket-leak regression — so it runs in default hermetic CI (and on `ubuntu-latest` runners, which ship tmux).
- Move `test_old_continuum_boot_cleanup_removes_stale_entries` onto the tmux-only gate too — it MOCKs `_launchctl` + fabricates files + calls `_clean_stale_continuum_boot` directly (hermetic, was over-gated), so DEFECT-5 cleanup is now guarded on every PR.

It pins gating granularity by **marker identity** (immune to a `reason` reword), rejects only `skip`/`skipif` module marks (a benign `filterwarnings` won't false-trip), pins the network gate's **condition** (a weakened gate that drops the opt-in/network operands is caught), exhaustively classifies every `test_*` defined in the module (forward + reverse, with a hermetic-exempt escape hatch).

- `pytest -q` (hermetic): **1014 passed, 10 skipped** — the leak regression + boot-cleanup + meta-test now RUN (previously skipped).
- `RIG_TMUX_E2E=1 pytest tests/test_tmux_e2e.py tests/test_tmux_e2e_gating.py`: **8 passed** (real tmux round-trip).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh`: **OK**.

This touches **no production code and nothing on the live machine** (launchd / the running tmux server / launchd agents were NOT touched). But per the task constraint it is left **open for CTO verification** rather than shipped. Not `gh ship`-ed.

title: feat(rig): provision per-repo linter/formatter config as a reconciled area
body:
## What

New `linters` REPO area: rig provisions per-repo linter/formatter config files declaratively, the same way every other category is reconciled (CTO decision #4136.2).

A config-driven `linters.items` map declares, per repo, `{ tool, role?, path, content, enabled? }`. `rig init`/`apply` writes/reconciles each file (create when absent, repair when drifted, **never** clobber a hand-written file without an on_conflict-honoring backup); `rig status` reports drift. apply and drift switch on the **same** `resolve_linter_config` state, so status can never misreport.

Wired into `config_schema.py` / `config.py` / `plan.py` / `runner.py` / `drift.py` / `areas.py` / `layers.py` / `schema.py` + `docs/config-schema.md` + `schema/rig.schema.json`.

## Safety / containment

- **Fail-closed at load** via the single `linter_path_escapes_repo` predicate, **re-enforced** as defense-in-depth in runner/drift/resolver. Rejects: absolute, `..`-escaping, backslash, `.git`-component, and `.`-only paths (repo root can never name a file).
- **Symlinks refused** at the leaf or any parent component (in-repo or escaping) — rig never writes through a link.
- **Non-directory parent** classified as io_error up front (status and apply agree) instead of a bare `FileExistsError` at apply.
- **Line endings normalized to LF** on both sides — a CRLF/CR `content:` literal converges instead of perpetually drifting (write CRLF → read LF → never-equal). Also covers a CRLF-on-disk file vs LF-in-config.
- **Empty content rejected** rather than writing a 0-byte file (runner + drift, mirroring the plan builder).
