title: feat(hooks): gate rig smoke on pre-commit locally (fast subset)
body:
## What & why

CTO 2026-06-16: `rig` smoke ran in **CI only** — it never gated commits **locally**. Two same-day prod failures (a stale `mcp.items.review` removed-slot, a dead config) shipped after a green `pytest` but a **broken real `rig status` flow**, caught only after push. This wires the local half of the requirement: a commit that breaks the real CLI flow is blocked on **pre-commit**, not just in CI.

ROADMAP: `agent-tools/ROADMAP.md` § "rig MUST gate smoke.sh on pre-commit + always run smoke" (req 1).

## How

- **`tests/smoke.sh --fast`** — the seconds-cheap pre-commit subset. Runs the CLI surface (`--help`/`--version`/`doctor`/`setup`-usage) + the real-catalog `rig status` regression legs (clean sample exit 0; removed slot → 3-part error + exit 4; non-git no-nag). **Skips** the heavy `rig init --yes` apply, the tg-ctl apply, and the full `pytest`. Self-skips the catalog legs (exit 0) when no agent-tools checkout is present, so a checkout-less contributor is **never blocked**. `--help` prints only the doc comment; an unknown arg exits 2.
- **`scripts/install-smoke-precommit.sh`** — run once per clone/worktree to wire a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` shim that execs the tracked gate. Idempotent; resolves the absolute git-dir (correct for worktrees/submodules); expands a `~`-prefixed `core.hooksPath`; refuses a symlinked or non-shell foreign hook; prepends **above** a no-shebang exit-first hook.
- **`scripts/smoke-precommit-hook.sh`** — the tracked gate. Runs `smoke --fast` (blocks on failure) with the `GIT_*` hook env **stripped** (so smoke's own `git`/`rig` calls stay hermetic — an env-leak found by dogfooding), then chains the global dispatcher with **fail-safe dedup**: it skips its own chain only when the `core.hooksPath` composer is active AND its `pre-commit` actually invokes the dispatcher (path-canonicalized, `~`/`$HOME`/symlink robust); otherwise it always chains (a duplicate read-only secret-scan beats *dropping* it).

## Acceptance evidence

- **Full unit suite green:** `1034 passed, 13 skipped` (was 1011; +24 new tests, all real — they drive a real `git commit` through the installed hook in HOME-isolated throwaway repos: block/pass, bypass, worktree commit, symlink/non-shell refuse, composer dedup + fail-safe, `~`-hookspath, git-env strip).
- **Full real-flow smoke green:** `smoke OK` (all apply legs + `1034 passed` pytest).
- **`--fast` runs in ~0.7s** and exercises the real-catalog `rig status` legs; skips the heavy apply + pytest.
- **Dogfooded:** this very PR's commit ran the gate through the global composer — `rig status: clean sample → exit 0`, `removed slot → 3-part error + exit 4`, all green, no `--no-verify`.
- **Pre-commit review:** glm + codex (single-seat) across rounds; every actionable finding fixed (tilde/`$HOME` hookspath, symlink + non-shell refuse, no-shebang insertion, fail-safe dedup, hermetic tests, the git-env leak) or justified (residual composer-grep edge, global non-rig `core.hooksPath` — documented in AGENTS.md).

## Known residual (justified, documented)

- A non-rig **global `core.hooksPath`** that does not trampoline into `$git_dir/hooks` bypasses the local gate — documented caveat in AGENTS.md (the standard rig composer trampolines correctly).
- The real-catalog `--fast` legs are not run in CI (CI has no agent-tools checkout — a pre-existing gap shared with the full smoke). Tracked as a follow-up.

body:
## What & why

ROADMAP §5 ("rig provisions REPOSITORY SETTINGS at init/apply") + CTO #4136.1 ("AUTONOMOUS, ASK-and-WAIT on missing auth"). rig now reconciles a repo's full GitHub settings surface autonomously, with **secure defaults ON** and two-way `rig status` drift, the same way it reconciles skills/hooks/CI. **Supersedes #37** (the merge-button-policy-only PR) — that block is folded in here, rebased onto the current architecture.

## Backends & what's reconciled (secure defaults)

**`gh api` backend** (all `argv`, never a shell; one `_gh_api` seam):

| block | endpoint | secure default |
|---|---|---|
| `github.ruleset` | branch ruleset | require-PR, block force-push/deletion, **REQUIRED STATUS CHECKS** auto-derived from the repo's merge-gating CI gates (`PR Checklist` + `review-threads`), admin kept able to merge |
| `github.merge` | `PATCH /repos` | squash-only (merge-commit/rebase OFF), auto-delete-head, allow-auto-merge, allow-update-branch |
| `github.ghas` | `security_and_analysis` + sub-resource + CodeQL endpoints | vuln-alerts + Dependabot + secret-scanning (+ push protection) + CodeQL default-setup |
| `github.actions` | two `actions/permissions` endpoints | Actions on, GITHUB_TOKEN **read-only**, workflows may not approve PRs |

**`agent-browser` backend** (`github.browser`): drives the settings UI for API-unreachable toggles; gated off at apply unless `RIG_GH_BROWSER=1`, loud degrade on a logged-out session.

## The #4136.1 auth gate (`github_auth.py`)

Every `gh api` provisioner clears the gate **before its first live read** — an unauthenticated `rig apply` **notifies the user via `tg`** and **blocks/polls** up to `RIG_GH_AUTH_WAIT` for login, then **resumes**. The autonomous default (0 budget) degrades loudly (a visible error result) instead of hanging or spamming the phone; a positive budget opts into the interactive "ask and wait", deduped per-kind across actions in one apply. Skipped under `RIG_GH_DRY_RUN`.

## Lockout-safe by construction

- The ruleset never emits the `update` rule (inherited guard); admins always retain a bypass.
- Required status checks are derived ONLY from CI gates that are **enabled AND written to `.github/workflows`** — requiring a check whose workflow isn't present (export-only, a custom target, a disabled gate) would wedge every PR, so it never happens. A hermetic test binds each required context to the job name in the workflow the same plan writes.

## Capability degrade

- No github remote → `skipped`. Failed repo read / no admin → a **visible** error (apply) / "could not verify" drift item (status) — never a silent green.
- A GHAS scanner unavailable on a private repo's plan **degrades loudly** and does NOT block the free features (vuln-alerts/Dependabot/CodeQL applied independently); a genuine auth/transient failure is a **hard error**, not a masked degrade. Disabling Actions skips the workflow-token PUT (which GitHub would reject).

## Tests — no real repo is mutated

`tests/test_github_settings.py` (80+ tests) + extensions to `test_github_ruleset.py`/`test_catalog_plan.py`. Every `gh` / `agent-browser` / auth-probe / git seam is monkeypatched — no network, no real repo, no phone, no browser. `RIG_GH_DRY_RUN` proves no mutation; a **live dry-run against `alex-mextner/rig-cli`** read the real state and was **byte-identical before/after**.

```
$ python -m pytest -q
1200 passed, 13 skipped
```

## Review

Nine rounds of pre-commit multi-model review (Opus fallback — glm was throttled). Every correctness finding fixed with a regression test: auth-gate-before-read (was dead code on the no-token case), GHAS free-features-not-blocked-by-unlicensed-scanner, hard-error-vs-degrade split classified on the full error string, the required-check lockout whitelist, the Actions-disabled convergence, the per-apply notify dedup, the browser login path-segment/SSO probe. Remaining notes are documented non-blockers (status API cost on default-ON blocks, `allowed_actions: selected` footgun, a few cross-field 422 validations left to live-degrade).

## ship = the merge wave decides

This track touches GitHub org/repo settings; this PR **applies nothing** to any live repo (dry-run-proven) and is ready for the green-CI-gated merge.

title: feat(rig): per-harness skill/instruction discovery for all supported harnesses (#9)
body:
## What

rig's skill harness-link was claude-code-only (`_HARNESS_SKILL_DIRS = {claude-code: ~/.claude/skills}`, config schema REJECTED opencode/codex/gemini/pi). This extends per-harness **skill/instruction discovery** to every supported harness, keyed off `harness.kind`.

New single source of truth `riglib/harness_skills.py` maps each kind to its discovery convention, in two families:

**skills-DIRECTORY harnesses** — rig symlinks each installed skill in (one `link_skill_harness` action per skill; the runner/drift are already harness-agnostic):
- `claude-code` → `~/.claude/skills`
- `opencode` → `~/.config/opencode/skill` (XDG-aware)

**instruction-FILE harnesses** — no per-skill dir; guidance reaches them via a global `AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md` the `agents_md` area maintains. rig links nothing (never guesses a dir) and records a status note naming the file so `rig status` isn't a silent empty area:
- `codex` → `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`
- `gemini` → `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`
- `pi` → `~/.config/pi/AGENTS.md`
- `commandcode` → `~/.commandcode/AGENTS.md`

## Behavior

- Config schema now **accepts** all of these in `harness.kind` (sourced from the registry, so the JSON-schema enum can't drift from `config.validate`). A typo still fails closed with the supported list.
- The auto/permission-**MODE** write stays claude-code-only and **self-skips** other kinds with a plan note (previously a hard reject for opencode; would've been a silent no-op now). Same for an explicitly-enabled `hook_bridge` on a non-claude kind.
- `permissions` already guards via `harness_supported()` — codex/gemini/pi report N/A cleanly (no KeyError), verified.
- `_resolve_harness_skill_dir` returns `None` for instruction-file kinds; an explicit `skills.harness_skill_dir` forces a directory link even there. The discovery note respects `skills.enabled: false`.

## Tests (under tmp HOME)

Provisioned + idempotent + drift for both skills-dir harnesses; no-link + explanatory note for each instruction-file harness; explicit-dir override links; auto-mode self-skip note per non-claude kind; explicit hook_bridge skip note; note suppressed when skills disabled. Full suite green (1219 passed, 13 skipped) + smoke.

Docs (`config-schema.md`/`README`/`AGENTS.md`) updated; `schema/rig.schema.json` regenerated and in-sync.

Closes #9 scope extension (the cc-only link from #9 was already in; this makes it all-harness).

Reviewed: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` — review-stamp matches the committed diff.

## Follow-ups (out of scope, not blocking)
- opencode auto/permission-**mode** write (its `opencode.json` `permission` block) is still unimplemented — the skill discovery is wired; the mode write is tracked separately.
- Instruction-file harnesses get skill *discovery* via AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md; aggregating skill **content** into those files (e.g. a `GEMINI.md` variant of the `agents_md` provisioning) is a separate area.

title: fix(tmux): neutralize pre-existing rig-owned plugin/continuum/resurrect init on migration
body:
## The bug (hit on the live machine 2026-06-18)

`riglib/tmux.py`'s tmux migration appended rig's `source-file` import to an existing hand-written `~/.tmux.conf` but left the user's **pre-existing** tpm/resurrect/continuum init LIVE above it → **DOUBLE INIT** on the next tmux start:

- the old `run-shell .../tmux-continuum/continuum.tmux` fired continuum-restore **before** rig's appended `source-file` set the login-shell `default-command` → restored panes spawned **non-login** (`~/.zprofile` skipped in every pane);
- the old `@continuum-boot 'on'` / `@resurrect-processes 'ssh ... rails ...'` fought rig's clean values;
- continuum's autosave hook (in `status-right`) got wiped because the old continuum init ran before the Moshi-ordering fix.

The module docstring already NAMED this "stale-session-on-reboot" bug and rig already had the precedent of commenting migrated lines (`# rig-migrated (now in rig.tmux.conf): `). This completes that migration.

## The fix

Migration now **neutralizes** the rig-OWNED init in the user's region, in **both import and block apply mode**, leaving only personal prefs + the single rig `source-file` (or managed block) active:

- the three rig `@plugin` decls (tpm, tmux-resurrect, tmux-continuum) — matched by **exact** quoted/bare spec (a fork `tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect-fork` is NOT swept; the specs are derived from `PLUGINS`, one source of truth);
- every `@continuum-*` / `@resurrect-*` option — anchored to a `set`/`set-option`/`set-window-option`/`setw` directive (a token inside a value or keybinding is NOT matched);
- the plugin-init `run-shell`/`run` lines — matched on the run **command**, not a nested arg (`run-shell "tar ... continuum.tmux"` stays live);
- the Moshi `status-left`/`status-right` wipe.

**Preserved (no over-reach):** third-party `@plugin` (rig's tpm loads it), all personal prefs, `update-environment MOSHI_CLIENT`, a real `status-right` value, and any rig-owned line a user GUARDED inside their own `{ ... }` conditional (structural brace skip with full nesting — never leaves a dangling brace). rig's own managed block (block mode) is skipped by both passes, so neutralization never corrupts rig's generated config. **Idempotent**: re-applying a migrated conf is byte-identical and never re-backs-up.

Also fixes a latent **perpetual-backup** bug: `has_inline_rig_settings` is now defined as "neutralization changes the user region" (single source of truth with the neutralizer), so a conf carrying only `update-environment MOSHI_CLIENT` no longer triggers a backup on every apply.

## Tests

- `tests/test_tmux.py`: full migration coverage — both modes, idempotency, third-party/pref preservation, nested + user-guarded braces, decorative-brace-in-value, fork/XDG/set-hook/abbreviation known limitations, `has_inline_rig_settings` consistency.
- `tests/test_tmux_e2e.py` (`@_requires_tmux`, hermetic, no network): two real-tmux **parse-validity** checks — a migrated legacy conf (with nested user braces) and a comment-only-brace body both load with `tmux ... new-session -d` exit 0; registered in the gating guard.
- The backward-incompatible scope (rig now also neutralizes unmodeled `@resurrect-strategy-vim` / `@continuum-boot-options`, recoverable from the timestamped `.rig-bak-<UTC>` backup) is documented in `docs/config-schema.md` + the module/function docstrings.

**CI run:** `python -m pytest -q` → 1241 passed, 13 skipped. `bash tests/smoke.sh` → OK.

title: test(smoke): real-catalog full-coverage leg + CI job against the live agent-tools catalog
body:
## What

rig discovers CI gates / skills / hooks by scanning an agent-tools checkout on disk, but the unit suite + smoke only exercised a **synthetic** in-repo fixture (a curated handful of slots). A rig change that breaks against the **real** catalog layout — a new slot type, a renamed dir, a catalog item rig can't resolve — was unit-GREEN but live-BROKEN. This exact class (`unknown ci item: pr-checklist`) has bitten before.

This adds a real-catalog drift guard.

## Changes

- **`tests/smoke.sh`** — `_real_catalog_full_coverage`: writes an everything-on `rig.yaml` (skills / agent_hooks / ci `all:true` + every by-type kind discovered on disk + dispatcher), runs `rig apply --dry-run` against the real catalog, and asserts:
  - exit 0 (rig can plan the whole real catalog),
  - **zero** unknown-item/slot errors (portable ERE detector — BRE `\|` is GNU-only and dead on macOS BSD grep),
  - the dry-run wrote nothing,
  - **every** `ci/<slot>/` dir on disk appears in the plan (bullet-anchored fixed-string match → catches a slot the scanner silently drops, even if the slot name appears inside another line's target path), and
  - **non-vacuous** coverage (fails if `ci/` is renamed/removed so the loop would pass hollow).

  Plan/dry-run only — no machine is mutated. It writes nothing, so it runs in `--fast` too (the pre-commit subset covers it).

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — a `real-catalog-smoke` job checks out the public `alex-mextner/agent-tools` repo (default-branch HEAD on purpose: a co-evolution drift guard must track the *current* catalog, so pinning would freeze the thing it watches) into a sibling path and runs `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` against it. **Resilient**: the catalog checkout is best-effort (`continue-on-error`); an unreachable/incomplete catalog SKIPS the job **loudly** (`::warning::` + a visible skip line) instead of hard-failing CI on infra it doesn't own.

- **`tests/test_smoke_precommit.py`** — `test_real_catalog_full_coverage_plans_every_item`: an opt-in pytest mirror (gated `RIG_SMOKE_FAST_E2E=1`) that SKIPS loudly without a checkout, so the leg is runnable locally and the hermetic `pytest -q` stays offline-safe.

- **`AGENTS.md`** — documents the new leg + CI job + opt-in mirror.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest -q` → **1241 passed, 14 skipped** (the +1 skip vs. before is the new opt-in test correctly skipping in the hermetic run).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` (full, real catalog) → exit 0; the coverage leg reports `zero unknown items; 13 ci slots covered` (ai-review, codeql, copilot-findings, dependency-review, leftover-grep, pr-checklist, pr-title-lint, review-threads, sast, screenshots, secret-scan, ship, tests).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → exit 0 in ~0.9s (pre-commit-safe).
- Adversarial: an injected new slot raises the covered count (no hardcoded list); a dropped slot — including the trap where its name appears in another line's target path — fails the guard; an empty `ci/` fails the vacuous-coverage check; the loud-skip CI path emits the warning and exits 0.

Reviewed with opus single-seat (`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8`); all actionable findings addressed (BRE→ERE portability, fixed-string + bullet-anchored slot match, vacuous-coverage guard, CI `--fast` to honor the plan/dry-run-only intent).

title: feat(doctor): guard against core.bare=true corruption on a working checkout
body:
## What

A non-bare working checkout with `core.bare=true` silently breaks **every** git operation there (`status`/`diff`/`commit`/`worktree` → `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`) and breaks ship's main-refresh. The 2026-06-18 incident hit rig-cli's own main checkout; the cause was never found. This adds a `rig doctor` guard that turns a baffling outage into a one-line diagnosis.

## Forensic conclusion (Part 1): the cause is NOT in rig

Searched `riglib/` + `bin/` + `scripts/` + `ci/` + `install.sh` and the **full** git history (`git log --all -S`).

- The only git-config **write** in the whole codebase is `_set_git_global()` (`actions/runner.py`): it writes **only** `--global` and **only** the literal keys `core.hooksPath` / `core.excludesfile` — never `core.bare`, never to a repo's local `.git/config`.
- The most invasive thing rig does to a repo's git dir is a marker block in `.git/info/exclude`. rig **explicitly refuses** to provision any path under `.git/` (`config.py` guard, tested in `test_linters.py`).
- `git log --all -S` for `core.bare` / `init --bare` / `clone --bare` / `worktree add` is **empty** — no such code has ever existed.

**Conclusion: no rig code path can corrupt `core.bare`.** The cause is external (a stray manual / other-tool `git init --bare`, a leaked `GIT_DIR` under a wrapper, or finger-trouble). So the highest-value deliverable is detection.

## The guard (Part 2)

`rig doctor` now scans the cwd repo + every worktree it lists and flags any checkout that has the working-checkout layout (a `.git` dir/file) yet git reports as **bare**.

Key design decisions (each pinned by a test):
- **Worktree-aware detection, not a raw config read.** A legitimate linked worktree of a *genuine* bare repo reads `core.bare=true` from the shared config but is a healthy work tree. Flagging it — and `--fix`-ing it — would **break that valid setup**. Detection uses `rev-parse --is-bare-repository` (the per-path effective answer), which is `false` for such a worktree.
- **`--fix` re-verifies.** It writes `core.bare=false` then re-checks effective bareness, because a `true` sourced from a worktree/`[include]` scope survives a plain local write — without the re-check `--fix` would falsely claim success.
- **Env scrubbing.** Every git call strips `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_CONFIG*`/discovery vars so a leaked hook env (rig now runs from pre-commit) can't point the verdict or the destructive `--fix` at the wrong repo.
- **New exit code 7** (repo corrupt) takes precedence over missing-dep (127) / missing-target (5); the `--help` epilog documents it.

## Part 3 follow-up (out of scope here)

If agent-tools' `ci/ship/ship.sh` main-refresh also broke on this corruption, harden its git ops to detect/abort on `core.bare=true` — **because** the same one-line config flip silently breaks ship for every repo, and a clear abort beats a confusing mid-ship failure. That's a different repo, so it is not fixed in this PR.

## Tests / gate

- `python -m pytest -q` → **1276 passed, 14 skipped**
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` → all legs green, **smoke OK**
- 58 dedicated tests in `tests/test_core_bare.py` + `tests/test_cli.py`, all using temp git repos — **no real machine repo is ever mutated**.
- Reviewed across 10 opus single-seat rounds; every substantive finding fixed (literal-`true` false negative, path quoting, the bare-repo-worktree false-positive/destructive-fix, env-leak hardening).

title: fix(rig): drop the dead mcp.items.review slot from the shipped template
body:
## Problem

The repo's committed `rig.yaml` declared the **removed** MCP slot:

```yaml
mcp:
  items:
    review:
      enabled: true
      command: "review --mcp"
```

But `review --mcp` was dropped in agent-tools #32, the real catalog has **no** `mcp/review` item, and rig's own `_REMOVED_SLOTS` registry already classifies `mcp.review` as removed. So `rig status` against the repo's **own** config died at exit 4:

```
error: removed mcp slot: review
  fix: remove `mcp.items.review` from .../rig.yaml
```

The smoke clean-sample uses a synthetic config that omits `mcp.review`, and the unit suite's *fake* catalog (`conftest.py`) creates a fake `mcp/review/` item — so both stayed green while the real flow was broken. Same class as the ROADMAP-flagged "unit-GREEN but smoke-BROKEN" failures.

## Fix (fix-or-remove → remove, per ROADMAP §9)

- Drop `mcp.items.review` from `rig.yaml`; keep the `mcp` block with empty `items: {}` + a comment explaining why review is not an MCP.
- Replace the dead `review --mcp` example in `docs/config-schema.md` with the catalog-endorsed code-search (serena) example + a note that `mcp.items.review` is a removed slot.

## Regression test (RED-first)

`tests/test_errors.py` gets two legs, both proven to fail with the dead slot re-added:

1. **Fast hermetic guard** — reads the real committed `rig.yaml` + the in-code removed-slot registry (no catalog needed; runs in every CI leg). Includes a positive control asserting the detector actually sees `mcp.review`, so it can't pass for the wrong reason.
2. **End-to-end leg** — runs the real `plan.build` validation of the actual `rig.yaml` against the **real** agent-tools catalog (the same path `rig status` runs); skips gracefully when no catalog is reachable.

## Verification

- New tests RED-first → GREEN (e2e leg raises the real `riglib.errors.UnknownItemError: removed mcp slot: review` from `plan.build` when the dead slot is present).
- `rig status --config rig.yaml`: no longer exits 4 on the removed slot.
- Full pytest suite: **1283 passed, 12 skipped**.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` and `--fast`: exit 0 ("smoke OK").
- ruff on changed files: clean.
- Review-gate (`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8`): **[ok]**.

Closes #59

title: test(rig): fake catalog mirrors reality — drop fabricated removed mcp/review slot
body:
## Problem (the masking)

`tests/conftest.py` fabricated a FAKE `mcp/review/` catalog item, and the drift/plan/catalog tests used `mcp.items.review` / `review --mcp` as a generic mcp fixture. But `review --mcp` was REMOVED in agent-tools #32 (review is a CLI + skill, not an MCP server); the REAL catalog (`agent-tools/mcp/`) has only a `README.md` — zero scannable mcp items — and `riglib.errors._REMOVED_SLOTS` classifies `("mcp","review")` as removed.

So the fake catalog did NOT mirror reality. `_validate_item_names` resolves a config's `mcp.items.<x>` against `catalog.names("mcp")`: under the fake catalog `review` was VALID (the dir existed) → validation passed; under the REAL catalog `review` is absent → removed-slot error (exit 4). That divergence is exactly the masking that let a dead `mcp.items.review` slot ship green in the shipped `rig.yaml` template — it only surfaced against the real catalog (PR #60).

Two test layers were already silently working around it (`test_plan_errors.py` hand-stripped the `review` item; `smoke.sh` guarded the declaration behind `if [[ -d "$SRC/mcp/review" ]]`).

## Fix

- **conftest**: fabricate a clearly-synthetic `mcp/fake-mcp` item instead of the removed `mcp/review`.
- **test_actions_drift / test_plan_errors / test_catalog_plan**: migrate every dependent fixture + assertion to `fake-mcp` (register-mcp, backup-convergence, drift detection, server-name rename, did-you-mean typo). The removed-slot test now hits the removed-slot path without hand-stripping the catalog — honest, since the fake catalog now mirrors reality (a positive control asserts `review` is absent).
- **Anti-masking guard** `test_fake_catalog_never_fabricates_a_removed_slot`: fails if any fabricated fake-catalog item is a `_REMOVED_SLOTS` entry. Verified it fails (`fabricates removed slot(s) ['mcp/review']`) when the fixture regresses — so a dead/removed slot used as a fixture is now caught by the unit suite, not only the real-catalog e2e.

## Verification

- Full rig suite: **1283 passed, 13 skipped** (was 1282 — the new guard).
- Ruff clean on all 4 changed files.
- Review-gate `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1`: no bugs found; both actionable notes (suite-wide rename sweep, `removed_slot` is public) verified resolved.

Closes #61

title: fix(status): missing-target scan follows the configured settings path, not a hardcoded ~/.claude (#63)
body:
## What

`rig status` / `rig doctor` scan the harness `settings.json` for hook commands pointing at a script gone from disk (the dead-rtk-hook case), surfacing it as a structured missing-target error before it bites at runtime as a generic "PreToolUse error". But `_scan_missing_targets` was **hardcoded** to `~/.claude/settings.json` — its own docstring flagged this as unfinished ("future multi-harness expansion").

## Why this was a bug

rig resolves the harness settings file per config: the `apply_harness`, `provision_permissions`, and `register_hook_bridge` plan actions each carry the resolved settings path as `action.target`, honoring a `harness.settings_path` / `permissions.settings_path` override and the harness kind (e.g. a non-`auto` mode writes the repo-local `.claude/settings.json`, not the one under HOME).

When a repo's rig.yaml points the harness settings at a non-default path (a supported, validated config), the old scan looked at the **wrong** file and silently reported nothing — a dead hook in the actually-managed settings file went unflagged. Exactly the silent-success failure the error-system v2 exists to kill.

## How

- New `_harness_settings_paths(plan)` derives the settings file(s) to scan from the harness-writing action targets (via `harness_settings_file`), deduped.
- `_scan_missing_targets(settings_paths)` scans those; `None` (the `rig doctor` case, no config loaded) falls back to the HOME default. An **empty** list is NOT `None` — it means this config provisions no harness settings file, so there is nothing to scan (scanning the HOME default there would cry wolf on an unmanaged file).
- Scoped to **claude-code**: the scanner understands only the claude-code `settings.json` `hooks` shape, so an opencode `provision_permissions` target (`opencode.json`, a different schema) is excluded. Keyed off `options['kind']`.

## Tests (RED-first)

- dead hook in a non-default settings file is flagged (would be missed before);
- empty list scans nothing, not the HOME default;
- opencode targets are excluded from the claude-hook scan;
- a **real-plan** integration test (harness + permissions + hook-bridge all claude-code) asserts every real builder tags `options['kind']` and its settings path is scanned — closing the gap that the unit tests hand-build actions.

Full rig suite green (1290 passed), ruff clean on changed files. Reviewed across opus + codex (both `[ok]`).

Closes #63

title: feat(provision): rig installs the personal CLI ecosystem (tg/review/task/draw) at apply
body:
## What

rig's PRIMARY purpose is installing our personal CLI tool ecosystem — but `rig apply` provisioned skills/agent-hooks/git-hooks/tmux/cron and **not** the CLIs (`tg`/`review`/`task`/`draw`), which were self-installed out of band. This adds a `tools:` provisioning category so `rig apply` installs + advertises the whole ecosystem, declaratively.

Closes #66.

## How

For each declared tool, rig runs the tool's **own `install.sh`** (which locates the repo, installs deps, symlinks the entry into the managed PATH dir, and runs `<tool> install-skill` to advertise it into the agent harness). rig never reimplements that — the tool stays the single source of truth for how it installs, so a tool changing its install is inherited for free.

```yaml
# GLOBAL layer (~/.config/rig/config.yaml) — per-MACHINE concern, never a committed rig.yaml
tools:
  enabled: true              # opt-in; absent/false/omitted provisions nothing
  target: ~/.local/bin       # managed PATH dir each tool symlinks its bin into
  items:
    tg:     { repo: ~/.files/repos/tg-cli }
    review: { repo: ~/xp/review-cli }
    task:   { repo: ~/xp/task-cli }
    draw:   { repo: ~/xp/draw-cli }
```

Mirrors the `tg_ctl`/`tmux` category shape: a stdlib-only effect-free `riglib/tools.py` shared by plan/apply/drift; the runner does the effectful install; drift diffs desired-vs-on-disk.

## Idempotency + safety

- **No-op when current**: a tool whose bin resolves AND skill is advertised is `skipped` — rig does not re-run `install.sh` nor delete a user's symlink.
- **Default OFF**: an absent/empty block, OR one that lists items but omits `enabled: true`, provisions nothing (truthy `enabled` check, not `is False` — so listing items can't surprise-install).
- **No foreign-binary masquerade**: a bin that resolves on PATH counts only when its real path lands inside the declared repo, so a same-named stranger (Taskwarrior `task`, another `draw`) does not read as installed.
- **Crash-safe timeout**: `RIG_TOOL_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_S` is parsed at call time with a fallback, so junk can't wedge the whole CLI at import.

## Drift

`rig status` flags a declared tool whose bin doesn't resolve (**missing** — apply runs its `install.sh`) or that resolves but isn't advertised (**modified** — apply re-runs `install-skill`).

## Tests

34 new tests in `tests/test_tools.py` (config parse/reject, spec resolution incl. the default-OFF regression, install/idempotency/already-installed-elsewhere/missing-repo/install.sh-failure/mixed-outcomes/dry-run, foreign-binary guard, timeout safe-parse, drift missing/modified/clean, plan emit/no-emit). Full suite green (1322 passed), schema regenerated + in sync, docs section added, ruff + mypy clean on the new code.

title: fix(version): rig --version reads pyproject dynamically (no stale literal)
body:
## Problem

`rig --version` printed a hardcoded `__version__ = "0.1.0"` in `riglib/__init__.py` that was never bumped across releases — a permanently-stale freshness signal, useless for telling which build you run or whether a fix landed. The pyproject `[project] version` was also stuck at `0.1.0` and could drift from the literal.

Closes #70.

## Fix

- **`pyproject.toml [project] version` is now the single source of truth.** New `riglib/_version.py` resolves the version via `importlib.metadata.version("rig-cli")` when installed, falling back to parsing the local `pyproject.toml` when running from a live checkout (the normal rig case — `bin/rig` adds the repo to `sys.path`, so no install metadata exists). Both paths converge on the same value.
- **`__version__` derives from that resolver** — no hardcoded literal remains.
- **Bumped `0.1.0` -> `0.2.0`** so `--version` reflects this change.
- **Stdlib-only at import time** (the package rule): `importlib.metadata` + a scoped `re` over the `[project]` table. Deliberately NOT `tomllib` — absent on Python 3.10, still in the CI matrix.

## Durable drift guard

`tests/test_cli.py` pins **`rig --version` == pyproject `[project] version`**, forced through the live-checkout path (`PackageNotFoundError` mocked) so it measures REAL drift, not local install state. Reintroduce a literal, or bump pyproject without the dynamic read flowing through, and CI goes red. A scoped-parser unit test also covers decoy `version` keys in other tables and `[`-array continuations.

## Verification

- `python3 bin/rig --version` -> `rig 0.2.0`
- Full suite green: `1330 passed, 15 skipped`
- Ruff clean on changed files

title: test(provision): regression-guard that rig provisions require-ticket-before-commit (#65)
body:
## What

Adds `test_real_catalog_provisions_require_ticket_guard` to `tests/test_errors.py` — a regression test asserting that `rig` provisions the `require-ticket-before-commit` agent-hook from the agent-tools catalog into every repo's plan.

## Why

agent-tools #92 made the require-ticket guard strict-by-default; rig must provably provision it into every repo (the CTO's "enforced in every repo"). Without this test, a regression — a catalog rename/move, or rig's default flipping the hook to opt-in — would silently un-provision the guard, and nothing would catch it until a human noticed ticketless commits sailing through.

## What it asserts

Mirrors the existing `test_real_catalog_*` harness (skips when no agent-tools checkout is reachable). Two halves, end-to-end against the REAL catalog:

1. **the hook EXISTS in the catalog scan** — a rename/move that drops `require-ticket-before-commit` is caught.
2. **rig's DEFAULT plan installs it** — builds a plan from a config with NO `agent_hooks` overrides, so it exercises rig's own default (`plan.build` does `setdefault("all", True)` for an enabled/absent agent_hooks block), and asserts an `install_agent_hook` action for the hook is emitted — i.e. `rig apply` would write its descriptor into `~/.claude/hooks`.

Building from the default (not a hand-forced `all: true`) is the point: it guards against the default itself regressing to opt-in.

## RED-first proof

Verified the test fails for the right reason in two regression scenarios:
- **catalog drops the hook** → half 1 fails: `require-ticket-before-commit missing from the real agent-tools catalog` (positive control confirms the other 16 hooks are still present, so the failure is specifically the missing guard, not a broken scan).
- **default flips to opt-in** (`all: false`) → half 2 fails: the hook is absent from the plan's `install_agent_hook` actions.

Full rig suite green (1330 passed, 16 skipped — the real-catalog tests skip without a catalog, as designed). Ruff clean on the changed file. Review-gate: `claude:claude-opus-4-8` `[ok]`.

## Note (pre-existing, out of scope)

The `test_real_catalog_*` family — including this test — skips in CI's unit job (no catalog) and is not run by the `--fast` real-catalog smoke job, so it currently only fires under a full local `smoke.sh` with the catalog present. That's a pre-existing weakness in the established pattern, not introduced here; tracked separately.

Closes #65

title: ci: run the real-catalog pytest guards in CI so they actually gate
body:
## The gap (Closes #73)

The `test_real_catalog_*` test family — including #72's require-ticket provisioning guard (`test_real_catalog_provisions_require_ticket_guard`, agent-tools#92) — **never ran in CI**. Those regression guards were theater: a regression would pass CI.

### Root cause

These tests `pytest.skip` without an agent-tools catalog (`Catalog.scan(None)` / `_agent_tools_source()` raises `CatalogError`), and the two smoke-e2e legs are additionally gated `@pytest.mark.skipif(RIG_SMOKE_FAST_E2E != "1")`. Two CI jobs exist:

- **`test`** (unit suite) runs `python -m pytest -q` with **no catalog** → every `test_real_catalog_*` SKIPS.
- **`real-catalog-smoke`** fetches the catalog (sets `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE`) but runs `smoke.sh --fast`, and `--fast` **skips the pytest leg entirely** (`smoke.sh` exits at its `--fast` early-return before the pytest section).

Net: the real-catalog pytest guards ran only under a full local `smoke.sh`, never in CI. A regression — rig stops provisioning `require-ticket-before-commit`, the `agent_hooks` default flips to opt-in, or a catalog rename rig can't resolve — was unit-GREEN and shipped unguarded.

The three affected tests:
- `tests/test_errors.py::test_repo_rig_yaml_plans_clean_against_the_real_catalog`
- `tests/test_errors.py::test_real_catalog_provisions_require_ticket_guard`  ← #72
- `tests/test_smoke_precommit.py::test_real_catalog_full_coverage_plans_every_item`

## The fix

A dedicated step in the existing `real-catalog-smoke` job (it already fetches the catalog + computes `$SRC`) runs **just** the real-catalog pytest leg with both gates lifted:

- `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE=$SRC` — resolves the catalog so the `Catalog.scan` / `_agent_tools_source` skips don't fire;
- `RIG_SMOKE_FAST_E2E=1` — lifts the opt-in `skipif` on the two smoke-e2e legs;
- `pytest -k real_catalog -v` — selects all three.

**Targeted over dropping `--fast`:** `--fast` also gates off the heavy `rig init --yes` apply / skill-install / tg-ctl / harness-symlink legs (already covered by `cleanroom-e2e`). Running the full smoke just to reach the pytest leg would add minutes of redundant, partly-flaky work.

### Vacuous-pass guards (so the gate can't pass while gating nothing)

The step fails loudly if:
- a real pytest failure occurred (checked **first**, so a mixed `1 failed, 1 skipped` reports FAILED — the true cause — not a mislabeled "skipped/theater");
- the selector collected **zero** tests (exit 5 / "no tests ran" — a rename broke `-k`);
- **any** test SKIPPED with the catalog present (env wiring broke — the gate is theater again);
- the **#72 require-ticket guard** didn't appear as PASSED by node-id (so a rename dropping it from the `-k` set can't be masked by the rest of the family staying green).

## Verification

Locally simulated every branch of the new step:
- happy path → all 3 RAN + PASSED, require-ticket pinned → step green;
- bad `-k` selector → "collected nothing" fires;
- missing `RIG_SMOKE_FAST_E2E` → a test skips → "SKIPPED/theater" fires;
- require-ticket test excluded (rename sim) → "require-ticket not in the run" fires.

Without the env, all 3 tests SKIP (the documented gap); with both env vars, all 3 RUN and pass. Full rig suite: `1330 passed, 16 skipped` (the skips are unrelated opt-in Docker/tmux e2e legs). The 33 ruff E702/F401 warnings are pre-existing on `origin/main` (ruff isn't in CI) and out of scope — filed as a follow-up note.

The merge CI will show the `real-catalog-smoke` job's new step running the three tests with a count > 0, none skipped.

title: feat(cli): uv-based install hints + condensed rig init/apply plan
body:
## What

Two `rig init` UX fixes from a CTO report. The machine: global Python is externally-managed (PEP-668, so a bare `pip install` errors) and `uv` is the toolchain.

### 1. Install hints prefer uv, never a bare `pip install`
- The **"textual not installed"** fallback prints a hint matched to **how rig itself is installed** (`uv-tool` / `pipx` / `source` / `unknown`) via `_rig_install_method` + `_tui_install_hint`. For a source checkout: `cd '<root>' && uv run --extra tui rig init` (or `uv tool install --from '<root>' 'rig-cli[tui]'`). Never `pip install 'rig-cli[tui]'`.
- **`rig doctor`** installs python deps via `uv pip install --python <interp>` when uv is present (falls back to `pip --user` only without uv).
- **install.sh** pyyaml bootstrap and the config-web `_INSTALL_HINT` / README are uv-ified.
- Comments are **honest**: uv does *not* bypass PEP-668 on a *system* interpreter — both uv and pip refuse a system-wide install there. It installs cleanly into a managed (uv/pipx) venv, which is the real fix; the source-install hint points at exactly that.

### 2. Condensed plan output
`_print_plan` collapses a large plan (a fresh init is ~124 actions) to a one-line **per-carrier summary**:

```
Plan: 124 action(s)  [on_conflict=backup]
  86 skills, 17 agent-hooks, 7 CI gates, 5 GitHub, 2 harness, 1 agents.md, 1 git-hooks, 1 gitignore, 1 models, 1 permissions, 1 ship gate, 1 tg-ctl
  (run with --plan to list all 124 actions)
```

`--plan` (on `init` / `apply` / `config set`) forces the full per-action list. A genuinely small plan still prints inline (`_PLAN_INLINE_MAX = 12`).

## Tests
- `rig doctor` prefers uv when present; falls back to `pip --user` without it.
- Every `_tui_install_hint` branch routes through uv/pipx, never bare `pip install 'rig-cli[tui]'`.
- Plan summarizes by default, lists fully under `--plan`, and stays inline for a small plan.

Full suite green (1337 passed, 16 skipped). Version `0.2.0` -> `0.2.1`.

Closes #79

title: feat(init): scaffold+preview by default, never presumptuously apply (#81)
body:
Closes #81.

## The complaint (CTO, verbatim)
> Много текста а что сделано не ясно. И не ясно что и почему не сделано и не понятно почему нельзя управлять процессом и зачем вообще что-то делать если от пользователя не получено никаких указаний.

`rig init` with no args, when the textual TUI wasn't installed, fell back to a "non-interactive default setup" that **silently wrote `rig.yaml` AND ran the full plan (mutating HOME)** — zero consent — and printed output that read as if it had *done* a bunch of things, when the plan is really a preview of what `rig apply` does.

## What changed (three principles)

1. **No presumptuous side-effects.** A bare `rig init` with no way to run the wizard — **no TTY** (piped / CI / agent) **or `textual` absent** — now writes NOTHING and applies NOTHING. It prints a non-destructive PREVIEW of what `rig apply` would do + exactly how to proceed. A new TTY gate (`is_interactive()`, both stdin+stdout) also fixes a latent hang where a no-TTY bare init tried to draw a fullscreen wizard into a pipe.
2. **Clarity (done vs preview vs skipped).** `rig init --yes` prints `wrote rig.yaml` + **"config only; NOTHING applied yet"** and labels the plan **"PREVIEW of \`rig apply\` (not applied)"**. An apply (`--apply`) shows the plan + per-action results, never a preview label. A no-write edge (`--config` already == the repo's `rig.yaml`) reports "Nothing written" instead of a phantom "scaffolded".
3. **Control.** The TUI wizard (Export-config-only vs Apply) stays the interactive surface; a new `--apply` flag is the explicit one-shot (scaffold + apply); `rig apply` is the separate apply step.

## ⚠️ DEFAULT-BEHAVIOR DECISION — please veto if wrong

**`rig init --yes` no longer applies.** It now SCAFFOLDS ONLY (writes `rig.yaml`, exit 0, nothing applied); the one-shot "configure + apply" is now **`rig init --yes --apply`**.

- Rationale: the CTO's complaint + the explicit "config only, nothing applied — the plan is a PREVIEW of `rig apply`" framing only hold if `init` doesn't apply. `init` = scaffold + preview; `rig apply` = apply. Clean two-verb model.
- This is a **breaking change** to a shipped command's contract. Anyone scripting `rig init --yes` expecting a full setup now gets a scaffold + exit 0 (no error). Mitigated: the output tells them to run `rig apply`, and `--apply` preserves the one-shot.
- **Back-compat audit:** the only *executable* callsites relying on apply-on-`--yes` were `tests/smoke.sh` and `tests/test_cleanroom_e2e.py` (both updated to `--apply`). No `scripts/`, git-hook, or CI workflow invokes `rig init --yes` for provisioning. The "one `rig init` = working setup" cleanroom narrative is preserved via `rig init --yes --apply`.
- Version bumped **0.2.1 → 0.3.0** (breaking default-behavior change → minor in 0.x). No CHANGELOG file exists, so this is the migration note.
- **Alternative if you veto:** keep `--yes` applying and move the "nothing applied" framing only onto the bare-init preview. Say the word and I'll flip it.

## Behavior matrix (new)
| Invocation | writes rig.yaml | applies | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rig init` (TTY + textual) | wizard decides | on Apply button | interactive wizard |
| `rig init` (no TTY / no textual) | no | no | PREVIEW + how-to-proceed |
| `rig init --yes` | yes | **no** | wrote + PREVIEW + "run \`rig apply\`" |
| `rig init --yes --apply` | yes | yes | wrote + Applying + results |
| `rig init --apply` | yes (default) | yes | one-shot from defaults |
| `rig init --dry-run` | no | no | preview ("(dry-run: nothing written)") |
| `rig init` on a repo that already has rig.yaml | refuses (`--yes`) / previews the existing config (bare/`--dry-run`) | no | "already exists → run \`rig apply\`" |

Kept #80's condensed plan + uv install hints intact.

## Tests
Full suite green (1352 passed). Added: bare-init writes-nothing preview (no-TTY + no-textual branches); `--yes` scaffold-only with the "nothing applied" framing + plan-labeled-preview; `--apply` / `--apply`-alone one-shots actually apply; `--dry-run` outranks `--apply`; clobber-guard fires before the catalog scan (precedence preserved on a broken source); external `--config` backup on both apply and non-apply paths; `--config == rig.yaml` no-phantom-write; existing-config preview reflects that config (not the default scaffold) on bare/`--dry-run`. smoke.sh + cleanroom e2e updated to `--apply`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Pre-existing `F401 time` unused import in `riglib/actions/runner.py` (origin/main, #67) — out of scope here.
- `_persist_rig_yaml` backup name has second granularity (`rig.yaml.rig-bak-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S`); two runs in the same second collide — pre-existing, low risk.
- `docs/config-schema.md` has descriptive "on `rig init` AND `rig apply`" phrasings now slightly imprecise (init scaffolds, apply applies); left untouched to keep this PR focused.

title: feat(init): auto-install the [tui] extra instead of printing a hint
body:
## Why

After #80 (uv-based install hints) and #82 (bare `rig init` previews, never presumptuously applies), an interactive `rig init` on a machine without the optional `[tui]` extra still just PRINTED a "go install textual yourself" hint and degraded to a preview.

CTO directive (Telegram): *"Да какая подсказка, все само должно устанавливаться!"* — when interactive setup is genuinely wanted, rig should self-bootstrap its own optional UI dependency and just launch the wizard.

Closes #83.

## What

- `_tui_install_command()` — the runnable twin of `_tui_install_hint`: an argv matched to how rig itself is installed (uv-tool → `uv tool install --reinstall 'rig-cli[tui]'`; pipx → `pipx inject`; source/unknown → `uv pip install --python <sys.executable>`, or plain pip into the venv / `pip --user` on a base interpreter). Returns `None` when no installer is on PATH.
- `_auto_install_tui()` — runs it with a bounded, env-overridable timeout (`RIG_TUI_INSTALL_TIMEOUT`, default 180s), re-checks importability, returns `True` only when textual+rich are importable in-process afterward. Every failure mode (no installer, offline, permission, timeout, non-zero exit, installed-but-unimportable) returns `False` — never raises, never hangs.

title: fix(init): failure-proof TUI install via rig-owned overlay dir
body:
Fixes `rig init` crashing or printing an un-actionable hint on PEP-668 externally-managed interpreters (Homebrew Python, Debian system Python) where neither `uv pip install --python <interp>` nor `pip install --user` can write into the interpreter's site-packages.

## Problem

When `rig` runs from a source-checkout symlink under a bare PEP-668-protected interpreter:
- `uv pip install --python <interp>` refuses ("create a virtual environment with uv venv")
- `pip install --user` is blocked by `externally-managed-environment`

Result: `rig init` auto-install silently fails and falls through to the "here's a manual command" hint — which is equally un-runnable.

## Solution

Install textual+rich into a rig-owned overlay directory (`~/.local/share/rig/tui-libs`, XDG-aware, overridable via `RIG_TUI_LIB_DIR`) using `pip/uv --target`. This dir is not a venv and not a managed environment — `--target` writes into it cleanly on any interpreter, PEP-668 or not. On the next call, `_inject_tui_lib_dir()` prepends it onto `sys.path` so the import resolves with zero subprocess.

## Changes

- `_tui_lib_dir()` — XDG-aware overlay path resolver
- `_inject_tui_lib_dir()` — idempotent `sys.path` injector; catches `OSError` + `RuntimeError` (the latter from `Path.home()` in Docker containers with no HOME/passwd entry — bug fixed in review)
- `_tui_install_command()` — source/unknown branch now uses `--target <overlay>` + `--ignore-installed` (pip) for full self-contained closure
- `_tui_install_hint()` — mirrors command exactly: `--python <sys.executable>` in uv branch, `sys.executable` instead of bare `python3` in pip branch (bug fixed in review)
- `cmd_setup()` / `cmd_init()` — inject overlay before importability check → zero-subprocess second run
- Test coverage: `_isolate_tui_lib_dir` autouse fixture, 7 new unit tests for resolution/injection/idempotency, updated assertions for `--python`/`sys.executable` correctness
- Version bump: 0.4.0 → 0.4.1

title: feat(permissions): rig-managed Claude Code deny/ask/allow — the outer belt (#100)
body:
Closes #100.

CTO decision (2026-07-01, verbatim): "Во, он тоже должен через rig приходить. Как и allow. Rig все все должен контролировать" — the Claude Code permissions layer (deny, ask, AND allow) must be provisioned/reconciled by `rig`, not hand-edited.

## What

Extends the existing GLOBAL `permissions` area (previously allow-only tool allowlist) so one `provision_permissions` action reconciles **every container** of the claude-code permissions layer in `~/.claude/settings.json`:

- **allow** — tool-derived entries (`Bash(<tool>:*)`, unchanged) **+ new raw `permissions.allow` config entries** (how a hand-grown allowlist gets adopted as declared config)
- **deny** — new baked conservative baseline (config `deny:` replaces it wholesale; `[]` disables)
- **ask** — new baked baseline (same semantics)

Permission rules are the OUTER belt: the harness evaluates deny → ask → allow **before** PreToolUse hooks, independently of the model, and a user-scope deny cannot be overridden by a project-level allow. The argv-parsing agent-hooks (`block-no-verify`, `block-raw-pr-merge`, …) stay the deep layer.

## Baked baseline (claude-code)

Matcher semantics verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (fetched 2026-07-01): `:*` = trailing word-boundary wildcard (equivalent to a trailing ` *`, matches end-of-string too); a mid-pattern `*` spans spaces; literal ` --flag ` boundaries exclude e.g. `--force-with-lease`; compound commands match per subcommand.

| List | Rule | Rationale (1 line) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deny | `Bash(gh pr merge:*)` | raw merges banned machine-wide; merges go through `gh ship` |
| deny | `Bash(git push --force:*)` | force push, flag-first |
| deny | `Bash(git push * --force *)` | force push, flag mid-position |
| deny | `Bash(git push * --force)` | force push, flag last (explicit end-anchor — no reliance on the trailing-`*`-matches-EOS reading) |
| deny | `Bash(git push -f:*)` / `Bash(git push * -f *)` / `Bash(git push * -f)` | same three positions for `-f`; word boundary excludes `--follow-tags` etc. |
| deny | `Bash(git commit --no-verify:*)` | hook-bypass commit, flag-first ONLY (see hook-only note) |
| deny | `Bash(sudo rm:*)` | no legitimate agent flow removes files as root |
| deny | `Bash(screencapture:*)` | screenshots go through Playwright/CDP (documented hard rule) |
| ask | `Bash(pkill:*)` / `Bash(killall:*)` | sometimes-legit (reaping own strays); broad pattern-kills have nuked other sessions before — prompt, do not block |
| ask | `Bash(git reset --hard:*)` / `Bash(git reset * --hard *)` / `Bash(git reset * --hard)` | destroyed uncommitted work before; three positions |

`--force-with-lease` (the safe force) is deliberately NOT matched. No baked rule is a bare tool name (`Bash`/`Bash(*)` as deny would remove the tool from the model's context) — unit-tested.

## Deliberately hook-only (and why)

- **`git commit --no-verify` with the flag in a later position** (`git commit -m "…" --no-verify`, the common shape): the only pattern that could catch it (`Bash(git commit *--no-verify*)`) also matches a commit MESSAGE that merely mentions the flag — this ecosystem writes such messages (a hook of exactly this false-positive class fired on this task's own ticket text). A deny that false-positives teaches routing around the belt. The flag-first prefix rule is the safe subset; `block-no-verify` (argv-level) remains authoritative.
- **Wrapper bypasses in general** (`sh -c`, `rtk git …`, env-runners): prefix rules anchor at the command start; only `timeout`/`time`/`nice`/`nohup`/`stdbuf`/bare `xargs` are stripped by the matcher. Hooks parse argv and stay the deep layer — the two are complementary, not redundant.
- **opencode deny/ask/raw-allow**: its `permission.bash` glob-key dialect is a different, unverified syntax — a deny you believe in but that never matches is worse than a reported gap. Dropped with a visible plan note; the tool-derived allowlist still works for opencode.

## Merge / drift semantics (test evidence in `tests/test_permissions.py`)

- **Union-assert, never delete**: every rig-managed entry is asserted present per container; user entries are preserved in place, dedup on overlap, re-apply is a byte-stable no-op (`test_apply_writes_deny_and_ask_containers_idempotently`, `test_apply_preserves_user_deny_and_ask_entries`, `test_apply_merges_raw_allow_rules`).
- **`rig status`** reports each missing rig-managed entry per container and reports user extras as `extra` drift **without ever deleting them**: allow extras are summarized into ONE counted item (the live list has ~170 entries; a per-entry dump would drown status), deny/ask extras are per-entry (small + loud) (`test_drift_missing_deny_ask_entries_then_converged`, `test_drift_reports_user_extras_and_apply_never_deletes`).
- **`deny: []`** disables the baseline but the container stays managed: an orphaned previously-applied baseline shows as per-entry extras instead of vanishing (`test_explicit_empty_deny_keeps_container_managed`).
- **Shape problems** (scalar `permissions`, non-array container) report as ONE `modified` matching the ONE error apply raises; non-string junk in a hand-mangled list no longer crashes apply (string-only membership) and is flagged `modified` by status (`test_apply_tolerates_and_drift_flags_nonstring_array_entries`).

## Dry-run (isolated HOME — the live machine was NOT touched)

Before: `harness permissions (allow / deny / ask): drift (25 declared-but-missing/modified, 1 on-disk-not-declared)` — 13 allow tools + 8 deny + 4 ask missing; 1 summarized extras item for the 2 pre-seeded user entries.
Apply: `added 13 to permissions.allow, 8 to permissions.deny, 4 to permissions.ask` (prior file backed up); user entries (`WebFetch`, `Bash(kubectl:*)`) and `defaultMode: auto` preserved.
Re-apply: `all 25 entries already in … Summary: skipped=1`.
After: `drift (1 on-disk-not-declared)` — only the user-extras item remains, naming the remedy ("adopt via permissions.allow or prune by hand").

## Suite

`pytest`: **1517 passed, 16 skipped** (baseline before this branch: 1505/16; +12 net new tests). Full `tests/smoke.sh`: OK, including the extended permissions leg (deny/ask baselines asserted in the isolated-HOME init). `rig schema --write` regenerated `schema/rig.schema.json`.

## Live-machine adoption (for the CTO/orchestrator to apply AFTER review — NOT done here)

The hand-grown `~/.claude/settings.json` allowlist audit: **158 entries to adopt** into `permissions.allow` of `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` (13 are already covered by the tool-derived defaults; **19 malformed `mcp__playwright_*` single-underscore entries** — wrong server-name form, they match nothing — are left OUT of the baseline so they surface as extras to prune). Dangerously broad entries **kept** (relied upon), flagged for awareness: `Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(ssh:*)`, `Bash(scp:*)`, `Bash(chmod:*)`, `Bash(perl:*)`, `Bash(python3:*)`, `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(docker run:*)`, `Bash(docker exec:*)`, `Bash(kubectl:*)`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch` — each is an arbitrary-code/exfiltration primitive that neutralizes the deny belt for a determined injection; tightening them is a separate decision.

The ready-to-paste config block is delivered with the handoff (proposed-permissions-config.yaml, 158 entries). Until it is adopted, `rig status` on this machine will show ONE summarized allow-extras item (~150 entries) — intended visibility, not a bug.

Review: `review diff --pool 1` × 3 rounds — R1 (Opus): end-anchored force-push forms added, drift shape-error dedup, defensive copy; R2 (codex): `deny: []` orphan visibility, opencode raw-allow leak, non-string junk apply/status parity — all fixed with tests; R3: clean ("No further action needed", "Missing Tests: None Found").

title: feat(config): worktree_only / orchestrator_only per-repo agent_hooks knobs
body:
## What this adds

Two per-repo **runtime** knobs in the `agent_hooks` block of a repo's committed `rig.yaml`:

- **`agent_hooks.worktree_only`** — enforces **worktree-only writes**. When on, the
  `worktree-only-writes` pre-write hook denies an Edit/Write while the checkout sits on the
  repo's default branch (main/master, detected via `origin/HEAD` / `init.defaultBranch`, never
  hardcoded). All authoring happens in a worktree on a feature branch; the default branch is for
  merge/pull/read-only. Deliberate one-off escape hatch: `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1`.
- **`agent_hooks.orchestrator_only`** — keeps the **orchestrator thin**. When on, the
  `orchestrator-stays-thin` hook blocks inline implementation (Bash / code Edits) by the main
  thread while still allowing read-only inspection and orchestration
  (`gh pr list/view/checks`, `gh ship`, `tg`, `review`, `git worktree list`). Escape hatch:
  `ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK=1` + reason.

These are **runtime** signals read by the agent-tools hook scripts directly from the committed
`rig.yaml` at fire time. **`rig apply` does not consume them** — there is nothing to install for
the value itself, so changing enforcement in a repo needs no re-apply (a fresh clone reads the
committed value directly). rig-cli's job here is only to (1) let the strict validator + published
`schema/rig.schema.json` **accept** the keys per-repo, and (2) carry the two hooks via the
already-registered PreToolUse matchers (`Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` and `Bash`), so no
new matcher is introduced and the change merges cleanly alongside the open lint-on-write bridge PRs.

## Defaults + semantics

| Key | Default | Polarity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `worktree_only` | `false` | **opt-IN** — a repo is never blocked unless it sets `true`. |
| `orchestrator_only` | `true` | **opt-OUT** — on by default; set `false` to exempt a repo. |

Both defaults are declared identically in `riglib/config_schema.py` (the authoritative Block/Leaf
registry) and the generated `schema/rig.schema.json`; a self-test asserts the committed schema
equals the in-code registry, so the two sources cannot drift.

## Why

Delivers Alex's tg#5742 (worktree-only workflow) and tg#5743 (orchestrator-only).

## The 3d-cli exemption

`3d-cli` legitimately works directly on `main`, so it is the canonical exemption example: it
leaves `worktree_only` **off** (default) and commits `orchestrator_only: false`.

## Provisioning — how a repo enrols

Set the booleans in the repo's committed `rig.yaml` under `agent_hooks`, e.g.:

```yaml
agent_hooks:
  all: true
  worktree_only: true       # opt IN to worktree-only writes
  orchestrator_only: true   # (default) keep the orchestrator thin
```

Because the hooks self-read the value at fire time, committing the change is the whole
enrolment — no per-repo `rig apply` is needed to flip enforcement.

## Activation

These knobs are **inert** until the corresponding agent-tools hooks (`worktree-only-writes`,
`orchestrator-stays-thin`) are installed. Final activation across repos is a single `rig apply`
**after** the agent-tools PRs merge — and it must be **serialized** with the open lint-on-write
work (rig-cli **#103**, agent-tools **#161**): run **ONE** `rig apply` after all of them land,
not several.

Note on rollout: because `orchestrator_only` defaults **on**, any repo that pulls in the
`orchestrator-stays-thin` hook via `all: true` and has NOT committed `orchestrator_only: false`
will start blocking inline work at activation. Repos that legitimately work inline (e.g. `3d-cli`)
must commit `orchestrator_only: false` **before** that `rig apply`. The escape-hatch env-var
names (`RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT`, `ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK`) must match the agent-tools hook impl
char-for-char — verify against the hook scripts in the agent-tools PRs.

## Review provenance

The base commit (`351eeff`) was originally committed via a `[skip-review]` emergency recovery
(dead-agent WIP preservation — unreviewed, not test-verified in that pass). This PR adds a
**proper review pass**: a multi-model `review diff` over the whole change, a fix for the one
actionable in-repo finding (the strict validator did not type-check the two new boolean knobs, so
it would have accepted `worktree_only: "no"` / `orchestrator_only: 1` while the schema types them
as `boolean` — now guarded with `_check_bool` + a parametrized regression test in `382c411`), and
the full suite green (**1532 passed / 16 skipped**).

title: feat(tools): keep provisioned tools fresh via scripts/deploy.sh on rig apply
body:
## What

`rig apply` provisioned each tool once (ran its `install.sh`, symlinked the bin, ran `install-skill`) and then short-circuited with **skipped** forever — it never pulled, so a provisioned checkout silently drifted behind `origin/main`. Concretely: the CTO's `tg` checkout was behind origin and missing new flags because `rig apply` never refreshes an already-installed tool.

This adds **apply-time freshness**: if a tool's repo ships a `scripts/deploy.sh`, `rig apply` runs it **before** the already-installed short-circuit, so an installed tool is kept current on every apply. `deploy.sh` owns all its own safety (refuses dirty/detached/diverged trees, ff-only `git pull`); rig just invokes it.

## Design

- **Opt-in per tool via `scripts/deploy.sh` only.** No generic/raw `git pull` fallback — a tool with no `deploy.sh` skips freshness (other tools opt in by adding one).
- **Non-fatal.** A non-zero exit (offline/dirty/diverged) is downgraded to a warning folded into the reported message — never an apply abort, mirroring the offline-safe `_git_clone` discipline.
- **Runs even when already installed** — that short-circuit is exactly what hid a stale checkout, so deploy runs before it (but after the missing-`install.sh` guard, so no script executes against a repo that isn't a rig tool — addresses a review P1).
- **Timeout-wrapped** with the existing `RIG_TOOL_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_S` (default 300s).

## Changes

- `riglib/tools.py` — `DEPLOY_SCRIPT = "scripts/deploy.sh"` constant + `ToolSpec.deploy_script` property (stdlib-only, effect-free).
- `riglib/actions/runner.py` — `_run_tool_deploy` + a shared `_run_tool_bash_script` core (extracted from `_run_tool_install`, behavior-preserving); `_maybe_deploy_tool` (non-fatal note) + `_with_note`; `_provision_one_tool` runs deploy after the repo guard, before the installed short-circuit, folding the deploy result into the message.
- `riglib/config_schema.py` + regenerated `schema/rig.schema.json` — `tools:` block doc note.
- `README.md` — freshness note + `RIG_TOOL_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_S` mention.
- `pyproject.toml` — version 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 (`--version` already resolves dynamically from pyproject).
- `tests/test_tools.py` — 4 new tests: deploy runs when present (even when installed), skipped when no deploy.sh, deploy failure non-fatal, and deploy NOT run when `install.sh` is absent (the P1 regression test).

## Tests

`python -m pytest -q` -> **1523 passed, 16 skipped** (skips are opt-in docker/tmux e2e + jsonschema-not-installed, same as CI).

## Review

Multi-model review (pool of 3: Opus / Codex / Gemini) — all `[ok]`. Codex's P1 (deploy ran before the `repo_present` guard) was fixed + covered by a regression test; Gemini's doc note (`RIG_TOOL_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_S`) added to the README. The paid reserve seats (Kimi/DeepSeek/Qwen/GLM-cc) were out of credits and excluded via `--pool 3`.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

`drift.py` `_check_tools` could gain an "upstream-behind" signal so `rig status` flags a stale-but-installed tool. This PR is apply-time freshness only.

title: fix(ship): never pin the machine agent-tools pointer at a transient temp checkout
body:
## Problem

`rig apply` writes the machine-level `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agent-tools/env` (`AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT`) that every repo's `gh ship` delegator sources when the env var is unset. The root was derived from `agent_tools_source`/`catalog.source` with no guard, so a one-off apply whose source resolved under a temp dir (a `mkdtemp` clone / `$TMPDIR` / `/tmp` — e.g. an agent testing agent-tools from a throwaway worktree) clobbered the durable pointer with a path that vanishes on cleanup.

Observed 2026-07-09 on the CTO's machine:
```
AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT=/private/var/folders/1c/.../T/tmpdhx8hi2a/agent-tools
```
Once that tempdir is gone, `gh ship` exits 127 for **every** repo on the machine (the delegator sources a dead path) until someone manually re-points it. Every merger agent had to override `AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT=/Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools` to land a merge.

## Fix

- **`transient_ship_root_skip_reason()`** — a shared predicate (mirrors `repo_self_hosts_ship`) used by BOTH apply (skip the write, keep any existing pointer) and drift (skip the check) so status/apply stay in lockstep. It fires only when the resolved root is under a temp dir AND the pointer file itself is persistent — the exact doomed-pointer case. pytest and a cleanroom isolated under `$TMPDIR` (both transient) proceed normally.
- Ordered AFTER the structural non-file/unreadable checks, so a genuinely broken machine env file still surfaces even under a transient source (parity both ways).
- **`env_file_pins_transient_root()`** — an already-poisoned pointer (its own `AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT` under a temp dir — the vanished-tmp bug state) keeps surfacing as `ship_env` drift regardless of whether it equals the current transient desired content. Apply can't repair it from a throwaway source, so it reports `skipped_transient` (a surfaced status, like `skipped_user`) until a durable apply runs.
- **`_system_temp_roots()`** probes `tempfile.gettempdir()` defensively (it can raise in a locked-down env) and falls back to hard-coded `/tmp` + `/var/folders` roots.

## Testing

- `tests/test_ship_delegator.py`: +9 tests (transient skip predicate, both-transient writes normally, existing-good-pointer intact, no doomed-pointer created, broken env file still surfaces under transient, already-poisoned pointer flagged even when it equals the source, delegator-written-but-skipped status, `gettempdir` raising).
- Full suite green: **1644 passed, 16 skipped**.

## Review

Iterated across four `review-cli` (codex) rounds. All concrete correctness findings addressed (drift/apply structural-check ordering, `skipped_transient` surfacing in both delegator branches, `gettempdir()` hardening, poisoned-pointer-equals-source edge).

One residual design ask was **declined**: emit permanent status drift for "transient source + absent/durable-broken pointer". Apply provably cannot repair that (no durable checkout to write), so flagging it would break the status↔apply parity invariant the codebase enforces, and `DriftItem` has no non-repairable "warning" tier. Apply already surfaces the condition at apply time via the `skipped_transient` note, and the common (durable-source) path self-heals a stale pointer on the next apply.

Closes #128

title: fix(tmux): boot agent injects Homebrew PATH + logging so continuum-restore fires on reboot
body:
Fixes #136

## Root cause (proven)
The launchd boot agent (`ai.hyperide.tmux-boot`) runs with launchd's minimal `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` — no `/opt/homebrew/bin`. The boot script survives (absolute tmux path), but the tmux **server** it spawns inherits that PATH, and tmux's continuum/resurrect `run-shell` hooks call **bare** `tmux` → not found → `get_tmux_option @continuum-restore` fails → defaults `off` → restore (and autosave) silently skipped. Empirically: under the minimal PATH a `run-shell` reads `@continuum-restore` as empty; under a Homebrew-inclusive PATH it reads `on`.

This same PATH bug was invisible to prior fixes because `test_tmux_e2e.py` runs the boot script under the harness's **full** PATH, and the plist had no logging.

## Change
- `render_boot_plist` now emits `EnvironmentVariables.PATH` (Homebrew-inclusive, keyed off the resolved tmux binary's own dir → correct on Apple-silicon and Intel) + `HOME`, and `StandardOutPath`/`StandardErrorPath` so the boot is no longer a black box. Mirrors the `tg_ctl` LaunchAgent pattern.
- `_resolve_tmux_bin` resolves from a stable source (first existing fixed install path, then `shutil.which`) and `tmux_bin` is baked once into `TmuxPlan`, so `rig apply`/`rig status` render byte-identical artifacts under any ambient PATH — no drift flap.

## Tests / gate
- `python -m pytest -q` → 1812 passed, 16 skipped.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → OK.
- Added PATH-injection, logging, determinism (cross-plan) and key-order unit tests.
- Verified live: installed plist + `launchctl bootstrap`; a `run-shell` on a server started under the fixed PATH resolves `tmux` and reads `@continuum-restore on`.

Follow-up: #138 (independent launchd autosave agent — the robust upgrade from the brainstorm).

title: feat(spotlight): universal Spotlight-exclude provisioning + post-apply verify framework
body:
Closes #137.

## What & why
Alex's Mac gets hammered after every reboot by Spotlight (`mds_stores`) reindexing gigabytes of dependency/build dirs (`node_modules`, `dist`, `target`, `.venv`, …). Two coupled features:

### Feature 1 — universal Spotlight-exclude provisioning
- New **opt-in, GLOBAL-only** `spotlight:` block. Drops the macOS sentinel **`.metadata_never_index`** into every dependency/build dir (frontend AND backend; config-driven `deny`/`extra`) under configurable dev roots (`~/work`, `~/xp`).
- Installs a **launchd re-sweep LaunchAgent** (RunAtLoad + daily, **with StandardOut/ErrorPath logging from the start**) so NEW projects get covered automatically.
- New `rig spotlight-sweep` subcommand (the agent's command; also a manual re-sweep).
- Never disables Spotlight, never forces a full-volume reindex. Default OFF — requires explicit `enabled: true` (an empty `spotlight: {}` provisions nothing). Gated by `RIG_SPOTLIGHT_DRY_RUN`.

### Feature 2 — post-apply verify framework (`riglib/verify.py`)
- Each provisioner declares one verifier keyed by action kind; `rig apply`/`rig init` run all checks at the end, report pass/fail/skip per provisioner, and exit non-zero on failure.
- Coupled to apply results (a stubbed/no-op action is not asserted). launchd checks are N/A-skipped on non-macOS and skipped under the per-provisioner dry-run flag.
- Dogfooded for spotlight; retrofitted for tmux + tg_ctl. Adding a check to a new provisioner is one `@register_verifier(kind)` function.

> Coordinates with #138 / `fix/tmux-boot-logging-restore` (independent tmux saver) which also wants a per-provisioner verify() hook — the registry here is the coherent shared seam.

## Live apply evidence (`rig apply --only spotlight`)
- Sweep: **1358** new `.metadata_never_index` sentinels across `~/work` + `~/xp` (verified: real `node_modules`/`dist`/`target`/`.venv` dirs carry the sentinel).
- launchd agent `ai.hyperide.spotlight-exclude` **loaded** (`launchctl list` rc 0, daily 04:30).
- Post-apply **verify: 3/3 PASS** (sampled sentinels present + plist present + agent loaded).
- `rig spotlight-sweep` idempotent: `0 new, 1363 already covered`, exit 0.

## Gate
- `pytest` — 1837 passed, 16 skipped.

title: feat(tmux): independent launchd autosave agent, decoupled from continuum status-right
body:
Fixes #138 — stacked on #139 (base = `fix/tmux-boot-logging-restore`; retarget to `main` after #139 merges).

## Why
tmux-continuum autosave rode on a 6-link fragile chain (status on, interval, PATH, status-right not wiped, tpm not re-init, the `#(continuum_save.sh)` interpolation alive) with zero observability. The launchd-minimal-PATH bug (#136) broke that chain and autosave died silently for a month. A multi-model brainstorm (Fable `claude-fable-5` + Sol `codex:gpt-5.6-sol`) converged: a data-protection mechanism must not depend on status-line rendering — provision an **independent** saver.

## What
- **`ai.hyperide.tmux-autosave` LaunchAgent** — `StartInterval` = `save_interval` min, Homebrew-inclusive PATH (no user-writable dir — Sol hardening), `HOME`, `StandardOut/ErrPath`.
- **`tmux-autosave.sh` wrapper** — absolute tmux path, own `mkdir` lock, resolves the resurrect dir **exactly as resurrect does** (honors `@resurrect-dir`, the `~/.tmux/resurrect`-if-exists quirk, else XDG), a **degenerate-save guard** (a bare boot-time `main` never clobbers a richer prior snapshot), calls resurrect `save.sh` directly, writes a health-state file + one log line.
- **`@continuum-save-interval '0'`** when the independent saver is on → one authoritative saver, no racing writers over `last`.
- **runner**: provision + gui-domain `bootstrap` on apply (stateless daemon → starts saving the current server with no reboot), suppressed on a conflict-skipped plist/script.
- **drift**: content-check the autosave plist; surface a leftover when disabled.
- **config**: `tmux.autosave {enabled,label,stale_after}` in schema + validator + docs + regenerated JSON schema.

## Verification (adversarial)
- Unit suite **1833 passed** / smoke `--fast` OK.
- Wrapper is `shellcheck`-clean; on isolated `TMUX_TMPDIR` sockets: real content → **saved a fresh `tmux_resurrect_*.txt`** (health `ok`); a bare `main` vs a 5-pane prior → **degenerate guard skipped** (health `skip`); the real resurrect dir stayed untouched.
- Review (`review diff`, glm pool) ran 3 rounds; the round-1 HIGH (`count_panes` double-print on 0) and the test-matrix gaps were fixed; only cosmetic Lows (noted "consistent with the boot pattern") remain.

Completes the durable tmux-continuum autosave fix (follows #139 PATH fix + #141 independent saver). The brainstorm-converged design (`review brainstorm`, 2026-07-13, Fable + Sol, unanimous) had two pieces still missing after #141:

1. **The launchd-minimal-PATH regression guard** — the exact test that reproduces the root cause every prior fix hid from itself.

This PR adds `_check_spotlight` to the drift dispatcher (`riglib/drift.py`).

Foundation + spec for the stack-preset system (Alex tg#8708). A repo declares a stack `l1/lang[/framework]`; rig provisions the matching **by-stack** skills on top of the universal set — the curation axis so a mobile repo doesn't get react skills and vice versa.

## What's here (foundation)
- **Spec**: `docs/specs/2026-07-15-stack-presets.md` (taxonomy, catalog layout, schema, detection, UX, migration, open questions).
- **Taxonomy + matching**: `riglib/stack.py` — l1 is a CLOSED six-enum (`mobile|frontend|backend|desktop|embedded|system`), lang required, framework optional; lang/framework OPEN vocabulary; hierarchical **prefix** inheritance (`mobile/swift/swiftui` pulls `mobile/swift` + `mobile/swift/swiftui` skills).
- **Schema**: top-level `stack` key + `skills.by_stack` block (`config_schema.py`, wizard Area in `schema.py`), fail-closed shape/enum validation + per-item `by_stack.items` validation (`config.py`). Regenerated `schema/rig.schema.json`.

title: feat(harness): provision auto-mode self-merge classifier carve-out (#142)
body:
Adds `harness.self_merge` (default ON, auto-mode only): `rig apply` appends a `\$defaults`-preserving carve-out to `autoMode.allow` in the user-scope Claude settings so an agent can self-merge a PR **it authored** via `gh ship` — clearing the Merge-Without-Review + Self-Approval soft blocks for its OWN PRs **without disabling the classifier**. Every other rule (notably the anti-exfil `hard_deny`) stays intact.

## One engine
schema (`schema.py` + `config_schema.py` + `rig.schema.json`) → `plan.build` (`_build_harness`, effective only when the mode resolves to `auto`) → `actions/runner.py::_do_apply_harness`, which now reconciles two managed things in the one settings file. The carve-out merge is additive (never clobbers the user's entries or the sibling `soft_deny`/`hard_deny` sections), idempotent, backup-safe. Drift surfaced by `rig status`.

## Activation
An agent writing this to its own live settings trips the **Self-Modification** soft block — so **you merge this PR, then run `rig apply`** to activate it. After that, agents can `gh ship` their own PRs and the whole merge backlog stops needing your hand.
