title: feat(ship): provision the machine-global gh ship alias durably
body:
## What

`gh ship` worked only because a smart-dispatcher `gh` alias was **hand-set** in `~/.config/gh/config.yml`. rig provisioned the per-repo delegator (`.claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh` — the alias's *target*) and a `~/bin/ship` copy, but **never the alias itself**. So on a clean machine / after a gh-config reset, `gh ship` silently became "unknown command", and an older ci-`ship` `gh_alias` path wrote an inferior `!~/bin/ship` copy-alias that could clobber the good hand-set one.

This provisions the **alias itself**, durably and idempotently, as a portable-constant dispatcher (repo delegator → canonical `ci/ship/ship.sh` via the machine env file). New GLOBAL `gh_ship_alias` area/category.

## Root cause (investigated, not assumed)
- `gh ship` today = a **global `gh` alias** (`aliases.ship`), hand-set to a smart dispatcher. It works, but is not rig-owned → can silently vanish.
- rig owned the delegator + env file + a `~/bin/ship` copy, plus an older ci-`ship` `gh_alias` writer that set `!~/bin/ship` (repo-blind, staleness-prone) — the competing/clobbering path.

## Key pieces
- `riglib/gh_ship_alias.py`: constant expansion (mirrors the delegator's **safe env contract** — explicit `AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT` wins, symlinked env refused); shared `resolve` (apply+drift) reading gh's config **YAML byte-exactly** (parsing `gh alias list`'s display format looped `update` forever); `unknown` state for an unreadable/malformed gh config (never clobbered, no traceback); `gh alias set --clobber` writer.
- Plan emits **one** alias action gated by `(ship_delegator on) OR (ci-ship gh_alias:true)`; target = gh's config path.
- Runner handler honors `on_conflict` + a `RIG_GH_ALIAS_DRY_RUN` guard; gh-missing self-skips (status/apply parity).
- ci-`ship` `gh_alias` no longer writes the alias itself (removed the second, unconditional writer racing the reconciler); orphaned `_gh_alias_set` deleted.
- drift / areas / layers / cli provenance wired.

## Proof
- `gh ship 999999` reaches `ship.sh` (GraphQL PR-resolution error, **not** "unknown command").
- Live-verified idempotent: `resolve` → `ok` after set, re-set stays `ok`.
- Behavioral `sh -c` tests prove the expansion reaches the delegator + canonical fallback + exits 127 when unresolvable + the safe env contract.

## Review
Codex seat's full review addressed (P1 double-writer, P1 unsafe env sourcing, P2 read-failure/target/provenance/smoke-isolation all fixed). Exec-bit drift on the shared delegator resolver deferred → #150. The review pool re-wedged on an orphaned glm-5.2 reviewer (network hang, killed); committed with sanctioned `REVIEW_SKIP`.

## Tests
Full `pytest` green (only the pre-existing `test_tmux_e2e_gating` import flake); `smoke.sh --fast` green.

title: fix(actions): guard link actions against source==target self-symlink
body:
## Problem

rig's opencode hook-bridge link action (and the skill-harness link action) resolved the link **SOURCE** onto its own **TARGET**, then backed up the real git-tracked file and replaced it with a **self-referential symlink** — corrupting the source module (`stat -L` → "Too many levels of symbolic links").

On 2026-07-15 this clobbered agent-tools' `lib/opencode_hook_bridge/plugin.js` (a tracked 104-line ES module → a symlink pointing at itself). opencode's hook bridge then silently stopped loading, and rig's catalog self-skipped it on every apply ("incomplete — missing plugin.js"). The tracked file has been restored separately.

Fixes #154

## Fix

New `_link_targets_itself(link_path, dest)`: normalizes both to an absolute path with the **parent resolved** but the **leaf kept verbatim** — deliberately *not* `resolve()`-ing `link_path` itself (it may already be the self-symlink whose `resolve()` raises `OSError: Too many levels of symbolic links`, and keeping the leaf verbatim means a legitimate symlink-at-`link_path` is not confused with its own target, so idempotent re-runs still work). When both normalize to the same path, the caller **skips** with a plan note instead of clobbering.

Applied early in both `_do_link_skill_harness` and `_do_register_opencode_hook_bridge`. The `OSError` branch fails **safe** (skip, never clobber). `install.py` already had an equivalent guard; `agents_md` (CLAUDE.md→AGENTS.md) and `codex_update` are safe by construction (distinct paths).

## Vulnerability sweep

All symlink-creating sites audited:
- `_do_link_skill_harness`, `_do_register_opencode_hook_bridge` — were vulnerable, now guarded.
- `riglib/install.py` — already guarded (early-return when harness dir == agents skill dir).
- `_do_provision_agents_symlink` (CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md) — safe by construction (distinct filenames).
- `riglib/codex_update.py` — temp-then-rename, distinct paths.

## Tests (TDD red-first)

- `source == target` is a no-op skip (never backs up + self-links) — both actions.
- positive: a legitimate distinct link still proceeds — both actions.
- positive: an idempotent symlink re-run is recognized as "already linked", not mis-flagged.

`python -m pytest -q tests/test_link_self_symlink.py` → 5 passed. Full suite green (pre-existing tmux-e2e-gating flake aside); `smoke.sh --fast` green.

## Review

Reviewed with `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8` — the shared opencode/glm reviewer was wedged session-wide, so it was excluded. Verdict `[ok]`, no blockers; the fail-open→fail-safe feedback was applied.

title: fix(catalog): install every *.json descriptor per agent-hook dir
body:
## Problem

`riglib/catalog.py` scanned each agent-hook dir with
`next(iter(sorted(d.glob("*.json"))), None)` — it took only the **first** sorted
`*.json` and discarded the rest. A hook dir shipping more than one descriptor
therefore installed only one of them.

The real casualty is `orchestrator-stays-thin/`, which ships **two** guards:
`orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-bash.json` and `orchestrator-stays-thin.pre-write.json`.
`.pre-bash` sorts first, so `.pre-write` — the guard that blocks inline
implementation by the main thread — **never installed**. Enforcement was silently
dropped: on machines that ran `rig apply`, the orchestrator pre-write guardrail
was not in place despite being enabled. (`worktree-only-writes` ships a single
pre-write JSON, so it was unaffected.)

## Fix

- `catalog.py`: discover **every** `*.json` in a hook dir into a new
  `Item.descriptors` tuple (keeps `meta["descriptor"]` = first for back-compat).
- `plan.py`: emit one `install_agent_hook` action **per descriptor** so all of
  them land — idempotent, backup-noted, drift-clean like the rest. Extracted the
  agent-hooks emission into `_plan_agent_hooks`.
- **Fail-closed** on a descriptor basename collision: two hooks writing the same
  basename into one target dir would clobber each other (a lost guard, drift never
  clean), so `plan.build` raises `PlanError` instead.
- `Action.describe()` now appends the descriptor so multi-descriptor plan/dry-run
  lines stay distinguishable.

## Tests (TDD, red-first)

- Fake catalog fixture gains a two-descriptor `dual-guard` hook.
- Catalog discovers both descriptors; plan emits an action for each.
- Multi-descriptor x multi-target fan-out yields N*M actions with no false
  collision (same basename in different target dirs is allowed).
- The collision `PlanError` path.
- End-to-end `run_plan`: both descriptors install -> re-apply skips both -> drift
  clean.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest -q` — 1917 passed (2 new), 18 skipped. The lone
  `test_tmux_e2e_gating` failure is the pre-existing, unrelated tmux-e2e-gating
  flake (`ModuleNotFoundError: tests.test_tmux_e2e`).
- `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE=... bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — green; full-catalog

- `review diff --staged` — verdict [ok], no blocking correctness bugs.

## Note

Because the pre-write guard never installed before this fix, machines that
already ran `rig apply` are missing it on disk. **A re-apply after this lands is
needed** to put the orchestrator pre-write guard in place.

Closes #156

title: fix(harness): self-merge writes ship rules to permissions.allow (the real Bash-gate unblock)
body:
## What #149 actually did, and why it was inert

#149 (`harness.self_merge`, merged to main) provisioned the self-merge carve-out into **`autoMode.allow`** only — a natural-language directive that clears the classifier's *semantic* soft blocks (Merge-Without-Review / Self-Approval).

But an empirical live test showed `gh ship` is blocked by the **auto-mode classifier's top-level Bash permission gate**, which vetoes `gh ship` *before* the classifier ever judges the merge. That gate is bypassed **only** by an explicit **`permissions.allow`** entry. So #149 targeted the wrong layer: the `autoMode.allow` string was never reached — `gh ship` never ran.

(It is NOT blocked by the `block-raw-pr-merge` agent-hook, which already whitelists `gh ship`/`pr-ship.sh`, nor by the settings merge deny — moot, since `ship.sh` calls the raw merge as a child process, not a gated tool call.)

## The fix

When `harness.self_merge` is true (auto-mode, claude-code), `apply_harness` now **also** appends to the user-scope `~/.claude/settings.json` **`permissions.allow`**:
- `Bash(gh ship:*)`
- `Bash(*/pr-ship.sh:*)`
- `Bash(*/ship.sh:*)`

This is the **HARD unblock** that clears the Bash gate. The existing `autoMode.allow` carve-out stays as the **SOFT-block clearance** — both layers are needed (Bash gate first, then the semantic soft-blocks). The raw-merge **deny is untouched**: `gh ship` remains the only merge path; we whitelist the ship *gate*, not a raw merge.

Code path: `schema` (`schema.py`/`config_schema.py`/`rig.schema.json`) → `plan._build_harness` (self_merge already resolves true under `auto`) → `actions/runner.py::_do_apply_harness` → new `_ensure_self_merge_permissions(data)` (self-targets `data["permissions"]`). Additive, idempotent, backup-on-conflict — same discipline as the rest of `apply_harness`. A **malformed** `permissions.allow` is left untouched (never clobbered; `provision_permissions` fail-closes on the shape). Drift (`rig status`) reports the ship rules missing under `self_merge`, and suppresses the rig-owned rules from permissions allow-extras **only** when an active self-merge action owns that same file (stray rules under `self_merge:false` still report).

## Test evidence
- Red-first for every behavioral change; each fix confirmed to fail without its code, then pass.
- New tests: ship rules land in `permissions.allow`; deny preserved; existing allow entries preserved; `self_merge:false` writes none; drift missing→synced; malformed allow left untouched; no-op detail doesn't falsely claim ship rules; malformed allow yields no false "absent" drift row; settings-file helpers normalize identically.
- `python -m pytest -q` → **1922 passed**, 18 skipped, 1 failure = the pre-existing tmux-e2e-gating flake (`ModuleNotFoundError: tests.test_tmux_e2e`), unrelated and present on clean `origin/main`.
- `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE=$HOME/xp/agent-tools bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → **smoke OK**.
- `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8` → verdict `[ok]`; four rounds of findings (codex + opus) addressed inline: malformed-allow non-clobber, conditional drift-extras suppression, self-targeting the permissions section, accurate no-op detail, and no false "absent" drift row.

## Activation (Alex's step — NOT done here)
`harness.self_merge` defaults **true**, so the machine-wide global config (`~/.config/rig/config.yaml`, `harness.mode: auto`) already enables it once this code lands. To make it explicit and then apply:

```
rig config set harness.self_merge true --global    # optional; default is already true
rig apply                                           # writes the ship rules to ~/.claude/settings.json
```

After `rig apply`, agent `gh ship` passes the Bash classifier deterministically. (I did NOT touch Alex's live `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` — self-modification wall.)

## Follow-up
#158 tracks the two codex P1 hardening items that push against this PR's deliberate design (apply_harness owns the allow): tightening the `*/ship.sh` globs, and guaranteeing the raw-merge deny co-provisions in non-default permissions layouts (permissions disabled / different kind / split settings_path). Safe in Alex's default single-file config where allow+deny land together.

title: feat(apply): preview-by-default with explicit commit step
body:
## What & why

Alex's complaint: `rig apply` dumps a ~220-action plan + a wall of notes and then **silently mutates** with no clear finish. This makes `rig apply` **preview-by-default** with an explicit commit step, and folds in the plan/notes UX fixes.

Closes #160.

## Command surface

| command | behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `rig apply` (bare) | **preview** — alias for `rig apply info`; prints the plan, states it's a preview, prints the exact `rig apply commit …` line (carrying the preview's own `-C`/`--config`/`--only`). **Mutates nothing.** |
| `rig apply info` | explicit preview (same output) |
| `rig apply commit` | **executes** the plan (today's apply behavior) |
| `rig apply --yes` | commit intent — executes headless (automation back-compat) |
| `rig apply commit --yes` | the explicit CI form |
| `rig apply --dry-run` | still forces a preview, even under `commit` |

One engine: `info` and `commit` share the same `plan.build`; only `commit` calls `actions.run_plan`. `rig setup` and `rig init --apply` still execute (migrated to `apply commit` internally).

## Plan/notes UX (Alex tg#8918)

- Plan groups **will-change vs already-in-sync**; no-op rows collapse behind a count unless `-v`/`--verbose`.
- Informational notes collapse to a one-line count (`--notes` to expand); **real-gap notes** (e.g. `hook_bridge: skipped`) are elevated to a ⚠ line. Classifier is deliberately narrow so intentional states (export-only CI, instruction-file harnesses) aren't flagged.
- **Per-phase progress** on the slow live-activation runners via a new pre-dispatch `on_start` callback in `run_plan`, so silence ≠ hang.
- **Full apply log** written to `~/.cache/rig/apply-<UTC>.log` on every commit regardless of console verbosity (best-effort — never fails the apply).
- Clear completion line: `✓ applied N (C changed, M unchanged) in Xs`, downgraded to ✗ when an action errored or verify FAILED (printed **after** verify, so a green marker never precedes a non-zero exit).

## Call sites migrated (so a bare `rig apply` never silently no-ops where it means to execute)

`tests/smoke.sh` (+ `--fast` preview marker), `tests/test_cleanroom_e2e.py`, the `rig setup` wizard, `test_cli`/`test_status_*`/`test_autonomous_mode`, and all `rig apply` guidance in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `install.sh`, the `install.py` skill, the `state.py` rig.yaml header, `config-web`, and error remediation hints across `missing_target`/`drift`/`github_auth`/`runner`/`config_web_service`.

## Tests / evidence

- `python -m pytest -q` → **1926 passed, 18 skipped** (the one `tmux_e2e_gating` failure is a pre-existing environment flake, tolerated per the task; confirmed it fails on the untouched tree too).
- `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE=… bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → green (the dry-run coverage leg now asserts the preview "nothing applied" marker).
- Full `bash tests/smoke.sh` → green, incl. the heavy `apply commit` idempotency + tg-ctl legs.
- New `tests/test_apply_preview.py` (13 tests): bare = preview mutates nothing + alias notice + commit hint; `info` == bare; `commit` applies; `--yes` headless; idempotent completion line; `--dry-run` still previews; no-config refusal on both paths; notes collapse/elevate/expand; **apply log written**; hint preserves `--config`/`--only`; verify-failure downgrades the completion marker.

title: feat(permissions): harness parity — opencode deny/ask + codex execpolicy
body:
## What & why

Closes #166. claude-code already gets the full rig-provisioned permissions belt (allow safe commands without nagging + a conservative deny/ask baseline). codex and opencode had only the flag-position **deny-dangerous** effect via the PreToolUse hook bridge — no permission layer to pre-allow safe commands or apply the coarse deny. This adds that layer for both, keeping the precise flag-position guards in the hook bridge (same coarse-belt / deep-layer split as claude-code).

## Change A — opencode deny/ask via `permission.bash`

- Adds an opencode entry to the rule containers pointing at the same `("permission","bash")` object (container `object`, values `"deny"`/`"ask"`), plus a baked **opencode-dialect** deny/ask baseline (`riglib/permissions.py::OPENCODE_DENY_RULES`/`OPENCODE_ASK_RULES`). Emitted **after** the allow keys so rig's denies sit past any broad `"*"`/allow (opencode is **last-match-wins**). Removes opencode from the deny/ask N/A table.
- Deny globs: `gh pr merge*`, `git push*--force*`, `git push -f*`, `git commit --no-verify*`, `sudo rm*`, `screencapture*`. Ask globs: `pkill*`, `killall*`, `git reset*--hard*`.
- **Fidelity gaps documented:** opencode `*` has no word boundary, so the force-push glob also catches `--force-with-lease` (the precise guard stays in the hook bridge). The user-facing `allow`/`deny`/`ask` config lists are claude-code dialect, so under `kind: opencode` they are dropped-with-note and the baked opencode baseline is used.
- Drift: deny/ask keys share `permission.bash` with allow, so extras are computed against the **union** of all roles' desired keys and reported **once per container** (no cross-role false "extra"). Self-merge ship-rule suppression moved into the same per-container pass.

## Change B — codex execpolicy `.rules`

- New `provision_execpolicy` plan action + `_do_provision_execpolicy` runner + `_check_execpolicy` drift, keyed off a new `HARNESS_EXECPOLICY` registry. Writes a **marker-delimited managed block** of Starlark `prefix_rule(...)` lines into `~/.codex/rules/rig-managed.rules` (codex auto-scans that dir at startup — no config.toml reference needed).
- `_render_codex_rule(tool)` renders an `allow` prefix_rule for the resolved tool set; a **minimal** coarse deny (`gh pr merge`, `sudo rm`, `screencapture`) renders `decision="forbidden"`.
- Idempotent (re-apply = byte-identical no-op), backup-on-conflict, preserves user lines outside the markers, drift-surfaced by `rig status`.
- **Fidelity gap documented:** `prefix_rule` is a leading-token prefix — a coarse `["git","push"]` forbidden would over-block ALL pushes, so the coarse deny stays minimal and flag-position guards stay in the hook bridge.

## Reframed the misleading note

`plan.py` no longer prints a bare "harness 'codex' has no allowlist (skipped)" — it now describes the achieved effect (execpolicy allow/coarse-deny + hook-bridge flag denies). Schema hints + `docs/config-schema.md` updated for both harnesses.

## Test evidence

- New `tests/test_execpolicy.py` (renderers, plan, marker-block apply/idempotency/skip-append/backup, drift missing to converged to stale/unbalanced) + new opencode deny/ask ordering + drift tests in `tests/test_permissions.py`.
- **Validated against the real binary:** `codex execpolicy check` — the generated block parses, `gh pr merge` yields `forbidden`, `tg hello` yields `allow`.
- Full unit suite green (1939 passed; the 2 non-passes are the pre-existing tmux-e2e-gating import flake and a pre-existing cross-file ordering flake in `test_codex_update_cli` — both pass in isolation, both unrelated to this change) plus `smoke.sh --fast` green.
- Two AI code reviews (`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8`) returned **[ok]** (no blocking issues). Review findings on the additive `skip` path and drift-message accuracy were folded in; a follow-up for positional drift on hand-reordered opencode keys is filed as #168.

## Activation

Requires `rig apply` on the machine to write the opencode deny/ask keys + the codex execpolicy block. codex execpolicy only fires when codex is a configured harness (`harness.kind`/`harness.kinds`).

title: feat(pi): provision the pi permission-guard extension (pi permission parity)
body:
## What

Provisions the pi `permission-guard` extension so **pi-harness repos get the same deny-dangerous / ask-risky command belt** the other harnesses get. pi ships no built-in permission system (it runs bash with the user's own privileges); its extension API can intercept the bash tool pre-execution, which is the sanctioned parity mechanism.

This is the **rig half**. The extension itself lives in agent-tools:
➡️ **Cross-repo dependency: alex-mextner/agent-tools#294** (the `permission-guard` extension). This PR installs that extension into pi's extensions dir and writes the policy it reads; it needs the extension present in the agent-tools catalog. **Do not merge before #294.**

## The engine path (one engine, two front-ends — unchanged)

- **catalog** (`riglib/catalog.py`): discovers `pi-extensions/<name>/` (requires an `index.ts` entry) → category `pi_extensions`.
- **plan** (`riglib/plan.py`): for `permissions.kind: pi` (or a pi harness), emits a `provision_pi_extension` action carrying the extension carrier, the install dir, the policy-file path, and the resolved policy document (baseline in the extension's flag-anywhere dialect: deny raw PR merges / force pushes / hook-bypass commits / root file removal / screencapture; ask before broad process kills and hard resets).
- **runner** (`riglib/actions/runner.py`): `_do_provision_pi_extension` copies the extension into pi's `extensions/` dir and writes the rig-owned policy JSON — idempotent (skip-if-identical), backup-on-conflict, `error` surfaced over `backed_up`.
- **drift** (`riglib/drift.py`): `_check_pi_extension` reports missing/modified for both the extension dir and the policy file.
- **permissions** (`riglib/permissions.py`): pi is **no longer an N/A skip** — `harness_permission_extension("pi")` + `pi_policy_document()` (deep-copied baseline). `config.validate` now accepts `permissions.kind: pi`.
- **harness_skills** (`riglib/harness_skills.py`): adds `pi_agent_dir()`/`pi_user_path()` (honor `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) and **fixes pi's global instruction path** (`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, not the wrong `~/.config/pi/AGENTS.md`).

## Proof it works end-to-end in real pi

- Extension unit tests: 32 matcher + handler-wiring tests green.
- rig unit tests: 21 new (`tests/test_pi_extension.py`), full suite `1933 passed` (only the pre-existing tolerated `test_tmux_e2e_gating` flake fails).
- `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE=… bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` green (full real-catalog dry-run, zero unknown items).
- **Real-pi end-to-end**: rig's real `provision_pi_extension` installed the extension + policy into a temp `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`; pi (driven by a deterministic faux provider) **auto-discovered** the extension and **blocked** `git push --force` with `isError:true` and the exact deny reason — the side-effect marker (only created if the command executes) was absent. Fail-closed (missing/malformed policy → baked baseline blocks) and ask-non-interactive→block also verified live.

## Not included

Does not merge. Off-scope matcher limitations (shell-wrapper / substitution / leading-redirect obfuscation) are documented in the extension README on #294 and remain the domain of the deeper argv-level agent-hooks.

Adds the two real ecosystem CLIs `pm` (pm-cli) and `research` (research-cli) to rig's default per-harness permission allowlist, so agents no longer get a permission prompt for them. They render as `Bash(pm:*)` / `Bash(research:*)` for claude-code (and `pm *` / `research *` for opencode).

Both are read-only coordinators — pm observes/reconciles project state, research runs multi-provider research/panels — neither edits code. They match the safe profile of the already-allowed `review`/`task`.

## Final default set

```py

```

- `riglib/permissions.py` — added `pm`, `research` to `DEFAULT_ECOSYSTEM_TOOLS` (+ docstrings).
- `riglib/stats/taxonomy.py` — added them to `OUR_CLIS` (adoption-stats taxonomy; else `test_stats` fails), with `pm`'s generic-name caveat noted.

## ⚠️ Security note (for CTO review)

This **widens the default permission allowlist**: it pre-allows `Bash(pm:*)` / `Bash(research:*)` — an unconditional wildcard over every subcommand — in **every repo rig provisions**. title: feat: rig-managed tmux focus-events + shell env vars (COLORTERM=truecolor)
body:
## Summary

Two related, independently-committed additions to rig's declarative config, both requested by Alex to replace hand-edited dotfiles with rig-managed provisioning:

**1. `tmux.focus_events` (Closes #204)** — models tmux's `focus-events` option as a proper rig-managed boolean, following the exact established pattern of every other modeled tmux boolean. `render_rig_conf()` emits an explicit `set -g focus-events on`/`off` (never omitted), placed first in the generated file since it carries no ordering dependency on the resurrect/continuum/tpm machinery.

**2. `env:` block — shell environment variables (Closes #206)** — a brand-new capability: rig owns a generated `~/.config/rig/env/rig.env.sh` (one `export KEY=value` per configured var) and ensures a `source` line is present in `rc_path` (default `~/.zshenv` — the only zsh startup file sourced unconditionally in every mode, including non-interactive shells). Mirrors `riglib.tmux`'s "generated file + spliced import line" idiom, but deliberately **position-tolerant** (not end-anchored like tmux) since a plain exported var has none of tmux's continuum-ordering hazard. Shell-injection hardening throughout: var keys validated as POSIX identifiers (both at config-validate time and again at render time), values `shlex.quote`d, the import line itself `shlex.quote`d rather than hand-placed quotes.

Follow-up filed: **#207** — a pre-existing, system-wide characteristic (shared by `env`/`tmux`/`gitignore`/`spotlight`) that a repo's own committed `rig.yaml` can declare a GLOBAL-labeled block with no layer enforcement. Confirmed not a regression from this PR; deferred as an architecture decision, not something either of these two features could fix in isolation.

title: feat(internal-dev): per-repo daemon auto-reload post-commit hook
body:
## Summary
- Adds `internal_dev.auto_reload_on_commit` (opt-in, default off): a committed, per-repo `post-commit` git hook that gracefully reloads a live-symlink/daemon rig-ecosystem tool (`tg-ctl restart` by default) when a commit touches configured daemon-source paths.
- Handles the `core.hooksPath` composer trampoline needed when the rig global-hook dispatcher shadows repo-local hooks.
- Config/schema/plan wiring + the pure hook-rendering module were already uncommitted in this worktree; this PR adds the missing runner action handler + drift checker the tests exercise, regenerates `schema/rig.schema.json`, and adds the docs section + registry-test updates.

## Review history
Four rounds of `review diff --staged` (Opus/Fable/k3 — Codex hit its usage cap every round) found and this PR fixes:
- Shell pathname expansion silently broke `case` glob matching for nested daemon-source paths (`set -f`)
- Hooks path resolved via `--absolute-git-dir`, which points at a linked worktree's private admin dir instead of the shared common dir git actually reads hooks from (`--git-common-dir`)

title: feat: make Rig the lint policy source of truth
body:
## What changed

Makes lint/format configuration a first-class Rig-managed area and moves rule policy ownership into Rig rather than hand-maintained Oxc files.

### Policy

`linters.rules` supports:

- built-in audited defaults
- `all: true`
- applicability groups
- per-rule `enable` / `disable`
- final per-rule `severity: off|warn|error`

The existing config cascade supplies precedence: built-in defaults < global Rig config < repository `rig.yaml`.

### Oxc readiness

Rig does not silently install a generated Oxc rule policy into a repository that cannot execute it. If Oxlint is absent (including repositories using a foreign linter such as ESLint/Biome), rule provisioning emits a non-mutating blocked/error action with a copy-ready migration prompt. If anti-slop is enabled, `@oxlint/plugins` must also be declared. Generic `linters.items` remain usable independently.

If Oxlint coexists with another linter, Rig can apply Oxc policy but reports the coexistence so duplicate/conflicting lint scripts can be removed deliberately.

### Managed files

Generated/source-backed comment-capable config files carry a Rig ownership header describing their source of truth and direct-edit contract. Strict JSON is left syntactically valid because it cannot contain comments. `oxlint.config.ts` is explicitly marked as reconciled by `rig apply`; temporary direct edits are diagnostic-only and must be moved into Rig policy before commit.

### Rule impact

Before changing generated Oxlint policy, `rig apply` runs a best-effort current-vs-proposed finding preview when the Oxc environment is executable and reports error/warning deltas. Missing Oxc is handled by the readiness gate instead of silently skipping the preview.

### Sources

anti-slop implementation source comes from the pinned `agent-tools/vendor/anti-slop` subrepo. The reviewed inventory includes the two opt-in API-shape rules; they remain off by default.

## Validation

Focused lint-policy/carrier/schema tests and the full pytest suite run in the integration workflow; normal repository CI still gates merge.

title: feat(worktree): standardize .worktrees/<name> convention + git-exclude registration
body:
## Summary
- Standardizes a new agent worktree's location on `<repo>/.worktrees/<name>` via the new `rig worktree create <name>` command, replacing the several ad hoc conventions that had grown up around the ecosystem (Claude Code's own `.claude/worktrees/` — already solved separately — plus a bare in-repo `.worktrees/` and a sibling-of-repo `.worktrees/`, neither previously coded anywhere in rig).
- Before running `git worktree add`, idempotently registers `.worktrees/` in the repo's `.git/info/exclude` — never the committed `.gitignore` — reconciled BEFORE creation so a marker conflict or unwritable exclude file is caught without ever leaving a half-created, unignored worktree behind. Reuses the same marker-splice primitives (`_find_marker_lines`, `_atomic_write_exclude`) and the worktree-aware `repo_info_exclude_path` resolver that the existing ship-delegator/opencode-bridge excludes already use.
- Hardened after a two-model AI code review (each finding independently reproduced against real git before fixing): rejects a `--branch`/`--from` value starting with `-` (closes a real git-option-injection path — `--from=--no-checkout` was silently read by git's own option parser as a flag, leaving an unpopulated worktree reported as success); refuses to create through a symlinked `.worktrees/`; reclassified exit codes (a git-level domain failure like a branch collision is a usage error, not "rig broke"; git-missing is a missing-dependency exit; a timeout is reported as a timeout); and corrected a factual error (inherited from the pre-existing ship-delegator docstring) claiming `.git/info/exclude` is private per-worktree — verified empirically it is the repo's single COMMON/shared exclude file.
- Deferred to follow-up tickets: #255 (consolidate the now-3rd copy-pasted exclude marker-splice reconciler into one shared helper), #256 (design question — should worktree creation always resolve to the primary checkout root, not nest inside a linked worktree), #257 (process-group-aware timeout handling for a hung post-checkout hook).

Closes #261

title: feat(worktree): rig worktree remove — the inverse of create
body:
## Summary
- Adds `rig worktree remove <name>`, the inverse of `rig worktree create`: force-removes the linked worktree at `<repo>/.worktrees/<name>` and deletes the branch it had checked out, reading the branch from `git worktree list --porcelain -z` rather than assuming it equals `<name>` (`create --branch` can diverge from the directory name).
- Refuses outright (no mutation at all) if the branch lookup itself can't be trusted, if `.worktrees/` is a symlink escaping the repo, or if `.worktrees/<name>` itself is a symlink.
- Also recovers a worktree whose directory was deleted by hand (`rm -rf`) but is still registered with git with a live branch.

## Review history
Reviewed across 7 rounds of `review diff` (task codes `worktree-remove`, `worktree-remove-v2`..`v7`, `worktree-remove-final`) across codex, claude-opus, kimi-code, and fable. A genuine bug was found and fixed during that process: a branch-lookup/detached-HEAD conflation that would leave a branch behind while reporting success. The final round (after adding the `.worktrees/<name>`-itself-is-a-symlink guard, which had not yet been covered by any prior round) came back with design-level suggestions only (destructive-by-design deletion semantics — matches `create`'s documented wholesale-teardown intent; test-coverage/refactor suggestions) and no confirmed correctness bug. One seemingly concrete finding (an unquoted `git branch -D <name>` argument) was verified as a false positive: git itself refuses to create any branch name starting with `-`, so the reported attack precondition cannot occur.

## Summary
- Adds `rig daily`: a categorized "what shipped" report over merged pull requests (Security / Infra-CI / Performance / Product-UX / Other), sourced from `gh pr list --state merged` — never an LLM call, never a ticket status.
- Per-repo watermark state (`~/.config/rig/daily-state.json`, written atomically) so a repeat run never double-reports, a failed/newly-added repo never borrows another repo's cursor, and a quiet-but-complete run still advances so a delayed next run doesn't fall back to the rolling default lookback.

Known, accepted, tracked limitations (rig-cli#281, documented in `riglib/daily/command.py`'s module docstring): `gh pr list` sorts by creation date not merge date (a stale-branch PR merged just now could in theory be missed with no warning), and the watermark is second-granularity with a strictly exclusive filter (a same-second merge race is a low-probability gap). ## Summary

`rig init` on a PEP-668 externally-managed Python (the default on modern Homebrew/distro Python) silently failed to install `textual`/`rich` via `install.sh` or `rig doctor --yes`, then told the user to "reinstall rig" with no command that actually fixes a local dev checkout. This is exactly the bug Alex hit live on his own machine.

- `doctor.py`: detect PEP-668 (`EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker, venv-aware via `sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix` so it never misfires inside a pipx/uv-tool install) and offer an explicit `--break-system-packages` fallback command alongside the plain one.
- `cli.py`: `rig doctor`, `rig doctor --yes`, and `rig init`'s no-textual preview all surface the fallback; name whichever of textual/rich is actually missing instead of hardcoding "textual"; lead with the checkout-fixing command (not `pipx`, which leaves the existing `~/.local/bin/rig` symlink in place) when externally-managed.
- `install.sh`: same diagnosis in its own best-effort warning, hedged for non-PEP-668 failure causes.

Closes #290.

## Process

7 rounds of review-cli's multi-model gate; real bugs caught and fixed along the way:
- round 1: `_install_cmd_for`'s early bail-out silently dropped python-dep install commands (and therefore the fallback) when no package manager was detected -- fixed by checking `dep.kind == "python"` before the manager check.
- round 3/4: `externally_managed()` false-positived inside a pipx/uv-tool venv (the venv's `sysconfig` stdlib path resolves to the marker-carrying BASE interpreter) -- fixed with a `sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix` guard, checked first.
- round 4: the "recommended" `pipx install rig-cli` fix doesn't actually replace the existing `~/.local/bin/rig` symlink from a local checkout install -- reordered to lead with the command that actually fixes the checkout.

A repeated codex claim that `uv` also needs `--system` alongside `--break-system-packages` was checked twice against the real `uv` on this machine (a `--dry-run` and a live install to a scratch `--target` dir) and does not reproduce -- `--python <interpreter> --break-system-packages` installs cleanly without `--system`.

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite: 2730 passed (2 pre-existing, unrelated failures confirmed against clean main -- `test_cmd_doctor_probe_exit_codes` genuinely lacks textual/rich on this dev machine; `test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` is a module-discovery quirk unrelated to this diff)
- [x] `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` -- green
- [x] Reproduced the exact bug live (`rig doctor` / `rig init --no-tui` on this machine, which is genuinely PEP-668 externally-managed) before and after the fix
- [x] New regression tests for: venv false-positive (both directions), no-package-manager edge case, textual-vs-rich naming, `rig doctor`/`rig doctor --yes` fallback output paths

title: feat(harness): register a Monitor PreToolUse matcher for the CC hook bridge (agent-tools#543)
body:
## Summary

Companion to alex-mextner/agent-tools#439 (now merged) — tracked by
alex-mextner/agent-tools#543 (this PR's title previously mis-cited an unrelated Linear
ticket in a different repo; corrected here). agent-tools#439 adds a
`subagent-no-monitor` hook that stops a dispatched subagent from calling Claude Code's
`Monitor` tool (the background event-stream watch that never notifies a subagent when it
finishes — the same wedge `subagent-no-bg-longproc` already blocks for a backgrounded Bash
command, hit here via a different tool). Its `Monitor -> pre-monitor` point mapping in
`lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py` is inert on its own: Claude Code only fires a `PreToolUse`
hook for a tool it has an explicit `settings.json` matcher for, and that matcher is written
here, in `hook_bridge_entries` — the same two-repo split `pre-agent` and `pre-skill` already
went through.

- `riglib/actions/runner.py`: add `("Monitor", cmd("PreToolUse"))` to the `claude-code`
  `PreToolUse` entries. Codex/opencode are unaffected — neither has a Monitor-equivalent tool
  today.
- `docs/config-schema.md`: documents the new matcher and the Codex/opencode gap.
- Strengthened the existing version-skew docstring in `hook_bridge_entries` to state
  explicitly (not just imply) that an unmapped `(event, tool)` pair makes the bridge emit
  nothing, so Claude Code sees no `permissionDecision` and the call proceeds allowed —
  addresses a review finding.
- `pyproject.toml`: version bump 0.32.1 -> 0.33.0 (ship's version-bump gate; this is a
  feature release).

**agent-tools#439 has now merged.** Once this PR merges too and `rig apply` (or an
equivalent manual `settings.json` edit) runs on a given machine, the block actually fires
end to end.

## Review

Three independent review rounds across this PR's lifetime (multi-model pool each time):
- **Opus: verdict CLEAN**, twice. Explicitly checked drift-on-legacy-install, idempotent
  re-apply, matcher-order sensitivity, Codex leakage, version skew, and (in the final round)
  the version-bump commit itself — all ruled out or covered by a test.
- **Codex/Fable** both flagged, at the time this PR was first reviewed, that agent-tools
  `main` didn't yet have the `Monitor -> pre-monitor` mapping merged. Expected — that was
  exactly the two-repo staging this PR documents; #439 has since merged and carries that
  half.
- **Codex** (final round) flagged that agent-tools' own `agent-hooks/README.md` and
  `subagent-no-monitor/README.md` still describe the registration gap as unresolved, which
  is now stale once this PR merges too — filed as a same-day follow-up doc fix on
  agent-tools main (registration is now genuinely live, not merely mapped).
- **Fable** also raised a broader, separate finding: Monitor's own command execution bypasses
  every existing `pre-bash` security guard (`block-raw-pr-merge`, `block-reset-hard`, etc.),
  since Monitor and Bash dispatch to different points. Tracked as
  alex-mextner/agent-tools#438 rather than folded into this — different problem, touches every
  existing `pre-bash` hook's threat model, deserves its own design pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_workflow_guard_knobs.py::test_pretooluse_matchers_cover_the_full_managed_set` —
      exact-set assertion updated to include `Monitor`.
- [x] `test_catalog_plan.py::test_plan_codex_bridge_does_not_wire_pre_agent_yet` — added
      `assert "Monitor" not in str(entries)` so a future accidental Codex leak fails loudly.
- [x] `test_actions_drift.py` — the "fully wired" fixtures for stale-command drift and
      skip-leaves-untouched now include a `Monitor` entry; added
      `test_hook_bridge_drift_missing_monitor_only`, mirroring the existing
      pre-agent/pre-skill upgrade-path tests: strips `Monitor` from an otherwise-wired
      `settings.json`, asserts drift reports the gap, asserts apply adds only `Monitor`
      while leaving the other four matchers untouched and un-duplicated.
- [x] `test_cleanroom_helpers.py` / `test_cleanroom_e2e.py` — the `_full_hook_bridge_settings`
      fixture and the Docker e2e's `check_settings.py hook_bridge` expected-matcher list both
      updated so a real `rig apply` run is checked end-to-end for the new matcher too.
- [x] Full suite (foreground): `uv run --with pytest --with tomli python -m pytest tests/ -q`
      → **2993 passed, 34 skipped**.

title: feat(harness): register an EnterWorktree PreToolUse matcher for the CC hook bridge
body:
## Summary

Companion to [alex-mextner/agent-tools#455](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/455)
(`enterworktree-foreign-guard`): that PR adds a `pre-worktree-enter` agent-hook that blocks
`EnterWorktree(path=...)` into a worktree a DIFFERENT agent created — the confirmed harness
bug where that call reports success and then permanently bricks the calling agent's Bash tool
for the rest of its session — plus the `(PreToolUse, EnterWorktree) -> pre-worktree-enter`
point mapping in `cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`.

Without an `EnterWorktree` matcher registered in `settings.json`, Claude Code never fires the
bridge for an `EnterWorktree` call and the new agent-tools hook stays inert — the same
"designed but dead" failure mode this ecosystem hit before when a bridge half landed without
its rig-cli matcher (`pre-agent`'s original agent-tools#18 gap, and `pre-skill`'s own
#288/#425 split, which this PR mirrors exactly).

Refs #297.

## What changed

- `hook_bridge_entries()` (`riglib/actions/runner.py`) adds an `EnterWorktree` `PreToolUse`
  matcher for `claude-code`, alongside `Bash`, `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`,
  `Agent|Task`, and `Skill`.
- `docs/config-schema.md`'s hook-bridge section lists the new matcher, and the Codex/opencode
  gap note now also documents `EnterWorktree` (neither harness exposes a worktree-switching
  tool today).
- Tests: the full-registration assertion, the idempotent-reapply block count, the
  exact-matcher-set unit test, the cleanroom e2e/helpers checker fixtures, a new
  missing-`EnterWorktree`-matcher drift test mirroring the existing missing-`Skill` test, and
  the two stale-command fixtures extended to include the new matcher.
- Version bump 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 (this repo's per-PR convention).

## Sequencing note

Landing this PR alone before agent-tools#455 merges is harmless: an unmapped `tool_name` is a
documented no-op in `dispatch.py`'s `point_for_event` — an `EnterWorktree` `PreToolUse` event
just falls through to CC's normal flow (no enforcement yet, but also no crash/block) until the
companion PR's point mapping lands too. Same split `pre-agent`/`pre-skill` shipped through
originally. `review diff --staged` (codex) flagged this exact gap during local review — it is
the intended, documented two-repo split, not a regression; noted here for the record.

title: feat(usage): add rig usage — cross-account Claude token/cost stats
body:
## Summary

Adds `rig usage`, a new command that reports real Claude token usage and a hypothetical cost estimate across every Claude account on this machine — the default account (`~/.claude/projects`) plus every account the separate `claude-rotate` tool manages (`~/.claude-accounts/account-*/projects`).

- Bare `rig usage` reports the current week AND current month.
- `--period day|week|month` narrows to one window.
- `--json` emits a stable, versioned contract (`schema`, `generated_at`, `disclaimer`, `accounts_scanned`, `undated_records_scanned`, `periods.*`) for unattended scripting.
- Cost is explicitly labeled **hypothetical, at published API list prices** — this is a Claude.ai subscription, not pay-per-token billing, so the dollar figure is illustrative only, never a real bill. A model ID not in the pricing table (exact match, or a known dated-snapshot alias like `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) is reported separately as "unpriced", never guessed at.
- Parsing is streaming/line-by-line with mtime-based file pruning, so a scheduled run only re-parses files actually touched in the requested window — never the whole log history.

### Handoff interface for the separate tg-cli scheduling work

The task also asked for a scheduled weekly/monthly Telegram push. That scheduling and the `tg /usage` bot command are being built independently, in the sibling `tg-cli` repo — not part of this PR. This PR's job is to make the interface tg-cli's scheduler will call clean and stable:

```
rig usage --json --period week    # run at end-of-week
rig usage --json --period month   # run at end-of-month
```

Both are pure reads (no state written). JSON envelope:

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "generated_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC — real wall-clock time of report generation>",
  "disclaimer": "<hypothetical-cost disclaimer text>",
  "accounts_scanned": ["default", "account-0", "account-1", "account-2"],
  "undated_records_scanned": 0,
  "periods": {
    "week": {
      "period": "week", "label": "2026-W35",
      "start": "...", "end": "...",
      "totals": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0, "cache_read_input_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0},
      "estimated_cost_usd": 0.0,
      "all_models_unpriced": false,
      "by_model": {"<model id>": {"totals": {"..."}, "estimated_cost_usd": 1.23}},
      "by_account": {"<account>": {"...totals..."}},
      "unpriced_tokens": {"<unpriced model id>": {"...totals..."}}
    }
  }
}
```

`undated_records_scanned` is deliberately top-level, not per-period — an undated record can't be placed into a specific window, so it would otherwise appear identically under both `periods.week` and `periods.month`, and a consumer summing it would double-count. `all_models_unpriced` lets a consumer distinguish "genuinely zero usage" from "every model in this window is unpriced" — both would otherwise read as `estimated_cost_usd: 0.0`.

Empty `accounts_scanned` (e.g. a misconfigured `$HOME` on a cron box) is a normal, non-error 0-token report rather than a hard failure — a fresh machine with no Claude usage yet is a legitimate state, not a misconfiguration, so this deliberately does NOT mirror `rig daily`'s "every source failed → nonzero exit" behavior. A consumer that wants to treat an empty scan as suspicious should check `accounts_scanned` itself.

### Known, accepted tradeoffs (documented in the module, surfaced here for visibility)

- **First-wins dedup**: the same `(message.id, requestId)` can legitimately appear more than once (a `--resume` replay, or a message split across session files); whichever occurrence is scanned first wins. Verified empirically that duplicates on this machine carry byte-identical usage figures. If a duplicate ever carries *different* figures (e.g. a mid-stream checkpoint followed by a larger final line), this undercounts using the first occurrence.
- **mtime-based file pruning is a heuristic, not a guarantee**: an append-only session file's mtime is always >= its newest line's timestamp, so a file whose mtime predates the reporting window (with a 48h safety margin for clock skew) is skipped without opening it. This is what keeps a scheduled run fast — it turns "parse years of history" into "parse the files actually touched this week." It is *not* proof against an adversarial or unusual backup/restore that preserves an old mtime on a file containing recent events; two reviewers disagreed on how much this matters (one called it a must-fix correctness gap, one called the 48h margin an accepted tradeoff already "ruled out"). Landed on: keep the pruning (the real, large performance win this repo's "don't blow up memory" ethos asked for) and document the heuristic honestly rather than trying to eliminate an unbounded edge case.

### Review

Went through five rounds of multi-model review (`review diff`). Real correctness bugs found and fixed along the way — not a rubber-stamp pass:
- a dedup key collision from an ambiguous string join (fixed with length-prefixed hashing)
- negative/boolean/oversized numeric token fields corrupting totals or crashing cost math (`OverflowError`, bare `Infinity` in JSON)
- a malformed 4300+ digit numeric literal aborting the whole scan (Python's int-string conversion limit, CVE-2020-10735)
- an undated first occurrence silently absorbing a real, later, in-window duplicate's tokens
- the mtime-pruning cutoff varying with which `--period` was requested, which changed which files got scanned and could make `--period week` alone disagree with the `week` section of a bare `rig usage` for the same underlying data — fixed by always cutting off at `min(week_start, month_start)`, independent of the requested periods
- C0-only control-character stripping leaving the C1 range open to terminal-escape injection via a crafted model/account string

Rounds converged from 2 High/P1 findings down to a single Low/cosmetic note by the final pass.

### Follow-up filed (not in scope here)

#313 tracks consolidating the three now-duplicated ISO-8601 timestamp parsers in `riglib` (stats, daily, and this module's own copy) into one shared leaf module — this module deliberately keeps its own copy rather than importing the stats one, to avoid pulling that unrelated subsystem's package-import chain into a command that has nothing to do with it.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — full unit suite, 2869 passed, 34 skipped, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`test_tmux_e2e_gating.py::test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` — verified identical on base commit `8ab4c56` before any of this PR's changes, so not a regression).
- [x] `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — clean.
- [x] `ruff check` on all changed files — clean.
- [x] Manually ran `rig usage`, `rig usage --json --period week`, `rig usage --json --period month` against this machine's real Claude Code logs (4 accounts, ~8700 session files) — correct output, no crash, sub-10s even scanning a full month unfiltered.
- [x] 61 new tests in `tests/test_usage.py` covering pricing math (including the cache-write/cache-read multipliers), dedup (including the cross-invocation-consistency regression), the unpriced-model bucket (including the dated-snapshot-alias case), malformed/adversarial input, mtime pruning (including the two-file cutoff-independence repro), and CLI wiring end-to-end.

Refs #312. Filed #313.

title: feat(config-web): machine-wide multi-repo console, drift panel, interactive apply
body:
feat(config-web): machine-wide multi-repo console, drift panel, interactive apply

Turns rig config-web from a single-repo config editor into a machine-wide
dashboard: one tab per rig-managed repo (discovered read-only from the
existing repository registry) plus a dedicated Global tab for
~/.config/rig/config.yaml alone. Each tab shows a drift panel (the same
two-way engine rig status uses) next to the settings, and an edit now offers
an interactive apply flow instead of silently writing only the config file:
a plan preview (mirrors rig apply info, via the exact same plan.build() call),
each action tagged by real kind (creates file, installs hook, permission/
guard, etc. -- derived from the actual handler registry in
actions/runner.py, never invented categories), confirm-or-skip individual
actions, then live per-phase progress as the SAME shared engine (plan.build +
run_plan) rig apply/rig init already use actually applies them -- never a
forked executor.

New modules: riglib/action_tags.py (the action-kind tag taxonomy, pinned to
the real handler registry by a completeness test), riglib/config_web_scopes.py
(scope discovery + the allowlist every multi-repo endpoint validates against),
riglib/config_web_plan.py (plan preview, fingerprinting, and the
ApplyJobStore that runs selected actions via the real run_plan in a
background thread with live progress).

Refactored riglib/cli.py's cmd_status: extracted compute_drift_report() into
riglib/drift.py as a shared, pure (non-mutating, idempotent) helper so both
`rig status` and config-web's drift panel use the identical engine --
previously an in-place plan mutation made a second call on the same plan
silently under-report.

Went through eight rounds of independent multi-model review (review-cli:
codex + GLM), each fixing real issues found: stored-XSS-adjacent unescaped
JS interpolation, a fingerprint that missed on_conflict/options/source
changes, a swallowed per-action apply failure reported as success, a
Global-tab edit gate that could be blocked by an unrelated repo's rig.yaml,
a Global-tab plan/view mismatch letting "Apply selected" execute hidden
settings, a Global-tab drift panel that falsely flagged every installed
skill/hook as "extra", a malformed registry entry crashing the whole
console, a fail-open skip_keys path, a slow-loris body-drain DoS on
/api/plan, and a script-data double-escape page-breaking bug. The two
remaining findings from the final round (catalog content not hashed in the
fingerprint; the apply lock is per-process not machine-wide) are explicitly
documented as accepted, bounded limitations rather than silently ignored --
both mirror pre-existing gaps in `rig apply` itself, not new regressions.

Docs updated to match: the config_web.py module docstring, the CLI help
description in config_web_service.py, AGENTS.md's config-web paragraph, and
README.md's command table all now describe the interactive-apply flow
instead of the old "edits never apply" behavior.

Fixes #310

title: feat(permissions): allow gh by default with a config opt-out
body:
Closes #332

## What

`gh` (the GitHub CLI) joins rig's default permission allowlist on every harness rig provisions, and a new `permissions.allow_gh` config key (default `true`) opts a machine or repo back out.

## Why

Everyday agent use of `gh` is read-heavy (`gh pr view`, `gh issue list`) and `gh ship` is the sanctioned merge path, yet rig deliberately excluded `gh`, so every call prompted. The CTO asked for `gh` whitelisted by default with a config opt-out.

## How

- `riglib/permissions.py`: new `DEFAULT_GIT_HOSTING_TOOLS = ("gh",)` folded into `DEFAULT_TOOLS`; the module docstring documents the residual write surface a blanket `gh` grant trades in (`gh api` merge routes, `gh auth token`, `gh repo delete`) and which layer closes what.
- `riglib/plan.py`: `_resolved_permission_tools()` is the single funnel for both the allowlist builder and the codex execpolicy builder; `allow_gh: false` is sugar over `disable: [gh]`, applied after `extra`/`tools`, so it always wins.
- `riglib/actions/runner.py`: opencode is last-match-wins, so rig's own deny/ask keys are re-anchored to the end of the container on every apply. Without this a machine that applied the old baseline first (deny present, no `gh` allow yet) would get the `gh *` allow appended after the deny and silently un-deny `gh pr merge`. The write decision now compares serialized bytes before/after so a pure reorder is still persisted.
- `riglib/config.py`, `riglib/config_schema.py`, `riglib/schema.py`, `schema/rig.schema.json`, `docs/config-schema.md`: validate, describe and document `allow_gh`.

## Tests

Full suite in the feature worktree: 2954 passed, 34 skipped. Four failures are unrelated to this change: `test_tmux_e2e_gating` and `test_codex_update_cli_missing_updater_returns_127` fail identically on `main`; the two `test_safe_codex_update_*` tests are order-dependent and pass in isolation.

New tests cover default-on, `allow_gh: false`, `allow_gh` vs `extra: [gh]`, `allow_gh` vs `tools: [gh, ...]`, the codex execpolicy path, and the opencode re-anchor.

title: fix(gitignore): ignore the Spotlight sentinel .metadata_never_index machine-wide
body:
## What

rig's `spotlight:` sweep drops the macOS Spotlight sentinel `.metadata_never_index` into dependency/build dirs — including a committed `vendor/` inside a git working tree. The file is untracked, so every worktree on the machine showed as dirty and `gh ship` refused to merge (`?? vendor/.metadata_never_index`; 17 of 25 agent-tools worktrees on 2026-09-05).

Fix at the source, in the rig-managed block of git's GLOBAL `core.excludesfile` (the same block that already ignores `**/.claude/worktrees/`):

- `GITIGNORE_DEFAULT_ENTRIES` gains `.metadata_never_index` (a bare basename ignores it at any depth, machine-wide, zero per-repo commits). The in-block comment now explains both lines.
- `resolve_global_excludes` (the ONE seam apply + drift share) reports `missing_entries` on the `update` state, and the `rig status` drift detail names the missing line(s) — `… differs from config — missing: .metadata_never_index (apply reconciles it)` — instead of a bare "differs", so an operator sees WHY a pre-#331 block is stale. Only the marker-delimited managed block is scanned (a user-authored copy of the line elsewhere in the file does not make the block current, so it must not hide the note). The no-missing message is byte-identical to before.
- Description surfaces updated in lockstep: `docs/config-schema.md` (incl. the `git add -f` / `!.metadata_never_index` caveat for repos that deliberately track the sentinel), the `rig setup` wizard hint (`riglib/schema.py`), the config-schema block doc + regenerated `schema/rig.schema.json`.
- The smoke apply leg asserts the new entry.

## Tests (TDD red-first)

- byte-pin of the new canonical block; default entries carry the sentinel
- a legacy (worktrees-only) block: drift `modified` names `.metadata_never_index`; apply upgrades it; second apply is `skipped` and byte-identical; drift clean
- a legacy block plus a hand-added sentinel line OUTSIDE the block still names the missing entry
- a `modified` block with nothing missing does NOT claim a missing entry; a padded entry the block carries verbatim is not reported missing
- **acceptance proof with a real `git`**: a repo whose committed `vendor/` carries the untracked sentinel (and a `.claude/worktrees/` dir) has an EMPTY `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` under the managed block — isolated via `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` + `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` + tmp `HOME`

`python3 -m pytest -q`: 2953 passed, 34 skipped; the 2 failures are pre-existing on `main` (`test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` fails identically on an untouched main checkout — local import-mode issue; `test_codex_update_cli_missing_updater_returns_127` passes in isolation, its 0.5 s probe timeout trips under machine load). `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast`: OK. The full `tests/smoke.sh` init leg (which runs the new sentinel assertion) passes; its later `rig status` leg fails on this machine on untouched `main` too (environmental, out of scope).

Deliberately NOT done here: the sentinel is an untracked file inside a tracked directory (Go/PHP `vendor/`), and skipping tracked dirs would defeat the Spotlight exclusion for exactly those repos. title: fix(launchd): guard live launchctl/crontab mutations against a sandboxed HOME
body:
## What

Every fsutil-based action follows `Path.home()`, so overriding `$HOME` LOOKS like a full sandbox — but `launchctl` acts on the real per-user `gui/<uid>` domain regardless of `$HOME`. A HOME-only-isolated `rig apply` (the pattern the project's own e2e scaffold-apply leg uses) bootstrapped the REAL `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl` agent from a plist under `/var/folders/.../T/tmpXXXX/home/Library/LaunchAgents/…` (pointing at a nonexistent tg-ctl binary in the scratch HOME); it crash-looped 23,641 times (exit 78, `EX_CONFIG`) until it was booted out by hand on 2026-09-05.

This adds a fail-closed guard in `riglib/actions/runner.py`:

- `_real_login_home()` — the uid's login home from the passwd database (`pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir`, resolved, `lru_cache`d), `None` if unknown.
- `_home_is_sandboxed()` — ONE shared predicate: `Path.home().resolve() != real login home` (both sides resolved, so `/var/folders` vs `/private/var` is not a false positive). Unknown login home, or `Path.home()` itself raising `KeyError`/`OSError`/`RuntimeError` (an unmapped-uid container with no passwd entry) → sandboxed (fail-closed).
- It feeds all four launchd-touching paths through their existing `_*_dry_run` seams — `_schedule_dry_run` (launchd + crontab), `_tmux_dry_run` (boot agent, autosave agent, stale-continuum cleanup, plugin clones), `_tg_ctl_dry_run` (bootstrap/bootout AND the predecessor teardown), `_spotlight_dry_run` — so a sandboxed run behaves exactly like the corresponding `RIG_*_DRY_RUN` env: the artifact is written, the live mutation is skipped. Confirmed no other call site (uninstall/remove/doctor path) reaches `_launchctl*`/`_write_crontab` outside these four handlers plus drift/verify.
- `_live_skip_reason()` renders the action detail; it never crashes even when a fresh `Path.home()` call fails (falls back to the raw `$HOME` env var), and never calls `Path.home()` again if the caller already resolved it. The env flag keeps its wording and takes precedence (`RIG_TG_CTL_DRY_RUN — skipped launchctl bootstrap`); a sandboxed HOME reports `HOME is overridden (<home> != <real home>) — skipped live launchctl bootstrap (sandboxed run)`. The tmux activation, silent under the env flag, surfaces the sandbox skip as a warning in the action detail (never as an error status).
- The post-apply **verify** framework follows the SAME predicate (`riglib/verify.py::_live_check_skip_reason` imports `_env_flag`/`_home_is_sandboxed` from the runner instead of keeping an env-only copy): under a sandboxed HOME it records a skipped loaded-check instead of probing the real domain and failing `rig apply` with exit 1.
- `rig status` drift suppresses the live loaded-probe for the models schedule and tg_ctl under the same predicate (spotlight and tmux already did), AND the crontab-platform "line not installed" check is gated the same way — so a sandboxed apply converges (exit 0) on both the launchd and crontab platforms, instead of reporting permanent drift.
- tg_ctl's sandboxed/dry re-apply against an already-current plist no longer claims "already installed and loaded" without probing — it now names the skip like schedule/spotlight already did.
- Probe-after-gate ordering: a re-apply against an already-current schedule/spotlight plist no longer runs the loaded-probe (a read of the real launchd domain) before the dry-run/sandbox gate.
- Docs: AGENTS.md and `docs/config-schema.md` state that a HOME override alone is not a launchd sandbox, that rig guards it automatically, and that the guard covers both platforms.

There is deliberately NO opt-in to force the live path from a foreign HOME: a launchd agent loaded from a plist under a HOME that is not the login home is exactly the incident. To exercise the live path on purpose, run with the real HOME; the action detail names both paths so the mismatch is never silent. **Known, documented limitation** (flagged in review, accepted as-is): a legitimately relocated `$HOME` (≠ passwd home) that would in fact load correctly into the user's own `gui/<uid>` session is treated the same as a scratch sandbox — the skip is silent in `rig status`/verify beyond the one apply-detail line. No opt-in exists for this today; a `doctor` check or informational drift item would be a reasonable follow-up but is out of scope for this fix.

## Tests (TDD red-first) — `tests/test_home_sandbox_guard.py`

- the predicate: differs → True; matches → False; symlink-resolved → False; unknown login home → True; `Path.home()` raising `KeyError`/`RuntimeError` → True (fail-closed, not a crash); `_real_login_home` comes from passwd
- per action (tg_ctl, models schedule, tmux, spotlight): with `Path.home` pointed at a tmp dir and NO `RIG_*_DRY_RUN` env, the artifact lands, the detail says `HOME is overridden … (sandboxed run)`, and NO launchctl subprocess runs — these tests restore the REAL `_launchctl*` seams and patch `subprocess.run` to fail on any `launchctl` argv, so a bypass of the seams would fail too; tg_ctl's stale predecessor plist stays on disk
- the inverse: `_real_login_home` pinned to the FAKE home → the existing (stubbed) live path runs (bootstrap / load / activation)
- env precedence: `RIG_TG_CTL_DRY_RUN=1` under a sandbox still names the env flag
- sandboxed re-apply against a current schedule/spotlight/tg_ctl plist: `skipped`, no launchctl probe, names the skip; the crontab branch under a sandbox never writes
- `rig status` drift: sandboxed HOME never probes launchd for schedule or tg_ctl (tripwire: probe function raises if called), and never reads the real crontab; the real-HOME counterpart still probes and still surfaces genuine "not loaded" drift
- verify under a sandbox records a skipped loaded-check and never spawns launchctl, and runs the check with the real HOME
- `_live_skip_reason` never crashes when `Path.home()` raises (falls back to the `$HOME` env var)
- existing live-path tests that fake HOME on purpose opt out via the shared `live_launchd_home` conftest fixture (test_tmux, test_tg_ctl, test_models_schedule, test_spotlight, test_verify; the `_activation_seams` helper and the opt-in test_tmux_e2e set the same attribute inline)

`python3 -m pytest -q`: 2970+ passed, 34 skipped; the only failures are pre-existing/environmental and unrelated to this diff (`test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` fails identically on an untouched main checkout; the `test_tools.py` codex-update tests are machine-load flakes — confirmed green in isolation, and that file isn't touched here). `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast`: OK. The smoke tg-ctl leg (a real HOME-isolated `rig apply commit` of a tg_ctl-only config) was run by hand on this branch: plist written, second apply idempotent, and — with `RIG_TG_CTL_DRY_RUN` unset — the guard alone kept `launchctl` untouched.

## Scope notes

- `_tmux_activate` and `_do_provision_tg_ctl` were already well over the ~80-line guideline before this change; this PR adds a handful of lines to each (the skip-reason rendering) and does not split them — that refactor is deliberately out of scope for a guard fix.

## Acceptance criteria (from the issue)

- [x] Documented (AGENTS.md + docs/config-schema.md) that a HOME-override sandbox does NOT sandbox launchctl-based actions — and that rig now detects it.
- [x] Scoped behind an automatic guard mirroring the existing `RIG_SCHEDULE_DRY_RUN` / `RIG_TMUX_DRY_RUN` pattern (the env flags remain the explicit seam).

title: feat(worktree): add rig worktree gc — classify and clean up worktree sprawl
body:
## Summary

- Adds `rig worktree gc [--repo <path>] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--older-than-days N] [--include-stale]`, a new reconciler (`riglib/worktree_gc.py`) that lists every worktree `git worktree list` knows about for a repo — wherever it physically lives, not just the standardized `.worktrees/<name>` — and classifies each as `live` / `prunable` / `dirty` / `merged` / `closed` / `no-pr-stale` / `active`. Liveness (a running `claude`/`codex`/`opencode` process has the worktree as its cwd) is checked first, absolutely, before anything else. Report-only by default; `--yes` removes only `merged`/`closed`/`prunable` (plus the branch); `no-pr-stale` additionally needs `--include-stale`. `--dry-run` always forces a preview even with `--yes`.
- `--repo` omitted fans out over every repo the machine-local repository registry already knows about (the same discovery `rig config-web` uses).
- `rig status` now prints a cheap stale-worktree count using the exact same classifier (no disk-size scan).
- This directly targets the ticket's own measured evidence: roughly 70 leftover worktrees and well over 100GB of duplicated `node_modules`/`.venv` directories across the ecosystem repos.

## Documentation-acceptance-criterion finding

I checked, rather than assumed, whether the worktree-isolation skill and this repo's own agent docs already name `rig worktree create` as the one way to create a worktree. In THIS repo (`rig-cli`), yes — `AGENTS.md` now has a "Worktree lifecycle" section stating `rig worktree create`/`remove`/`gc` as the one door. But the actual skill agents reach for when told to isolate parallel work — `skills/by-type/monorepo/worktree-isolation` — lives in the separate `agent-tools` repository, which `rig-cli` consumes read-only (see this repo's own "integration seam" rule) and cannot patch from here. That skill currently still teaches a raw `git worktree add ../.worktrees/agent-$run_id -b work/$run_id` pattern (a sibling-of-repo location — one of the very conventions this ticket exists to retire) and never mentions `rig worktree create`. This is documented in `AGENTS.md` as a tracked, explicit follow-up that needs a separate PR against `agent-tools`.

## Safety design

- Liveness is checked first, absolutely, with fail-safe-toward-"keep" semantics on any uncertainty (a degraded `pgrep`/`lsof` snapshot marks everything live rather than everything safe).
- Every removal gets a fresh, per-entry recheck (liveness, dirtiness, and unpushed-commit reachability against both the current HEAD and the specifically-planned branch) immediately before the destructive `git worktree remove --force` call, closing most of the window between planning and execution.
- A merged/closed branch is only removable once its commits are unreachable from no surviving remote-tracking ref — with squash/rebase-merge + `fetch --prune` (a common GitHub setup) that's never true, so those worktrees classify `dirty` and are kept, safety over auto-clean effectiveness. Documented in the README caveat and the module's own "Known limitations" section (about 15 explicitly enumerated, deliberate trade-offs, all failing toward "keep, don't remove").

## Known, accepted trade-offs surfaced repeatedly across review (not fixed, by design)

- `git worktree remove --force` does not specially protect ignored-but-present local files (a `.env`, a generated artifact) — this matches `rig worktree remove`'s own existing behavior; gc's safety checks are about committed-work reachability, not about every file that happens to sit in the directory.
- PR state is a single per-run snapshot (one `gh pr list` fetch); a PR opened on an already-classified branch in the exact window between that snapshot and the entry's removal is not re-verified before removal (re-verifying would mean an extra `gh pr list` round-trip per removable entry).
- `rig status`'s stale-worktree count reuses the full classifier as instructed, which means it also pays for one `gh pr list` call (up to a 30s timeout) and `lsof` calls per matched process on a repo with linked worktrees; `RIG_STATUS_SKIP_WORKTREE_GC=1` opts out.

## Test evidence

- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_worktree_gc.py` — 83 passed.
- `python -m pytest -q` (full suite) — 3075 passed, 34 skipped, 1 failed. The 1 failure (`tests/test_tmux_e2e_gating.py::test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned`) is confirmed pre-existing and unrelated — it reproduces identically on the untouched `main` branch tip (a `ModuleNotFoundError` for `tests.test_tmux_e2e`, unrelated to this change).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — OK.
- Reviewed with `review diff --staged --task GH-329` across 24 iterative rounds (Claude Opus, Codex, GLM, Sonnet, Fable across correctness/consistency/architecture/quality/performance roles), fixing every genuine correctness/data-safety finding along the way (liveness ordering under a symlink-loop exception, a per-entry removal exception no longer discarding the whole run's report, a non-`\n` unicode line separator no longer truncating a liveness-check path, malformed/unrecognized PR records no longer trusted for merged/closed classification, and a malformed or empty/null repository-registry entry no longer crashing or silently widening the fan-out to the wrong directory). The final rounds' remaining findings were either style/design opinions (module size, comment verbosity, naming) or the already-documented trade-offs above, repeatedly re-raised without a new concrete scenario — both left as-is and noted here rather than chased further.

title: feat(harness): fold tg-ctl's Codex Stop hook into rig's own hook bridge (tg-cli#308)
body:
## Summary

Every Codex CLI session on a machine that runs both rig and tg-ctl currently prints a warning that it is loading hooks from two different files (`~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.codex/config.toml`), because each tool provisions its own Codex `Stop` hook in a different place. Codex supports multiple hook entries per event within one file, so this teaches rig's own codex hook-bridge provisioning to also emit tg-ctl's `codex-usage-hook` command as a second entry in the same `Stop` array in `~/.codex/config.toml` — the file rig already owns and reconciles — instead of tg-ctl writing a second, separate file.

- `hook_bridge_entries()` (runner.py) now appends any `action.options["extra_stop_hooks"]` after the bridge's own `Stop` entry (codex only); absent/empty regresses to the exact prior single-entry behavior.
- `_build_hook_bridge_for_kind` (plan.py) populates that option by default whenever a codex hook bridge is being provisioned (`harness.kind: codex`, or `codex` listed in `harness.kinds` alongside a different primary kind).
- The actual fold-in decision lives in one new function, `riglib/tg_ctl.py::codex_usage_hook_command` — resolves `bun_path`/`tg_ctl_path` through the exact same `build_tg_ctl()` logic the tg-ctl LaunchAgent plist itself uses, renders `bun <tg_ctl_path> codex-usage-hook` (not the script invoked directly), and fails closed (folds in nothing) unless the tg-ctl script exists AND bun itself exists and is executable — so a machine that never installed tg-ctl, or lacks a runnable bun, never gets a Codex hook that fails every session end.
- New `tg_ctl.codex_usage_hook` config key (default `true`) lets a user opt out of just the fold-in while keeping the tg-ctl daemon itself enabled; independent of `boot`.

**Cross-repo scope note**: this is the rig-cli half of a two-repo fix. tg-ctl's own detection logic — to stop writing `~/.codex/hooks.json` once it sees this `config.toml` entry — is being implemented separately in the tg-cli repo. Until that lands, a machine that already ran `tg-ctl install-hooks` keeps its existing `hooks.json` entry alongside this new one; the dual-source warning is only fully eliminated once both halves are deployed together. This repo's half does not touch tg-cli and does not need to.

Refs tg-cli#308, rig-cli#341

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 3014 passed, 34 skipped, 1 failed (pre-existing, unrelated `test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` import-caching issue — confirmed identical on clean `main`)
- [x] `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — green
- [x] `ruff check` on all touched files — clean (one pre-existing unrelated unused-import warning in `plan.py`, confirmed present on clean `main`)
- [x] New tests cover: default fold-in, disabled via `tg_ctl.enabled`, disabled via `tg_ctl.codex_usage_hook`, missing tg-ctl script (fail-closed), missing/non-executable bun (fail-closed), custom `tg_ctl_path`, non-codex harness (no effect), a secondary codex bridge alongside a different primary harness, independence from `boot`, and idempotent re-apply (no drift, no duplicate entries)
- [x] `review diff` (multi-model, several rounds) — addressed every actionable finding: shared bun/tg_ctl_path resolution (no duplicated path logic), invoking via `bun <script>` rather than the script directly, the bun-executable-bit fail-closed check, and doc/schema wording precision for the secondary-harness case. The one recurring finding (existing `hooks.json` installs aren't migrated) is the explicit, documented cross-repo dependency above — tg-cli's job, not rig-cli's, per the two-repo design.
