title: feat(harness): register omp as a supported agents-hooks/v1 bridge
body:
## What

Registers **omp** as a fourth supported agents-hooks/v1 hook-bridge harness kind, following the exact existing claude-code / codex / opencode pattern, and fixes the "silent skip" bug where rig only warned about a harness having zero hook-bridge coverage if the user had explicitly opted in.

> **Dependency — do not merge ahead of it without reading this.** This is the rig-cli half of a two-repo change. The agent-tools half (`lib/omp_hook_bridge/{dispatch.py,__main__.py,extension.ts,README.md}`, branch `feat/omp-hook-bridge`) is **alex-mextner/agent-tools#556** (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/556) — OPEN and **not merged** at the time of opening this PR. Hold `gh ship` on this PR until #556 merges. Merging rig-cli first is still SAFE: `_build_hook_bridge_for_kind` fail-closes when the module directory is missing from the checkout — verified live against the current agent-tools main, it emits `hook_bridge: skipped — .../lib/omp_hook_bridge is incomplete in this agent-tools checkout (missing dispatch.py, __main__.py, extension.ts; …)` and wires nothing. Neither half is fully functional alone until both merge and `rig apply commit` runs — the same companion-PR shape the Monitor PreToolUse matcher (#296 / agent-tools#543) used.

Refs alex-mextner/rig-cli#342 (closes gap #2 of the rig-cli#337 catalog; ticket closes only via task-cli acceptance).

## How

- **`riglib/plan.py`** — `omp` added to `_HOOK_BRIDGE_HARNESSES` as format `omp-extension`; `_hook_bridge_spec_for_kind` special-cases it (like codex) so the extension path is resolved dynamically under `omp_agent_root()` (honors `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `PI_CONFIG_DIR`). `bridge_required` now needs `extension.ts` to exist in the checkout (fail-closed); `expected_suffix` is `.ts`. `_agent_hooks_target_for_kind` special-cases `omp` → `<agent root>/hooks` dynamically. Deliberately **no** codex-style divergence block for omp: the omp dispatcher ports `omp_agent_root()`'s env precedence itself, so it independently resolves the same descriptor dir with no baked override (a baked one would only turn the plain symlink into an unnecessary wrapper).
- **`riglib/actions/runner.py`** — `_do_register_omp_hook_bridge`: symlinks `<omp agent root>/extensions/zz-agent-tools-hook-bridge.ts` → `<agent-tools>/lib/omp_hook_bridge/extension.ts`. When a custom `agent_hooks.target` **or** `hook_bridge.python` is configured it writes a tiny `.ts` wrapper module instead (sets `OMP_HOOKS_DIR` / `OMP_HOOK_BRIDGE_PYTHON`, then `await import()`s the real extension — the same shape as opencode's wrapper; a symlink cannot carry an env var). Idempotent, backup-on-conflict, self-symlink guard. A rig-owned prior artifact (a symlink demonstrably targeting the bridge, or a wrapper rig itself wrote — recognised by its full header + footer template shape) is always replaced on a mode/content switch regardless of `on_conflict`; a genuinely foreign file **or foreign symlink** respects skip/backup.
- **`riglib/drift.py`** — `_check_omp_hook_bridge`: missing / points-elsewhere / real-file-instead-of-symlink / wrapper-differs detection, mirroring the opencode check without its repo-local git-exclude or legacy-cleanup concerns.
- **`riglib/harness_skills.py`** — `omp_user_path()`, the omp analog of `codex_user_path()`, so the two omp path joins share one helper.
- **`riglib/cli.py`** — the silent-skip fix. The `hook_bridge: skipped — kind '<kind>' has no supported agents-hooks bridge yet` plan note now fires on **every** plan build for a kind with no bridge (pi/commandcode), not only when `hook_bridge.enabled: true` was set; an explicit `hook_bridge.enabled: false` still suppresses it. `rig status` did not print plan notes at all, so it gets a dedicated `_print_hook_bridge_coverage_gaps` call-out — the acceptance criterion names `rig status` specifically. The note phrase is a single constant (`plan.HOOK_BRIDGE_NO_SUPPORT_PHRASE`).
- **`riglib/action_tags.py`** — the `register_hook_bridge` description names the omp extension symlink alongside opencode/codex (config-web plan preview no longer mis-describes it).
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — fakes an `omp_hook_bridge` trio alongside the existing cc/codex/opencode fakes. **Docs** updated; `pyproject.toml` bumped 0.33.0 → 0.34.0 per the per-commit convention.

Format name settled on: `omp-extension`. Symlink target settled on: `zz-agent-tools-hook-bridge.ts` (keeps the opencode plugin's `zz-` late-load naming, `.ts` because the source is `.ts` and omp natively loads TypeScript extensions).

## Tests (TDD, red-first for the acceptance-criterion test)

`python3 -m pytest -q` → **3015 passed, 34 skipped, 1 failed** — the one failure is `tests/test_tmux_e2e_gating.py::test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` (`ModuleNotFoundError: tests.test_tmux_e2e`), which fails **identically on the unmodified base `7359ce4`** under this machine's Python 3.14 (`git stash` → same failure); `tests/test_cli.py::test_codex_update_cli_missing_updater_returns_127` also failed on base in one run (probe-timeout flake). Neither is touched by this diff. `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → OK, including the real-catalog full-coverage dry-run against the agent-tools worktree (zero unknown items).

One randomized-order run showed `test_omp_hook_bridge_repoints_existing_symlink` failing; it passed in isolation, in the whole file, in a `-p no:randomly` full run and in two further randomized full runs — not reproduced. It is most likely a pre-existing test-isolation leak elsewhere (cwd or `os.environ` mutated without monkeypatch) that random ordering exposes; noted, not hidden.

New/changed tests: plan-level (`test_plan_omp_*` × 6 incl. `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` following, wrong-suffix skip, missing `extension.ts` fail-closed), runner/drift (`test_omp_hook_bridge_*` × 14: link, idempotent, re-point, backup, skip, drift missing, wrapper for custom target / custom python / both transitions under `on_conflict=skip`, wrapper content change under skip, header pin), the acceptance-criterion tests `test_hook_bridge_gap_note_fires_without_explicit_enable` (+ its opt-out twin) and `test_status_reports_zero_hook_bridge_coverage_without_explicit_enable`. `test_explicit_hook_bridge_on_non_claude_kind_notes_skip` drops `omp` from its parametrize (omp now has a bridge).

## Verification — what was REAL vs SYNTHETIC

**Real** (sandboxed `$HOME`, throwaway repo with `harness: {kind: omp}`, `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE` = the agent-tools `feat/omp-hook-bridge` worktree, all live-daemon dry-run vars set):
- `rig apply commit --yes` → `✓ applied 41 action(s) (34 changed, 7 unchanged)`; on disk: `~/.omp/agent/extensions/zz-agent-tools-hook-bridge.ts` is a **symlink → `<agent-tools>/lib/omp_hook_bridge/extension.ts`**, sitting next to the untouched `rig-permissions-guard.ts`; `~/.omp/agent/hooks/` holds 28 descriptor JSONs.
- Second `rig apply commit` → `0 changed, 41 unchanged` (idempotent); `rig status` → `harness auto-mode + hook bridge: in sync`.
- `rig status` for `kind: pi` with **no** `hook_bridge` block → `⚠ hook_bridge: skipped — kind 'pi' has no supported agents-hooks bridge yet`; with `hook_bridge: {enabled: false}` → no note.
- Fail-closed against the **unmerged** primary agent-tools checkout → no action, actionable skip note (quoted above).

**Synthetic tool-call, real everything else** (the live-parity proof, acceptance criterion #4): a hand-written omp `tool_call` JSON piped into the **real** `python3 -m omp_hook_bridge tool_call` from the agent-tools worktree, reading the **real** descriptors that `rig apply commit` installed in the sandboxed `~/.omp/agent/hooks`:
- `bash` → `git reset --hard HEAD~1` → `{"decision": "block", "reason": "Refusing a \`git reset --hard\`…"}` (block-reset-hard).
- `edit` on the repo's default branch with `agent_hooks.worktree_only: true` → `{"decision": "block", "reason": "You are on the default branch (main) — the worktree-only workflow forbids authoring files here…"}` (worktree-only-writes — the exact rule the ticket names).

**Attempted, inconclusive:** a live `HOME=<sandbox> omp -p "…"` run failed before reaching any tool call on the sandbox's model config (`400 "bge-m3:latest" does not support chat`) — a model-selection problem in the sandbox, not the extension. Not blocking per the brief; reported as not proven.

## Review (review-cli, multi-model, several rounds; Opus / Codex / Sonnet; GLM seat 429'd each time)

Fixed here: `hook_bridge.python` silently ignored for omp (now forces the wrapper + `OMP_HOOK_BRIDGE_PYTHON`); explicit `hook_bridge.enabled: false` opt-out was dead code after the unconditional note (ordering fixed + test); symlink→wrapper, wrapper→symlink and wrapper-content-change transitions never converging under `on_conflict=skip` (rig-owned artifacts now always replaced; 3 tests); rig-ownership detection hardened from a copyable first line to full header+footer shape; `UnicodeDecodeError` escaping the `except OSError` on wrapper reads; a dead `_HARNESS_AGENT_HOOK_TARGETS["omp"]` entry (removed — second unenforced source of truth); a re-typed note literal in `_NOTE_ATTENTION_MARKERS` (removed — `"skipped"` already matches); inaccurate "never repo-local" docs/docstrings; `action_tags` description; a brittle test assertion.

Verified not bugs: `agent_hooks.enabled: false` short-circuits in `_build_hook_bridge` before the gap note (tested live); drift.py's local runner import mirrors `_check_opencode_hook_bridge`'s own pattern; `rig status` has no JSON mode and never routes notes through `_print_notes`, so no double print.

Deliberate / precedent (documented, not changed): the unconditional gap note is acceptance criterion #3 verbatim; `settings_path` is an unvalidated escape hatch for **every** kind (codex/opencode too) — an omp override outside `extensions/` would be inert, same as pointing codex's at a file codex never reads; only a symlink that *demonstrably* targets the bridge (the current `extension.ts`, or a prior checkout's `lib/omp_hook_bridge/extension.ts`) is re-pointed without honoring `on_conflict` — it carries no user data, like `link_skill_harness`; a **foreign** symlink (a user's own extension linked at the managed path) now goes through skip/backup like any foreign file, with the link itself preserved as a restorable `.rig-bak-*` under `backup` (addresses the Codex-connector P2 thread on this PR); a user-level harness config has last-apply-wins semantics across repos with differing `agent_hooks.target` (identical for codex's global `config.toml`); the TOCTOU between two *concurrent* `rig apply` runs is the codebase-wide single-writer assumption; wrapper installs don't hot-reload an updated checkout (identical to opencode's wrapper).

Follow-ups: **rig-cli#346** — dedupe the opencode/omp register+drift logic (~150 near-identical lines; opencode's own wrapper branch still has the `on_conflict=skip` transition gap fixed here for omp). Cross-repo: agent-tools' `dispatch.py::_omp_agent_root()` uses `os.path.expanduser` only while rig's `omp_agent_root()` also expands `$VAR` — a literal `$HOME` in `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` would diverge (reported to the agent-tools PR author; not fixable from this repo).

title: fix(worktree-gc): a pid that exits mid-scan is "not live", not "unknown"
body:
## What

`rig worktree gc` decides which worktrees are "live" (an agent is sitting in them) by running `pgrep` for agent pids, then one `lsof` per pid to read its working directory. When a pid exited between those two calls, the `lsof` failure was treated as "cannot verify" and the WHOLE snapshot degraded to "every worktree of this repo is live" — so gc refused to clean worktrees that were actually free because a process happened to exit during the scan.

Observed live (the gc implementer's own dry run over `~/xp`): 4 removable entries in one pass, 8 a few minutes later; the difference was exactly `gitapp` and `hyperos-handoff`, marked live by pids that were already dead.

## Fix

After an `lsof` failure the pid is probed with `os.kill(pid, 0)` (the POSIX existence check, sends nothing):

- `ProcessLookupError` (the process is gone) → not live, skip it, keep scanning.
- Anything else (probe succeeds, `PermissionError`, `lsof` missing, a zombie, a reused pid) → the previous fail-safe behaviour is kept unchanged: the whole snapshot is untrusted and every worktree is treated as live, with a sharper stderr reason ("matched pid N is still running but its cwd could not be determined").

The decision is fail-safe by construction: only a pid that PROVABLY no longer exists is downgraded; every uncertain outcome (including the pid-reuse race and an unreaped zombie, where signal 0 still succeeds) resolves toward "live" and never toward removal.

Stdlib-only at import time, as before.

## Tests

The old fail-closed test would have called the real `os.kill(123, 0)` after this change (host-dependent), so it is replaced by four hermetic tests that fake `os.kill` as a signal-0-only probe:

- vanished pid is skipped and the loop continues to record the live pid's cwd (two pids, so "skipped" is distinguishable from "returned early");
- live pid + `lsof` error still fails closed with the stderr warning;
- `lsof` missing (`OSError`) for a live pid fails closed;
- `PermissionError` from the probe fails closed.

Evidence (rebased onto `main` at effc1bf, 2026-09-06):

- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_worktree_gc.py` → 86 passed.
- `python3 -m pytest -q` → 3121 passed, 34 skipped, 8 failed. All 8 are pre-existing and unrelated: `tests/test_tmux_e2e_gating.py::test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` (a local `tests.test_tmux_e2e` import-path issue, fails identically on untouched `main`) and 7 `tests/test_tools.py::test_safe_codex_update_*` cases that use a 1-second `probe_timeout_s` against a fake shell script and time out when the machine is under load — the same family fails on the untouched `main` checkout in the same session (4 of them there, a different subset each run), so this is load-dependent flakiness, not this change.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` → smoke OK.

## Acceptance proof: a real dry run on this machine

`python3 bin/rig worktree gc --dry-run --repo /Users/ultra/xp/rig-cli` with THIS branch's code, while several agents were actively working in rig-cli worktrees (including the one authoring this PR). Zero "liveness check could not be verified" warnings on stderr; every worktree with a running agent process is classified `live`, and nothing is proposed for removal:

| worktree | branch | class | why | action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `~/xp/.worktrees/task-code-format-config` | `feat/task-code-format-config` | **active** | PR #217 open | kept |
| `~/xp/rig-cli-worktrees/308-readme-ecosystem-block` | `feat/308-readme-ecosystem-block` | **dirty** | dirty: 12 changed file(s) | kept |
| `~/xp/rig-cli-worktrees/ecosystem-readme-308` | `feat/308-ecosystem-readme-block` | **dirty** | dirty: 18 changed file(s) | kept |

No blocking findings; verdicts CLEAN. Sonnet's two minor notes: (a) the trailing `return False` in `_pid_vanished` could be folded into the `except OSError` arm — declined, behaviour-identical and a diff edit would invalidate the diff-bound review record for a style nit; (b) audit that no pre-existing test reaches the real `os.kill` — done: the only tests whose fake `pgrep` returns a pid are the four new ones, and each patches `worktree_gc.os.kill`; the three older `_live_process_cwds` tests all return an empty `pgrep` and never reach the probe.

title: feat(status): report provenance-known items as informational, not drift (#357)
body:
## What

`rig status` scans the machine-wide targets (`~/.agents/skills`, `~/.claude/hooks`, `.github/workflows`, the MCP registry) and reported every undeclared item as drift, so a freshly applied reference machine printed 48 disk→config drift lines — a newcomer reads that as "the install is broken". This teaches `rig status` **provenance**: an undeclared item whose origin rig can name is filed as a *known* item (informational, never counted, never touching the exit code); an item it cannot place stays drift.

New module `riglib/provenance.py` (the classification, documented in `docs/config-schema.md#provenance`):

| item | known when | otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| skill with a **catalog** name | `skills.known`, or byte-identical to the catalog source (another repo's by-type/by-stack apply) | drift (stale/foreign copy under a catalog name) |
| any other skill | `.installed-by` marker → `.blurbs/<name>.md` → the `skills` CLI lockfile (`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`) → shipped ecosystem allowlist → `skills.known` | drift (unknown origin) |
| hook descriptor with a **catalog** id | `agent_hooks.known`, or its `cmd` runs a script inside that catalog hook's dir | drift |
| any other hook descriptor | `installed_by` key → agent-tools ops-installer list → `agent_hooks.known` | drift |
| CI workflow | `ci.known`, or a stem that is not a catalog slot (the repo's own workflow) | drift (undeclared catalog gate) |
| MCP server | `mcp.known` | drift |
| permission entry beyond the baseline | always "kept", origin named (former rig defaults `gh`/`git`/`uv`/`bun` from #41→#165, a disabled baseline rule, a hand-added entry) | — |

- `<category>.known` is a new schema key for `skills` / `agent_hooks` / `ci` / `mcp` (registry, JSON schema, validator, docs). This also unblocks #365: the global config on the reference machine already declares `skills.known` and rig 0.34.1 refused to load it.
- `rig install-skill` writes the `.installed-by` marker (rig dogfoods the contract it asks the ecosystem installers to follow — umbrella: agent-tools#562).
- `rig status` prints known items under two dim headings (`known, not managed by rig` / `your additions, kept`), one line per origin group, names capped at 12; the config-web drift panel renders the same groups.
- rig-cli's own `rig.yaml` declares `stack: backend/python` so status stops nagging.

## Before / after on the reference machine

**Literal current state** (rig 0.34.1, real global config): every rig command fails — `error: unknown skills key: known` (#365).

**With the `skills.known` block stripped so 0.34.1 loads** (rig 0.34.1 in the rig-cli checkout; the run used an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` copy of the global config, so the config→disk section of that run is the override's artifact and is omitted — the disk→config section is the machine):

```
      skills: drift (43 on-disk-not-declared)
      agent-hooks (v1 descriptors): drift (1 on-disk-not-declared)
      harness permissions (allow / deny / ask): drift (3 on-disk-not-declared)
      CI gates: drift (1 on-disk-not-declared)
    disk→config drift (47) — on disk, not declared:
      ▸ permissions/claude-code: 153 entries in permissions.allow beyond the rig-managed baseline …
      ▸ permissions/claude-code: 'Bash(rg --pre*)' in permissions.deny but not in the rig-managed baseline …
      ▸ permissions/claude-code: 'Bash(rg * --pre*)' in permissions.deny but not in the rig-managed baseline …
      ▸ agent_hooks/agent-browser-session-claim.pre-bash: hook descriptor on disk but not declared in config …
      ▸ skills/<43 lines> …
    disk→config drift (1) — on disk, not declared:
      ▸ ci/ci: workflow on disk but not declared in config
```

**This branch** (`python3 bin/rig status` in the worktree, real global config, exit 3 only for config→disk items `rig apply commit` converges):

```
      skills: in sync  (43 known, not rig-managed)
      agent-hooks (v1 descriptors): in sync  (1 known, not rig-managed)
      harness permissions (allow / deny / ask): in sync  (9 your additions, kept)
      CI gates: drift (5 declared-but-missing/modified)  (1 known, not rig-managed)

  GLOBAL — machine-wide (from ~/.config/rig/config.yaml)
    known, not managed by rig (44) — informational, not drift:
      ▸ skills (5) installed by the `skills` CLI (`npx skills add`; recorded in .skill-lock.json): agent-browser (by vercel-labs/agent-browser), vercel-composition-patterns (by vercel-labs/agent-skills), …
      ▸ skills (25) declared known in your config (skills.known in /Users/ultra/.config/rig/config.yaml): audit-xcode-security-settings, c-bounds-safety, … and 13 more
      ▸ skills (2) ecosystem tool skills (shipped allowlist; the tool wrote no marker yet): daily, rig
      ▸ skills (7) installed by their own tool's `install-skill` (marker present): dev, draw, research, review, stt, task, tg
      ▸ skills (4) rig catalog items not selected by this repo's config (installed by rig for another repo's type/stack, or disabled since) — remove by hand if unwanted: parallelize-independent (by rig), squash-merge-cleanup (by rig), subagent-handoff-contract (by rig), worktree-isolation (by rig)
      ▸ agent_hooks (1) written by an agent-tools ops installer (not via the rig catalog): agent-browser-session-claim.pre-bash (by agent-tools)
    your additions, kept (9) — beyond the rig baseline; rig never removes them:
      ▸ claude-code:permissions.allow (3) former rig defaults (rig-cli#41, dropped in #165), kept: Bash(git:*), Bash(uv:*), Bash(bun:*)
      ▸ claude-code:permissions.deny (2) your own entries beyond the rig baseline, kept: Bash(rg --pre*), Bash(rg * --pre*)
      ▸ opencode:permission.bash (4) former rig defaults (rig-cli#41, dropped in #165), kept: gh *, git *, uv *, bun *

  REPO — this repository (from ./rig.yaml)
    known, not managed by rig (1) — informational, not drift:
      ▸ ci (1) this repository's own workflows (not rig catalog gates): ci.yml
```

The remaining `CI gates: drift (5 declared-but-missing/modified)` is the committed-workflow-vs-catalog-source question, handled separately in the `ci-catalog-sync` worktree — deliberately not touched here.

## Decisions worth a second look

- The two hand-added deny forms `Bash(rg --pre*)` / `Bash(rg * --pre*)` are NOT adopted into the baseline: the baseline already carries the five precise forms from #211, and `permissions.py` documents why `--pre-glob`/`--pretty` are deliberately not globbed. They are reported as kept additions; prune by hand if unwanted. The sibling exec vectors (`--hostname-bin`, `-z`) stay tracked in #279.
- `git`/`uv`/`bun` (claude-code allow) and `gh`/`git`/`uv`/`bun` (opencode `permission.bash`) are reported as former rig defaults, kept — not adopted into `permissions.allow` and not pruned. Adopting them would re-grant what #165 deliberately dropped; pruning live allow entries is Alex's call.
- Permission extras have no unknown-origin→drift path any more (review finding): before this branch allow extras were ONE summarized count line, so a rogue appended entry was invisible there too; a rogue deny/ask entry only tightens policy. The baseline rig asserts (missing/modified entries) stays drift.
- `<category>.known` lists cascade like every list (a repo list replaces the global one), so machine-wide lists belong in the global config — documented, no union semantics added.

## Tests

`tests/test_provenance.py` (new, hermetic: fake agent-tools + tmp HOME) pins every acceptance point of #357: marker / blurb / lockfile / allowlist / `skills.known` skills are known; an unknown-origin skill, a catalog-named skill with foreign content, an undeclared catalog gate workflow, an unknown hook and a catalog hook id with a foreign `cmd` stay drift; the rig-managed `rg --pre` deny baseline never shows as an extra; user deny/allow extras render as kept; known items never affect `in_sync`; `rig install-skill` writes the marker; the config-web payload lists known items and stays in sync. Plus: `test_agent_hooks_known_by_full_stem_leaves_the_sibling_point_as_drift`, `test_page_known_panel_groups_caps_and_escapes`.

- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3177 passed; the one failure (`test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned`) fails identically on `main`.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast`: OK.
- `review task GH-357 --check --min-roles 3`: passed (4 roles).

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/357
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/365
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/562

title: feat(harness): write the auto/permission mode for codex, opencode and omp, not only claude-code
body:
## What

Every configured harness kind now gets its own auto/permission-mode key written by `rig apply`, through the same reconciler path claude-code always had: `harness.kind` + `harness.kinds` → `plan.build` (one `apply_harness` action per kind) → `run_plan`, writing only the managed key into the harness's own config file, idempotent + backup-on-conflict, drift surfaced by `rig status`.

Closes gap 1 of the second-class-harness catalog: https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/337 — the feature ticket is https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/355.

## The registry (one entry per kind — `riglib/harness_mode.py`)

| Kind | File | Key | auto | interactive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| claude-code | `~/.claude/settings.json` | `permissions.defaultMode` | `auto` | `default` |
| codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | `approvals_reviewer` (root key, TOML edited as text before the first table) | `auto_review` | `user` |
| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `permission."*"` | `allow` | `ask` |
| omp | `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` | `tools.approvalMode` — written by the existing guard-interlocked permissions approval action (one owner of the key); its value now follows the harness auto intent | `yolo` | `always-ask` |
| pi, commandcode | — | n/a (no documented approval setting) — recorded with the reason, printed as a visible plan note and a `rig status` line, never a silent skip | — | — |

The auto intent is a pinned `mode:` the primary kind knows (it is the exact value claude-code has always written verbatim, overriding `auto_mode`, so every kind follows the same precedence), else `harness.auto_mode` — so the live global config (`kind: claude-code, kinds: [codex, opencode, pi, omp], mode: auto`) means auto for codex and opencode too. A `mode:` string the primary kind does not know declares no intent for the other kinds: nothing is written for them (a claude-code primary still writes its own `mode:` verbatim), an elevated note names the real values, and every affected kind is listed as "not written" on `rig status`. An undeclared intent leaves an additive kind untouched (a skills-only `kinds: [opencode]` must not get its posture changed behind the user's back).

omp convergence fix on the way: the approval action used to treat ANY differing on-disk value as a user conflict — so after rig wrote `yolo`, flipping to `auto_mode: false` never re-enabled prompts. A value rig itself installed (per its receipt) is now rig-owned and converged; a user-set value is still left untouched with drift visible.

codex: rig deliberately does not touch `approval_policy` / `sandbox_mode` — `approval_policy = "never"` auto-rejects escalations (network, outside the workspace), so `gh`/`git push`/`tg` would fail fast under the default sandbox.

`rig status` gains a `harness auto-mode per kind` block naming key/file/value per kind.

## Migration note (0.34 → 0.35)

A config that already lists `kinds: [codex, opencode]` with `auto_mode: true` / `mode: auto` used to get only a "write skipped" note; the first `rig apply commit` on 0.35 now writes `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"` and `permission."*": "allow"` into the user-scope harness files (backed up under the default `on_conflict: backup`). `rig apply info` shows the actions before anything mutates.

## Also in this PR

- The flaky codex safe-update tests (`tests/test_tools.py::test_safe_codex_update_*`, `tests/test_cli.py::test_codex_update_cli_missing_updater_returns_127`) were load-dependent: a sub-second probe budget raced three process spawns against a fake shell script. Hanging fakes now short-circuit through an `instant_hang` fixture (a sentinel line on the fake) and the CLI test stubs the probe; the budget is a 30 s hang guard only.

## Review

`review task GH-355 --check --min-roles 3` passes (architect, consistency, correctness, quality; 4 distinct models across the rounds). Findings from the two staged rounds were applied before commit: the intent is resolved once in `_build_harness` and handed to the per-kind builders (no contradictory "not declared" notes on an unknown `mode:`, for a claude-code primary too); an additive `kinds: [pi]` next to `auto_mode: true` is informational instead of an attention item on every apply; a known pinned `mode:` wins over `auto_mode` for every kind (claude-code's existing precedence, so `auto_mode: false, mode: auto` no longer leaves claude-code auto and codex interactive); the omp approval action converges a value rig itself installed; the codex TOML validity check falls back to the `tomli` backport on Python 3.10 before running unvalidated (as the existing hook-bridge TOML merge does — `tomli` is a test extra, not a runtime dependency, on purpose).

Known, deliberately left: `rig status` rows for note-only kinds are recovered from the plan notes (a structured per-kind plan field is the cleaner follow-up).

Pre-existing on `main`, not from this branch: `tests/test_tmux_e2e_gating.py::test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned` fails locally under Python 3.14 (`No module named 'tests.test_tmux_e2e'`) at `b5e3acc` too.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q` — 3184 passed, 1 failed (the pre-existing tmux-gating failure above), 34 skipped
- [x] `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — OK
- [ ] post-merge on this machine: `rig apply info` shows the new `apply_harness` actions, `rig apply commit --yes`, the managed key in each harness file, `rig status` in sync, a second apply reports 0 changed

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/355, https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/337

## Gate-review follow-ups (9b7d637 + the hardening commit after it)

- **A primary kind's own pinned `harness.mode` is written verbatim.** `kind: opencode, mode: deny` stays `deny` (it used to be reduced to the boolean intent and relaxed to `ask`); `kind: omp, mode: write` stays `write`. Additive kinds still get the mapped intent value only — the primary's string is harness-specific.
- **No TOML parser (Python 3.10 without `tomli`) fails closed for codex**, for an existing AND an absent `config.toml`: nothing is written or created, and both the apply error and `rig status` name the `pip install tomli` remedy.
- **omp drift is receipt-aware**, like the writer: a value rig itself installed reads "rig-installed; config now declares X — apply converges it; on_conflict=skip leaves it", the "never clobbers — change it by hand" wording is kept for a genuinely user-set value.
- **The approval receipt keeps the original pre-rig `previous` and `backup`** across a convergence (a deprovision must restore what the user had, never rig's own intermediate `yolo`).
- **The guard interlock gates only a RELAXING write** (anything short of `always-ask`, so `write` too); tightening back to `always-ask` goes through with the guard belt missing — a user who removed the guard is no longer stuck in yolo.
- **`rig status` renders an unknown `harness.mode` containing ` — ` intact** (the row is sliced on the note's known suffix, never split on the delimiter).
- **An object/array under a JSON mode key is a conflict left untouched**, matching the TOML inline-table contract.

title: fix(schema): route the machine-wide known-lists to the GLOBAL layer per option
body:
## What

The option registry (`riglib/schema.py`) gains a per-option writable-layer override (`Option.layer_override`, validated to GLOBAL/REPO; `Option.layer` honours it; `Area.options_for_layer()` splits a mixed area). The three machine-wide known-lists — `skills.known`, `agent_hooks.known`, `mcp.known` — are marked GLOBAL inside their otherwise repo-writable areas; `ci.known` stays REPO.

Every editing surface now routes by the OPTION's layer, not only the area's:

- **config-web**: the Global tab renders every GLOBAL-writable *option* (`_area_view`), so skills / agent-hooks / MCP appear there with only their `.known` field, badged GLOBAL; a repo tab keeps every field with its own layer badge. Edit routing (`_target_path`, `handle_edit`'s Global-scope guard) already went through `option.layer`, so a `skills.known` edit from any tab now writes `~/.config/rig/config.yaml`.
- **`rig setup` wizard**: the write path already used `opt.layer`; `render_state` now tags an option whose layer differs from its area (`known … [GLOBAL]`) so the user sees where the edit lands.
- **`rig config set <key>`** without `--global` refuses a GLOBAL-layer option the same way it refuses a global-only block (`_global_layer_refusal`, one helper deciding both the gate and its wording), so the three editors never disagree.
- docs: `docs/config-schema.md` provenance section + the three `known` rows.

Review findings addressed across three recorded iterations (GH-372): Opus's missing tests (`config set --global` round trip; a repo-scope `handle_edit` of `skills.known` routes to the global file; the full Global-tab page render with the now-mixed areas); Sonnet's quality items (explicit `is not None` in `Option.layer`, `layer_override` kwarg name, one message-returning gate helper in `config set`, write-path tests parametrized over all three keys); Codex's P1 on `mcp.known` (next paragraph) and its P2 on the concurrent unlocked read-modify-write of the global file, which is pre-existing for every global-only key (`tg_ctl`, `tmux`, `mode`) and is tracked separately as #376. Codex's iteration-3 P1 — a Global-tab edit rolls back when no agent-tools source resolves from the global-only config (the tab anchors at `$HOME` with the repo layer off, a deliberate #318 choice) — is likewise pre-existing for every Global-tab option (the pre-existing Global-scope tests on main already set `RIG_AGENT_TOOLS_SOURCE` for that reason) and is tracked as #377; the repo-tab edit of the same field uses the repo's cascade and is unaffected.

Codex P1 (iteration 1) argued `mcp.known` should stay REPO because `mcp.target` can be pinned per repo. Kept GLOBAL per the ticket: the default MCP target (`~/.claude/mcp`) is machine-wide and `rig status` groups `mcp` GLOBAL; the cascade exposure it describes exists on main whenever the list sits in the global config (the documented remedy), independent of which editor wrote it. The escape hatch for a repo with its own repo-local target — a hand-committed repo-level `mcp.known` REPLACES the global list for that repo — is now documented in the option hint + config-schema.md and pinned by `test_hand_committed_repo_known_list_replaces_global_for_that_repo`.

Deliberately NOT changed: the Global tab's plan and drift panel stay restricted to the global-only *categories* (`build_scope_plan` / `compute_scope_drift`). A known-list edit changes what is *known*, not what is applied, and widening the Global drift scan to the skills/hooks/MCP dirs would flood that tab with every repo-tab-installed item (the reason that restriction exists). The provenance effect is visible on each repo tab's drift panel. Also not changed: a list ALREADY committed in a repo `rig.yaml` keeps shadowing the global one until removed by hand — rig never migrates or deletes config (documented). Per the PR review thread on this (Codex P2): the repo tab now flags such a field as **shadowed** (`FieldView.shadowed_by`, the repo file + its value, with the reason an edit lands in the global file and takes effect only once the repo entry is removed), and the `rig setup` wizard prints the same note before prompting — so the edit never looks like a silent no-op.

## Why

PR #369 added the four `KIND_LIST` known options, which inherited category-level REPO routing from `writable_layer_for_category`. Codex (P2, review iteration 11 on GH-357) found that `rig setup` and the config-web therefore wrote a machine-specific list into the committed repo `rig.yaml`; the list cascade REPLACES the global list, so a globally declared known skill (e.g. `swiftui-pro`) re-surfaced as drift for that repo, and the config-web Global tab could not even show the option (it rendered whole GLOBAL-writable areas only).

Refs #372

## Tests

TDD red-first: 12 new tests failed before the fix; 25 new tests in total after the review rounds, all green.

- `tests/test_setup_wizard.py`: registry routing (`skills/agent_hooks/mcp.known` → GLOBAL, area + `ci.known` stay REPO), override validation, `options_for_layer`, `render_state` per-option tag, the hermetic ticket scenario (global `skills.known: [swiftui-pro]` + a wizard edit → global file updated, repo file has no list, `known_names_from_config` for the repo still carries `swiftui-pro`), `ci.known` lands in the repo file, the hand-committed repo-level `mcp.known` escape hatch.
- `tests/test_config_web.py`: Global tab shows exactly the three `.known` fields (GLOBAL-badged), repo tab tags `skills.known` GLOBAL inside the REPO area, the hermetic scenario end to end through `apply_edit` → `plan.build` → `drift.detect` (planted `swiftui-pro` is KNOWN, not extra), all three lists parametrized through `apply_edit` and a repo-scope `handle_edit`, `ci.known` stays repo, Global-scope `handle_edit` accepts `skills.known` and still refuses `skills.enabled` / `ci.known`, the full Global-tab page + tab-switch fragment render through the real template.
- `tests/test_config_getset.py`: `config set skills.known|agent_hooks.known|mcp.known` without `--global` exits 2; `--global` round-trips into the global file; `config set ci.known` is repo-local.

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/382
Depends on https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/396 (`review install-commit-hook --print-gate`) — merge that first.

## Problem

The dispatcher's `review-gate` composer was copied verbatim from agent-tools like every other composer, but its real owner is review-cli. The two copies forked (review-cli#211's trivial-delta tolerance never reached the installed gate), and `rig status` reported the stale installed gate as CLEAN because it was compared against the stale source.

## Change

- `riglib/review_gate.py` is the seam: asks the installed review-cli for the gate body (`review install-commit-hook --print-gate`), falls back to the agent-tools copy with a reason that lands in the action detail and the drift item text (review not installed / predates `--print-gate` / timed out).
- `rig apply commit` installs the composers per file; `review-gate` comes from review-cli when it answers.
- `rig status` compares the installed `review-gate` against the same source, so a gate that only equals the agent-tools copy is now drift ("differs from review-cli's --print-gate output") and a re-apply converges it.
- Test seam `RIG_REVIEW_BIN` (empty = disabled; the unit suite sets it autouse so no test ever shells out to a real `review`).

## Tests

`tests/test_review_gate_source.py`: resolver seam (which / override / disabled), every fallback class, apply from review-cli + idempotency + upgrade from the stale copy with backup, drift against review-cli / against source / missing.

title: fix(spotlight): one coverage predicate for apply, verify and status; working re-sweep agent argv
body:
## What

`rig apply commit --yes` reported `0 changed` and its verify line said `20/20 sampled matched dirs carry .metadata_never_index`, while `rig status` a second later said `65/2500 dependency/build dirs lack .metadata_never_index`. Two independent defects behind it, both fixed here.

### 1. Verify sampled 20 dirs; status scanned all of them; nothing could tell "new since the sweep" from "the sweep missed it"

- `spotlight.scan_coverage` is now the ONE read-back predicate for the post-apply verify step and `rig status` drift. Both check EVERY matched dir (the directory walk was already the whole cost — ~10 s for ~2600 dirs on the reference machine, unchanged; classifying each dir is one extra `stat`).
- Every sweep records which dirs it visited AND the selector it swept with — roots, denylist, max depth — (`~/.cache/rig/spotlight-last-sweep.json`, atomic write). A record made for a different selector (a `.venv` newly added to `deny` without an apply), or one of the wrong JSON shape, reads as "never swept" — strict, never permissive (review round 1 caught the roots-only keying). An uncovered dir the last sweep VISITED is **stale** — real drift, fails verify. An uncovered dir the sweep never saw is **pending** — it appeared afterwards (every `pytest` run mints `__pycache__` dirs) and is an informational note printed dim beside "in sync", never counted, never in the exit code. With no usable record everything uncovered is stale.
- The record stores each visited dir's filesystem identity (device + inode), captured at the visit — so `rm -rf dist && mkdir dist` after the sweep is a NEW dir (new inode → pending), while the same inode with no sentinel is the hand-deleted case (stale). Identity, not a filesystem timestamp, decides the split: `st_birthtime` only exists on macOS/BSD, and elsewhere deleting the sentinel out of a dir bumps its ctime, which would excuse exactly the hand-deleted-sentinel case.
- `rig status`, the config-web drift panel and the JSON scope drift all carry the notes (`DriftNote`), so no surface silently drops them. The note shows the age of the last sweep, so a loaded-but-failing re-sweep agent is visible.

### 2. The daily launchd re-sweep agent never worked on a checkout install

The plist argv was `<python> -m riglib spotlight-sweep`, which assumes a pip-editable install. With the symlink-shim install (`~/.local/bin/rig` → `<checkout>/bin/rig`) launchd runs from `/` with no `PYTHONPATH`, so all 9 runs on the reference machine died with `No module named riglib` — an 18-day-old `node_modules` recreated nightly by a mirror job stayed uncovered because the only sweep that ever ran was the one inside `rig apply`. `default_sweep_cmd` now runs `<checkout>/bin/rig` when that shim exists beside `riglib`, and falls back to `-m riglib` for a pip/pipx install. The plist content changes, so the next `rig apply commit` honestly rewrites and reloads it (and `RunAtLoad` fires a real sweep immediately).

## Tests

Hermetic (tmp HOME): no record → everything stale; stale vs pending split; hand-deleted sentinel is stale; record ignored for other roots / order-insensitive / corrupt; apply marks all 25 unmarked dirs and a second apply changes nothing; status agrees with apply right after it; drift names the stale count; a never-seen dir is a note, not drift; verify checks every dir (fails on the 26th) and passes with a note for pending; the note renders beside "in sync"; sweep argv shim vs module form; `describe_age`.

- `python3 -m pytest -q` — 3275 passed, 34 skipped (one pre-existing, unrelated failure also on main: `test_tmux_e2e_gating_granularity_is_pinned`, `No module named 'tests.test_tmux_e2e'`)
- `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — OK

This scaffold intentionally does not decide the following — they need a decision before

title: feat(github): manage require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes, mode-gated
body:
## Summary

- rig now declaratively manages GitHub's `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` ruleset knob through the existing `github.ruleset` engine, instead of requiring a one-off manual `gh api ... -X PUT` per repo.
- This knob has **no unconditional default**: it is only defaulted to `false` for a repo whose *effective* `mode.name` is `autonomous` (a machine-wide, cascaded setting — `mode` is a GLOBAL-only category rejected from a committed per-repo `rig.yaml`). A non-autonomous repo is never touched; an explicit `github.ruleset.require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` in a repo's own config always wins over the mode-gated default.
- A ruleset update PUT replaces the entire `pull_request` rule's parameters, so an unrelated knob drifting would otherwise silently reset an unmanaged live value to GitHub's platform default. `carry_over_unattributed_approval` preserves the live-fetched value across such a PUT when the knob is unmanaged.
- `rig status` surfaces drift via the existing shared `github_ruleset_state` classification — no changes needed in `drift.py`.
- The setup wizard / config-web never claim to know the live GitHub value for an unmanaged repo: `schema.effective_value` returns an `UNMANAGED` sentinel instead of a hardcoded `False`.

## Important caveat — the exact mechanism was not independently confirmed

GitHub's own documentation scopes this rule to a PR **opened under an app identity not attributed to a person** (the documented example is the Copilot coding agent), not to "any commit an agent authored inside an otherwise human-opened PR." Checking agent-tools directly: its recent merges are all attributed to the human login `alex-mextner`, and the ruleset's rule-suites evaluation log shows zero failed pushes in the last 30 days. So I could not confirm from available evidence exactly why this rule fired and blocked `gh ship`'s merge there. What is confirmed: the rule was found **ON** (`true`), it was hand-patched to `false` via a raw `gh api` PUT on 2026-09-07 as an emergency stopgap, and that stopgap is now durable/reconcilable through this change regardless of the precise causal mechanism.

## Known follow-up (not blocking)

The config-web admin console (a secondary surface, not `rig apply`/`rig status`) renders this field as a plain checkbox, which can't fully express the tri-state unmanaged/true/false semantics — an "unmanaged" badge/hint is now shown so it never silently reads as "off", but toggling from unmanaged to an explicit `false` still requires two clicks (on then off), and the badge doesn't clear until page reload after a successful edit. Low severity (config-web edits only write `rig.yaml`; nothing reaches GitHub without a separate, explicit `rig apply` step with its own plan preview) — worth a follow-up ticket for a real tri-state control.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 3301 passed, 34 skipped (2 pre-existing unrelated ANSI-color failures on this machine confirmed on untouched `main`, deselected)
- [x] `bash tests/smoke.sh --fast` — OK
- [x] `rig schema --check` — in sync
- [x] Live verification: `rig status` on this repo now correctly flags `alex-mextner/rig-cli`'s own ruleset as drifted (its live `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` is currently `true`)
- [x] New tests cover: no drift when in sync, a PUT firing on drift with the corrected value asserted in the payload, `mode: autonomous` gating on/off, idempotent re-apply, the unmanaged-value carry-over across an unrelated PUT, and the `UNMANAGED` display sentinel in the wizard/config-web

title: feat(permissions): deny EnterWorktree and raw git worktree add
body:
## Summary

Ban Claude Code `EnterWorktree` (and raw `git worktree add`) in favor of `rig worktree create`.

`EnterWorktree` can itself create a worktree at a model-supplied path, which is the location-bypass `rig worktree create` exists to close. A whole-tool deny in the baked `permissions.deny` baseline means `rig apply` provisions it with no config, re-apply is a no-op, and `rig status` flags a missing entry as drift — so the tool never prompts (it is refused).

The Bash counterpart is the prefix deny `Bash(git worktree add:*)` (plus opencode / omp / Codex renderings of the same intent). The child `git worktree add` inside `rig worktree create` is not a gated tool call, so the sanctioned path still works (same pattern as `gh ship` vs `gh pr merge`).

Prefix-only on purpose: `git -C` / `--git-dir` forms do not match. A mid-pattern would also match a commit message that mentions "worktree add". That argv-precise backstop belongs in https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/610 (`block-raw-worktree-add`), which stays unmerged.

The original EnterWorktree friction ticket asked for a path-scoped allow; this PR takes the deny path instead.

## Tests

- plan emits `EnterWorktree` and `Bash(git worktree add:*)` in `deny_rules`
- apply writes them; re-apply is a no-op
- `rig status` / drift names a missing `EnterWorktree` deny as missing
- omp / opencode / Codex belts carry the shared `git worktree add` intent

title: feat(bun): splice isolated linker + globalStore into ~/.bunfig.toml
body:
## Why

Worktree-heavy agent work multiplies `node_modules` by N. bun's default (hoisted, `globalStore` off) clonefile-copies into every tree. bun's global virtual store only applies with the isolated linker — `globalStore` alone is a no-op.

`rig apply` now splices **both** keys into `~/.bunfig.toml` when `bun.enabled` is true (GLOBAL-only, default OFF):

```toml
[install]
linker = "isolated"
globalStore = true
```

## uv (out of scope to provision)

uv already uses a global cache (`~/.cache/uv`). macOS default link-mode is clone (APFS CoW; `nlink=1` so `du` still looks like copies). `link-mode = hardlink` in `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` shares inodes. This PR does **not** provision `uv.toml`.

## Inode-sharing proof

Throwaway bun projects (not this Python repo), bun 1.4.1-canary.1, project `bunfig.toml` with `linker = "isolated"` + `globalStore = true`, deps `ms@2.1.3` + `picocolors@1.1.1`:

| | proj-a | proj-b |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `du -sh node_modules` | **0B** (symlink tree) | **0B** |
| `du -shL node_modules` (follow) | 132K | 132K |
| `find -type l` | 6 | 6 |

Shared realpaths (same inode):

- `ms` → `~/.bun/install/cache/links/ms@2.1.3-c0b1531a62e8680e/node_modules/ms` inode=`636274660` nlink=`6`
- `picocolors` → `~/.bun/install/cache/links/picocolors@1.1.1-7a85ff629f303704/node_modules/picocolors` inode=`636274665` nlink=`9`

Store dirs `nlink=3` (two projects + store). `du -sh ~/.bun/install/cache/links` = 84K.

Throwaway cleaned up.

## Tests

`python -m pytest tests/test_bunfig.py` — 26 passed.

## Refs

https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/416

omp helpers that yield stay idle on the live roster until process exit (or a positive user TTL). Parent must still confirm live proof before ticking done.

title: feat(permissions): deny osascript/System Events across all guard belts
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/489

## Problem

Alex kept getting macOS "bash would like to access data from other apps" TCC prompts. Root-caused by a scout investigation (history://FindTccPrompterSource): `~/.files/bin/vscmd` (a personal script actively invoked by Claude Code / omp subagents to reload/command VS Code and Cursor) uses `osascript` + `tell application "System Events"` to send keystrokes. Secondary/tertiary triggers exist too (`git-worktree-runner`'s terminal-tab detection, the iMessage MCP plugin's outbound-message osascript call), but none of that matters to *this* fix -- the fix is generic: nothing in this repo's agent-issued bash surface has a legitimate reason to invoke `osascript` directly, and the existing `rig-permissions-guard.ts` (and its sibling belts) simply had no rule for it.

## Fix

Add an `osascript` deny rule to the **single structured rule registry** (`riglib/permissions.py`) that already backs this repo's four permission belts -- following the exact precedent set by the pre-existing `screencapture` rule (same class: a TCC-gated macOS primitive with a documented non-TCC alternative, no legitimate direct-bash use case in this ecosystem). Because it's registry-driven, `rig apply` reproduces it on any machine, not just this checkout:

- `OMP_GUARD_DENY_RULES` -> generated `~/.omp/agent/extensions/rig-permissions-guard.ts` (omp's `tool_call` hook -- ARGV-precise, blocks the bash command **before** it ever reaches the OS, which is the layer that actually stops the TCC prompt for omp sessions).
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DENY_RULES` -> `permissions.deny: ["Bash(osascript:*)"]`.
- `OPENCODE_DENY_RULES` -> `permission.bash: {"osascript*": "deny"}`.
- `CODEX_DENY_RULES` -> `~/.codex/rules/*.rules` coarse `forbidden` prefix rule.

Docs (`docs/config-schema.md`, `rig.yaml`, `riglib/schema.py` wizard hint) updated to name the new rule alongside `screencapture` everywhere the existing baseline is described. `pyproject.toml` bumped 0.40.1 -> 0.41.0 (minor: additive feature).

## Does this fully stop the prompt?

For the **bash-tool** path (the PRIMARY vscmd trigger): yes, unconditionally -- once `rig apply` regenerates the guard on a machine, `osascript ...` run via the omp/claude-code/opencode/codex agent bash surface is denied outright, no exceptions, no hatch. There is deliberately **no** allow-list/ask-tier escape hatch for this rule (matching `screencapture`, not `pkill`/`git reset --hard`): the investigation found zero legitimate direct-bash use of `osascript` anywhere in this ecosystem's own tooling, so a hard deny carries no false-positive cost. If a genuine future need for one-time osascript access ever arises, the existing `ask`-tier mechanism is the right shape for it (confirm-gated via harness UI, blocks headless) -- but that's a deliberate follow-up, not silently smuggled into this deny rule.

Two things stay **out of scope** for this PR, flagged for follow-up rather than silently left broken:

1. **vscmd itself loses this capability** (its System-Events keystroke-injection path now hits the deny and gets a clear guard-reason error, not a silent hang) -- it should migrate to a non-AppleScript control channel, e.g. VS Code's own `code --command <id>` CLI or an IPC/socket-based remote-control extension, instead of simulated keystrokes. Not attempted here per the assignment ("stop the prompt", not "preserve every vscmd feature").
2. **The `eval`-tool escape hatch**: a sibling investigation (FixBunTccPrompts) found the omp guard's `tool_call` handler only inspects `toolName === "bash"`, so an `eval`-tool code cell that shells out to `osascript` directly (e.g. via `child_process.execSync`) is NOT caught by this rule. title: feat(tmux): generalize exact-id session-resume to omp and Codex CLI
body:
## Summary
User report: omp/codex tmux sessions don't restore after reboot; only Claude Code (cc-restore) had exact-id resume. This generalizes cc-restore to omp and Codex CLI, both of which DO support resuming an exact prior session (verified via `omp --help`/`codex resume --help` on this machine — see investigation notes below).

## Investigation (ground truth, not assumption)
- `omp --help`: `-r, --resume=<value>  Resume a session (by ID prefix, path, or picker if omitted)`. Session store: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl`, verified the slug is the cwd **relative to $HOME** with `/` -> `-` (dots preserved) — a live on-disk dir `-xp-review-cli-.worktrees-450-mimo-seat` proves it, different from Claude Code's full-path/dot-folding convention.
- `codex resume --help`: `codex resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]` (SESSION_ID is a UUID). Codex's session store is **not cwd-keyed on disk**: `~/.codex/sessions/<local-Y>/<local-M>/<local-D>/rollout-<local-ISO-ts>-<uuid>.jsonl`; cwd lives only in each file's first `session_meta` JSON line (verified against real rollout files on this machine).
- Both mechanisms are real and reliable, so this shipped as **full exact-id session-restore**, mirroring cc-restore, not the bare-`@resurrect-processes` fallback.

## Changes
- `riglib/tmux.py`: new `render_omp_save/restore` and `render_codex_save/restore` methods (mirroring `render_cc_save/restore`'s structure — process-tree BFS keyed on the harness's own executable-match pattern, session-id lookup from that harness's own store, exact `--resume`/`resume` relaunch into a FRESH shell pane only). Generalized the `@resurrect-hook-post-save-all`/`post-restore-all` wiring to **chain** every enabled harness's script into the single hook value (`cc-save.sh; omp-save.sh; codex-save.sh`, `eval`'d in sequence by tmux-resurrect) instead of one `set -g` clobbering another. Generalized the claude-only `@resurrect-processes` exemption to omp/codex too (same rationale, same regression guard).
- New config: `tmux.omp_restore.enabled` / `tmux.codex_restore.enabled` (both default `true`, mirroring `cc_restore`), threaded through `build_tmux()`/`TmuxPlan`, `riglib/plan.py`, `riglib/actions/runner.py`, `riglib/config.py` validation, `riglib/config_schema.py` (+ regenerated `schema/rig.schema.json`), `docs/config-schema.md`.
- claude's own behavior is byte-identical when omp/codex restore are off (regression-guarded by test).

## Tests
`tests/test_tmux.py` — ~60 new tests mirroring the existing cc_save/cc_restore coverage: config validation, resurrect-processes exemption (on/off, independently per harness), hook wiring/chaining (present when enabled, absent when disabled, exactly-one `set -g` per hook point), script rendering (shebang, process-tree match pattern, cwd encoding, resume/fallback commands, shell-quoting, fresh-shell-only skip logic), `managed_scripts()` presence/absence, idempotency across two `build_tmux()` calls, and a pre-upgrade `Action.options` replay defaulting to on.

Full suite: `3485 passed, 41 skipped` (10m local run).

## Live verification (isolated tmux server, NOT the real session)
- Every generated script passes `bash -n`.
- A real `tmux -L <private-socket>` server sources the generated `rig.tmux.conf` cleanly; `show-options -g` confirms the resurrect/continuum options AND the chained hook values (`cc-save.sh; omp-save.sh; codex-save.sh`) are exactly as designed.
- End-to-end with fake `omp`/`codex` processes (`exec -a <name> sleep 600` as direct children of real tmux panes) + real on-disk session-store fixtures: `omp-save.sh` correctly detected the pane, encoded its cwd, and picked the **newest** of two session files by mtime; `codex-save.sh` correctly scanned the local-date directory and matched cwd from the rollout's `session_meta` line. Repointing the map at a fresh pane and running `omp-restore.sh` typed the exact expected `cd <cwd> && omp --resume <path>` into it.
- Isolated server + sandbox HOME torn down after verification; the user's real tmux session/socket was never touched.

## Not fixed / known limitations (documented in code + docs)
- codex-save.sh bounds its session-store scan to the last 2 local-date directories (not the whole multi-GB store) — a cwd whose most recent codex session predates that window is missed. Documented tradeoff (unbounded scan on every periodic resurrect save is not acceptable).
- omp's cwd-encoding fallback for a cwd OUTSIDE `$HOME` is best-effort (full-path encoding) — omp's own out-of-`$HOME` slug convention wasn't directly confirmed (verification focused on the common in-`$HOME` case, which IS confirmed).
- `review diff` was unavailable for this PR — the entire configured reviewer board was quota/credit-exhausted at review time (GLM weekly limit hit, Grok out of credits, opencode idle-timeouts) — noted per this task's own fallback instruction rather than silently skipped.

## Coordination
TmuxMouseCopy (clipboard/copy-mode) and TmuxPtyErrors (launchd/pty) are landing sibling PRs touching overlapping files (`render_rig_conf`, `riglib/config.py`, `schema/rig.schema.json`, `docs/config-schema.md`) from their own worktrees concurrently — expect a manual rebase/sequential merge, not a clean 3-way auto-merge.

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/494

title: perf(stats): cache parsed session files to skip the full-corpus rescan every run
body:
## Problem
`rig stats show` re-reads, re-JSON-decodes, and re-categorizes (shlex-tokenizing every
shell command via `taxonomy.categorize`) **every session log file on the machine, from
every harness, on every single invocation** -- even though a harness session's log file
is append-only-then-frozen: once a session ends, its file never changes again.

cProfile on `rig stats show --format json` (stdout redirected to a file, to avoid
pipe-buffer skew from an unread stdout pipe):

```
42.8s total run
  41.4s command.collect()
    22.0s codex.py iter_invocations/_iter_session (146.7k session reads)
    13.7s taxonomy.categorize -> detect_our_cli -> _tokenize (275k calls, ~1.9M shlex tokens)
    11.3s omp.py iter_invocations/_iter_session (123k session reads)
     7.8s claude_code.py iter_invocations/_iter_session (10.9k session files)
    10.2s json.loads (1.56M JSONL lines decoded)
```

This is a genuine "full corpus scan" repeated from scratch on every run: nothing is
cached between invocations, so a machine that's been running agents for months (275k+
historical invocations here) pays the full O(all-time-history) parse+categorize cost
every single time someone runs `rig stats show`, even to check yesterday's numbers.

## Fix
Add a per-source on-disk cache (`riglib/stats/sources/_cache.py`) of the fully-parsed,
**unfiltered** invocation list for each session file, keyed by `(path, mtime_ns, size)`.

- Cache hit (closed sessions -- the overwhelming majority): skip re-reading/re-decoding/
  re-categorizing the file entirely.
- Cache miss (a new file, or one of the handful of sessions still actively being appended
  to -- mtime/size changed): re-parse just that one file and refresh its cache entry.
- The cache always stores the **unfiltered** parse, so one entry serves any future
  `--repo`/`--harness`/`--since` query -- filtering stays a cheap post-cache in-memory step.

Wired into all 5 source parsers (`claude_code`, `codex`, `gemini`, `omp`, `opencode`);
`_iter_session`/`_invocation` internals are untouched, only each `iter_invocations()` now
routes through the cache.

## Proof
Real timed run against this machine's actual `$HOME` (275k+ invocations across 5 harnesses):

```
cold: 26.83s   warm: 1.33s   speedup: 20.2x
```

Verified with a new test file (`tests/test_stats_cache.py`, 5 tests, all passing):
- warm-cache run byte-identical to cold-cache run
- a session file that **grows** between two runs is correctly re-parsed (never served
  stale/truncated data) -- confirmed live too: my own active omp session log grew between
  timed runs and the cache correctly picked up the new lines each time
- a warm cache entry correctly answers a `--repo` query it was never asked with before
  (proves the cache stores the full unfiltered parse, not a filtered subset)
- a corrupted cache file degrades to a full reparse, never breaks `rig stats`
- direct (de)serialization round-trip coverage

No stats output is dropped, changed, or double-counted -- the cache is purely an
optimization, transparent to every existing filter/format.

## Testing
```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_stats.py tests/test_stats_hatches.py tests/test_stats_omp_source.py tests/test_stats_cache.py -q
# 95 passed
```

Refs #499

title: feat(readme): reconcile a marked README Ecosystem block from one canonical registry
body:
Refs #308

## Problem

Every ecosystem repo hand-copies an `## Ecosystem` README section listing the sibling tools (rig-cli, tg-cli, review-cli, agent-tools, draw-cli, 3d-cli, task-cli, dev-cli, hyperide.ai), and it silently drifts because there is no reconciler for it — only copy-paste. task-cli/dev-cli had none at all; research-cli carried a stale ad-hoc note.

## Fix

`riglib/ecosystem_readme.py` is the ONE canonical registry (`ECOSYSTEM_TOOLS` + a pure, deterministic `render_ecosystem_block()`). A new opt-in `ecosystem_readme:` config block (default OFF, matching `tools:`/`project_tools:` in spirit) lets `rig apply` splice the rendered section between `<!-- rig:ecosystem-block -->` / `<!-- /rig:ecosystem-block -->` markers in a target repo's README.md, reusing the same `_splice_managed_block` machinery the codex execpolicy `.rules` block already uses:

- **Missing README** → create the file with the block.
- **Missing block in an existing README** → insert it, preserving every other line verbatim.
- **Unchanged registry, re-apply** → byte-identical no-op (all results `skipped`).
- **Stale block** → reconcile it in place, backing up the prior file first under `on_conflict=backup`; `on_conflict=skip` leaves a drifted block untouched (surfaced, not silently dropped).
- **Unbalanced/misordered markers** → hard error, apply refuses to guess; the file is left untouched.
- **A pre-existing, unmarked `## Ecosystem` heading** (the primary migration case — see Review below) → hard error asking for a hand migration, never a silent duplicate section.

`rig status` reports the same drift (missing / stale / unbalanced / unmarked-heading-conflict) via `riglib/drift.py`, and the area is registered in `riglib/schema.py` / `riglib/areas.py` so `rig setup`/`rig init` offers to turn it on during onboarding, the same registry every other opt-in area (`project_tools`, `linters`, …) uses.

rig-cli's own `rig.yaml` now sets `ecosystem_readme.enabled: true` and README.md's `## Ecosystem` section is wrapped in the managed markers (dogfooding #308) instead of being the hand-written block it replaces — `tests/test_ecosystem_readme.py::test_rig_cli_readme_block_matches_the_canonical_renderer` pins that the checked-in README stays byte-identical to the renderer.

`pyproject.toml` bumped 0.42.0 -> 0.43.0 (minor: additive feature).

## Review

`review diff --task 308` (quorum: Sonnet, Opus-omp, Fable — Opus/GLM/Grok were rate-limited/paywalled and the reserve degraded to 3 of 4 seats) surfaced one real, actionable correctness bug (Opus-omp): enabling `ecosystem_readme` on a repo that **already** hand-copies an unmarked `## Ecosystem` section — the feature's own stated primary use case — silently appended a *second*, misplaced heading at the end of the file while leaving the stale original untouched and invisible to `rig status` (the managed block itself read as in-sync). Fixed in a follow-up commit: `riglib/ecosystem_readme.has_unmarked_ecosystem_heading()` detects that case and both apply and drift now hard-error/flag it as a conflict needing a hand migration, same "refuse to guess" stance as an unbalanced marker pair. New tests cover the apply refusal, the drift verdict, and the detector directly.

The remaining findings were style-only or pre-existing/out-of-scope, waived:
- Sonnet: minor duplication (read-and-decode-error branch also lives in `drift.py`), a generically-named shared path-escape helper (`linter_path_escapes_repo`) now used outside linters, a trivial one-line accessor, and a CRLF-vs-LF mixed-newline cosmetic edge case on append — none affect correctness, deferred as style nits.
- Fable: the canonical-block design intentionally drops any per-repo-specific prose from the managed section (documented tradeoff in the module's own docstring, not new); `on_conflict=backup` littering a `README.md.rig-bak-*` file is the SAME convention every other managed block in this codebase already uses (execpolicy, MCP config, harness guard, …), not something this PR introduces; a README-as-symlink escaping the repo-containment guard is inherited from the pre-existing `linters` guard this reuses, not a new exposure.

## Verification

New `tests/test_ecosystem_readme.py` covers all 4 acceptance criteria plus config validation, drift, and the duplicate-heading fix:
- renderer (non-empty registry, markers + every tool present, deterministic)
- plan gating (disabled / absent / enabled / custom `target`, orphaned-block note when disabled)
- **insert**: fresh README created, block inserted into an existing README preserving hand-written content
- **no-op**: re-apply with an unchanged registry is byte-identical (`skipped`) both for a freshly-created README and one that started with existing content
- **update**: stale block reconciled with a backup under `on_conflict=backup`
- **conflict**: `on_conflict=skip` leaves a stale block untouched; unbalanced markers hard-error on apply and are reported as `modified` drift; an unmarked pre-existing `## Ecosystem` heading also hard-errors on apply (never a silent duplicate) and reports as `modified` drift, not `missing`
- config validation: unknown keys, non-bool `enabled`, `target` escaping the repo
- dogfood: rig-cli's own README block matches the canonical renderer byte-for-byte

Targeted suite green in a worktree rebased onto current `main`:
```
tests/test_ecosystem_readme.py tests/test_config_schema.py tests/test_setup_wizard.py \
tests/test_status_areas.py tests/test_actions_drift.py tests/test_drift_report.py \
tests/test_action_tags.py tests/test_execpolicy.py tests/test_permissions.py
461 passed, 2 skipped in 30.06s
```

## Files

- `riglib/ecosystem_readme.py` (new): canonical tool registry, renderer, and the unmarked-heading conflict detector
- `riglib/actions/runner.py`: `_do_apply_ecosystem_readme` handler (splice/insert/backup/skip/hard-error, including the duplicate-heading refusal), registered under `apply_ecosystem_readme`
- `riglib/plan.py`: `_build_ecosystem_readme` (gating, target containment check, orphaned-block note)
- `riglib/config.py`, `riglib/config_schema.py`, `schema/rig.schema.json`: `ecosystem_readme.{enabled,target}` validation + schema/docs
- `riglib/schema.py`, `riglib/areas.py`: onboarding-wizard/status-area registration
- `riglib/drift.py`, `riglib/action_tags.py`, `riglib/layers.py`: two-way drift reporting for the new area
- `rig.yaml`, `README.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`: rig-cli's own dogfood opt-in + managed block + migration note
- `tests/test_ecosystem_readme.py` (new): full coverage described above

title: fix(tmux): decouple mode-keys from clipboard, always render it
body:
## What

Folds the narrower `tmux.clipboard.mode_keys` knob (shipped in #484) into a standalone
`tmux.copy_mode.mode_keys`, rendered **unconditionally** (like `focus_events`), decoupled
from `tmux.clipboard` resolution.

## Why (evidence)

Refs #325.

#484 fixed the common case (clipboard enabled + a clipboard command resolves on the host):
`riglib/tmux.py`'s `render_rig_conf` only emitted `set -g mode-keys vi` **inside** the
`if self.clipboard_enabled and self.clipboard_command:` gate. A user who sets
`tmux.clipboard.enabled: false`, or is on a host with no `pbcopy`/`wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel`
on PATH, never got that `set` line at all — tmux's own `emacs` `mode-keys` default stayed
live, so `v`/`Space` in copy-mode did nothing, independent of clipboard. That's issue #325's
original repro (Alex: "the yellow highlight appears then just disappears, nothing gets
copied"), just reachable outside the clipboard-enabled path #484 covered.

This finishes an abandoned uncommitted worktree from a prior session (`fix/tmux-copy-mode-vi`,
branched off an older commit before #484 merged) — re-implemented against current `main`
as `tmux.copy_mode.mode_keys` since `main` had since gained `tmux.clipboard.mode_keys`,
which this PR now supersedes and removes (never referenced by any `rig.yaml` in the fleet).

## Changes

- `riglib/tmux.py`: `DEFAULT_MODE_KEYS`/`VALID_MODE_KEYS` (renamed from the `_CLIPBOARD_`
  variants), `_resolve_mode_keys` (renamed from `_resolve_clipboard_mode_keys`),
  `TmuxPlan.mode_keys` (renamed from `clipboard_mode_keys`) rendered unconditionally as
  `setw -g mode-keys {value}` in its own section, ahead of the clipboard bind-key block.
- `riglib/config.py`: validates `tmux.copy_mode.mode_keys` (was `tmux.clipboard.mode_keys`)
  against `VALID_MODE_KEYS`.
- `riglib/config_schema.py`, `schema/rig.schema.json`: new `tmux.copy_mode` block
  (`mode_keys` enum `vi`/`emacs`, default `vi`); `tmux.clipboard` no longer accepts
  `mode_keys`.
- `riglib/plan.py`, `riglib/actions/runner.py`: thread `copy_mode` through
  `_build_tmux`/`tmux_plan_from_action` the same way `focus_events` is threaded.
- `docs/config-schema.md`: documents `tmux.copy_mode.mode_keys` as its own key.
- `tests/test_tmux.py`, `tests/test_config.py`: default/override/clamp coverage for the new
  knob, plus a full `rig.yaml -> plan -> render` round trip through `tmux_plan_from_action`.

## Test proof

Scoped runs only (no full suite), from the worktree:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_tmux.py tests/test_config.py -q
544 passed in 0.98s

$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_config_schema.py -q
56 passed, 2 skipped in 0.06s

$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_config_schema.py tests/test_cli.py -k schema -q
61 passed, 2 skipped, 77 deselected in 0.12s
```

`test_schema_file_exists_and_in_sync` confirms `schema/rig.schema.json` matches the
`config_schema.py` registry (no drift); `test_cli.py`'s `rig schema --check` test confirms
the committed schema file is in sync.

title: feat(git-hooks): global hook dispatcher — run every global hook in every repo
body:
## Global git-hook dispatcher

A single, extensible mechanism so a growing set of global git hooks runs in **every** repo
on the machine — including repos whose local hook manager (lefthook → `.git/hooks`, husky →
`.husky/_`) or raw `.git/hooks` overrides `core.hooksPath` and would otherwise shadow the
global hooks entirely.

### Model
- **One entry point**: `~/.config/git/run-global-hooks <event>`.
- **One drop-in dir**: `~/.config/git/global-hooks.d/<event>/`. A global hook is just an
  executable file there. The dispatcher runs them all in sort order; any non-zero blocks.
- **Every repo calls the dispatcher once per event.** Adding a new global hook later is a
  single-file drop — it then runs in every wired repo with **zero per-repo edits**.

### What's in `git-hooks/global-dispatcher/` (shipped twins of the live `~/.config/git/`)
| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `run-global-hooks` | the dispatcher (sorted, stdin-spooled, any non-zero blocks) |
| `global-hooks.d/` | single source of truth; `10-secret-scan` (gitleaks staged block+warn tiers) |
| `hooks/` | the global composers: repo-local hook → dispatcher → review-gate |

title: feat(git-hooks): per-repo commit wiring + local-vs-global dedup for the dispatcher
body:
Two CTO-requested follow-ups to the global git-hook dispatcher
(`git-hooks/global-dispatcher/`).

## 1. Per-repo commit wiring

`install-local-hooks.sh` gains:

- **`--commit`** — after wiring, commit **only the exact tracked files this run wrote**
  (`lefthook.yml` / `.husky/<event>` / `.githooks-skip`, tracked via a `TOUCHED` list),
  with a fixed conventional message and `--no-verify` (committing the wiring through the
  very hooks being installed would be circular). It never sweeps unrelated work: it
  **refuses** if a file it would touch was already dirty (worktree, index, or untracked),
  canonicalizes paths so a relative `core.hooksPath=../shared-hooks` outside the repo is
  excluded, and is idempotent. A real `git add`/`commit` error exits non-zero; "nothing to
  commit" / "refused (dirty)" are deliberate no-ops.
- **`--no-dedup`** — skip the auto secret-scan detection.
- A **preflight** rejects a symlinked / non-regular `.githooks-skip` **before** mutating any
  hook file; the writability check runs on the write path only when a write is needed.

Wiring a tracked manager config is now a reproducible, committable step.

## 2. Dedup local-vs-global (run each check exactly once)

When a repo has a local hook manager **and** the global dispatcher, the same fragment
could run twice. Fix:

- Every global fragment declares a stable **capability id**: a `# global-hook-id: <id>`
  header, else the basename minus a numeric `NN-` prefix (`10-secret-scan` →
  `secret-scan`).
- A repo opts out of an id so the dispatcher skips that **one** fragment there. Sources:
  `git config hooks.skipGlobal`, env `GLOBAL_HOOKS_SKIP`, and a tracked
  `<repo>/.githooks-skip` (one id per line, `#` comments). Deterministic whole-line match.
- `install-local-hooks.sh` **auto-detects** an *active, blocking* local secret scan in the
  **active manager's** pre-commit and writes `.githooks-skip`. Detection is conservative:
  it reads only `run:` command values (not `fail_text:`/metadata), ignores comments and any
  command with a control operator (`|`, `&`, `;`, `&&`, `||` — possible status masking),
  stale inactive configs, and pre-push-only scans; it does recognize path-qualified
  (`./bin/gitleaks`) and env-prefixed (`VAR=x gitleaks`) invocations and `run: |` block
  scalars.

### Security model (deterministic & documented)

`secret-scan` is marked `# global-hook-protected: true`. For a **protected** id, only
sources a cloned repo cannot forge may skip it:

- `git config hooks.skipGlobal` — **always** (a tree can't ship `.git/config`), read with
  the ad-hoc value-injection config-env channels stripped (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`);
- the **tracked** `.githooks-skip` — **only** under `git config hooks.trustSkipFile true`.

The env var and a cloned repo's tracked file alone are **ignored** for protected ids, the
fragment **still runs** (fail-safe), and the retrofit never auto-writes a trusted git
config — you opt in explicitly. Symlinked skip files are rejected. The residual env
file-redirection vectors (`GLOBAL_HOOKS_DIR`, `HOME`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` → a repo-shipped
config) are dominated by "running an untrusted repo's hooks = arbitrary code execution"
and documented as the explicit `THREAT BOUNDARY` rather than chased.

## How double-runs are verified

`git-hooks/global-dispatcher/selfcheck.sh` is a standalone harness (no framework): it
builds throwaway repos and a fake `gitleaks` under an **isolated** git/XDG config and
exercises the real scripts. **77 assertions, all green**, covering:

- the dispatcher runs a fragment, and the tracked file / git config / env each skip it;
- with a local secret scan present and a trust opt-in, the protected global copy is skipped
  so the check runs **exactly once** (no double-run); by default it runs locally-plus-globally
  (fail-safe);
- the full conservative-detection matrix (comments, neutralizers `|| / ; / | / &`, masking
  `; echo` / `| tee`, pre-push-only, stale/mixed managers, path/env-prefixed gitleaks,
  `run:`-only vs `fail_text:`, block scalars);
- the trust model (protected vs unprotected; env and forged/redirected git-config rejected;
  symlinks rejected);
- `--commit` safety (only touched files, refuses pre-dirty / staged-rename / out-of-repo,
  idempotent, preflight + write-path checks prevent partial installs).

Run it: `sh git-hooks/global-dispatcher/selfcheck.sh`. All shell is POSIX `sh`,
shellcheck-clean, macOS + Linux.

Reviewed across 15 rounds of `codex exec review` (no short timeout); all findings fixed and
covered by tests, converging to operator-knob / log-wording polish.
