title: feat(lib): add agenttools_log shared structured JSONL logging library
body:
## What

Adds **`lib/agenttools_log`** — the agent-tools ecosystem's shared **structured JSONL logging** library. One JSON object per line, **stdlib-only** (no `pino`, no `structlog`, no `python-json-logger`). It generalizes the exact shape `rig-cli`'s `riglib.logging` already emits by hand, lifted into one importable package so `review-cli`, `rig-cli`, and future Python CLIs log identically.

This is the **library only** — wiring it into `review-cli`/`rig-cli` is a deliberate follow-up (review-cli is being edited concurrently).

## Record shape

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-15T09:00:00.123456+00:00","level":"INFO","logger":"agenttools.myapp","msg":"server started","port":8080,"pid":1234}
```

`ts` (ISO-8601 UTC) / `level` / `logger` / `msg` + arbitrary structured fields. `exc` (on `exc_info`), `stack` (on `stack_info`).

## Public API

- `get_logger(name) -> StructuredLogger` — per-module logger, auto-configures once from env. Accepts structured kwargs (`log.info("x", k=v)`) **and** stdlib-style lazy `%`-formatting (`log.info("x=%s", v)`).
- `configure(*, level, fmt, stream, log_file, force)` — explicit (re)configuration; explicitly-passed args win over env; thread-safe (RLock) idempotent first-use.
- `reset()` — teardown (mainly tests).
- `StructuredLogger` (`.debug/.info/.warn/.error/.exception`), `DEBUG/INFO/WARNING/ERROR`.

## Config (env)

| Env var | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTTOOLS_LOG_LEVEL` | `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error` | `info` |
| `AGENTTOOLS_LOG_FILE` | a path (append JSONL, forced `0600`) | stderr |
| `AGENTTOOLS_LOG_FORMAT` | `json` / `pretty` | `json` |

## Dependency decision

**Stdlib `logging` + a ~one-class custom JSON formatter, zero runtime deps.** Both existing consumers already do this by hand (review-cli prints to stderr with no log dep; rig-cli ships a `logging.Formatter` subclass), and the ecosystem is stdlib-first by directive. `structlog` would be heavy for no gain; `python-json-logger` is thin but still an unnecessary dependency surface in every consumer.

## Safety posture

- **Never crashes the caller** — formatter, log calls, and `configure` all swallow their own errors.
- **`0600` file perms** on every open, even pre-existing files — mirrors `review-cli`'s `stats.py`.
- **Degrades to stderr** on file-open failure, with a **JSON-only** diagnostic so the default stream stays pure JSONL.
- **Pretty mode escapes control chars** to stay single-line (no forged log lines).
- No automatic redaction (structured fields make intentional logging easy).

## Tests

36 pytest tests, all green: JSONL shape (valid JSON per line + required keys), level filtering, env config, file sink + `0600` (incl. pre-existing file), never-crash-on-bad-field, `%`-formatting (with `exc_info` + fields), thread-safe concurrent first-use (no duplicate handlers), no-fd-leak across 50 reset cycles, JSON-only fallback diagnostic.

```
36 passed
```

## Dogfooded

Reviewed with the review-cli BOARD (`review --staged`) across **three rounds**; every real finding fixed (positional-only `msg`, fd-leak on file sink, `force=False` idempotency, explicit-stream-vs-env precedence, `stack_info` emission, thread-safety, pretty single-line, `%`-args support, JSON-only fallback). Final round only pedantic items, all addressed.

## Integration seam (follow-up)

```toml
# consumer pyproject.toml
[project]
dependencies = ["agenttools-log"]
```
```python
from agenttools_log import get_logger
log = get_logger(__name__)
```
`rig-cli`'s `riglib.logging` can become a thin re-export; `review-cli` can adopt incrementally.

title: ci: make security gate templates degrade gracefully on feature-less repos
body:
## Problem

The rig wave-1 rollout PRs (draw-cli #3, tg-cli #25, 3d-cli #6) **hard-failed** on three of the new CI gate templates the moment they landed on a fresh private repo, blocking the whole rollout. Root causes, each confirmed from the failing-step logs (`gh run view --log-failed`):

| Gate | Root cause (from logs) |
| ---- | ---------------------- |
| **dependency-review** | `actions/dependency-review-action` hard-fails: `Dependency review is not supported on this repository. Please ensure that Dependency graph is enabled`. The Dependency Graph is OFF by default on private repos. |
| **gitleaks** (secret-scan) | `🛑 GITHUB_TOKEN is now required to scan pull requests`. The template only set `GITLEAKS_LICENSE`, never `GITHUB_TOKEN`. (The `push` trigger doesn't need it, so it passed — masking the bug; only `pull_request` runs failed.) |
| **CodeQL self-gate** | On a Python/shell repo with zero JS/TS, the hardcoded `javascript-typescript` matrix entry fatally errors (`No source code seen`, exit 32) → no SARIF → gate fails on an inapplicable language. Plus: the self-gate's own in-source suppression couldn't match YAML (`#`) comments and only checked the one line directly above a finding. |

## Fixes (resilient where the feature is absent, still BLOCKING where present)

- **`ci/dependency-review/workflow.yml`** — preflight step probes the Dependency Graph (the SBOM endpoint returns 200 when enabled, 404 when not) and runs the gate **only when the graph is available**; when off it **skips cleanly with a `::notice::`** + the (free) enable link instead of hard-failing. The instant the graph is enabled the gate goes live with no edit. README corrects the inaccurate "needs GHAS" claim (the graph is free) and recommends a rig follow-up to enable it on apply.
- **`ci/secret-scan/secret-scan.yml`** — add `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` to the gitleaks env (the auto-provisioned token; no PAT/secret to create).
- **`ci/codeql/workflow-selfgate.yml`** — preflight detects whether the repo actually contains source for each matrix language and **skips that language cleanly** when absent, instead of hard-failing on "No source code seen". In-source suppression now (a) accepts `# codeql[<rule>]` (YAML/`actions`, Python, shell) as well as `// codeql[<rule>]` (JS/TS), and (b) matches the marker **anywhere in the contiguous comment block** directly above a finding (stops at the first blank/non-comment line, so no cross-statement leak) — so a multi-line justification works.
- **`ci/leftover-grep/workflow.yml`** — suppress the two by-design `actions` findings (`cache-poisoning/poisonable-step`, `untrusted-checkout/medium`) that the CodeQL self-gate raises on this template's own `pull_request_target` + PR-head-fetch pattern (data-only, never executed — see the template's own HARD RULE) with justified `# codeql[...]` markers, so the rig's own gate doesn't trip on the rig's own shipped workflow.

## What still legitimately fails (NOT a template defect)

The CodeQL self-gate correctly catches **real** findings in some repos' own code — these are the gate working as intended, not infra failures, and are intentionally NOT papered over:
- **tg-cli**: 8 pre-existing JS/TS findings (sanitization / double-escaping / file-system-race) in its own source — need a fix-or-justify decision by the owner.
- **3d-cli / tg-cli**: a couple of `actions` findings in each repo's **own** pre-existing `ci.yml` (missing-permissions, unpinned-tag) — fixed legitimately in the rollout PRs (permissions block + SHA pins), not by suppression.

## Recommended rig follow-up (not in this PR)

`rig apply` should enable the Dependency Graph + Dependabot vulnerability alerts on apply:
```
gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo} \
  -F security_and_analysis.dependency_graph.status=enabled
```
so the dependency-review gate is live from day one instead of skipping.

title: feat(lib): model manifest + daily freshness checker (#3685)
body:
## What & why (#3685, pairs with #3681)

The model-version-currency system the CTO approved: a central **model manifest** with capability tags, a **daily checker** that proposes version bumps, plus the contracts to validate them. Paired with rig provisioning the checker as a daily noon cron (see the rig-cli PR).

## Manifest — `lib/contracts/models.yaml`

Single source of truth: per-provider current-best concrete model ids, each tagged with `capabilities`, plus a symbolic `roles:`/`aliases:` map.

- **`vision` is load-bearing** (#3681 image-review filter): `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` is code-only with **NO vision**; `kimi-k2p6-turbo` **HAS vision**. The `vision` role MUST resolve to a vision-capable entry.
- `roles:` = architect / fast / code / reasoning / **vision**; `aliases:` includes `<provider>:latest`.
- Validated by `lib/contracts/models.schema.json` (JSON-Schema) **plus** the checker's `--validate` (the vision / `<provider>:latest` cross-references a schema can't express).

## Checker — `lib/checker/model_freshness.py`

Stdlib-first (yaml lazy, urllib for HTTP). Reads the manifest, polls provider model-list endpoints (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/commandcode/z.ai) with keys **harvested** from env + the same `.env` fallbacks review-cli reads (a provider with no key is **skipped**, never a crash), and **PROPOSES** a bump when a newer same-family version appears — a `gh` PR editing `models.yaml`, or a dated report if `gh`/auth is absent. **Semi-automatic: propose, never auto-merge** (a newer model can regress). Idempotent: no duplicate PR for the same bump.

## Multi-model review applied (review-cli, pool=4)

Real findings fixed: dated/build-suffix version matching (`claude-opus-4-8-20260101`, `gemini-2.5-flash-002`) so bumps actually fire for anthropic/gemini; `--dry-run` no longer writes a report; `new_id` inserted via a callable replacement (no `re.sub` escape interpretation); `propose_via_gh` threads `manifest_path`; gemini key sent as a header not a URL param; honest "incomplete coverage" messaging; actionable pyyaml-missing error.

title: feat(agent-hooks): format-on-write post-write formatter hook
body:
## What

Adds a new agent-hook **`format-on-write`** that makes code formatting a **harness concern**: every file the agent writes/edits is run through the project's **configured** formatter automatically, on just that one file, in place. This generalizes the "an `oxfmt --write` step in `lefthook.yml`" pattern (hyper-canvas) out of any one repo and lifts it to every write, every project, every supported language — so formatting stops being a per-project / per-extension manual step or a commit-time cleanup.

## New `post-write` contract point

The documented points were `pre-bash` / `pre-write` / `stop`. A formatter rewrites a file **in place**, so the file must exist first — `pre-write` only sees *proposed* bytes and is for *blocking* a write before it lands. So this adds a **`post-write`** logical point to `agents-hooks/v1`: "react to a *completed* write" (the file is on disk; `args.path` + `event.cwd` carry it). Documented in `agent-hooks/README.md` with the point-class explanation, and mapped to a `PostToolUse` matcher on the Write/Edit tools.

## Detection table (repo-config, extension), repo-local preferred over global

| ext | candidates | invocation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.json/.css/.md/.yaml/.html/...` | oxfmt → prettier → biome | `--write <f>` / `format --write <f>` |
| `.py/.pyi` | ruff → black | `ruff format <f>` / `black -q <f>` |
| `.go` | gofmt | `gofmt -w <f>` |
| `.rs` | rustfmt | `rustfmt <f>` |

Repo-local lookup is anchored on the `.git` root (only fires inside a worktree). No formatter configured/available → **no-op**.

## Never blocks

`on_error: open` and **no `block` path at all** — every failure mode (no formatter, tool missing, formatter non-zero, timeout, bad event) → `allow`. Formatting is a convenience; the `pre-commit` git-hook format step stays the *gate*. Escape hatch: `NO_FORMAT_HOOK=1`. Inner 8s run-timeout under the 10s host ceiling.

## Tests / proof

- 16 hermetic pytest cases (`tests/test_format_on_write.py`): detection-table ordering, path resolution (key precedence + relative-against-cwd), escape hatch, all fail-open modes, **local-bin preferred over global**, and an **end-to-end run via a fake local formatter**. `ruff` clean, full repo suite green (52 passed, 1 pre-existing skip).
- Manually self-tested against real `gofmt` / `rustfmt` and a fake `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` (formats a deliberately mis-formatted file; no-ops when no formatter maps).

## Also

- Bumps the root README hook inventory 7 → 8; adds `post-write` to the install-point list.
- `rig.yaml`: notes `all: true` auto-discovers it (no per-hook entry needed; `post-write` → `PostToolUse` mapping).
- `pre-commit-gate` skill: one-line "let the hook format; don't hand-format".

## Reviewed

Ran `review --staged` (multi-model) twice and addressed the actionable findings before pushing.

> Note: this is the agent-tools generalization of hyper's **dev** `oxfmt`-via-lefthook step. Hyper's **runtime/product** formatting (recast format-preserving AST writes in `AstService.ts`, on canvas mutation) is unrelated product behavior and was deliberately left untouched.

title: feat(hooks): bridge agents-hooks/v1 → Claude Code so guards actually fire (#18)
body:
## Problem (#18, verified live, not hypothetical)

agent-tools ships agent-hooks (`block-raw-pr-merge`, `block-secrets-write`, `enforce-timeout-on-bash`, …) that speak `agents-hooks/v1`: a JSON descriptor + an executable, installed into `~/.claude/hooks/`, signalling BLOCK via **exit code 10**.

**Claude Code never runs those descriptors.** CC only runs hooks declared in `settings.json` under PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop. Nothing reads `~/.claude/hooks/*.json`. Confirmed on this machine: the only PreToolUse hooks CC actually executes are `rtk-rewrite.sh` and `tg-ctl` (both in `settings.json`); the rig-installed descriptor JSONs sit there inert. So every agent-hook was **inert in CC** and the "auto-mode is safe because the guards intercept" pillar was **false**.

## The bridge

`lib/cc_hook_bridge` — a stdlib-only dispatcher CC's `settings.json` calls once per event. It reads the CC tool-call JSON, maps `(event, tool)` to a logical v1 point (`Bash`→`pre-bash`, `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`→`pre-write`, `Stop`→`stop`), runs the matching descriptors (priority order), and translates the v1 exit-10 BLOCK into CC's block signal.

### Confirmed CC contract (NOT assumed)

Confirmed against the live docs — <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks> — with installed CC **2.1.177**:

| CC event | Block mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| `PreToolUse` | exit 0 + `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}` |
| `Stop` | exit 0 + `{"decision":"block","reason":"…"}` |

**Why structured JSON, not exit 2?** The docs are explicit: *"Claude Code only processes JSON on exit 0. If you exit 2, any JSON is ignored."* Exit 2 blocks but discards the reason. `permissionDecision: "deny"` carries the full v1 `message` to the model — strictly richer, and matches the installed `rtk-rewrite.sh` style. **PostToolUse is intentionally NOT wired** — the tool already ran, so it cannot block (documented).

### pre-write payload normalization (security fix from review)

A CC `MultiEdit` puts content in `edits[].new_string` and `NotebookEdit` in `new_source`, but the pre-write guards only scan flat `content`/`new_string`/`text`. `to_v1_event` flattens all of it into `args.content` so a secret hidden in a MultiEdit can't slip past `block-secrets-write`. One place, every pre-write hook stays correct.

### Fail policy

- **Dispatcher: fail-OPEN** — any internal error is swallowed and the call allowed; a broken bridge never wedges a tool call.
- **Per-hook: honors `on_error`** — exit 10 blocks; a hook error (bad exit / timeout / unrunnable cmd / bad `timeout_ms`) with `on_error=closed` → DENY, `open` → allow. A bad `priority`/`timeout_ms` in ONE descriptor is resolved per-descriptor (a fail-closed gate still DENIES), not bubbled to the top-level fail-open.

## Clean-room proof (verify, don't promise)

`tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py` (19 tests, full suite 55 passed / 1 skipped) installs the **real** guards in an isolated `$HOME` and runs the dispatcher as a subprocess — exactly how CC invokes it.

Direct end-to-end against the REAL `block-raw-pr-merge`, via the exact command rig writes:

```
--- BLOCK case (gh pr merge 42 --admin) ---
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny",
 "permissionDecisionReason": "Refusing a raw `gh pr merge` (incl. --admin): it bypasses
  the ship gates (green CI + required screenshots). Use `gh ship <PR>` instead …"}}

--- PASS case (gh ship 42) ---
stdout=[]   (empty = allow → tool proceeds)
```

The MultiEdit-secret security fix, end-to-end against REAL `block-secrets-write`:

```
--- MultiEdit, AWS key in edits[].new_string (SHOULD BLOCK) ---
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny",
 "permissionDecisionReason": "Refusing to write what looks like a AWS access key id …"}}

--- MultiEdit, no secret (SHOULD PASS) ---
stdout=[]   (empty = allow)
```

Key tests (all PASSED):
- `test_real_guard_blocks_raw_pr_merge` / `test_real_guard_passes_benign_bash`
- `test_to_v1_event_normalizes_multiedit_into_content` / `…_notebook_new_source`
- `test_bad_timeout_ms_on_closed_gate_blocks` / `test_bad_priority_does_not_crash_dispatch`
- `test_stop_block_emits_decision_block` / `test_fail_open_on_garbage_stdin` / `test_first_block_wins_collects_reason`

## rig wiring

A **separate rig-cli PR** (`register_hook_bridge` action) registers this dispatcher into `settings.json` on `rig apply`. This PR ships only the dispatcher rig points at.

## Reviewed

Multi-model `review --staged` run; findings addressed (PostToolUse cannot-block clarified, MultiEdit/NotebookEdit payload gap fixed + proven, per-descriptor int-parse isolation, `__all__` export, extensibility docs). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(ci): drop GHAS/licensed gates for free OSS engines (gitleaks binary, dep-audit)
body:
## Why
The rig-shipped CI gates depended on **paid** GitHub features, so they hard-failed on org/private repos (surfaced on hyperide/hyper-saas #463):
- `secret-scan.yml` used `gitleaks/gitleaks-action` → requires a paid `GITLEAKS_LICENSE` on **organizations** ("[org] is an organization. License key is required.").
- `dependency-review.yml` used `actions/dependency-review-action` → requires **GHAS** on **private** repos; hard-fails "not supported … requires GitHub Advanced Security" *even with the free Dependency Graph on* (the template's old README claim that GHAS is 'only for the dashboard' was wrong).

CTO decision (tg#3774): drop GHAS/licensed gates entirely, use free OSS engines everywhere.

## Changes
- **secret-scan.yml** — install + run the **gitleaks OSS binary** directly (`gitleaks dir`). Same engine + ruleset as the Action (the Action is just a wrapper); zero license. Verified parity: the binary is MIT and `gitleaks.toml` already `useDefault=true` (full stock ruleset).
- **dependency-review.yml** — drop the GHAS action; gate = **`dep-audit.sh`** (whole-tree bun/npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/cargo/go audit, no GitHub feature). Equal-or-better vuln coverage (whole-tree vs PR-diff). Documents the one lost capability — **license policy** — to be filled by an OSS license gate (#21).
- READMEs corrected to match (parity table added).
- **CodeQL actions self-gate** suppressions in `leftover-grep`/`review-threads` were already correct (`# codeql[...]` present, right placement) — untouched. The #463 CodeQL failure is a stale rollout copy; a rig re-apply with these templates fixes it.

## Coordination
The rig-side (which gates apply per-repo, auto-mode provisioning) and the hyper #463 application are owned by the parallel rig agent. This PR is the **source-template** fix only (ci/ files), no rig/auto-mode changes. Related: #18/#20 (hook bridge), #21 (license gate), #22 (dashboard).

## Verify
YAML validated. `gitleaks dir` / `dep-audit.sh` exit non-zero on findings (fail-closed).

title: refactor(rig): slim repo rig.yaml to repo-level only
body:
## What

Slims the committed `rig.yaml` down to **repo-level config only**. The machine-wide blocks (`defaults`, `skills`, `agent_hooks`, `git_hooks`, `mcp`, `harness`) now live in the **GLOBAL layer** `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` and are no longer repeated here.

Kept in the repo file:
- `version: 1`
- the `ci:` block (repo-level gate — CI lives in `.github/workflows`)

Removed: `scope`, `defaults`, `skills`, `agent_hooks`, `git_hooks`, `mcp`, `harness`.

## Why

The cascade is by **location**: a config at `~/.config/rig/config.yaml` is global, a committed `rig.yaml` is that repo and overrides it. The per-machine installs a developer carries across every repo belong in the global layer; this committed file should only carry what is specific to THIS repo.

Removing `harness:` from this committed file also stops any older rig from re-writing a committed **project bypass** into `.claude/settings.json` on checkout. Harness auto-mode is now applied by the global config to `~/.claude/settings.json` (user scope), which is the only slot Claude Code honors for `defaultMode`.

## Verification

`rig apply -C . --dry-run` runs clean (exit 0, 80 actions). The plan still includes all global blocks coming from the global config — skills (both `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills`), agent-hooks → `~/.claude/hooks`, git-hooks dispatcher → `~/.config/git/global-hooks.d`, mcp/review → `~/.claude/mcp`, harness → `~/.claude/settings.json` — **plus** this repo's `ci`. title: feat(lib): add shared dependency-free retry helper (agenttools_retry)
body:
A small stdlib-only retry utility the ecosystem tools can share, per ROADMAP
section 3.6. Provides a retry() callable + a @retries(...) decorator over one
RetryPolicy/execution loop, so the imperative and declarative entry points can
never drift.

- Configurable max_attempts, exponential backoff (base_delay * factor**n) capped
  at max_delay.
- DETERMINISTIC, seedable jitter: the jitter source is a random.Random the policy
  owns (jitter_seed= or an injected Random). Never the process-global random
  module, so tests are reproducible and one caller can't perturb another.
- Retryable predicate by exception type (retry_on=) and/or return value
  (retry_if_result=); anything unmatched propagates/returns immediately.
- on_retry hook (RetryState per attempt) for logging/metrics; a failing hook
  can't break the loop.
- Injectable sleeper (defaults to time.sleep) so tests run instantly and assert
  the exact backoff schedule.

Zero runtime deps (functools + random + time). README + 24 pytest tests covering
succeeds-first-try, succeeds-after-N, exhausts-and-raises (reraise + RetryError),
the configured backoff schedule via a fake clock, deterministic jitter,
result-based retry, the on_retry hook, and non-retryable/KeyboardInterrupt
propagating immediately.

title: feat(lib): generalized two-layer config-cascade loader (agenttools_config)
body:
## What

Extract the tool-agnostic **LOADING / CASCADE / PATH** logic out of `rig-cli`'s `riglib.config` into a reusable shared lib — `lib/agenttools_config/` — so any ecosystem CLI (`rig`, `review`, `task`, …) gets the same `~/.config/<tool>` + per-repo overlay semantics from one importable loader.

ROADMAP §3.4: *cascade + env precedence + `~/.config` paths*.

## The cascade (two layers, by location)

| Order | Layer | Path | Role |
| ----- | ----- | ---- | ---- |
| 1 (base) | Global | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<tool>/config.yaml` → falls back to `~/.config/<tool>/config.yaml` | machine-wide defaults |
| 2 (wins) | Per-repo | `<repo_root>/<tool>.yaml` | committed source of truth; overrides global |

A `--config PATH` flag (`explicit_config=`) replaces the per-repo layer.

## Merge rule

Deep dict merge, per-repo winning: nested **dicts** merge recursively; **lists and scalars replace wholesale** (lists are atomic, never appended) — verbatim from the reference impl.

## What is deliberately left OUT

Any tool's **domain schema**. The reference impl knew rig's keys (`skills`/`ci`/`mcp`/…); this library knows none. A caller passes a `schema_validate` callable to enforce its own schema fail-closed — the hook is sovereign (if it raises, the exception is surfaced unchanged). `rig-cli` can pass its existing `riglib.config.validate` verbatim.

## Invariants

- **stdlib-only at import time** — PyYAML is imported lazily inside the loader, so `<tool> --help`/`doctor` work without it (verified by blocking the `yaml` import and importing the package + doing an empty load).
- **Fail-closed on a malformed file** — unreadable file, invalid YAML, or non-mapping root each raise `ConfigError` (a `ValueError` subclass), never a raw PyYAML traceback.

## Files

- `lib/agenttools_config/{__init__,core}.py` — the loader (`load_config`, `deep_merge`, `global_config_path`, `repo_config_path`, `LoadedConfig`, `ConfigError`).
- `lib/agenttools_config/README.md`, `pyproject.toml` (`agenttools-config` distribution; lazy PyYAML dep).
- `tests/test_agenttools_config.py` — **25 cases**: global-only, repo-only, both (repo wins), deep merge of nested dicts, list replacement, XDG override (+ empty-XDG fallback), `include_global=False`, explicit-config replace/missing, missing-file handling, empty-file, non-mapping/invalid-YAML fail-closed, and a `schema_validate` hook (receives merged dict, a raising hook surfaced, arbitrary exception propagates unchanged, no-hook = no schema check) + `deep_merge` unit cases.
- `lib/README.md` — register the new module in the table.

## Tests

```
$ uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest tests/test_agenttools_config.py -q
25 passed
$ uv run --with ruff ruff check lib/agenttools_config/ tests/test_agenttools_config.py
All checks passed!
```

Wiring `rig-cli` (and other CLIs) onto this loader is a deliberate follow-up — this package ships standalone.

title: feat(lib): add advertise — shared install-skill core
body:
## What

Extract the **install-skill** logic copy-pasted across `rig` / `review` / `tg` / `draw` / `task` into one importable, **stdlib-only** lib module: `lib/advertise/`. The CLIs can later `from advertise import install_skill` and drop their hand-rolled copies.

It does the two things every `<tool> install-skill` does:

1. Write `SKILL.md` into `~/.agents/skills/<tool>/` (the Agent Skills standard location), idempotently.
2. Symlink that skill dir into each harness discovery dir (`~/.claude/skills/<tool>`) — a skill that lives only in `~/.agents/skills` is invisible to the harness.

This PR **does not touch the CLIs** — it ships the lib standalone for them to adopt.

## Safe-symlink discipline (mirrors rig's `riglib.install`)

- correct link → no-op; wrong/**dangling** link → re-pointed; real (non-symlink) dir/file → governed by `on_conflict` (`skip` default / `backup` / `overwrite`); self-link skipped when the harness dir IS the agents dir.
- Fixes two bugs the naive copies (review/tg/draw) carry: `not link.exists()` never repairs a stale link, and a dangling link reads as "exists" (follows symlinks) and stays broken. Here the test is `is_symlink()`.

## API

`install_skill(tool, skill_md=… | source_dir=…, *, skills_dir, harness_dirs, on_conflict)` → `InstallResult` (with per-harness `HarnessLink`). Supports both content models: inline `skill_md` (rig/task/review) and `source_dir` overlay-copy (preserving mode bits, so a shipped `scripts/run.sh` stays executable). Harness-link failures are recorded on the result, never raised — the SKILL.md write is the one load-bearing step.

## Hardening from the pre-commit multi-model review

- `on_conflict` validated up front — a typo can't fall through to the destructive `overwrite` branch.
- `harness_dirs` accepts one path or a sequence — a bare string is not iterated per-char.
- `source_dir` validated **before** any `mkdir` — a bad call leaves no orphan dir; and copy preserves the executable bit.

## Tests

36 HOME-isolated pytest cases: fresh install, idempotent re-run, wrong link re-pointed, dangling link repaired, real dir/file left untouched (+ backup/overwrite), self-link guard, multi-harness, `source_dir` copy (content + exec bit + mode-only re-sync), argument guards, the `_main` CLI path, best-effort link-failure recording.

title: feat: strict-ticket-discipline skill + require-ticket-before-commit guard
body:
ROADMAP §8 (task-cli integrations): a universal skill teaching ticket-first discipline, plus the agent-hook that enforces it at commit time. Pairs with task-cli.

## What

- **`skills/universal/strict-ticket-discipline/`** — every non-trivial change (feature/bugfix/refactor) starts from a ticket (task-cli / GitHub Issue / Linear) with **acceptance criteria + motivation + user-impact** written down *before* work begins, and the commit references it. Covers what counts as non-trivial, why before-not-after, and the common rationalizations (retroactive ticket, empty criteria, reference only in chat).
- **`agent-hooks/require-ticket-before-commit/`** — `pre-bash` guard (`agents-hooks/v1`). On `git commit`, scans the commit message and branch name for a ticket reference. If none and the commit isn't an exempt chore/WIP/merge:
  - **default: warn** (`on_error: open`, advisory `allow` + message) so it can never over-block real work;
  - **`REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=1`: block** (exit 10).

## Ticket-detection heuristic (documented)

Deliberately broad — a miss only nags (fail-open). Detects `#NNN`, `org/repo#NNN`, `GH-NNN`, `KEY-NNN` (≥2 uppercase, so `A1-456` doesn't false-hit), `task:…`/`task #…`/`T-NN`, trailer keywords *followed by a real ref* (so `fix: null deref` is correctly NOT a reference), and full tracker URLs. Message is pulled from `-m`/`-mMsg`/`--message=`/`-F` (relative `-F` paths resolve against the event `cwd`). Exemptions: conventional chore types (`chore`/`docs`/`style`/`ci`/`build`/`test`/`revert`, configurable via `REQUIRE_TICKET_EXEMPT_TYPES`), `wip`/`fixup!`/`merge`/`revert` markers, and `--amend`/`--continue`/`--abort`/`--skip`.

## Tests

title: fix(ship): CI gate — refuse on no-CI, watch pending CI, grace for fresh PRs

title: Surface mandatory always-apply skills (delegate-work-to-subagents + visual-proof-cycle)
body:
## Why

Two recurring, expensive agent failures — including in the main orchestrator thread:
(a) doing non-trivial work **inline** instead of delegating to subagents, and (b) claiming
a user-visible change is "done" **without ever looking at the rendered result**. Root cause:
no "delegate all work" skill existed, and the mandatory skills were not surfaced as
always-apply anywhere an agent reliably reads.

## What this does

1. **New skill** `skills/universal/delegate-work-to-subagents/SKILL.md` — the main thread is
   an orchestrator: plan → decompose → dispatch (the `Agent` tool / a dynamic workflow) →
   verify; it does not implement multi-step work inline. Strong always-on frontmatter trigger.
2. **`AGENTS.md`** (new) — a prominent **"Always-apply skills"** section naming the two
   mandatory skills, their trigger conditions, and the durable mechanism.
3. **`README.md`** — the new skill added to the inventory (37 universal) and an always-apply
   callout in "Using the skills".

## How mandatory skills are now durably surfaced

- Both are **universal** skills, so `rig` installs them by default on every machine
  (`skills.universal.all: true` in the global rig config — default-on, opt-out). No new flag
  needed; the install path already covers them.
- Their **strong frontmatter `description`** is the when-to-use trigger the harness uses to
  surface a skill on any matching task.
- **`AGENTS.md`** is the per-session backstop: harnesses inject it as context each session,
  so the mandate is in front of every agent (orchestrator and subagents) on every task.

## Honest scope note — no SessionStart hook

There is **no in-repo SessionStart blurb/hook to extend** (the draw/review/tg blurb lives in
the user's personal `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, not this repo). The agent-hooks contract and the
`lib/cc_hook_bridge` dispatcher support only `PreToolUse` / `Stop` / `PostToolUse` — there is
no SessionStart point. Adding one would mean a new logical point + bridge `_KNOWN_EVENTS`
entry + rig-cli `settings.json` wiring (a separate repo) + CC's distinct SessionStart payload
/ `additionalContext` output schema — a cross-repo feature, not "extend a blurb", and a
SessionStart descriptor today would be **inert** (the bridge would never invoke it). So the
durable mechanism is AGENTS.md + the universal-skill default-install + frontmatter triggers,
which are real and verifiable, rather than an inert hook.

Docs-only; English-only; no Cyrillic.

title: docs: stop duplicating universal mandatory skills into AGENTS.md (reconcile #45 to #44)

## What

Reconciles `main` so it complies with the rule PR #44 established, which PR #45 then regressed.

**Background.** PR #44 (`docs(readme): universal mandatory skills live in rig's layer, not in AGENTS.md`) set the rule: a project's `AGENTS.md` / repo-level `CLAUDE.md` is for **project-specific** guidance only. Cross-project, always-apply **mandatory universal skills** (`delegate-work-to-subagents`, `visual-proof-cycle`) are surfaced by **rig's universal skill layer** (`skills.universal.all`) + each skill's own frontmatter `description` — never duplicated into an individual `AGENTS.md`.

PR #45 then merged (3 min after #44) an `AGENTS.md` with a prominent **"Always-apply skills (mandatory)"** table, plus README callouts pointing at it — directly contradicting #44. `main` now both forbids the duplication (README, from #44) and ships it (AGENTS.md + README pointers, from #45).

## Changes

- **`AGENTS.md`** — remove the "Always-apply skills (mandatory)" section. Replace with a short note that no such list lives here: universal mandates come from rig's layer + the skill's own trigger, and `AGENTS.md` stays project-specific. The repo-specific operational guardrails (review-before-commit, atomic commits, ship gate, fresh worktree, English-only) stay.
- **`README.md`** — stop pointing the "Two of these are always-apply" callout and the Inventory entry at the now-removed `AGENTS.md` section. The skill's frontmatter trigger is the single source of truth; the skill remains listed in the inventory.

It already lives on `main`. **This PR does not add or modify any skill**; universal skills live in rig's universal layer, not in `AGENTS.md`.

## How the mandatory skills are surfaced (no AGENTS.md involvement)

Both `delegate-work-to-subagents` and `visual-proof-cycle` live under `skills/universal/`. rig's global layer (`~/.config/rig/config.yaml`, `skills.universal.all` default-on) installs every `skills/universal/*` skill into the harness's skills dir; each skill's frontmatter `description` is the trigger the harness fires on. ## What

Adds `lib/agenttools_tmux_inject` — a stdlib-only helper to inject text/keys into a named tmux pane/session via `send-keys`. A finishing agent posts a line into *another* agent's interactive pane (e.g. `task-cli` types "done, deploy unblocked" into the pane of the agent that was blocked on it).

## API

- `inject(target, text)` — type text + press Enter (the headline call)
- `send_keys(...)` — low-level primitive (`enter` defaults to `False`)
- `has_session`, `list_panes`, `resolve_target`

title: feat(lib): universal zsh tab-completion generator + auto-installer (agenttools_completion)
body:
## What

A new stdlib-only shared module **`agenttools_completion`** under `lib/`: a universal zsh tab-completion **generator** + idempotent **auto-installer**. It introspects an argparse parser tree and emits a valid `#compdef` zsh completion script — no hand-written, drift-prone completion files.

## Generator — `generate_zsh(parser, prog) -> str`

- Subcommands from `add_subparsers` → `_SubParsersAction.choices`, **recursively** (nested `rig stats show` / `demo config get` complete).
- Per-command options: long (`--foo`) + short (`-f`), brace-grouped (`{--verbose,-v}`), help as the zsh description.
- `choices=[...]` on options **and** positionals → offered as `(a b c)` value groups.
- Value-taking options without choices (`--config PATH`) → complete to `_files`; flags stay no-arg.
- Subcommand label from `help=` with `.description` fallback.
- `argparse.SUPPRESS` help → **empty** description, never the literal `==SUPPRESS==`.
- State-machine dispatch (`_arguments -C` + `case $state` + `case $line[1]`) so a global flag before the subcommand never misroutes.
- **zsh-safety:** every description/value escaped (colon, single-quote via `'\''`, bracket, backslash). Pinned by tests that run **real `zsh -n`** and **autoload under `compinit`**.

## Installer — `install` / `uninstall` / `status`

- Writes `<comp_dir>/_<prog>` (default `~/.zsh/completions`, mode `0644`).
- Guarded, **idempotent** fpath+compinit block in `~/.zshrc` between sentinel lines (re-install never duplicates).
- `comp_dir` / `zshrc` injectable (tests never touch the real `~/.zshrc`); the block records its target dir so `status` / `uninstall` are **comp_dir-aware** and never cross-contaminate.
- `uninstall` removes the file and drops the block only when no managed `_*` file remains; idempotent.
- Returns `InstallResult` / `UninstallResult` / `StatusResult` (booleans + a ready-to-print `human` string).

## Proof

- `lib/agenttools_completion/demo_cli.py` — always-present end-to-end proof (`python -m agenttools_completion.demo_cli | zsh -n /dev/stdin`).
- Test suite also generates a real `_rig` from rig-cli when importable (best-effort, gated read-only — no rig dependency).

## Tests

32 module tests + the real `zsh -n` / autoload checks. Full repo suite: **174 passed, 2 skipped** (no regressions). Ruff clean.

## Follow-up (documented in README, NOT done here)

Per-tool `<tool> completion install|uninstall|status` wiring into each real CLI is left as a deliberate follow-up (avoided editing other repos).

title: feat(lib): shared service-manager agenttools_service (run/start/stop/status/enable/disable + launchd/systemd autostart)
body:
## What

The shared **`agenttools_service`** lib — one reusable service-manager so every long-running server in the ecosystem (review dashboard, config-web, tg-ctl, future daemons) gets identical lifecycle subcommands instead of hand-rolling them. This is the foundation a prior workflow's dashboard agent already imports; the lib PR died 10x on a transient throttle and never landed, leaving that import unsatisfied. This lands it.

## Public interface

```python
from agenttools_service import Service, ServiceManager, add_service_subcommands, dispatch

Service(name, argv, port=None, host="127.0.0.1", tool=None, description="", home=None)
  # -> .pidfile (~/.local/state/<tool>/<name>.pid), .logfile (~/.cache/<tool>/<name>.log),
  #    .url, .label, .systemd_unit_name, .state_dir, .cache_dir

ServiceManager(service, platform=…, has_systemctl=None, autostart=None, spawner=…, runner=…,
               alive=…, signaller=…, foreground_runner=…)
  .run()      -> int                 # foreground/blocking
  .start()    -> ServiceStatus       # detached background daemon, writes pidfile
  .status()   -> ServiceStatus        # {running, state, pid, port, url, enabled}
  .stop()     -> bool
  .enable()   -> ServiceStatus       # install OS autostart AND start now
  .disable()  -> ServiceStatus       # remove OS autostart AND stop

add_service_subcommands(subparsers, *, manager_factory, service_name, help_text=None)
dispatch(args, *, on_no_subcommand) -> int     # bare invocation = HELP, never launches
run_action(manager, action) -> int             # exit codes 0/3/4/127
```

Autostart backends: `LaunchdBackend` (macOS LaunchAgent), `SystemdUserBackend` (Linux `--user` unit), `NoopAutostartBackend` (no-systemd fallback). `select_autostart_backend(...)` picks by OS. Pure unit generators `render_launchd_plist` / `render_systemd_unit` are directly tested.

## Design

- **Single-owner, no double-start**: when launchd/systemd owns the process (`RunAtLoad` / `enable --now`), the manager does NOT also pidfile-spawn it.
- **Idempotent + removable**: re-`enable` overwrites the unit in place; `disable` is a no-op when absent. install/uninstall gate on the control-command rc so a failed `launchctl`/`systemctl` is never reported as enabled and never orphans a unit.
- **Fail-closed validation**: slug name/tool, no control chars in argv/description/host (path-traversal + systemd-unit-injection guards); rejects empty `tool` and whitespace-bearing `host`.
- **Stdlib-only** except `agenttools-daemon` (reused for the pidfile machinery, not reimplemented).

## Tests

98 unit tests under a tmp HOME with a fake runner + fake spawner — **no real autostart, no real process, no network**. Covers start/stop/status/enable/disable, launchd/systemd install/uninstall (incl. failure-reports-false), unit generation/escaping, and all validation. mypy-clean on the source. Full repo suite: 513 passed, 6 skipped.

## Review

title: feat(lib): shared help-formatter (agenttools_help) + error/exit-code layer (agenttools_errors)
body:
Implements the ROADMAP item **"ONE shared help-formatter in agent-tools/lib"** + the shared error/exit-code layer (error-system v2). Two new stdlib-only nested-pyproject lib modules — the shared foundation; **no CLI is refitted** (separate follow-up).

## `agenttools_help` — one shared help formatter
Help built as **data** so the help-clarity rules live in one place and a fix lands everywhere:
- `Palette` — one ANSI scheme (semantic roles), `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`/TTY precedence.
- `HelpFormatter` — banner, usage line(s), subcommands list, option sections; `.render()`.
- **ACTUAL defaults** — `Option(default=…)`; a switch with no default shows none (no misleading "default: none").
- **Scoped** subcommand options — `Section(scope="run")` → `options for \`run\`:`, can't leak into the global block.
- **Topic-help** — `TopicRegistry` → `<tool> help <topic>`, advertised in the main help (replaces bespoke `--format-help` flags).
- **Install-state** — `InstallState` + ✓ / ○ / ⚠ glyphs (configured / pending / conflict).
- `options_from_argparse` — harvest an existing argparse parser's flags (single-source).
- ANSI-safe wrapping: color applied **after** `textwrap`, whitespace normalized so annotation-coloring offsets never drift.

## `agenttools_errors` — one shared error/exit-code layer
- `AgentToolError` + per-class subclasses; 3-part **what / why / how-to-fix** message.
- **Stable per-class EXIT CODES** as a public contract (`0/1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8/127`), matching rig's numbering so rig can adopt without renumbering. `EXIT_CODES` table for `--help`.
- `render()` — the 3-part block; **sanitizes control / C1 / bidi chars** from user-controlled fields before printing (ANSI/spoofing defense), our own color codes added after.
- `guard()` — renders + returns the stable code; normalizes a missing/bool return to `EXIT_INTERNAL`; never swallows real bugs (they propagate).
- `did_you_mean` (length-prefiltered Levenshtein), per-tool `RemovedSlotRegistry`, and the unknown-item / missing-dep / missing-target / not-a-repo builders.
- Exceptions stay **hashable + identity-equal** (`@dataclass(eq=False)`) and round-trip their full payload through **pickle/copy** (`__reduce__` over `dataclasses.fields`).

## Quality
- Stdlib-only at import (argparse lazy-imported); both **build as wheels** and import cleanly.
- **164 module tests** across the two suites; **full suite 677 passing, 6 skipped**.
- Reviewed with `review diff --staged -m glm` (multiple rounds; all correctness/security findings fixed — remaining items are non-blocking test-coverage / two-module-duplication polish, the modules being independent dists by design).

title: feat(skills): add universal adversarial-verification skill
body:
## Motivation / user value

Migrates the HyperIDE rule *"Адверсариальная проверка (доказательство от обратного)"*
(`docs/rules/development.md`, Stage 3) into the agent-tools universal skill catalog as a
generic, parameterized, product-agnostic writing-skill. Closes the gap where agents
"verify" a fix by confirming the happy path instead of trying to break it — the most
common way a fix ships that only ever worked on the one input that was tried.

## Carrier choice (enforced mechanism)

Per [`docs/carrier-decision-guide.md`](docs/carrier-decision-guide.md), this is a
**pure-judgment rule** ("did you try to break it", "is this an artifact or restated
intent", "name the floor") with no mechanical check that captures it. The strictest
*honest* carrier is therefore a **skill** — a gate or hook here would be all false
positives (you cannot regex "try to refute the claim"). This matches its siblings
`gan-critic-loop` and `visual-proof-cycle`, which are also skill-only. Universal skills
are scanned live by `rig` and installed by default (`skills.universal.all`), so dropping
the directory is the registration — no central registry edit needed.

## What it says

- **Attack the claim** — construct the input where it MUST fail (empty/null/boundary/
  malformed/concurrent), don't wait for a counterexample to wander in.
- A **"no longer happens" / "always works"** claim demands a refutation attempt; if a
  counterexample is found, decide intended-boundary vs bug; if not, document which cases
  were tried.
- **Proof = artifact** (rendered DOM, generated output, test run, screenshot), not "the
  helper returns empty" / "correct by construction". Walk the real path end-to-end.
- **Name the floor** — state explicitly where the fix does NOT hold.

Cross-links `gan-critic-loop` (separate the attacker from the author) and
`visual-proof-cycle` (look at the real render).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `skills/universal/adversarial-verification/SKILL.md` authored, English-only, no Cyrillic
- [x] writing-skills format: `name`/`description` frontmatter, `name` == directory, "Use when…" trigger
- [x] Generic / parameterized — no HyperIDE product specifics
- [x] Cross-links `gan-critic-loop` and `visual-proof-cycle` (both resolve to real dirs)
- [x] GREEN-verified: frontmatter parses, no duplicate skill name, full repo suite green
- [x] README inventory count reconciled to the on-disk total (verified by artifact, not arithmetic)
- [x] Pre-commit `review -m glm` ran on the final diff; committed without `--no-verify`

## Proof (this is a docs/prose skill — behavioral proof, not a screenshot)

Adversarial self-check of the README count finding (the skill eating its own dog food):
glm's review claimed the count should be 38 by *arithmetic* (old 37 + 1 new). I refused
the arithmetic and walked the real path — the on-disk artifact:

```
$ find skills/universal -name SKILL.md -type f | wc -l                       # 39 (with new)
$ find skills/universal -name SKILL.md -type f | grep -v adversarial- | wc -l # 38 (before)
```

The README's "37" was already stale by 1 from a prior merge; the correct post-addition
total is **39**, proven by the filesystem, not by trusting the old number. Full suite:
`707 passed, 9 skipped` (pytest exit 0).

title: feat(skills): universal-mandatory learn-from-feedback skill
body:
## What

Adds `skills/universal/learn-from-feedback/SKILL.md` — a **mandatory-always** universal skill (same tier as `delegate-work-to-subagents`), provisioned to every project/user by rig's `skills.universal.all` default-on layer plus a strong always-triggering frontmatter `description`. No per-repo registry edit needed; dropping it in `skills/universal/` IS the mechanism (per AGENTS.md "universal skills layer").

Implements the ROADMAP item **"MISSING universal-mandatory skill: extract lessons from process mistakes + user complaints."**

## Trigger

Any user complaint / correction / visible frustration ("again", "third time", "I keep telling you", "stop doing this", "you always/never"), a silent re-ask for the same thing, OR a self-noticed repeated process failure.

## Mandate (three steps, every time)

1. **Name the root cause — the general class, not the surface instance** ("I run destructive git ops without checking state", not "I force-pushed over their branch").
2. **Extract the generalizable lesson** — the rule that prevents the whole family of failures on tasks you can't foresee.
3. **Record it durably** — a MEMORY.md memory file (behavioral how-I-work lesson), a ROADMAP/ticket entry (implies a fix/follow-up), or escalate to a hook/rule/config (mechanizable) per `promise-durable-action` — then confirm the write landed.

Cross-links `promise-durable-action` (a verbal "I'll be careful" is empty — turn it into a mechanism now) and `task-completion-selfcheck` (confirm the lesson was recorded, not just the instance patched). Both cross-referenced skills verified present in-repo (no dangling refs).

## Acceptance evidence (RED/GREEN per writing-skills)

**RED (baseline, no skill).** Two complaint pressure-scenarios via `claude -p` subagents:
- *"THIRD time you force-pushed over my branch and wiped my commits"* → agent recovered the instance / offered one hook, but **never named the class root cause and never recorded a durable lesson**.
- *"You keep writing giant 600-line functions… every single PR"* → same: patched the symptom, no generalizable-lesson artifact.

**GREEN (skill loaded).** Same two scenarios → both runs executed **all three mandatory steps**: named the root cause as a class, stated the generalized rule (`--force-with-lease` only / function-length guard), created a durable MEMORY entry + pointer and **read it back to confirm it landed**, and proposed the mechanizable escalation gated on consent. Behavior measurably shifted from "apologize + patch instance" to "patch instance + record lesson".

**Format / hygiene:**
- English-only — zero Cyrillic (`grep -P '[\x{0400}-\x{04FF}]'` clean).
- Frontmatter `description` 408 chars (< 500 target).
- Follows writing-skills SKILL.md structure (overview, trigger, mandatory steps, quick-reference table, common mistakes, why).

**Suite green:** full `pytest tests/` → **707 passed, 9 skipped** (the `ci/tests` merge gate). Change is markdown-only; the pre-existing `ruff F401` in `lib/agenttools_help/core.py` is on origin/main untouched and out of scope (smallest-change).

title: feat(agent-hooks): 5 enforcement-doctrine PreToolUse hooks (orchestration + skills + visual proof)
body:
## What

Implements the flagship CTO 2026-06-17 ask from ROADMAP — **"DOCTRINE: enforce correct agent behavior with PreToolUse hooks (rig-provisioned), not prompts/promises"**. Behavioral rules that live only in prose regress; this encodes five of them as `agents-hooks/v1` **PreToolUse** descriptors, carried into Claude Code via `lib/cc_hook_bridge`.

## The five hooks

| # | hook | point | behavior |
|---|------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `background-subagent-gate` | `pre-agent` | block a non-trivial **foreground** subagent dispatch → set `run_in_background:true` or use a Workflow |
| 2 | `orchestrator-stays-thin` | `pre-write` + `pre-bash` | warn→block the main thread doing a non-docs code Edit/Write or implementation-shaped multi-step Bash |
| 3 | `no-long-inline-process` | `pre-bash` | hard-block `review` / `*--watch` / build-test suites / long `sleep` in the orchestrator |
| 4 | `skills-read-gate` | `pre-bash` | warn→block a commit/build when mandatory skills have no fresh invocation marker |
| 5 | `visual-proof-gate` | `pre-bash` | block a commit staging user-visible files with no looked-at-screenshot marker |

## Doctrine compliance (the "fighting rigidity" requirements)

- **Satisfiable** by an honest action — invoke the skill / touch the proof marker / set `run_in_background:true` / use the documented escape.
- **Tiered** — gates 2 & 4 WARN first (per-`(cwd, point)` marker) then BLOCK; gate 3 is a clear-cut hard block; gates 1 & 5 block with a satisfiable path.
- **Subagent-exempt** (gates 1-3) via a reliable signal: CC's top-level `agent_id`/`agent_type`, forwarded by the bridge. A `tool_input`-**forged** `agent_id` is dropped so it can't self-exempt the orchestrator.
- **Honest escape hatch** — `ALLOW_*=1` + a REQUIRED `ALLOW_*_REASON`, and/or an inline `# *-ok: reason` sentinel; a reasonless override still blocks (mirrors `block-raw-pr-merge`).

## Bridge change (`lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`)

- New `pre-agent` point for the `Agent`/`Task` tools.
- Forward top-level `agent_id`/`agent_type` into the v1 event (the main-vs-subagent signal); drop any `tool_input`-injected copy.

> **rig-cli follow-up (separate repo):** for CC to actually *fire* `pre-agent`, rig-cli must add an `Agent|Task` PreToolUse matcher to `settings.json` (`hook_bridge_entries`). The bridge half (point mapping + signal forwarding) lives here; the docs annotate `pre-agent` as **bridge-ready, not yet live in CC**.

## Tests

819 passed, 9 skipped (pre-existing optional-dep skips). Per hook: block + allow + subagent-exempt (1-3) + escape; plus bridge routing/forwarding/forgery-drop and regex-anchoring edge cases. Three rounds of `review diff --staged` (glm) addressed: chained-command bypass, unanchored build/commit/sleep regexes, forged-agent_id precedence, and a cross-harness trust-boundary doc contract.

## Registration

All five added to the `AGENTS.md` and `agent-hooks/README.md` hook tables.

title: feat(skills+hooks): model-fallback skill + cross-harness error-fallback hook
body:
## What

Implements the **Model-fallback skill + cross-harness hooks** roadmap item: a universal-mandatory skill and an `agents-hooks/v1` error-detection hook that auto-fall down a cross-harness chain when the main model hits repeated transient errors (rate-limit / overload / API 5xx), instead of stalling, dying, or cutting fan-out.

```
claude:fable -> claude:opus -> oc:GLM-5.2 -> codex:gpt5.5
```

The chain deliberately crosses harnesses so a whole-provider outage (an Anthropic throttle) routes onto a different provider's quota. This is the throttle that killed agents today — retry, then fall to a different provider.

## Deliverables

- **`skills/universal/model-fallback/SKILL.md`** — mandatory tier (rig provisions by default), English-only, writing-skills format, RED/GREEN-verified. The discipline: classify first (only a *transient model error* counts — a failing test/refusal does not), retry a few times, drop to the next entry on the Nth consecutive error, surface the active model, return to the top on recovery, fail loud at chain end.
- **`agent-hooks/model-error-fallback/`** — the enforcement hook:
  - `fallback_chain.py` — pure, dependency-free error-count / threshold / swap / redispatch / recover / exhaustion state machine (the unit-tested, load-bearing half).
  - `model_error_fallback.py` — the `agents-hooks/v1` stop-hook I/O shell. In-harness = model swap; cross-harness = `redispatch_to` on a **fall** (re-run failed work elsewhere) or `prefer_next` on a cross-harness **recover** (work already done — switch preference, never re-run). Fail-open on every path.
  - `model-error-fallback.stop.json` descriptor + `README.md`.
- **One chain definition** — `lib/contracts/models.yaml` grows `fallback_chain:` (+ a `fallbackStep` `$def` in the schema), read by every harness (cc/codex/oc/pi) so they agree on priority. The baked-in default mirrors it for offline use.

## Key behaviors

- Classification isolated to the **error channel** (`error_text`/`detail`); `output`/`message` are never classified, so an agent writing about "rate limiting" isn't misread as hitting one.
- An explicit truthy `error`/`model_error` wins over `success` — a coarse host can't mask a real error and starve the fallback.
- Transient regex: 429 / 500-504 / 520-524 (Cloudflare) / 529 (Anthropic overloaded); rejects refusals ("no/great capacity") and 501.
- Fail-open: unreadable/corrupt snapshot, unavailable state dir, non-object stdin, non-dict args all reset-and-allow, never crash. Structured `exhausted` flag at chain end.

## Tests

`tests/test_model_error_fallback.py` — the full state machine, classifier, manifest+schema validation, snapshot round-trip + corruption, and the hook protocol incl. every fail-open path. **Full suite green** (900 with pyyaml+jsonschema, 815 CI-style; ruff clean). Reviewed across multiple opus rounds; all substantive findings fixed; known limitations (no file-lock, no state-dir TTL, recovery needs an explicit success signal) documented in the hook README.

Builds on the merged `agenttools_providers` failover; pairs with the transient-rate-limit lesson (retry-then-fallback, not reduce-fan-out).

title: feat(agent-hooks): no-shell-file-edit pre-bash gate (block sed -i/perl -i/awk in-place + redirect onto a tracked source)
body:
## What

A new `pre-bash` agent-hook that enforces the hyperide rule **"edits only via Edit/Write; no `sed`/`perl`/`awk` for editing files."** A shell in-place edit or a redirect that overwrites a tracked source file bypasses Edit/Write — no reviewable diff, no formatter, no file-state tracking. This hook hard-blocks that and points the agent at Edit/Write, with a controllable escape hatch.

## Blocked (each decided from a PARSED command — never a raw substring)

- in-place stream editor on a tracked source file: `sed -i`, `perl -i`/`-pi`, `gawk -i inplace`, clustered `-Ei`/`-ri`/`-ni`, `--in-place`, `-i.bak`
- `>`/`>>` redirect onto a tracked source file — incl. glued operators (`app.ts>app.ts`), bash `>|` and zsh `>!` force-clobber, `>& file`, fd-numbered (`2> app.ts`)
- `tee FILE` / `tee -a` / `dd of=FILE` writing a tracked source file
- the same wrapped in `bash -c '…'` / `sh -c '…'` (incl. nesting + the outer redirect), `$(…)` / backtick substitutions, leading `VAR=val` and `timeout`/`env`/`command`/`exec`/`builtin` wrappers, and shell glob / brace expansion

## Allowed

Read-only `sed`/`awk`/`grep` filters, `gawk -i json` (non-inplace include), `>&2` fd-dups, writes to `/tmp` or new/non-source files, and the raw-string decoys (the flag inside a string / comment / commit message).

## Not a raw-string match

The command is heredoc-stripped, comment-stripped (quote- AND comment-aware), split on real shell separators, shlex-tokenized, and the in-place flag / redirect target are read off the argv — closing the #59 raw-substring bypass class. `on_error: open` (a parse/scan failure fails toward allow, never wedging the tool call).

## Tests

100+ cases in `tests/test_no_shell_file_edit.py` run against a **real temp git repo** (block / allow / decoys / escape hatch / documented scope boundaries / fail-open branches). Full suite green (1117 passed, 11 skipped).

## Review

7 rounds of `review diff --staged` (claude-opus-4-8); each surfaced finding was fixed: heredoc-in-quotes/comment bypass, brace expansion, zsh `>!`, plus doc/test cleanups. Final round: no bugs, no regressions, no security issues; fail-open branches covered.

body:
## What

Migrates the **CTO decision-request discipline** (from hyperide `docs/rules/cto-decision-requests.md`, Russian) into agent-tools as an enforced, advertised mechanism. Part of CTO request **#4133** (migrate hyperide rules into agent-tools as ENFORCED mechanisms, advertised, not just skills). Translated to English; **zero Cyrillic** in all repo files.

## Primary deliverable — the skill (the behavioral core)

`skills/universal/decision-request-discipline/SKILL.md` — when/how an agent escalates a product/architecture decision to the human (CTO):

- **Brainstorm-first** across a model quorum; escalate ONLY on genuine model disagreement or an irreversible high-blast-radius call. A quorum-settled question forwarded as "A or B?" is a violation.
- **Never relabel a product feature as a risk/vuln/hazard** — name the concrete harm or it isn't a risk.
- The **open-PR-mention trigger**, the **mandatory pre-question self-check**, the **consult chain**, the **out-of-band channel** (Telegram) requirement.
- The strict **8-point question format** (context, glossary, problem, options with REAL pros/cons, recommendation, where-to-look refs, screenshots, pseudocode).
- The **"child-repo diff as formatted Telegram text, never a raw `.patch`"** rule with its `tg` workarounds (neutral cwd, `TG_AI_MODEL=claude`, ≤3000-char chunks) and the PR-base-derived diff command.
- The **PR-or-drop** required fields.

Structure/tone/frontmatter mirror the existing universal skills (`learn-from-feedback`, `adversarial-verification`, `promise-durable-action`, `strict-ticket-discipline`).

## Secondary — an advisory hook (honest assessment of what's enforceable)

`agent-hooks/decision-request-format/` (pre-bash, `on_error=open`). A behavioral escalation norm is mostly NOT deterministically enforceable — but ONE part is: at **send time**, a `tg --tag decision …` is a concrete, parseable trigger. The hook parses the message body (shlex, **not** raw-string matching — reusing the `_unwrap_segment`/wrapper-peel discipline of the `no-shell-file-edit`/`no-long-inline-process` siblings; also peels a bare `NAME=VALUE` prefix since the skill literally prescribes `TG_AI_MODEL=claude tg …`) and, if it's missing the structural markers (Context / Options / Recommendation), emits an **exit-0 ADVISORY** naming what's absent.

**It is advisory, never a hard block** — a malformed decision request must stay *sendable*; wedging the send would be worse than the malformed message. The value it adds over the skill alone is purely **timing**: it fires at the exact moment the skill's self-check is supposed to run but routinely gets skipped under load — the one moment a skill can't act. **NOT subagent-exempt** (the skill routes the *drafting* to a subagent, so the check binds it too). Escape hatch: `ALLOW_RAW_DECISION_REQUEST=1` or inline `# decision-request-ok: <reason>`.

I did **not** build a hard-blocking hook for show — a hard block on a heuristic body-check would be dishonest enforcement. The advisory is the strictest mechanism that's genuinely correct here.

## Advertising

Added to the **AGENTS.md pre-bash hooks table** (additive, localized to the hooks section so it merges cleanly alongside the concurrent require-review edits). The **skill is deliberately NOT added to a skills table**: this repo's own convention (AGENTS.md "universal skills layer" + README) is that universal skills are a default-on rig layer advertised via each skill's frontmatter trigger + the SessionStart blurb — *never* listed in AGENTS.md, since duplicating pins a stale copy. Listing it would contradict that.

Two related fixes to `agent-hooks/require-review-before-commit/require_review.py`, one PR.

## (A) ROADMAP "require-review-before-commit too broad"
The gate fired on docs-only commits and on `git stash`, and honored no per-commit skip.

- **Docs-only diffs ALLOW without a marker** — every staged path is documentation: a doc
  extension (`*.md`/`*.mdx`/`*.markdown`/`*.rst`/`*.adoc`/`*.rdoc`/`*.pod`) anywhere, or a
  non-code file under a `docs/` dir. Source/script/config is **never** docs (a `*.py`,
  `docs/conf.py`, `docs/Makefile`, or a top-level `requirements.txt` still gates).
- **Real per-commit skip read from the COMMAND** — inline `REVIEW_SKIP=1 git commit …` (scoped
  to the commit segment), or a `[skip-review: <reason>]` commit-message trailer.
- **Non-commit git ops are not gated** — `git stash`, `git worktree`, `git status`, `git add`.

## (B) SECURITY (task #20) — the skip-flag check was bypassable
`SKIP_COMMIT.search(command)` ran on the **raw** Bash string, so a `--continue/--abort/--skip`
token in a shell comment / commit message / pathspec / sibling command bypassed the REVIEW gate.
Ported the proper-parsing `is_skip_commit` that landed in #59 (`visual-proof-gate` /
`skills-read-gate`) and hardened it well beyond:

- shlex tokenization with `punctuation_chars` — splits **glued** separators (`a&&git`, `|&`,
  `;&`), handles **multi-line / CRLF** commands (newline = separator), and **word-boundary**
  comment stripping (a glued `#` is a literal, not a comment).
- scope every check to the **real `git commit` segment** (executable IS git, incl. absolute
  path); `git config commit.gpgsign` / `git help commit` / `git commit-graph` never match.
- the argv parser is the **sole authority** (no regex pre-filter that could early-allow).
- strip **every value-flag's value** — a skip token in `--author '--skip'` / `--date` / `-C` /
  `--fixup` can't forge an exemption; stop at `--` (pathspec); strip shell redirects.
- docs fast-path also **forfeits** when the commit draws beyond the index: `-a`/`-am`,
  `-p`/`--patch`/`--interactive`, `--pathspec-from-file`, an explicit pathspec, a
  `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`/inline `GIT_DIR=` redirect, or a staging op earlier in the chain.

**Documented limit:** a program-wrapped commit (`sudo`/`env`/`bash -c`/subshell) is not gated —
`on_error: open`, process discipline, not a security boundary.

## Tests
70 require-review tests in `tests/test_require_review.py` (docs-only-allowed, REVIEW_SKIP/trailer
honored, stash/worktree ungated, every bypass closed — comment/message/pathspec/sibling, glued
separators, value-flag-value skip token, multi-line/CRLF, chain staging, index-extending flags).
Full pytest suite green (1104 passed). Reviewed across multiple rounds with
`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8`; every flagged bypass closed.

title: fix(ci/ship): harden ship.sh against exit-128 (multi-worktree + non-masking cleanup)
body:
Salvages two genuinely-unshipped, real `ci/ship/ship.sh` hardening fixes (re-derived clean against current `main`, covered by new hermetic tests). These are the exact exit-128 failures that make a clean squash-merge look like a failed ship.

## Fix 1 — multi-worktree handling
A branch can be checked out in **more than one** worktree (git permits it; a stray/leftover tree often lingers). `main` resolved the branch to a single `$WT` via awk `$2`, which **concatenated two paths into one string** — feeding that to `git -C` / `git worktree remove` exit-128 d.

Now collect **all** matching worktrees into a `WTS=()` array and iterate:
- bash-3.2 compatible (stock macOS bash is 3.2) — every empty-array expansion guarded with the `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` idiom so `set -u` does not trip;
- awk `substr($0,10)` instead of `$2`, so a **space in the worktree path** is not truncated (and Apple git 2.39 s missing `-z` porcelain variant is not needed).

## Fix 2 — cleanup must not mask merge success
Post-merge housekeeping (remote-branch delete, worktree/branch removal, main refresh) used to abort the script on any non-zero, so a **successful squash-merge reported as a FAILED ship** (the exit-128 that made clean ships look broken).

Cleanup now runs in a function with `set +e`: each step **warns but never propagates**; the merge is reported first and cleanup can only warn (`cleanup || warn` belt-and-suspenders).

## Tests — `tests/test_ship.py` (new, hermetic)
Temp git repo + a fake `gh` on PATH (no network, no real PR). Three tests:
1. two worktrees on one branch do **not** exit-128 (both removed individually);
2. a successful merge is **still reported** when a worktree cannot be removed — asserts the warn-don t-abort path actually fired (so it cannot go false-green);
3. a **spaced-path** worktree is collected and removed (covers the `$2 → substr($0,10)` fix).

All three **fail against the old `ci/ship/ship.sh` and pass against the fixed one** (verified by swapping the script and re-running).

## Scope / verification
- Touches **only** `ci/ship/ship.sh` (+76/-33) and `tests/test_ship.py` (new). Nothing else.
- `shellcheck ci/ship/ship.sh`: only the pre-existing SC2016 info note on the GraphQL query (identical on `main`), nothing introduced.

title: feat(skills): evidence-first ticket-documentation standard in strict-ticket-discipline
body:
## What

Migrates the hyperide `ticket-documentation-standard` (CTO request #4133) into agent-tools by **extending** the universal `strict-ticket-discipline` skill. Source: `hyperide/docs/rules/ticket-documentation-standard.md` (Russian), translated to English; zero Cyrillic, no transliterated examples.

## Structure decision: extend, not a companion skill

The on-main skill already covered Motivation / Acceptance / User-impact / commit-reference. This PR adds the distinctive **evidence-first 6-section standard** as a new `## What a ticket must contain` section plus a `## Do not` block:

1. **What is concretely wrong** — pinned with `file:line` or the exact misbehaving user action ("X does Y when it should do Z").
2. **Evidence captured FIRST, at creation time** — the load-bearing rule: UI bug -> a Playwright/Docker screenshot of the broken state (never `screencapture`); CI/gate failure -> failing run output / finding count; pure logic -> offending snippet + failing repro. "Before" mandatory at creation; "after" follows once fixed. If a proof genuinely can't exist yet, say so and capture current/broken behavior.
3. **Where this came from** — origin: session / audit / review / brainstorm + related ticket/PR/migration.
4. **What happens if we don't do it** — concrete consequence + how it hurts the USER specifically.
5. **Acceptance criteria** — checkbox list, each provable, each naming its proof method.
6. **Pseudocode** — minimal, when the fix shape is non-obvious.

A single richer skill avoids two overlapping skills. Cross-linked to `visual-proof-cycle` (the capture, applied at ticket time), `adversarial-verification` (trust the proof, not your assertion), `deferred-findings-tracking`, `promise-durable-action` — all verified to exist.

## No AGENTS.md edit

Universal skills are a default-on rig layer, discovered by the `SKILL.md` file itself; they are deliberately NOT listed in AGENTS.md (listing pins a stale copy — AGENTS.md line 171 makes `skills/universal/` the source of truth). Extending an existing skill therefore needs no advertising edit.

## No hook enforcement (intentional)

This is a behavioral norm -> the skill is the correct mechanism. An evidence-*presence* hard block is heuristic and impractical: you cannot reliably detect from a commit whether a real screenshot is attached to a Linear ticket. The existing `require-ticket-before-commit` hook already enforces the ticket-*reference* half; gating on evidence presence would be fake enforcement, so it's omitted by design.

## CI

`uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests/` (the exact `.github/workflows/tests.yml` gate; `TEST_PATHS=tests`) -> **1302 passed, 11 skipped**. There is no `tests/smoke.sh` in this repo; the pytest suite is the full gate. Doc-only change; nothing regressed.

title: fix(ci/ship): self-clean PR worktree+branch when shipping from inside it
body:
## Problem
When `gh ship` / `ci/ship/ship.sh` runs from INSIDE the PR's own worktree, the post-merge cleanup's SELF-guard refused to `git worktree remove` the tree out from under the running session — so a successful squash-merge left BOTH the local worktree AND the merged local branch behind. Across a swarm session these orphan worktrees pile up (the source of the 34->2 hygiene-sweep debt).

## Fix
After the merge succeeds, cleanup now RE-ROOTS into the main checkout (`cd "$MAIN_CHECKOUT"`) before removing the PR's worktree + local branch — you can remove a worktree once you're no longer inside it. The process's cwd becomes the deleted dir, but since we've already cd'd to main, the rest of cleanup and the script's exit are valid. A caller-contract NOTE on stderr tells the parent shell its cwd is gone so it can `cd` out.

Builds directly on #64's `cleanup()`.

## Safety (does NOT regress #64)
- Keeps multi-worktree array collection (bash-3.2-safe empty-array guard) and cleanup-failure-never-masks-merge (`set +e`, warn-don't-abort, always exit 0 post-merge).
- Hardens the dirty-tree guard to apply to ALL worktrees: confirm clean (`git status` succeeds AND empty) before any destructive op; never force-remove or detach an unverified/dirty tree; skip re-root when there's no distinct main checkout (or it's nested under the worktree).
- Cross-repo/fork ship still leaves the fork's branch alone.

## Tests (`tests/test_ship.py`, extends #64's file)
ship-from-inside-the-worktree self-clean (worktree + branch removed, exit 0, valid cwd); dry-run no-op + no false NOTE; two-worktree self-clean; dirty-self and dirty-non-self left in place; no-reroot-target leave; self-removed-but-branch-kept interaction.

Full repo suite: **1310 passed, 11 skipped**. `shellcheck -S warning` clean; `bash -n` clean.

## Poetic justice
This PR's own ship will exercise exactly this code path (shipping from inside the worktree) — the feature dogfoods itself.

title: fix(agent-hooks): parse commands in block-no-verify instead of raw-regex
body:
## Motivation

`block-no-verify` was the last enforcement-hook sibling still matching the raw
command string with a flat regex (the #59 family — visual-proof-gate,
skills-read-gate, no-long-inline-process — and require-review-before-commit
were already converted to proper argv parsing). The raw-regex approach had two
real failure modes, both observed live this session:

- **Over-fire (false positive):** a flag-like token or trigger word inside a
  message body, a quoted argument, or a sibling command in a chain tripped the
  gate. A real shipping commit was false-blocked twice because its message
  mentioned the flag the hook looks for.
- **Under-fire (false negative / bypass):** a genuine skip flag hidden via a
  wrapper or quoting slipped past the flat regex, defeating the gate.

## What changed

Port the #59 argv-parsing discipline to `block_no_verify.py`: peel wrappers,
split on real separators, parse the actual subcommand and its flags. The
hook-skip flag is flagged only as a real parsed flag on a real commit/push
segment. For push, only the long form is a skip (the bare short flag there is
dry-run). The hooksPath config override stays blocked, parsed as a real config
arg, never as a substring of a message. Fail-closed on unparseable input.

## Acceptance

- [x] message body / quoted arg / sibling command containing the trigger words → allowed (FP fixed)
- [x] real skip flag (bare, clustered, wrapped, positioned) → blocked (FN fixed)
- [x] push bare short flag (dry-run) → allowed; push long-form skip → blocked
- [x] hooksPath override → blocked as a parsed arg
- [x] unparseable command → fail-closed (blocked)
- [x] 143 unit tests pass; full suite green

Closes the last raw-string-match sibling in the enforcement-hook family.

title: fix(ci/ship): abort early + clearly on a core.bare=true working checkout
body:
## What

Add an **early guard** to the shared `ci/ship/ship.sh` (used by agent-tools, rig-cli, review-cli) that aborts clearly when a **working** checkout has `git config core.bare = true` — a real corruption class (external cause; rig-cli #19/#52 detect + `--fix` it).

## Why

Under `core.bare=true`, every git op in a working tree fails fatal with `this operation must be run in a work tree`. ship.sh's post-merge main-refresh / worktree ops then failed **confusingly mid-ship** (it bit a real ship this session). The guard catches it **before** any destructive git op and aborts with `exit 1` (ship's uniform `Refusing:` preflight code), naming the repo + the one-line fix — rather than auto-fixing (ship must not silently rewrite repo config).

## Guard points (all pre-merge)

- **cwd (subdir-robust)** — fires before `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` would die bare. Distinguishes a corrupt working checkout from a **genuine bare repo** (or a subdir of one) via `rev-parse --is-inside-git-dir` + an ancestor-`.git` walk, so it never false-positives on a legitimate bare repo nor recommends the bare-breaking `core.bare false` there.
- **main checkout** (`SHIP_MAIN_CHECKOUT`) — guards the post-merge refresh target.
- **each linked PR worktree** — catches **worktree-scoped** `core.bare=true` (`extensions.worktreeConfig` + `config --worktree core.bare true`), which the main guard misses and which would make the dirty-check read a corrupt tree as "clean" (swallowed fatal) and risk removing unshipped work.

The printed fix is **scope-aware** (`--worktree` form for worktree-scoped corruption, else shared-config form) and **shell-quoted** so it's paste-safe for paths with spaces, `$`, or single quotes.

Preserves #64's "cleanup never masks merge success" and #68's self-clean invariants. bash 3.2 compatible.

## Tests (`tests/test_ship.py`)

core.bare main / cwd-root / cwd-subdir abort early with the diagnostic + nonzero exit; healthy repo, genuine-bare-repo root + subdir, and a genuine-bare-repo linked worktree do **not** trip the guard; a worktree-scoped-corrupted linked worktree aborts and its printed `--worktree` fix round-trips to repair it; the special-char-path fix command is paste-safe (round-trips through a shell).

## Verification

title: fix(agent-hooks): close block-no-verify sudo value-flag bypass + over-block (#69 follow-up)
body:
## Motivation

#69 ported `block-no-verify` to argv parsing but shipped two regressions, both
verified live:

- **BYPASS (#36, security):** `sudo -u git git commit --no-verify` was **allowed**.
  The wrapper unwrap mis-took the `-u` operand value (`git`) for the wrapped
  executable and stopped peeling, so the real `git commit --no-verify` behind it was
  never inspected. Probe against merged main (`df4906c`): `decision: allow`.
- **OVER-BLOCK (#37):** benign commands carrying a `commit`/`mergeCommit` substring
  or awkward quoting (`gh pr view N --json mergeCommit`, `git merge --no-verify`,
  `git commit -m "merge commit cleanup"`) fail-closed-blocked. This bit real verify
  commands this session.

## What changed

- Model **per-wrapper value-consuming flags** — sudo `-u/-g/-c/...`, timeout `-s/-k`,
  nice/ionice/taskset operands — and skip the operand slot **without** the
  `_is_git_executable` guard: the user/group may legitimately be named `git` (two
  `git` tokens: the `-u` value, then the real executable). Boolean wrapper flags that
  look value-like (`sudo -s` = run a shell, not an operand) are NOT treated as value
  flags, so they can't eat the wrapped git and open a *new* bypass.
- Parse the real git subcommand + flags instead of substring-matching trigger words,
  killing the over-block. `--no-verify`/`-n` is flagged only as a real parsed flag on
  a real commit/push segment (push: long form only — bare `-n` there is dry-run).
- Fail-closed on genuinely unparseable input is preserved.

## Verification

- `sudo -u git git commit --no-verify` → **block**; `sudo -u git git status` → allow
- `sudo git commit --no-verify` → block; `git commit --no-verify` / `-n` → block
- `gh pr view N --json mergeCommit` / `git merge --no-verify` / message with
  `merge commit` → **allow**
- +410 test lines (sudo-value bypass, per-wrapper value/boolean separation, mandatory
  operand wrappers, over-block message/quoting). **318 hook tests + full suite 1628
  passed, 11 skipped.**
- Gate review (claude-opus-4-8): no blocking findings — "mergeable as-is".

## Known limitation (documented, by design)

`runuser -u git -- git commit --no-verify` and other unlisted privilege wrappers stay
bypassable — pinned by `test_known_limitation_unlisted_privilege_wrappers_not_gated`
and justified by the same doctrine as `bash -c`: this gate is **process discipline,
not a security boundary**. Tightening the privilege-wrapper set tracked as a follow-up.
