title: fix(agent-hooks): gate runuser's direct-exec form in block-no-verify (sudo sibling)
body:
## Motivation

#36/#69 closed `sudo -u git git commit --no-verify`, and the gate-review on #71 flagged
`runuser` as "the most live uncovered vector." Its **direct-exec** form slipped
(confirmed on `origin/main`, `decision: allow`):

```
runuser -u git -- git commit --no-verify     # -u user [--] command: execs the command directly
```

## What changed

Gate `runuser` like `sudo`, from the authoritative **man7 runuser(1)** option set
(fetched, not guessed — runuser isn't on macOS to probe locally):

- **`_WRAPPERS`** ← `runuser`.
- **`_WRAPPER_VALUE_FLAGS`** ← every separate-operand option: `-c/--command`,
  `--session-command`, `-g/--group`, `-G/--supp-group`, `-s/--shell`, `-u/--user`,
  `-w/--whitelist-environment`. Listing them ALL is mandatory — a missing value-flag
  shifts the parse and re-opens the #69 class (the documented half-add trap).

**Only the `-u user [--] command` form is gated**, because only it execs the command
directly. The su-compatible `[-] user [args]` form passes its trailing args to the
user's login **shell**, not a direct exec — so `runuser alice git commit --no-verify`
does not run `git commit`. Gating it would add only over-block with no bypass closed,
and its exec semantics are version/shell-dependent (unverifiable on this host), so it's
left ungated as a best-effort limitation like `unshare`/`nsenter`/`chroot`.

> An earlier revision of this PR added `runuser` to `_OPERAND_DROP_WRAPPERS` to gate the
> positional form too. The gate-review correctly flagged that as gating a non-bypass
> (the positional args go to the shell), so it was **reverted** — value-flags only.

## Verification

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `runuser -u git -- git commit --no-verify` | allow | **block** |
| `runuser -u alice git commit --no-verify` | allow | **block** |
| `runuser -s /bin/sh -u git -- git commit --no-verify` | allow | **block** |
| `runuser -u git -- git status` | allow | allow |
| `runuser alice git commit --no-verify` (su-positional) | allow | allow |
| `runuser - alice git commit --no-verify` (login-dash) | allow | allow |
| `runuser -c '…' git` | allow | allow |
| `sudo -u git git commit --no-verify` (regression) | block | block |

New `test_runuser_direct_exec_form_gated_positional_form_not`; `runuser` added to
`test_crux_per_wrapper_value_flags_no_boolean_collision`; removed from the unlisted-
wrappers known-limitation list. **318 hook tests + full suite 1637 passed, 11 skipped.**

## Known residuals (documented + test-pinned)

- The su-compatible positional form (`runuser alice git commit …`) is ungated — its args
  go to the shell, not a direct exec; best-effort, like other namespace wrappers.
- Narrow over-block: `runuser git commit --no-verify` — a user literally named `git`
  (common) plus a command literally named `commit` reads as `git commit` at argv[0] and
  blocks. A command named `commit`/`push` is near-nonexistent, so it's accepted.

Closes #39.

title: fix(orchestrator-stays-thin): never block a fully read-only shell chain
body:
## Problem (Closes #80)

The orchestrator-stays-thin pre-bash hook over-blocked ONE legitimate class: a **fully read-only** shell chain of 3+ commands. `find ... | grep ... | head` and `tail X | grep Y | wc -l` tripped the `len(CHAIN.findall()) >= 2` implementation-shape rule in `_is_implementation_bash` and got warn-then-blocked — even though every segment is read-only inspection, exactly the multi-stage inspection the orchestrator is supposed to do inline. The `READ_ONLY_BASH` carve-out only protected an UNCHAINED single command.

Found live this session: the hook blocked a legitimate `find|grep|head`.

### Repro (before)
```
'find . -name foo | grep bar | head' -> is_implementation = True
'tail -100 log | grep err | wc -l'   -> is_implementation = True
```

## Fix

New `_is_all_read_only(command)`: a command is inspection when **every** chain segment's HEAD matches `READ_ONLY_BASH` (across `|`, `&&`, `;`, `||`, newline) and it carries no heredoc. `_is_implementation_bash` returns `False` early for such commands, regardless of chain length.

Key design points:
- **Per-segment-HEAD, not a whole-string scan.** A build/edit token used only as an argument/needle of a read-only command (`cat tee.log`, `grep cargo notes`) stays allowed. `tee`/`sed -i` are *unanchored* in `BUILD_EDIT`, so a naive whole-string veto would mis-flag those inspections (caught in review and regression-guarded).
- **All existing block behavior preserved.** A real build/edit or heredoc segment has a non-read-only head -> breaks `all(...)` -> the caller judges it as implementation. Heredocs, `sed -i`/`tee`, build/install runners, mixed read-only+impl pipes all still block.
- **`git` is narrowly scoped** in `READ_ONLY_BASH` (status/log/diff/show/branch), so a mutating git chain (`git add && git commit && git push`) is NOT waved through — no security regression.
- **Head-anchor invariant guarded.** A test asserts a build/edit HEAD with a read-only needle in its args (`sed -i ... grep.py`) still blocks, so a future de-anchoring of `READ_ONLY_BASH` fails loud.

## Tests

`tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py` (43 hook tests, all green; full repo suite 1658 passed / 11 skipped):
- 3-4 segment read-only pipe ALLOWED (never warns, never blocks)
- read-only pipe with one `sed -i` / `npm install` / `tee` / heredoc segment STILL BLOCKED on repeat
- build-token-as-argument (`cat tee.log`, `grep cargo notes`) stays ALLOWED
- build/edit HEAD with read-only needle in args STILL BLOCKED (anchor invariant)
- read-only `&&`/`;` chain ALLOWED; mutating git chain STILL BLOCKED
- existing single-command, redirect, heredoc, and impl-chain cases unchanged

Two review rounds (`review diff --staged`, claude-opus-4-8) -> `[ok]`; both flagged findings (whole-string BUILD_EDIT regression, anchor invariant, doc drift) addressed.

title: feat(research-cli): adopt shared agenttools_errors (what/why/how-to-fix + structured exit codes)
body:
## What

Wires `research-cli` (`tools/research-cli/`) onto the ecosystem's shared **`agenttools_errors`** layer (error-system v2). Until now research-cli hand-rolled every failure as a bare `print(f"research <cmd>: {exc}")` + an ad-hoc per-command exit code (`2`/`69`/`70`) — the symptom but no **why** or **how-to-fix** — even though the shared module already implements exactly that pattern and is already importable here (the same `lib/` `sys.path` shim `providers.py` installs).

## Changes

- **`research_cli/_errors.py`** (new) — the ONE import point for research-cli, re-exporting the shared error classes/builders + the exit-code constants research-cli returns. Adds `lib/` to `sys.path` like `providers.py`; stdlib-only, so `--help`/`--version` stay fast and offline.
- **`cli.py`** — an unknown command raises the shared `unknown_item_error` (so it gets the **did-you-mean** heuristic against the command list); a command-load failure raises a structured `AgentToolError`. Both run under `guard`, rendering the 3-part block + a stable per-class code instead of a bare print.
- **`ask`/`board`** — their diagnosed failures (empty question, unreachable board, malformed manifest) raise `UsageError`/`NetworkError` and render through `guard`.

## Exit-code contract migration (documented in docstrings + README)

| Failure | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no seat answered | `69` (`EX_UNAVAILABLE`) | `7` (`EXIT_NETWORK`) |
| malformed/missing manifest | `70` (`EX_SOFTWARE`) | `2` (`EXIT_USAGE`) |
| unknown command | `2` (bare string) | `4` (`EXIT_UNKNOWN_ITEM`, with did-you-mean) |

A caller now branches on ONE contract across every tool. argparse's own flag-parsing usage errors stay with argparse (terse usage + exit `2`, the conventional CLI behavior); the shared block covers the errors the command code raises itself.

## Tests

RED-first regression tests (`tests/test_research_cli_errors.py`) assert the rendered block contains the **fix** hint and the right exit code per failure class: unknown command + did-you-mean, no-close-match command list, empty question, unreachable board (deterministic — keys cleared, empty cwd, no network), malformed manifest for both commands, an engine `ValueError` → usage, and a broken command module → internal. The one legacy CLI test is updated to the corrected unknown-command contract.

- No new runtime dependency (the lib is stdlib-only).

title: feat(checker): adopt shared agenttools_errors in model-freshness CLI (#89)
body:
## What

Extends the `agenttools_errors` (error-system v2: structured WHAT/WHY/HOW + stable per-class exit codes) adoption to `lib/checker/model_freshness.py` — the model-currency cron checker — exactly as #85 did for research-cli. ## Why

Two concrete defects in the old `main()`:

1. **Wrong exit code for an invalid manifest** — `--validate` failure returned `1`, but the public exit-code contract reserves `1` (`EXIT_INTERNAL`) for *unexpected bugs / tracebacks*. A malformed or invariant-violating manifest is a **config** error -> now `EXIT_CONFIG` (`2`), matching the load-failure path (which already returned 2). A wrapper can now tell "the manifest is bad" from "the checker crashed".
2. **Missing PyYAML mis-classified** — collapsed into a generic manifest error (exit 2); it is genuinely a **missing-dependency** failure -> now `MissingDepError` (`127`) with the install command, via a new `MissingYamlError(ManifestError)` subclass that the existing `except ManifestError` in `run()` / the tests still catches.

- `main()` renders every failure through `agenttools_errors.guard()`: the 3-part `error:`/`why:`/`fix:` block on stderr + the stable per-class code. An unexpected bug still **propagates** (traceback + `1`), kept distinct from a diagnosed config error.
- Body split into `_run_cli(args)` (raises structured errors) + a thin `main()` (parse + `guard`) so `main()` stays small.
- A `sys.path` bootstrap (`lib/` **appended**, not prepended — the `agenttools_*` packages are uniquely named) lets the sibling `agenttools_errors` import resolve when the cron runs the file **directly as a script**, not just when imported as `checker.model_freshness`.

title: feat(agent-hooks): require-ticket-before-commit STRICT by default + rig-provisioned (Closes #92)
body:
## What

Make the `require-ticket-before-commit` agent-hook **strict by default**: a no-ticket,
non-chore `git commit` now **BLOCKS** (exit `10`, decision `block`) with no env needed —
strict is no longer opt-in. Closes #92.

## Why

A warn-only ticket gate is a suggestion the swarm ignores. The CTO wants every change to
start from a ticket; enforcing it mechanically (mid-session, before the commit) is the only
thing that actually moves the discipline. It must not wedge legitimate work, so every valid
ticket-reference form passes and there are explicit per-commit escapes.

## Behavior

**Blocks by default** — stable marker leads the block message:
`[require-ticket] BLOCKED: no ticket reference` (the task-cli Docker test can assert one fixed string).

**Accepted reference forms (all PASS):** `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` / `#N` / a KEY-NUM
task-cli/Linear id (`ENG-456`) / `task:ABC-12` / a `[ticket: <id>]` trailer (now first-class).

**Deliberate escapes (mirror the review-gate's `REVIEW_SKIP`):**
- `[skip-ticket: <reason>]` message trailer (reason mandatory — blank still blocks),
- inline `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1 git commit …` (scoped to the commit segment; a sibling
  assignment or a falsey value does **not** bypass),
- `REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=0` opts the whole gate back to warn-only.

The marker appears **only** on a real block — the warn-only allow emits a neutral
"no ticket reference found" advisory (Opus review caught the marker-leak; fixed + tested).
`on_error` stays `open`: a **crash** still fails open so a bug never wedges committing.

## Provisioning

rig already auto-discovers this hook (catalog directory scan + global `agent_hooks: all: true`),
so `rig apply` installs the descriptor into every machine's `~/.claude/hooks` — verified the
descriptor is installed and in the `cc_hook_bridge` pre-bash list. Catalog descriptor + README
updated to match the new default.

title: fix(agent-hooks): argv-scope require-ticket detection (stop "commit"-mention over-block)
body:
## Problem (agent-tools#97)

`require-ticket-before-commit` decided "is this a commit?" by raw-string matching
`\bgit\b.*\bcommit\b` over the **whole command**, so any benign command that merely
**mentioned** both words was blocked. A subagent hit this **live this session**: its
`gh issue create` calls were blocked because the issue title/body contained the words
"git commit". The strict gate was false-positive-blocking the CTO and every agent.

Over-match examples that were wrongly blocked (all now ALLOW):
`gh issue create --body "...git commit..."`, `echo "git commit"`,
`git log --grep=commit`, `git config commit.gpgsign true`, `git help commit`,
`git commit-graph write`, `grep "git commit" src/`, a `tg` status report talking about a commit.

This is the exact over-match class `block-no-verify` already fixed in #59 (raw-string → argv parse).

## Fix

Replaced the raw regex with a real **argv parser**, adapted from `block-no-verify` (the
authoritative copy) and trimmed to what this gate needs:

- tokenize (quote-, comment-, separator- and multi-line-aware)
- split on shell separators
- strip leading shell noise / redirects / inline env
- peel wrapper executables (`env`/`sudo`/`runuser`/`timeout`/`nice`/`flock`/… incl.
  `sudo -u git`, `runuser -u u --`, operand-drop wrappers)
- keep a segment whose executable is `git` and subcommand is exactly `commit`

The gate now fires **only** on a real `git commit` invocation — including behind those
wrappers, `git -C <repo>`, multi-line `git add` + `git commit`, subshells, and a
path-qualified `/usr/bin/git` — never on a substring / argument / message-body mention.

All prior behavior is preserved against the **parsed** segment: strict-by-default block
on a no-ticket commit (exit 10 + stable marker), every accepted ticket form
(`Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` / `#N` / `KEY-NUM` / `task:` / `[ticket:]`), the exemptions
(chore/docs/wip/merge, `--amend`/`--continue`/`--abort`/`--skip`), and the escapes
(`[skip-ticket: <reason>]` / `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1` / `REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=0`).

### Also fixed (surfaced by argv-first parsing)

- `current_branch` used `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which returns the literal
  `HEAD` on an **unborn branch** (a repo's first commit) and missed a branch-encoded
  ticket → switched to `git branch --show-current` (returns the name even pre-first-commit).
- `is_skip_commit` now skips message-bearing short-cluster values (`-am '--amend'`), so a
  skip flag that is only the commit **message** can't falsely exempt a real commit.
- ticket/message extraction now also reads a glued `-FPATH` file (git accepts `-F path`
  and `-Fpath`), alongside the already-handled `-mMSG` / `--message=` / `--file=`.

code (it blocked them); they pass now. Added to **both** the hook-local suite
(`test_require_ticket.py`) and the CI-collected mirror
(`tests/test_require_ticket_before_commit.py`, 22 → 39 cases) so CI gates the regression.

- benign "commit"-mention commands → ALLOW
- real no-ticket commit (bare, wrapped, path-qualified, `git -C`, after a mentioning sibling) → BLOCK (exit 10 + marker)
- every ticket form + both escapes → still work
- new: glued `-mMSG`/`-FPATH` ticket detection, `-am '--amend'` skip-flag-in-message, wrapped `git -C` branch-ticket end-to-end

Full agent-tools suite green (1704 passed, 12 pre-existing skips); ruff clean.

`flock -c`) and a `git --exec-path <val> commit` global-flag edge — both shared with the
sibling `block-no-verify` gate (same `_GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE_FLAGS` set), out of scope for an
`on_error: open` discipline gate.

title: fix(require-ticket): fail open on `-F -` (stdin) message + pin `-F`/`--file` read parity
body:
## Problem

`require-ticket-before-commit` could not see the commit message when it was supplied via `git commit -F -` (stdin). The message on `-F -` lives on **git's own stdin**, which a PreToolUse agent-hook **cannot** read (the hook's stdin is the JSON event, not git's). The code passed the literal `-` to the message-file reader, which tried to open a file named `-`, failed, found no ticket, and **BLOCKED** — even for a legitimately-ticketed commit. The only escape was `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1`, which bypasses the whole gate. Multiple subagents hit this and had to skip, so the gate was effectively defeated for the `-F -` commit form.

(`-F <file>` reading itself already landed in #100; this PR closes the remaining **stdin** gap.)

## Fix

For `-F -` **specifically**, the gate now **fails open (allows)** rather than false-block, and emits a loud `allow` note that this is an unreadable-message bypass surface — so it stays visible in the hook log. This is the only `-F` form that fails open.

- `commit_reads_stdin_message()` detects the stdin sentinel in all four spellings: `-F -`, `-F-`, `--file -`, `--file=-`.
- `_read_message_file()` short-circuits the `-` sentinel instead of opening a file named `-` (no spurious read warning).
- `_file_flag_values()` factors out the `-F`/`--file` value extraction; a **parity test** pins that the message reader and the stdin detector agree on every spelling, so a readable `--file <file>` ticket is never silently dropped.
- README documents the `-F -` fail-open limitation and the editor-commit (no `-m`/`-F`) branch-only check.

## What's unchanged (verified)

- `-F <file>` / `-F<file>` / `--file <file>` / `--file=<file>` with a ticket → **ALLOWED** (file read from disk).
- a readable `-F` file with no ref → **BLOCKED**.
- `-m "Closes #1"` → **ALLOWED**; `-m "no ref"` → **BLOCKED**.
- editor commit (no `-m`/`-F`) → unchanged (branch-name check only).

## Tests (RED-first)

New tests in both the co-located suite and the CI-collected mirror reproduce the `-F -` false-block (RED), prove the fail-open-with-log fix (GREEN), and add `-F`/`--file` read-parity coverage across all four spellings. Full repo suite: **1728 passed, 12 skipped**; ruff clean. Review gate `[ok]` (claude:claude-opus-4-8 seat).

Closes #101

No UI change — `--no-screenshot-ok` applies (backend agent-hook only).

title: fix(require-ticket): flip -F - (stdin) from fail-open to fail-closed-with-hint
body:
## What

Flip the `require-ticket-before-commit` hook's `-F -` (stdin) handling from **fail-open** (agent-tools#102) to **fail-closed-with-hint**.

`git commit -F -` streams the commit message on git's own stdin, which a PreToolUse hook cannot read. #102 chose to allow such commits with a logged note — but that made `-F -` a free bypass of the ticket gate, contradicting the strict-by-default intent. This blocks it instead, with an actionable hint.

## Behavior

- `git commit -F -` (all spellings: `-F -`, `-F-`, `--file -`, `--file=-`) with **no ticket in the branch name** → BLOCKED (exit 10, `[require-ticket] BLOCKED` marker) with a hint naming the readable ways to satisfy it.
- `-F -` on a **ticket-encoded branch** (`feature/ABC-12-foo`) → ALLOWED. The stdin block runs *after* branch-name ticket detection, so it stays consistent with the editor-commit path (also unreadable pre-commit, checked against the branch only). This was a review finding — the first cut blocked before branch detection.
- `-F <file with Closes #N>` → ALLOWED (read + checked, unchanged).
- `-m "Closes #N"` → ALLOWED; `-m "no ref"` → BLOCKED (unchanged).
- `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1 git commit -F -` → ALLOWED (the inline env escape is read from the command, not stdin).
- `REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=0` → downgrades the `-F -` block to a warn-only allow, like every other no-ticket case.

The hint deliberately does **not** offer the `[skip-ticket: <reason>]` trailer for `-F -` — that trailer would live in the unreadable stdin message and can't work (a second review finding). Only the inline `REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP=1` applies to a stdin-message commit.

## Docs / tests

- Module docstring, README, and the descriptor's behavior note updated from "fail-open" to "fail-closed-with-hint".
- Flipped the #102 fail-open tests to fail-closed in both test files (`agent-hooks/.../test_require_ticket.py` and `tests/test_require_ticket_before_commit.py`).
- Added coverage: every stdin spelling fails closed; ticket-branch `-F -` allows; non-ticket-branch `-F -` blocks; inline-skip escape on `-F -` allows; warn-only downgrades.

Full agent-tools suite green (1735 passed, 15 skipped). Ruff clean. Review-gate `[ok]` (claude:claude-opus-4-8).

Closes #104

## What

New `ci/trivy/` CI slot — a portable, rig-provisionable **Trivy filesystem scan**, the catalog equivalent of the bespoke Trivy steps repos hand-roll (the gap #24 calls out).

- **Block tier exits with trivy's own code** via `set +e; trivy; rc=$?` — not the `if trivy; then … $?` trap where `$?` after a false `if` is 0 (would print FAIL but exit 0 → green CI on a real finding).

- **`set -f` (noglob)** around the unquoted `$TRIVY_EXTRA` so a glob in `--skip-files *.lock` reaches trivy literally.

title: fix(require-ticket): de-cluster combined short flags so -am extracts the message
body:
## What

Fixes #109 — the canonical `require-ticket-before-commit` hook's argv parser did not de-cluster combined short option groups, so `git commit -am "..."` (the common `-a` + `-m "..."`) lost the commit message. The token `-am` matched no branch in the message-extraction path, leaving `message == ""`:

- a ticketed `-am "Closes #5"` false-**BLOCKED** in strict mode;
- a `-am "chore: ..."` **lost its exemption** (empty message → not exempt).

Same clustered-short-flag class block-no-verify fixed in #36–#40.

## Fix

A shared `_decluster_short_message_flag` reads a short cluster the way git's commit parser does — left-to-right, the **first** value-consuming letter wins, taking the rest-of-cluster as a glued value (`-amMSG` → `MSG`; `-amF` → `F`, *not* a separate `-F`; `-aFpath` → file `path`) or, when it is the cluster's last char, the next token (`-am MSG`, `-aF file`).

It distinguishes the message/file letters (`m`/`F`) from the other value-consuming short flags (`-C`/`-c`/`-t`/`-u`/`-S`), which swallow their own value — so a trailing `m`/`F` after them is that value, not a message (git parses `-Cm` as `-C m`, `-Sm` as keyid `m`, etc.). The message reader, the `-F` stdin-sentinel detector, and the skip-flag scan all route through it, keeping the two parsers in lock-step (parity test) — so a `-m`/`-am`/`--message` whose value looks like `-F -` is not misread as an unreadable-stdin commit, and a separate `-C`/`-c`/`-t`/`--reuse-message` value token is skipped by both.

## Preserved

`-m`/`-mMSG`/`-F`/`-FPATH`/`--file=`, the `-F -` fail-closed-with-hint, `Closes #N`/`KEY-NUM` detection, the `[skip-ticket:]`/`REQUIRE_TICKET_SKIP` escapes, the strict-block exit 10 + marker. A benign clustered-flag non-commit (`tar -amF`) still passes (no over-block — the #37/#40 cautionary tale).

## Tests (RED-first)

- `git commit -am "Closes #5 fix"` → ALLOWED; `-am "no ticket"` → BLOCKED; `-am "chore: ..."` → ALLOWED.
- `-amF`/`-aF file`/`-aF<glued>`/`-a -m`/`-m`/`-F`/`--file=` all correct; escapes work; benign clustered non-commit passes.
- Review-driven parity tests: `-am -F -`/`--message -F -` not a stdin block; `-Cm`/`-um`/`-Sm`/`-C -m x`/`-t -F -` not a message; `-S -m`/`-u -m` still read the ticket.

All 3 review findings (parity break, `-C`/`-c`/`-t`/`-S`/`-u` value letters, trailing-flag warning) addressed. Full `tests/` suite green (1807 passed), ruff clean.

## Follow-up

task-cli vendors a byte-identical copy of this hook; after this lands, the task-cli drift-check (task#34) will flag the vendored copy as stale — a task-cli re-sync (`scripts/resync_vendored_hook.py`) is needed (separate repo, not in this PR).

Closes #109

title: fix(agent-hooks): block-no-verify emits an actionable fail-closed message (not "could not inspect")
body:
## What

When `block-no-verify` can't parse a command that plausibly is a `git commit`/`push`, it fail-closes — correctly — but emitted a generic `block-no-verify: could not inspect the command (fail-closed)`. An agent whose commit merely had an apostrophe in a single-quoted `-m` message read that as a BROKEN HOOK rather than a quoting problem (reported by the #109 agent).

## Investigation finding

The originally-suspected mechanism — "backticks/flags in a **heredoc** confuse the tokenizer" — does NOT reproduce: `_strip_heredocs` removes the body before tokenizing, so heredoc commit messages (apostrophes, backticks, `--flag` text) are handled and ALLOW (#37/#40 already covers this). The only residual over-block is a genuinely-unbalanced-quote commit, which **cannot be safely narrowed to allow** — a quote-recovery heuristic provably swallows a real `--no-verify` into the message and reopens the bypass.

## Fix (decision unchanged — message + precision only)

- The fail-closed decision STILL BLOCKs in both cases. Only the message improves, split by reason:
  - **unbalanced quotes on a plausible git commit/push** → actionable hint: name the unbalanced quotes, point at `-F <file>` / a heredoc.
  - **obfuscation (`env -S`/`--split-string`) at a command head** → a firm refusal (no quoting-softening).
- `env -S` detection is anchored to a COMMAND HEAD (string start / after a shell separator / behind an inline `VAR=val`), so a benign commit whose MESSAGE merely mentions `env -S` and is unparseable for another reason gets the quoting hint, not the obfuscation refusal.

## Tests (RED-first)

- Apostrophe in a single-quoted `-m` message → BLOCK with the actionable "unbalanced quotes" message (not "could not inspect").
- Obfuscation → firm refusal; obfuscation WINS when both predicates hold (branch-order pin).
- Benign commit MENTIONING `env -S` + apostrophe → quoting hint, not obfuscation refusal.
- Event-parse failure keeps its own message (no leak of the command-level hint).
- Every real-bypass test (#36/#39) and over-block test (#37/#40) stays green. Full suite: 326 tests, ruff clean.

Closes #113

## What

## The bypass (RED-first, reproduced then closed)

`_OTHER_VALUE_LONG` listed only `--reuse-message`/`--reedit-message`/`--fixup`/`--squash`/
`--template`, but git-parseopt also consumes a **mandatory separate next token** for
`--author`, `--date`, `--cleanup`, `--trailer`, and `--pathspec-from-file` (each declared
`OPT_STRING`/`OPT_STRING_LIST`/`OPT_PATHSPEC_FROM_FILE` with no `PARSE_OPT_OPTARG`). Because
the parser didn't skip those values, a `-m`/`-F`-looking value was re-read as a real flag and
diverged from git:

```
git commit --author '-m' 'ABC-1: ok'
```

- **Real git:** `author="-m"`, `'ABC-1: ok'` is a PATHSPEC, no message in argv → editor opens,
  the commit is **ticketless**.
- **Old parser:** skipped `--author` (`i+=1`), de-clustered the value `-m` into a message flag,
  ate `'ABC-1: ok'` → phantom ticket → the gate falsely **passed**.

## Fix

1. Add the five flags to `_OTHER_VALUE_LONG`, so both message parsers skip the flag **and** its
   value (matching git). A glued `--author=…` carries its own value and, by exact-set
   membership, does **not** consume the next token.
2. Wire `_takes_following_message_value` (used by `is_skip_commit`) to also return True for
   `_nonmessage_flag_consumes_next(tok)` — closing an asymmetry where a value-bearing flag's
   value that looked like a skip flag (`--author '--amend'`, `-C '--amend'`) was misread as a
   real `--amend`. The fall-through is guarded so a message/file token is judged **entirely** by
   its de-cluster result and never reaches `_nonmessage_flag_consumes_next`, so a glued message
   ending in `c`/`C`/`t` (`-amFixIt`) is never misread as a `-C`/`-c`/`-t` next-token consumer.

`--gpg-sign`/`-S`/`-u` stay omitted on purpose (optional, only-glued value); a regression test
pins that a separate `--gpg-sign -m …` still reads the following real `-m`.

## Tests

- **RED-first:** 12 of the new cases fail against the old parser; green after the fix.
- The five-flag `-m`/`-F`-looking-value bypass; the `-F -` stdin misread; the legit path (a real
  following `-m` ticket still allows); the `is_skip_commit` asymmetry; the glued-short-message
  edge cases; and the `--gpg-sign` / clustered-`-aC` / glued-`-Cabc` symmetry pins.
- Full hook suite green (223 require-ticket cases; whole `tests/` 1839 passed / 15 skipped),
  ruff clean.

## Review

`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8` → **[ok]** (no blocking bugs / regressions;
git semantics re-verified against `builtin/commit.c`).

title: fix(agent-hooks): require-ticket resolves abbreviated git-commit long flags (close ticket-gate bypass)
body:
## What

Closes #120. Makes the `require-ticket-before-commit` agent-hook resolve `git commit` long
options by **git's unambiguous-prefix rule** instead of exact string, closing the abbreviation
form of the ticket-gate bypass #119 fixed for the exact spelling.

## The bypass (residual after #119)

`#119` added the value-bearing long flags (`--author`/`--date`/`--cleanup`/`--trailer`/
`--pathspec-from-file` + the reuse/reedit/fixup/squash/template family) to the value-consuming
set, but matched them by **exact string**. git resolves any **unambiguous prefix** of a long
option, so the divergence stayed open via the short form:

```
git commit --au '-m' 'ABC-1: ok'
```

- **Real git:** `--au` = `--author`, `author="-m"`, `'ABC-1: ok'` is a **pathspec**, no message
  in argv → the commit is **ticketless**.
- **Old parser:** `--au` not recognized as value-consuming → its value `-m` de-clustered into a
  message flag and ate `'ABC-1: ok'` → phantom `ABC-1` ticket → gate falsely **ALLOWed**.

## The fix

`_resolve_long_option` maps a `--xxx` token to its canonical `git commit` option the way git's
parseopt does: exact match wins, otherwise an **unambiguous** prefix resolves, an **ambiguous**
prefix (matches >1 option — `--t` → trailer/template, `--d` → date/dry-run, `--f` → file/fixup)
or an unknown token → `None`. git **errors** on an ambiguous prefix and never commits, so `None`
is the safe answer (no over-consume, no phantom ticket). Ambiguity is computed against the **full**
`git commit` long-option set, not only the value-consumers.

All three argv parsers (`commit_message_from_argv`, `_file_flag_values`, `is_skip_commit`) and
`_takes_following_message_value` go through the shared resolver, so:
- an abbreviated value flag skips its value everywhere (bypass closed);
- an abbreviated `--message`/`--file` still has its value **read** (no over-block of a legit
  ticketed abbreviated commit);
- an abbreviated skip flag (`--am` → `--amend`) is still treated as not-a-fresh-commit.

Glued `--author=…`/`--mess=…` carry their own value and don't consume the next token; `--gpg-sign`/
`-S`/`-u` and their abbreviations stay non-consuming (optional/glued value only).

The full git-commit option set, every abbreviation resolution, and the ambiguity boundary are
**verified against real git**.

## Tests (RED-first)

`test_e2e_abbreviated_author_dash_m_pathspec_blocks` reproduces the bypass — it returns
ALLOW/exit 0 against the old exact-match parser and BLOCK/exit 10 after the fix. New
`AbbreviatedLongFlagPrefix` class covers the resolver, the bypass close, the ambiguity reject,
the legit ticketed path, abbreviated message/file reads, the import-time guard, and
`_is_skip_flag`.

- 144 hook tests green; full repo suite **1842 passed, 15 skipped**; ruff clean.
- All prior #111 (`-am` de-cluster), #114/#119 (value flags, `-F`/stdin), over-match (#97),
  over-block (#37/#40-class) tests stay green.

## Review

`claude-opus-4-8 [ok]` (substantive logic/security review) + `gemini [ok]` (final diff, no
actionable findings).

title: fix(ci): harden three shipped CI-gate workflows (#129)
body:
## What

Salvage + finish of agent-tools#129: three real bugs in the shipped `ci/<slot>/` gate workflows that `rig` copies verbatim into every consumer/bot repo (so a bug here is a bug in every rigged repo). Each bug made a provisioned gate either fail-CLOSED (red CI on a clean repo) or — worse — silently fail-OPEN (green CI while the gate scanned nothing).

### 1. `ci/dependency-review/` (SECURITY) — self-weakenable gate + missing toolchain
- Ran the PR's OWN copy of `workflow.yml` + `dep-audit.sh` under plain `pull_request`, so a PR could neuter the very gate it must pass. Switched to the **trusted-base `pull_request_target`** model (mirrors `ci/leftover-grep`): the BASE workflow + script run; the PR head is fetched as a git **object** and materialized in a **side worktree**, audited only as **DATA** (auditors read lockfiles, never run install/lifecycle scripts). No `actions/checkout` of PR code, no build/install step → the pwn-request RCE is avoided by construction (`contents: read`).
- `setup-bun` was commented out, so a `bun.lock` repo fail-CLOSED (no `bun` → `dep-audit.sh` reds CI). Now shipped **ENABLED + SHA-pinned**.

### 2. `ci/leftover-grep/` — shallow-fetch silent no-op
- A `--depth=1` PR-head fetch shares no merge-base, so `base...HEAD` no-op'd and the gate silently PASSED. The script also read the diff via a process substitution that swallowed `git diff` errors. Workflow now deepens the fetch + verifies a merge-base (fail closed); the script materializes the lines + gates on `$?`, fails closed on an unresolvable explicit base, and drops the bare `=======` conflict-marker false positive.

### 3. `ci/codeql/workflow-selfgate.yml` — SIGPIPE self-disable
- `git ls-files | grep -qiE` under `set -o pipefail` returned 141 (SIGPIPE) when grep matched early → the `if` took the else branch → CodeQL self-disabled on a language whose source IS present. Now materializes the file list and greps a here-string (no pipe), fail closed on a git/grep error.

## Tests

`tests/test_ci_gate_bugs_129.py`: behavioral tests that **reproduce each bug mechanism AND prove the fix** (e.g. the old `grep -q` pipe form self-disables, the `--depth=1`/orphan diff no-ops). yaml-gated structural tests skip cleanly in the dependency-free CI env; the behavioral tests still run.

## Follow-ups (in-flight on this PR)

Review board surfaced that the no-arg `pip-audit` audits the runner env, not the PR's Python manifests under the new model, and that `govulncheck` builds source (so the "auditors only read the lockfile" claim must exclude it). Comment/doc accuracy fixes follow in subsequent commits.

Closes #129. Supersedes the duplicate #130.

title: fix(agent-hooks): no-long-inline-process argv-aware match (close "review"-substring false-positive)
body:
## What

Makes the `no-long-inline-process` pre-bash agent-hook **argv-aware**: it now
shell-tokenizes the command and flags a long-running process only when the
**real invoked command** (`argv[0]` after peeling inline env + no-op wrappers) is
the runner — instead of raw-matching long-process patterns anchored on shell
separator chars (`(`, `|`, `;`, `&&`) and a bare `--watch` substring.

## Why (#60)

Those separator chars also appear **inside quoted argument strings**, so the old
raw regex mis-read benign commands as real long-process invocations and BLOCKED
them:

- `tg --tag report --title x "we ran review-qa (review) today"`
- `git commit -m "wire --watch flag"`
- `git commit -m "fix; npm test now green"`
- `tg "status: (sleep 600 elapsed) done"`

## How

`shlex` tokenization (quotes/heredocs/comments honored) → split into real
segments → for each segment peel leading shell noise / inline `VAR=val` / no-op
wrappers (`timeout`/`env`/`nice`/`time`/…) → inspect `argv[0]`. A keyword inside
an argument to a different command no longer trips it, while a genuine inline
`review` / `npm test` / `--watch` / long `sleep` still blocks — including wrapped
(`timeout 5m review`), inline-env (`CI=1 pytest`), and unquoted
substitution/subshell (`$(npm test)`, `(review)`) forms. Documented under-block
(`"$(…)"`, `bash -c`, `xargs`) and a rare residual over-block (a quoted token
equal to exactly a lone separator) are pinned by tests.

## Tests

- 117 hook tests in `tests/test_no_long_inline_process.py` (new #60 quoted-arg
  cases, command-substitution still-blocks cases, parser-branch coverage).
- Full repo suite green: 1962 passed, 17 skipped.

Refs #60

title: fix(ci/leftover-grep): two-dot fallback so shallow PRs keep scanning (don't fatal every PR)
body:
## Problem

The shipped `ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh` gate diffs `base...HEAD` (three-dot), which needs a reachable merge base. Under a shallow `--depth=1` PR-head fetch (`pull_request_target`) the merge base is unreachable, so `git diff` **fatals**. Post-#131 that fatal is correctly caught fail-closed by the `if ! emit_lines` materialization gate — but the consequence is that **every** shallow PR (clean or not) hard-fails the gate (over-fail-closed), making a block-tier gate unusable on the exact checkout CI hands it.

(Found via garage-band #3, where the same catalog script blocked legitimate shallow PRs; fixed there as the two-dot fallback. This ports that proven fix back to the catalog so all provisioned repos converge on the next `rig apply`.)

## Fix

Port garage-band's proven approach to `emit_lines`:

1. **Probe the merge base** (`git merge-base "$base" "$LEFTOVER_HEAD"`); when unreachable, fall back to the **two-dot** `base..HEAD` diff (no merge base needed) so the gate **keeps scanning** instead of fataling every shallow PR.
2. A truly uncomputable diff (a bogus/missing head object) still fatals **both** ranges and is caught fail-closed — now with a message that points at `actions/checkout fetch-depth: 0` as the remedy.

Two-dot is the **safe direction** for a security gate: it over-blocks (a diverged base can surface lines the PR did not add) rather than silently passing, and it catches every PR-added leftover except the degenerate case of a line identical to one already in `base` in the same file; `fetch-depth: 0` restores exact three-dot semantics. The full-fetch path is unchanged.

## Tests (`tests/test_ci_gate_bugs_129.py`)

- no-merge-base orphan + planted leftover → two-dot **catches** it (rc 1); clean orphan → **PASS** via two-dot (no over-fail-closed);
- bogus head SHA → **fail-closed** (rc 1) with the `fetch-depth: 0` hint;
- a **faithful real shallow clone** (`file://` + `--depth=1` on both branches, shared ancestor unfetched, histories overlapping) proves the fallback catches the PR's leftover on representative shallow content (where the old unconditional three-dot would have fataled);
- a guard test pins the merge-base probe + two-dot range against regression;
- the three-dot path is unchanged when a merge base exists.

Full suite: **1966 passed, 17 skipped**. Single-seat `review diff` returned `[ok]`.

Refs #130

title: fix(ci/review-threads): re-run on review/comment events to close the stale-green gap (#65)
body:
## Problem (agent-tools#65)

The shipped `ci/review-threads/workflow.yml` gate only triggered on PR-lifecycle events
(`opened`/`synchronize`/`reopened`/`ready_for_review`). So a review thread **added after**
an earlier green check left the required `review-threads` status **dishonestly green** — a PR
could be merged via the GitHub UI over a fresh unresolved thread. (`gh ship` re-checks threads
at merge time, so the ship path was always safe; the **required GitHub status** was the lie.)

## Fix

Re-run the gate when an unresolved thread *appears*:

- `pull_request_review` (types: submitted, edited, dismissed)
- `pull_request_review_comment` (types: created, edited, deleted)

Both run on the **PR merge ref** (`GITHUB_REF = refs/pull/N/merge`, verified against the raw
GitHub Actions event docs), exactly like `pull_request` — so GitHub attaches their check-run
to the PR and branch protection's required `review-threads` context is refreshed on the PR head.

**Tamper-resistance kept (and hardened):** under those events the *default* checkout ref is the
PR merge ref, which **contains the PR's edits to the gate script**. The checkout now pins
`ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}` (trusted base) for every trigger, so the base
copy of `review-threads.sh` always runs. Token stays read-only.

**PR-number resolution:** unchanged — every pull_request-family trigger carries
`github.event.pull_request.number`; manual runs fall back to the `pr_number` input.

### Deliberately excluded (each a false-coverage no-op — documented in-workflow so a future agent doesn't "fix the gap" by adding a dud)

- `issue_comment` — runs on the **default-branch SHA**, so its check-run never attaches to the
  PR head where branch protection looks. It would re-run but never update the required status.
- `pull_request_review_thread` (resolved/unresolved) — **not a supported Actions trigger**
  (webhook-only; absent from the entire events-that-trigger-workflows list). Listing it would
  silently never fire.

**Residual gap (safe direction):** *resolving* the last thread fires no supported Actions
trigger, so the check won't auto-flip back to green — push / `workflow_dispatch` / ship preflight.
Staying red is conservative: it never lets an unresolved thread merge, only delays the green.

### Also

- `concurrency` group per PR (`cancel-in-progress`) to coalesce the review-submit fan-out
  (1 review + N comment events) — safe because each run re-queries live thread state.
- New `tests/test_review_threads_gate.py`: trigger set, excluded-event guards, base-ref pin,
  per-event PR-number resolution, and **behavioral** tests of `review-threads.sh` (fail-closed
  on gh error, page summing, `IGNORE_OUTDATED`) driven by a stubbed `gh`.

## Validation

- Full suite green: `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/` → **1977 passed, 28 skipped**.
- AI review (`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8`) → `[ok]`. Early rounds disputed
  the check-run/SHA association; refuted against the raw canonical GitHub docs (merge-ref →
  PR-associated, unlike `issue_comment`), and the final round confirmed the `issue_comment` and
  `pull_request_review_thread` exclusions are correct.

Provisioned repos converge on the next `rig apply`.

title: feat(agent-hooks): subagent-no-bg-longproc — stop a subagent backgrounding review/long-process and wedging (#52)
body:
## What

A new `pre-bash` agent-hook, **`subagent-no-bg-longproc`**, that blocks a dispatched **subagent** from **backgrounding a long process** and then wedging forever (agent-tools#52).

### The wedge (seen ~6x in one session)
A subagent runs a long process — a multi-model `review`, a build/test suite, a `--watch` loop, a long `sleep` — with `run_in_background: true` (or a shell `&` / `setsid`), then ends its turn *"awaiting the completion notification"*. But a **subagent is NOT re-invoked by a background-completion notification — only the main loop is.** So it idles forever with uncommitted work and no PR, and the orchestrator has to catch the rest-notification, kill the stray process, and salvage the half-done work by hand.

### The mechanism
This gate is the exact **inverse** of `no-long-inline-process` (which tells the *orchestrator* to dispatch long work to a *background* subagent, and is subagent-exempt): a **subagent** must run its **own** long work in the **foreground** and block on it.

It fires **only** when all three hold:
1. the tool use is a **subagent's** (`agent_id` present — a trusted transport-level signal `cc_hook_bridge` forwards and a worker can't spoof itself out of);
2. the command is a **long process** (same argv-aware detection as the sibling, kept in step by a drift-guard test);
3. the command is **backgrounded**.

Backgrounding binds to the long-process command with correct bash **job** semantics, not the whole line: `echo started & review …` (review foreground) is allowed, while `review … &`, `review | tee log &`, `review && commit &`, `run_in_background: true`, and `setsid review` are blocked. A `&` fused into a redirection (`2>&1`/`>&`/`&>`) is ignored; a long process inside a nested shell construct before a trailing `&` is a **documented under-block** (the safe direction for this `on_error: open` discipline gate).

### Signal availability
A `pre-bash` hook **does** see the wedge signals: `cc_hook_bridge` passes the whole Bash `tool_input` (incl. `run_in_background`) through under `args`, and forwards CC's top-level `agent_id`/`agent_type`. CC fires `pre-bash` for a subagent's Bash call today — no rig-cli follow-up needed (unlike the `pre-agent` point).

### Escape hatch (reason required)
`ALLOW_SUBAGENT_BACKGROUND=1` + `ALLOW_SUBAGENT_BACKGROUND_REASON='why'`, or inline `# subagent-bg-ok: why` (matched only in a real, quote/heredoc-aware shell comment; a reasonless override still blocks).

## Ships

title: feat(ship): review-dwell gate — block merge before review questions can form
body:
## Problem

The `gh ship` merge path (`ci/ship/ship.sh`) gated review only on **unresolved** review threads. `0 unresolved threads` is **vacuously true** when no review has posted yet — so a PR opened and `gh ship`'d within seconds passed the gate before any multi-model / CI-AI / human review could form its questions. That is the premature-merge gap: hooks let PRs merge without waiting for review comments to form.

Root cause: `ci/ship/ship.sh` review gate counted only the unresolved-thread *count*; there was **no minimum dwell window** between the last push and the merge. `require-review-before-commit` runs at commit-time on a local marker, not at merge-time on the PR's review state.

## Fix

A **review-dwell gate** in the central ship script: refuse to merge until at least `SHIP_REVIEW_DWELL` seconds (default **600**) have elapsed since the PR's last head update. Async review then has time to land; whatever it posts becomes a thread the existing unresolved-threads gate forces resolved. The two compose: **time to form** + **must resolve**.

- Window start = `max(createdAt, head-commit pushedDate, committedDate)`. `pushedDate` is GitHub's head-update signal (restarts the window on a force-push to an already-open PR — addresses the inline-review finding); `committedDate` is the fallback when GitHub leaves `pushedDate` null.
- Runs **independently of `--skip-ci`**. **Fail-closed**: unreadable/unparseable timestamps refuse.
- **Override**: `--no-review-dwell-ok <reason>` (logged) or `SHIP_REVIEW_DWELL=0`.

## Tests

8 new cases in `tests/test_ship.py` (block fresh PR, pass aged PR, override flag, dwell=0, PR-open floor, **force-push fresh pushedDate w/ old commit**, fail-closed on unparseable, reject non-numeric window). Full `tests/test_ship.py` green (40), review-threads gate green.

## Review

`review diff --pool 2` ran inline: gemini clean; codex raised the committedDate-vs-push-time force-push case, folded in via `pushedDate`.

title: feat(ship): detect CI unavailable and gate locally
body:
## Summary

When GitHub Actions is structurally down (billing, runner quota, infra failure), all CI checks fail and `gh ship` was blocking the merge unconditionally — even when the code itself is fine. This PR adds detection + a local fallback gate so a real CI outage doesn't freeze delivery.

- **Detection** (`ci_appears_structurally_down`): fires when ≥ 80% of checks failed AND either the GitHub status page shows Actions degraded OR all workflow runs completed in < 30s (too fast for real tests)
- **Local fallback gate** (`run_local_ci_gate`): runs local tests (auto-detects uv/npm/cargo), scans PR diff for leftover markers (TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX), checks PR body for unchecked `- [ ]` items, re-checks review threads
- **Threshold fix**: replaced `total*8/10` (integer truncation — 50% would trigger the 80% gate for 2-check PRs) with cross-multiplication `failed*10 >= total*8`
- **Bug fix**: `grep -c` exits 1 on 0 matches; `|| echo 0` doubled the output to `"0\n0"` — fixed with `|| true`
- **Test knobs**: `SHIP_TEST_CI_DOWN=1` (force-trigger without network), `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD` (override test runner), `SHIP_TEST_DIFF` (inject diff content)

title: fix(review-gate): use `command git` to bypass shell aliases in hash computation
body:
## Summary

- Replace bare `git` with `command git` in all git calls in the review-gate hook
- `command` bypasses shell aliases and functions, ensuring the real git binary is called
- Prevents hash mismatch when tools like rtk rewrite `git diff` output

## Problem

The review-gate hook computes `h=$(git diff --no-ext-diff --cached | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1)` to verify a commit was reviewed. RTK (Rust Token Killer) rewrites `git diff` into a compact summary format completely different from git's unified diff — producing a different hash from what review-cli writes (which calls the real `git` binary via `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, bypassing aliases).

Result: the hook blocks a legitimately-reviewed commit because the hashes don't match.

## Fix

`command git` (POSIX) bypasses shell aliases and functions but still resolves via PATH — so it always calls the real git binary, matching what review-cli's subprocess call produces.

Applied to all three git calls in the hook: `git diff --cached --name-only`, `git diff --no-ext-diff --cached`, and `git rev-parse --git-path review-stamp`.

Closes #155

## Test plan

- [x] Full test suite: 2079 passed, 21 skipped (no regressions)
- [x] End-to-end test: `rtk git commit` with correct review stamp passes, without stamp blocks
- [x] Hash verification: `command git diff --no-ext-diff --cached | shasum` produces same hash as `hashlib.sha256(diff.encode()).hexdigest()` in review-cli Python

title: feat(git-hooks): pre-push protect-main — block direct pushes to main/master (HYP-856)
body:
## What

GitHub branch protection is unavailable on the free plan (the API returns 403) and paying is not an option — so the server cannot reject a direct push to `main`. This PR ships the client-side enforcement through the global-dispatcher path so it provisions to every repo/machine via `rig apply`.

Linear: [HYP-856](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-856)

### 1. `global-hooks.d/pre-push/10-protect-main` (new shipped fragment)
- blocks any push to `refs/heads/main` / `refs/heads/master` with a message pointing to the PR flow (`gh ship`)
- **protected** fragment: a cloned repo's `.githooks-skip` / env `GLOBAL_HOOKS_SKIP` cannot silently disable it
- honest, audited escape hatch: `PUSH_MAIN_OK=1 PUSH_MAIN_REASON="why" git push …` allows the push and appends one line **per protected ref** to `~/.cache/agent-tools/overrides.log`; a failed append is loudly reported as UNAUDITED
- branch deletions / tags / feature refs pass untouched (default-branch deletion is refused server-side on every plan)

### 2. Composers dispatch exactly ONCE (bug found during verification)
A template-shim (`init.templateDir`) or retrofit-injected local hook already calls `run-global-hooks`; the composers then dispatched AGAIN → every fragment fired twice (double secret scans, duplicate audit lines). Fixed with a positive runtime marker (`GLOBAL_HOOKS_DISPATCH_MARKER`) touched by the runner itself — degradations are all fail-SAFE (worst case: the old double-run; a shim with a missing runner path still gets stage-2 dispatch, no fail-open).

## rig.yaml / provisioning
Fragments are per-file and default-on — after this merges, `rig apply` installs the fragment wherever the dispatcher block is enabled:

```yaml
git_hooks:
  dispatcher:
    enabled: true
    fragments:
      secret-scan:  { enabled: true }
      protect-main: { enabled: true }   # optional line — fragments default ON
```

## Verification
`sh git-hooks/global-dispatcher/selfcheck.sh` → **ALL PASS**, incl. 18 new assertions: block main, allow feature branch, override + exactly-one audit line per ref, multi-ref (main+master) block naming both refs, deletion pass-through, dispatch-once with the template shim, comment-only mention, missing-runner fail-open guard.

## What & why

The `orchestrator-stays-thin` delegate hook (which enforces `delegate-work-to-subagents`) warn-then-blocked two classes of the orchestrator's OWN legitimate work:

1. **The gated merge `gh ship`** — the one repo mutation that belongs at orchestrator altitude. The auto-mode classifier denies it *inside* subagents, so if the hook blocks the orchestrator's inline ship too, **nobody** can run the sanctioned merge. Observed live as warn-then-block **flapping** (the gated-ship / G-6/G-7 deadlock). Closes **#159**, delivers **task #23**.
2. **Reporting (`tg`) and read-only verification** — a multi-step `tg` report (`tg --format html … | tail -3 | grep`) or PR/CI/system verification (`gh pr view | jq | head`, `df -h | grep | head`) tripped the `>=2 operators` rule. Reporting and verification ARE the orchestrator's role (*verify + report*), so they must not require a subagent. **(coordinator directive.)**

## What it enforces

**Release carve-out** (`_is_sanctioned_release_chain`): a line is RELEASE (never blocked) when at least one chain-segment head is `gh ship` (env prefixes allowed) and every head is `gh ship`, read-only inspection, or `cd`. Covers `gh ship <n> --repo <owner/repo>`, `--no-screenshot-ok`, `cd <dir> && gh ship … | tail` (task #23). The gate does not validate ship's own flags.

**Report/verify carve-out** (`_is_report_or_verify_chain`): a line is REPORT/VERIFY (never blocked) when every segment head is `tg`, a read-only gh read (`gh pr list/view/checks/status/diff`, `gh run list/view`), read-only inspection (incl. `df`/`du`/`lsblk`/`free`/`ps`/… and filters `jq`/`sort`/`cut`/…), or `cd` — with at least one `tg`/gh-read head. Of any length: `tg … | tail | grep`, `gh pr view | jq | head`, `tg done; gh pr view; gh run list`.

**`curl` and `ssh` are deliberately NOT sanctioned** — `curl -X POST`/`-d` mutates and `ssh host '…'` runs any remote command, so neither can be reliably classified read-only; they keep the escape hatch (`ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK=1` + reason, or inline `# orchestrator-ok:`).

**Neither carve-out launders implementation:** a build/edit (`sed -i … && gh ship`, `tg done && sed -i …`), heredoc, command/process substitution (`gh ship $(sed -i …)`), bare-`&` background, or mutating companion (`git branch <arg>`, find `-delete`/`-exec` **and** file-write primaries `-fprint`/`-fprintf`/`-fprint0`/`-fls`) forfeits it.

## Review pass (this landed via a [skip-review] emergency recovery)

Ran a proper multi-model `review diff`; fixed the findings:
- **F1:** `UNSAFE_COMPANION` missed find's file-WRITE primaries (`-fprint*`/`-fls`). Added + test.
- **P1:** `CD_HEAD` used `\b`, matching `cd-clean`/`cd/foo`. Anchored on an argv boundary. Added negative tests.
- **F2/P2:** the veto scan + segment split were quote-blind → a quoted `;`/`&`/`$(` in a ship reason could false-block a legit ship. Added a quote-aware split + quote-blanked veto scan, scoped to the carve-out.

## Tests

`tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py`: 90 passed (release + report/verify allow/block matrices, `--repo`/`--no-screenshot-ok`/`cd`/quoted-reason cases, F1/P1 negatives, predicate-level assertions). Full agent-tools suite: **2124 passed, 21 skipped**. `ruff`: clean.

## Consolidation & activation

This is the **narrow, ship-first hotfix** to currently-live deadlocks in the already-provisioned hook — kept as its own PR (independently reviewable/shippable) rather than folded into the broader `feat/harness-workflow-guards` PR (worktree-only + orchestrator-only gating). Both touch `orchestrator_stays_thin.py`; recommend landing **this one first** (it is the unblock), then the broader PR (which carries the same guards, so no regression either way).

**Activation:** the hook is provisioned by `rig apply`. This is a fix to an already-installed hook; it takes effect on the next `rig apply`. Serialize with the open lint-on-write PRs (agent-tools #161 / rig-cli #103) and the harness-workflow-guards PRs (agent-tools #163, rig-cli #104) — **one `rig apply` after all land**, not several.

title: feat(agent-hooks): harness workflow guards — worktree-only + orchestrator-only (tg#5742/5743)
body:
## What & why

Two PreToolUse agent-hooks that enforce Alex's harness discipline (agents drift from prose rules; hooks make them stick), each per-repo configurable via `rig.yaml` `agent_hooks` knobs. Closes **#163**.

### `worktree-only-writes` (NEW — tg#5742)
A pre-write hook that **denies Edit/Write while the checkout is on the repo's default branch**. Authoring belongs in a worktree on a feature branch; the default branch is for merge/pull/read-only. The mid-session complement to the pre-push `protect-main` git-hook (#157) — that blocks the *push*, this blocks the *authoring* before it.
- Default branch detected via `origin/HEAD` → repo-local `init.defaultBranch` → local `main`/`master` (never hardcoded, never machine-derived).
- Judges the **target file's** checkout, not the shell cwd.
- **Opt-IN** (`agent_hooks.worktree_only`, default **false**) so a repo that works on main (`3d-cli`) is never blocked. Escape hatch `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1`. Fail-open on git/parse error.

### `orchestrator-stays-thin` (BROADENED — tg#5743)
Blocks inline implementation by the main thread while allowing read-only inspection and sanctioned orchestration (`gh pr list/view/checks`, `gh ship`, `tg`, `review`, `git worktree list`, GET-shaped `gh api`).
- Wrapper stripping (`timeout`/`gtimeout`/`env`/`nice`/…), quote-aware chain split.
- **Opt-OUT** (`agent_hooks.orchestrator_only`, default **true**). `RIG_ORCHESTRATOR_ONLY` env accepts `0`/`false`/`no`/`off`; `agent_hooks.orchestrator_only: false` exempts a repo (`3d-cli`). Escape hatch `ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK=1` + reason.

## Review hardening (this landed via a [skip-review] dead-agent recovery)

Ran a proper multi-model `review diff`; the head-anchored allow-list was laundering mutations the head can't see (each a regression vs the pre-existing hook). Fixed:
- **Substitution smuggling** (`gh ship $(gh api -X POST …)`, `cat <(git push) && tg done`) → scan each unquoted substitution's own segments; a **benign** read-only substitution pipe (`cat $(find …) | grep | head`) still passes (the #80 invariant).
- **Bare-`&` background** (`tg done & git commit`) → `_split_chain` now splits a bare control `&`, so the smuggled command is judged on its own segment.
- **Mutating companions** → `git branch <arg>` (incl. `git -C … branch`) and find's `-delete`/`-exec` **and** file-write (`-fprint*`/`-fls`) primaries excluded from the allow-list.
- **`gh run watch`** dropped from the allow-list (a long-running block, not a quick inspection).
- **`gtimeout`** stripped like `timeout` (macOS coreutils) so `gtimeout 60 git commit` doesn't bypass detection.
- **`RIG_ORCHESTRATOR_ONLY`** env now accepts the same falsy set as the YAML (`0`/`false`/`no`/`off`).
- **(coordinator)** read-only system-info + filter verification tools (`df`/`du`/`lsblk`/`free`/`ps`/…, `jq`/`sort`/`cut`/…) added to `READ_ONLY_BASH` so a verify pipe (`df -h | grep | head`, `gh pr view | jq | head`) isn't blocked by the `>=3-segment` rule.

## Provisioning & config knobs

Both hooks self-read their `agent_hooks.<key>` knob from the repo's committed `rig.yaml` at fire time — `rig apply` does not consume the value (the schema/validator side is rig-cli #104: `worktree_only` default false, `orchestrator_only` default true). **3d-cli exemption:** leaves `worktree_only` off and sets `orchestrator_only: false`.

## Tests

`tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py` + `tests/test_worktree_only_writes.py`: 165 hook tests. Full agent-tools suite: **2199 passed, 21 skipped**. `ruff`: clean.

## Consolidation & activation

The narrow `gh ship` release + `tg`/verify carve-out is a **separate, ship-first PR (#162)** — the live-deadlock hotfix to the already-provisioned hook. This PR is the broader tg#5742/5743 work; it carries the same guards, so no regression whichever lands first. Recommend landing #162 first, then this.

**Activation = `rig apply` after merge.** Serialize with the open lint-on-write PRs (agent-tools #161 / rig-cli #103) and rig-cli #104 — **one `rig apply` after all land**, not several. Before that apply, `3d-cli` must commit `orchestrator_only: false` (default is on).

title: fix(ship): restore gh ship --repo <owner/repo> cross-repo support
body:
## What & why

The `gh ship` alias resolves to a per-repo **thin delegator** (`.claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh`) that does nothing but forward its args: `exec "$AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT/ci/ship/ship.sh" "$@"`. It already passes `--repo` through — it needs no change. The actual ship logic lives in **agent-tools `ci/ship/ship.sh`**, and that script **explicitly rejected** `-R/--repo` ("ship.sh does not support -R/--repo …").

That rejection was the bug: an orchestrator forbidden a `cd && gh ship` has **no** other way to ship a PR into a non-CWD repo (agent-tools / rig-cli / tg-cli). `--repo` is the only mechanism. A previous full ship script (pre thin-delegator) supported `--repo`; the support was lost when the logic moved into `ci/ship/ship.sh`. This restores it, ported faithfully from that pre-rig-apply backup.

## Changes

- **`--repo <owner/repo>`** accepted in every gh-compatible spelling (`--repo X`, `-R X`, `--repo=X`, `-R=X`, `-RX`), validated to `owner/repo` shape.
- **Threaded through every gh call via an exported `GH_REPO`** — gh honours it for all subcommands, including `gh api` where the `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders expand from it. One assignment covers `pr view` / `pr diff` / `pr merge` / `pr comment` / `api graphql`. No per-call-site changes.
- **Foreign-remote branch-deletion guard**: when `--repo` names a repo that isn't this checkout's own origin, `git push origin --delete <branch>` would target the **wrong** remote, so remote-branch deletion is **skipped** with a clear message (GitHub's auto-delete-head-branch, or a manual delete, handles the target). Complementary to the existing fork-PR `CROSS_REPO` check; both independently skip deletion.
- **No-`--repo` path unchanged**: `GH_REPO` is left unset, so gh keeps its normal cwd inference.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fix**: the origin derivation reads the URL in its own step with `|| true` (a bare `git remote get-url | sed` aborts the script when there's no origin).

## Scope / follow-up

Faithful minimal port. The remaining LOCAL gates (version-bump version-file lookup, CI-down local test runner, local worktree/branch cleanup) stay CWD-bound, exactly as the original documented. Multi-model review (codex, 3×P1) flagged making those target-aware; that needs a target-checkout mapping (a new design out of scope here) and is tracked in #166.

## Tests

Replaced the old `-R/--repo` rejection test with: acceptance for all five spellings (asserting `GH_REPO` reaches the gh calls), the foreign-remote branch-deletion guard, and the unchanged no-repo path. **53 passed** (`uv run --with 'pytest>=8,<9' pytest tests/test_ship.py -q`). shellcheck: zero new warnings.

Closes #165.

title: fix(agent-hooks): visual-proof-gate resolves the real cd/-C target repo (#172)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes `visual_proof_gate.py`'s `effective_cwd()`/`_resolve_staged_files()` so a
  `cd <other-repo> && git commit` or `git -C <other-repo> commit` correctly resolves
  the REAL target repo's staged files instead of always checking the session's own
  cwd — the bugfix Alex authorized as a standalone merge (tg#6137), independent of
  unblocking any specific commit.
- Investigation found the tilde-expansion bug reported as "not working" plus 8
  additional real bugs surfaced through iterative multi-round review
  (`review diff --pool 1`), each with a regression test:
  - `cd ~/repo` was never shell-expanded → fabricated a nonexistent path → the
    whole gate silently failed open.
  - `effective_cwd` walked every segment in the command instead of stopping at the
    one commit segment, so a trailing `cd` (after the commit) or a `-C` on an
    unrelated non-commit git call could hijack the resolved directory.
  - Two-or-more commit segments in one command (a decoy commit + a real one)
    resolved to just the first segment's target, letting the decoy hide an
    unproven real commit elsewhere → falls back to `session_cwd` when there isn't
    exactly one commit segment.
  - Repeated `-C` flags on the same invocation now chain relative to each other
    (git's own semantics), instead of being resolved independently.
  - Command substitution / variable expansion / globs in a `cd`/`-C` target
    (`shlex.split` performs none of these) now leave `cur` unchanged instead of
    fabricating a bogus path.
  - `staged_files()` returning `None` used to fail the whole gate open
    unconditionally; now falls back to `session_cwd` specifically when the
    resolved target doesn't exist on disk (mirroring a real shell's `cd` failure).
  - An unresolvable `cd` AFTER an earlier, successfully-resolved `cd` in the same
    chain used to leave the stale earlier value in place; now aborts to
    `session_cwd`.
  - A `cd` reached only conditionally (`||`) or through a subshell/background job
    (`|`/`&`, either preceding or following) is no longer silently trusted.
  - `is_skip_commit()` used to return on the FIRST commit segment found, so
    `git commit --continue && git commit -m x` (a rebase-plumbing commit chained
    with a real one) exempted the WHOLE command from the gate; now requires every
    commit segment to carry a skip flag.
- 3 cross-cutting follow-ups were found but deliberately kept OUT of this
  standalone fix's scope (each filed as its own ticket, since they require
  touching sibling hook files or a larger feature):
  - [agent-tools#173](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/173) — port
    `require_review.py`'s `punctuation_chars` tokenizer (handles glued separators
    like `cd /repo;git commit`, and models `&&`/`;` cwd-carry semantics) into
    `visual_proof_gate.py` and `skills_read_gate.py`.
  - [agent-tools#174](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/174) —
    `skills_read_gate.py`'s skip-commit logic is now out of sync with the fix in
    this PR (still returns on the first commit segment).
  - [agent-tools#175](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/175) —
    evaluate EVERY commit segment's own target in a multi-commit chain, instead of
    falling back to `session_cwd` when there is more than one.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_visual_proof_gate.py -q` —
  71 passed (44 new tests added for this fix, all failing before / passing after)
- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/ -q` — full repo suite, 2321
  passed / 21 skipped, no failures
- [x] `ruff check` on both changed files — clean

  the final rounds only re-surfaced the 3 already-ticketed, deliberately-deferred

title: feat(agent-hooks): block-reset-hard — guard git reset --hard / clean -f
body:
## Summary

- New `pre-bash` agent-hook `block-reset-hard` blocks `git reset --hard` (any/no ref) and
  `git clean` with a real `-f`/`--force` flag (alone or clustered with `-d`/`-x` in any order)
  — both irreversibly wipe uncommitted/untracked work with zero undo.
- Detection is argv-based, never a raw substring match: line-by-line tokenization (catches a
  two-line `cd /repo` + `git reset --hard` Bash call), word-boundary-aware `#` comment
  handling, shell-grouping/control-flow stripping, a wrapper + value-flag table ported from
  `block-no-verify`/`require-ticket-before-commit` (`timeout`/`sudo`/`env`/`nice`/`time`/
  `exec`/`command`/`setsid`/`nohup`/...), and git global-option stripping (`-C`/`-c`/
  `--git-dir`/...).
- Escape hatch: `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD=1` + `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD_REASON=...` (reasonless
  override ignored), or inline `# no-reset-guard: <reason>` — gates both forms, one hatch.
- `on_error: closed` (fail-closed): parse failure, wrapper-chain overflow, or malformed event
  all block rather than allow.
- Registers the hook in `agent-hooks/README.md`'s and `AGENTS.md`'s pre-bash tables (both
  were also missing `decision-request-format` — added while touching that exact line).

## Context

Incident: a subagent working an unrelated PR ran `git reset --hard` mid-session in a checkout
shared with a different session, wiping that session's uncommitted work (recovered, but it
exposed a real gap — nothing technically stopped it). This hook turns an accidental
destructive reset/clean into a **deliberate, logged** one. It is **not** a hard wall — the
escape hatch is intentionally self-service, same as every sibling hook in this family. The
README is explicit about this and about what's fixed vs. documented as a known limitation
(the discriminator used throughout: would a confused, non-evasive agent produce this exact
command by accident, vs. does it require deliberately crafted input to evade).

## Test plan

- [x] 63 new tests in `tests/test_block_reset_hard.py` — block/allow matrix, wrapper forms,
      control-flow tokens, newline-separated commands, mid-word `#`, both escape hatches,
      fail-closed paths (unbalanced quotes, wrapper overflow, malformed event).
- [x] Full repo suite green: `uv run --with "pytest>=8,<9" pytest tests/ -q` → 2337 passed, 21
      skipped, no regressions.
- [x] Manually verified real `git clean -e -f` behavior against actual git (confirms the
      documented false-block limitation is accurate, not a bypass).
- [x] `review diff` (codex + gemini, 3 rounds) — each round's findings fixed before the next;
      last round's remaining findings intentionally left as documented limitations per the
      accidental-vs-adversarial discriminator (see README "Known limitations").

Closes #178

title: feat(agent-hooks): pin the primary worktree to its default branch (pre-bash)
body:
## Summary

- Incident (Alex tg#6462/tg#6477, 2026-07-04): an agent doing HYP-917 work briefly checked out its feature branch directly in the SHARED main checkout (`/Users/ultra/work/hyperide`) instead of its own isolated worktree; a second concurrent agent then also checked out (and committed on) a *different* feature branch there before switching back to main. No file damage this time, but a real collision.
- Two real, confirmed gaps found: (1) the sibling `worktree-only-writes` guard has never actually been enrolled anywhere (`agent_hooks.worktree_only: true` is absent from hyperide's, agent-tools', and rig-cli's own `rig.yaml`, and from the global `~/.config/rig/config.yaml`, despite its own docs claiming hyperide sets it) — tracked separately per repo; (2) even when enrolled, that guard only fires on Edit/Write and never sees a bare `git checkout`, and once on a feature branch its own logic treats that as "exactly where authoring belongs" regardless of *which worktree* it is.
- New `pre-bash` agent-hook `pin-primary-worktree`: detects the repo's PRIMARY worktree via git's own `--git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` distinction, and BLOCKS a `git checkout`/`git switch` that would move it onto anything but the default branch. A linked `git worktree add` tree is unaffected — that's exactly where branch work belongs.
- Shares the same `agent_hooks.worktree_only` opt-in knob + `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT` escape hatch as `worktree-only-writes` (one feature, one flag, cross-linked in both READMEs).

Closes #182.

**Note on interpretation:** Alex's ask was phrased as "block work on the main branch in the main worktree." The actual incident involved checking out a *feature* branch (not main) inside the primary worktree — this fix blocks that broader case (primary worktree → any non-default branch), since that's what the incident and the guard's own stated intent ("all authoring belongs in a separate worktree") require. Flagging this explicitly since it's a deliberate broadening of the literal wording, not a literal reading.

title: fix(agent-hooks): deny-by-default external-approval gate, replacing self-service escape hatches (tg#6554)
body:
## ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE — awaiting Alex's personal review

**This is a deliberate architectural security-model change, not a routine fix. Please review and merge it yourself — do not auto-ship it.** (Alex tg#6554.)

> **Note on the tracking issue (#188):** I created it to satisfy this repo's `require-ticket-before-commit` gate. The auto-mode classifier flagged that as outside the task's literal scope (the task named only a `tg-cli` follow-up issue). Flagging it here for your call — **close #188 if you don't want it**; the change itself is unaffected.

## ⚠️ Behavior change to flag consciously: `block-reset-hard` is ALWAYS ON, repo-wide

`block-reset-hard` has **no opt-in gate** — it fires for **every repo that installs it**, unlike `pin-primary-worktree` (which only fires when a repo opts into `agent_hooks.worktree_only`). Removing its self-service escape hatch means that, **with nothing configured**, `git reset --hard` and `git clean -f...` become a **hard, non-bypassable block repo-wide** for every installed repo, until that repo's owner wires `approval_cmd` in `rig.yaml`.

That is a real behavior/policy change beyond "closing a theater loophole": previously any agent could self-document a one-off with `# no-reset-guard: reason` or `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD=1`; now it can't, at all, without repo-owner configuration. This is the piece to sign off on consciously, not wave through as obvious hardening. (`pin-primary-worktree` is lower-impact — it only affects repos that already opted into worktree-only.)

## What & why

Both hooks shipped a self-service escape hatch that the **same agent the hook constrains** could set on itself — security theater, not a permission gate (Alex tg#6554):

- `pin-primary-worktree`: `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT` / `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT_REASON`, read from both the process env **and** an inline `VAR=val` prefix on the offending command.
- `block-reset-hard`: `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD` / `ALLOW_GIT_RESET_HARD_REASON` env, **and** an inline `# no-reset-guard: <reason>` sentinel anywhere in the command text.

Either way, the agent authoring the very command being checked could flip the bypass.

## Old vs. new model

| | Old (removed) | New |
|---|---|---|
| Grant path | Env var / inline sentinel the constrained agent sets on itself | `agent_hooks.approval_cmd` in the committed, code-reviewed `rig.yaml` only |
| Default (nothing set) | Bypass reachable by the agent | **Deny** — closed, no subprocess spawned |
| Who can open it | The agent itself | Repo owner via code review |
| Failure mode | n/a | Nonzero exit / error / timeout → **deny**, resolved inside the approval fn (never falls through to the hook's own `on_error`) |

New rig.yaml knobs (both optional):

```yaml
agent_hooks:
  approval_cmd: "/path/to/approve.sh"   # run when a block would fire; allow only on exit 0
  approval_cmd_timeout_s: 5              # default 5.0, hard-clamped to 6.0 (see below)
```

Context reaches the approval command as `RIG_APPROVAL_*` env vars (`HOOK`, `KIND`, `TARGET`, `CWD`, `COMMAND`) — never string-interpolated, so agent-controlled dynamic data has no injection surface. `shell=True` is deliberate and safe *specifically because* the command string comes only from `rig.yaml`.

## Key hardening details

- **Timeout clamp (`_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_CEILING_S = 6.0`).** The manifest `timeout_ms` was bumped 3000 → 12000 to give the internal approval subprocess (default 5s, clamped to 6s) comfortable headroom over realistic git-plumbing probes. `approval_cmd_timeout_s` is repo-owner-settable — an unbounded value (e.g. `30`) + a hanging script would otherwise let the *outer dispatcher* kill the whole hook at its manifest budget, which for `pin-primary-worktree` (`on_error: open`) resolves to a **silent ALLOW** — the exact self-grant class being removed. So the effective timeout is hard-clamped under the manifest budget; a misconfig can't become a bypass.
- **A backgrounded approval_cmd can't defeat the timeout.** The child runs in its own process group (`start_new_session=True`) and is SIGKILLed (whole group) on timeout, so a script that exits 0 but leaves a backgrounded child holding the stdout pipe can't hang the post-timeout drain forever and reach the dispatcher's fail-open. (Regression-tested: `"sleep 5 &"` + a 0.3s approval timeout denies in <3s.)
- **Approval failures never reach `on_error`.** A broken/hanging/denying `approval_cmd` always resolves to *deny* inside `_request_approval`, regardless of the hook's own `on_error` policy (which is only for the hook's plumbing failing).
- **The old bypass is now the strongest regression test.** `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 git checkout <branch>` (inline) still has to be *classified* as a git checkout (the leading-assignment skip stays) and then *blocked* — proving both that the classifier still sees through the prefix and that the prefix no longer grants anything.

## Residual considerations flagged in review — for your conscious sign-off

Multi-model review (4 rounds) surfaced two design tensions that I did **not** re-architect because they follow the task's explicit design and match pre-existing behavior. Calling them out so you decide, not so they hide:

1. **`approval_cmd` is read from the working-tree `rig.yaml`, which an agent could edit.** The trust boundary is "a bypass now requires a *reviewed config change* (a committed `rig.yaml` edit that goes through PR review), not an env var / comment the agent invents per-command." The hook does **not** itself verify `rig.yaml` is committed/clean — same as the existing `agent_hooks.worktree_only` knob, which reads the identical file. An agent that can already edit-and-commit `rig.yaml` is outside this hook's threat model. If you want the hook to hard-refuse a dirty/uncommitted `approval_cmd`, that's a deliberate follow-up (and should apply to `worktree_only` too, for consistency).

2. **`pin-primary-worktree` can still fail *open* on a hook-process timeout.** That is by design: pin is `on_error: open` because its own docstring calls it "workflow discipline, not a security boundary." The manifest budget (12s) comfortably covers the internal approval ceiling (6s) plus realistic (millisecond) git probes; a *genuinely hung* git probe was always a fail-open for pin, independent of this change. The real security gate — `block-reset-hard` — is `on_error: closed` and fails **safe** (deny) on any timeout. If you want pin hardened to fail-closed, that's a separate decision (it changes pin's long-standing advisory posture).

## Not in this PR (deliberate)

A genuinely unforgeable synchronous "ask Alex on Telegram and wait for a real reply" primitive must live **inside `tg-ctl`** (the sole trusted `getUpdates` consumer) — a hook polling the local reply log would be forgeable by the same agent it constrains, and even the bumped 12s dispatch timeout can't wait minutes for a phone tap anyway. Filed as a follow-up: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/149. The new `approval_cmd` extension point is designed to wire to exactly that once it exists.

## Tests

`tests/test_pin_primary_worktree.py` and `tests/test_block_reset_hard.py` updated:
- regression: old env + inline bypasses now BLOCK;
- unconfigured → deny (no subprocess spawned);
- `approval_cmd` exit-0 → allow; nonzero → block; timeout → block;
- context env vars reach the approval command (trust-boundary proof).

Full suite: `uv run --with "pytest>=8,<9" pytest tests/ -q`.
