body:
## Summary

- Adds `skills/universal/message-scope-verification/SKILL.md`: before dropping unfinished
  work (uncommitted changes, an open ticket, a running task) to act on a *new* inbound
  message, check whether the message actually reads as on-topic or as something from an
  unrelated project/repo/ticket/topic that never came up in this session. If it looks
  misdirected, ask the user to confirm before switching — don't silently abandon
  in-progress work on a guess.
- Requested by Alex (tg#6682): a message about an unrelated VS Code-extension task landed
  in the wrong agent pane/session. Rather than assign blame for that specific incident, he
  asked for a durable, harness-agnostic instruction so this class of misdirection gets
  caught by *any* agent, in *any* repo, going forward.
- Bumps the stale `README.md` "Universal skills: 39" inventory count to 45 (the real count
  including this addition) and lists the new skill in the inventory prose.

## Mechanism (why this needs no rig-cli change)

Confirmed via `riglib/catalog.py` + `AGENTS.md`'s "zero registration" section: `rig`
dynamically scans `skills/universal/<name>/SKILL.md` — dropping the directory here *is*
the whole registration story. Every repo with `skills.universal.all: true` (rig's default)
picks this up on the next `rig apply`, and `rig`'s per-harness `harness_skills.py` linking
makes it discoverable across every supported harness (claude-code, codex, opencode, etc),
not just one repo.

Per `docs/carrier-decision-guide.md`: this is a pure judgment call ("is this message
actually for me") with no mechanical/regex check — a **skill** (advisory), not an
agent-hook or git-hook, is the correct carrier.

## Live-provisioning test (not just a dry-run)

Ran a real (non-`--dry-run`) `rig apply` against a scratch test repo, with
`agent_tools_source` pointed at this branch and `HOME` overridden to an isolated scratch
dir:

```
rig-msv-skills-target/message-scope-verification/SKILL.md   <- materialized, correct content
rig-msv-fake-home/.claude/skills/message-scope-verification -> .../rig-msv-skills-target/message-scope-verification
                                                               <- harness-symlink resolves correctly
```

Confirmed via `ls`/`readlink`/`cat` through the symlink, not just the plan text.

**Caveat found during this test (filed separately, not blocking this PR):**
`rig apply`'s `tg_ctl/boot` action calls `launchctl`, which is NOT `HOME`-scoped like every
other action (fsutil copies/symlinks, git config) — it operates on the real `gui/<uid>`
launchd session regardless of `$HOME`. This silently repointed a live LaunchAgent at a
nonexistent scratch path during testing. Filed as
[rig-cli#116](https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/116); does not affect the
skill content or the zero-registration mechanism this PR relies on. A follow-up scoped to
`--only skills` avoids the issue entirely.

Also filed [agent-tools#191](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/191) for
pre-existing (not introduced by this PR) stale Inventory counts elsewhere in the same
README section (Agent-hooks, CI slots) that a review pass surfaced — left out of this diff
to keep it minimal.

      format (compared against `learn-from-feedback`, `decision-request-discipline`).
- [x] `review diff --staged` (2 rounds: fixed a stale inventory count and a universal skill
      wrongly cross-referencing a by-type-only skill by unqualified name).

      proves materialization + harness-linking with correct content (see above).

title: fix(agent-hooks): skills-read-gate is_skip_commit no longer exempts on first commit segment (#174)
body:
## Summary

- `skills_read_gate.py`'s `is_skip_commit()` returned as soon as it found the FIRST
  `git commit`-shaped segment in a chained bash command, and judged the exemption of the
  WHOLE command from that one segment alone. A chain like
  `git commit --continue && git commit -m "real change"` has a legitimate no-op
  `--continue` first and a real, substantive commit second — the old code saw `--continue`
  on segment #1 and exempted the entire chain, so the second (real) commit's author never
  had to satisfy the mandatory-skills-read gate.
- Fix: collect every commit-shaped segment in the chain and require **all** of them to
  carry a skip flag (`--continue`/`--abort`/`--skip`) before treating the whole command as
  exempt. Any single non-skip commit segment now forces the gate to fire.
- Ports, verbatim, the identical fix already implemented and review-approved for
  `visual_proof_gate.py`'s mirrored parser in open PR #176 (itself fixing #172) — that PR's
  own docstring flags this exact file as a known gap ("the mirrored parser in
  skills_read_gate.py still has the original first-segment bug — port this same fix
  there").

Closes #174.

## Scope note — visual_proof_gate.py intentionally NOT touched here

`visual_proof_gate.py` has the byte-identical bug in its mirrored `is_skip_commit`, but its
fix is **already implemented in open PR #176** (checks green, unmerged — that PR also does
larger, unrelated `effective_cwd`/cross-repo work on top of it). Re-implementing the same
~4-line change here would collide with #176 on the same function. The two SYNC'd parsers
are back in step once #176 merges — this PR does not need to wait on that, since it only
touches `skills_read_gate.py`.

Also note: PR #189 (a deny-by-default external-approval change to two other hooks) is a
different bug class entirely — it removes self-service escape hatches, unrelated to this
chained-segment exemption bug. The `pin-primary-worktree` hook has no `is_skip_commit` at
all (it gates checkouts, not commits); its own "chained bypass" concern is tracked
separately as #196 (per-segment approval, not exemption).

An automated `review diff` pass on this branch (correctly) flagged the two-file sync gap as
a P1 finding, since it can't see #176's in-flight state — that's this scope note's context.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_skills_read_gate.py -q` — 45 passed (43 existing + 2 new)
- [x] `pytest tests/ -q` (full suite) — 2369 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed
- [x] New regression test: a chained `--continue` plumbing commit followed by a real `-m`
      commit (and `;`-separated variant) now correctly WARN-then-BLOCKs (gate fires)
      instead of being wrongly exempted
- [x] New regression test: two chained `--continue` invocations (all-skip chain) still
      correctly stay exempt (ALLOW even on repeat)
- [x] Existing skip-flag / comment-injection / subagent-exemption tests still pass
      unchanged
- [x] Direct adversarial probe of `is_skip_commit()` against the exploit and legitimate
      cases (see session transcript)

title: feat(agent-hooks): RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* live Telegram escalation (tg#6554, tg#6660)
body:
## Summary

Closes #199. Refs tg#6554, tg#6660, tg-cli#149.

Stacks on **#189** (not yet merged) — this PR's diff includes #189's commits until that
merges; the diff to actually review here is just this branch's own commits on top
(`chore(lint)` + `feat(agent-hooks): RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*`).

Alex's original ask (tg#6554) proposed an external-approval extension point, which #189
shipped as `agent_hooks.approval_cmd` (a repo-owner-configured shell command in a committed
`rig.yaml`). After seeing #189, Alex clarified (tg#6660) he wants something more specific and
generic: an agent that wants a justified, one-time override sets
`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_<HOOK_ID>=<written justification>`, and the hook itself — with **zero
repo-level configuration required** — sends that justification to Alex over Telegram and
blocks for a real yes/no, one time only.

This PR adds exactly that, as a new shared library (`lib/agenttools_hatch_escalation`),
wired into both `pin-primary-worktree` and `block-reset-hard`, checked **before** the
existing `approval_cmd` fallback from #189 (which remains available, unchanged, for repo
owners who want a non-Telegram approver).

It depends on a **parallel, separate PR in tg-cli** (against
[tg-cli#149](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/149)) that adds a generic
`tg-ctl ask "<question>" [--timeout <seconds>]` CLI mode (exit 0 = approved, exit 1 = denied
for any other reason) — that PR is still in progress; this PR's `tg-ctl` resolution simply
returns "not available" (deny) if that binary/mode isn't present yet, so it's safe to merge
independently in either order.

## Security properties (all unit-tested — 2402 passed, 21 skipped, ruff clean)

- **Unset env var** → unchanged deny-by-default, no Telegram contact at all.
- **Blank or bare-flag value** (`=1`, `=true`, ...) → treated as an explicit **invalid**
  request: denied outright, does **not** fall through to `approval_cmd`. Deliberately
  stricter than "treat as unset" — the whole point of this feature is closing the
  `RIG_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1`-shaped hole, so a malformed attempt at the new mechanism must not
  get a free pass either.
- **`tg-ctl` resolution never consults ambient `PATH`** — the constrained agent runs in the
  same process tree and could shadow a PATH-resolved binary in the same turn
  (`export PATH=/tmp/evil:$PATH`). Resolution only checks a fixed, hardcoded list of
  well-known absolute install locations, or an explicit `agent_hooks.tg_ctl_path` in a
  **committed** `rig.yaml` (trusted config, not a same-turn-settable env var). A test proves
  a PATH-shadowing attempt is not what gets invoked.
- **Any internal error resolves to deny**, never allow (`request_hatch_approval` never lets
  an exception escape as anything but a denial).
- **One-time only**: the env var authorizes exactly the command that triggered the check;
  nothing persists.

## Flagged for your review, not decided unilaterally

1. **Relationship to #189's `approval_cmd`**: this PR makes `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` the
   PRIMARY path (checked first) and leaves `approval_cmd` as a secondary/custom fallback.
   Is that the right precedence, or should `approval_cmd` go away entirely once this lands?
2. **Timeout ceiling, cross-repo**: both `*.pre-bash.json` manifests raise `timeout_ms`
   12000 → 930000 (900s `tg-ctl ask` cap + 30s margin) so the outer dispatcher doesn't kill
   the hook into a silent allow (`pin-primary-worktree` is `on_error: open`) while a live
   Telegram wait is still in flight. **This is a real, user-visible behavior change**: an
   agent's Bash tool call can now legitimately hang up to ~15 minutes waiting on your tap,
   versus ~12 seconds before. Separately, **any consuming repo's `settings.json` entry that
   drives `cc_hook_bridge` for these hooks must also raise its own Claude Code hook
   `timeout`** past 900s — Claude Code's own default hook timeout (600s) would otherwise
   preempt this descriptor first and silently defeat the wait. That's a per-repo config
   change outside this PR's scope; flagging so it isn't silently broken in practice.
3. Two unrelated pre-existing `ruff` violations (unused import, ambiguous variable name)
   fixed in their own separate `chore(lint)` commit — trivially revertable if you'd rather
   keep this PR scoped to only the feature commit.

## Do not merge

This is a security-relevant change to two safety gates. Left open for your personal review.

title: feat(lib): agenttools_stall_watchdog — tiered warn/abort stall detection by watched-file mtime (#205)
body:
## Summary

Closes #205. Refs tg#6942 (Alex's original ask), tg#6962/tg#6967/tg#6973 (his live-test corrections).

A new `lib/agenttools_stall_watchdog` package: tiered **warn-then-abort** stall detection for a long-running process by watching **one file's mtime** — a background `Agent`-tool subagent's transcript (`subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`) or any e2e/test/build run's output log (`npm test`, Playwright, Electron launch). Built from the real incident where a background run sat stalled ~2 hours because the orchestrator polled manually every 20-30 min.

## The two tiers (channels per Alex's corrections)

| Tier | Default | Action | Audience |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WARN | 5 min | stdout line + one-line tmux pane nudge (`agenttools_tmux_inject`) | the watching agent — ENGLISH; nothing to Alex by default |
| ABORT | 30 min | stdout line, exit 2 + SIGTERM→SIGKILL of `--pid`'s process group + `tg` alert with explicit-field template + full diagnostic pointer | `tg` → Alex — RUSSIAN; `--tg-on-warn` opts warn tier back in |

Production defaults are exactly the original ask (5m/30m); any scaled-down test run must pass `--test` — messages then carry a mandatory test marker + the exact scaled threshold + 'prod default 5m/30m' (tg#6973).

## The honest limit (stated, not papered over)

An in-session `Agent`-tool subagent has **no OS pid and no tmux pane** (verified: `.meta.json` has no pid; no per-subagent process in `ps`). Nothing external can abort it — only the orchestrator's own `TaskStop`. So for that case the ABORT action IS the diagnostic pointer (path + quoted `stat`/`tail` + `SendMessage`/`TaskStop` hint) delivered to the orchestrator/Alex; the real kill only happens when a real `--pid` exists. Two deployment modes: in-session `Monitor` command (`--dry-run`, stdout lines are the events) or standalone daemon.

## Verification

- **69 unit tests** (fake clock/mtime seams, no real sleeps) + full repo suite green (2528 passed).
- **Live smoke test** (real tmux pane, real `tg` delivery, real dummy process, scaled 8s/20s thresholds): both tiers fired on time, dummy pid killed, pane nudge single-line English, tg alert Russian with test marker.
- **3 rounds of `review diff`** (opus+codex board), all findings addressed with regression tests, including two caught ONLY by the live test:
  - a multi-line pane injection gets **executed line-by-line by the target shell** (one of the message's own `tail` lines actually ran) → nudge is single-line by contract;
  - diagnostic `stat`/`tail` commands now `shlex.quote` the path (copy-paste injection);
  - kill runs before the notifications and wording says 'attempted' (no overclaimed kill);
  - `pid<=0` refused (would killpg the watchdog's own group); never killpg own process group (`nohup &` pattern); pre-existing stale file gets measure-from-start grace instead of an instant false ABORT killing a fresh pid; RECOVER reports the real stall duration; `abort_after<warn_after` is a clean parser error; leading-dash tg message padded.

## Do not merge

Orchestrator ships after verification — subagents don't merge.

title: test(stall-watchdog): real subprocess/tmux end-to-end proof under a simulated stall (#209)
body:
## What & why

`agenttools_stall_watchdog` shipped 2026-07-08 (#205/#206) with a thorough unit suite — but every test drives either `Watchdog` with a fake clock or `cli.run_watch` with `time.time`/`time.sleep` monkeypatched. **Nothing proved it fires when actually run for real.** A CLI-wiring bug, a real-clock timing bug, or a broken tmux-delivery path would pass the whole suite and still leave the watchdog silently dead in production — the exact multi-hour-stall failure mode this tool exists to prevent.

This adds `tests/test_agenttools_stall_watchdog_e2e.py`: it launches the **real** `python -m agenttools_stall_watchdog watch` CLI as a subprocess (real clock, real `time.sleep`, real tmux pane — no monkeypatching of time or `Watchdog`), lets real wall-clock time elapse with no writes past scaled-down 2s/4s thresholds, and asserts:

- the **WARN** tier delivers its English nudge to a real tmux pane, and
- the **ABORT** tier makes the real process exit code **2**.

Plus a negative control (a fresh file must not fire on a single `--once` poll).

## KEY RESULT: does the watchdog actually fire? YES.

Real end-to-end run (private tmux socket, real subprocess), captured live:

```
=== SUBPROCESS EXIT CODE: 2 ===
=== SUBPROCESS STDOUT ===
[stall-watchdog] WARN: /tmp/proof.jsonl — 2s with no transcript progress
[stall-watchdog] ABORT: /tmp/proof.jsonl — 4s with no transcript progress
=== TMUX PANE CONTENTS (the delivered nudges) ===
GOT[... [stall-watchdog] stall warning: watched process — no progress for 0.0min (proof.jsonl); ...]
GOT[... [stall-watchdog] ABORTED: watched process — no progress for 0.1min (proof.jsonl); ...]
```

Test output: `2 passed` with `ASW_REAL_TMUX_TESTS=1`, `2 skipped` in the default hermetic gate. Stable across 3 repeat runs. Full package suite: `72 passed`.

## Design notes / review findings addressed

Follows the existing opt-in real-tmux contract from `test_agenttools_tmux_inject.py`:
- **env-gated** behind `ASW_REAL_TMUX_TESTS` — skipped in the default hermetic `pytest tests/` gate and when tmux is absent, so CI stays deterministic;
- **private `-L` socket + `AGENTTOOLS_TMUX_BIN` shim** so the subprocess and the fixture talk to the same throwaway server and the user's real tmux is never touched;
- **echo-loop pane** (not a login shell) so the nudge is displayed, not shell-parsed;
- **WARN asserted specifically** (not "warn OR abort"), so an abort-only regression that drops the tier-1 nudge fails here;
- documents the `started_at` clamp: **backdating mtime does NOT simulate a stall** (that path is deliberately defended against, per a prior review finding), only real elapsed no-write time does.

## Follow-up filed (not fixed here)

#210 — `build_nudge_line` output contains unescaped shell metacharacters (`[stall-watchdog]` brackets). Harmless against an agent REPL (the documented target), but if `--tmux-target` is ever pointed at a raw shell prompt the nudge gets parsed as a command line (`zsh: bad pattern`). Doc-or-escape follow-up.

Ticket: #209

title: fix(agent-hooks): delegate ALL gh to subagents + clearer block message (reverts #159/#162 carve-out, tg#7103)
body:
## Summary
Two commits on this branch, both on `agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin`:

1. **Clearer block message** (`ec65f33`) — rewrites the `delegate-work-to-subagents` MESSAGE so it explains WHY the orchestrator is blocked (an intentional, CTO-agreed operating model, not friction to bypass), HOW to proceed (dispatch a subagent), and that it's a joint decision.

2. **Delegate ALL `gh` to subagents** (`c533db5`) — the CTO reversed the `gh ship` / read-only-`gh` orchestrator carve-out (Alex tg#7103). The orchestrator now delegates `gh ship` AND CI/PR verification (`gh pr checks/view`, `gh run`, `gh api`) to a subagent, exactly like `git commit`.

## What changed (commit 2)
- `ORCH_ALLOW`: dropped every `gh` entry. Only `tg`, `review`, `git worktree list` remain sanctioned orchestration.
- Removed the `gh api` GET-vs-mutation machinery (`_GH_API_HEAD`, `_gh_api_is_mutation`) — moot once no gh runs inline.
- Added `_is_gh_command`: any segment whose command head is `gh` (any subcommand) is an impl-signal. shlex+basename catches path-qualified heads (`/usr/bin/gh ship`), both branches skip `VAR=val` env-prefixes, and an unbalanced-quote segment falls back to a conservative head regex (block). `gh` as an argument/needle (`cat gh.md`, `git log | rg gh`) is NOT swept in.
- A dispatched subagent (`agent_id` present) stays exempt and runs gh/ship freely — the gate governs the orchestrator only.
- Updated MESSAGE, module docstring, pre-bash descriptor `description`, and README.md.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py` — 193 passed (rewrote the entire gh-allowed corpus to the new doctrine; added path-qualified / unbalanced-quote / env-prefix / subagent-exempt / direction-reversal tests)
- [x] `pytest tests/` full suite — 2536 passed, 23 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` — clean
- [x] `review diff -C .` — [ok], all findings addressed (path-qualified gh normalization, unbalanced-quote conservatism, env-prefix symmetry)

## Deadlock owner (must verify in tandem)
If the external CC-harness **auto-mode classifier** still denies SUBAGENTS from running `gh ship`, delegating ship to a subagent while blocking the orchestrator here reintroduces the #159 release deadlock. Within agent-tools a subagent CAN ship (`block-raw-pr-merge` allows `gh ship`), so the risk is only the external classifier — it must be verified/loosened alongside this change.

title: feat(ship): review-quorum preflight gate (Guard-B, self-merge-authority)
body:
## Summary

Guard-B of the self-merge-authority program: a hard-enforced review-quorum preflight gate in the canonical `ci/ship/ship.sh`, alongside the existing unresolved-threads / review-dwell / screenshot / version-bump gates.

Before merging, ship derives the PR's task code (`$REVIEW_TASK_CODE`, else a `HYP-<n>`/uppercase ticket token from the branch name, else the PR body) and queries `review task <code> --check --min-iter <N> --min-models <M> --json` (fallback `--quorum-check` for an older review-cli).

- **Bar met** → prints `[ship] AUTHORITY CONFIRMED — review quorum met: N iterations across M models for <CODE>. Self-merge authorized by the review-quorum gate.` and proceeds.
- **Bar short / no task code / `review`|`jq` missing / store unreadable** → **fail-closed refuse**.
- **Disable** the whole gate with `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM=0` (ops off-switch).
- **Audit**: one JSONL line (`authorized` / `bypass:approved` / `bypass:denied` / `refused`) per gated ship to `$SHIP_AUDIT_FILE` (default `~/.config/agent-tools/ship-audit.jsonl`); jq-less printf fallback (control-char-safe) so the line never drops.

### Bypass = live Telegram approval, NOT a self-service flag (per CTO tg#7306)

No override flag exists. When the bar is not met and the agent genuinely needs to proceed, it sets `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM="<justification>"`, which routes through `ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py` → the shared `agenttools_hatch_escalation` lib (the SAME lib `pin-primary-worktree` / `block-reset-hard` use) to `tg-ctl ask` Alex live; proceeds ONLY on his real-time approval. Blank/bare denied; unset prints the how-to and refuses.

**Hardened against self-authorization across four review rounds.** Within the trust model — `gh ship` runs from the orchestrator's canonical checkout with a trusted `PATH` (documented in the README; a hostile `PATH` or a PR-worktree `ship.sh` defeats *every* gate, not just this one) — nothing the PR contents or the env value carries can forge approval:
- No `SHIP_HATCH_TG_CTL` / `SHIP_HATCH_LIB_DIR` env knobs (removed).
- tg-ctl resolves off the OS account's **real home** (`pwd.getpwuid`), not `$HOME` and not the PR's repo — a doctored `HOME` or a PR-committed `rig.yaml` cannot redirect approval.
- The shared lib loads by **explicit file path** (not by-name off `sys.path`), registered in `sys.modules` before exec, and the helper runs under **`python3 -I`** — a malicious `PYTHONPATH` / `sitecustomize` cannot inject an always-approve module.
- Approval requires the helper's explicit stdout **sentinel** (`APPROVED …`) plus exit 0, so a benign/broken `python3` fails **closed** (no fail-open asymmetry vs the other gates).

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_ship.py` — 77 cases, with adversarially-verified regressions for every hardening: `resolve_home` ignores `$HOME`; a PR-committed / doctored-HOME `rig.yaml` can't approve; a `PYTHONPATH` hijack (malicious dir before the real lib) still loads the real lib; a fake `python3` exiting 0 fails closed; detached-copy fails closed; jq-less audit still lands with valid JSON.
- [x] Full repo suite: `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest -q` → **2766 passed, 23 skipped**.
- [x] `bash -n` + `shellcheck -x ci/ship/ship.sh` clean; `ruff check ci/ship/review_quorum_hatch.py` clean.
- [x] `review diff -C .` across five rounds; every finding addressed (self-service override → hatch; four self-authorization vectors; audit drop/escaping; docs/contract drift).

Ref #224.

title: fix(ship): fail-closed review-quorum gate against hollow 0/0 pass (#242)
body:
## Problem (#242)

The Guard-B self-merge review-quorum gate in `ci/ship/ship.sh` could authorize an **empty** quorum. On 2026-07-10, shipping review-cli #141, the `gh ship` subprocess printed `review quorum met: 0 iterations across 0 models` and **still authorized** — defeating the ≥3×3 self-merge bar.

## Root cause — two compounding bugs

1. **Wrong JSON keys.** `ship.sh` parsed `.iterations` / `.distinct_models` — keys review-cli **never emits**. review-cli's `quorum_check` emits `passed_iterations` / `distinct_models_passed`. So ship's counts were **always 0** (the "0/0" in the incident log was this parse artifact, not a store miss).
2. **Blind trust of `.passed`.** ship authorized purely on the subprocess's boolean `.passed`, never independently re-checking the numbers against its floor. A `passed:true` with a hollow 0/0 record — an older review-cli without the `min>=1` guard, a task-code miss, or a hostile `review` on `PATH` — self-merged.

The test suite never caught it because the fake `review` CLI in `test_ship.py` **mirrored ship's buggy keys** (`iterations`/`distinct_models`) and self-computed `passed`, so it validated a fiction.

## Fix (fail-closed)

- **Read the real keys** (`passed_iterations` / `distinct_models_passed`) — no fallback to the never-emitted legacy names, so a legacy-only payload reads 0/0 and refuses.
- **Re-derive the verdict from the counts.** Authorize ONLY when `passed==true` AND no `error` key AND both counts `>0` AND both meet the floor. The subprocess's boolean is never trusted alone.
- **Clamp `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_ITER`/`MIN_MODELS` to a hard minimum of 3** (raise-only): any unset / `0` / negative / non-numeric / below-3 value resolves to 3, so the floor can never silently be 0, and a positive sub-floor override (e.g. `2`) can't weaken the bar.
- Docs (`README`/`AGENTS`/header comment) corrected to "PASSED iterations", the ≥3 clamp, and the fail-closed re-check.

## Tests

Fixed the fake `review` to emit the **real** keys. New regressions (all adversarially verified — revert the fix → red):
- forged `passed:true` with 0/0 counts → **refused**
- real 3×3 record → **authorized** (proves the real keys are read)
- legacy-key-only payload (`passed:true`, 3×3 under old key names) → **refused**
- `MIN_ITER/MODELS=0` env + hollow record → clamped to 3, **refused**
- below-floor positive `2×2` override → clamped to 3, **refused with 2/3**

Full ship suite: **95 passed**.

Refs #242.

title: fix(block-raw-pr-merge): close the bare-newline / post-heredoc merge evasion (#213 follow-up)
body:
## What

Minimal follow-up carrying the **only** uncovered delta from the claude hatch stack (#231/#232/#233, all squash-merged): the `block-raw-pr-merge` **bare-newline evasion**, fixed WITHOUT the comment-swallow regression that a naive `.replace("\n", ";")` reintroduces.

`_split_segments` fed the whole command to shlex, which consumes a **bare newline** as whitespace — so `echo ok`+newline+`gh pr merge 1 --admin` collapsed into one `echo`-headed segment and the raw merge on the second line was **ALLOWED with no approval** (empirically `DETECTED=False` on current `main`).

## Fix

A quote-, escape-, comment- and heredoc-aware `_normalize_newlines` pass runs **before** tokenizing, and shlex's own commenter is disabled. Each step closes a distinct evasion surfaced across ~8 rounds of iterative Codex review; every one is **adversarially verified** (revert the step, and the raw merge is allowed with no approval):

- **bare newline to `;`** separator (the core bug), with a `#` comment dropped only to **end of its line**, tracked by an explicit word-boundary flag (so an escaped space `echo foo\ #` does not spoof a comment start);
- **`\`-newline continuation REMOVED** (parts join with no space) — a space would split `g\`+newline+`h pr merge` into `g h ...` and miss it;
- **backslash escaping honored** so an escaped quote (`echo \"`+newline+`gh pr merge`) can't spoof quote state; single quotes suppress escaping;
- **`lex.commenters = ""`** so a literal mid-word `#` (`echo foo#bar && gh pr merge`, a URL `#frag`) isn't truncated to end of input;
- the inserted **`;` is space-padded** so it can't glue to a preceding `)` into a `);` run that `_split_segments` wouldn't treat as a separator;
- **heredoc bodies skipped whole** (so a `gh pr merge` in a commit-message heredoc isn't falsely blocked), **fail-closed**: delimiter is the quote-removed shell word, and the body is skipped only when its terminator is actually found ahead — a mis-detected `<<` (arithmetic `(( a << b ))`, an unterminated heredoc) skips **nothing**, so a real merge after it is still detected (over-block is the safe direction; swallowing would be a bypass).

## What is NOT here (already on `main`)

`main` already carries the rest of the hatch stack: the `resolve_home()` P1 self-approval fix (`pwd.getpwuid`, not cwd/repo-local `rig.yaml`), the `\`-newline whitespace-drop, the inline-env prefix strip across skills / visual-proof / require-ticket, and the adversarial repo-local `rig.yaml tg_ctl_path` tests (`test_repo_local_rig_yaml_tg_ctl_path_is_ignored`). Only the bare-newline case — and the shell edge cases a correct fix must not reintroduce — was missing.

## Tests

- 23 new regression tests in `tests/test_block_raw_pr_merge.py` (bare newline, comment-vs-newline, mid-word `#`, escaped quote/space, continuation-inside-command-word, heredoc body / punctuated / quote-removed delimiters, arithmetic `<<`, `)`-glue).
- Full suite green: **2976 passed, 23 skipped**.

## Review status

Iterated `review diff -C ... -m codex` to convergence over the parser edge cases (8 rounds, each finding fixed + tested). The final confirmation pass is pending — Codex hit its usage limit mid-run. Full suite is green and every finding to date is fixed and adversarially verified. **Not self-shipping** — flagging for a final Codex pass + human merge.

Refs #213 #234

title: fix(block-raw-pr-merge): close command-substitution + gh-api merge bypasses (#248)
body:
## What

Closes the command-substitution raw-merge bypasses tracked in #248 in the `block-raw-pr-merge` agent-hook, plus the same-class gh-api / wrapper / interpreter vectors that a multi-model review surfaced while iterating to convergence. Same bug class as the bare-newline (#247) and gh-api (hyperide HYP-960) holes.

## The two headline bypasses (#248, both pre-existing on main)

The argv scanner missed a raw `gh pr merge` hidden in **command substitution**, because the substitution body stays inside one token so `argv[0]` is never `gh`:

1. **Backtick**: `` `gh pr merge 1 --admin` `` — not detected.
2. **Double-quoted `$()`**: `echo "$(gh pr merge 1 --admin)"` — the `$(...)` is kept as one double-quoted literal token and never inspected, though a real shell executes it.

(A bare `$(gh pr merge 1)` was also missed — the issue claimed `$()` was detected, but it was not.)

## Fix — extend the #247 over-block defense-in-depth net

Rather than perfectly parse shell, detect the executable-position merge even when tokenization hides it, over-blocking in the safe direction while keeping the anchor-on-invoked-command logic so plain mentions still pass.

- **Command / process substitution**: extract every *executed* body (`$( … )`, backticks — both incl. inside double quotes — and `<( … )` / `>( … )` unquoted), quote-aware so a single-quoted body stays inert, and re-scan each recursively. POSIX-unescape a backtick body so a nested `` \`…\` `` is visible; the reader is comment-aware so a `)` inside a `#` comment doesn't close `$()` early. Only executable regions are scanned — a `$()` in a `#` comment or a **quoted** heredoc body (`<<'EOF'`, literal) stays allowed; an **unquoted** `<<EOF` body (expanded) is blocked.
- **gh api merge routes** (#248 acceptance): `gh api …/pulls/<n>/merge` with a write method, and `gh api graphql` `mergePullRequest` / `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` mutations. A graphql query fed from a file/stdin or containing any `$`/backtick, and a shell-expanded REST method (`-X $METHOD`), are over-blocked (fail closed — unprovable at pre-exec). Skip `gh` global flags (`gh -R o/r pr merge`), and fix `@`-fragmentation so `-F query=@f graphql` resolves.
- **Invoked-command resolution**: see through a wrapper prefix (`env`/`sudo`/`timeout`/… best-effort list, incl. path-qualified and `env bash -c '…'`), and re-scan a shell interpreter's `-c` string / `eval` argument (incl. combined `-cx` opts).

title: fix(ship): dedup CI statusCheckRollup to latest-run-per-check (#260)
body:
## Problem

The Guard B ship gate (`ci/ship/ship.sh`) CI-status check counted **every** `statusCheckRollup` entry without deduping by check name. GitHub keeps multiple entries per check name when a workflow is re-run — it does **not** collapse to the latest run.

Observed live on **PR #653** (2026-07-12): the "PR Checklist" check has stale `FAILURE` runs from when acceptance boxes were unchecked. After the boxes were ticked, GitHub's own `mergeStateStatus` is `CLEAN`, but ship.sh still saw `PR Checklist -> FAILURE ×2` and refused. Re-running does not help (the checklist workflow reads the historical `pull_request.body`) and only adds more stale entries. This blocked all in-flight ext PRs and the 0.1.69 release.

Live proof on PR #653's real rollup: raw 20 entries → old buggy count **2 failing** (blocks); deduped 15 → **0 failing** (passes); latest `PR Checklist` run is `SUCCESS`.

## Fix

Collapse the rollup to the **latest run per check** before evaluating pending/pass/fail — matching how GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus`. The key and recency rule are built so it never collapses two genuinely-distinct checks and never weakens the gate:

- **Group by `__typename + workflowName + detailsUrl-host + name/context`.**
  - `__typename` keeps a `StatusContext` and a `CheckRun` that share a name apart.
  - The `detailsUrl`/`targetUrl` host keeps two different third-party providers that post an identically-named `CheckRun` with a null `workflowName` apart (a passing provider can't hide a failing one), while a re-run of one check shares its host and still dedups.
  - `workflowName` keeps a same-named check from a different workflow apart.
- **Recency (`_dts`):** rank by the run's own timestamp (`completedAt // startedAt // createdAt`) when it has one — a re-run always post-dates the run it replaces. **Only** a run with *no* timestamp at all AND still queued/in-progress gets a sentinel that sorts above any timestamp, so a timestamp-less queued re-run is **watched to completion** instead of being dropped below the stale completed FAILURE it replaces. A timestamped stale `PENDING` does **not** dominate a newer settled `SUCCESS`.

Fail-closed is preserved: a check whose **latest** run is `FAILURE`/pending still gates. `_dsettled` is derived from the existing `SETTLED_FILTER` so the two "settled" definitions can't drift.

## Tests (7 new, all adversarially verified)

- `stale_failure_with_newer_success_does_not_block` — old FAILURE + newer SUCCESS same name → merges (mixed distinct checks).
- `latest_run_failure_still_blocks` — latest run FAILURE → refuses.
- `pending_rerun_is_watched_not_blocked_by_stale_failure` — old FAILURE + queued re-run (null timestamps) → watched to its SUCCESS, then merges.
- `stale_pending_statuscontext_yields_to_newer_success` — timestamped stale PENDING must not dominate a newer SUCCESS.
- `same_name_statuscontext_and_checkrun_do_not_collapse` — cross-type same name → failing CheckRun still gates.
- `distinct_providers_same_name_checkrun_do_not_collapse` — two providers, same name, null workflow, different host → failing one still gates.
- `same_name_different_workflow_do_not_collapse` — same name, different workflow → failing one still gates.

Each guard is adversarially verified: reverting it re-breaks its case. Full suite: **102 passed**.

## Review

Multi-model `review diff --preset heavy` (Opus, Codex, Gemini, GLM, **Fable**, Sol). Fable and Sol returned `[ok]` (no blockers). Two P1s raised across passes were fixed in-branch: distinct-provider identity (`detailsUrl` host in the key) and pending-timestamp ranking (sentinel only for timestamp-less queued runs). Sol's remaining **[P1] pagination beyond `contexts(first:100)`** is a **pre-existing** fail-open independent of this change — tracked as **#262**, out of scope here.

Refs #260. Follow-up: #262. Sibling of the review-threads-stale family.

title: fix(ship): run local gate on empty rollup during a CI outage (#269)
body:
## What

Closes #269. When CI is billing-blocked or Actions is down, GitHub often never enqueues the workflows, so `statusCheckRollup` comes back **empty**. `gh ship` then hard-refused ("NO CI checks") and the only escape was `--skip-ci` — a merge that verifies **nothing** locally. The local-gate machinery existed (the checks-FAILED structural path) but was **unreachable** for the most common outage shape — Alex's "денег нет, CI будет часто ложиться" case.

## How

An empty rollup after the register-grace window is classified as an outage **only when** the PR's pushed base branch (`origin/<baseRefName>`) carries a workflow whose top-level `on:` block declares a `pull_request`/`pull_request_target` trigger:

- **Structural, indentation-aware detection** — a trigger is an inline scalar/list, a block key, or a direct-child list item. Never a substring in a `branches:`/`paths:` filter value, a nested branch name, a comment, or a job `if:` expression.
- **Read from committed + pushed remote state** (`git ls-tree`/`git show` on `origin/<base>`), not the mutable worktree — an untracked / locally-modified / committed-but-unpushed workflow can't flip the decision.
- On a match, ship runs the **same** local fallback gate the checks-FAILED path uses (tests + leftover scan + PR checklist + review threads) and, only if fully green, falls through to the **normal non-admin merge** — identical posture to the existing structural-outage path, so **branch protection still gates it** and ship never silently `--admin`-bypasses.
- No workflow / non-PR-only workflows (push/schedule) → hard refuse stands. A foreign target (`--repo` / `GH_SHIP_REPO` / `GH_REPO`) → hard refuse (local gate runs against this checkout, not the target; relates #166).

**Residuals** (documented + pinned by tests): a filtered `pull_request` trigger (branches/paths/types) is still treated as an outage (the local gate runs, so the merge is verified); quoted-key `"on":` / flow-mapping `on: { … }` forms conservatively hard-refuse (safe direction).

## Tests

18 new/updated `test_empty_rollup_*` / `test_nonempty_rollup_*` cases in `tests/test_ship.py` covering: outage→green-local-gate→merge; red-local-gate→refuse; no-workflow / push-only / bare-list-branch / quoted-filter / untracked / unpushed → refuse; block-form + `pull_request_target` positives; foreign `--repo`/`GH_SHIP_REPO`/`GH_REPO` → refuse; base≠default → refuse; non-empty-rollup doesn't enter the path; a fake-`gh` argv assertion proving the merge carries no `--admin`.

- `python -m pytest tests/test_ship.py tests/test_block_raw_pr_merge.py` → **282 passed**, exit 0
- `ruff check tests/test_ship.py` → clean
- `shellcheck -S warning ci/ship/ship.sh` → 8 pre-existing warnings, **0 new**

## Review

7 rounds of multi-model `review diff` (Opus + Codex + others). Final round: **no blocking bugs; all dangerous directions fall toward refuse** (Opus). The trigger-detection and foreign-target classes were driven to structural closure across rounds; remaining items are documented safe-direction residuals.

## Docs

`ci/ship/README.md` + `AGENTS.md` ship contracts updated for the exception.

title: feat(ship): gate --skip-ci behind a one-time Telegram HATCH approval (deny-by-default) (#279)
body:
Closes #279.

## What
Gate `gh ship --skip-ci` behind a one-time Telegram HATCH approval (deny-by-default) instead of a free self-service admin bypass. Reuses the existing shared hatch mechanism, mirroring the review-quorum gate (Guard-B).

`--skip-ci` skipped the entire green-CI gate AND branch protection (admin merge) and an agent could set it itself. The legitimate "CI billing-blocked / infra down" case is already auto-handled on the `SKIP_CI=0` path (auto-detect outage → local fallback gate → normal non-admin merge), so `--skip-ci` was purely a blind self-authorized bypass.

## How
- `ci/ship/ship.sh`: at the merge step, when `SKIP_CI=1`, `_skip_ci_hatch_gate` runs **before** the admin merge. Deny-by-default: unset `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_SKIP_CI` → refuse with how-to; set → route through the helper; proceed ONLY on exit 0 **and** a leading `APPROVED` sentinel (fail-closed on a broken/fake `python3`). `SKIP_CI=0` billing-outage auto-fallback untouched.
- `ci/ship/skip_ci_hatch.py`: new helper, hardening parity with `review_quorum_hatch.py` — `python3 -I` isolation, `spec_from_file_location` fixed-path lib import, `resolve_home()` authority (never repo/cwd), APPROVED sentinel, own `skipci:bypass:*` audit line, blank/bare short-circuited locally before any tg-ctl round-trip. Dry-run previews send **no** Telegram round-trip and never claim a live approval, but still enforce deny-by-default.
- No agent-settable off-switch (an off-switch would defeat the gate). Threat-model caveat documented (a PATH-controlling shipper can defeat any gate — same as the review-quorum gate).
- Audit decisions namespaced `skipci:bypass:approved` / `skipci:bypass:denied` / `skipci:refused` (with `gate:"skip-ci"`); docs (ship.sh usage, `ci/ship/README.md`, `AGENTS.md`) updated for the new contract + enum.

## Tests
- 13 new skip-ci tests: in-process live approve/deny + dry-run; e2e deny-by-default, set-but-blank, fail-closed (fake `python3`), **approved → admin merge**, dry-run (no false approval), dry-run blank-deny. Audit single-write invariant asserted (exactly-one line).
- Migration of the ~42 pre-existing `--skip-ci` shortcut tests: real-`ship.sh` tests now run the normal non-admin merge via a GREEN `statusCheckRollup` from the fake `gh` (`--skip-ci` dropped); copy-`ship.sh` hatch tests get a fake approving `skip_ci_hatch.py` beside the copy.
- **Full agent-tools suite green: 3101 passed, 23 skipped.**

## Review
`review diff --pool 2`, three rounds. Core gate rated **[ok]** by Opus (correctness) and Gemini (contracts). All P1/P2 findings addressed: dry-run false-"APPROVED by Alex" fixed; blank/bare guard made local; audit single-write assertions added; stale `--skip-ci` billing-guidance docs updated. (Codex timed out on the last round — infra, not a finding; it was `[ok]` in the prior rounds.)

title: feat(lib): agenttools_rig_delegate — shared rig-aware install-hooks decision
body:
## What

Adds `lib/agenttools_rig_delegate/` — the single place every ecosystem CLI decides, at the top of its `install-hooks` command:

- **rig present** → DELEGATE to rig (rig owns the hooks; the CLI runs `rig apply` / `rig config set` instead of writing hook files itself).
- **rig absent** → run the tool's own direct installer (the FALLBACK), so a no-rig machine still gets working hooks.

This is the foundation for Alex's tg#8672 ("install hook просто делают rig set если обнаружен rig"): it removes the double-source-of-truth that produces codex's `loading hooks from both …/hooks.json and …/config.toml` warning.

## Surfaces

- **Python CLIs** (review, …) import it: `delegate_or_fallback(rig_args, fallback)`.
- **Non-Python CLIs** (`tg-ctl` is a bun/TS binary) shell out to the `__main__` mirror: `python3 -m agenttools_rig_delegate {detect | delegate …}`.

## Design notes

- Detection is robust: rig is "present" iff a runnable `rig` resolves (PATH + well-known bins + `RIG_BIN`); a mere source checkout is not enough.
- A rig that is present **but fails** surfaces its exit code — it never silently falls back (that would re-create the double-write).
- Stdlib-only at import (`os`/`shutil`/`subprocess`).

## Tests

15 tests (`tests/test_rig_delegate.py`) cover detection, delegation, fallback, and the CLI mirror. `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_rig_delegate.py -q` → 15 passed. `ruff check` clean.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs, tracked)

1. **rig-cli**: make rig the single codex-hook source — write to codex's honored location and fold in the tg-ctl usage-telemetry Stop hook (so removing tg-ctl's direct write loses no capability).
2. **tg-cli / review-cli**: call this helper — delegate when rig present, keep direct install as fallback.
3. **Codex hook TRUST decision needed from Alex** (see the thread) — rig's codex guards are currently untrusted → inert in autonomous `codex exec`; consolidation alone does not make them fire.

title: fix(block-raw-pr-merge,ship): unblock review-thread resolves; auto-resolve addressed bot nits
body:
## What
Fixes the wedge where `gh ship` tells an agent to resolve review threads but the `block-raw-pr-merge` agent-hook blocks the only API to do it.

## Hook fix (`block-raw-pr-merge`)
The hook fail-closed on **any** `gh api graphql` query carrying a `$` (a GraphQL variable), so `resolveReviewThread` / `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply` were blocked as if they were a raw `gh pr merge`. Now the decision is made by **shell quoting read from the raw command** (shlex erases it from parsed tokens):

- a **single-quoted** `$t` is a literal GraphQL variable → **allowed** (the query GitHub receives is exactly the text the hook read; the literal `mergePullRequest`/`enablePullRequestAutoMerge` scan is authoritative);
- a **shell-expandable** `$`/backtick (unquoted, double-quoted, concatenated, glued flag forms, or inside a `$( … )`/backtick substitution or `bash -c` rescan) is **over-blocked** (the shell could splice a merge field past the literal scan).

Implemented by blanking single-quoted `$`/backtick before the (heredoc-aware, normalized) token pipeline + an argv-anchored expandable-query check applied at **every recursion depth**. A raw `gh pr merge` and a literal merge mutation are **still blocked**.

## `gh ship` feature
New opt-in `--resolve-addressed-threads` (or `SHIP_RESOLVE_ADDRESSED_THREADS=1`) auto-closes **only** threads that are safe without a human — unresolved + `isOutdated` (a later commit addressed the code) + authored **entirely** by bots — before every review-thread gate (main + CI-down fallback). Fail-closed on >100 comments, null totalCount, null/ghost author. Human or still-current threads are never touched and still block.

## Tests / proof
Hook match-change (resolve allowed in every quoting/flag/recursion form; every merge route still blocked — proof artifacts captured across 8 review rounds) + ship auto-resolve wiring, dry-run, opt-in default-off, resolve-failure fail-safe, CI-down ordering, and the real jq eligibility program. Docs synced (AGENTS.md, both READMEs, descriptor, --help). Gate green: ruff + `pytest tests/` (3152 passed).

Reviewed across 8 rounds (multi-model `review diff`) to convergence — both reviewers [ok], no actionable findings.

body:
## What & why

Companion to tg-cli#202. `tg` now enforces the decision-request format **deny-by-default** on `--tag decision|question`: a malformed escalation is BLOCKED (exit 1) unless it carries options-as-a-table/list with pros/cons, a recommendation, context, a `file:line` "where to look", AND readability structure (per-section `<h3>`/`<h4>` headings, bullet lists, `<hr>` dividers — no wall of text). Markdown pipe grids auto-convert to a real Telegram `<table>`.

This skill (`skills/universal/decision-request-discipline`) is provisioned machine-wide via `rig`, so it now documents:
- that the format is **machine-enforced** by `tg` (not just a style suggestion),
- the structure/readability requirement (tg#8970 — an 8-point message can still be rejected if it's a wall of text),

title: fix(block-raw-pr-merge,ship): close three hook accuracy gaps
body:
## Summary

Closes three accuracy gaps in the `block-raw-pr-merge` agent-hook and the `gh ship --resolve-addressed-threads` feature.

- Fixes #289 — `block-raw-pr-merge` no longer false-positives on a non-`gh` command (e.g. a Telegram report) whose unparseable argument merely mentions merge tooling in prose. The unbalanced-quote fallback now anchors on a best-effort invoked-command prefix before applying the raw merge-hint regex; a real `gh`/shell/`eval`/wrapper merge on the same fallback path still blocks.
- Fixes #284 — `block-raw-pr-merge` now fails closed on a `gh api graphql` field whose KEY (not just its value) is shell-expansion-derived: `-f $FIELD`, `--raw-field=$FIELD`, and a bare post-endpoint `$ARGS` token could previously splice a merge mutation past the literal `query=` scan. A literal non-`query` key with an expandable value (`-F id=$NODE_ID`) still passes.
- Fixes #285 — `gh ship --resolve-addressed-threads` now excludes a bot-authored, outdated review thread from auto-resolution when any comment carries a high-severity marker (P0/P1/critical/blocker/security), so a still-valid high-severity bot finding is never silently merged just because a later commit made the thread `isOutdated`. A plain bot nit is still auto-resolved as before.

## Process

- All code changes were written by `codex exec` (non-interactive Codex CLI), per this session's delegation requirement — the orchestrator did not hand-edit the fix code.
- TDD red-first for each ticket: a failing test was written and confirmed failing before the fix.
- Independent adversarial verification: after each Codex pass, the orchestrator re-ran the real detection code (or the extracted `jq` filter) against additional boundary cases beyond Codex's own tests. This caught one real gap in the first pass of #285 — a hyphen-suffixed severity marker (`"P1-blocking issue"`) was wrongly treated as safe to auto-resolve, because the boundary regex excluded hyphens to avoid a different false-positive (`"security-first-initiative"`). A follow-up Codex pass fixed it by dropping the hyphen from the boundary class, accepting the resulting over-exclusion on compound words as the safe direction.
- A multi-model `review diff` (Opus + Fable personas) ran against the combined diff. It raised one structural finding — the new #284 check implicitly depends on `_API_VALUE_FLAGS` staying complete, which was previously cosmetic and is now load-bearing — now covered by a regression test and an explanatory comment. Three lower-priority findings (ship.sh's severity vocabulary breadth, the eligibility jq living in a shell string, and missing severity-filter coverage on the CI-down fallback path) were filed as separate follow-up tickets (#298, #299, #300) rather than bundled into this change.

## Test plan

title: feat(block-raw-pr-merge,gh-graphql): precise merge scan + a gh api graphql alias (ghgql)
body:
## What & why

Two coupled changes. Closes #302.

### 1. `block-raw-pr-merge` blocks merges more precisely
The guard's blunt "`mergePullRequest` token anywhere in the graphql call" scan false-blocked a **read-only** `gh api graphql` query that only NAMES a merge token as data — e.g. a code/PR `search(query: "mergePullRequest")`. That is not a merge and must be allowed.

`_graphql_carries_merge_mutation` now strips GraphQL **string literals** and **`#` comments** from the readable `query` value before scanning, and scans every non-`query` token raw. The stripper mirrors GraphQL lexing, including the block-string `\"""` escape. Still fail-closed and blocked:
- a real `mergePullRequest(` / `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` / `enqueuePullRequest` / `mergeBranch` field call,
- a merge token OUTSIDE a readable `query` value (non-`query` field, bare arg),
- an unprovable/expandable/file/stdin-backed query,
- `gh pr merge`, the REST `…/pulls/<n>/merge` write. `gh ship` stays allowed.

### 2. A convenient, read-only-by-default `gh api graphql` alias
Ships as the `gh-graphql` universal skill: the **`ghgql`** wrapper (single-quoted inline query, `-F` variables, `--paginate`, `@file`/stdin, `--dry-run`, `--jq`). It refuses a mutation by default.

Because a command-string PreToolUse hook cannot see the `gh` subprocess `ghgql` execs, the guard now **maps a `ghgql …` invocation to the `gh api graphql` request it runs**, so a merge through the wrapper — even with `--allow-mutation`, a `@file`/stdin query, or a smuggled second `query=` field — is blocked. `ghgql` is never a raw-merge bypass. Named `ghgql` (not `ghq`) to avoid colliding with x-motemen/ghq.

## Coupling
The alias's typical read-only invocation is proven NOT blocked by the refined hook (`test_gh_graphql_helper_readonly_recipe_is_allowed`, `test_ghgql_readonly_and_non_merge_writes_allowed`). rig provisions the skill via its catalog in the coupled PR: **alex-mextner/rig-cli PR (feat/provision-gh-graphql-alias)**.

## Tests
Full agent-tools suite: **3273 passed, 6 skipped**. New coverage: read-only string-literal/comment/escaped-block-string queries allowed; the full landing-mutation set blocked; every `ghgql` merge route blocked; `ghgql` wrapper behavior (`tests/test_ghgql_wrapper.py`). TDD red-first.

Multi-model review (opus) ran each iteration and closed **two real bypasses** it found: a cross-line `#`-comment-quote phantom span, and two `\"""` escaped block-string delimiters straddling a real `mergePullRequest(` call. Final verdict: no bypass found.

title: fix(ship): local-test-runner subdir + audited config fallback (#309)
body:
## Summary

- `_local_test_runner()` in `ci/ship/ship.sh` only checked the repo **root** for `pyproject.toml`/`package.json`/`Cargo.toml`. Monorepo-of-fixtures layouts (e.g. `hyper-ext-e2e`, whose real test suite lives in `e2e/package.json` with no root-level manifest) always fell through to "no recognized test runner found" and permanently blocked `gh ship`'s CI-down local fallback gate, even though tests genuinely exist and pass.
- Adds two additive capabilities, preserving all existing root-detection behavior:
  1. **Audited per-repo `$root/.ship-config` file** — `KEY=value` lines, `#`-comments, two whitelisted keys (`SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR`, `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD`). Read from the last **committed** content at `HEAD` (`git show HEAD:.ship-config`), never the working tree. Outranks both heuristics below it (rig.yaml and auto-detect), stays below the pre-existing test-only `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_CMD` env var. `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR` is validated both lexically (no `..` component, not absolute, not root-equivalent) and physically (a symlink can't resolve the directory outside the repo, or back to the repo root itself).
  2. **Bounded subdirectory auto-detection scoped to `e2e/` ONLY**, one level deep. (An earlier iteration also guessed `test/`/`tests/`, but three independent review rounds flagged that those directory names are exactly where repos most often keep fixture manifests unrelated to the real suite — narrowed to just `e2e/`, the concrete case that motivated this feature.)
- Split into six small, single-purpose functions (`_ship_config_load`, `_ship_config_dir_is_safe`, `_dir_is_real_descendant_of_root`, `_ship_config_run`, `_local_test_try_dir`, `_local_test_runner`), all 10–58 lines, under the repo's ~80-line function ceiling.
- Updated `ci/ship/README.md` and the in-file header comments to document the new file and the full revised precedence order.

## Review history (six rounds, all `[ok]`)

This PR went through six rounds of multi-model `review diff` (rounds 1–3: claude-fable-5 + claude-opus-4-8; rounds 4–6: full pool including codex). Every round surfaced genuine, substantive findings that were fixed before the next round — including two exit-code-sentinel collisions (the same class of bug, caught once and then caught again one abstraction level up), a `.ship-config` "audited" claim that wasn't actually enforced against the mutable working tree, a symlink-escape gap, and a SIGPIPE risk in a NUL-byte defense (the fix for which itself had a bug caught by the test suite before shipping). Full details are in the final commit message on this branch.

**Deliberately NOT fixed here (flagged for a separate follow-up decision, not self-filed as tickets):**
- Whether `ROOT` in the CI-down gate as a whole (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff) can point at the launcher's checkout rather than the PR's own head — raised independently at P1 by the Codex reviewer in three separate rounds. This affects the entire local-fallback gate architecture, not just the subdirectory/`.ship-config` additions, so it's out of scope for this PR.
- A pre-existing gap (unrelated to this diff) where the CI-down detection's failed-rollup path doesn't apply the same foreign-repo-target guard the empty-rollup path already has.
- A check-ordering question: the local fallback gate's manifest/config detection runs before this script's pre-existing dirty-worktree check elsewhere in the flow.
- A design-consistency suggestion that an invalid-but-present `.ship-config` (rejected `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR`) should fail closed rather than fall through to auto-detect, matching how other invalid-DIR cases already fail closed — considered, but deferred since several already-passing tests deliberately pin the current fall-through behavior and changing it needs its own careful pass.

## Test plan

- [x] 37 new tests added to `tests/test_ship.py`, matching the existing `repo_with_pr_worktree` / `_run_ship_cidown` / `_fake_gh_cidown_dir` / `_fake_gh_vbump_dir` fixture styles — covering the subdirectory auto-detect, every `.ship-config` precedence/validation case, both exit-code-sentinel-collision regressions, both symlink-escape cases, the NUL-byte guard (and its own empty-file edge case), and the version-bump-gate exemption's exact-path matching.
- [x] Full suite: `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` → **141 passed before this change, 177 passed after** (36 net-new tests — one obsolete test from an earlier iteration was replaced by two more precise ones). No regressions.
- [x] `bash -n ci/ship/ship.sh` — syntax check clean.
- [x] Function-length self-check: all six touched/added functions are 10–58 lines, comfortably under the repo's ~80-line ceiling.
- [x] Confirmed zero review-quorum-gate code in this diff (`git diff origin/main -- ci/ship/ship.sh | grep -i quorum` → no matches) — this PR is scoped strictly to the local-test-runner detection logic.

Tracking issue: #309. Related (different repo, same gap from the consuming-repo angle, not this repo's own ticket): hyperide `HYP-1100`.

title: fix(ship): stop leftover-marker XXX gate false-positiving on mktemp templates
body:
## Summary

- `_local_leftover_check` in `ci/ship/ship.sh` (~line 539) scanned PR diff additions for `TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX` as plain substrings, so any line using bash's conventional `mktemp` template suffix (e.g. `mktemp -d "/tmp/foo.XXXXXX"`) tripped the `XXX` branch and blocked an otherwise-clean PR from the `ship.sh` CI-outage local fallback gate.
- Confirmed false positive on hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e#137, which is what surfaced this bug.
- Fix: `XXX` now requires a run-length guard, `(^|[^X])XXX($|[^X])` — a portable idiom (no `\b`/`-w`) already used elsewhere in this repo (`ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh`'s focused-test check) — so `XXX` fails to match only when it's part of a run of 4+ X's (the mktemp-template shape). It deliberately still catches an `XXX` marker embedded in an identifier, e.g. `XXX_REMOVE_BEFORE_MERGE` or `fooXXX_debug()`, which a generic word-boundary fix would have missed.
- `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK` deliberately keep plain substring matching: widening them to whole-word would create a fail-open divergence from `ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh`'s untracked-TODO/FIXME check, which also substring-matches so it catches sentinel identifiers like `TODO_REMOVE_BEFORE_MERGE`. There's no known real-world false positive for these three that would justify that regression.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the false positive against a `mktemp -d "/tmp/foo.XXXXXX"` line before the fix
- [x] Added `test_cidown_mktemp_template_not_flagged_as_leftover` — mktemp template must NOT block
- [x] Added `test_cidown_standalone_xxx_marker_still_blocks` — a genuine standalone `XXX` marker must still block
- [x] Added `test_cidown_three_x_mktemp_template_still_blocks` — pins the documented residual limitation (a bare 3-X template `foo.XXX` is indistinguishable from a real marker and still blocks)
- [x] Added `test_cidown_todo_fixme_hack_substring_still_blocks` — a `TODO_`-prefixed sentinel identifier still blocks (keeps parity with `leftover-grep.sh`)
- [x] Added `test_cidown_xxx_sentinel_identifier_still_blocks` — an `XXX_`-prefixed sentinel identifier still blocks (narrower fix than a generic word-boundary)
- [x] Full suite: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` → 146 passed
- [x] Reviewed via `review diff` (multi-model: codex + Fable) across 3 rounds; addressed every finding (scoped the fix to XXX only instead of widening all 4 markers to avoid contract drift with `leftover-grep.sh`, switched from a generic word-boundary to a run-length-only guard so embedded sentinel identifiers like `XXX_REMOVE_BEFORE_MERGE` are still caught, added tests pinning every documented trade-off)

title: feat(ship): accept bare GitHub issue numbers as task codes via .ship-config
body:
## Summary

`ship.sh`'s review-quorum gate only recognized `HYP-123`/`XX-123` style task codes. Repos whose task-cli backend is GitHub Issues (bare `#NNN`, no ticket-code convention of their own) could never derive a task code and were permanently refused by the gate — this blocked agent-tools#349.

Adds a third whitelisted `.ship-config` key, `SHIP_TASK_CODE_PREFIX=<PREFIX>`: when set, a bare `#NNN` found in the branch name or PR body synthesizes `<PREFIX>-NNN` as the task code — **never the bare `#NNN` itself**.

## Why the synthesized prefix, not the bare number

review-cli's quorum store is a single global file keyed only by the task-code string, with no per-repo scoping. Two different repos both deriving bare `#346` (e.g. `agent-tools#346` and `rig-cli#346`) would silently share — and falsely satisfy — each other's review-iteration count. The prefix is what keeps the code collision-free per repo.

## Behavior

- Opt-in and additive only: `HYP-`/`XX-` codes still take precedence; an unset prefix leaves existing behavior completely unchanged.
- `SHIP_TASK_CODE_PREFIX` must be 1-40 uppercase letters/digits — a malformed value invalidates the whole `.ship-config` file (fail-closed, same policy as an unsafe `SHIP_LOCAL_TEST_DIR`).

## Companion rig-cli PR

Adds `task.code_prefix` to rig.yaml + a `rig apply` action that writes it into `.ship-config` (rig-cli, separate PR).

## Test plan

- [x] 4 new tests: opt-in synthesis, no-optin unchanged, HYP- precedence over synthesized code, malformed-prefix rejection
- [x] Full suite: 193 passed, no regressions

title: fix(agent-hooks): restore gh-ship + add tg carve-out for orchestrator (#159)
body:
## What & why

Restores a NARROW slice of the old `gh ship` orchestrator carve-out (agent-tools#159 /
agent-tools#162) that PR #212 (tg#7103) removed: the orchestrator may run `gh ship <PR#>`
inline again, same as a dispatched subagent — matched only on the exact shape (head `gh`,
next token literally `ship`, next token a bare PR number). Every OTHER `gh` subcommand
(`gh pr merge`, `gh run`, `gh pr checks`/`view`, `gh api`, and `gh ship` with no PR number
or a non-numeric argument) still delegates to a subagent, exactly as PR #212 left it.

Authorized directly by Alex (the CTO): earlier this session he clarified via Telegram
(tg#9977) that "the orchestrator CAN gh ship like agents can, but BY DEFAULT agents do
it" — the default stays delegation, this PR is the sanctioned exception, never
implemented until now. He then explicitly approved restoring the carve-out via a direct
"Да" (Yes) reply (tg#11055) to the exact question "Разрешить оркестратору самому делать
gh ship (carve-out) - да/нет".

Closes the loop on the gated-ship deadlock originally described in agent-tools#159: the
auto-mode classifier denies subagents from running `gh ship` in some configurations while
this hook independently blocked the orchestrator's own inline ship — leaving nobody able
to run the one sanctioned merge action. This PR does **not** touch the separate,
unrelated concern tracked in agent-tools#336 (the auto-mode classifier also blocking
invocation of the `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` escalation hatches themselves) — that issue stays
open and is out of scope here.

## UPDATE: `tg` carve-out (tg-carveout-159)

Extended per a second, separate, direct Alex authorization on the same branch/PR
(Telegram, direct reply): *"Но оркестратор ещё и tg:* должен уметь, т.е. все команды
tg-cli"* — the orchestrator should ALSO be able to use `tg:*`, i.e. ALL tg-cli commands
(send text, `--file`, `--photo`, `--format html`, `--tag`, `--reply-to`, `voice setup`,
everything — implemented broadly, no subcommand narrowing, unlike `gh ship`'s
single-shape carve-out).

`tg` was already sanctioned via `ORCH_ALLOW`'s plain `tg\b` regex since agent-tools#164
(this was NOT a case of the orchestrator being blocked from `tg` — the practical need was
already met). This adds `_is_tg_command`, a shlex-based predicate formalizing that
allowance as an explicit, unit-testable, basename-exact head-match, wired into
`_seg_is_allowed` the same way `_is_gh_ship_command` is (allow-side only — unlike `gh`,
`tg` was never an impl-signal head, so nothing needs exempting in `_seg_is_impl_signal`).

**The predicate REPLACES the old regex outright, not alongside it.** An earlier draft of
this PR kept both — review (Fable) correctly identified that as unreachable dead code:
since `ORCH_ALLOW` was checked FIRST in `_seg_is_allowed`'s OR-chain and matched a strict
superset of what the new predicate could ever grant, the addition shipped zero actual
behavior while adding a second, silently-disagreeing definition of "is this segment `tg`".

**Side effect: fixes agent-tools#370 for the `tg` case.** The old regex's `\b`
word-boundary also fires before a hyphen, so it incorrectly matched `tg-foo` — a
DIFFERENT command — as sanctioned orchestration. `_is_tg_command` is basename-exact, so
`tg-foo` is now correctly rejected end-to-end (same "chained >2 steps" doctrine as any
unclassified command: allowed alone or in a 2-segment chain, warn-then-blocks once
chained into 3+ segments). `review`'s matching `\b` quirk (`review-foo`) is **left
unchanged** — filed as the surviving half of agent-tools#370, out of scope here
(parameterizing into a shared exact-head helper and wiring `review` to it was considered
and deliberately deferred — a real improvement, but broader than what was asked).

**Deliberately NO path-qualification support**, despite `_is_gh_command` accepting any
path — resolved across two review rounds, not shipped as a guess:
- Round 1 (Fable): mirroring `_is_gh_command`'s blanket basename normalization over-grants
  in the UNSAFE direction for a GRANT-direction predicate (`_is_gh_command` is
  DENY-direction — over-matching there only routes more to a subagent, the safe failure
  mode; a match in `_is_tg_command` means "never even warn").
- Round 2 (Opus + Fable): the first fix (absolute-paths-only) was disproven empirically —
  `/tmp/tg` is just as easy to write as `./tg`, so it narrowed nothing real. A hardcoded
  bin-dir allowlist was checked against the authoring machine's actual `tg` install
  (`~/.files/bin/tg` — not on any short "standard" list) and rejected as unreliable.
- Given this gate's own stated threat model (discipline, not a security boundary) and
  that the practical need is fully met by subcommand breadth alone, path-qualification
  was dropped entirely.

## What changed

`agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py`:

- New `_is_gh_ship_command` predicate — deliberately shlex-based, not a head regex, since
  it needs argument-POSITION awareness (`gh`, then literally `ship`, then a bare
  ASCII-digit PR number) that a regex like the existing `ORCH_ALLOW` can't express.
- New shared `_gh_argv_after_env` helper (env-prefix skip + basename normalization),
  used by both `_is_gh_command` and the new `_is_gh_ship_command`, so that logic is
  written once instead of duplicated.
- `_seg_is_allowed` / `_seg_is_impl_signal` wired to recognize the narrow ship shape as
  sanctioned. The exception is composed as `_is_gh_command(segment) and not
  _is_gh_ship_command(segment)` — not an early return — so a future impl-signal check
  appended to that function can't be silently exempted by accident.
- Per-segment scope preserved throughout: a real mutation anywhere else on the line (a
  build/edit, a companion `git push`, a live substitution — `$()`/backtick/`<()`/`>()` —,
  a sibling `gh` mutation, a subshell group, any real chain operator including
  `||`/`|&`/a bare `&`/a newline) still warn-then-blocks. The carve-out never launders the
  rest of a line.
- `--skip-ci` on a `gh ship` is intentionally NOT specially vetted by this gate — it has
  its own separate, independently deny-by-default live-Telegram hatch inside
  `ci/ship/ship.sh` (`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_SKIP_CI`); duplicating that check here would
  be the wrong layer.
- **New:** `ORCH_ALLOW`'s `tg\b` regex alternative REMOVED; new `_is_tg_command` predicate
  added as the sole authority, wired into `_seg_is_allowed` (see UPDATE section above).
- **New:** `_is_all_inline_allowed`'s docstring clarifies it has no "at least one
  orchestration head" requirement — a per-segment universal check, not a membership
  check — since two independent review rounds initially misread the mechanism that way.

`agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/README.md` and the `.pre-bash.json` descriptor:
updated to document the restored `gh ship` carve-out and the `tg` carve-out, their exact
matching shapes, what does and does not qualify, the laundering guards, and the
explicitly-accepted design tradeoffs for both (cross-repo `--repo` scope, chained
multi-ship, the FIND_MUTATION/BUILD_EDIT-shaped-text gray zone, and the no-path-
qualification decision for `tg`).

## Tests

34 new/rewritten tests for `gh ship` + 40 new tests for the `tg` carve-out in
`tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py` (248 → 294 total tests in the file across the
whole diff). Coverage includes:

- The `gh ship` allow matrix: bare `gh ship <PR#>`, with `--screenshot`/`--repo`/
  `--skip-ci`/read-only plumbing, env-prefixed, path-qualified, `gtimeout`-wrapped,
  quoted-digit PR numbers, chained with a `tg` report.
- The `gh ship` still-delegated matrix: no PR number, a non-numeric argument, a flag
  before the number, `gh pr merge`, `gh run`, `gh pr checks`/`view`, `gh api`, `gh ship
  $PR` (a shell variable — the hook only sees literal pre-expansion text).
- The `tg` allow matrix: plain text, `--file`, `--photo`, `--format html`, `--tag`,
  `--reply-to`, `voice setup`, `help`, env-prefixed (single and multiple), `gtimeout`- and
  `env`-wrapped, chained with itself/`review`/`git worktree list` at any length.
- The `tg` rejection matrix: any path-qualified head (relative AND absolute — `./tg`,
  `/opt/homebrew/bin/tg`, `/tmp/tg`), both on the shlex branch and the unparseable
  fallback; `tg-foo` (basename-exact, closing agent-tools#370's tg half end-to-end,
  pinned at both 2- and 3-segment chain lengths).
- The laundering guards (shared pattern for both carve-outs): every real chain operator
  (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `|&`, a bare `&`, a newline), every live-substitution form
  (`$()`, backticks, `<()`, `>()`), a sibling `gh` mutation on the same line, and a
  `(...)` subshell group.
- A structural cross-check that `ci/ship/ship.sh`'s own `--skip-ci` deny-by-default hatch
  (the safety argument for not re-vetting it here) actually exists and is wired into the
  real call graph, not just present as a string.
- Explicit acceptance matrices tying each carve-out together in one test: orchestrator
  `gh ship <N>` / `tg <anything>` is allowed; orchestrator `gh pr merge` / raw `gh` / a
  code `Edit`/`Write` / other implementation-shaped `Bash` still warn-then-block; a
  dispatched subagent is unaffected either way (runs everything freely, repeat or not).

Full repo test suite: **3403 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed** — confirmed with multiple
clean runs (the 3486/4 count from the original `gh ship`-only revision reflects a
different authoring environment; this sandbox's own collected-test count differs
similarly even on the unmodified base commit, but **0 failures either way**, verified
directly). `ruff check`: 9 pre-existing findings (all in pre-existing code this PR
doesn't touch), confirmed unaffected — identical count and locations on the base commit.

## Review

Self-reviewed synchronously (`review diff -C .`, pinned to `claude:claude-opus-4-8` +
`claude:claude-fable-5` only — codex excluded per the confirmed recursion bug in
alex-mextner/review-cli#180). The original `gh ship` carve-out went through 7 iterations.
The `tg` carve-out addition went through 5 further rounds as the design was tightened
from an unreachable dead-code addition (round 1's first draft) through a real but
non-narrowing "absolute paths only" restriction (round 2's fix attempt), to dropping
path-qualification entirely and consolidating `_is_tg_command` as the sole, load-bearing
authority for the `tg` allowance (rounds 3–5), fixing agent-tools#370 for the `tg` case
as a byproduct. All substantive findings were either fixed or explicitly documented as
accepted, scoped design decisions consistent with this hook's stated threat model (a
cooperative orchestrator; `on_error: open`; discipline, not a security boundary).

## Not doing here

- Not merging/shipping this myself — reporting the PR back per the dispatch instructions.
- Not touching agent-tools#336 (the classifier-blocks-hatch-invocation issue) — separate,
  unrelated, and still open.
- Not re-litigating the general "orchestrator delegates almost all `gh`" policy from
  tg#7103 — this PR carves out exactly one shape, nothing broader.
- Not fixing `review`'s matching word-boundary bug (`review-foo`, agent-tools#370's
  surviving half) or building the shared parameterized head-match helper Fable's review
  suggested — both are real, deliberately deferred as broader than what was asked.

title: feat: integrate anti-slop TypeScript policy
body:
## What changed

- adds a stack-level `frontend/ts/anti-slop` skill with preferred repair patterns and the complete TypeScript escape-hatch baseline
- aligns `ts-strictness` with boundary parsing instead of propagating `unknown`/ad-hoc narrowing through application code
- replaces the example Lefthook grep gate with local Oxlint enforcement
- documents which existing checks anti-slop replaces and which layers remain (`tsc`, general lint/format)
- specifies the intended Rig `linters.bundles` consumer contract for vendored anti-slop source

## Policy composition

Anti-slop handles evidence-preservation/assertion patterns. Oxlint built-ins handle the remaining escape hatches:

- `typescript/no-non-null-assertion`
- `typescript/ban-ts-comment` with `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-nocheck` banned and `@ts-expect-error` allowed only with a description

This lets repositories retire the regex `as any | as unknown as | @ts-ignore` check once the Oxlint config is provisioned.

## Validation

Reviewed the branch diff against `main`. This change is policy/docs/example-hook only; the actual directory-bundle reconciler is tracked separately in `rig-cli` because current `linters.items` only provisions exact-content files.

title: feat: vendor lint rule subrepos
body:
## What changed

Adds two pinned Git subrepositories under `vendor/`:

- `vendor/anti-slop` → the reviewed `alex-mextner/anti-slop` fork, pinned to the merged revision containing the standardized rule guides/diagnostics and reviewed API-shape fixes.
- `vendor/ai-automation` → upstream `typeonce-dev/ai-automation`, pinned to an exact reference revision for provenance and rule-catalog research.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Subrepo presence does not enable rules. Rig remains the policy source of truth: it decides applicability, `all`, group selection, per-rule enable/disable, and severity from global config + repo `rig.yaml`.

## Provenance and licensing

`ai-automation` currently exposes no license metadata in its GitHub repository. Keeping an exact upstream gitlink preserves provenance without copying its implementation into agent-tools. We therefore treat it as a reference/catalog source unless licensing is clarified; independently implemented rules can be added to our own providers.

## Why

- preserve source history and provenance
- pin exact revisions rather than silently following upstream
- make source updates explicit pointer changes
- keep implementation sources separate from Rig policy

title: docs: define Rig TypeScript rule policy
body:
## What changed

Defines the final Rig/agent-tools TypeScript policy catalog, one focused guide per policy rule, and the comparison with anti-slop.

Rig is the broader policy layer. `anti-slop` contributes structural AST rules; compiler strictness, boundary parsing, domain modeling, semantic type-aware assertion analysis, suppression policy, rule applicability, and severity remain Rig-owned concerns.

The document includes a grouped rule table with links to rule guides, the `all` / group / enable / disable / severity control model, and the precedence of built-in defaults < global Rig config < repository `rig.yaml`.

The Venn-style diagram is stored as source (`.mmd`) beside the rendered SVG and the Markdown embeds the SVG. The recommended JS/TS toolchain is Oxc (Oxlint + Oxfmt), with type-aware unsafe/unnecessary assertion checks.

`unknown` remains valid at a genuine unvalidated boundary: decode/parse there, then pass named domain types inward.

title: feat: add Rig-owned Oxc TypeScript carriers
body:
## What changed

Adds canonical Oxc TypeScript carrier files used by Rig. The checked-in Oxc files are templates/carriers, not policy authority: Rig renders effective rule selection and severity from built-in defaults + global config + repository `rig.yaml`.

The Oxfmt carrier remains reusable configuration. The generated `oxlint.config.ts` in managed repositories must carry a Rig ownership header and is reconciled by `rig apply`; direct edits are diagnostic-only and must be moved back into Rig policy before commit.

Vendored anti-slop supplies rule implementations only. Rule enablement remains independent and Rig-owned.

title: docs: define rule-source profiles and ai-automation adoption

## What changed

- records anti-slop vs ai-automation provenance and licensing boundary
