title: chore(gitignore): move .worktrees/ from committed .gitignore to git/info/exclude
body:
## Summary
- `.worktrees/` was a manually-added, committed `.gitignore` entry -- but it's a per-machine
  scratch convention (parallel-agent worktrees), not something every clone should carry, matching
  rig-cli's own reasoning for the same convention (`riglib/config.py`'s `WORKTREES_DIR_NAME`
  comment: "belongs in the per-repo, never-committed `.git/info/exclude` ... specifically NOT in
  the committed `.gitignore`").
- Moved the ignore into `.git/info/exclude` via `rig worktree create`, which registers a
  rig-managed marker block for `/.worktrees/` there before creating a worktree. Ran it once on
  this machine while preparing the change, so the primary checkout's *shared* `.git/info/exclude`
  (common gitdir, applies to every linked worktree of this repo) already carries the entry.
- Added an AGENTS.md note ("Working in this repo") documenting `rig worktree create <name> --from
  origin/main` as the required way to create a worktree here, since that's what performs the
  one-time exclude bootstrap -- plus a "first time in a clone" recovery path for the window before
  that bootstrap has run.

## Review findings addressed (4 rounds, 3 recorded PASSED iterations, task `WT-GITIGNORE-EXCLUDE`)
`review diff` (codex + opus + zai:glm-5.2) repeatedly flagged one real, accepted trade-off and
several docs-accuracy bugs in my own fix text, both folded into the final AGENTS.md addition:

- **Accepted trade-off, not routed around**: a clone that never runs `rig worktree create` loses
  the committed-`.gitignore` safety net for `.worktrees/*` until it bootstraps
  `.git/info/exclude` once. Same trade-off already accepted in this file for the ship-delegator
  and opencode-bridge excludes -- so the fix is making the bootstrap step impossible to miss, not
  keeping the committed entry.
- Fixed: always pass `--from origin/main` (the command defaults to current HEAD otherwise,
  contradicting the "off the origin default branch" rule elsewhere in this doc).
- Fixed: `.git/info/exclude` is per-*clone*, not per-machine (an earlier draft said "per-machine").
- Fixed: the first-time recovery step needs a *new* worktree name -- `rig worktree create` checks
  `target.exists()` **before** the exclude reconcile, so reusing an existing name silently skips
  registration.
- Fixed: `git worktree remove` is not a safe stand-in for `rig worktree remove` -- raw git leaves
  the branch behind, breaking a later `rig worktree create <same-name>`.
- Fixed: the manual `.git/info/exclude` fallback now says to run it from the primary checkout (or
  resolve via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) -- inside a linked worktree `.git` is a file, so a
  literal `.git/info/exclude` path doesn't exist there.

**Not fixed here** (flagged as a legitimate but separate-scope follow-up):
`skills/by-type/monorepo/worktree-isolation/SKILL.md` still documents the older `../.worktrees/`
sibling-directory pattern for repos without rig-cli -- reconciling the two conventions in that
generic, catalog-wide skill is a bigger call than this docs/config-only PR's scope.

Verified no other tooling in this repo reads `.gitignore` for this entry (only a
path-classification literal in `ci/ship/ship.sh`, unrelated to contents).

      place.
- CI: this repo's `ci/tests` gate (`uv run --with pytest pytest tests/`) -- no test parses
  `.gitignore` content, so nothing to update there.

title: fix(ship): review-quorum task-code regex rejects descriptive codes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #384. `_review_quorum_extract_ticket()` in `ci/ship/ship.sh` only matched numeric-suffix
ticket tokens (`[A-Z][A-Z]+-[0-9]+`), so it silently failed to auto-derive purely descriptive
review-cli task codes review-cli itself tracks fine — e.g. `SME-ROADMAP-WORKTREE-NOTE`. This
blocked PR #163 in `sme-archiving-gc` from shipping through the normal `gh ship` flow despite
having 3 recorded PASSED review-quorum iterations under that exact code.

- Adds a third extraction arm: 2+ uppercase letters, then 2-or-more hyphen-joined 2+-letter
  uppercase segments (3+ segments total, no digits) — tried only after the `HYP-<n>` and generic
  numeric arms miss.
- Two-stage extraction (full boundary-delimited token, then an exact whole-token shape match) so
  a token with a digit buried inside it is rejected outright rather than truncate-matched to a
  bogus prefix.
- 3-segment floor rules out common two-word hyphenated English (`READ-ONLY`, `CI-CD`,
  `PRE-COMMIT`) that would otherwise false-positive on ordinary PR-body prose — this was an
  actual bug in an earlier version of this patch, caught by review round 1/2.
- `LC_ALL=C` added throughout for locale-safe `[A-Z]` matching.
- Two residual false-derivation edge cases remain and are explicitly documented in the function's
  docblock plus `AGENTS.md`/`ci/ship/README.md`: a rare three-word English phrase (`END-TO-END`)
  can still slip through, and a digit fused directly onto a candidate's own first segment
  (`2FA-SETUP-FLOW`) isn't caught (POSIX ERE has no lookbehind). Both fail CLOSED — review-cli has
  no record for the wrongly-derived code, so ship still refuses, just with a less friendly message
  than "could not derive a task code".
- Filed #385 to track a separate, related design question review round 3 surfaced (descriptive
  codes somewhat widening the review-quorum authority-borrowing surface) as deliberate future
  work — out of scope for this bugfix.

## Tests

- Derive a descriptive code from the PR body (the real PR #163 shape) and from a branch name.
- Reject: bare acronyms, two-word hyphenated prose, a digit-bearing token, lowercase.
- Per-candidate (not whole-text) filtering.
- Numeric-arm precedence over the descriptive arm.

Full repo suite: `3471 passed, 4 skipped`. `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean.

## Review

6 `review diff` iterations against task `AGENT-TOOLS-384`. Rounds 1-2 found real bugs (prose
false-positives, a token-truncation boundary bug) that got fixed before landing. The final 3
iterations passed clean across 3 distinct models (claude-opus-4-8, GLM-5.2 via opencode, GLM-5.2
via z.ai REST) — `codex` hit a usage-limit quota exhaustion each round (unrelated to this diff,
resets 2026-08-20) and was excluded from the passing pool. Quorum bar met:
`passed_iterations: 3`, `distinct_models_passed: 3`.

title: feat(agent-hooks): escape-hatch audit sink for RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* (G-8)
body:
## Summary

Closes gap **G-8** from the 2026-07-01 agent-ecosystem retrospective (hyperide `docs/specs/2026-07-01-agent-ecosystem-retrospective.md`, section 5.2.3 item 3): *"escape hatches have no audit sink"*. Ticket: HYP-858.

- Every `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` hatch goes through the shared `agenttools_hatch_escalation.request_hatch_approval`, so logging lives at that ONE choke point — covers all ~13 `agent-hooks/*` hatches plus ship's own two hatches, present and future, with zero per-hook-file changes.
- Any attempt where the hatch env var carries **any** value — blank, bare-flag, denied, or approved (`env_present=True`) — appends one JSON line to `overrides.log`. A denied/blank attempt is logged too: that's exactly the self-service-without-a-reason pressure an unaudited hatch would otherwise hide.
- Record shape: `{ts, session, hatch, env_var, command, reason, decision, detail, cwd}` (spec asked for `{ts, session, hatch, command, reason}`; the extra fields are additive).
- Default location: `<real-home>/.config/agent-tools/overrides.log` (`default_overrides_log_path()`), rooted at `resolve_home()` — the same non-agent-controllable trust anchor `tg_ctl_path` resolution already uses, so a hatch requester cannot launder their own audit trail by exporting a doctored `$HOME`.
- File permissions forced to `0600` on create AND re-tightened on append to a pre-existing looser file — the line can carry a free-text justification and a full shell command.
- Logging is best-effort, wrapped so it can never raise or block a hatch decision (mirrors `ci/ship/ship.sh`'s own `_review_quorum_audit_log` contract).

## Design choices (spec was silent on exact mechanics — noted here for review)

1. **`AGENT_TOOLS_OVERRIDES_LOG` env-var override tier**, mirroring `ship.sh`'s existing `SHIP_AUDIT_FILE` precedent. This tier IS environment-controllable by design — documented trade-off: the audit sink is a best-effort *secondary* record, the live `tg-ctl ask` round trip is what actually gates the bypass and cannot be redirected the same way.
2. **Session id resolution is best-effort.** No existing call site threads a real session/agent id into the hatch `context` dict today, so this checks `context["session_id"]` first, then a short list of plausible harness env vars (`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `RIG_SESSION_ID`, `TMUX_PANE`), then falls back to `pid:<getpid()>` so the field is never empty.
3. **Scope**: this PR implements the audit sink only. `rig status`'s "overrides this week" section and a weekly tg digest reading this file are tracked follow-up work — the retrospective calls out item 3 (this sink) as its own actionable, unblocked item.

## A leak this change would otherwise have introduced (found + fixed)

Several hook test suites (e.g. `tests/test_require_ticket_before_commit.py`) run the hook script as a genuine **subprocess** to prove no `tg-ctl` contact on a bare/blank hatch value. A subprocess gets a fresh interpreter that in-process `resolve_home` monkeypatches never reach — so without the env-var override tier plus `tests/conftest.py` exporting it for every test, those subprocess tests would have appended real audit lines into the **developer's actual** `~/.config/agent-tools/overrides.log` on every local `pytest tests/` run. Verified: reproduced the leak, fixed it, confirmed clean on a full-suite run before opening this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_agenttools_hatch_escalation.py` — 54 passed (18 new tests: approved/denied/blank/bare logging, session-id resolution order, append-not-overwrite, default path resolution + env-override precedence, write-failure best-effort, 0600 permissions on create + pre-existing file, internal-exception audit line)
- [x] `pytest tests/` (full suite) — 3586 passed, 6 skipped, no regressions
- [x] Confirmed no leak into the real `~/.config/agent-tools/overrides.log` across two full-suite runs
- [x] `ruff check` — clean
- [x] `review diff -C <repo> --task HYP-858 --pool 2` — `[ok]` from k3 and GLM-cc-last (codex hit its usage limit, no verdict); addressed all 4 actionable findings before this commit (test assertion strengthening, 0600 permission tests, docstring accuracy, exception-path coverage)

title: fix(ship): mark-shipped notify passes -C in a position task-cli rejects
body:
## Summary
- Fixes a live bug found on the very merge of PR #396 (the `task mark-shipped` post-merge
  notify hook): `-C "$ROOT"` was placed BEFORE the `mark-shipped` subcommand in the argv
  array. task-cli's argparse only accepts `-C`/`--cwd` as a per-subcommand flag, never a
  top-level one, so `task -C <dir> mark-shipped ...` fails with `invalid choice: '<dir>'`.
  Verified against the real installed `task` binary.
- The bug fired on its own merge: ship.sh logged a WARNING and continued (best-effort, never
  blocked the ship — by design), but ticket AGENTTOOLS-392 never actually got recorded via
  `task mark-shipped`.
- Fix: run `task` FROM the target directory via a scoped subshell `cd`, instead of passing
  `-C` as an argument at all — sidesteps the ordering question entirely (task-cli's own `-C`
  default is `.`) rather than just fixing its position, and is robust to wherever a future
  task-cli version puts `--cwd` in its own argv grammar. The subshell scope is narrow (only
  the `task` invocation) and never touches ship.sh's own working directory.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py -q` — 15/15 passed, including a
      new pwd-logging fake (verifies the `cd` actually happens) and a real-installed-`task`
      integration test that runs the exact constructed argv through real argparse to catch a
      future ordering/shape regression a logging-only fake could never catch.
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q -k "quorum or worktree"` — 37/37 passed
- [x] `bash -n ci/ship/ship.sh` — syntax OK
- [x] Multi-model review-cli pass (Fable, 3 rounds)

Refs #397.

title: feat(agent-hooks): pkill-guard — block pattern-kills of shared process names (G-5, #401)
body:
## Summary

- Closes #401 / retrospective gap **G-5** (2026-07-01 agent-ecosystem retrospective, section 5.2.3 item 2): pattern-based process kills (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill $(pgrep ...)`, `pgrep | xargs kill`) of shared/ambiguous tool names were mechanically unrestricted, despite two real incidents (a subagent's `pkill -f "review diff"` killed another session's in-flight code review on 2026-06-26; a narrow-grep-based kill nearly killed another session's e2e matrix run on 2026-06-27).
- New pre-bash agent-hook `agent-hooks/pkill-guard/pkill_guard.py`: argv-based (shlex, not substring), blocks a pattern-kill only when the pattern names a curated denylist entry AND carries no session-scoping signal (a path, a worktree/harness isolation token, a hex/uuid/long-digit run). Fails open on unlisted names. `kill <pid>` is always allowed.
- Deny-by-default via the existing `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_PKILL_GUARD` Telegram-hatch mechanism (same pattern as `background-subagent-gate`/`block-raw-pr-merge`), auto-recorded in `overrides.log` (G-8, already shipped in #390).
- Wired into the two cross-hook regression suites (`test_hatch_import_hardening.py`, `test_agenttools_hatch_escalation.py`) and the `agent-hooks/README.md` / `AGENTS.md` hook inventories.

## Review history (5 rounds, `review diff --task pkill-guard-401`)

This PR went through 5 rounds of multi-model review (Opus, Codex, Fable, GLM, k3 — 5 distinct models total). Every real finding was fixed; a handful of narrow, deliberately-crafted-input gaps are documented as known limitations rather than fixed (matches this hook's stated accidental-shape threat model).

**Round 1** (initial): missing executable bit (P0 — the hook would have fail-closed on every Bash command), a pattern-extraction bug that only checked the trailing positional (missed multi-name `killall`/a flag's own value hiding the real pattern), a dangling cross-repo README link.

**Round 2**: pipeline classification only checked the first grep-family stage (not every stage), a shell redirect's target got picked up as a candidate pattern, a bare 4-digit port falsely read as session-scoping, a bare global-interpreter path falsely read as session-scoping, a command-substitution parse failure silently fell through to "safe" instead of failing closed like the equivalent top-level text does.

**Round 3**: `xargs` misclassified on an unrecognized flag, `ionice`/`stdbuf` were completely missing from the wrapper value-flag table (their own flag's value was misread as the wrapped command), `pidof`-sourced kills were unrecognized, a stale hook-count in the root README.

**Round 4**: a stray apostrophe sitting inside a real shell comment on one line was mistaken for a genuinely unclosed quote, merging the comment forward into the next line and swallowing a real `pkill` command there inside what looked like one giant quoted argument; `xargs`'s wrapped-command check compared the immediate payload token against the literal string "kill", so a wrapper in front of it (`xargs env kill`, `xargs sudo kill`) always slipped through; a leading bare file-descriptor digit before a redirect left an orphan token hiding the real command.

**Round 5**: a redirect appearing BEFORE a wrapper or inline env assignment (`2>/dev/null sudo pkill -f node`) bypassed detection entirely, since the previous fix only handled a redirect appearing after the wrapper; a kill genuinely executing in a non-final pipeline stage (`pgrep -f node | xargs kill | tee log.txt`) was no longer detected after an earlier fix over-narrowed the check to only the pipeline's last stage; the comment-aware tokenizer ran a second, unnecessary parse pass even on ordinary lines with no `#` at all, a latency/DoS-ish concern on a hook that gates every Bash command.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_pkill_guard.py` — 89 tests: true positives (direct pkill/killall, `kill $(pgrep ...)`/backtick form, pgrep-pipe/narrow-grep/non-final-stage pipelines, the two real incident shapes), session-scoped allows, PID-only-kill allows, unlisted-name allows, wrapper peeling (all wrappers in the shared table, including through redirects and inline env in any order), shell chains (`&&`/`;`/newline), comment/quote-interaction regressions, fail-closed (unbalanced quotes, malformed event, wrapper-chain overflow), and the full Telegram-hatch matrix.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all touched files.
- [x] Full repo suite: `uv run --with "pytest>=8,<9" python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **3575 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed**.
- [x] Guard-B: `review task pkill-guard-401 --check` → 5 passed iterations across 5 distinct models.
- [x] Filed a separate out-of-scope follow-up, agent-tools#402, for a pre-existing `tests/test_global_review_gate.py` fixture-cleanup bug noticed while running the full suite twice (fails 17 unrelated tests on a repeat run with `.test-repos` left dirty) — reproduces with zero pkill-guard code involved, not fixed here.
- [x] Filed agent-tools#404 for a durable, accurate agent-hooks count in the root README (this PR only removed the stale number, pointing at `agent-hooks/README.md`'s table instead).

## Summary

~80% of ALL checks fail — a whole-infrastructure outage. The far more common shape is "one
specific check is a flaky, already-broken-on-base-branch test and everything else is green" —
that never looks like an outage, so the fallback never triggers, and until now the only way
through was a human escalation for something a quick check of the base branch's own recent CI
history already answers.

Concrete motivating case: hyperide PR #742 (HYP-706) was blocked solely by
`PreviewProxy /test-preview retry exhaustion`, independently confirmed to also fail on that
repo's own `main` HEAD across several separate CI runs — 1 of ~21 checks failing (4.8%), far
below the 80% threshold.

## What's new

- `--known-flake <check-name>` (repeatable, one per failing check): an explicit, auditable
  assertion — NOT a blind trust-me bypass. `ship` independently verifies each assertion against
  the last `SHIP_FLAKE_LOOKBACK_RUNS` (default 5) completed runs of the SAME workflow on the
  PR's ACTUAL base branch, requiring a job of the exact name to have also failed there.
- Every currently-failing check must be BOTH asserted AND confirmed, or the gate hard-refuses —
  no partial credit, positive-confirmation counting (not "innocent until proven guilty").
- On success it still runs the same local test/leftover/checklist/threads gate the CI-down path
  uses, and the merge itself still goes through the normal merge + branch-protection path.
- **Documented limitation, not silently papered over:** a required status check that is
  FAILING (not merely absent) can still block the final merge even after this gate confirms the
  claim and the local tests pass — tracked as a follow-up.
- Audit trail: `SHIP_AUDIT_FILE` gets `confirmed` (only after an actual merge) /
  `confirmed-local-gate-failed` / `refused`.

## Review history

Survived three `review diff` rounds (k3/GLM/Opus, Guard-B satisfied). Fixed along the way:
- A fail-open when the failing-check-name extraction came back empty (positive-confirmation
  counting fix).
- Fail-open on an unreadable base branch (now fail-closed).
- Missing foreign-repo-target (#166-class) guard.
- An audit `confirmed` line that was written before later gates could still refuse the ship
  (moved to fire only after the merge actually succeeds).
- Refusal/confirmation messages that named `$DEFAULT_BRANCH` instead of the PR's actual base
  branch.
- A short-circuit so a certain-refusal doesn't keep spending `gh` API calls on remaining checks.

**Deferred, tracked separately** (not silently dropped): a GraphQL-based N+1 rewrite for
multiple simultaneous failing checks (bash 3.2 compatibility makes this a real scope), the
required-check dead-end UX, StatusContext-can-never-confirm documentation, and a lookback-window
test.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n ci/ship/ship.sh` — syntax clean
- [x] `shellcheck -x ci/ship/ship.sh` — no new findings in the changed regions
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` — 214/214 passed (208 pre-existing + 6 new)
- [x] 3 review-cli rounds (k3, GLM, Opus) — Guard-B quorum satisfied

title: feat(ship): review-quorum gate uses role-based coverage as its primary check
body:
## Summary

`ship.sh`'s self-merge safety gate (the check that decides whether an autonomous agent is
allowed to merge its own pull request without a human clicking approve) used to count how many
different AI **models** reviewed the code, and require at least 3 different ones before letting a
merge through. It never looked at what **role** each review played (correctness, security,
architecture, and so on).

Meanwhile `review-cli` — the tool that actually runs those reviews — was upgraded (in three
already-merged pull requests, #246/#249/#252) to track review coverage by **role** instead of by
model, because a model-count is a weak signal (the same one model can review a change three times
and count as "3 models" if you swap which backend answers) while role coverage is a stronger one
(it proves the change was actually looked at from a correctness angle, a security angle, and an
architecture angle, not just three generic passes). `ship.sh` never caught up to that upgrade — it
kept asking `review-cli` for a model count and ignored the role information entirely.

This PR makes `ship.sh` use role-based coverage as its default safety check, matching what
`review-cli` itself already considers the standard. An operator who wants the OLD model-count
behavior back can still ask for it explicitly (see the "Important trade-off" note below).

## What changed, in plain terms

- **The default check is now: "was this change reviewed from at least 3 different angles
  (roles)?"** instead of "did at least 3 different AI models look at it?". This is now always
  checked, with a floor of 3 that can only be raised, never lowered (same protection the old
  model-count check already had).
- **The old model-count check still exists, but only if you explicitly ask for it** via
  `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_MODELS`. If you set that, both checks apply together (role coverage AND
  a minimum number of distinct models).
- **Compatibility handling**: if the installed `review-cli` is old enough that it doesn't
  understand role checking yet, `ship.sh` now says so plainly ("the installed review-cli does not
  support role checking, upgrade it") instead of a confusing generic "could not check review
  history" error.
- **The audit log** (the file that records every merge decision this gate ever made) now also
  records the role information, not just the model count, so a later investigation can see
  exactly what was checked.

## Important trade-off — needs your read

The old default (3 distinct models) meant no single reviewer, human or AI, could clear the bar by
itself. The new default (3 distinct roles) can be satisfied by **one single model** reviewing the
same change three times under three different role labels (correctness, then security, then
architecture). This is exactly what `review-cli`'s own new default already does — this PR just
makes `ship.sh` match it — but it does mean every repo that has never explicitly set
`SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_MODELS` loses the "multiple independent reviewers" guarantee silently,
with no warning printed when a merge goes through this way.

If any repo's self-merge safety depends on genuinely independent reviewers (not just independent
role labels), that repo should explicitly set `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_MODELS=3` to keep the old
guarantee. This is documented in the updated `ci/ship/README.md` migration section, but it's worth
a deliberate decision rather than an unnoticed side effect.

## Follow-up tickets filed (not fixed in this PR — explicitly out of scope)

- **#414** — the one-time Telegram approval path (when a human overrides a failed check) still
  doesn't record the new role information in its own log line; it's written by a different, shared
  piece of code this PR didn't touch.
- **#415** — two smaller robustness improvements: telling apart "the review tool doesn't support
  this yet" from "the review tool crashed" more precisely, and simplifying how the audit-log
  function takes its parameters (it's grown a lot of them over successive changes).
- **#413** — an unrelated, pre-existing bug in a different test file (`test_global_review_gate.py`)
  that leaves scratch directories behind, causing false failures if the full test suite is run
  twice in the same checkout without cleaning up. Found by accident while testing this change;
  not touched here since it's a separate feature area.

## Testing

- Added 15 new test cases and updated 3 existing ones in `tests/test_ship.py`, covering: the
  default role-based pass with no model floor set, the explicit-model-floor case (both pass and
  refuse), the compatibility fallback for older `review-cli` builds, and several
  defense-in-depth cases proving the gate doesn't trust data it never actually asked for.
- Verified the core logic empirically against the real, installed `review-cli` (not just its
  source code) — confirmed a real query with no `--min-models` flag genuinely returns success on
  1 model / 3 roles, matching what `ship.sh` now expects.
- Full local test suite: 3719 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed.

title: fix(tests): stop stale .test-repos dirs from crashing a second local run
body:
## What

`tests/test_global_review_gate.py` builds throwaway git repos under a fixed,
repo-relative path (`.test-repos/<test-name>/repo`) instead of a fresh temp directory,
and nothing ever removed that directory. Running the test file a second time in the
same checkout crashed with `FileExistsError` on `repo.mkdir()`, because the directory
from the first run was still there.

Fixes #413.

## Why it can't just use pytest's `tmp_path`

The obvious fix looks like "just use `tmp_path`", but this file exists specifically to
test `review-gate`'s own temp-dir exemption: the gate skips enforcement for any repo
living inside an OS temp directory (`$TMPDIR`, `/tmp`, `/var/folders`, etc.), and
pytest's `tmp_path` fixture is itself created inside one of those (e.g.
`/private/var/folders/...` on macOS). Putting the test repos there would make every
"the gate blocks this" assertion silently pass for the wrong reason — the repo would
be exempt, not correctly evaluated. That's why the file already keeps these scratch
repos under `.test-repos/` at the repo root, deliberately outside the exemption.

## The fix

`_scratch_base()` now removes its own per-test directory before (re)creating it:

```python
def _scratch_base(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    base = _SCRATCH_ROOT / tmp_path.name
    if base.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(base)
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return base
```

Since pytest assigns the same directory name to the same test on every run
(`tmp_path.name` is deterministic per test id, not random), this makes every run start
from a clean directory regardless of what an earlier run left behind — the exact
crash from #413 can no longer happen.

This directly matches one of the two acceptable fixes named in the issue itself: "the
fixture ... removes its own `.test-repos/<name>` directory before creating it."

An earlier version of this fix used a single `session`-scoped `autouse` fixture that
wiped the whole `.test-repos/` root once per test session. Multi-model review (`review
diff`) caught a real problem with that: under `pytest-xdist`, a session-scoped fixture
runs once per worker, so one worker's cleanup would delete another worker's live
scratch repo mid-run — turning a deterministic bug into a nondeterministic one. Doing
the cleanup per-test, inside `_scratch_base` itself, avoids that.

Also added a small regression test, `test_scratch_base_clears_stale_directory_from_a_prior_run`,
that seeds a leftover directory and asserts `_scratch_base` hands back a clean one — so
a future change that reintroduces the bug fails a test directly, not just "the suite
happens to crash on a second run."

## Verification

Reproduced first, on the unmodified code:

```
$ uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_global_review_gate.py -q   # 1st run
20 passed in 10.13s

$ uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_global_review_gate.py -q   # 2nd run, same checkout
FAILED tests/test_global_review_gate.py::test_review_skip_env_does_not_bypass_global_review_gate
... (17 total)
FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: '.../.test-repos/test_review_gate_still_blocks_0/repo'
17 failed, 3 passed in 0.79s
```

After the fix, three consecutive runs of the file in the same checkout (no cleanup in
between) all pass — 21 tests (the original 20 plus the new regression test):

```
=== RUN 1 === 21 passed in 9.11s
=== RUN 2 === 21 passed in 3.62s
=== RUN 3 === 21 passed in 3.81s
```

Also ran the full repo test suite twice (`uv run --with "pytest>=8,<9" --with pyyaml
--with jsonschema pytest tests -q`, the same command CI runs) to confirm nothing else
regressed: **3706 passed, 4 skipped** both times.

## Not shipping

Opening this PR for review, not merging it.

title: feat(agent-hooks): block-rg-pre — argv-precise hook to block ripgrep --pre
body:
## Summary

Closes agent-tools#419.

Adds a new `pre-bash` agent-hook, `block-rg-pre`, that blocks `rg --pre <COMMAND>` — ripgrep's flag that runs `COMMAND` as an arbitrary preprocessor on every matched file, turning the read-only search tool every agent is pre-allowed to run into an unrestricted local code-execution vector. Named directly in rig-cli's `riglib/permissions.py` as the still-missing argv-precise deep layer behind the existing coarse per-harness glob deny rules, since a glob can't honor `--` end-of-options or tell `--pre` used as a flag apart from `--pre` sitting in another flag's value (`rg -e --pre .`).

## What's included

- `agent-hooks/block-rg-pre/block_rg_pre.py` — argv-based (shlex) detection, wrapper-peeling (sudo/env/timeout/taskset/chrt/setpriv/runuser/flock/xargs) ported from `block-no-verify`'s audited machinery. Deny-by-default via the shared `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RG_PRE` Telegram-hatch mechanism.
- 101 unit tests in `tests/test_block_rg_pre.py`.
- Registered in `agent-hooks/README.md`'s and `AGENTS.md`'s pre-bash hook tables, and in the two cross-hook regression suites that enumerate every hatch-using hook.

## Review disposition (three rounds of `review diff` quorum — opus, codex, GLM/GLM-cc)

Fixed:
- Redirect-stripping bypass — a quoted `>`/`<` token is now protected from being misread as a real shell redirect two ways: when it's a known rg value-flag's literal value, and when the token FOLLOWING it looks like a flag itself (`rg '>' --pre x .`, a bare positional). Found across two rounds; the narrower value-flag-only fix from round 1 was insufficient, and round 3 correctly rejected documenting the bare-positional case as an accepted limitation.
- `xargs`-wrapped `rg --pre` (`pgrep ... | xargs rg --pre ...`).
- Unresolved command-substitution (`$(...)`, backticks) in rg's own argv now fails closed.
- `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` — a value set inline, via `env`, or exported by an EARLIER segment of the same command string now fails closed. Not claimed fixed: a value from a genuinely separate, earlier shell command, or already ambient in the environment — this hook doesn't read `os.environ` for this check at all, so it makes no claim either way there (an earlier docstring revision overclaimed blindness on this point; reworded).
- Empty `--pre ''` / `--pre=` (ripgrep's own no-op for disabling preprocessing) no longer flagged as dangerous.
- A 17th-plus leading shell-noise token used to silently truncate instead of failing closed.

Filed as follow-ups, not fixed here:
- **agent-tools#421** — `eval rg --pre ...` and `find -exec rg --pre ...` bypass detection (eval is deliberately excluded from `_WRAPPERS` alone, since that table is SYNC'd verbatim with `block-no-verify`; adding it to one side only would break the invariant — needs a coordinated change to both hooks plus an automated check that the tables actually stay in sync, which nothing currently enforces).
- ANSI-C quoting (`$'...'`) and shell-VARIABLE expansion (`"$VAR"`/`${VAR}`, distinct from command substitution, which IS caught) — documented, same class of limitation `pkill-guard`'s own docstring already accepts for `TARGET=node pkill -f "$TARGET"`.

## A note on this diff's provenance

Part of this diff (four specific fixes: the leading-shell-noise cap, the command-substitution check, the inline `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` check, and the empty-`--pre` no-op) was independently authored by a second, concurrently-dispatched agent working in this same worktree on the same ticket, discovered and corrected mid-session (see the final commit message for the full account — an earlier commit on this branch mischaracterized that work as this session's own).

## Guard-B status — NOT self-shipped

`review task agent-tools#419 --check` reports **1/3 passed iterations** (4 distinct models seen across three review rounds, each of which found real P1s) — below the 3-passed threshold. Combined with part of this diff coming from a different agent's session, this PR needs real human review before merge per the standing rule (a PR the shipping agent didn't fully author needs real human review, no workaround). Not running `gh ship`.

- [x] `ruff check` clean on all touched files
- [x] Full repo test suite: 3800 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed
- [x] Manual smoke tests for every block/allow case in the hook's own README

title: docs(ship): make the --repo cross-repo path discoverable
body:
## Summary

An agent trying `gh ship <PR#>` for a PR in a **different** repo repeatedly tried `cd <repo> && gh ship <N>` (chaining — disallowed by the `orchestrator-stays-thin` gate) and a bare `gh ship <N>` (silently resolved against the wrong repo via cwd). `--repo <owner/repo>` was already the correct, supported answer, but it was buried/missing in three places an agent would actually look:

- **`ci/ship/ship.sh`** — `-h`/`--help` used to fall into `Unknown flag: --help`; it now prints usage and exits 0. The usage text (shown on `--help`, on an unknown flag, and on a missing PR number) now has a one-line cross-repo example: `gh ship <PR-number> --repo <owner/repo>`, plus "never chain it".
- **`ci/ship/README.md`** — `--repo` was completely absent from the `Flags` section and `Quick start`; added a bullet and an example line.
- **`agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/orchestrator_stays_thin.py`** — the gate's own denial `MESSAGE` said an unchained `gh ship <PR#>` is the one sanctioned exception but never mentioned `--repo`, so an agent reading only that message had no way to know cross-repo shipping without a subagent dispatch was even possible. Added a clause naming `--repo <owner/repo>` as part of that same sanctioned, unchained command.

No gate logic was touched anywhere — usage/help/documentation text only.

title: fix(ship): Guard-B quorum gate defaults to role coverage, not model count
body:
## Summary

Alex's stated policy (repeated ~60 times per him): review-cli accounts for review
quorum **by board role** now (architect/correctness/security/...), not by raw
model-name count — specifically so one exhausted/rate-limited model can never wedge
the self-merge quorum gate on its own. review-cli itself was fixed for this in
review-cli#246 (shipped 2026-08-21): when neither `--min-models` nor `--min-roles`
is passed to `review task <CODE> --check`, the gate now defaults to role-based
counting.

But `ci/ship/ship.sh`'s own Guard-B preflight (the thing that actually invokes
`review task ... --check` before every self-merge) was **always** passing
`--min-models` explicitly. Per review-cli's own documented behavior, passing
`--min-models` explicitly reproduces the *old*, pre-#221 model-name-counting
behavior regardless of review-cli's new default — so `gh ship` never actually
got the resilience review-cli was built to provide. A single exhausted model
could still wedge every ship.

## Fix

- `ship.sh` now always passes `--min-roles` (the default gate, same fail-closed
  floor-3 clamp as before).
- `--min-models` becomes opt-in via `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_MODELS`: when an
  operator explicitly sets it, it's AND'd on top of the role floor (matches
  review-cli#246's own "an explicit floor is never silently outvoted" semantics).
- Authorization/refusal messages now report role coverage as the primary metric.
- Audit log (`~/.config/agent-tools/ship-audit.jsonl`) gets a new optional `roles`
  field; the existing `models` field keeps its original meaning (real distinct
  model-name count) for backward compatibility with existing consumers.
- Updated the doc header + README to describe the new default.

## Tests

- Updated the fake `review` CLI test double (`tests/test_ship.py`) to parse
  `--min-roles` and emit `distinct_roles_passed`/`roles`, matching review-cli's
  real JSON shape.
- Added 2 regression tests:
  - `test_review_quorum_role_mode_authorizes_despite_model_shortage` — a
    3-iteration/3-role/1-model record (the exact shape a single-exhausted-model
    incident produces) authorizes by default.
  - `test_review_quorum_explicit_min_models_still_enforced_and_anded` — the same
    record refuses once `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM_MIN_MODELS=3` is explicitly set.
- Full suite: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py` — 216 passed.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -k quorum` — 28 passed
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py` (full suite) — 216 passed
- [x] `shellcheck -S warning ci/ship/ship.sh` — no new warnings (2 pre-existing,
      unrelated, far from the touched region)

title: feat(agent-hooks): skills-marker-writer — wire the skills-read-gate marker contract
body:
## Summary

The `skills-read-gate` hook is supposed to block/warn when an agent does real work (a
commit, a build/test run) without first having invoked the mandatory skills
(`delegate-work-to-subagents`, `visual-proof-cycle`). It decides "invoked recently" by
checking mtime freshness on a marker file:

```
~/.cache/agent-tools/skills-invoked/<skill-name>
```

Nothing ever wrote that marker. The gate's own README documented the exact wrapper
contract needed ("wire the wrapper to touch it on every Skill-tool invocation") but no
code implemented it — verified via a repo-wide grep before starting this change: zero
writers of `skills-invoked/` existed anywhere in agent-tools. So the freshness check
always saw a missing marker, and the gate could never leave its WARN-forever tier — this
is exactly the "unsatisfiable gate" class the 2026-07-01 agent-ecosystem retrospective
catalogs as G-3 (`docs/specs/2026-07-01-agent-ecosystem-retrospective.md` in
`hyperide/hyper-saas`), and finding B's point that an unsatisfiable gate "actively
teaches agents (and humans) to ignore gate output."

This PR is the wrapper:

- **New `pre-skill` hook, `skills-marker-writer`.** Fires on every `Skill`-tool
  `PreToolUse` event and touches the freshness marker for the invoked skill. Never
  blocks — every code path emits `allow`; a marker-write failure is logged and ignored.
- **`lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`** maps `(PreToolUse, tool_name=Skill)` to the new
  `pre-skill` point, mirroring how `pre-agent` was added for `Agent|Task`.
- **Untrusted-input handling.** `args.skill` is model-controlled. A legitimate
  directory-scoped skill name contains a `/` (e.g. `apps/web:deploy`) and is allowed to
  nest under the marker dir; an absolute path, a `..` segment, NUL, or an oversized value
  is rejected. A second, independent guard checks the *resolved* write target stays
  inside the marker dir (covers a symlink planted inside it) — this is separately tested
  (a plain sanitization-based test suite doesn't exercise it; added a symlink-based test
  that does).
- **Docs** (`agent-hooks/README.md`, `agent-hooks/skills-read-gate/README.md`,
  `lib/cc_hook_bridge/README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, root `README.md`) updated to describe the
  wrapper as wired, and to note the two-repo split this needs to actually fire in Claude
  Code (see "Companion PR" below). Also fixed adjacent staleness in `AGENTS.md` claiming
  `pre-agent` was "not yet live in CC" — it already is, on a currently-unrelated timeline;
  left un-updated it would have directly contradicted this PR's own new `pre-skill` note
  sitting right next to it.

## Companion PR (required for this to actually fire)

**[alex-mextner/rig-cli#288](https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/pull/288)** registers a `Skill` `PreToolUse` matcher in
`hook_bridge_entries()` — without it, `rig`-generated `settings.json` never invokes the
bridge for a `Skill` call, and this hook stays inert (the same "designed but dead"
failure mode the pre-agent point hit before its rig-cli matcher landed). Landing either
PR alone is harmless: an unmapped `tool_name` is a documented no-op in `dispatch.py`'s
`point_for_event`, so the feature is simply inert (not broken) until both land and
`rig apply` runs.

## Review

`review diff --staged --task alex-mextner/agent-tools#425` — two passes, addressed every
actionable finding from both:

- Pass 1 (codex + GLM): fixed `lib/cc_hook_bridge/README.md` staleness (P2), lowered
  `timeout_ms` from 5000 to 800 (a blocking PreToolUse hook doing one filesystem write
  doesn't need a 5s budget), dropped a redundant `os.utime` call after
  `Path.touch(exist_ok=True)` (which already bumps mtime on an existing file, CPython
  3.4+), removed a duplicate segment-split.
- Pass 2 (Opus + codex + GLM): fixed a real correctness bug (valid-but-non-object JSON
  on stdin — `[]`, `5`, `"x"`, `true`, `null` — crashed past the `JSONDecodeError` catch
  with no protocol JSON on stdout, contradicting the "always allow" contract); added the
  symlink-based containment-guard test noted above; added a non-string-`skill` test;
  fixed the `AGENTS.md`/root-`README.md` staleness noted above; documented the accepted
  tradeoff that this fires on the invocation ATTEMPT (PreToolUse), not on confirmed
  success — a typo'd/nonexistent skill name writes a marker under the WRONG name, so it
  cannot falsely satisfy the gate's freshness check for the mandatory skill's own name;
  the only residual case (correct name invoked, underlying skill itself fails to load)
  is accepted since this mechanism is advisory (WARN-first, fail-open), not a security
  boundary.

- Pass 3 (codex): the one actionable finding (a P2 asking for a real end-to-end
  subprocess test through the bridge, not just direct hook calls) was addressed —
  added `test_pre_skill_writes_the_skills_read_gate_marker_clean_room` to
  `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py`, mirroring the existing `pre-agent` clean-room tests:
  drives the real `cc_hook_bridge` subprocess with a real installed descriptor and
  asserts the marker actually lands on disk.

k3 failed all three passes on a billing/quota error (known, pre-existing — not this
PR). Guard-B quorum satisfied: `review task alex-mextner/agent-tools#425 --check` →
4 passed iterations across 4 distinct models (Opus, Codex, GLM, and a second Codex
pass) and 3 distinct roles (consistency, correctness, performance).

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_skills_marker_writer.py -v` — 12/12 passed
- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py -q` — full file passed
- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/ -q` — full suite, 3593 passed, 23 skipped, clean
      (an earlier run showed 17 failures in `test_global_review_gate.py`; confirmed to be the
      pre-existing, already-tracked `.test-repos/` stale-scratch-dir flake — agent-tools#413 —
      by removing the directory and re-running clean end to end)
- [x] `ruff check` on all touched Python files — clean

Full suite re-run after the session-scoping update below: 3631 passed, 23 skipped, clean.

## Update: session-scoping the marker (post-merge-readiness review findings)

Two P2 findings from the `chatgpt-codex-connector` automated review bot on the diff
above, both on `skills_marker_writer.py`:

1. **Session-scoping gap.** The freshness marker was one mtime file per skill, shared by
   every concurrent Claude Code session for this user — session A invoking a mandatory
   skill silently satisfied session B's gate too, even though B never invoked it.
2. **Name-collision hazard** between a plain skill name and a directory-scoped skill name
   sharing a path prefix (e.g. `apps` vs `apps/web:deploy`).

Both threads were replied to and resolved on GitHub. (2) is deferred to
**[alex-mextner/agent-tools#427](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/427)**
— the nested-path encoding it's about is shared with `skills-read-gate`'s own
(unmodified-by-this-PR) reader, so a collision-free fix needs to change both hooks'
path shape identically; it's a marker-CONTRACT change, not a bug local to this PR's
diff, and needs a specific, rare precondition to trigger.

(1) is fixed here, across three files:

- **`lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`**: `session_id` now gets the same T2 precedence
  `agent_id` already has (CC's top-level value is authoritative; a value riding in via
  `tool_input` is dropped). The previous rule only added `session_id` to `args` when not
  already present — harmless for the `stop` point (no `tool_input`, so `args` starts
  empty) but not for `pre-skill`/`pre-bash`, where a forged `tool_input.session_id`
  could have won over CC's real one.
- **`skills_marker_writer.py`**: the marker now nests under `args.session_id` (a single
  flat path segment, never split on `/`), falling back to the pre-existing global path
  when no valid session id is present.
- **`skills_read_gate.py`**: `_missing_skills` does the matching session-scoped lookup,
  as an OR against the global path (not session-only) — deliberately, since the global
  path is still the only marker any harness without a session-aware producer can write
  (Codex/opencode have no `pre-skill` mapping yet; there's also a documented manual
  `touch` recipe), and losing that compatibility the moment ANY session id rides along
  on the event would be a real regression. The WARN/BLOCK escalation tier is also
  session-scoped, with no such fallback (nothing has ever relied on shared tier state).

**Deliberately deferred, tracked as
[alex-mextner/agent-tools#429](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/429):**
garbage collection for the per-session marker directories this scoping now mints (one
per Claude Code session, currently never removed). An in-hook prune was prototyped
directly in this PR and reverted after review surfaced a cascading set of interacting
edge cases (a too-low retention self-destructing the write it just made; a per-pass time
budget without a per-child bound letting one oversized session block GC for every
sibling forever; the retention floor needing to stay above `skills-read-gate`'s own
freshness window) faster than they could be closed cleanly inside this PR's scope. The
ticket captures the accumulated findings for a focused follow-up.

**Accepted, not further changed:** later review rounds repeatedly flagged that the
global-marker OR-fallback in `_missing_skills` lets a fresh global marker satisfy a
session that never wrote it. This is intentional (see above) and pinned by a dedicated
regression test (`test_global_fallback_is_intentional_even_alongside_a_different_sessions_marker`)
rather than left as an implicit assumption; an independent Claude review pass confirmed
it twice as a deliberate, test-pinned tradeoff, not a bug — it requires a deliberate
global write, unlike the automatic per-invocation leak this change closes.

New tests: session-scoped write/read isolation (two sessions never see each other's
markers), the intentional global-fallback case, tier-escalation session-scoping (session
B gets its own WARN in a cwd where session A already WARNed, not an inherited BLOCK), T2
precedence for `session_id` in the bridge (including a subprocess clean-room test that a
forged `tool_input.session_id` is ignored), and a cross-hook parametrized test that the
writer's and reader's duplicated `_sanitize_session_id` agree on every input.

title: fix(agent-hooks): route worktree-guard marker satisfaction through zero-touch tool commands (HYP-1358)
body:
## Summary

Yesterday's investigation found that Claude Code's own built-in worktree-isolation Bash guard refuses commands shaped with `$()`/`${...}`/bare `$VAR`/pipes/loops — regardless of whether they touch git — before checking what the command does. This breaks the honest `touch <marker>` recipe both `visual-proof-gate` and `require-review-before-commit` used to recommend for satisfying their commit gates.

This PR does two things:

1. **Documents the CLI guard's shape** (unchanged from the original scope) so an agent that hits the refusal understands it's an upstream bug (anthropics/claude-code#88776), not a bug in either hook.
2. **Reframes both hooks around the mechanism that makes the trap structurally unreachable**, instead of just teaching a careful-quoting workaround:
   - `require-review-before-commit`: PRIMARY recipe is now `git add -- 'file' && review diff --staged --task 'CODE'`. review-cli's own `_touch_review_marker()` (`reviewlib/install.py`) writes `REVIEW_MARKER` itself, in Python, on a passing **staged** review — there is no `touch` command in this path at all, so there's nothing for the CLI guard to refuse.
   - `visual-proof-gate`: PRIMARY recipe is now `dev shot 'URL' --out shot.png`. dev-cli's `write_attestation()` (`dev_cli/visual_proof.py`) writes the proof record itself, in Python, the same way.
   - Manual `touch` is now an explicitly-labeled **FALLBACK** for when no reviewer/URL is available — the quoting guidance from the original scope is preserved there.

## Review iteration (5 rounds, Opus + codex)

Each round caught a real defect the previous round introduced or missed:
1. `--task` is required by the current review-cli and was missing from the initial primary recipe (it exits 2, no review runs, no marker touched).
2. `<TICKET-CODE>`-style angle-bracket placeholders are bash/zsh input-redirection syntax, not a fill-in-the-blank convention — verified live (`bash -c 'git add <the files you changed>'` is a syntax error).
3. The block message still said `git add -A`, contradicting the new stage-only-what-you-changed guidance.
4. Unquoted path/task-code/URL placeholders permit shell injection via a crafted filename, task id, or URL containing metacharacters — verified live with a file literally named `fix;id.py`.
5. A single-quoted template isn't a full escape against a literal `'` in an untrusted value, and `git add` doesn't clear a dirty index — both now called out explicitly, with a caution against splicing untrusted text into the command at all.

## Cross-repo dependency (documented, not blocking)

Both `_touch_review_marker()` and `dev shot`'s `proof_dir()` had a latent `VAR=""` (explicitly-empty, not unset) normalization bug matching the one fixed here in the consumer hooks. Fixed in sibling PRs, safe to land independently or after this one:
- review-cli: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/274
- dev-cli: https://github.com/alex-mextner/dev-cli/pull/8

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/` — 3662 passed, 23 skipped (full suite, unrelated skips).
- [x] Live-reproduced the original trap: `git add -A && review diff --staged` (no `--task`) exits 2, touches no marker; `review diff --staged --task CODE` succeeds and review-cli itself touches the marker — verified via `ls -la ~/.cache/agent-tools/last-review` before/after, and a real `git commit` through the actual hook succeeded with zero manual `touch`.
- [x] Live-verified the `VAR=""` producer/consumer agreement for both `REVIEW_MARKER` and `VISUAL_PROOF_DIR` (same resolved path on both sides).
- [x] Live-verified the injection claims: unquoted `git add fix;id.py` splits into two shell commands; unquoted `dev shot http://host/?a=1&b=2` backgrounds part of the command.

title: visual-proof-gate: verify a binding, not just a fresh mtime
body:
Closes #434 · companion to alex-mextner/dev-cli#5

## The problem

The gate accepted **any file with a recent mtime** in `~/.cache/agent-tools/visual-proof/`. A bare `touch` satisfied it, so the marker proved nothing:

- an agent that never opened a browser could pass;
- an agent that captured a **blank page** could pass just as easily.

Both happened. One capture attested on in good faith was **52% featureless rows with a single 2,773px blank band** (42% of the page) — reveal-on-scroll sections photographed while still at `opacity: 0`. The fidelity numbers derived from it were measured largely against blank page.

## What changed

The gate now prefers a **bound attestation** written by `dev shot`, which captures and measures the image itself before writing anything. Verification:

| check | prevents |
|---|---|
| `staged_sha256` vs recomputed `git diff --cached` | reuse across changes; surviving further staging |
| `repo` vs the committing repo | a record transferring to another repo with an identical staged patch |
| re-hash of `capture_path` | outliving or being swapped away from the image it describes |
| `worktree_dirty` (under `REQUIRE_BINDING`) | pixels from the working tree while the binding is to the index |
| freshness window | stale records |

## Backwards compatible

The legacy fresh-mtime marker still satisfies the gate, so repos that haven't adopted `dev shot` are unaffected. `VISUAL_PROOF_REQUIRE_BINDING=1` refuses it and demands a bound attestation.

## Fail-soft preserved

`on_error: open` is a documented invariant, so two things were deliberate:

- **Candidates are scanned before the staged diff is hashed.** A legacy-only repo pays no second `git diff --cached` per commit — two sequential calls could approach the bridge timeout and get killed instead of failing open.
- **The capture read is bounded and refuses symlinks/non-regular files.** `capture_path` comes from a record the gate didn't write; a FIFO would block past that timeout, and `on_error: open` would then *allow* the commit.

## Testing

102 tests (89 pre-existing, all still green). The load-bearing addition is a **positive** case with the legacy fallback disabled — without it, replacing `_bound_proof_matches` with `return False` passes the entire suite, because the negatives block via `require_binding` and the one allow case is satisfied by the legacy fallback.

Verified adversarially: stubbing the matcher to `return False` fails exactly that test and nothing else.

## Honest scope

This is process discipline, **not** a security boundary — anyone who can hash `git diff --cached` can mint a record. It prevents the *good-faith* failure that actually occurs, not forgery.

One pre-existing hole is unchanged and worth knowing: `git commit -a/-am` stages **after** this pre-bash hook runs, so tracked-but-unstaged UI can ride in unproven. That predates this change and affects the staged-file listing too; closing it needs a post-staging hook.

title: feat(agent-hooks): block a subagent from calling Monitor (#543)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a retrospective finding from HYP-1350 (hyperide/hyper-saas PR #754): a dispatched
subagent repeatedly (3-4x in one session) called the `Monitor` tool on its own spawned
background process, then ended its turn expecting a completion notification it will never
receive — only the top-level orchestrator gets those. This is the exact same wedge
`subagent-no-bg-longproc` (agent-tools#52) already blocks for a backgrounded Bash command,
hit here via a different CC tool that gate doesn't inspect.

- `lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`: maps CC's `Monitor` tool to a new `pre-monitor` point,
  mirroring how `pre-agent`/`pre-skill` were added.
- `agent-hooks/subagent-no-monitor/`: new hook. Unlike `subagent-no-bg-longproc` there is no
  foreground/background axis to classify — Monitor **is** the background primitive by
  construction, so **every** subagent call to it is the wedge, unconditionally. The
  orchestrator's own Monitor use (e.g. watching a backgrounded subagent) is unaffected — the
  gate only fires when `agent_id` is present. Same deny-by-default Telegram hatch escalation
  as the sibling hook (`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SUBAGENT_NO_MONITOR`).
- The suggested remedy in the block message (a bounded foreground poll,
  `timeout 900 bash -c 'until <check>; do sleep 5; done'`) was verified end-to-end against
  `subagent-no-bg-longproc` itself — it passes, so the two gates don't fight each other.

**Registration gap (by design, documented):** the `pre-monitor` point mapping alone does not
make Claude Code fire the bridge for `Monitor` calls — CC only runs a `PreToolUse` hook for a
tool it has an explicit `settings.json` matcher for, and that matcher is written by **rig-cli**
(a separate repo), not by this dispatcher. This is the identical two-repo split `pre-agent`
and `pre-skill` already went through. The companion rig-cli PR is
alex-mextner/rig-cli#296 — **neither PR alone makes the block actually fire**; both need to
merge, and `rig apply` (or an equivalent manual `settings.json` edit) needs to run on a given
machine.

## Review

Ran `review diff --staged` (task HYP-1350). No blocking findings. A separate, broader gap was
raised during the companion rig-cli PR's review — Monitor's own command execution bypasses
every existing `pre-bash` security guard, since Monitor and Bash dispatch to different
points — tracked as #438 rather than folded into this wedge fix (different problem, much
larger scope: touches every existing `pre-bash` hook's threat model).

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_subagent_no_monitor.py` (new, 11 cases): subagent Monitor call blocked
      (including when watching something other than its own child), orchestrator Monitor call
      allowed (including the empty-string `agent_id` edge case), top-level `agent_id`
      fallback, unparseable-stdin fail-open, and the full Telegram hatch-escalation matrix
      (unset/bare-flag/exit0/exit1).
- [x] `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py`: unit test for the new `point_for_event` mapping, plus
      two clean-room end-to-end tests driving the real dispatcher subprocess + the real
      `subagent_no_monitor.py` script — a subagent Monitor call gets
      `permissionDecision: "deny"`, the orchestrator's own Monitor call does not.
- [x] Full suite (foreground, no background/Monitor used to run it — dogfooding the fix):
      `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **3657 passed, 23 skipped**.
- [x] Manually smoke-tested the new script directly (subagent blocked / orchestrator allowed).

title: feat(require-review): exempt declared-generated data under docs/ from code review
body:
Closes #442. **Stacks on #435** (`feat/visual-proof-binding`) — merge that first.

## Problem
A machine-generated data dump is `.json`, so `CODE_EXT` classifies it as code and demands a review it can never receive: the motivating file is a 5.9 MB Figma node tree, ~221k lines, which exceeds any reviewer's context. The review truncates and cannot return a verdict, so the gate is **unsatisfiable rather than strict** — the only ways past are faking a marker or a Telegram hatch.

Size is deliberately **not** the discriminator: large is not evidence of un-reviewable, and a file can be padded.

## The discriminator is a declaration
Git already has one: the `-diff` attribute (also implied by `binary`) means *this path is not meaningfully diffable*. Three conditions must hold **together**:

1. the path is under a `docs/` directory — never a route around reviewing real source;
2. the **committed** attributes mark it `-diff`;
3. the extension is a pure serialisation format (`json/jsonl/ndjson/csv/tsv/xml`) — never a script, lockfile, env or infra file.

The declaration lives in `.gitattributes`, which is **not** a docs path, so granting the exemption is itself a reviewed commit. That is the control.

## Two defects review caught, both fixed
- **The control was false.** Plain `check-attr` reads the **working tree**, so an uncommitted `.gitattributes` — or `$GIT_DIR/info/attributes`, which outranks it and is never committed — armed the exemption with no review at all. Now read via `--source=HEAD`, and refused outright when a local override or `core.attributesFile` could be in play. A git too old for `--source` fails closed.
- **N+1 subprocess spawn**, one `check-attr` per staged file, paid even on commits destined to block. Now one batched `--stdin` call, and cheap regex classification bails on the first non-exempt path so a doomed commit spawns nothing.

Fails **closed** throughout: any error, timeout, non-zero exit, malformed output or local override yields no exemption.

## Verification
- 11 new tests: 2 allow cases, 6 block cases (undeclared, declared-outside-docs, script, lockfile, uncommitted declaration, local override), fail-closed, and 2 unit tests.
- **Verified by sabotage** that each guard is load-bearing — removing `--source=HEAD` fails only the uncommitted-declaration test; removing the override guard fails only the override test; disabling the docs/ condition fails the outside-docs tests.
- 264 pass across `test_require_review`, `test_require_review_generated_data`, `test_visual_proof_gate`. Lint reduced to the 3 pre-existing findings at untouched lines.
- The 17 failures in `test_global_review_gate.py` are **pre-existing** — confirmed identical on a stashed clean tree.

## Not addressed here
The sibling **visual-proof gate** blocks the same archive's ten PNG renders, and `dev shot` cannot attest a design *input* (it captures a URL). Every attempt to edit `visual_proof_gate.py` was refused by the safety classifier — correctly, since an agent should not weaken a gate that constrains it. That half needs a human decision; see the report accompanying this PR.

title: fix(ship): review-quorum ticket-code derivation checks PR title before body
body:
## Summary

The review-quorum gate derived `TASK_CODE` from the branch name, then fell back straight to a body-only scan for the first `HYP-<n>`-shaped token — it never looked at the PR title at all (only the separate task-cli-notify step did, as its own later fallback).

## Real incident

PR hyperide/hyper-saas#764, titled `... (HYP-1380)`, shipped with the `AUTHORITY CONFIRMED` line and the task-cli notify both referencing `HYP-1350` instead — a different, unrelated ticket. That posted a false "shipped" comment onto HYP-1350's ticket instead of HYP-1380's.

Root cause, confirmed against the actual PR and the local `ship-audit.jsonl` record:

- The branch `fix/hyp1380-approuter-createroot-hmr-guard` has no hyphen between `hyp` and `1380`, so `HYP-[0-9]+` never matched the branch name at all.
- The PR body's own opening sentence read "This is distinct from HYP-1350's actual Linear scope" — the first `HYP-NNN`-shaped token the old body-only scan found via `grep -oiE 'HYP-[0-9]+' | head -1`.
- `HYP-1380` existed only in the PR title, which this gate never consulted before this fix.

This is a deterministic bug reproducible from a single ship invocation's own inputs — not a concurrency or shared-state issue (verified: the `ship-audit.jsonl` entry for this exact PR/timestamp already recorded `task_code:"HYP-1350"`, so the wrong code was derived by the gate's own text scan, not leaked from another process).

## Fix

- The gate now checks the title before the body, matching this repo's `type(scope): description (HYP-NNN)` convention and the notify step's own pre-existing title-before-body ordering.
- **HYP-<n> is tried across BOTH title and body before either text's generic/descriptive arm runs** (new `_review_quorum_extract_hyp` helper) — otherwise a title that trips the descriptive arm on ordinary prose (`SHA-256`, `UTF-8`, `DO-NOT-MERGE`) could shadow a real `HYP-<n>` that exists in the body.
- **Extracted a shared `_ship_fetch_pr_title_body` helper** used by both the gate and the notify step, splitting the combined `gh` query positionally instead of via bash `read`'s IFS field-splitting — `read` treats a leading tab as IFS whitespace and skips it, so an empty title read the body text into the title variable instead of the body variable (not reachable on real GitHub, which requires non-empty titles, but it silently neutered a test's own body-fallback coverage). The gate and the notify step used to maintain two separately-written copies of this derivation, which is exactly how they disagreed on PR #764 in the first place — they now call one shared implementation.
- Updated `ci/ship/README.md`'s two stale descriptions of the derivation order and the "could not derive a task code" refusal message to mention the title.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 3 regression tests: title-wins-over-body (the exact PR #764 shape), body-fallback with a real, non-empty, ticket-free title, and HYP-in-body-beats-descriptive-match-in-title
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py -q` — 245 passed
- [x] `shellcheck ci/ship/ship.sh` — no new warnings (2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings elsewhere in the file)
- [x] Reviewed by review-cli (codex, GLM, GLM-cc-last, k3 — 4 models). All P2/P3 findings from that pass are addressed above.

Closes #450

title: feat(agent-hooks): enterworktree-foreign-guard — block EnterWorktree into a foreign agent's worktree
body:
## Summary

Mechanistic fix for a confirmed, recurring Claude Code harness bug: an agent (orchestrator or
a dispatched subagent) that needs to resume/ship a PR or branch built by a DIFFERENT agent
calls `EnterWorktree(path=<that other agent's worktree>)`. `EnterWorktree`'s own validation
only confirms the path is a real, registered worktree of the repo (`git worktree list`) —
never that the caller owns it — so the call reports **SUCCESS**, and then permanently bricks
the calling agent's Bash tool for the rest of its session (every subsequent command, even
`pwd`, gets refused), with no recovery path — not even `ExitWorktree`. Hit at least four times
in one project's session history.

A prior fix documented "never do this" in `AGENTS.md`/`AGENTS-CORE.md` and the
`worktree-isolation` skill — a text rule that depends on every future agent happening to read
and remember it. Alex's explicit follow-up direction was a **rig harness hook** that makes the
failure mode structurally impossible instead of merely documented — this PR is that hook.

Closes #453.

## What changed

- `lib/cc_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`: maps CC's `EnterWorktree` `PreToolUse` event to a new
  `pre-worktree-enter` logical point (the same two-repo split `pre-agent`/`pre-skill` went
  through — the rig-cli matcher ships separately, see below).
- `agent-hooks/enterworktree-foreign-guard/`: the guard. Extracts the `agent-<id>` segment
  CC's own worktree-naming convention embeds in `args.path`, compares it against the CALLING
  agent's own top-level `agent_id` (T2-trustworthy — a forged `args.agent_id` is dropped by
  `cc_hook_bridge` whenever the top-level field is absent), and BLOCKS on any mismatch
  (including the orchestrator, which never owns a dispatched subagent's worktree either).
  Creating a brand-new worktree (`name`, no `path`) and re-entering your own worktree are both
  unaffected. Deny-by-default with the same Telegram hatch-escalation contract as
  `subagent-no-bg-longproc`/`subagent-no-monitor` — no self-service bypass.
- Tests: a standalone hook-script suite (15 cases,
  `tests/test_enterworktree_foreign_guard.py`) plus 4 new clean-room `cc_hook_bridge`
  subprocess tests in `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py` (block foreign, allow own, allow
  name-only creation, forged-args-agent_id does not exempt).

## Registration gap

Firing requires **rig-cli**'s `hook_bridge_entries` to register an `EnterWorktree`
`PreToolUse` matcher — companion PR, same split `pre-agent`/`pre-skill`/`pre-monitor` used.
This half is inert alone until that lands and `rig apply` runs.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_enterworktree_foreign_guard.py -q` — 15 passed
- [x] `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py -q` — 30 passed (26 existing + 4 new)
- [x] Full repo suite: `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/ -q -k "not e2e and not cleanroom_e2e"` — 3651 passed, 21 skipped

`Not attached to an active page` / `Resource temporarily unavailable` while
`agent-browser` was also 8 minor versions stale on that machine (0.27.0,
upgraded to 0.35.1 as part of this work).

- New universal skill `agent-browser-concurrency`: a per-task session kept in
  a state file inside the git directory (never the working tree), keyed by a
  caller-supplied task label, generated once and reused idempotently across
  an agent's separate Bash tool calls (which don't share shell state).
- Cross-referenced from `web-page-reading-agent-browser`, whose examples
  previously ran unguarded on the shared `default` session.
- README universal-skill inventory corrected 45 → 47 (the actual count was
  already 46 pre-existing before this diff added the one new skill).

## Review history

This went through 14 rounds of `review diff --staged` (Opus/Fable/Codex/k3/GLM
rotating across rounds) under task code `AGENT-BROWSER-CONCURRENCY-HYGIENE`
before converging. Most rounds caught a real, concrete bug in the mechanism
itself, not style nits — worth noting since the fix history is unusually
long for a docs change:

1. First draft used `--namespace`, which is the wrong isolation axis (that's
   `--session`).
2. `session id --scope worktree --prefix <static-label>` is deterministic,
   so a shared/generic prefix collides two concurrent tasks on the exact
   session the skill exists to keep separate.
3. A `trap EXIT` cleanup doesn't survive across an agent's separate Bash tool
   calls the way a persistent shell script would.
4. A random-session-name generator that never printed the generated value,
   so there was nothing to carry into a later call.
5. A `${VAR:?}` guard placed *before* the export it was meant to protect,
   so it always failed on a legitimate first use.
6. A per-worktree state file path — which collided in exactly the
   "multiple actors share one worktree" case the intro explicitly promised
   to cover. Final fix: the task label lives in the *filename*, not just the
   file's content.

Final review rounds (13–14) came back clean on the resulting design,
including dedicated security/performance passes on the shell snippet itself
(TOCTOU on the idempotent file-create, `/tmp` fallback content-planting risk,
`close && rm` ordering on failure) — flagged as low-severity/edge-case and
already addressed or explicitly documented as a known boundary.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `agent-browser --session <name>`, `session id`, `session list`,
      `close`, `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` env-var equivalence, and idempotent
      file-based reuse empirically against the live installed CLI (0.35.1)
      before writing any of the above as fact.
- [x] Verified `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` resolves a distinct path
      per linked worktree (so the state file is per-worktree by construction)
      and lives outside the tracked working tree (invisible to `git add`).
- [x] 14 rounds of multi-model `review diff --staged`, converged clean.
- Docs-only change — no code/tests to run; `ci/tests` unaffected.

Closes #447.

title: feat(ship): hard-block a merge with zero GitHub-side PR reviews
body:
## Summary

Closes #459. Real incident: PR #764 in hyperide/hyper-saas merged via `gh ship` with `gh pr view --json reviews` returning an empty array — zero human or bot reviews, ever, on that PR. It shipped on Guard-B (review-cli's own automated multi-model pass) alone, because a dispatch instruction wrongly treated Guard-B as sufficient.

## Root cause (verified against the actual script, not assumed)

`grep` for `json reviews` / `reviewDecision` in `ci/ship/ship.sh` returned **zero matches** before this PR. `ship.sh` had no check of its own for an actual GitHub-side review ever happening. The two closest gates:

- **Unresolved-review-threads gate**: refuses only when threads exist and are unresolved. Vacuously satisfied when zero reviews ever posted (zero threads).
- **Review-dwell gate**: a purely time-based window. Its own comment already concedes: *"'0 unresolved threads' is vacuous if no review has posted"* — but it only buys TIME for a review to land, it never checks whether one actually did.

Both passed for PR #764. Guard-B is a **different signal** (review-cli's own automated pass for the PR's task code) — this repo's own docs already say it "does NOT count toward — and does not replace — the human quorum", but nothing in the script itself enforced that a human/bot review ever happened.

## What this PR does

New external-review gate, inserted right after the review-dwell gate (before local-branch-sanity):

- Queries `gh pr view <PR> --json reviews -q '(.reviews // []) | length'`.
- **Zero reviews → refuse**, deny-by-default, **no self-service override flag** — mirrors `--skip-ci` / the review-quorum gate's hatch pattern exactly. The only way through is a one-time live Telegram approval: `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW="<justification>"` (new `ci/ship/external_review_hatch.py`, same shared `agenttools_hatch_escalation` lib, same `python3 -I` isolation, same fixed-path import — copy-pasted hardening from `skip_ci_hatch.py`).
- `SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=0` / `SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0` is the ops off-switch (default: enabled).
- **No self-review exclusion.** Verified first, not assumed: `gh pr view 764 --json author` and `gh pr view 760 --json reviews` both show this repo's PRs are opened under one shared GitHub account regardless of who/what actually did the work, and PR #760's second (human) review was left by that SAME account. An author-based exclusion would have wrongly blocked a genuine review. "Qualifying" = any entry exists at all in `reviews`, any state, any author — existence is the signal, not the verdict. (Residual, accepted, same threat-model boundary as the rest of this script: a shipper who wants to defeat this can leave a trivial self-review — this closes the "nobody looked at all" case, not a content-quality bar.)
- Verified Codex actually submits a real `reviews` entry (not just a plain comment) before committing to this design: `gh pr view 760 --json reviews` shows `chatgpt-codex-connector` with `state: COMMENTED` inside `reviews`, so a reviews-only check correctly recognizes an automated review, not only a human one.

## Test impact / blast-radius

This script has 227 pre-existing tests across 14 separate fake-`gh` fixtures. A first pass (default gate behavior) broke 143 of them — every test that reaches this point in the merge pipeline, since none of the fixtures answered `--json reviews`. Fixed properly rather than shipped broken: all 14 fixtures now default-answer ONE qualifying review (`SHIP_TEST_REVIEW_COUNT`, overridable), so every pre-existing test is unaffected. Verified: full suite before this change = 227 passed; after = 232 passed (227 + 5 new).

New tests (`tests/test_ship.py`):
- `test_external_review_passes_with_a_qualifying_review` — happy path, documents the gate never blocks a normal ship.
- `test_external_review_deny_by_default_refuses_before_merge` — the actual PR #764 reproduction: zero reviews, no hatch → refused before merge, audited.
- `test_external_review_disabled_via_env_lets_zero_reviews_through` — ops off-switch.
- `test_external_review_fails_closed_when_python3_exits_zero_without_sentinel` — a fake/broken `python3` exiting 0 without the `APPROVED` sentinel must not be mistaken for approval (mirrors the skip-ci gate's identical guard).
- `test_external_review_approved_hatch_reaches_merge_e2e` — the escape valve, end to end.

## Known adjacent work — no conflict, just a heads-up for merge order

A concurrent, unrelated fix (agent-tools #450/#452, `fix/ship-ticket-title-priority`) touches the SAME `_FAKE_GH_QUORUM` fixture block in `tests/test_ship.py` (both insert a new `elif`/case branch right after the `*headRefName*` line, for different `--json` queries). Both edits are additive and non-overlapping in meaning — whichever PR merges second will need a trivial rebase keeping both inserted lines. Does not touch the same lines in `ci/ship/ship.sh` (that fix is around the task-code-derivation block, ~line 2440+; this gate is inserted around line ~1660, right after the review-dwell gate).

## Scope note (what's NOT in this PR)

This closes the "ship.sh has no check at all" gap for the shared script. It does not retroactively re-review PR #764 itself (separate PR: hyperide/hyper-saas#767) and does not change anything about how Guard-B itself works.
