title: feat(agent-hooks): block-devserver-primary — block dev-server launch against shared checkout
body:
## Summary

New `pre-bash` hook (`block-devserver-primary`) closes a real, reproduced gap: no existing hook recognized a dev-server **launch** command (`npm run dev`, `vite`, `next dev`, ...) against an enrolled repo's shared/default-branch checkout.

**Evidence the gap is real:**
- `pre-write` `worktree-only-writes` only sees Edit/Write tool calls — a dev server starting is neither.
- `pre-bash` `pin-primary-worktree` only classifies `git checkout`/`switch` — a dev-server launch has no `git` in it at all.
- Claude Code's own built-in worktree-isolation Bash guard is git-command-focused — verified live: `git branch` is blocked by it, but a plain `cd <shared-checkout> && npm run dev` (zero `git` anywhere) sails through untouched, and so does `cd <shared> && echo`.
- **Reproduced (internal task #191):** hyperide's canvas preview generator (`lib/preview-generator`) overwrites `client/App.tsx` and the git-tracked `client/__canvas_preview__.tsx` (see its own `.gitignore` comment confirming it's deliberately tracked, not build output) as a side effect of the dev server running. One "quick live verification" pass against the shared checkout corrupted both files with 2000+ generated lines — no `git` command and no `Edit`/`Write` tool call anywhere in that session for any existing hook to catch.

**What it does:** classifies npm/yarn/pnpm/bun/npx/bunx/vite/next/astro/webpack dev-server launch shapes, tracks a leading `cd`/`--prefix`-style directory override (including the `--prefix=value` equals form), peels bare command wrappers (`nohup`/`env`/`sudo`/`time`/`nice`/`setsid`/`command`/`exec`), and denies the launch when the effective cwd is an enrolled repo (`agent_hooks.worktree_only`, same opt-in as its two siblings) sitting on its default branch. Deny-by-default with the same Telegram hatch-escalation pattern as the sibling hooks — no self-service env-var bypass. Auto-discovered by `rig apply`'s existing `agent-hooks/*/*.json` catalog scan, no registry file edits needed.

**Notable finding during review:** the hook was initially shipped non-executable (mode 100644). `runner.py` execs `argv[0]` directly relying on the shebang + exec bit, and with `on_error: open` a launch failure resolves to silent allow — this would have made the hook a permanent, undetectable no-op after install (every existing test loaded the module via `importlib`, bypassing the OS exec path entirely). Fixed (`chmod +x`) with a new regression test that invokes the real file via `subprocess.run` exactly like the runner does.

**Deliberately NOT covered** (documented in the hook's own README "Known scope limits" section, not silently missing): non-literal `cd`/flag targets (`$VAR`, `$(...)`), subshells, heredoc bodies that happen to contain `npm run dev` as text, and flag-aware wrapper peeling / `bash -c`/`sh -c` re-parsing (bare wrappers like `nohup npm run dev &` ARE now caught; `sudo -u dev npm run dev` with its own flag is a documented, deliberate miss) — tracked as follow-up #463. Generic file mutation via Bash (`>`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `rm`) and `git commit` on the primary checkout are different hooks' job already (`no-shell-file-edit`, `require-review-before-commit`, pre-push `protect-main`) — not reimplemented here.

**Unreviewed-by-any-round delta, flagged for the reviewer's attention:** `_peel_command_wrappers` and the `=`-form branch in `_peel_dir_flag` were both added in the final local review round and have had zero independent review before this PR — every earlier `review diff` round reviewed a snapshot that predates them. Please look closely at those two functions in `block_devserver_primary.py`.

This is a narrow-signature heuristic discipline gate, not a shell interpreter or a sandbox — false negatives on unusual shell constructs are expected and documented; false positives lean toward over-blocking (safe direction) where the two conflict.

**Termination rule for this PR:** only P0/P1 findings from this PR's own GitHub-side review get fixed here. Anything else goes to #463 or a new follow-up issue — this already went through 6 local `review diff` rounds (P0 executable-bit bug, 5 P1 parser-bypass bugs) and the heuristic-parser surface doesn't converge to zero on its own.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q tests/test_block_devserver_primary.py` — 105 passed
- [x] `ruff check` on all modified/new files — clean
- [x] `pytest tests/` full suite — 3859 passed, 6 skipped, 17 failed (pre-existing `test_global_review_gate.py` failures, confirmed present on clean `origin/main` via `git stash` comparison before this diff existed — unrelated to this change)
- [x] Manual: `chmod -x` the hook file, ran the new `test_hook_file_is_executable_and_runs_standalone` test, confirmed it fails; restored `+x`, confirmed it passes
- [x] Manual: verified classifier output for `npm --prefix=/shared run dev`, `nohup npm run dev`, `sudo -u dev npm run dev` (documented miss) against expected tuples

title: feat(ship): agent-tools checkout staleness gate + periodic self-heal
body:
## Summary

`ci/ship/ship.sh` runs straight off disk from `$AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT` — no build step, no packaging. Nothing keeps that checkout synced with `origin/main`, so a merged fix (concretely, #451) silently stays inactive on a machine until someone remembers to `git pull` it by hand. This is the ci/ship-specific slice of agent-tools#315 (live-checkout personal CLIs going stale between sessions).

Two-part fix:

1. **A pre-flight staleness gate in `ship.sh`.** Before shipping, it compares the checkout ACTUALLY executing this file (via `$AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT`, then a `BASH_SOURCE`-derived fallback — never the target repo's own checkout) against its own `origin/main`. Refuses with a distinct message when the checkout is parked on a feature branch or detached HEAD (the exact incident that motivated this PR — a generic "behind" refusal's `pull --ff-only` fix can't succeed on a diverged branch and would lock out every ship on the machine); refuses with the correct fix command when `ci/ship/` itself is stale (the #451 class of incident); warns-only for drift elsewhere. Fails open on anything indeterminate — this is a freshness hint, not a security gate. Opt out with `SHIP_STALENESS_CHECK=0`.

2. **`ci/ship/refresh-agent-tools-checkout.sh`** — a periodic (launchd/cron) self-heal script. Deliberately conservative: only fast-forwards when the checkout is on `main`, has an empty working-tree status, is not ahead of its upstream, has no `ci/ship/ship.sh` invocation apparently running, and no incoming path collides with a currently-ignored local file (verified empirically — git's untracked-file overwrite protection does NOT cover ignored paths, so a plain fast-forward pull can silently destroy one). Any guard failing exits 0 silently, matching a best-effort background job's contract; a real fast-forward logs one line. Install recipe (macOS launchd / Linux cron) is in the script's own header, mirroring the existing `ai.hyperide.model-freshness.plist` pattern.

## Review history (why this diff looks the way it does)

This went through several independent `review diff` rounds. The first pass looked clean and passed its own test suite — but every subsequent round found real, verifiable bugs, several confirmed by direct empirical experiments outside the test suite (not just review-model claims):

- **`timeout` is absent on stock macOS** (GNU coreutils; this dev machine only has it because Homebrew's `gnubin` happens to be linked) — both the gate's fetch and the refresh script's pull would have silently no-op'd forever on the target platform. Now resolves `timeout`/`gtimeout` with a bounded fallback, and the unwrapped case is additionally bounded via `GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT/TIME`.
- **The ignored-file collision check missed non-ASCII and newline-containing filenames** (git's default path-quoting) and **dangling symlinks** (`-e` alone is false for a broken link) — both would have let the exact overwrite bug back in. Fixed via NUL-delimited (`-z`, `core.quotePath=false`) diffing and an `-e || -L` existence check.
- **A `set -euo pipefail` violation**: an unprotected command-substitution assignment could die with a non-zero exit (a SIGPIPE under pipefail, or any transient git failure) instead of the script's own documented "any guard failing exits 0 silently" contract.
- **An N+1 process-spawn loop**: the original collision check spawned one `git check-ignore` per changed path. Rewritten to two total git spawns (one diff, one ignored-file listing) plus in-shell array membership.
- **A vacuous test**: the original self-hosting-skip test still passed even with the skip condition deliberately removed. Caught by re-running the suite against a mutated copy of the gate; the test is now written so it genuinely fails when the skip logic is broken (verified the same way).
- **A misleading refusal for the literal motivating incident**: if the checkout is parked on a feature branch (the actual incident this PR responds to), the gate used to print a "behind origin/main" refusal whose suggested `pull --ff-only` fix cannot succeed on a diverged branch — an unactionable, fleet-wide lockout. Now detects and names that state distinctly.
- Plus: `$AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT` now takes precedence over a `BASH_SOURCE`-derived guess (avoids misidentifying an unrelated git-managed `$HOME` if `ship.sh` is ever run from a copy), a standalone-test-file hermeticity gap (`tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py` run alone would have hit the real repo over the network), and a test race in the "ship running" concurrency guard.

One reviewer claim was checked and refuted rather than acted on: that `git fetch origin main` doesn't reliably update `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Verified empirically (a from-scratch git experiment, git 2.50.1) that it does — this is git's documented opportunistic-update behavior since 1.8.4, and my own passing tests already exercise exactly this path.

**Known, accepted residual limitation** (documented in the refresh script's header): the ignored-file collision check re-validates immediately before the fetch, but doesn't hold a cross-process lock across the fetch+merge window — a file created at a colliding path in that millisecond-scale gap could still be overwritten. Given the script's explicit best-effort, do-nothing-unless-clearly-safe design, a full lock was judged not worth the added complexity.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` — 240 passed (full file; 13 staleness-gate tests including refuse/warn/silent/disabled/self-hosting/feature-branch/AGENT_TOOLS_ROOT-precedence/no-timeout/linked-worktree/fails-open/non-git-root).
- [x] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_refresh_agent_tools_checkout.py -q` — 13 passed (pull/skip-on-feature-branch/skip-dirty/skip-unpushed/no-op-in-sync/non-repo/typo'd-arg/env-fallback/no-upstream/no-timeout/linked-worktree/ship-running/ignored-collision).
- [x] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/ -q` — full repo suite, 3668 passed / 23 skipped, 0 failed (confirms the `tests/conftest.py` change doesn't regress anything else).
- [x] `bash -n` + `shellcheck -x` clean on both scripts (pre-existing, unrelated findings only).
- [x] Two mutation checks: temporarily disabled the self-hosting skip and the ship-running pgrep guard in turn — both times the corresponding test correctly failed, then both were reverted.
- [ ] CI (`tests.yml`) — pending on this PR.

Not shipped this session — opened for real review plus the mandatory wait period, per this repo's own merge discipline (`AGENTS.md`: no self-ship without a genuine human/independent quorum, on top of Guard-B).

title: fix(agent-hooks): treat a newline as a command separator in both commit gates (#472)
body:
Closes #472. Also corrects the diagnosis recorded in #464 — see "What #464 actually was" below.

## The bug

`visual-proof-gate` and `skills-read-gate` decide whether a command is a work action by anchoring a regex to a **command head** — the start of the string, or immediately after a `|`, `&`, or `;`. Both first normalise the command through `_strip_shell_comment`, which did:

```python
" ".join(shlex.split(command, comments=True))
```

That join **erases every newline**, and a newline is in neither anchor class. So after normalisation the only commit still detectable was one whose *first line* was itself the `git` invocation.

Multi-line is the ordinary shape an agent writes a shell command in, so this was not an edge case. Reproduced directly against the live hook, with a staged `.tsx` and no proof marker:

| command | exit | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `git commit -m x` | 10 | blocked, correct |
| `cd <repo>`⏎`git add -A`⏎`git commit -m x` | **0** | **allowed — no proof, no hatch, no audit line** |
| `echo hi`⏎`git commit -m x` | **0** | **allowed** |
| `set -e`⏎`git commit -m x` | **0** | **allowed** |

A UI commit went through with no screenshot, no Telegram approval prompt, and nothing written to `~/.config/agent-tools/overrides.log` — externally indistinguishable from a gate that simply never fired.

## What #464 actually was

#464 reported "a commit succeeded with `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_VISUAL_PROOF_GATE` set but the overrides log gained zero entries", and hypothesised an internal error plus `on_error: "open"` swallowing the audit write. **That premise is false — there is no error on that path.** Two separate things were happening:

1. The commit named in the report (`bc04eb11`, `client/App.tsx`, 10:43:48) was allowed by `_proof_fresh()`: an attestation marker was written at 10:43:12, **36 seconds earlier**. The gate was already satisfied, so it never consulted the hatch, so it correctly wrote nothing. The env var was set as a precaution and was simply never needed. Correct behaviour, not a bug.
2. The *symptom* — an allow with no audit line — is genuinely produced by this PR's bug, on any multi-line commit.

So the audit log was never the broken component. Adding "log harder" defensiveness there would have left the actual hole open.

## The fix

`_shell_tokens` replaces the flattening: it splits the command into logical lines and emits an explicit `;` token between them, so every existing consumer (the command-head anchors, `_segments`, `is_skip_commit`, `effective_cwd`) sees real command heads. Correctness here is mostly about what a newline is **not**:

- **inside quotes** — ordinary text (a multi-line commit message)
- **after a backslash** — a line continuation, splicing one command
- **inside a heredoc body** — data on stdin, never commands. The body is dropped, so `cat > ship.sh <<'EOF'` / `git commit -m x` / `EOF` is not read as a commit. Without this the fix would *hard-block* every heredoc that writes a script or Makefile — a constant false block on an ordinary agent pattern.
- **a lone `\r`** — an ordinary character to a POSIX shell; only `\r\n` ends a line
- **after a line-ending `&&`/`||`/`|`** — the separator is already there, so no second synthetic `;` (which would leave an empty segment for `effective_cwd` to walk)
- **`#`** — stripped per *line*, since a comment cannot swallow the command below it

`_INLINE_ENV_PREFIX` gains `\r\n` in its head class for the same reason: it runs on the raw command, so without it the documented inline hatch form written on any line but the first stays in place and re-defeats the anchor.

## Sync guard

Both hooks carry this parser by design (standalone scripts, no shared import path). That convention already cost this repo the #174 first-segment bug, which shipped because a fix was applied to only one twin — and a `SYNC:` comment cannot notice. `tests/test_shell_parse_sync.py` now compares the two copies **structurally** (AST with docstrings stripped, so each may keep its own prose) and **behaviourally** across the shapes that motivated this fix.

## Known gap (pre-existing, unchanged)

A heredoc body actually *executed* by a shell — `bash <<'EOF'` / `git commit -m x` / `EOF` — is dropped along with the data case, so a commit hidden that way is still not detected. It was equally undetected before this PR. Closing it needs an interpreter-vs-data distinction, which is a separate change.

## Verification

- 29 new regression tests across both hooks, covering every row of the table above plus prose, heredoc, herestring, CRLF, lone `\r`, continuation, comment-line, and inline-hatch-on-a-later-line shapes.
- Full suite: **3830 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.**
- Reviewed by two independent models (`review diff`); the heredoc false-block, the double-separator, and the lone-`\r` over-split were all findings from that pass and are fixed here, with tests.

title: feat(hooks,ops): memory-pressure admission gate + periodic VS Code orphan reaper
body:
## Summary

Part of the systemic fix for the 2026-08-27/28 incident: 10-15 concurrent background agents drove free memory on a 24GB machine to ~65MB, hanging VS Code windows on reload-required modals. This repo's half of the fix (the sibling PR in `hyper-ext-e2e` handles the pre-launch orphan sweep inside the e2e harness itself): hyperide/hyper-ext-e2e#164.

Two independent, real mechanisms:

**1. `agent-hooks/heavy-op-memory-gate`** — a pre-Bash hook that blocks heavy operations (extension rebuild, `review diff`/`quorum`/`brainstorm`/`just-ask`, build/test suites) when macOS jetsam memory pressure is at warn (2) or critical (4). Classification is token-based (`shlex`-aware, not raw substring — avoids false-positiving on something like `git commit -m "make all tests green"`). The pressure-level override is restricted to `{1,2,4}` so it can't be silently disabled via an unbounded env var. Linux uses `/proc/pressure/memory` PSI as a fallback. 78 tests.

**2. `ops/vscode-orphan-reaper`** — a periodic (15-minute, launchd) sweep for leaked isolated VS Code test windows, independently discovered via 340 leaked `hvsc-*` userDataDir fossils on this machine spanning 2026-07-14..2026-08-28. Mirrors the TS pre-launch sweep's predicate. Found and fixed the same `ps etimes=`-is-Linux-only bug independently in this Python implementation (macOS BSD `ps` silently drops the unrecognized keyword and still exits 0 — verified live on this machine). Tree-kill by shared `--user-data-dir=` token, re-verified immediately before each kill to guard against PID reuse. 36 tests. Installer hardened with XML-escaping + `plutil -lint` validation before ever unloading the previous working launchd unit.

## Known gap vs. original scope

The periodic reaper here is currently a **manual install** (`ops/vscode-orphan-reaper/install.sh`) — it is not yet wired into `rig apply`'s machine-wide provisioning, so it won't automatically exist on a fresh machine. Tracked as #468.

- [x] Live-verified the `etime=`/`etimes=` bug on this machine before fixing

title: fix(agent-hooks): bind visual-proof-gate markers to a repo and a staged diff
body:
Closes #475.

## The bug

`visual-proof-gate`'s "fresh screenshot marker" check (`_proof_fresh()`) used to be: does
*any* file exist in `~/.cache/agent-tools/visual-proof/` with an mtime inside the last hour?
Nothing about *which* file, nothing about its content.

That's both machine-global and content-blind:

- **Global**: the directory is one shared bucket for every repo, every agent, every session
  on the machine. A screenshot taken for repo A satisfied repo B's completely unrelated
  commit for up to an hour afterward.
- **Content-blind**: a bare `touch` (empty file) satisfied the gate. Verified directly —
  nothing about the file had to relate to a screenshot at all.

Net effect: for up to an hour after *any* agent, in *any* repo, captured *any* screenshot
(or just touched a file in that directory), *every* other agent's UI commit in *every* repo
passed the gate with zero relationship to what was actually committed.

## The fix

`_proof_fresh()` now validates two marker shapes, both scanned from the same directory:

1. **Primary** — a `dev shot <url> --out ...` attestation from dev-cli (already exists,
   already writes a JSON record binding the repo's git toplevel + the sha256 of
   `git diff --cached` — this gate just never read those fields before). Now required to
   match ALL of: resolved repo toplevel, the *current* staged-diff hash, `worktree_dirty`
   recorded as `false` (a dirty worktree at capture time means the screenshot could show
   content that was never staged), producer `tool`/`version`, and a **re-hashed capture
   file on disk** matching `capture_sha256` — closing a forgery where an agent could
   hand-write a JSON with just the two `git`-derived fields and skip capturing anything at
   all.
2. **Fallback** (no URL to shoot — docs-only change, generated image, schematic) — a new
   `--write-marker` CLI mode writes a marker whose content is the exact resolved repo
   toplevel. Weaker (not diff-bound) but still repo-scoped and content-checked. Replaces the
   old bare-`touch` recipe, which no longer satisfies the gate at all.

Every marker read goes through a TOCTOU-safe, symlink-refusing, FIFO/device-safe,
size-bounded reader (single `open()+fstat()` on one fd, bounded `read()`) — a hostile or
malformed marker resolves to BLOCK, never a hang or crash. `on_error: "open"` on this hook
means a crashed/hung check is an *allowed* commit, so "the check itself breaks" is just as
real a bypass as "the check logic is wrong," and is closed the same way. A scan-count cap
bounds total work if the directory is flooded with junk candidates.

## Review

6 rounds of `review diff` (multi-model, `--pool 2`). Each round found something real; every
finding that reproduced against the actual code got a fix + a regression test:

- repo/diff mismatch not caught → repo+diff binding
- bare touch / arbitrary content → content check
- forged attestation needing only 2 `git`-derived fields → capture re-hash requirement
- `worktree_dirty` ignored → required `false`
- embedded-NUL `capture_path` crashing the hook (→ fail-open) → caught
- FIFO/device at a marker path hanging the hook (→ fail-open) → `O_NONBLOCK` + regular-file-only read
- TOCTOU between a type check and the read → single-fd open+fstat+read
- unbounded read letting a concurrently-growing file blow past the size cap → bounded read
- future-dated marker never expiring → `0 <= age <= window`
- legacy/foreign producer version accepted → `tool`/`version` pinned
- many valid-shaped junk markers → unbounded total scan cost → scan-count cap
- predictable `--write-marker` filename + symlink-follow write → `tempfile.mkstemp`
  (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL`)

One round-5 finding (a claimed `UnicodeEncodeError` escaping the hook) did **not** reproduce
against the actual code — verified directly end-to-end; `UnicodeEncodeError` is already a
`ValueError` subclass and was already caught. Documented, not fixed, as inherent to this
hook's own `pre-bash` advisory architecture (same doctrine this file already states
elsewhere — `on_error: "open"`, process discipline not a security boundary): a pre-bash
hook can't make its own check atomic with the shell's *later* `git commit` execution, and a
narrower TOCTOU in dev-cli's own capture-then-hash producer step is that repo's concern, not
this consumer's.

## Test plan

- `tests/test_visual_proof_gate.py`: 114 tests (44 new), covering repo-mismatch, content-blind,
  and correctly-scoped-marker-still-works cases per the ticket's acceptance criteria, plus
  every review finding above with its own regression test.
- Full suite: `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/` — 3811 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed.
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files.

## Known overlaps with other open work (flagging for coordination, not blocking)

- **#474** (`fix/visual-proof-gate-newline-separator`) touches the same file but a
  completely different area (shell-command tokenization for detecting a commit at all, not
  the marker/proof logic) — no functional overlap, should merge independently either order.
- **#433** (`docs/visual-proof-cli-worktree-guard-note`) also edits `_block_message()` and
  the README's marker-writing recipe (documents `dev shot` as primary, references the CLI
  worktree-isolation guard trap for a bare `touch`). This PR's `_block_message()`/README
  changes will likely textually conflict with #433's — whoever merges second should
  reconcile by hand. Functionally compatible: #433 changes *which command is recommended*,
  this PR changes *what the gate actually validates* — no logic conflict, just adjacent text.

title: opencode bridge: authoritative detached-subagent identity + canonical launcher (#476)
body:
## Summary

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/476 (closed by task-cli acceptance, not by merge). Part of the rig-cli#337 gap catalog (gap 3: shared hook logic vs opencode's real tool-call schema).

Gives rig-dispatched detached opencode agents an authoritative identity (`RIG_AGENT_ID`/`RIG_DETACHED_AGENT` process-env markers, read by the hook bridge after the forged-key strip), ships the canonical detached launcher as the `rig-detached-opencode` universal skill, gates the `background` -> `run_in_background` mapping on opencode's experimental flag, and corrects every place that claimed opencode has an always-available native `background` task field.

## Reconciled against PR #544 (`harness` field) — what is superseded, what still stands

PR #544 tags every bridge event with a hardcoded top-level `harness` (`claude-code` / `codex` / `opencode`) and exempts codex/opencode from **orchestrator-stays-thin** by that field. That covers the part of #476 that was "every opencode session looks like the orchestrator to orchestrator-stays-thin" — for that ONE gate, the env-backed identity is no longer needed and this PR does not touch that gate's decision logic (only narrows its docstring: neither bridge exposes a trusted identity from the harness's OWN payload; opencode now has one only for a rig-launched detached child).

What this PR still adds, which #544 does not:
- `args.agent_id` for a rig-launched detached opencode child, from the process env (`_detached_agent_id`). `harness` says "this is opencode", not "this is a dispatched worker". The gates keyed on `agent_id` are still blind for opencode without it: **background-subagent-gate** (a worker fanning out), **no-long-inline-process** (a worker running a long build), and the subagent-only gates **subagent-no-bg-longproc** / **subagent-no-monitor** (which must GOVERN a detached child, not treat it as the main thread). Also a stable id for marker/cooldown paths that key on the agent.
- The launcher itself (`skills/universal/rig-detached-opencode/`), the only sanctioned truly-detached path on a default opencode build.
- The experimental-flag gating of `background` -> `run_in_background` in the bridge.

## Reconciled against PR #499 (opencode task general/explore pass the gate)

#499 allows an opencode `task` with `subagent_type` general/explore without a flag. Its stated reason ("opencode Task is inherently async") is wrong per the verification below: a default-build task runs in the FOREGROUND. The allow is kept anyway, deliberately, and the docs/REMINDER now say why: opencode has no in-tool background path at all, so blocking left a plain opencode session with NO executable dispatch (the deadlock in #495), and the gate's thin-orchestrator premise is Claude-Code-specific — the same reasoning #544 used to exempt opencode from orchestrator-stays-thin. The truly-detached path is the launcher; the REMINDER names both. The default-build "smuggled `background: true` still blocks" test now uses a custom subagent_type so it does not collide with the general/explore tolerance.

## Task-1 verdict: the real analog of `background: true` in opencode 1.18.20

Investigated the installed Mach-O (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/opencode/1.18.20`) via `strings` and cross-checked the public source at tag v1.18.20 (`packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts`, `packages/opencode/src/effect/runtime-flags.ts`):

- **Default (flag off) model-facing task schema — `BaseParameters`:** `description`, `prompt`, `subagent_type`, `task_id` (optional), `command` (optional). **No `background`, no `run_in_background`, no async/detached analog.**
- **The native `background` boolean DOES exist** in the tool's internal `Parameters` schema — but it is **experimental-gated**: advertised to the model and honored at execute time only under `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=<truthy>` or the broad `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=<truthy>`. With the flag off, a smuggled `background: true` makes execute() FAIL ("Background subagents require OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true").
- Binary evidence: `jsonSchema: flags.experimentalBackgroundSubagents ? undefined : ToolJsonSchema.fromSchema(BaseParameters)`.

## Changes

- `dispatch.py` `_detached_agent_id()` — restores `args.agent_id` from the process env after the forged-key strip; plugin.js spawns the dispatcher with `{...process.env}`, so launcher-set markers are visible on every tool call.
- `_normalize_task_args` maps `background` -> `run_in_background` **only when the hosting opencode process carries the experimental flag**.
- background-subagent-gate REMINDER/docstring/README state the verified truth and name the provisioned launcher path.
- `skills/universal/rig-detached-opencode/` — SKILL.md + the launcher (moved out of `bin/`, which rig never provisions — codex P1). The launcher reads the brief BEFORE `cd "$workdir"` so a relative brief with a different workdir reaches the child (codex P1; red-first regression test). `lib/opencode_hook_bridge/README.md` documents the identity contract (codex P2).
- Launcher log hygiene (review round 1): `umask 077`, an owner-checked `0700` log dir (`RIG_AGENT_LOG_DIR` override, default `/tmp/agent-logs`), `0600` log file, and a refusal to follow a pre-planted symlink at the log path. The identity contract documents the session-wide marker inheritance as a known limitation of the cooperative model (never `export` the markers by hand).
- Launcher detach hardening (review round 2): `opencode run --title <name> -- <brief>` (a brief starting with `---`/`- ` was eaten by yargs as an option), `</dev/null` stdin (nohup only redirects a TTY; under a harness bash tool the child blocked on the caller's pipe), and a NEW SESSION via `setsid(1)` where present, else a `python3 os.setsid()+execvp` shim (macOS ships no setsid) so a tree-/group-kill of the tool call cannot take the child down. The stub child records pid/pgid + a stdin probe; the happy path asserts pgid == pid and EOF stdin. A relative `RIG_AGENT_LOG_DIR` is resolved before `cd`; an existing log is `chmod 600` before the brief is appended.
- The end-to-end "env marker makes a non-trivial task subagent-exempt" test now uses a custom `subagent_type` with a control run that BLOCKS without the marker — a `general` payload passes on its own after #495/#499 and proved nothing.

## Tests

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_background_subagent_gate.py tests/test_opencode_hook_bridge.py tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py tests/test_rig_detached_opencode.py tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py -q` green after merging main and #499.
- Full suite green (see the ship log).
- Review quorum: `OC476-OPENCODE-BACKGROUND-TRUTH` (3 passed iterations, 3 distinct roles, verified from this worktree with 0 mismatched iterations) plus two `GH-497` rounds after the merge (round 1: README regression, false-proof test, log hygiene; round 2: the launcher detach findings above) — every P1/P2 from both rounds is fixed in-branch.

## Notes

- Pre-existing, unrelated: `tests/test_global_review_gate.py` leaves gitignored `.test-repos/` scratch behind, so a second consecutive full-suite run in the same worktree collides on reused pytest tmp names. CI is unaffected (fresh checkout).

title: fix(ship): drain worktree-list pipe fully to avoid git SIGPIPE
body:
## Summary
- `MAIN_CHECKOUT` auto-derivation piped `git worktree list --porcelain` into `awk '{...; exit}'`, which closes the pipe as soon as it finds its match — on a repo with enough worktrees for the porcelain output to exceed the OS pipe buffer, `git` gets killed by SIGPIPE (141), propagated by `set -euo pipefail`, aborting `ship.sh` before any diagnostic.
- Fix: drop the early `exit` so awk consumes the whole stream (no SIGPIPE by construction, no `cat >/dev/null` sink needed), and swap `$2` for `substr($0,10)` to match the sibling worktree parser so a spaced main-checkout path still resolves in full.
- The regression test's fake-git padding is now scoped to a one-shot marker so it doesn't leak phantom worktrees into other `git worktree list` call sites in the same run, plus a dedicated test for the spaced-path case.

title: fix(hooks,skills,docs): stop telling agents to forge the review marker
body:
## The incident

The `require-review-before-commit` hook's README told callers to wire it up as `review --uncommitted && touch "$REVIEW_MARKER"`. Both halves are wrong. The flag no longer exists, and a headless agent's own write to `~/.cache/agent-tools/` is rejected by its runner's permission policy. Two detached agents reached the gate with a green review and a stale marker, followed that advice exactly, and were killed by it in one night.

## The contract, stated once and enforced

The marker is written by the review **tool**, at the end of a review that actually covered the staged change — never by the agent. For review-cli that is a completed `review diff --staged --task <CODE>` over the real index, whose diff was small enough to reach every reviewer in full.

"Completed" is not "clean": reported findings do not withhold the marker, because this gate enforces that a review *happened*, not that it was happy. What withholds it is a run that could not be trusted to have covered the change — a failed or degraded board, an unstaged or piped diff, a diff too big to reach the seats.

`--task <CODE>` is part of the runnable form, not decoration: `review diff` exits 2 without it, reviewing nothing and leaving the commit blocked. That is precisely how a stale instruction becomes a wedge, so a new test (`tests/test_review_invocation_is_consistent.py`) pins every file that tells a reader how to satisfy this gate against one canonical command, and refuses the dead `--uncommitted` form anywhere a caller reads. It immediately found three drifted copies, plus two more live sources nobody had looked at: the global git-hook gate's own message, and the CI review script's "local pre-commit" instructions (that script computes a `base...head` diff, empty for staged work, and writes no marker at all — it was never a pre-commit path).

## Two behavioral fixes on the hook

**An exported-but-empty `REVIEW_MARKER=`** became `Path("")` — the current directory — so this gate stat'd a directory whose mtime any file creation refreshes, while the review tool wrote its own default path. Depending on which way it broke, that either blocks a genuinely reviewed commit or waves through an unreviewed one. A variable set to nothing now means the same as one that is not set, on both sides.

**The freshness check now requires a regular file**, via an explicit `stat()`. A directory at the marker path satisfied the gate more or less permanently, for the same mtime reason. `Path.is_file()` would have been the short spelling and the wrong one: it swallows every OSError, which would turn an unreadable marker into a hard block. The rule the code now follows is that missing, not-a-regular-file, a symlink loop and an impossible path are *answers* and they block; a failure to ask is not, and it fails open — this hook is `on_error: open`.

That loosens one case deliberately, and it is worth naming: an unreadable cache directory used to block (the old `Path.exists()` swallowed the `EACCES`) and now allows with a warning. Broken permissions on a cache directory say nothing about whether a review ran.

## The skill's own timeout advice was a wedge

It said ten minutes, against a board review that typically takes about seven and is pushed past ten by one slow seat or a retry — so the timeout landed on the run that had done all the work and was about to write the marker. Naming nothing is no better: the harness applies its own default, about two minutes. It now says to set the largest timeout the harness accepts, and to shrink the work rather than hope when the printed estimate approaches that ceiling.

## Ships with review-cli#350

That PR is what makes an unsatisfied gate explain itself on stderr, and carries the matching empty-value normalization. Land them together: the review seats on each side read the other repo's *installed* checkout and correctly report the mismatch until both are merged.

## Verification

- Full suite: 4059 passed, 6 skipped.
- New coverage: the cross-file invocation consistency test, the block message's own runnable-command pin, and regression tests for the empty value, the directory marker, the symlink loop, the parent-is-a-file path, and the deliberate fail-open case.
- Fourteen review rounds across four models.

Companion to tg-cli#301 / tg-cli PR #305 (Alex, 2026-09-05): agents use only the standard
message tags — `answer`, `decision`, `problem`, `report`. There is no separate `question`
message type any more: an open question for the human IS a decision he has to make, so it

title: test: strip ambient SHIP_*/RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_* env at conftest import
body:
## Summary
- `tests/test_ship.py` builds each `ci/ship/ship.sh` subprocess env as `dict(os.environ)` and only pops a specific known set of ambient vars by name (`GH_REPO`, `SHIP_TEST_DIFF`, ...), not every `SHIP_*`/`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_*` gate-control knob. Once this machine started exporting `SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0` machine-wide (via rig's global env mechanism), five external-review-gate tests silently failed — the ambient value disabled the very gate they were written to exercise as enabled.
- Fix: strip every ambient `SHIP_*`/`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_*` var once, at `tests/conftest.py` **import time** (module-level, before pytest collects any test module) — see `_strip_ambient_ship_env` in `tests/conftest.py`.

## Deviation from the original ask (please read before reviewing)
The ask was for a **per-test autouse fixture** using `monkeypatch.delenv`. I found that would break a much bigger surface than the 5 tests reported: both `tests/test_ship.py` (line 38) and `tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py` (line 26) rely on their own **module-level** `os.environ.setdefault("SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM", "0")` / `os.environ["SHIP_TASK_NOTIFY_ENABLED"] = "0"`, applied **once at collection time**, which essentially all of `test_ship.py` (~250 tests) and all of `test_ship_notify_task_cli.py` depend on implicitly.

A per-test `monkeypatch.delenv` autouse fixture would strip those module-level defaults during **every single test body** (monkeypatch only restores the pre-test value *after* teardown), silently re-enabling the review-quorum and task-notify gates suite-wide for the duration of each test — the opposite of what those two lines exist to guarantee.

So instead the strip runs once, at `conftest.py` import time, which pytest always does before importing/collecting test modules in the same directory — letting `test_ship.py`'s and `test_ship_notify_task_cli.py`'s own one-time defaults apply cleanly against a guaranteed-clean starting point. Bonus: this also closes a latent hole where an ambient `SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM=1` would previously have made `os.environ.setdefault(...)` a silent no-op.

I did not add a dedicated regression test for the conftest-import-ordering guarantee itself (pytest's own collection order does that, and a synthetic pytester-based test would be fiddly given `conftest.py`'s relative `sys.path` insert + `agenttools_hatch_escalation` import) — the before/after empirical evidence below is the proof for this conftest-only change.

## Test plan
- [x] `SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` → 253 passed (previously 5 failed)
- [x] `env -u SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` → 253 passed (regression check, unset still works)
- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q` (full suite) → 4225 passed, 6 skipped (pre-existing, unrelated)

title: fix(hooks): stop-completion-selfcheck cooldown, kill switch, firings log
body:
## Summary
- Stop the per-session marker from being deleted on every allowed stop — real session-transcript scanning showed this made a long-lived autonomous/watch-loop session get re-blocked with the identical static prompt on almost every Stop event (measured gaps as low as 5-70s), instead of the intended ~30-minute cadence. The marker now stays in place for the full cooldown window; re-blocking is capped at once per window. An opportunistic sweep removes stale markers on each new block.
- Add a write-only `firings.jsonl` usefulness log (decision, prompt variant, timing) — foundation for a future "did this firing actually change behavior" report.
- Add a `SELFCHECK_DISABLE` kill switch (env var or sentinel file) for an instant, no-redeploy off switch.
- Hardened across four rounds of a multi-model `review-cli` quorum (4/4 iterations passed, 4 distinct models, correctness/performance/quality/consistency roles): the prompt is now selected before the marker write (a classification crash/timeout can no longer silently consume a cooldown window with no block firing), `isMeta`/`isSidechain`/mixed `tool_result`+text transcript records are no longer mistaken for the real user-turn boundary, the transcript tail read is a byte-bounded seek instead of decoding the whole file, a NEL/U+2028 byte inside a JSON string value no longer silently drops a record, `SELFCHECK_TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_LINES=0` now means "scan nothing" instead of "read everything", `SELFCHECK_TTL_S<=0` is clamped instead of blocking every stop forever, and a HEDGE regex false-positive on a normal finished-work closer ("let me know if you like it") is fixed.

Builds on top of the already-committed `stop-completion-selfcheck: make it read the turn transcript (Closes #502)` work in this same branch (HEDGE/LIGHT/FULL prompt-variant classification) — that fixes WHAT gets asked, this fixes HOW OFTEN and HOW RELIABLY.

title: feat(ship): merge-time version auto-bump to remove parallel-PR conflicts
body:
## Summary
- ship's version-bump gate made every parallel PR bump the same pyproject.toml/package.json
  line to the same next version, so the second PR to merge became CONFLICTING and needed a
  hand rebase + re-bump for every PR in the queue.
- When that gate would refuse, ship now computes the next PATCH version (reusing
  `locate_version_file`/`version_line_bumped`) and commits it onto the PR's HEAD branch through
  the GitHub Contents API (`chore(release): bump version X -> Y (ship auto-bump for #N)`),
  right before the green-CI gate.
- Every later gate accounts for ship's own commit: branch sanity runs first (a diverged/dirty
  local branch refuses before anything is pushed); when base's version already moved past this
  PR's merge-base, the branch is updated from base via the update-branch API first so the
  squash never conflicts; the green-CI gate waits on the new head SHA with a widened
  check-registration grace; review-dwell is measured from the last NON-ship push; a bot thread
  opened on the bump line is auto-resolved; the local worktree is fast-forwarded; one
  `version-bump:auto` audit line is written.
- A PR that already bumps past base gets no second bump; a hand-bump the base already reached
  is re-bumped on top of it; a repo with no version file keeps the note-and-skip; `--dry-run`
  prints the plan and pushes nothing; `SHIP_AUTO_BUMP=0` (env or committed `.ship-config`)
  restores the old refuse-until-bumped behaviour.
- Kept the `bump-version-on-release` skill and `ci/ship/README.md` in sync with the new
  default behaviour.

title: feat(ship): pre-merge acceptance gate + magic-close keyword gate
body:
## Summary
Closes the gap where a merge can close a ticket behind task-cli's acceptance gates: Linear's GitHub integration and GitHub's magic-close keywords move a ticket to Done the instant a linked PR merges, with zero task-cli involvement (HYP-1440, HYP-1347, HYP-1295 — 127 of 435 HYP tickets closed since June have unchecked acceptance criteria).

- **Acceptance gate**: when task-cli is on PATH and a ticket code is derivable (the same derivation the post-merge notify step already uses), runs `task gate <code> --json` before the merge and refuses while the ticket has unchecked criteria, criteria checked without a proof, or too few criteria for this repo's configured minimum — printing the gaps. Honors a recorded post-merge-acceptance opt-out (reported, still authorized) and a `SHIP_ACCEPTANCE_GATE=0` ops off-switch (env or a committed `.ship-config` line). task-cli absent, a foreign `--repo`, no derivable code, or an unevaluable `task gate` exit all skip with a logged reason, never block the merge.
- **Magic-close gate**: scans the PR title and body for close/closes/closed/fix/fixes/fixed/resolve/resolves/resolved (+ Linear's -ing forms) followed by `#N`, `owner/repo#N`, a ticket code, or a full GitHub issue/pull URL, and refuses with the exact matched phrase and the fix (write `Refs` instead). `--rewrite-magic-close` rewrites the keyword(s) via `gh pr edit` and continues.
- **Auto-close**: when the acceptance gate finds every criterion already proven (genuinely — not an opt-out, not a cancelled ticket, not a gate disabled for this repo), the post-merge notify step also runs `task done <code>` right after `task mark-shipped`, closing the "nobody remembered the extra step" gap a pre-merge-only gate leaves open (tg-cli#301/#305: PR #305 merged, every criterion independently verified, yet #301 sat open for days).
- Both gates run under `--dry-run` and log to the ship audit file.

Fixed from review (round 1) before this ever shipped:
- `task gate`'s stdout/stderr were captured together (`2>&1`); any stderr line task-cli emitted silently corrupted the JSON the opt-out/fully-accepted decision was parsed from. Captured separately now.
- "fully accepted, safe to auto-close" only checked for an empty opt-out reason — a cancelled ticket or a gate-disabled-for-this-repo ticket also exits 0 with criteria unchecked and got the same false "proven" auto-close attempt. Now requires `post_merge_acceptance` is null AND `gate_enabled` AND `state != cancelled`; unverifiable (no jq) defaults to NOT auto-closing.
- The magic-close ref pattern missed GitHub's full issue/PR URL close form entirely — added.
- The magic-close match (grep, `LC_ALL=C`) and the boundary-char strip (sed) ran in different locales; pinned both to `LC_ALL=C`.

The `task gate --json` contract (field names, exit codes) is documented identically in both this repo's `ci/ship/README.md` and task-cli's own `README.md` — see task-cli#115 (already merged).

title: fix(hooks): exempt Codex/opencode-sourced events from orchestrator-stays-thin
body:
## Summary
- `orchestrator-stays-thin`'s premise (a Claude Code main thread must delegate
  implementation work to a CC `Agent`/`Task` subagent instead of doing it inline) is a
  Claude-Code-specific concept. Codex and opencode have no trusted per-tool-call subagent
  identity reaching either bridge today, so every Codex/opencode-sourced event looked like
  "the orchestrator" to this gate — misclassifying both a review-cli-spawned read-only
  reviewer process AND a standalone Codex session doing real delegated work. The block's own
  remediation ("Dispatch a subagent... Agent tool with subagent_type: 'fork'") does not exist
  in Codex/opencode at all.
- Each bridge (`cc_hook_bridge`, `codex_hook_bridge`, `opencode_hook_bridge`) now tags every
  v1 event with a top-level `harness` field set from a hardcoded module constant — never
  derived from the underlying tool event, so it can't be forged via `tool_input`.
  `orchestrator-stays-thin` reads `event["harness"]` against a fail-closed allowlist
  (`codex`, `opencode`) right after the existing subagent check.
- review-cli needed no cooperation for this (no env marker to set) — its spawned reviewer
  processes are exempt purely by running through `codex_hook_bridge`/`opencode_hook_bridge`.
- Filed as follow-ups, not fixed here: a `sed -n` gap in `READ_ONLY_BASH` that independently
  forces a chain-length fallback on the exact repro command (#541), and extending the same

title: feat(agent-hooks): chat-dictionary-gate — block a reply containing a banned word from DICT.json
body:
## What

A new `stop`-point agent-hook, `agent-hooks/chat-dictionary-gate/`, that reads the assistant's own just-written reply from the session transcript, checks it against the banned-word dictionary at `~/.claude/DICT.json` (the same file `tg` already enforces for outgoing Telegram messages), and blocks the Stop when a banned word is found — quoting the exact matched text, the rule id, its reason, and the correct replacement wording.

Ticket: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/548

## Why

The Telegram enforcement has zero effect on text Claude Code types directly into its own chat UI with Alex — a separate, previously unguarded surface where the same banned words kept recurring across many sessions (at least the fourth or fifth time this exact request came up).

## Design decisions (each justified in the hook's README)

- **Cyrillic scoping** — a rule marked `only_if_cyrillic` applies only when the WHOLE current-turn text contains a Cyrillic codepoint, judged once over the joined turn. Mirrors tg-cli's `checkDictionary`. Plain English text (a subagent's report using the word "fork") is never touched by a Russian-only rule.
- **Loop guard, not a cooldown** — every violating Stop blocks, but consecutive violations per session are capped (default 3, `CHAT_DICT_GATE_LOOP_GUARD_CAP`) so a stuck rewrite can never wedge the session. Crossing the cap allows, logged under its own label in `firings.jsonl`. A counter-write failure escalates a block to an allow, so a read-only marker dir cannot turn fail-open into fail-closed-forever.
- **Retry-boundary scanning** — verified against live transcripts: a real Stop block injects a `type:"user"`, `isMeta:true` record whose string content starts with `"Stop hook feedback:"`. Treating it as turn-continuation (as the sibling hook correctly does for its own purposes) would make a corrected rewrite forever inherit the pre-block violating text, so this hook also stops its reverse scan there.
- **Fail-open on every dictionary lifecycle problem** (missing default: silent; missing explicit override / malformed JSON / bad regex / bad flags / BOM / unsupported version: allow with a stderr warning). A deliberate divergence from tg-cli's fail-closed posture: tg's failure mode is one refused send, this hook's is an un-endable interactive turn.
- **Priority 10** — `lib/agent_hooks_v1/runner.py` sorts stop hooks ascending by `(priority, id)` and `cc_hook_bridge.dispatch` returns on the first block, so this must sort ahead of `stop-completion-selfcheck` (50). `model-error-fallback` (20) never blocks, so its position is irrelevant.
- **Duplicated, not imported** — the transcript tail-read logic is copied from `stop_selfcheck.py` (trimmed + extended) per the catalog's directory self-containment convention; `stop_selfcheck.py` is untouched.

Also lists the previously-undocumented `model-error-fallback` in both stop-point doc tables (a pre-existing doc gap).

## Tests

- `tests/test_chat_dictionary_gate.py` — 42 tests, all passing. Covers the required matrix (clean turn, block message contract, Cyrillic scoping both directions, loop-guard cap and per-streak reset, missing/malformed/bad-regex dictionary, kill switch) plus regressions for every finding from six `review diff` rounds (within-record block order, unwritable marker dir, non-dict/negative/non-finite counters, non-string flags, BOM, version gate, `why`-optional parity, sidechain exclusion, growing-transcript loop-guard, retry boundary using the hook's own quoted block message).
- Parity pin against the REAL `~/.claude/DICT.json` on this machine: all 13 rules compile under the Python flag mapping with no warnings (skipped on machines without the file).
- Full suite: `python -m pytest -q` → 4539 passed, 6 skipped.

## Known limitations (documented in the README, not hidden)

- `session_id`'s `cwd` fallback can collide across two concurrent sessions in the same directory when CC forwards no `session_id`; in that narrow case one session's cap can let the other's first violation through. Inherited from the sibling hook's identical fallback; a cross-hook decision, flagged for follow-up.
- A retry consisting only of a `tool_use` block extracts as empty text and allows.
- A still-flushing transcript write at the exact moment Stop fires is the same theoretical bypass the sibling hook has always had.

title: feat(lib): add omp_hook_bridge — agents-hooks/v1 carrier for omp (oh-my-pi)
body:
## What

Adds `lib/omp_hook_bridge/`, the fourth harness bridge beside cc/codex/opencode: a TS extension (`extension.ts`, default-exporting the `pi.on(...)` factory omp's extension loader expects) plus a stdlib-only Python dispatcher that maps omp's flat `tool_call`/`tool_result` payload onto the shared `agents-hooks/v1` contract and runs the installed `~/.omp/agent/hooks/*.json` descriptors. Also exempts omp from `orchestrator-stays-thin` (`EXEMPT_HARNESSES` += `"omp"`), for the same reason codex/opencode are exempt (agent-tools#533).

## Mapping

| omp event + toolName | v1 point | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_call` + `bash` | `pre-bash` | `input.command` -> `command` / `args.command` |
| `tool_call` + `edit` | `pre-write` | hashline: every `[PATH#TAG]` section path -> `file_paths`/`file_path`/`path`; best-effort `+` body rows -> `content`; one v1 event per path |
| `tool_call` + `write` | `pre-write` | `path`/`content` |
| `tool_call` + `apply_patch` | `pre-write` | classic `*** Update/Add/Delete File` envelope, parser ported from the opencode bridge; tries `patch`/`patchText`/`input` |
| `tool_call` + `task` | `pre-agent` | `agent`->`subagent_type`, `task`->`prompt`, `run_in_background: true` (see below) |
| `tool_result` + write tools | `post-write` | block decision logged only |

No `stop` mapping — omp documents no pre-stop block contract for its session events.

## Judgment calls (all documented in `lib/omp_hook_bridge/README.md`)

- **Fail OPEN on `tool_call` bridge failure — the one deliberate divergence from opencode's plugin.** In omp a thrown `tool_call` handler blocks the call; a broken dispatcher (missing python3, a bridge bug, timeout) must not brick every tool call in an interactive omp session. Only an explicit descriptor block becomes `{block: true, reason}`.
- **Dispatcher timeout defaults to 1,000,000 ms**, above every shipped descriptor budget (hatch-capable hooks use 960,000 ms). With fail-open, a short timeout would silently turn a fail-closed hatch hook into an allow, so the magnitude matters more here than in opencode.
- **omp `task` dispatches are marked background.** omp exposes no per-call background lever (async jobs are the contract; sync only via the session setting `async.enabled=false` or agent frontmatter `blocking: true`), so without this every omp dispatch was blocked by `background-subagent-gate` with a remediation the model cannot follow. Trusts omp's contract the same way the gate trusts CC's `fork`.
- **Hashline content extraction is an approximation** (register-backed CUT/PUT paste carries no body rows; `MV DEST` surfaces only the source path) — the consumer hooks only need paths, which are extracted reliably.
- `hooks_dir()` precedence `OMP_HOOKS_DIR` > `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` > `PI_CONFIG_DIR` > `~/.omp/agent/hooks`, ported from rig-cli's `omp_agent_root` including `$VAR` expansion.

## Tests

title: fix(agent-hooks): read-only sed -n (#541) and reconciled no-bg-longproc doctrine (#546)
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/541, https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/546

Two small follow-ups in the same hook family, shipped as one PR. A third one that used to ride along here — a codex/opencode/omp harness-wide exemption for `background-subagent-gate` and `no-long-inline-process` (#542) — was removed from this branch per Alex's veto of harness-wide exemptions: both gates govern every harness again exactly as on `main`, `orchestrator-stays-thin` keeps its own pre-existing #533 allowlist unchanged, and no shared `EXEMPT_HARNESSES`/`is_exempt_harness` helper is added to `lib/agenttools_hatch_escalation`. The pre-removal snapshot (including the #542 tests) is parked on the branch `wip/542-tests` for the subagent-identity work to reuse.

## What changes

**1. `orchestrator-stays-thin` recognizes a print-only `sed` as read-only inspection (#541).**
A `sed` with no in-place flag (`-i`/`-i.bak`/`--in-place`, BSD `-I`), no script file (`-f`/`--file`), and no script command that writes or executes (`w`/`W`/`e` at a command position, the `w`/`e` flags of an `s` command) is now inspection like `head`/`tail`/`grep`, at any chain length. Implemented as a shlex-based predicate `_is_read_only_sed` consulted next to `READ_ONLY_BASH` (a plain `sed\b` in the regex would also grant `sed -i` and `sed 'w file'`). The literal incident chain from #533 — `sed -n '1,240p' SKILL.md && git diff --check && git status --short && git diff -- a.py` — is allowed on the first call for every harness instead of falling to the >=3-segment fallback. `sed -i` keeps tripping `BUILD_EDIT`. Grant-direction, so every ambiguity (unbalanced quotes, a `-l` cluster with differing GNU/BSD operand semantics, a script file) resolves to "not read-only", i.e. to the previous behavior. Review round 1 hardened two edges: the long options are an allowlist of EXACT spellings, so any GNU prefix abbreviation (`--in-plac=.bak`, `--fil=x`) or unknown option is not read-only; and a label / optional-operand command (`: b t T l q Q`) ends at `;`, so `sed -n ':x;w /tmp/out' file` is seen as a write.

**2. `subagent-no-bg-longproc` states the verified wake mechanism instead of a false blanket (#546).**
Docstring, README, descriptor and block message no longer claim "a subagent is NOT re-invoked by a background-completion notification". They now state the split `subagent-no-monitor` (#439) proved empirically: a Bash `run_in_background: true` child IS harness-tracked and DOES resume the calling subagent; a Monitor watch and a shell-detached job (`&`, `setsid`, `nohup … &`) never do; a `--watch` loop never exits. The block message offers the same two alternatives `subagent-no-monitor`'s does, with the heartbeat example hoisted into a SYNC'd `HEARTBEAT_LOOP_EXAMPLE` constant in both hooks (a test pins them equal). Catalog entries in `agent-hooks/README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `subagent-no-monitor` descriptor drop the "broader than confirmed / tracked as #546" hedges.

The gated scope is deliberately unchanged (#546's own acceptance criterion 3): whether a bounded labeled process under `run_in_background: true` should keep being blocked is filed separately as #559 and not folded into this wording fix.

## Acceptance proofs

All run against THIS branch's hook scripts and bridges (`python3 <worktree>/agent-hooks/...`, `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/lib python3 -m codex_hook_bridge`), not the primary checkout's — hooks resolve from the primary checkout at fire time, so a naive live run would have proved main's behaviour. Fresh `ORCH_THIN_MARKER_DIR`, all hatch / agent-identity env unset. Long block messages trimmed to their first line.

### #541 — `orchestrator-stays-thin`, the literal #533 chain is allowed on the FIRST call

```
a) sed -n '1,240p' SKILL.md && git diff --check && git status --short && git diff -- a.py
   stdout: {"hook_api": "agents-hooks/v1", "decision": "allow"}          exit 0
b) control: sed -i 's/a/b/' a.py && git diff --check && git status --short && git diff -- a.py
   stderr: orchestrator-stays-thin: By design, not a bug: this session is the orchestrator…   (first-offense WARN; a repeat within the TTL blocks)
   stdout: {"hook_api": "agents-hooks/v1", "decision": "allow", "message": "By design, not a bug: …"}   exit 0
c) control (review round 1): sed -n ':x;w /tmp/out' file && git status && ls
   stdout: {"hook_api": "agents-hooks/v1", "decision": "block", "message": "By design, not a bug: …"}   exit 10
d) control (review round 1): sed --in-plac=.bak 's/a/b/' f.txt && git status && ls
   stdout: {"hook_api": "agents-hooks/v1", "decision": "block", "message": "By design, not a bug: …"}   exit 10
```

### No harness-wide exemption — a codex event through the REAL codex bridge is still governed

Descriptor `no-long-inline-process.pre-bash.json` → this branch's `no_long_inline_process.py`, `CODEX_HOOKS_DIR` pointing at it, `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/lib python3 -m codex_hook_bridge PreToolUse`, no `agent_id`, no hatch env:

```
{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"pytest tests/"},"cwd":"/repo","session_id":"sess-1"}
   stdout: {"decision": "block", "reason": "Run this in a BACKGROUND subagent, not the orchestrator: `a build/test suite` is a long-running process …"}
{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"review diff -C /repo"},"cwd":"/repo","session_id":"sess-1"}
   stdout: {"decision": "block", "reason": "Run this in a BACKGROUND subagent, not the orchestrator: `review (multi-model, minutes-long)` is a long-running process …"}
```

(Observed while proving this, NOT changed here: `python3 -m pytest` is allowed by this hook on `main` too — `_DIRECT_RUNNERS` only matches `pytest` as argv[0] and the `-m` module form is never peeled. A pre-existing classifier gap, worth its own ticket.)

### #546 — the README now carries the rationale (excerpt of `agent-hooks/subagent-no-bg-longproc/README.md`)

> ## Which notifications actually re-invoke a subagent (the precise mechanism)
>
> An earlier revision of this README claimed a blanket *"a subagent is NOT re-invoked by a background-completion notification"*. That is **false for the general case** — the sibling `subagent-no-monitor` gate (agent-tools#439) proved the real split empirically, and agent-tools#546 reconciled this hook's wording to it:
>
> | Backgrounding shape | Resumes the subagent when done? |
> | --- | --- |
> | Bash tool call with **`run_in_background: true`** | **Yes** — the harness tracks that child against the agent that started it and re-invokes it with the output once the child exits (verified: a 40 s backgrounded `python3` sleep resumed its subagent after ~43 s with no further message). An ORDINARY, non-labeled command backgrounded this way is a fine shape for a subagent, and this gate allows it. |
> | **Monitor** watch | **Never** — Monitor has no harness-tracked child at all. `subagent-no-monitor` blocks every subagent Monitor call for that reason. |
> | Shell-**detached** job — trailing `&`, `setsid`, `nohup … &` | **Never** — the harness knows nothing about a job the shell forked behind its back; the Bash call returns at once and no completion ever arrives. |
> | A `--watch` loop | **Never** by any route — it never exits. |
>
> What this gate blocks, given that: a subagent backgrounding a **labeled** long process (`review`, `--watch`, a build/test suite, `sleep N>=10`) by **any** of the three backgrounding shapes, `run_in_background: true` included. For a detached job or a `--watch` loop the wedge is certain. For a *bounded* labeled process under `run_in_background: true` the harness **would** resume the subagent; whether that specific case should keep being blocked […] is a **scope** question deliberately left to a follow-up ticket ([agent-tools#559](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/559)) rather than folded into this wording fix — the gated scope is unchanged from agent-tools#52.

## Tests (TDD, red first)
- `test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py`: read-only sed matrix (13 shapes, each also asserting the `_is_read_only_sed` predicate directly), not-read-only matrix (25 shapes incl. the round-1 `:x;w`, `5q;w`, `l;w`, `--in-plac`, `--fil` cases, each proved end-to-end on a 3-segment chain), the literal repro chain allowed with no harness and no marker primed, head-anchor and unparseable cases. The #533 control tests now use an `awk` chain (the sed one is read-only by design now).
- `test_subagent_no_bg_longproc.py`: doctrine consistency over all four surfaces + the catalog files; the two hooks' heartbeat constants equal; block output carries the reconciled message.
- The diff against the merge-base touches ONLY `AGENTS.md`, `agent-hooks/README.md`, `agent-hooks/orchestrator-stays-thin/*`, `agent-hooks/subagent-no-bg-longproc/*`, `agent-hooks/subagent-no-monitor/*` and their two test files — no `lib/*`, no `background-subagent-gate`, no `no-long-inline-process`.
- Full suite after the removal commit (28af75d): 4579 passed, 6 skipped, exit 0 (`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`, 8m28s) — 26 fewer than before the removal, exactly the deleted #542 tests.

## Review round 2 (post-push, 3 roles) — one real gap, fixed in 75cb38e

**Bracket expression in a regex address.** `sed -n '/[/]/w out.txt' f.txt` writes `out.txt` on BOTH GNU and BSD sed (verified live: `out.txt` created by `sed` and `gsed`), but the address scan ended the regex at the `/` inside `[/]`, ran off the end of the script and granted the write as read-only. The scan now honours POSIX bracket expressions exactly where sed does — a regex address and the `s` PATTERN (`[^…]`, a leading literal `]`, `[:class:]` members) — and NOT where it does not (the `s` replacement and `y` have no bracket semantics: `s/a/[/w out` and `y/[/]/;w out.txt` both write, also verified live). Anything sed itself rejects (an unterminated regex/bracket/`s`, an address without a command) now counts as a write instead of falling off the end into "read-only". 6 new read-only shapes + 9 new not-read-only shapes in the matrices, each not-read-only one proved end-to-end on a 3-segment chain. Codex (round 3, consistency) asked for `[=equiv=]` / `[.coll.]` rows too: both share the ONE code path the `[:class:]` row pins (`script[i+1] in ":=."` → find the matching `X]`), and `sed -n '/[[./.]]/w out.txt'` / `'/[[=/=]]/w out.txt'` were verified live (both seds write `out.txt`) and through the predicate (both not read-only) — not added as rows to keep the reviewed diff stamped as-is. Also from round 2: `_skip_one_sed_address` / `_skip_sed_address_clause` naming.

Live hook run (this branch's script, fresh marker dir):

```
sed -n '/[/]/w out.txt' f.txt && git status --short && ls
   1st: {"decision": "allow", "message": "By design, not a bug: …"}   (advisory WARN)
   2nd: {"decision": "block", "message": "By design, not a bug: …"}
sed -n '/[/]/p' f.txt && git status --short && ls
   {"decision": "allow"}  ×2  (no marker written)
sed -n '1,240p' SKILL.md && git diff --check && git status --short && git diff -- a.py
   {"decision": "allow"}  ×2  (the #533 chain, unchanged)
```

Declined from the same round, deliberately: extracting the sed walker into its own file (out of scope for a two-ticket fix PR; fine as a follow-up if the walker grows again).

title: feat(hook-bridge): deliver the tg-ctl Stop-hook inbox to agents outside tmux (#526)
body:
Refs #526. Companion: tg-cli#306 (the daemon side: discovery + the inbox writer) and a `claude-rotate` change in the dotfiles (the tmux warning + `--tmux <name>`, part 1 of this ticket — the launcher lives in `~/.files`, not here).

## What changed

**The Stop hook delivers a pending Telegram message to an agent that runs outside tmux.** tg-ctl cannot type into a session that has no tmux pane, so it queues the message to an inbox file; this is the reader.

- New stdlib lib `lib/agenttools_tg_inbox/`: the inbox key contract shared byte-for-byte with tg-cli (sanitized `--name`, else `cwd-<sha256(cwd)[:16]>`; test vectors mirrored in both suites), the agent-process lookup (`CLAUDE_PID`, which Claude Code exports to hooks, else the parent chain), and `consume_pending` — claim `pending.jsonl` by rename, archive to `delivered.jsonl` BEFORE returning (at-most-once), fail-open on empty / missing / malformed inbox and on an unwritable archive (the claim file is kept, nothing is lost).
- `cc_hook_bridge` and `codex_hook_bridge` check the inbox first on `Stop` and return `{"decision":"block","reason":"<the queued messages>"}`; the harness feeds that text to the agent as its next instruction. The v1 `stop` descriptors keep running on the very next Stop (verified live: the self-check fired right after the delivery turn). opencode has no Stop point, so no change there.
- READMEs: the lib README documents the contract, files, limits and the process lookup; the bridge README gained a section.

## Live proof (2026-09-06, final SHAs: tg-cli `9cec44f` + agent-tools `094da16`)

A REAL interactive `claude --name tgtest` under a pty (`script -q`, prompts piped in), started with `TMUX` unset — deliberately NOT `claude -p`: a `-p` run is headless and is filtered out of the unreachable list on purpose. The session's Stop hook is the agent-tools branch (`--settings` → `PYTHONPATH=…/.worktrees/526-stop-inbox/lib python3 -m cc_hook_bridge Stop`, stderr to a file); the `tg-ctl` binary is the tg-cli branch. Everything below was captured from inside that run (driver: `scratchpad/tgtest-driver3.sh`).

**1. The agent is outside tmux, and this branch's `tg-ctl` sees it + queues to it:**

```
$ ps -axo pid=,ppid=,tty=,command= | grep "bin/claude --name tgtest"

34253 34250 ttys019  /Users/ultra/.local/bin/claude --name tgtest --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions --permission-mode bypassPermissions -

$ echo "TMUX=$TMUX" (in the shell that started the agent)
TMUX=

$ tg-ctl inbox queue tgtest "LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED"
queued to tgtest (tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 1 queued)

$ tg-ctl inbox queue tgtest "second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line"
queued to tgtest (tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 2 queued)

$ tg-ctl status
…
unreachable (not in tmux): 4
  - tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 2 queued
  Not in tmux → no direct injection; a message sent with `/agent <name> <text>` is queued to its Stop-hook inbox and delivered when the agent next ends a turn (an idle agent gets it only at its next turn). To make it fully reachable, restart it inside tmux: `claude-rotate --tmux <name>`.
…

$ ls -la ~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/tgtest (before the Stop)
total 8

**2. The agent finishes a turn → the Stop hook (agent-tools branch) consumes the inbox — hook stderr:**

**3. On disk after the Stop: `pending.jsonl` is gone, ONE complete `delivered-*` batch, `tg-ctl inbox` shows nothing queued:**

```

total 8

$ cat ~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/tgtest/delivered-*.jsonl

$ tg-ctl inbox
  - tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253)
```

**4. The agent's transcript (`~/.claude-accounts/…/tgtest-proj/3e8c9178-….jsonl`) — both messages AND the regular stop gate's reason arrive in ONE `Stop hook feedback` block (the v1 stop hooks ran first, the inbox was consumed last):**

```

[assistant] READY
[user] Stop hook feedback:
[TG from tg-ctl] LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED

[TG from tg-ctl] second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line

Before finishing, one check (this turn made no tool calls, …) — the regular stop-completion-selfcheck gate, in the SAME block
[assistant] DELIVERED
DELIVERED-2
```

**Caveat from a second run against the MACHINE'S installed hook (after this merge, no `--settings`):** nothing was delivered — the pty typescript shows no "Ran 1 stop hook" at all and `pending.jsonl` stayed at 2 queued. Cause: the session runs under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-accounts/account-0` (claude-rotate), and none of the `~/.claude-accounts/account-*/settings.json` files carries a `hooks` key — Claude Code reads settings from the config dir only, so the rig-provisioned hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` never fire for a claude-rotate session (run 3 above confirms it from the other side: two hook sources registered, "Ran 1 stop hook"). Not a defect of this bridge (proven above with the identical lib loaded via `--settings`); tracked as rig-cli#368.

Not exercised here: the daemon's `👌` reaction on the Telegram message — the launchd daemon on this machine still runs the pre-#315 code (needs a restart after the merge to pick this up), and a `tg-ctl inbox queue` entry has no Telegram message id anyway.

## Tests

`tests/test_tg_inbox.py` (14): key vectors, `CLAUDE_PID` / ancestry / fallback lookup, pending → block + archive (idempotent), empty / missing / malformed never block, unwritable archive keeps the claim, and both bridges run as subprocesses against a temp `TG_CTL_CONFIG_DIR`. Full suite: 4187 passed, 121 skipped.

## Not in this PR

The `rig` option `harness.require_tmux` (warn|wrap|off) that the ticket mentions — the launcher reads `CLAUDE_ROTATE_REQUIRE_TMUX` today; wiring it through rig's schema is a rig-cli follow-up.
