title: fix(ship): derive the task code from a same-repo issue URL (and Linear URL)
body:
Refs [#564](https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/564)

## The problem — two gates that contradicted each other

`gh ship`'s review-quorum gate derives the PR's ticket code from the branch name, then
the PR body. It recognized bare forms only: a Linear-style `TEAM-<n>` code, a descriptive ALL-CAPS
code, or a keyword-anchored bare reference such as `Refs` followed by `#548` (PR #511). But task-cli's own `links` gate REQUIRES a ticket
to be referenced as a markdown link / full URL — never a bare `#548`. So a PR body written
correctly for task-cli carried no shape ship's matcher recognized, and ship refused it with
`could not derive a task code`. Two agents hit this today and worked around it by hand-setting
`REVIEW_TASK_CODE` — the manual step that gets forgotten, at which point the gate is
back to refusing.

## The fix

A LAST-fallback arm in `_review_quorum_extract_ticket`: a full GitHub issue URL of the PR's
**own** repo yields the same literal `#<n>` the anchored `Refs #<n>` arm yields (PR #511), so
review-cli's quorum record and task-cli's routing see ONE code regardless of body syntax.
Bare, markdown-linked, `www.` host and a trailing `#issuecomment-…` anchor all work; no keyword
anchor is required (the links gate's own output is `Refs [#548](https://…)`, where the `[` sits
between any keyword and the URL, so demanding an anchor would defeat the purpose).

Fail-closed rules, mirroring the keyword arm's hazards:

- The URL's `owner/repo` must equal the PR's own repo (compared case-insensitively). A link to
  **another** repo's issue is never this PR's ticket — cross-repo companion links are routine in
  this ecosystem, and deriving one would query the wrong quorum record and later mark the wrong
  issue shipped.
- Only `/issues/<n>` counts. A `/pull/<n>` link is a pull request, not a ticket.
- Two DISTINCT same-repo issue URLs are ambiguous and derive nothing. The same issue linked
  twice is one ticket.
- An unknown own-repo (no GitHub origin, no `--repo`, no PR URL) derives nothing — "same repo"
  is unverifiable, so the gate refuses rather than guessing.

`_ship_own_repo_slugs` resolves the PR's own repo once per run as a SET of slugs: the explicit
`gh` target (`GH_REPO`, so a foreign `--repo` ship compares against the TARGET repo, not this
checkout), this checkout's GitHub origin, AND the live PR URL (`gh pr view --json url`). All
three are kept rather than first-non-empty (Codex review finding on this PR): after a repository
rename/transfer an existing clone keeps the OLD, redirecting origin slug while the live PR and
its issue links carry the NEW one, so trusting the origin alone would classify a correct
same-repo link as foreign and refuse. GitHub redirects the old slug to the same repository, so an
issue URL under either slug is this PR's own; the same issue linked under both slugs is still one
ticket. The live lookup costs one `gh` call, only on the URL path.

A Linear issue URL (`https://linear.app/<team>/issue/<TEAM-n>/<slug>`) carries the code in its
path and was already derived by the existing `HYP-<n>` / `PREFIX-<n>` arms — pinned with a test rather than
changed, so both URL forms task-cli's links gate demands stay covered end to end.

The magic-close gate (PR #540) is untouched and still correct: `Refs <full-url>` remains a
non-closing reference, while `Closes <full-url>` is still refused. Post-merge notify (PR #534)
still passes the literal `#<n>` to `task mark-shipped`.

## Dogfood

This PR's own body references its ticket **only** as the full-URL markdown link at the top —
there is deliberately no keyword-anchored bare-number reference to it anywhere in this text, so
the code ship derives can only have come from the new URL arm. Ship's own derivation log line is
pasted below and into the ticket as the acceptance proof.

## Tests (TDD, red-first)

`tests/test_ship.py` — same-repo URL (bare / markdown / `www.` + comment anchor / duplicated)
derives `#548`; another repo's issue, a same-owner different-repo issue, a `/pull/<n>` link, two
distinct same-repo issues, a non-GitHub host and a non-issue GitHub path all derive nothing; an
unknown own-repo fails closed; an explicit keyword-anchored bare reference (`Refs` + `#12`) still wins over a URL elsewhere in the body;
Linear URLs derive their `TEAM-<n>` code (both the HYP team prefix and a generic prefix).

(Example codes above are written as placeholders on purpose: ship's matcher reads this very
body, so a literal example code would be derived instead of the URL-linked ticket.)

`tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py` — a URL-derived code reaches `task mark-shipped '#105'`
literally; another repo's issue URL calls `task` not at all.

`tests/test_ship_ticket_gates.py` — the pre-merge acceptance gate gates on the URL-derived
`#115`; `Refs <full-url>` and `Refs [#115](<full-url>)` are confirmed NOT magic-close keywords.

A second commit adds `|| true` to the new `grep -c` (a review finding: `grep -c` exits 1 on a
zero count, which under this script's `set -euo pipefail` is exactly the URL-only path this
change serves; verified in isolation that the unguarded form aborts the shell). A third commit adds the slug-set
resolver described above plus two function-level tests (a stale-origin clone derives the ticket
from a new-slug URL; the origin slug still works when the `gh` URL lookup fails offline).

Red-check: the four positive derivation tests fail against `origin/main`'s `ship.sh` and pass
with this change. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py
tests/test_ship_ticket_gates.py -q` → 353 passed.

### Derivation proof

Ship's own log line from the real (non-dry-run) merge of this PR, showing the code derived from
the full issue URL above:

```
[ship] AUTHORITY CONFIRMED — review quorum met: 3 iterations across 3 roles for #564. Self-merge authorized by the review-quorum gate.
[ship] magic-close gate: no close/fix/resolve keyword targets an issue or ticket in #566's title/body/commits.
```

(Real `gh ship 566` run, no `REVIEW_TASK_CODE` in the environment, branch `fix/ship-url-task-code` carries no code — the only source for `#564` is the full issue URL at the top of this body. The second line is the magic-close gate accepting `Refs <url>` as a non-closing reference.)

title: fix(ship): validate the derived task code against task-cli's id grammar
body:
## What

`ci/ship/ship.sh`'s acceptance gate is a **merge gate**, so what it hands `task gate` has to be a ticket. The shape check was `_ship_looks_like_a_ticket_id` = "contains a digit", which is not a shape at all — it admitted codes task-cli can only 404 on.

This replaces it with task-cli's own id grammar (`tasklib/cli.py::_route_id_to_project`): `#<n>`, a bare `<n>`, or one alphanumeric team prefix + `-` + digits. It also rejects a candidate that names **the pull request under ship**, in all three spellings. Both rules go through a single `_ship_task_code_candidate_ok`, so all four candidate sources apply them identically, and a rejected candidate still falls through to the next source.

## Why — two classes reached the gate on 2026-09-06

Evidence from `~/.config/agent-tools/ship-audit.jsonl`:

**1. review-cli CHECK codes — the gate failed OPEN.** A review check code is a different entity from a ticket. Each carries digits, so each passed the old check; `task gate` 404s → exit 2 → the gate logs "could not evaluate" and **skips**:

```
{"pr":"349","gate":"acceptance","decision":"skipped","task_code":"rig-cli-341","detail":"could not evaluate: exit 2"}
{"pr":"556","gate":"acceptance","decision":"skipped","task_code":"rig-cli-342","detail":"could not evaluate: exit 2"}
{"pr":"352","gate":"acceptance","decision":"skipped","task_code":"rig-cli-342","detail":"could not evaluate: exit 2"}
{"pr":"497","gate":"acceptance","decision":"skipped","task_code":"OC476-OPENCODE-BACKGROUND-TRUTH","detail":"could not evaluate: exit 2"}
```

Four merges shipped with the acceptance gate never actually running — it failed open on exactly the input it exists to reject.

**2. The PR's own number — the gate judged the wrong ticket.** PR #499 carried its real ticket (#495) in **both** its branch (`495-opencode-task-gate`) and its title (`… (#495)`), but a `GH-499` reuse won the first candidate slot. The gate judged issue #499 — unrelated, zero criteria — and refused. The merge was unblocked only by recording a **false** post-merge-acceptance opt-out on #499, which is still on that issue.

## Reproduction (before)

```
$ task gate rig-cli-342 --json   ; echo $?
error: github: HTTP 404 … /issues/rig-cli-342
2
$ task gate '#499' --json | jq '.criteria, .below_minimum'
0
true
```

## Tests — red first

New coverage in `tests/test_ship_ticket_gates.py` (fake-`gh` + fake-`task` harness, no network): a review check code, a descriptive review code carrying digits, and the PR number in all three spellings (`GH-1`, `#1`, bare `1`) each fall through to the body's real ticket; with nothing else derivable the gate reports an honest "no task code" skip rather than gating the PR against itself; a bare issue number is still accepted.

Two tests in `tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py` encoded the old behavior (`GH-105A` and `SME-ROADMAP-NOTE-42` reaching `task mark-shipped` verbatim) and were updated deliberately — both are unroutable by task-cli. The regex-anchor property one of them pinned moved to a direct unit test of `_ship_normalize_gh_code_for_task_cli`.

```
tests/test_ship_ticket_gates.py + tests/test_ship_notify_task_cli.py   89 passed
tests/test_ship.py                                                    253 passed
tests/test_conftest_ship_env.py                                         3 passed
```

## Known limit, documented in the code

An ordinary hyphenated word ending in digits (`UTF-8` from a title like "Handle UTF-8 decoding") is a well-formed id shape and cannot be rejected without the registered Linear team list, which ship.sh does not have. It is well-formed for a team that does not exist, so task-cli answers exit 2.

## Review

One `review diff` round (Sonnet quality + Fable architect; GLM seats were rate-limited). Findings taken: the bare `<n>` self-PR spelling was untested (pinned), and the `[ -n "$PR" ]` guard's invariant is now stated explicitly along with why it is written to fail open. Not taken, with reasons in the commit: collapsing the four candidate blocks into a loop would force the `gh pr view` round trip the title/body sources are deliberately lazy about; a cross-repo test asserting this grammar still agrees with task-cli's `_route_id_to_project` cannot run hermetically here and is left as a follow-up.

## Review rounds 2 and 3 (907e7b7)

Recorded under `GH-565` (`review task GH-565`). Folded in from round 2: a rejected candidate is announced on stderr with its source instead of being silently replaced by a different ticket (Fable); `_ship_code_names_this_pr` checks `$PR` digits-only via `${PR:-}` — the script runs under `set -u`, and a non-numeric operand in `$(( ))` is a fatal bash syntax error that would kill ship.sh (Opus, Sonnet); the grammar function is one alternation regex, cross-referencing `GH-<n>` (Opus); a table test pins the grammar's edge cases (Sonnet, Fable). Verified against `tasklib/cli.py::_route_id_to_project`: task-cli routes `#<n>`/`<n>` to the single GitHub project and `PREFIX-<n>` by upper-cased prefix, so a lowercase prefix is accepted here too.

Not taken: the acceptance gate still fails OPEN when `task gate` exits 2 for a well-formed code that names no ticket (a typo, or `UTF-8` from a title). That is a separate hole in the gate's exit handling, not in the input shape — filed as #569. The comment narrative (PR numbers, dates) stays: this file documents incidents inline by convention.

title: feat(agent-hooks): one subagent identity for codex/opencode/omp, no harness exemptions (#573)
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/573 (supersedes the harness-exemption approach of https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/542; Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/337)

## What changes for a person using codex, opencode or omp

Today the delegation gates either did not exist for your harness (orchestrator-stays-thin exempted codex/opencode/omp wholesale, #533/#544) or refused you with advice you could not follow (no-long-inline-process told a codex session to use Claude Code's Agent tool — 184 such refusals in one live codex session). After this PR every subagent-aware hook behaves identically on claude-code, codex, opencode and omp: the orchestrator is gated, a delegated child is not, and every refusal names the delegation recipe for THE harness you are in.

## Identity design (per harness) — never from tool arguments

| harness | how the bridge knows a tool call is a subagent's |
| --- | --- |
| claude-code | unchanged: CC's own top-level `agent_id`/`agent_type` (T2 precedence) |
| codex | (1) codex's OWN top-level `agent_id`/`agent_type` on every hook event inside a `collaboration.spawn_agent` child thread — captured verbatim on 0.153.4, kept as a test fixture; (2) the child thread's ROLLOUT `session_meta` behind the event's top-level `transcript_path` — `thread_source: "subagent"`, `parent_thread_id` == the event's `session_id` (a child's `session_id` is the parent's), `id` == the filename's trailing uuid != `session_id`; this is the record the 2026-09-05 `~/work/private` audit found on every thread the old bridge refused as "the orchestrator"; (3) `RIG_AGENT_ID`/`RIG_DETACHED_AGENT` from the new `rig-detached-codex` launcher; (4) process ancestry (a `codex exec` started from a codex session's shell tool). Ruled out: an env var — the hook process env carries only `CODEX_HOME`/`CODEX_MANAGED_*` (captured); `CODEX_THREAD_ID` goes to the shell tool's child, not to hook commands |
| opencode | (1) the plugin tags a `task` CHILD SESSION's tool calls with top-level `agentId`/`agentType` — opencode runs a task subagent as a child session; its `session.created` event carries `parentID` and its tool calls arrive with the child's `input.sessionID` (captured on 1.18.20; `client.session.get` fallback); (2) launcher env markers (existing, #476); (3) process ancestry |
| omp | (1) the hook-bridge extension tags a `task`-spawned in-process child's tool calls with its session id — ONLY when it is a later-than-first extension registration AND its session file is child-shaped (nested under the parent session's stem dir, or an `omp-task-*` temp dir), both omp's own bookkeeping; forwarded as top-level `agentId`/`agentType` to the dispatcher, which never reads identity from `input`; (2) launcher env markers from the new `rig-detached-omp`; (3) process ancestry |

Shared helper: `lib/agent_hooks_v1/subagent_identity.py` (env markers + one `ps` snapshot walk; a codex invocation is two contiguous processes — node wrapper + vendor binary — so only a same-harness process past a non-harness break counts). Every failure path yields no identity → governed (fail closed in the relax direction). Forged `agent_id`-shaped keys in tool args are stripped by every bridge before any of this runs.

## Hooks

- `orchestrator-stays-thin`: `EXEMPT_HARNESSES` / `_is_exempt_harness` removed. A missing or unknown `harness` tag stays governed.
- `agenttools_hatch_escalation.delegation_recipe(harness)` / `foreground_recipe(harness)`: the one table of per-harness recipes (every gated hook already hard-loads that module). `orchestrator-stays-thin`, `no-long-inline-process`, `background-subagent-gate`, `subagent-no-bg-longproc` compose their refusal from it; unknown/missing tag → every recipe; a `harness` under `args` neither relaxes nor steers.

## Launchers

`skills/universal/rig-detached-agent` is the one launcher core (validation, private log, env markers, real detach: new session + `</dev/null` + `--` before the brief); `rig-detached-opencode` / `rig-detached-codex` / `rig-detached-omp` are thin wrappers that resolve the core relative to their own real path (works through `~/.codex/skills` symlinks). Child argv: `opencode run --title <name> -- <brief>`, `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust --skip-git-repo-check -- <brief>`, `omp -p --auto-approve -- <brief>`.

**`codex exec` runs no hooks at all without `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`** (verified: untrusted and trusted project, 0.153.4). The flag is what makes the launcher child GOVERNED; a hand-run `codex exec` is ungoverned today anyway.

## Tests (red-first)

`tests/test_codex_subagent_replay.py` — the audit's REAL refused tool calls replayed through the real bridge + the real hook scripts (in-process, every other identity source pinned off), against the real `session_meta` records of the audited sessions (`16-13` "Singer", spawned by `16-05`; only the ~20 KB `base_instructions` text trimmed): `review diff -C …` (blocks_raw row 11, `no-long-inline-process`) and the `gh pr list …` PR inventory (row 2, `orchestrator-stays-thin`) from the delegate → ALLOW (never even warned); the same from the orchestrator's session_meta → refused with the codex recipe (and no `subagent_type: "fork"` CC-only advice); a forged `tool_input.agent_id`/`agent_type` from the orchestrator → still refused. Plus the consistency facts one by one (thread_source, parent != session_id, id == session_id, filename/id mismatch, malformed/oversized/missing first line, `tool_input.transcript_path` ignored).

`tests/test_subagent_identity.py` (new), per-bridge identity tests with the captured codex child-thread event and an omp extension driver that registers twice, per-hook harness-recipe tests (orchestrator → gated with the right recipe; launcher-env child → allow; ancestry child → allow; forged `args.agent_id` → stripped, still gated), `tests/test_rig_detached_launchers.py` (the launcher suite parametrized over the three harnesses + wrapper/core contract). Full suite: see the checks.

## Live proof (this machine, 2026-09-07, codex-cli 0.153.4 / omp 18.0.11)

Hooks for every run come from the WORKTREE (`CODEX_HOOKS_DIR` / `OMP_HOOKS_DIR` → descriptors whose `cmd` is the worktree's hook scripts; `PYTHONPATH=<wt>/lib` for the codex bridge; `-e <wt>/lib/omp_hook_bridge/extension.ts` or a proof agent dir whose `extensions/` symlinks it for omp). ### 7. captured harness facts the design rests on

- codex `PreToolUse` inside a `collaboration.spawn_agent` child thread carries TOP-LEVEL `agent_id`/`agent_type` (the parent's does not); `session_id` stays the parent's; `transcript_path` is the child rollout. Kept verbatim as a fixture in `tests/test_codex_hook_bridge.py`.
- That fixture's `transcript_path` rollout (`…-01a07892-b5aa-7b82-bb84-071da23eb340.jsonl`) is still on this machine: its first line is `session_meta` with `thread_source: "subagent"`, `parent_thread_id: 01a07892-678c…` == the event's `session_id`, nickname `Hubble` — the captured hook event and the rollout record describe the same child, so sources (1) and (2) agree by construction (`agent_id` == rollout `id`).
- The audited sessions (`~/.codex/sessions/2026/09/05/rollout-2026-09-05T16-13-43-01a0717d-2948-…`, `16-13-54-…`, `16-14-08-…`, cli_version 0.153.4) carry the same record shape with `parent_thread_id: 01a07175-ba7e-…` (session `16-05`) — the bridge of the day stripped every identity (`origin/main` drops `agent_id`), which is why 25 of the audit's refusals landed on delegates.
- CI: `tests/test_subagent_identity.py::test_real_process_table_parses_this_process` failed on Linux because procps clips `ps` `args` to 80 columns off a terminal; `_process_table` now passes `-ww` (a harness under a long install path was invisible to the ancestry walk the same way); regression test spawns a child with a 190-char argv.
- `codex exec` runs NO hooks unless `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` is passed (0.153.4; tested in an untrusted and a trusted project). The launcher passes it; a hand-run `codex exec` (review-cli's reviewer: `codex exec -s read-only -C <cwd> --ephemeral`) is ungoverned today regardless of this PR.
- omp runs a `task` subagent in-process, invokes the extension's default export once more for it; the child's `sessionManager.getSessionFile()` is nested under the parent session's stem dir (or `omp-task-*` temp dir with `--no-session`); root has a top-level file or none.

## Review rounds (task `#573`, bar: 3 passed iterations across correctness/consistency/quality)

Round 2 and 3 findings, all applied: `background-subagent-gate` uses `delegation_recipe`'s own harness list + fallback (no second list to drift); the `rig-detached-agent` core refuses a brief over 100 000 bytes (Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) or one that with the inherited environment exceeds `getconf ARG_MAX` (macOS bounds argv+env together) BEFORE detaching — previously it printed "launched" and the child died of `E2BIG`; the ancestry walk is proven against a real process tree (`test_real_ancestry_walk_end_to_end`: a `/bin/sh` stub under a unique harness name, nested through a plain `sh`); the four hook test files share one `tests/_delegation_fixtures.py::RECIPE_NEEDLE`; an unknown/unhashable `harness` tag at the gate → every recipe (pinned). Answered without a code change: review-cli's reviewers need no identity — the opencode reviewer is the deny-all `read-only-reviewer` agent (no bash/edit, the gated points never fire) and the codex reviewer is a `codex exec` without hook trust (no hooks at all); the per-tool-call cost of the rollout read (one ≤20 KB line) + one `ps` snapshot is inherent to a per-hook process and accepted.

## Left open

- codex `collaboration.spawn_agent` has no `pre-agent` mapping (its `message` is encrypted, so triviality is unjudgeable) — the background-subagent-gate does not see codex dispatches.
- Ancestry proves "a same-harness session sits above this one"; it cannot tell a native in-process spawn whose children carry no env (that is what the codex top-level field, the omp extension signal and the opencode session parentID are for).
- PR #560 touches `orchestrator_stays_thin.py` too; whichever merges second rebases.

title: fix(ship): scan every task-code candidate, fail closed on task gate exit 2, look GitHub-issue codes up under both spellings
body:
Three robustness fixes to `gh ship`'s ticket-code derivation and its two ticket gates, found live on 2026-09-06 (PR #560 / PR #567).

Tickets:
- https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/571 — a rejected first candidate hid the real `Refs #<n>` in the same text
- https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/569 — the acceptance gate failed OPEN on `task gate` exit 2
- https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/572 — the review-quorum lookup never matched `#<n>` against a `GH-<n>` record

## What changes

**1. The extractor returns EVERY candidate; the callers filter (issue 571).**
`_review_quorum_extract_ticket_candidates` yields every ticket-like token of a text, one per line, in arm-priority order (HYP arm, generic `PREFIX-<n>`, descriptive ALL-CAPS, then the at-most-one GitHub-issue candidate — keyword-anchored `Refs #<n>` else a same-repo issue URL), duplicates removed. The acceptance/notify derivation validates each candidate (task-cli id grammar, self-PR rule) and takes the first survivor; it falls to the next source only when a source has NO survivor. Precedence `$REVIEW_TASK_CODE` → branch → title → body is unchanged. Every rejection is logged with its reason and source; the accepted code and its source are logged too (and the source survives into the refusal text — the derivation is called directly, not in a subshell). PR #560's ORIGINAL body (an incidental mention of its own number in the GH spelling, inside the acceptance proofs, ahead of the real keyword-anchored reference to issue 541) is a fixture regression test (`tests/fixtures/pr560_body.md`): the gate now asks task gate for issue 541.

**2. `task gate` exit 2 for a derived code REFUSES (issue 569).**
A code WAS derived but task-cli cannot resolve it (a typo'd id, a hyphenated word that passed the grammar, a backend error) is a broken PR, not an unguarded one. `_acceptance_gate` refuses with the code, the exit, task-cli's own `error: …` line and the SOURCE the code came from, pointing at the two remedies (`REVIEW_TASK_CODE=<code> gh ship <pr>` / `SHIP_ACCEPTANCE_GATE=0` for a genuine outage). Audit decision: `refused:unresolvable`. What identifies task-cli's answer is a line STARTING with `error: ` on stderr or stdout (one predicate for "is it task-cli" and "what did it say"); an exit 2 without such a line is still the PATH-collision skip (a foreign `task` binary). "No code derivable at all" still skips with the existing `no task code` audit line.

**3. The review-quorum gate scans candidates and looks a GitHub-issue code up under BOTH spellings (issues 572 and 571, criterion 3).**
The gate's own derivation now uses the same candidate extractor. Per candidate: query `#<n>`, then `GH-<n>` (and vice versa); the spelling that meets the bar authorizes and is the one named in the `AUTHORITY CONFIRMED` line and the audit record. A candidate with a record that falls short is THE task (refuse, the twin listed as "also tried"); a candidate with NO record under either spelling — review-cli's own answer, zero counts AND `error: no recorded review iterations` (zero counts alone are a short record) — moves the scan to the next candidate, then the next source (the body is fetched only when no branch candidate has a record). Admission here is "has a record", deliberately not the acceptance gate's grammar (a `GH-<pr>` or descriptive review-check code is a legitimate record key). An empty answer on every query tier is still "could not query" (refuse at once — unless a short record is already in hand, which is then the verdict). Split records are NOT summed. `REVIEW_TASK_CODE` gets the same dual lookup and is now documented (header + README).

**4. The acceptance gate's reuse of the quorum gate's code (review round 4).**
A code the quorum gate found is reused WITH the source it came from (`the branch name` / `the PR body` / `$REVIEW_TASK_CODE`), so an exit-2 refusal on it names the real source instead of `$TASK_CODE`. A record-less or unqueryable spelling that the quorum gate's live Telegram hatch waved through is CLEARED, never reused — the acceptance gate derives afresh (branch → title → body) instead of asking task-cli about an incidental `UTF-8` and refusing right after the approval. When the PR's own repo cannot be established at all (no GitHub origin, no `--repo`, no PR URL), an issue link is reported as "cannot be told from another repo's" rather than as another repo's.

**Two deliberate non-changes.** (a) The acceptance gate does NOT scan past a grammar-valid token task-cli cannot resolve (`Fix the UTF-8 decoding.` followed by a keyword-anchored reference to issue 77 refuses on `UTF-8`, naming the source and the `REVIEW_TASK_CODE=` fix): scanning past an unresolvable code would let a typo'd real ticket silently hand the gate to whatever candidate comes next — fail-closed wins; the quorum gate, whose scan moves on only on review-cli's own no-record answer, is documented as the stricter/looser pair it is. (b) No cap on the number of candidates the quorum scan tries per source: the body is author-controlled, the lookups are local `review task --check` calls, and the GitHub-issue candidate sits LAST in arm order, so a cap would cut the real reference before it is reached.

## Tests

- `tests/test_ship_ticket_gates.py`: PR #560 fixture → task gate for issue 541; grammar-rejected candidate before a keyword-anchored reference to issue 77; source precedence survives the continuation; every candidate rejected → skip; exit-2 refusal (+ dry-run, + `error:` line on stdout, + non-task-cli exit 2 still skips); foreign-repo issue link reported.

title: fix(omp-bridge): await the dispatcher instead of freezing the omp interface (#558)
body:
https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/558

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/558

## What

The omp hook bridge (`lib/omp_hook_bridge/extension.ts`) spawned the Python dispatcher **synchronously**, which froze omp's single-threaded interface — no repaints, no keypresses — for the whole dispatch: up to the full Telegram-approval window of a hatch-capable hook. The `tool_call` handler now **awaits** an asynchronous `spawn` (resolving on the child's `close`, so stdout is fully drained). omp's `emitToolCall` awaits whatever the handler returns, so the decision still arrives before the tool runs.

Unchanged: the stdin JSON contract, the `OMP_HOOK_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_MS` budget (2,000,000 ms), and the fail-OPEN policy — a launch failure, crash, timeout or unparseable output still resolves to "allow" and never throws (a thrown handler is how omp blocks a call).

Also in this change:
- On timeout the child gets SIGTERM first and SIGKILL after a 2 s grace (the synchronous spawn also sent SIGTERM).
- omp can now exit mid-dispatch (Ctrl-C, `/exit`, a crash), which the frozen loop made impossible; every running dispatcher is tracked and SIGTERMed on `session_shutdown` and on process `exit`, so a quit mid-hatch never orphans a dispatcher.
- The dispatcher's stderr is forwarded as it arrives, line by line, tagged `omp-hook-bridge[<event> <toolCallId>]`, so a hook that explains itself while it waits is visible while waiting, and two overlapping dispatches stay attributable.
- A one-shot stderr notice after 10 s explains a long hold and names omp's own timeout setting.

## Behaviour change to know about (not a pure refactor)

omp bounds a `tool_call` handler with `extensionHandlers.toolCallTimeoutMs` (**default 30,000 ms**) and, when it fires, resolves the call to `{block: true, reason: "Extension … timed out after 30000ms"}` — fail-closed (verified in omp's `runner.ts`, `emitToolCall`). The old synchronous spawn evaded that timer by accident (a blocked loop cannot run it); the awaited spawn does not. Until the setting is raised, any hook that holds a call longer than 30 s — every Telegram approval hatch — ends as an omp-generated block rather than the hook's own verdict. Safe direction (a denied hatch never becomes an allow), but not the hook's decision. The README documents the required ordering (`descriptor timeout_ms < OMP_HOOK_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_MS < toolCallTimeoutMs`) and the config to set; provisioning it through rig is https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/363. The same synchronous spawn still exists in the opencode bridge: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/568.

## Proof

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_omp_hook_bridge.py -q` → 68 passed (9 new bun-driven cases: event loop keeps turning during a dispatch, block/allow propagate, crash fails open, budget kills the child, SIGTERM-first + SIGKILL grace, post-write path awaits, slow-dispatch notice only for `tool_call`, two dispatches overlap, reaper on process exit and on `session_shutdown`). `bun test` → 51 pass (the repo's TypeScript tests; `extension.ts` itself is exercised through the pytest bun drivers).
- Live proof on omp 18.0.11 with a throwaway `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`OMP_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (its `extensions/` links this branch's `extension.ts`; its `hooks/` holds one descriptor whose hook sleeps 20 s then allows; a second extension writes a 1 s heartbeat; a local deterministic OpenAI-compatible stub issues the `bash` call, since no real provider on this machine has working credentials). The real `~/.omp/agent/extensions/zz-agent-tools-hook-bridge.ts` symlink was never touched.
  - **old code (origin/main):** 1 heartbeat in 20 s — the loop was frozen for the entire hold; decision arrived after 20.0 s.
  - **new code:** 20 heartbeats over 19 s, worst gap 1.00 s, decision arrived after 20.0 s, tool ran (`proof-ok`), the 5 s notice line printed.

title: fix(no-long-inline-process): gate a test suite behind its launcher — python -m, uv run, npx (#584)
body:
https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/584

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/584

## What

The `no-long-inline-process` hook — the gate that keeps test suites out of the orchestrator's main thread — recognised a runner only as a bare `argv[0]` (`pytest`, `vitest`, …). The most common spellings of a test run passed ungated: `python3 -m pytest -q` (the replay command this repo documents), `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/` (every rig.yaml test script), `npx vitest`, `poetry run pytest`.

The classifier now peels a **launcher** and classifies what it executes, recursively:
- interpreter module runs: `python`/`python3`/`python3.12`/`pypy` `-m pytest|unittest`, including clustered and glued short options (`-um pytest`, `-Wignore -m pytest`, `-mpytest`); a script path, `-c code` or stdin is not a module run;
- `uv run`, `uvx`, `poetry|pipenv|pdm run`, `coverage run`, `npx|bunx`, `npm exec`, `pnpm exec|dlx`, `yarn exec|dlx|run`, `bun run|x`.

Each launcher's value-taking options are skipped with their value, so `uv run --with pytest ruff check .` runs `ruff` and stays allowed. An option the table does not model leaves its value at `argv[0]` — never a runner — so the miss is an allow (the gate's fail-open direction), never a false block. `unittest`, `tox`, `nose2` join the direct runners. The subagent exemption (trusted `agent_id`) is decided before classification and is unchanged; it is pinned for the new forms.

## Proof

`python3 -m pytest tests/test_no_long_inline_process.py -q` → 179 passed (37 new block cases with the exact command strings, 17 allow cases, 3 subagent-exempt cases, a nesting-cap case). Descriptor description and README list the launcher forms.

## What

Fixes one line in AGENTS.md's autonomous-thread-resolution section that described a passed review-quorum as "multi-model consensus cleared" — this is loose, outdated wording left over from before review-cli#246 made role-based coverage the default gate.

Alex reported an omp session incorrectly explaining a ship failure as "quorum needs ≥3 models, Claude/GLM in cooldown" — but the actual gate (correctly documented two sections later in the same file, and in ship.sh's own comments) requires ≥3 distinct BOARD ROLES among passed iterations, not 3 distinct models. title: fix(require-ticket-before-commit): neutralize heredocs before parsing a commit message
body:
## Summary

- The `require-ticket-before-commit` hook's shlex-based tokenizer had zero heredoc awareness, so a multi-line commit message authored via this repo's own documented pattern (`git commit -m "$(cat <<'MSGEOF' ... MSGEOF)"`) corrupted its quote/comment tracking. This went wrong in both directions: a real ticket reference past a stray embedded quote in the heredoc body could be mistaken for a shell comment and silently dropped (a **false BLOCK** on a correctly-ticketed commit), and an odd embedded-quote count could leave the whole command looking quote-unbalanced, making the on_error=open gate fail OPEN and silently **ALLOW** a genuinely ticketless commit. A heredoc body line that happened to parse as its own valid shell segment could also be mistaken for a real command.
- The fix (`_neutralize_heredocs`) replaces every heredoc in the command with an opaque sentinel token *before* any shlex-based parsing runs, tracking quote state per a small stack of frames (one pushed per `$(` or an opening backtick, since command substitution starts a fresh parsing context even inside outer quotes). `_resolve_message_value` unwraps the documented `-m "$(cat <<'MSGEOF' ...)"` shape back to the real message text, and `_heredoc_body_for_target` matches a `-F <path>` against a heredoc that wrote that same path earlier in the SAME command, reading the captured body directly instead of the disk (which does not have the file yet at PreToolUse hook time).
- **Three rounds of review-cli caught real gaps in the fix itself before it shipped** (all fixed here, except the two exotic round-3 shapes noted below):
  - Round 1: a heredoc inside a backtick substitution had no parsing frame; a compact heredoc opener with no space (`cat<<'EOF'`) broke the sentinel's word boundary; multiple heredocs chained on one line (`cmd <<A <<B`) only used the first one's body instead of the last (the one real shell redirection actually wires up); and the `-F`/heredoc "must write before it's read" ordering check had no protection at all against a heredoc written *after* the commit that reads it.
  - Round 2 (found reviewing round 1's own fix): a `<<` inside a shell `#` comment was still read as a real heredoc opener — the most serious finding across all three rounds, since it let the neutralizer swallow a REAL, ticketless `git commit` on the next line as if it were heredoc body text, causing the hook to silently **ALLOW** it; the round-1 ordering check anchored itself to an independent text search for the word "commit" that unrelated prose (`echo commit`) could mis-anchor, causing a false BLOCK; and the redirect-target parser truncated a quoted path with an embedded space at the first space.
  - Round 3: two genuinely exotic shapes (arithmetic-context `<<` and fd-prefixed chained heredocs) — see Known Limitations below; filed as a follow-up rather than expanded here.
- Added 30 new regression tests (mirrored across the two test files) covering the exact repro shapes from #503, #406, #430 and #570's primary scenario, positive-path regressions (a heredoc message with no ticket must still BLOCK), #570's "bonus repro", and every round-1/round-2 review finding.

## Issues addressed

- Refs #503 — the canonical tracking issue for this bug family.
- Refs #406, #430 — duplicates of #503, closed separately with a comment pointing here.
- Refs #570 — a related but distinct variant (`-F <path>` written by a heredoc in the same command, plus a silent read-failure and a `cd`-relative-path case). This PR addresses #570's primary repro (the heredoc-written `-F` file, now also ordering-safe) and its "bonus repro" (a heredoc body mistaken for a real command), but does **not** fix two of its five acceptance criteria: AC3 (resolving a relative `-F` path against a shell `cd <dir> &&` earlier in the command, as opposed to `git -C <dir>`, which already worked) and AC4 (naming the unreadable path + OS error in the BLOCK message itself, currently only a stderr warning). #570 stays open for that remaining scope.

## Known limitations (intentionally out of scope for this PR)

- **Arithmetic context** (`(( 1 << EOF ))`) and **fd-prefixed chained heredocs** (`cat <<A 0<<B`) are misread by the neutralizer — both are real gate holes in principle, but neither shape appears in the documented commit pattern or any of the four original issues; found by review-cli's third round. Tracked as a follow-up: #601.
- A trailing same-line redirect immediately after a heredoc operator (`cmd <<EOF > file`) is not specially handled.
- Nested, escaped backticks inside a backtick substitution are not specially handled.
- #570's AC3 (a `-F` path resolved against a shell `cd <dir> &&` earlier in the command) and AC4 (naming the unreadable path in the BLOCK message) — see above.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest agent-hooks/require-ticket-before-commit/test_require_ticket.py tests/test_require_ticket_before_commit.py -q` — 292 passed (262 pre-existing + 30 new)

- [x] `ruff check` on the three changed files — clean
- [x] Live validation: every commit on this PR was authored via the exact heredoc `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"` pattern this fix targets, and the fixed hook correctly parsed and allowed them.
- [x] Manually reproduced and re-verified all four round-1 findings and all three round-2 findings directly against the hook (both the exploit direction and the legitimate-case direction) before and after each fix.
- [x] Round 3's two findings (arithmetic context, fd-prefixed chained heredocs) reproduced against the live hook and confirmed exotic/out-of-scope per review; filed as #601.

title: fix(dependency-review): only fail on advisories new vs. the base branch
body:
## Summary

- `dep-audit.sh` audited the whole current tree unconditionally, so every PR in a repo with ANY pre-existing high+ transitive advisory failed this gate forever, regardless of what the PR itself changed. `hyperide/hyper-saas#780` (a docs-only PR, zero dependency changes) failed on 6 pre-existing `browserslist`/`fast-uri` advisories it never touched.
- `dep-audit.sh` now takes an optional second positional argument, `BASE_DIR` — the base branch's checked-out tree. For the bun/npm/pnpm/yarn branches (the ones with a `--json` output whose advisory records carry the same GitHub Advisory Database numeric id — verified live against a real advisory, id `1153171` / `GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx`, identically across bun/npm/pnpm's `--json` output) it also audits `BASE_DIR` and diffs by that id: an advisory present in **both** trees is printed as a visible informational warning but no longer fails the check; an advisory present **only** in the PR head is genuinely new and still fails it.
- `workflow.yml` passes `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (already the base branch's own checkout under `pull_request_target`) as `BASE_DIR` for PR events; a push with no PR to diff against is unaffected (old whole-tree behavior, unchanged).
- Every path that can't establish a trustworthy baseline (`jq` missing, no `BASE_DIR`, an unresolvable `BASE_DIR`, no matching lockfile there, an unparseable audit run) fails OPEN toward the **original** whole-tree behavior — never a crash, never a silent pass.
- Python/Rust/Go audits (`pip-audit`/`cargo-audit`/`govulncheck`) are **unchanged** — still whole-tree only. Their `--json`/structured output isn't verified against this id scheme in this pass, so scoping them is left for a follow-up rather than guessed at.

Closes task-cli#140 (tracked in a separate ticketing system, not a GitHub issue in this repo).

## Review rounds

Two `review diff` rounds ran against this PR; findings from each were fixed:

**Round 1** — a real, serious bug: the JSON-based advisory extraction alone could be fooled by a future ecosystem's `--json` schema not matching the parser (e.g. different key casing), silently reporting "trustworthy" with an empty advisory set even when the audit tool's own plain-mode exit code said otherwise — swallowing a real failure into a false pass. Fixed by cross-checking the tool's own plain-mode exit code against the extracted id set; any disagreement now falls back to the original whole-tree behavior instead of trusting the (possibly wrong) parse. Also tightened `has_lockfile`'s npm case to require an actual lockfile, not just a bare `package.json`.

**Round 2** — five more findings, all addressed:
- Consolidated two differently-worded log messages that fired for the same "no baseline available" condition into one.
- Simplified `json_advisory_ids`'s return code to a single non-zero failure signal (a documented 1-vs-2 distinction that neither call site actually consumed).
- Added `local` to every helper function's variables (currently harmless since ecosystem detection is a mutually-exclusive if/elif chain, but the code anticipates extending scoping further, where global clobbering would matter).
- Added test coverage for the relative-`BASE_DIR` resolution path (previously only absolute paths were exercised) and for npm's actual `--json` shape (nested under `vulnerabilities`/`via`/`source`, materially different from bun's flat `id`-keyed array — previously only bun's shape was exercised).
- Left as an explicitly documented tradeoff, not fixed: each ecosystem now runs its audit command up to 3x per CI run (was 1x) — plain + `--json` for the current tree, `--json` for the base tree — tripling exposure to registry rate-limiting. title: fix(ci/review-threads): remove tamperable pull_request_review triggers (task-cli#143)
body:
## What

`review-threads.yml` (agent-tools#134) added `pull_request_review` / `pull_request_review_comment`
as re-evaluation triggers to close the "stale-green" gap (#65: a review thread added after an
earlier green check left the required status dishonestly green). That change assumed those
events "also run the trusted default-branch copy of this workflow file", the way
`pull_request_target` does — which is why the file's own checkout step already pinned to
`base.ref` for tamper resistance.

That assumption was wrong (task-cli#143). Per GitHub's own documented event table
(`GITHUB_SHA`/`GITHUB_REF` columns in "Events that trigger workflows"),
`pull_request_review`/`pull_request_review_comment` carry the **same** ref as plain
`pull_request` — the PR **merge branch** (`refs/pull/N/merge`) — not the default branch. Only
`pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` are documented to source the workflow **file itself**
from the default branch; every other pull-request-shaped event (including these two) executes
the workflow **definition as the PR itself edited it**. So a PR author could edit
`review-threads.yml` to skip/remove/replace the job specifically on review-triggered runs —
defeating the exact protection #134 claimed to add, and doing so more dangerously than the
pre-#134 state, since it creates a false sense the gate got *stronger*.

Concrete bypass: PR gets an initial green `pull_request_target` run → author edits this
workflow to no-op the job on review events → reviewer adds an unresolved thread → the review
event fires but the (author-edited) job does nothing → the required `review-threads` status
stays stale-green.

## What I changed

- Removed `pull_request_review` / `pull_request_review_comment` as triggers on
  `ci/review-threads/workflow.yml`. This is **the safe floor**: exact same coverage as
  pre-#134 (the gate only re-evaluates on PR lifecycle events, tamper-resistant via
  `pull_request_target`), with no false claim of tamper-resistant re-evaluation.
- Corrected the false claim in the workflow's own header comment and in
  `ci/review-threads/README.md` (the "Re-evaluation" and "Security note" sections both
  asserted the wrong trust boundary).
- **A second, related fix from this PR's own review-cli round (codex finding):** the
  checkout's `ref` fell back to an **empty string** for `workflow_dispatch` (no
  `pull_request` in that event's payload), relying on `actions/checkout`'s ambient default —
  which for `workflow_dispatch` is whatever ref it was **dispatched against**, not reliably
  the default branch (GitHub docs: a workflow can be dispatched "against any branch or tag
  via the API or CLI" once it has run at least once). A collaborator with dispatch access
  could have run this workflow against a branch carrying edited gate-script content — the
  original header comment's claim that this "falls back to the default branch (also
  trusted)" was itself unverified and, per `actions/checkout`'s own documented default
  behavior, likely wrong. Now pins explicitly:
  `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref || github.event.repository.default_branch }}`.
- Red-first regression tests:
  `tests/test_review_threads_gate.py::test_does_not_trigger_on_pull_request_review{,_comment}`
  and `::test_checkout_ref_falls_back_to_the_real_default_branch_for_workflow_dispatch` —
  each confirmed failing against the pre-fix `workflow.yml`, passing after.
- Full suite: 4787 passed, 6 skipped, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure
  (`test_agenttools_errors.py::test_guard_returns_code_and_prints_for_known_error`, an
  ANSI-color-escape assertion that reproduces identically on unmodified `main` — not touched).
- review-cli round 1 (codex + a Claude Sonnet quality pass) found 2 real findings (both
  above) and 3 quality/duplication notes (docstrings trimmed to point at the README instead
  of repeating the full rationale in four places).

## What I did NOT verify live, and why

The task's acceptance criteria ask for live confirmation against a real throwaway PR. I
attempted this (a throwaway branch/worktree with a distinguishing probe step added to
`workflow.yml`) but `gh repo create` and `git push` were both denied by this session's
permission classifier (confirmed with `git push --dry-run`, which succeeds — only the real
network write is blocked). The trust-boundary claim above is therefore an **inference from
GitHub's documented event table**, not a live-confirmed fact. Ten-minute repro for whoever can
push:

```bash
# on a branch, add a distinguishing step right after the checkout step in
# ci/review-threads/workflow.yml, e.g.:
#   - run: echo "PROBE=PR-VERSION-RAN" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
# open a PR, submit a review comment (gh pr review --comment), then check whether the
# pull_request_review-triggered run's log/step-summary shows the probe step at all —
# absent = base copy ran (current code's assumption); present = PR copy ran (task-cli#143's
# claim). Also worth confirming while there: does a Checks-API check-run named
# "review-threads", created via `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/check-runs` with GITHUB_TOKEN, show
# up as satisfying the SAME required-status-check context branch protection would look for —
# this gates whether the schedule-cron option below is viable at all.
```

## Live severity finding, worth flagging on its own

`gh api repos/<repo>/branches/main/protection` on `agent-tools`, `rig-cli`, and `tg-cli` all
return `required_conversation_resolution: false` and `required_status_checks: null` — **this
gate is not enforced anywhere today**, by branch protection or by the native
"Require conversation resolution before merging" toggle the README recommends alongside it. So
the practical severity of the bug fixed here is "a false claim of added protection", not "an
active bypass of a real, currently-enforced gate" — worth deciding whether to also turn on
`required_conversation_resolution` (the native closer nobody has enabled) independent of this
fix.

## Options for closing the #65 gap for real (not implemented — needs a human call)

The AC literally wants the check to go red even if a PR *disables* its own review-triggered
recheck — no `pull_request_review`/`pull_request_review_comment`-based design can satisfy that,
since a PR can always suppress its own trigger. Three options, in order of how much they
actually close the literal AC:

**A — remove + honest docs (this PR).** Floor option. Same coverage as pre-#134, correctly
documented, reversible in one commit. Does not Refs #65's stale-green gap at all — reverts to
its pre-#134 state.

**B — keep pull_request_review/pull_request_review_comment, but stop calling it
tamper-resistant.** Keeps the honest-PR re-check UX (fast feedback for reviewers who aren't
adversarial), keeps the tamperable path, with docs that say so plainly instead of claiming a
trust boundary that doesn't exist. Not proposed here because it still lets a bad-faith PR do
exactly the bypass in task-cli#143 — I don't think "keep it but document the hole" clears the
bar for a merge-gate.

**C — a `schedule` cron sweep on this same base-sourced workflow.** The only design that
literally satisfies AC#2 (unsuppressable by the PR — schedule triggers always use the
default-branch file and a PR cannot touch cron activity). It would list open PRs, re-run
`review-threads.sh` per PR, and post each result via the Checks API (`gh api
repos/OWNER/REPO/check-runs`) rather than relying on the job's own implicit check-run (which for
a `schedule`-triggered run attaches to the default branch tip, not the PR head — the same
false-coverage-no-op trap this file already documents for `issue_comment`). Not implemented
here because it rests on exactly one fact I could not verify without push access: whether a
Checks-API check-run created by `GITHUB_TOKEN` under the name `review-threads` actually
satisfies the same required-status-check context GitHub Actions' own implicit check-run would
have used. If it doesn't, C is a bigger, more-privileged (`checks: write`) version of the same
false-coverage mistake being fixed here. Real cost either way: 5–30 minute latency (cron
cadence) times every open PR times every rig-managed repo, recurring.

**Recommendation:** ship A now (the floor, no false claims, reversible). If the stale-green gap
still matters enough to close for real, do the one live check that unblocks C (a throwaway
schedule-triggered check-run + `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/status` or the branch-protection
required-checks response, to see whether it's recognized), then build C behind that answer.

## Downstream propagation

This is the canonical source (`~/xp/agent-tools/ci/review-threads/`), propagated to every
ecosystem repo via `rig apply`. rig-cli and tg-cli (at least) currently have the buggy,
*uncommitted* #134-era resync of this file sitting in their primary checkouts — deliberately
not committed there yet, specifically because of this bug. Once this PR merges, a future `rig
apply` (or another resync pass) in those repos should pick up the fixed version instead of the
buggy one. No action needed in those repos from this PR.

title: feat(agent-hooks): block a raw git worktree add/remove outside .worktrees/
body:
## Summary

- rig-cli's own `AGENTS.md` documents `<repo-root>/.worktrees/` as the ONLY sanctioned worktree location (GH-329: ~70 leftover worktrees scattered across five ad-hoc conventions, tens of GB of duplicated `node_modules`/`.venv`) — but that rule was documentation only, with zero enforcement. The same five-conventions problem was confirmed still happening live in rig-cli the same day this was written (`git worktree list` showed worktrees in `/private/tmp`, a sibling `-worktrees/` dir, a `-wt-*` dir, and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`).
- Adds `block-raw-worktree-add`, a `pre-bash` agent-hook that argv-parses (shlex, chain-aware, reusing `pin-primary-worktree`'s `--git-common-dir` repo-root primitive) any `git worktree add`/`git worktree remove` and BLOCKS one whose target does not resolve under the repo's `.worktrees/`, pointing at `rig worktree create`/`remove`/`gc` instead.
- `rig worktree create`'s own internal `git worktree add` call is a plain subprocess spawned from inside the `rig` process, never routed through the agent's own Bash tool, so this hook never sees it and needs no process-ancestry trust mechanism — verified by reading `riglib/worktree.py` before writing this hook, not assumed.
- Deny-by-default, with a Telegram hatch (`RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RAW_WORKTREE_ADD`) for a genuine one-off, copying `block-raw-pr-merge`'s hatch usage pattern exactly.
- No `rig.yaml` opt-in flag: it installs everywhere the catalog is applied, like `block-raw-pr-merge`/`block-no-verify`. rig-cli's own catalog scan is directory-convention-based (`agent-hooks/<name>/<name>.<point>.json`), so **no rig-cli change is needed** for this to be picked up.
- A `.worktrees` directory that is itself a symlink escaping the repo root is refused rather than trusted (mirrors `riglib/worktree.py::_target_escapes_repo`).
- `git worktree prune`/`list`/`lock`/`unlock`/`move`/`repair` are deliberately out of scope (see the hook's module docstring / README).
- Known, deliberately unclosed residuals are named explicitly in both the docstring and the README: a `bash -c`/`sh -c`/`eval`-hidden invocation, and a harness-native worktree path (e.g. Claude Code's own `EnterWorktree`) that never goes through the agent's Bash tool at all and so cannot be seen by any `pre-bash` hook.

title: fix(block-raw-pr-merge): close a decoy head-shaped wrapper-flag bypass
body:
## Summary
- agent-tools#606: adversarial re-audit of block-raw-pr-merge to check whether the historical, privately-held ROADMAP.md bypass (2026-07-18 → 07-23) is still live.
- **Historical bypass status: already fixed.** It was the crafted-argument clustered short-flag gap in `gh api` parsing, closed by #333/#335 on 2026-07-24 — confirmed by re-testing every documented defense class against the current hook.
- **New real gap found and fixed:** `_resolve_invoked_argv` returned only the FIRST token in a wrapped segment whose basename matched a head (`gh`/a shell interpreter/`eval`). A wrapper's own flag VALUE that happens to be head-shaped hijacked that match — `env -u gh gh pr merge 1` (`-u`'s argument is literally the string `gh`) resolved to `['gh', '-u', 'gh', 'pr', 'merge', '1']`, whose `sub[0]` is `'gh'` not `'pr'`, silently missing the real merge one token later and wrongly **ALLOWING** a command that genuinely invokes `gh pr merge` (confirmed live: `env -u gh gh --version` really does print the gh version). Same hijack via `xargs -E gh -I{} gh pr merge {}`.
- Fix: `_resolve_invoked_argv_candidates` returns every head-shaped token in the segment, not just the first; `_is_merge_route` and `_graphql_query_field_is_expandable` now check every candidate and block if any resolves to a merge route. This can only add over-blocks (the safe direction), never remove a detection the old single-match scan already made.
- Also added `find` to `_WRAPPERS` — its `-exec`/`-execdir`/`-ok`/`-okdir` actions genuinely exec the given argv (`find . -exec gh pr merge {} \;`), the same threat class already covered for `xargs`, and now safe to scan generically given the multi-candidate fix.
- README documents the fix and adds a **"Known scope boundary"** section naming two residual bypass classes tested and confirmed still open by design (an arbitrary interpreter or script file exec'ing `gh`, and a raw HTTP client hitting GitHub's API directly) — both fundamentally unbounded for an argv-parsing pre-bash hook, matching the existing "documented residual" framing already in the file.
- `ROADMAP.md`'s stale 2026-07-18 → 07-23 entries are updated to the real, current state.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_block_raw_pr_merge.py` — 354 passed (343 existing + 11 new regression tests for both findings, plus benign-`find`/wrapper-usage-stays-allowed tests)

## Summary

- Adds `lib/agenttools_taskref/` — a new shared library that validates a candidate task/ticket code (`--task CODE`, `$REVIEW_TASK_CODE`, or any similar free-form "which ticket is this for" string) against a repo's own `task.yaml` / `rig.yaml` `task:` block, read the same way task-cli's own `tasklib/config.py` reads it.
- `backend: github-issues` — only a real, resolvable issue/PR number in the repo's own `github.repo` (or an explicit `owner/repo#N` cross-repo form) validates, confirmed via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>` (the issues endpoint also resolves PR numbers — verified live against alex-mextner/review-cli#419). A numeric-shaped string that 404s is rejected exactly like a free-text slug.
- `backend: linear` — only a code carrying the repo's actual configured `linear.team` prefix validates; a mismatched/made-up prefix names the correct one.
- An absent `task.yaml`/`rig.yaml` is deliberately NOT itself a rejection — task-cli works with zero config on an ordinary GitHub repo (defaults to `github-issues` + `github.repo: auto` resolved from git `origin`), and this library matches that. The real "unresolvable" failure is a `github-issues` repo with no git origin, or a `linear` repo with no configured team.

## Why

A live sweep of `~/.config/review-cli/run-stats.jsonl` this session found the ecosystem's history full of invented, non-resolvable task codes recorded as if they were real ticket references — bare placeholders like `CODE`/`TEST-1`, free-text slugs like `ambiguous-create-dedup`, and at least one fabricated code (`RIG-CLI-298-VERSION-BUMP`) caught live this session. ## Scope

Wiring review-cli's `--task CODE` / `$REVIEW_TASK_CODE` to actually call this validator is tracked separately as [review-cli#427](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/427) — it needs a deliberate test-seam decision (dozens of review-cli's own tests use placeholder codes like `TEST-1`/`CODE` against a tmp `REVIEW_STATS_FILE`), rather than a fail-closed change rushed into this PR. title: fix(worktree-only-writes): stop silently substituting cwd for an unresolvable write target
body:
WORKTREE-ONLY-TARGET-DIR

Refs #615

## What
`worktree_only_writes.py`'s `_target_dir()` fell back to the bare session `cwd` when `args` carried no file_path/path/notebook_path at all — with NO signal that a fallback happened (undocumented, unintentional).

## What changed
- `cwd` is now a **deliberate, documented, tested** fallback for the no-usable-path case (agent-tools#615), not the prior implicit fallthrough. An earlier iteration of this PR instead made this case fail-open (allow); adversarial review (review-cli, xai/grok-4.6 security seat, then claude-fable-5 architect seat) found that a real regression: codex's `apply_patch` bridge (its only write tool) genuinely produces a path-less pre-write event when its patch-envelope parser finds no file path in the command text — failing open there would silently disable the guard on a real main-branch write. Reverted to keep judging `cwd` directly, now with a docstring/tests making the choice explicit instead of an accidental fallthrough. A key present but blank/wrong-typed gets the identical outcome (no incoherent split between the two "no path signal" shapes).
- Investigated fixing the companion relative-hashline-path bug reported live in #613 (cwd on the primary/main checkout, the file really being edited living in a separate feature-branch worktree) by resolving a relative path against whichever OTHER git worktree of the same repo actually had it on disk. **That approach was reverted** — adversarial review found it exploitable: a relative write whose underlying tool resolves the path against `cwd` (main) would be silently ALLOWED whenever any sibling worktree happened to already track a file at that same relative path. A relative path is still judged against `cwd`, unchanged from before this PR, documented as a known limitation in `_target_dir`'s docstring — the sound fix (omp exposing an already-resolved absolute path via the bridge) is tracked in #616.

## Tests
- `tests/test_worktree_only_writes.py`: unit tests asserting the deliberate cwd fallback (missing key, blank key, wrong-typed key — all identical outcome); an integration test asserting BLOCK on an enrolled main-branch cwd with no path key (the codex apply_patch-parse-miss shape); a regression test proving a coincidental sibling-worktree match no longer bypasses the guard.
- `tests/test_omp_hook_bridge.py`: the sibling-worktree-bypass regression proven through the full bridge → hook chain with a real hashline patch.
- Every behavioral test was verified to genuinely FAIL against the pre-fix/pre-revert code at each stage (confirmed by temporarily reverting and re-running).

Full targeted suite: `tests/test_worktree_only_writes.py`, `tests/test_omp_hook_bridge.py`, `tests/test_hatch_import_hardening.py` — 153 passed.

## Review history (why this PR went through multiple revisions)
This PR went through 3 substantive review-driven revisions before settling, each catching a real issue:

title: fix(omp-hook-bridge): map eval/hub tool calls to pre-write/pre-bash hook points
body:
Closes #614

## What
`lib/omp_hook_bridge/dispatch.py`'s `point_for_event` only recognized `bash`/`edit`/`write`/`apply_patch`/`notebook`/`task` — an omp `eval` tool_call (arbitrary code that can write files) or `hub` tool_call (`op:start` launches a background process) silently bypassed every installed hook.

## Fix
- `eval` → write-shaped (`pre-write`/`post-write`). `_eval_content_buckets` heuristically scrapes `Path(...).write_text/write_bytes`, `Bun.write`, `fs.write*/append*` (Sync or not, with or without `fs.` prefix), `open(...).write(...)`, and a path-less bare `.write(...)`/`.write_text(...)` fallback — escape-aware, string-prefix- and backtick-literal-tolerant, and escape-DECODING. Every write call's content is aggregated per resolved target (never just the first), and a multi-target call (including a path-less bucket) fans out one v1 event per target, mirroring `edit`/`apply_patch`. Forged `file_paths`/`command`/`path` are always stripped.
- `hub` → `pre-bash`. `_hub_command` synthesizes an argv string via `shlex.join` from `op:start`'s `application`+`args`; every other op synthesizes no command. `hub`'s own `input.cwd` overrides the session cwd on the synthesized event, so cwd-sensitive hooks judge the right directory.
- `eval`'s `command` field is forced empty regardless of any raw `command` key, closing a fallback path-allowlist bypass in `block-secrets-write`.

## Argument-shape assumptions (uncertain — documented in code comments)
- `eval` input: `{language, code, title?, reset?, timeout?}` (also accepts `content` as an alternate key for the code string).
- `hub` input: `{op, application?, args?, name?, cwd?, env?, ready?, ...}`.
Neither is pinned by omp's own docs; inferred from the harness's own tool schemas and documented precisely as best-effort in `dispatch.py` and `README.md`.

## Tests
`tests/test_omp_hook_bridge.py`: new unit tests for `point_for_event` mapping, hub cwd forwarding, and eval write-scraping; end-to-end tests proving real `block-secrets-write`/`no-long-inline-process` descriptors fire against eval- and hub-shaped events, including every bypass class found during review (decoy-path `ALLOW_PATH` hiding, multi-target fan-out, path-less-bucket dropping, backtick/escape decoding, `open()` path-concatenation misattribution). Full suite verified passing (85 test cases, including parametrized) via direct function-level execution — the machine's `pytest`-invocation memory-pressure gate was intermittently active from concurrent sibling work during this session.

title: fix(omp-hook-bridge): map tool_call+yield to v1 stop

This maps `tool_call`+`yield` → v1 `stop` so `stop-completion-selfcheck` fires before the helper parks. Yield retries share a stable session id (not per-call toolCallId) so the cooldown cannot wedge.

title: fix(ship): authorize review-quorum on filled roles, not models
body:
## What
Review-quorum (Guard-B) now authorizes on **roles filled** (`distinct_roles_passed`), not `distinct_models_passed`.

One padded model (review-cli#433 / astra) filling every board role ships **without** a Telegram hatch. `distinct_models_passed` is telemetry — 0 or 1 is fine. `passed_iterations` must be >0 (hollow-payload guard) but need not meet `MIN_ITER` when roles are filled. review-cli `passed=false` (it still ANDs min_iter) does not block.

`SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM=0` is **forbidden**: rejected at parse, gate stays enabled. Test isolation uses `SHIP_TEST_DISABLE_REVIEW_QUORUM=1` only.

Hatch Telegram context leads with `distinct_roles_passed`; zero models/iterations are omitted so Alex no longer sees `distinct_models: 0` / `iterations: 0`.

## Why
Alex 2026-09-08: many ship-review-quorum hatch Approves. One model must fill every role (full orthogonality). Hatch payload still showed distinct_models: 0, iterations: 0.

title: fix(orchestrator-stays-thin): recognize nested omp subagent regardless of harness label
body:
## What

`orchestrator_stays_thin.py`'s `_is_omp_nested_session()` no longer restricts its nested-`PI_SESSION_FILE` subagent-identity trust tier to `event["harness"] == "omp"`. It now recognizes a nested omp Task/eval child regardless of which model harness backs that omp session (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, or an untagged harness).

## Why

That restriction made the trust tier unreachable for a Claude-Code-backed omp session — the machine default per `rig.yaml`'s `harness.kind: claude-code` — because `cc_hook_bridge` always stamps `event["harness"] == "claude-code"`. That field identifies the hook **transport**, not whether omp is orchestrating on top of it. As a result, a genuine nested omp Task/eval subagent running under that harness was misclassified as the top-level orchestrator, and its `git commit` was denied by the "stay thin" gate (live incident, agent-tools#676).

The sibling hook `no-long-inline-process/no_long_inline_process.py` has the identical trust tier and never had this `harness == "omp"` restriction — this fix brings the two back into lockstep.

This is a corroborating duplicate of agent-tools#679: a single-level Task-tool child hitting the identical block on `gh`/multi-step-bash commands (not just `git commit`), same root cause. #679 should close as duplicate-fixed once this merges.

## Test

- `tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py`: replaced the now-incorrect `test_nested_pi_session_does_not_exempt_non_omp_harness` (which pinned exactly the bug's behavior) with `test_nested_pi_session_exempts_regardless_of_harness` (parametrized over claude-code/codex/opencode) and `test_nested_pi_session_exempts_with_no_harness_tag`. Added `test_main_pi_session_file_still_blocks_regardless_of_harness` as a new regression guard (the original `test_orchestrator_git_commit_still_blocks_with_main_pi_session_file` is unchanged). Added `test_single_level_nested_session_exempts_gh_and_multistep_bash_claude_code` (parametrized over `gh issue list` / `gh pr checks 123` / a multi-step bash chain), covering the #679 duplicate.
- `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py`: added two clean-room end-to-end tests that drive the **real** `cc_hook_bridge` subprocess plus the **real** `orchestrator-stays-thin` script against a **real** temp git repo:
  - `test_nested_omp_subagent_under_claude_code_harness_git_commit_allowed_clean_room` — the #676 repro. Proves the git commit is now allowed, and actually performs it.
  - `test_bare_orchestrator_git_commit_still_blocked_clean_room` — precision control proving a genuine top-level orchestrator with no subagent identity at all is still warn-then-blocked through the same real pipeline.

Verified: the new allow-path test fails on the pre-fix code with the exact same block message as the live incident, and passes on the fixed code. Full targeted suite (`test_cc_hook_bridge.py`, `test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py`, `test_no_long_inline_process.py`, `test_omp_hook_bridge.py`) is green — 791 passed.

title: fix(ship): detect billing-block CI outage via check-run annotation text
body:
## What

`ci_appears_structurally_down` (in `ci/ship/ship.sh`) had two outage signals: the
GitHub status page, and a run-level timing heuristic (`_ci_runs_timing_suspicious`,
all workflow runs completing in under 30s). Neither caught a real billing-block
outage hit live today on `sme-archiving-gc` PR #401: GitHub queued the run for
2m33s before rejecting the job — the job itself only took 2s once it (didn't)
start — so the run's overall wall-clock span looked nowhere near "suspiciously
fast," and `ship` refused to fall through to the local fallback gate even though
this was exactly the outage that gate exists for.

Confirmed root cause via the GitHub API directly: the check-run's own annotation
carries GitHub's fixed message verbatim: *"The job was not started because recent
account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased."*

## Fix

Added `_ci_billing_block_annotation_detected`: for the PR's head SHA, list
check-runs, and for every one with `conclusion == "failure"`, fetch its
annotations and match that fixed message text (case-insensitive, tolerant of
either the payments or spending-limit half). Wired in as a third OR'd signal
alongside the status-page and timing checks — same permissive semantics, same
fail-safe-to-"0" behavior on any API hiccup.

## Testing

- Added `test_billing_block_annotation_detected_without_escape_hatch`, which
  does **not** set `SHIP_TEST_CI_DOWN=1` — it drives the real detection path
  with a fake `gh` answering the two actual `gh api` calls the new function
  makes, and asserts `billing_block=1` / `timing_suspicious=0` specifically, to
  prove the new signal (not an old one) is what fires.
- Full suite: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ship.py -q` → **282 passed**.
- `shellcheck -x ci/ship/ship.sh` → no new warnings (only pre-existing ones,
  unrelated to this diff).

## Review

`review diff --task SHIP-BILLING-ANNOTATION --preset light` was attempted but
every provider in the pool failed on the same outage already tracked in
review-cli#460 (GLM/Grok weekly quota exhaustion, resets 2026-09-10 21:15). Fell
back to a careful manual self-review — traced both new `gh api` calls against the
real GitHub responses that reproduced PR #401's failure, and confirmed the OR-wiring
preserves prior behavior when `head_sha` lookup itself fails.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(stop-completion-selfcheck): harden marker freshness + JSONL tail parsing
body:
## Summary
Hardens `stop-completion-selfcheck`:
- HEDGE-pattern doc wording fix (non-functional).
- `fresh()`: a future-dated marker mtime (clock skew, restored cache, tampered/copied file) no longer reads as "fresh" — treated the same as absent/stale, since the marker is no longer consumed on allow, so a future mtime could otherwise suppress the self-check indefinitely.
- `_tail_lines`: switched from `splitlines()` to `split("\n")` — `splitlines()` also splits on `\r`, NEL, U+2028/U+2029, which CC's JSON.stringify does not escape inside a string value, so a raw one pasted into a tool_use input/result would get spuriously cut in two and silently dropped by the following `json.loads` failure, which could misclassify a worked turn as LIGHT/HEDGE.
- Turn-boundary detection: a `tool_result` block alongside a `text` block in the same record (e.g. CC injecting a system-reminder mid-turn) is now also recognized as a continuation, not a new user turn boundary.
- New regression coverage (37 tests) for all of the above.

Recovered from a stray worktree (real, substantial uncommitted work — 1174 lines) during a repo-wide worktree reconciliation sweep.

**Not yet rebased onto current main** — `stop_selfcheck.py` has diverged significantly since this branch's base and a mechanical rebase produced 8 conflicts including one spanning ~500 lines; rather than risk a rushed/incorrect resolution of a safety-critical hook under time pressure, this is pushed on its original base for a deliberate follow-up rebase pass. Marked draft for that reason.
