title: fix(orchestrator-stays-thin): exempt data-only cat-heredoc substitution from HEREDOC veto (#699)
body:
Fixes agent-tools#699.

## Root cause
orchestrator-stays-thin's `HEREDOC` regex unconditionally marks ANY heredoc as implementation-shaped, checked in `_is_all_inline_allowed` and `_is_implementation_bash` *before* the documented `tg`/`review` sanctioned-orchestration exemption ever runs. A live incident (Alex, 2026-09-09) showed a subagent's routine `tg --tag report --format html "$(cat <<'EOF' ...multi-line HTML report... EOF)"` -- the standard, quote-safe way to hand a large multi-paragraph message to `tg` without hand-escaping every embedded quote/apostrophe -- hard-BLOCKing, then needing a live Telegram hatch escalation just to get through. This contradicts AGENTS.md's documented claim that tg/review are 'never gated'.

## Fix
Add `_DATA_HEREDOC_SUBST` + `_neutralize_data_only_heredocs()`: recognizes ONLY the narrow, verified-safe shape `$(cat <<'DELIM' ... DELIM)` / backtick-`cat` where the heredoc's terminator is immediately followed (whitespace only) by the substitution's own closing paren/backtick -- i.e. `cat`'s stdout is captured ONLY by the substitution, never written to a file or executed. That shape is neutralized to an inert placeholder before the rest of the module's heredoc/mutation/chain-length classification runs. Every other heredoc (a real write, `bash <<EOF` execution, one that doesn't immediately close its substitution) is untouched and still trips `HEREDOC` exactly as before.

## Testing
- All 435 pre-existing tests in `tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py` still pass unmodified (including the three heredoc-blocks pins: `test_tg_command_with_heredoc_still_blocks`, `test_heredoc_to_file_blocks_on_repeat`, `test_read_only_pipe_with_heredoc_segment_blocks_on_repeat`).
- 8 new regression tests added, including the exact incident command shape (`test_tg_report_with_data_only_heredoc_allows`), the `review` equivalent, a laundering-resistance check (a data-only heredoc feeding a chain with a real mutation still blocks), the backtick form, and a parametrized negative-case sweep (exec heredoc, write heredoc, non-`cat` head) confirming the carve-out does not over-match.
- `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_orchestrator_stays_thin.py -q` -> 443 passed.

title: feat(ship): auto-bypass review-quorum/external-review hatches on confirmed fleet-wide capacity outage
body:
## What

Wires `ci/ship/ship.sh`'s review-quorum (Guard-B) and external-review hatch gates to consult review-cli's own `review capacity-check --json` before ever prompting the manual `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_REVIEW_QUORUM` / `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW` Telegram hatch.

Adds `_review_capacity_all_exhausted`, which fails closed on any missing `review`/`jq` binary, non-zero exit, unparseable JSON, or a missing/non-true `all_exhausted` key. ONLY when review-cli confirms every configured board seat is exhausted right now does ship auto-proceed, with an audited justification (`auto-proceed:capacity-outage` / `external-review:auto-proceed:capacity-outage` in `SHIP_AUDIT_FILE`) instead of prompting.

Every other refusal reason (too few iterations/roles, an undiscoverable task code, zero GitHub reviews with nobody having looked, a genuine CI failure) is completely unaffected — the green-CI gate runs unconditionally earlier in the script and already blocks a real test failure before either hatch gate is ever reached.

Companion slice: review-cli's own `review capacity-check --json` / `board_capacity_report()` (the contract this consumes) landed in [alex-mextner/review-cli#473](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/473).

## Why

Alex has repeatedly complained that every PR across the fleet hits the same manual hatch prompt for the identical, already-diagnosed root cause: a fleet-wide review-cli provider capacity outage that no individual PR can control. The gate is doing its job (correctly refusing/escalating) but re-escalating the SAME known cause on every single PR wastes his time and trains him to rubber-stamp the hatch.

## Safety

- Auto-bypass fires ONLY on positive, machine-readable confirmation that every configured seat is exhausted (`all_exhausted: true`, which itself requires `models` non-empty and `available` empty). Any seat with no evidence keeps `all_exhausted: false`, which alone preserves today's exact manual-hatch-or-refuse behavior.
- A genuinely red CI is never waved through: the green-CI gate runs unconditionally earlier in the linear `set -euo pipefail` script and `exit 1`s on an unresolved real failure before either hatch gate is ever reached — proven by `test_review_quorum_real_ci_failure_still_blocks_even_with_all_exhausted_capacity` (a real, non-outage-shaped CI failure blocks regardless of a faked all-exhausted capacity-check).
- Decision strings are `auto-proceed:capacity-outage` / `external-review:auto-proceed:capacity-outage` — deliberately not containing the substring `"bypass:"`, so rig-cli's `hatches.py` abuse dashboard never miscounts an auto-resolved gate as a manual agent-invoked hatch.
- No ambient env-var off-switch — this is a pure additive capability, always consulted, always fail-closed on any uncertainty.

## Tests

5 new tests in `tests/test_ship.py`:
- `test_review_quorum_auto_bypasses_on_confirmed_fleet_exhaustion`
- `test_review_quorum_partial_exhaustion_still_blocks`
- `test_review_quorum_real_ci_failure_still_blocks_even_with_all_exhausted_capacity`
- `test_external_review_auto_bypasses_on_confirmed_fleet_exhaustion`
- `test_external_review_partial_exhaustion_still_blocks`

All 5 pass. Full scoped rerun (`pytest tests/test_ship.py -k "review_quorum or external_review"`) — 97 passed, 0 regressed, confirming every pre-existing test's outcome is unchanged.

## Docs

- `ci/ship/README.md` — extended the review-quorum and external-review gate table rows.
- `ci/ship/ship.sh` header comments for both `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SHIP_*` knobs.
- `AGENTS.md` — new bullet in the "Hatch requests are an ask, not a grant" section.

title: fix(hooks): audit every hatch attempt in one dispatch, not just the first
body:
## What

Refs #713: `overrides.log` (the `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` escape-hatch audit sink,
gap G-8) silently dropped later hatch attempts when a single dispatch
invocation carried more than one `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` var at once.

## Why

Every harness bridge (`cc_hook_bridge`, `codex_hook_bridge`,
`opencode_hook_bridge`, `omp_hook_bridge`) runs the applicable `agents-hooks/v1`
descriptors for one logical point in priority order, and previously returned
as soon as the FIRST descriptor blocked:

```python
for spec in specs:
    outcome, reason = run_hook(spec, v1_event, warn=_warn)
    if outcome == "block":
        return reason        # later specs never ran
return None
```

Each hatch-using hook only calls `request_hatch_approval` (and therefore
`agenttools_hatch_escalation._append_overrides_log`) from inside its own
subprocess. If an earlier descriptor denied its own hatch and blocked, every
LATER descriptor — including any of its own pending hatch requests — never
ran at all, so its hatch attempt vanished from the audit trail with zero
signal.

## Fix

All four `dispatch.py` modules now run every descriptor for the point to
completion, tracking only the FIRST blocking reason to return. The
harness-visible block decision is unchanged (still the first blocker's
reason, verified unchanged by the existing `test_first_block_wins_collects_reason`)
— only audit completeness is fixed.

## Testing

- New regression test `test_multiple_hatch_vars_in_one_invocation_are_all_audited`
  in `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py`: installs two pre-bash descriptors, each
  with its own `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` var set to a blank value (a real "use" of
  the mechanism that is denied locally, never contacts `tg-ctl`), runs one
  dispatch, and asserts `overrides.log` has one entry per hatch id.
  - Verified this test FAILS on the pre-fix loop (only the first hatch id is
    recorded) and PASSES after the fix.
- Full `tests/test_cc_hook_bridge.py` suite: 65 passed.
- `tests/test_codex_hook_bridge.py`, `tests/test_opencode_hook_bridge.py`,
  `tests/test_omp_hook_bridge.py`: 183 passed, 1 pre-existing failure
  (`test_codex_bridge_without_env_marker_still_blocks_long_process_end_to_end`)
  confirmed to fail identically on a clean `main` checkout — unrelated to this
  change, not touched here.

title: fix(review): stream backend output live + preserve partial output on timeout
body:
## Problem

`_run()` used `subprocess.run(stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, timeout=...)` for **every**
backend call. That has two failure modes the panel modes (`--brainstorm`/`--quorum`/
`--just-ask`) hit hard:

1. **Zero real-time visibility** — `subprocess.run` blocks until the child exits, so a
   long codex/claude run looks frozen the entire time.
2. **Partial output is lost on timeout** — on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` the exception
   propagates and the captured buffer is discarded, so a timed-out panel call returned
   **empty** after exit 124 instead of the partial answer.

## Fix

New streaming runner `_run_streamed()` (`subprocess.Popen`) for the long backend calls
(codex / opencode / claude). `_git_diff` and the opencode `git init` stay on the plain,
quiet `_run`.

- **Real-time tee** — stdout *and* stderr are drained on daemon threads, each line
  appended to an in-memory accumulator **and** flushed to a per-call log file under
  `~/.cache/review-cli/logs/` (override `$REVIEW_LOG_DIR`). `tail -f` shows live progress.
- **Announce** — panel modes print the live-log path to stderr at the start of each call;
  the plain single-diff review path stays quiet.
- **Partial-on-timeout** — the timeout is enforced on the **process** via
  `proc.wait(timeout)` (not on pipe EOF), so a leaked stdout fd held by an
  escaped/daemonized descendant can never hang the call. On timeout the child's whole
  **process group** is `SIGTERM`→`SIGKILL`ed and the partial buffer is **returned** with
  a `[review-cli] TIMEOUT after Ns — partial output above]` marker and returncode 124 —
  never raised away.
- **Hardening from review** — log dir 0700 / files 0600 (logs persist reviewed
  prompts/diffs that may carry secrets); the log header records only `backend + argv[0]`,
  not the full argv; the log handle always closes via `try/finally`; the process group is
  reaped even after the direct child exits or escapes.
- Returns a `CompletedProcess`-compatible object, so `review_codex`/`review_opencode`/
  `review_claude` needed only a one-line swap. **Happy path is unchanged** — full output
  still returned and printed at the end.

## Evidence (real codex)

- **Real-time:** during `review --brainstorm … -m codex`, the live log grew incrementally
  while the child ran (e.g. model-output lines 17 → 32 → ... mid-run), not all-at-once at
  exit.
- **Partial-on-timeout:** `review --just-ask "…long…" -m codex --timeout 5` now returns
  `## codex [exit 124]` with the `TIMEOUT after 5s` marker and the captured preamble,
  instead of empty. No orphan codex processes survive (process group reaped).
- **Happy path:** `review --just-ask "ping: reply OK" -m codex` → `OK`, exit 0.

## Tests

`tests/test_streaming.py` (wired into `tests/smoke.sh`), all stdlib, no backends required:
- log grows incrementally **before** the child exits;
- timeout preserves partial stdout + marker, rc 124;
- a grandchild **in** the process group doesn't hang the runner and is reaped;
- a grandchild that **escapes** the process group (own session, inherits stdout) still
  doesn't hang — timeout is independent of pipe EOF;
- clean exit with a child holding the pipe returns rc 0 and leaks no grandchild;
- log files are 0600.

`bash tests/smoke.sh` green. Reviewed with `codex exec review` across multiple rounds; all
findings (process-tree kill, log perms, handle leak, stderr-drain race, watchdog
false-positive, returncode, EOF-independent timeout) fixed.

title: fix(brainstorm): stdin transcript, incremental discussion log, standard log dir
body:
The claude backend died at brainstorm round 2+: the round prompt embeds the whole
prior transcript and was passed as a `-p <payload>` ARGV argument, which grows
past ARG_MAX (~1 MB) → execve E2BIG → no output. Now fed over STDIN like the codex
backend's `-`.

Also:
- **Incremental discussion log** (`<logdir>/<stamp>-brainstorm.md`, 0600, O_EXCL,
  tail -f-able) flushed per round + moderator decision + synthesis. The whole
  conversation used to be held in memory and printed only at the end, so a
  timeout/kill lost everything. A read-only log dir degrades to no-log, never
  takes down a brainstorm.
- **Standard log location**: ~/.cache → macOS `~/Library/Logs/review-cli`, Linux
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/review-cli/logs` (relative XDG ignored; default ~/.local/state).
  `$REVIEW_LOG_DIR` override preserved.

Review-gate findings addressed: claude-p's inner `claude` exec still re-argv's the
prompt and the opencode backend's CLI is argv-only, so the ~1 MB ceiling isn't
fully gone — `_payload` now prints a size WARNING and the README says so honestly.
New tests: stdin payload > pipe buffer round-trips without deadlock; log_dir
darwin/XDG/relative branches. All 11 streaming tests pass.

`review dashboard` — a local-only web dashboard for the review-cli logs. Boots a SPA
served from `127.0.0.1` (loopback only, no external bind), reads the JSONL chat logs from

9. **Prompts** — prompts issued per run

title: feat(review): opus-first moderator with runtime fallback + git-root cwd resolution
body:
Two related review-side improvements requested after the headless-opus fix landed. Two clean commits, bundled in one PR because they touch adjacent lines of `tests/smoke.sh`.

## 1. Moderator: opus-first priority + runtime fallback (`e43102c`)
The `--quorum`/`--brainstorm` moderator was chosen once up front and called with no recovery — if that backend failed or hung at run time the synthesis was lost. And it couldn't be opus, because the headless claude backend was unreliable (now fixed).

- `MODERATOR_CANDIDATES = (claude:claude-opus-4-8, codex, gemini)` — **opus is the default moderator**, codex/gemini are fallbacks.
- `pick_moderators()` returns the ordered candidate list (explicit `--moderator` first, then available candidates, then `panel[0]`; order-preserving de-dup).
- `run_moderator()` walks that list **at run time**: first result that succeeds (exit 0 + non-empty) wins; otherwise it logs and falls back to the next. This catches what a cheap availability probe can't — a backend whose binary exists but that dies at run time (e.g. an Anthropic-disabled model like fable times out / returns empty). All-empty-success is normalized to a failure so callers never report a synthesis that isn't there; a lone moderator string is tolerated.
- `brainstorm` promotes the candidate that actually worked to the front, so a dead top moderator is paid **once**, not re-tried at the head of every round + the final synthesis.

## 2. cwd: resolve to git repo root + warn off-repo + document `-C` (`da3ac4b`)
review runs the diff and the claude/opus workspace in `cwd` (default `.`). Agents commonly invoke it from a scratch/temp dir and forget `-C`, so it silently reviewed the wrong place (**often /tmp**) and returned an empty/irrelevant result.

- `_effective_cwd()` resolves to the enclosing git repo root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, also robust from a subdir) and **warns loudly** when cwd is not a git repo, pointing the caller at `-C <project-root>`.
- The skill (`reviewlib/install.py`) now shows `-C <repo>` in every example, adds an **"ALWAYS pass -C"** section, and documents the non-tty stdin trap (`review … < /dev/null`). Blurb mirrors it.

## Tests
- `tests/test_moderator.py` — 10 cases (ordering / availability filter / de-dup / first-success / exit-fallback / empty-output-fallback / all-fail / all-empty-is-failure / single-string).
- `tests/test_cwd.py` — repo-root / subdir-resolves-to-root / non-repo-warns.
- Both added to `smoke.sh`; full smoke green. One codex review round on each commit; all findings addressed.

title: feat(claude): API backend variant (Anthropic-compatible) alongside the CLI
body:
Requested follow-up: make the claude/opus backend work where the `claude` CLI isn't installed but an API key is. Adds an HTTP variant so the backend runs **two ways**.

## API variant (new)
`review_claude_api()` POSTs the **Anthropic Messages format** to `{ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL}/v1/messages` (default `https://api.anthropic.com`; point it at any Anthropic-compatible gateway — e.g. **CommandCode** via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). Needs only a key — no `claude` binary, no workspace.

- **Auth mirrors the Anthropic SDK / claude CLI env surface:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → `x-api-key`, else `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` → `Authorization: Bearer`. Sends `anthropic-version` + a non-default `User-Agent` (some gateways behind Cloudflare 403 the bare urllib UA with "error code: 1010").
- Parses `content[].text`; **empty output, HTTP errors, and malformed/unreadable responses** all become a normal nonzero `ReviewResult` so the moderator fallback engages instead of crashing.

## Dispatcher
`review_claude()` now routes:
- `REVIEW_CLAUDE_MODE=api|cli` forces a variant.
- Otherwise **conservative auto**: the CLI when the `claude` binary is present (subscription, no API cost, reliable now that workspace trust is deterministic), the API only when there's no binary but a key is set. **A stray key in the env never silently switches a working CLI host to the paid API.**

The claude-p path is unchanged, extracted verbatim to `review_claude_cli` (shared read-only system prompt → `_CLAUDE_REVIEW_SYSTEM`). `backend_available("claude:...")` mirrors the dispatcher (forced mode → that variant; else key OR claude-p). The skill documents both modes + env vars + the actual auto-selection.

## Tests
- `tests/test_claude_api.py` — 14 cases: dispatch matrix (incl. the key-present-but-CLI-wins regression guard), request shape/headers/payload, x-api-key vs Bearer, HTTP-error + malformed-JSON surfacing, empty-output-as-failure, mode-aware `backend_available`.
- Two existing tests updated to target `review_claude_cli` directly (the dispatcher is now env-dependent).

title: feat(review): reviewer board — per-model role lenses (HYP-741)
body:
Stacked on #5 (commandcode/z.ai provider backends + api|cli mode). **Do not merge before #5.**

## What
A configurable **reviewer board**: the default plain `review` panel assigns each model its OWN review role/lens, so the panel covers the diff broadly instead of every model doing the same generic pass. Built into the existing diff-review path (one `PanelJob` per reviewer); the opus-first moderator is unchanged.

## The board (out of the box, no config file needed)
| Reviewer | Backend | Role | Lens focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opus | `claude:claude-opus-4-8` | architect | architecture, design coherence, API shape, abstraction boundaries |
| Codex | `codex` | correctness | logic bugs, regressions, edge cases, null/async/race, off-by-one |
| Gemini | `gemini` | consistency | cross-file consistency, dead refs, contract drift, whole-repo coherence |
| DeepSeek | `commandcode:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` | performance | complexity, hot paths, allocations, async/concurrency, N+1 |
| Kimi | `commandcode:moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` | quality | readability, naming, duplication, code smells, idiom |
| Qwen | `commandcode:Qwen/Qwen3.7-Max` | security | injection, authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, SSRF |
| GLM | `commandcode:zai-org/GLM-5.1` | tests | missing tests, untested branches, boundary conditions, error-path coverage |

commandcode model ids are byte-exact against the gateway /models catalog.

## How config.yaml drives it
```yaml
board:
  - { model: "claude:claude-opus-4-8", role: architect }
  - { model: "commandcode:Qwen/Qwen3.7-Max", role: security, name: Qwen }
```
`load_board()` validates each entry: unknown `role` -> keeps the reviewer but uses the generic prompt (warns, never crashes); a malformed entry is skipped; empty/absent `board:` -> the built-in `DEFAULT_BOARD`. Model aliases expand (`glm46` -> `zai:glm-4.6`).

## CLI
- Board is the **default** for plain review. An explicit `-m` (exact models) or `--no-board` bypasses it.
- `review --show-board` lists `model -> role` + live availability (read-only; no key printed, no model called).

## Graceful degradation
A reviewer whose backend isn't available (no key / not on PATH) is **skipped and logged** via `backend_available` — the board shrinks, never crashes. commandcode reviewers need `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`, gemini needs its key; absent -> they drop out and the board runs with Opus/Codex/Gemini.

## Security
No API key is ever written to disk — keys are only READ from env / the existing `~/.config/review-cli/.env` loader. Tests mock urllib / subprocess; no live model calls.

## Tests / gate
- `tests/test_reviewer_board.py` — 18 cases: default-board shape (byte-exact), config parsing (override / unknown-role fallback / bad-entry skip / alias expand), role-lens injection, graceful skip of unavailable reviewers, `mode_review` board path exit codes, CLI wiring (explicit -m / --no-board disable, default activates). All offline.
- Full `tests/smoke.sh` green (incl. existing provider-keys + visual suites).
- `codex exec review --uncommitted`: no actionable issues.

title: feat(specweb): interactive web reviewer for spec markdown (HYP-743)
body:
## What

A new universal subcommand **`review spec-web <spec.md>`** — an interactive web server for reviewing a spec, GitHub-review style.

- **Select any text** in the rendered spec → popup → **ask a question / leave a comment** anchored to that selection.
- Comments accumulate in a **pending batch** (a "Pending review (N)" tray); one **Submit review** flips them to `submitted`.
- **Inline answers** thread under each comment; status lifecycle `pending → submitted → answered → resolved`, with filters.
- Reusable for **any** spec markdown file; serve over **Tailscale** to review from a phone.

## Layout

- **Desktop (≥900px):** two panes side-by-side (spec left, comments right, draggable divider).
- **Mobile (<900px):** comments as a **bottom sheet** under the spec.
- Both panes **collapse/expand** from the topbar.

## Architecture (`reviewlib/specweb/`)

- **`render.py`** — markdown → HTML server-side, GitHub heading-slug scheme (so the spec's own `[§9.4](#94-…)` links resolve). Figures referenced as `./assets/fig-*.svg|png` are served as **real HTTP resources** at `/asset/<name>` (never inlined — the bug a prior static file had). Link-scheme sanitization + XSS-safe href handling for untrusted specs.
- **`store.py`** — per-spec JSON store at `~/.config/review-cli/spec-web/<sha1-of-abspath>.json` (mode `0600`), comment/reply/pending→submit lifecycle, seed import, markdown export.
- **`server.py`** — stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Reads open; writes origin-guarded (**Host allowlist + CSRF Origin match + `Content-Type` + body-size cap**, anti-DNS-rebinding). Tailscale identity **discovered at runtime** (`tailscale status`), never hardcoded; figures-only asset serving with symlink-escape defence.
- **`static/`** — vanilla JS+CSS SPA. Quote re-anchoring is offset-aware, handles cross-node selections (spanning inline markup) and multi-thread sharing on one passage, with an "unanchored" sidebar fallback (never crashes).

## Routes

`GET /` · `GET /static/<app.css|app.js>` · `GET /asset/<name>` · `GET /api/spec` · `GET /api/comments` · `GET /api/export` · `POST /api/comments` · `POST /api/comments/<id>/{reply,status,delete}` · `POST /api/submit` · `POST /api/import`

## Quality

- **41 spec-web tests** (render slugs/figures/XSS, store CRUD/submit/seed/export/0600, server routes, origin-guard + anti-rebinding, symlink-escape, unanchored fallback) + smoke wiring. **Full suite green.**
- **`codex exec review --uncommitted`**: clean final verdict — *"I did not find any actionable correctness, security, or maintainability issues"* — after iterative hardening of ~18 rounds of findings.
- **Browser smoke** (headless Chrome): desktop (1400px) + mobile (390px) confirmed — spec renders, figures load, mobile = comments at bottom; cross-node and duplicate-quote anchoring verified.

title: feat(review): per-run stats + startup ETA + no-external-timeout advertising (HYP-744)
body:
## What & why

HYP-744 — give `review` per-run stats, a startup ETA, and a no-external-timeout contract so agents stop short-timeouting a multi-model / multi-round run (which only emits its synthesis at the very end). Two commits: the existing per-run stats + ETA commit (rebased onto current `origin/main` — the spec-web #11 + dashboard #6 merges), and a new commit completing the no-external-timeout / internal-backstop piece.

## The 3 spec points

1. **Run-stats log** — every run that dispatches a backend appends a structured record (mode, pool_size, model names, real monotonic wall-clock, ok/fail counts) to an append-only JSONL at `~/.config/review-cli/run-stats.jsonl` (0600; `$REVIEW_STATS_FILE`-overridable). `reviewlib/stats.py` + `cli._run_mode_with_stats`. *(already implemented; verified)*
2. **Startup pool-ETA** — at dispatch, before the long work, `review` prints a one-line ETA to stderr keyed on `(mode, pool_size)` (falls back to pool-only, then a "no history yet, expect MINUTES" line). `reviewlib/stats.py:announce_eta`. *(already implemented; verified)*
3. **No external timeout + internal ≤4h backstop** — *(added in this PR)* `review` now advertises and behaves as having NO external timeout. The only bound is an INTERNAL ≤4h backstop (`reviewlib/backstop.py`): `main()` arms a watchdog that force-terminates a genuinely wedged run with exit 124. `$REVIEW_BACKSTOP_SECONDS` can only LOWER the ceiling, never raise it past 4h. The SKILL.md / blurb / README now state this and the old contradictory "if you must bound it, give it MINUTES" bullet was removed.

## Backstop hardening (from the codex review rounds)

- **KILL-FIRST child reaping** — on fire it SIGKILLs each registered backend subprocess's OWN session group (no blocking SIGTERM grace), so even a SIGTERM-ignoring backend is bound and the reap can't be preempted by the deadman. A child registry in `process.py` (`_register_child` / `kill_live_children`) makes the backends — which run in their own sessions and survive a plain exit — findable.
- **Never kills the caller** — it never signals the CLI's own / the caller's process group (`review` is often a child sharing a group with the caller's shell).
- **Deadman** — guarantees `os._exit(124)` even if the stderr announce blocks on a full, undrained pipe.
- **Server subcommands exempt** — `dashboard` / `spec-web` run until Ctrl-C and are not bounded.

## Rebase conflicts resolved

- `cli.py` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `__init__.py` (mergiraf) — kept both sides' additions.
- Semantic fix line-based git missed: origin/main added a `round_no` param threaded through `run_single`/`run_panel`/`run_moderator`; this branch had refactored a `_run_moderator_inner` helper that ended up referencing an out-of-scope `round_no`. Threaded the param through the helper and updated the run-stats test stubs to accept the `round_no` kwarg.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/ -q -s`: **363 passed** (14 new backstop tests).
- `bash tests/smoke.sh`: **green** (backstop + run-stats stages wired in).
- **codex `review --uncommitted`: clean** — "No actionable correctness issues were found." Four P2s found across the rounds (server subcommands backstopped; orphaned backend children; announce could deadlock on a full pipe; deadman could preempt the SIGKILL + skill docs contradiction) all fixed and locked with tests.

title: feat(board): default pool of 4, drop --no-board, brainstorm + diff grounding (HYP-745)
body:
Implements the CTO-locked board redesign (HYP-745 / task #59). Exactly the three requested points, no over-reach.

## 1. Default reviewer POOL SIZE = 4 (`--pool N`)
The built-in 8-seat `DEFAULT_BOARD` is now a **reserve**: a plain `review` runs only the **first 4 seats** by default. New `--pool N` flag (default 4) sizes how many of the board's seats run — the **first N** participate, the remainder is the reserve. `--pool 0`/`--pool 8` runs all eight. The board is **never off** — `--pool` only sizes it.

- `config.select_pool(board, pool)` — first-N selection, clamped, returns a copy (never a mutating slice-view).
- `cli.validate_board()` applies the slice after `load_board`.
- `--show-board` tags each seat `pool`/`reserve` **by index** (honoring an explicit `--pool`).
- run-stats records the **sliced** `pool_size` (4 by default, N with `--pool N`).

## 2. `--no-board` removed entirely
Dropped the argparse arg, the `args.no_board` branch in `use_board`, and every `--no-board` usage in the tests. The board cannot be disabled — an explicit `-m` or a config `models:` list still bypasses it.

## 3. `--brainstorm` combines with a diff
When a working-tree / `--staged` / piped diff is present, every persona `PanelJob` (ARG_MAX-safe via `PanelJob.diff` over stdin) and the moderator + final synthesis see it as constant **grounding context**, with a prompt note pointing at the diff block — so you brainstorm ABOUT a specific change. No diff -> pure ideation, byte-for-byte as before. Brainstorm diff acquisition is optional (excluded from `needs_diff`): a non-repo / git failure degrades to ideation rather than aborting, even with `--staged`; an empty / `< /dev/null` stdin still falls back to the working tree (matching every other mode and the documented redirect convention).

## NOT touched (explicitly out of scope)
- Plain-review per-seat **role lenses** are unchanged.
- `REVIEW_ROLES` / `DEFAULT_BOARD` membership, seat order, and structure are unchanged.

## Docs
README, CHANGELOG, and `SKILL_MD` (install.py) updated for: default pool 4, the 8-seat reserve, no `--no-board`, and brainstorm + diff.

- `bash tests/smoke.sh` → green (13 suites).
- `uv run --with pytest --with pillow --with pyyaml pytest tests/ -q -s` → **391 passed**.
- Wheel builds (`uv build --wheel`).

title: feat(board): priority-ordered failover reviewer pool
body:
## What

The reviewer board is now a **priority-ordered** list of 8 models (strongest first), and a plain `review` runs a **pool of 4** chosen by **priority + availability**, with two layers of failover so the run keeps **4 working reviewers** even when models are unavailable or fail mid-run.

### Startup failover
The active pool = the top-4 **AVAILABLE** seats by priority. A higher-priority seat whose backend isn't reachable (no key / not on PATH) is **skipped** and the next-priority seat pulled up, so the run starts with 4 working models.

### Mid-run failover
A seat that **fails during the review** — backend error, timeout, empty output, or an "unavailable" reply (e.g. a paywalled model returning *"… is currently unavailable"*, rc=0 but unusable, which the cheap key/CLI probe can't detect) — is replaced by the next-priority **reserve**, repeating until 4 working verdicts are produced or the reserve is exhausted (then it degrades gracefully, logs it, and exits non-zero).

Each seat keeps its own **role/lens**: priority decides *who* sits, the role decides the *lens*; a promoted reserve brings its own lens. `--pool N` overrides the default 4 (top-N available, same failover); `--pool 0` runs all available.

## Priority order (easily re-rankable)
Reorder `DEFAULT_BOARD` in `reviewlib/config.py` (or a `config.yaml` `board:` list) — top = highest priority:

1. Fable 5 — `claude:claude-fable-5`
2. Opus 4.8 — `claude:claude-opus-4-8`
3. GPT-5.5 — `commandcode:gpt-5.5`
4. Kimi K2.7 — `commandcode:moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code`
5. GLM-5.2 — `zai:glm-5.2`
6. Qwen3.7-Max — `commandcode:Qwen/Qwen3.7-Max`
7. DeepSeek-V4-Pro — `commandcode:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`
8. Gemini — `gemini`

Right now Fable 5 is paywalled, so the working pool-4 = **Opus / GPT-5.5 / Kimi / GLM-5.2** (Fable skipped via mid-run failover — its rc=0 "currently unavailable" body is treated as a failed seat and backfilled).

## `--show-board`
Lists the board in priority order with a `#` rank, tags each seat `pool` / `reserve` / `unavail`, and shows the live pool:

```
Reviewer board (8 seats, priority-ordered, source: default; live pool = top 4 AVAILABLE by priority, 4 filled, the rest reserve — size with --pool N):

   #1  [pool   ]  Fable     architect    claude:claude-fable-5  [available]
   #2  [pool   ]  Opus      correctness  claude:claude-opus-4-8  [available]
   #3  [pool   ]  GPT-5.5   consistency  commandcode:gpt-5.5  [available]
   #4  [pool   ]  Kimi      performance  commandcode:moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code  [available]
   #5  [reserve]  GLM       quality      zai:glm-5.2  [available]
   ...
```

## Where it lives
- `config.py` — priority-ordered `DEFAULT_BOARD`, availability-aware `select_pool`, `split_pool_reserve`, `_effective_pool_size`.
- `panel.py` — `result_is_usable` (failure / "unavailable" classifier), `run_board_with_failover` + `FailoverOutcome` (mid-run backfill loop), `build_board_job`.
- `modes/review.py` — board path does startup + mid-run failover.
- `cli.py` — passes the full board + `pool_size`; the ETA keys on the planned pool, run-stats records the **actual** usable models (a backfilled reserve under its real model id); rewritten `--show-board`.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_failover_pool.py`: startup skip of an unavailable top model, mid-run backfill keeping the count, the rc=0 "unavailable" sentinel triggering a backfill (the exact Fable case), `--pool N`, priority order, graceful degradation, tally correctness, lens-travels-with-reserve, marker robustness (a short real review saying "X is not available" is NOT misclassified).
- CLI failover run-stats coverage in `test_run_stats.py` (backfill records actual models, exhausted-reserve degrades to exit 1).
- Full pytest suite (415) + `tests/smoke.sh` green; wheel builds.

## Dogfood
Reviewed with the review-cli board itself. Findings fixed: tightened the "unavailable" markers (dropped the too-broad `is not available`), replaced an `assert` with `zip(strict=True)`, replaced `id()`-keyed maps in `--show-board` with index-based tagging, extracted `_effective_pool_size` to de-dup pool sizing, added CLI failover stats tests. Also documented the migration note: existing `config.yaml` `board:` order is now interpreted as priority.

title: feat(cli): -o output flag (noclobber-safe) + agentic read-only opencode backend
body:
Two CTO-required changes to the Python \`review\` CLI.

## Task 1 — \`review -o FILE\` / \`--output FILE\`
Agents that ran \`review … > out.md\` hit a **silent failure under zsh \`noclobber\`**: the \`>\` refuses to overwrite an existing file and the command dies with no review and no error. review-cli is Python, so \`-o\` writes the result with \`open(...,"w")\`, bypassing the shell redirect (and thus noclobber) entirely.

- Creates parent dirs, overwrites, **strips ANSI/OSC escapes** (clean file), and **still prints to stdout** (a write-through stdout tee).
- Pre-scanned out of argv in \`main()\` so it works for **every** dispatch path (review/panel modes + the bare subcommands like \`install-skill\`/\`dashboard\`/\`spec-web\`).
- Handles all forms: \`-o F\`, \`--output F\`, \`--output=F\`, \`-o=F\`, \`-oF\`; **stops at \`--\`**; **never steals a value-taking flag's argument** (\`review --just-ask --output\` keeps \`--output\` as the question).
- Written on any **completed** run (including a non-zero one like "No diff to review"), but **NOT on an early \`SystemExit\`** — an argparse usage error or \`--help\` never truncates a pre-existing target (**data-loss guard**).
- SKILL.md + README + \`--help\` steer agents to \`-o file.md\`, not \`> file.md\`.

## Task 2a — opencode reads the real repo, read-only (agentic)
\`review_opencode\` used to run in an empty temp \`git init\` dir, so it only saw the diff in the prompt — the same blindness as the raw-API seats. It now runs in the **real \`-C\` repository** (\`opencode run --dir <repo>\`), exactly like the codex backend, so an \`oc:\` seat can **read any project file**.

- **Safety** is enforced by the \`read-only-reviewer\` agent (denies \`edit\`/\`write\`/\`bash\`/\`webfetch\`). **Live-proven**: \`oc:opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free\` opened \`reviewlib/backstop.py\` (NOT in the diff) and returned \`run_backstop\`; the working tree stayed clean.
- **Falls back to an isolated temp dir (diff-only)** when \`-C\` is not a git repo **or** when the repo ships its own opencode config (\`.opencode/\` / \`opencode.json\`/\`.jsonc\`). A repo-local agent can **override** the global read-only agent and re-enable write/bash — **verified live**, and no opencode env flag (\`OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG\`, \`OPENCODE_PERMISSION\`, inline \`OPENCODE_CONFIG\`) suppresses it — so review refuses to run agentically on such a repo (**sandbox-trust safety**, found in board review).
- \`--show-board\` now labels each seat \`agentic\` (codex/opencode/claude-CLI) vs \`diff-only\` (gemini/z.ai/commandcode/claude-API), tracking the real cwd.

## Task 2b — api-only seats stay raw (opencode cannot drive them)
The commandcode and z.ai board seats are **NOT** routed through opencode:
- opencode's \`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible\` adapter does **not reliably drive the Command Code gateway** — the request hangs / returns empty, verified across **reasoning AND non-reasoning** models and **streaming + simulateStreaming**, while the same models answer correctly over **raw HTTP**.
- **z.ai/GLM is not an opencode-native provider** and would hit the same custom-provider path.

So the agentic real-repo treatment applies to opencode-native models (\`oc:deepseek/…\`, \`oc:fireworks/…\`, the free \`oc:opencode/…\` gateway); commandcode/z.ai keep the direct keyed-HTTP path. The priority order + failover from #14 are untouched.

## Tests & verification
- \`tests/test_output_flag.py\` (22) + \`tests/test_opencode_realrepo.py\` (7) — **hermetic** (mock \`_run_streamed\`/\`_which\`/\`_ensure-agent\`; pass with **no opencode on PATH** and an isolated \`HOME\`), plus smoke.sh assertions wired for CI.
- \`bash tests/smoke.sh\` green; \`pytest tests/ -q -s\` **445 passed**; wheel builds.
- **Dogfooded with the review board** across multiple rounds; every actionable finding addressed (data-loss-on-SystemExit, the project-config security hole, value-taking-flag mis-parse, ANSI/OSC stripping, cwd-aware labels, hermetic tests).
- NOTE: the commandcode provider is mid-outage (\`error code: 1010\`) — its 4 board seats show \`exit 403\` in the dogfood runs; the reachable seats (Opus/GLM/Gemini) reviewed in full.

title: fix(specweb): universal pointer-event selection popup (iOS/touch + desktop)
body:
## Problem

In the `review spec-web` reviewer, selecting spec text to ask a question about a fragment **did nothing on iPhone/iPad**. The selection -> `.sel-popup` flow triggered only on `mouseup` with mouse coordinates, which iOS Safari never delivers.

## Fix — ONE universal pointer path (no mouse-vs-touch branches)

Per the directive, the trigger is now input-agnostic, covering mouse + touch + pen through a single code path:

- **`pointerup`** on the document = immediate, desktop-friendly trigger.
- **Debounced `selectionchange`** (200ms settle) = the reliable signal iOS uses to finalize a selection via the native callout (it swallows the `pointerup` over selected text). Both funnel into one `onSelection()`.
- **Popup positioned by selection geometry** — `range.getBoundingClientRect()`, never pointer x/y.
- **Selection text + section/offsets captured and stashed at popup-show time.** iOS clears the live selection the moment the popup is tapped, so the composer reads the stash, never `getSelection()`.
- **Popup buttons fire on `pointerup`/`pointerdown`** (a bare `click` is flaky after a touch selection). `pointerdown` `preventDefault` keeps the selection alive; a self-healing timestamp guard drops the trailing synthetic click while keyboard/assistive clicks still open the composer.
- **CSS**: `.spec-body` stays text-selectable on every device (`-webkit-user-select:text`); popup is non-selectable with `touch-action:manipulation` (consolidated into the existing `.spec-body` rule, no duplicate selector).

This is **one unified pointer path**, not separate mouse and touch branches.

For each profile: programmatically build a Range and apply it as the Selection (fires `selectionchange`), dispatch a real `pointerup`, assert `.sel-popup` becomes visible, then tap "Ask question" via `pointerup` **after `removeAllRanges()` simulates iOS clearing the live selection** — and assert the composer opens with the **stashed** quote.

| iPhone 14 | touch | popup shown over selection, composer opens with stashed quote |

title: feat(dashboard): Tailscale exposure (--host) + live SSE activity stream
body:
## What

Two additions to `review dashboard`, both mirroring the spec-web Tailscale pattern and stdlib-only (no new deps).

### Task 1 — `--host` + Tailscale exposure
- `review dashboard --host 0.0.0.0` binds all interfaces; default stays `127.0.0.1` loopback-only.
- The anti-DNS-rebinding `_host_allowed` guard now consults an **allowlist** (`allowed_hosts()` = loopback + the machine's discovered Tailscale DNSName/IPs + `$REVIEW_DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS`) instead of being disabled. An arbitrary rebound `Host` is still 403'd; only the explicit Tailscale host is admitted — same as `spec-web`.
- The write CSRF guard (`_origin_is_allowed`, renamed from `_origin_is_loopback`) is widened to the same allowlist, so a remote reviewer on the Tailscale host can POST feedback/links while a foreign `Origin` still 403s.
- Startup banner prints the discovered Tailscale URLs; `/api/health` now returns `allowed_origins`.

### Task 2 — SSE live stream (CTO #3627: "стримить всё что происходит в реальном времени")
- `GET /events` (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`): a long-lived handler tails `log_dir()`, diffs each artifact's `(mtime, size)` once a second, and pushes:
  - `log` events — one per changed `.log`/`.md` artifact (filename, backend, round, completed, has_error) — the immediate "a call is streaming" signal;
  - `run` events — the affected session summaries, **same shape as `/api/runs`**, so the front-end refreshes a row in place.
  - heartbeat comments keep the connection alive through Tailscale/proxies.
- The existing `ThreadingHTTPServer` means the long-lived stream never blocks the JSON endpoints; a `_sse_stop` flag ends the loops on shutdown. `/events` inherits the Host-allowlist guard (foreign Host → 403).
- Front-end (`assets/app.js`) subscribes via `EventSource('/events')`, shows a live indicator, and coalesces a burst into one reload so a streaming run updates the list **without a manual refresh** (and never yanks an open session-detail view).

## Verification
- Live instance bound `*:8788`, served **HTTP 200 on `http://ultras-mbp.tailbfe8ea.ts.net:8788/`**, `allowed_origins` included the Tailscale host, and writing a new log file streamed both `log` and `run` SSE events to a connected client.
- `bash tests/smoke.sh` green; `python3 tests/test_dashboard.py` 50/50 green.

## Tests added
- `--host` allowlist: configured Tailscale Host served, foreign Host 403, loopback served.
- Tailscale-`Origin` write allowed; foreign-`Origin` write 403 (CSRF intact).
- `/events`: foreign-Host 403, `text/event-stream` content-type, a live `run`+`log` event with payload-shape assertions.

## Review
Reviewed with review-cli (`review --staged --pool 3`, multi-model); actionable findings applied (rename `_origin_is_loopback`→`_origin_is_allowed`, brainstorm `log` events also trigger a coalesced reload, stuck-indicator fallback, `_SSE_RECENT_RUNS` constant, the Tailscale-Origin-write + `/events` Host-guard tests).

title: feat(modes): move review modes from flags to first-class subcommands
body:
## What

Moves the review **modes** (brainstorm / just-ask / quorum + the default diff review) from `--` flags into mandatory **subcommands** backed by a plugin-directory-style **mode registry** — generalizing the per-project `features/visual` MODULE registry to the core modes. The CTO's confirmed redesign ("в review все еще старая система с -- а не подкомандами").

## New CLI surface

```
review review <args>        # diff review (the DEFAULT; requires a diff)
review brainstorm <topic>   # multi-round persona ideation; composable with --diff/--staged
review just-ask <question>  # single-shot panel question (alias: review ask "Q")
review quorum <question>    # experts cite evidence + a moderator finds quorum
```

- **Bare `review …` (no subcommand) defaults to the `review` mode** — `review -C <repo>`, `review --staged`, `review --visual shot.png` all keep working. A one-line migration hint prints to stderr the first time; it **never hard-errors** on a missing subcommand.
- The mode **flags** `--brainstorm` / `--quorum` / `--just-ask` are **removed** — they now print a helpful "use the subcommand" pointer and exit `2`.
- `--visual` stays a **composable flag** (orthogonal to the mode) on every subcommand.
- `--rounds` / `--max-rounds` are now **brainstorm-only** (so `review just-ask --rounds 5` correctly errors).
- `dashboard`, `spec-web`, `install-skill`, `install-commit-hook`, `register-module`, the per-project visual-module verbs — all unchanged.

## Mode registry (plugin-directory modules)

```
reviewlib/modes/
  contract.py   # ModeSpec descriptor + ModeContext  (mirrors features/visual/contract.py + module_api.py)
  registry.py   # MODES + get_mode / known_subcommands / default_mode / iter_modes  (mirrors features/visual/registry.py)
  review.py     # MODE = ModeSpec(subcommand="review",     diff_policy="require",  …)
  brainstorm.py # MODE = ModeSpec(subcommand="brainstorm", diff_policy="optional", …)
  just_ask.py   # MODE = ModeSpec(subcommand="just-ask",   diff_policy="none",     …)
  quorum.py     # MODE = ModeSpec(subcommand="quorum",     diff_policy="none",     …)
```

Each mode module exposes a top-level `MODE = ModeSpec(...)` (exactly how a visual module exposes a top-level `MODULE`). **Adding a mode = drop a `modes/<name>.py` + list it in `registry.MODES` — no `cli.py` surgery.**

## lib | cli | mcp

`reviewlib/` is the engine; `cli.py` is a **thin** argparse front-end over mode handlers; the **mcp** layer is not built but the seam is kept clean (handlers thin over the lib, so an MCP wrapper / another CLI can reuse the engine). Documented in `README.md` (new "Architecture" section) + new `AGENTS.md`.

## Docs + skill

`README.md` (Quick start / Modes / Flags / How-it-compares) and `reviewlib/install.py` (`SKILL_MD` + `SKILL_BLURB`) migrated to the subcommand syntax.

## Tests

`bash tests/smoke.sh` (CI's invocation) green — every flag-based test migrated to subcommands (handlers patched in their own modules, since dispatch is registry-driven now), plus new `tests/test_mode_subcommands.py` covering dispatch, default-to-review, brainstorm `--diff`, removed-flag errors, and the registry contract. The two-model `review --staged` gate passed (exit 0).

title: feat(specweb): phase-2 bidirectional review — agent handoff, drafts, reply
body:
Phase 2 of the spec-web interactive spec reviewer: three CTO-requested architectural features that turn it into a persistent, bidirectional review channel between a human reviewer and the launching agent.

> **Stacked on #28** (spec-web-ux / phase-1, still open against `main`). Until #28 merges, the diff here includes phase-1's mobile-UX commit. Review/merge #28 first, then this rebases cleanly.

## Feature 1 — Submit delivers to the agent (no markdown export)
Removed the "Export review as markdown" button, the `GET /api/export` route, `export_markdown()`, and the `--export` flag. On **Submit** the server records the batch and the blocking `review spec-web` process prints the **structured review** (a one-line compact JSON object with each comment's `id`/`kind`/`status`/`quote`/`section`/`body`/`replies` + `counts`) to stdout, framed by `<<<REVIEW-SPEC-WEB-SUBMITTED` … `REVIEW-SPEC-WEB-SUBMITTED>>>`. The launching agent parses the single line after the begin marker (marker-substring-safe). Each submit enqueues its **own snapshot** (a `queue.Queue`, not an `Event`) so rapid submits each re-emit their batch with no coalescing. `--exit-on-submit` returns after the first submit. The on-disk store stays the single source of truth.

## Feature 2 — In-progress drafts autosave to disk, reload-safe
The composer autosaves half-typed text (debounced ~500ms) to the server under a per-slot key (`new` + `edit:<id>`), persisted in the per-spec JSON. On load the most recent draft is **restored into the composer**. Emptying the box clears the draft immediately; Cancel/close keeps the current text; a saved note's draft can't be resurrected by a stale in-flight autosave (abortable autosave + a trailing explicit clear); a failed create/edit re-arms autosave. `import_thread(replace)` also wipes prior drafts/`last_submit`. New routes: `GET /api/drafts`, `POST /api/drafts/<slot>`.

## Feature 3 — `review spec-web reply <id> <answer> --spec <spec>`
The agent answers a reviewer's question/remark. The reply threads into the store stamped with the `agent` author — the **UI styles it distinctly** (accent border + AGENT badge) and an open page **polls** and picks it up (polling holds off while a half-typed inline reply is open). The reply is **also delivered to Telegram** via the `tg` CLI on PATH (best-effort: a missing/failing `tg` logs and continues, never failing the reply; `--no-tg` skips; long bodies are clipped under Telegram's limit).

## Durability / correctness
Cross-process file locking: a `review spec-web reply` process writes the same store file as the running server, so every load-modify-write is guarded by an advisory `flock` (sibling `.lock`) plus the in-process `RLock` — no lost update. JSON booleans rejected as char offsets. `--spec` is value-taking so the `-o` pre-scan can't steal a spec path; `spec-web reply` is short-lived (not a persistent server) so `-o`/backstop apply.

## Tests & quality
- **72 spec-web tests** (was 47, +25), all green; full `tests/smoke.sh` passes.
- **9 rounds** of multi-model `review --staged` (Codex/Opus/Fable/GLM/Gemini). Real findings fixed each round: event coalescing, watcher re-read race, cross-process write race, an in-flight-autosave resurrection (P1), import-replace not clearing drafts, failed-submit disabling autosave, polling wiping an inline reply, the `--spec` pre-scan, marker safety.
- Previewed live via agent-browser: agent reply styling, draft restore on reload, the create-race (no stale draft), and the inline-reply-survives-poll fix.

Stack: stdlib HTTP server + vanilla JS + JSON store. No new deps; stdlib-only at import.

title: feat(sessions): resumable brainstorm sessions (list + resume)
body:
## What

Adds `review sessions` — list and **resume** brainstorm sessions parsed from the on-disk discussion logs (`<logdir>/<stamp>-brainstorm.md`), including **dead/interrupted** runs (crashed / killed / timed out, no synthesis), not just completed ones.

```
review sessions          # recent COMPLETED sessions (newest first, cap 20)
review sessions -a       # ALL sessions incl. interrupted (cap lifted)
review sessions -s <id>  # RESUME: reload transcript, continue from completed_round+1, synthesize
```

## How

- **`reviewlib/sessions.py`** (lib): tolerant parser for a possibly-interrupted log (missing synthesis, empty `(no output)` rounds, zero usable rounds), stable short session id from the filename stamp, list/find (exact id or unambiguous prefix; ambiguous prefix → error with the full ids), and resume by seeding `mode_brainstorm` with the prior transcript + persona rotation + start round, appending continued rounds + synthesis to the **same** log.
- **`mode_brainstorm`** gains optional seed params (`seed_transcript` / `seed_persona_index` / `start_round` / `resume_log` / `synthesize_only`). The fresh-start path is **byte-identical** (regression-verified).
- `sessions` is a **bare management subcommand** wired in `cli._dispatch` like `dashboard` — registers no `ModeSpec`, so it never collides with the mode registry (per AGENTS.md).
- **Spoof-resistant parser**: round headings count only when **sequential**, the moderator heading only for the active round, `# Final synthesis` only inside the moderator block — a persona echoing those markers in its body can't fake structure or falsely complete-and-truncate.

## Design decisions

- Default (no `-a`) = recent **completed** only (the "finished work" subset).
- Already-completed resume is **refused** unless `--force`, which **re-synthesizes** with NO new rounds.
- A session that crashed **after** the moderator's `DECISION: STOP` (before synthesis) resumes by **synthesizing only**.
- Resume reuses the saved topic/panel/moderator (the moderator `>`-chain is split back into candidates); `-m` / `--moderator` / `-C` override.
- `--diff` / `--staged` re-attach the current diff as grounding on resume (original grounding isn't persisted).

## Tests

`tests/test_sessions.py` — 17 cases (id derivation, completed/interrupted/empty/zero-round parsing, structure-spoofing resistance, list default-vs-all, find exact/prefix/unknown/ambiguous, resume seed, at-cap & stopped-without-synthesis synthesize-only, force re-synthesis, moderator-chain split + `--diff`, end-to-end CLI wiring). Backends stubbed where defined; logs isolated to a temp `$REVIEW_LOG_DIR`. Wired into `tests/smoke.sh`.

`bash tests/smoke.sh` → **green, 18/18 suites** (incl. visual).

## Review

Reviewed via **codex** on this exact diff; all 5 findings addressed (log-structure spoofing, STOP-without-synthesis resume, ungrounded resume, moderator-chain split, exit-code). The repo's own `review --staged` gate needs live model backends (currently down), so a codex AI review was used instead.

README.md (user-facing) + AGENTS.md (architecture note) updated, English-only.

title: feat(dashboard): per-model health + problematic-count badge on Models & roles tab
body:
## What this adds

A **per-model health view** on the dashboard's "Models & roles" tab plus a **count badge** on the tab button showing how many board models are currently *problematic*. The CTO diagnosed that most of the review board is failing for different reasons; this surfaces it at a glance.

### Backend (`reviewlib/dashboard/parser.py`)
- `classify_call(call)` buckets each backend call into a health class from the EXIT code + stderr + body sentinels.
- `model_id_for_call(call)` gives **model-level** granularity: the shared `commandcode` / `z.ai` backends split by their `… API <model>` header into board ids (`commandcode:<model>` / `zai:<model>`); the `claude` wrapper splits into **Fable** (paywall body) vs **Opus** (the header is identical for both).
- `compute_model_health(sessions)` rolls up per board model: ok-rate, dominant failure class, current class, `problematic` flag — covering every board model (no-data seats included) plus any non-board model seen in the logs. `compute_stats()` now carries `model_health` + `problematic_count`, served through the existing `/api/stats`.

### Health classes
| class | signal |
|---|---|
| `paywall` | body `currently unavailable` (matched on a whitespace-collapsed form — the logger strips whitespace). EXIT is often 0; the **body** is the failure, not the code. → Fable |
| `auth` | EXIT 401 / stderr `{"error":"bad key"}` → z.ai / GLM |
| `blocked` | EXIT 403 / `error code: 1010` (Cloudflare) → commandcode (Kimi/Qwen/DeepSeek) |
| `timeout` | EXIT 124 / `TIMEOUT` marker |
| `empty` | EXIT 0 but no real content (`output_tokens=0` / framing-only body) |
| `ok` | real verdict body, EXIT 0 |
| `error` | any other non-zero exit |

### "Problematic" definition
A model is problematic when it is currently in a **hard-unavailable** class (paywall/auth/blocked), **or** its fail-rate over the window `>= PROBLEMATIC_FAIL_RATE` (0.5), **or** its most-recent `PROBLEMATIC_RECENT_N` (3) calls all fail. Both thresholds are module constants. The tab badge count = number of problematic **board** models.

### Frontend (`assets/`)
- `app.js` `PANELS.models` renders per-model health rows: status pill (reusing the `.badge` palette — **red** for hard-unavailable, **amber** for degraded, **green** for ok), ok-rate %, an ok-bar, and counts. The existing usage + roles lists are kept.
- `index.html` adds a `<span class="tab-badge">` inside the Models & roles button; `app.js` `updateTabBadges()` populates it with `problematic_count` and hides it when zero.
- `app.css` adds `.tab-badge` + `.model-health` styles consistent with the existing `.badge` palette.

title: fix(cli): graceful errors outside a git repo instead of raw tracebacks
body:
## Problem (CTO 2026-06-16)

Running a bare `review` (the diff-review default) **outside a `.git` repo** threw a raw `RuntimeError` + Python traceback (`cli._dispatch` → `_git_diff` → `git diff` failed). A user just trying the tool got a stack trace.

## Fix

- **git is required ONLY by the REVIEW mode** (bare `review` / `review review`, incl. `--staged`). `just-ask` / `quorum` / `brainstorm` and the meta flags (`--list-defaults` / `--show-board` / `--help`) work **anywhere** — no git needed. A **piped diff on stdin** still works without a repo (stdin short-circuits the gate).
- Outside a repo, the review path fails **gracefully** (no traceback): a 3-part **WHAT / WHY / HOW** message and a **stable `EXIT_NOT_A_REPO=3`** (distinct from argparse's usage-2), per `structured-exit-codes`. Cheap, correct repo detection via `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` (`_is_git_repo`).

```
[review-cli] not in a git repository (/path).
  the diff review needs a repo to diff (it reviews your working-tree / staged changes).
  fix: run a mode that needs no git — `review just-ask "..."` / `review quorum "..."` / `review brainstorm "..."` — or cd into a repo and re-run.
```

## Hardening (surfaced by the multi-model review panel — all reviewers green)

- **No traceback on ANY path**: `_git_diff`, `_is_git_repo`, `_effective_cwd`, and `backends._opencode_runs_in_repo` catch `OSError`/`TimeoutExpired` from the git spawn (stale `-C /missing/path`, missing/wedged git). `_git_diff` normalizes every failure to the single `RuntimeError` the OPTIONAL probes (`--visual` / brainstorm / panel `--diff|--staged`) already catch to degrade to `""`.
- **In-repo `git diff` failure** (corrupt index, wedge) on the required path → graceful **`EXIT_GIT_DIFF_FAILED=4`** (distinct from not-a-repo), not a traceback.
- **Panel `--staged`/`--diff` outside a repo** degrades to no-context (`diff_policy="none"`), never the confusing "run just-ask" message at someone already running it.
- Suppress the misleading "reviewing it as-is" warning on the review hard-fail path (it contradicts the hard-fail); no-git modes that DO proceed keep it.
- **Docs**: corrected `review -C <repo> <subcommand>` examples to subcommand-first (`review just-ask "Q" -C <repo>`) in README + the installed skill text (`install.py`) — the dispatcher only recognizes a mode as `argv[0]`, so the old order parse-errored.

## Exit codes
| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | gate result (e.g. "No diff to review." — pre-existing) |
| 2 | argparse / usage |
| **3** | **not a git repository (`EXIT_NOT_A_REPO`)** |
| **4** | **in a repo but `git diff` failed (`EXIT_GIT_DIFF_FAILED`)** |
| 124 | internal backstop |

## Tests
- New `tests/test_no_git_repo.py` (20 tests): real `bin/review` subprocess (isolated HOME) + in-process dispatch with stubbed handlers. Covers the 3-part message + exit 3 + no traceback; meta/no-git modes work anywhere; piped diff needs no repo; stale/missing `-C`, missing/wedged git, and in-repo git-diff failure all graceful; real empty repo regression-safe (exit 1 + "No diff to review.").
- Wired into `tests/smoke.sh` (the CI runner) + an inline bash non-git assertion block.
- Updated the pre-existing `test_cli_default_review_staged_nonrepo_*` (it asserted the OLD traceback behavior → now asserts the graceful `EXIT_GIT_DIFF_FAILED` contract).
- **`bash tests/smoke.sh` green: 548 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 tracebacks**, all 21 suites incl. the new `no-git-repo` one.

## Known follow-ups (pre-existing, out of scope — not introduced here)
- `_dispatch` keys diff behavior on `mode.name == "brainstorm"` rather than `ModeSpec.diff_policy` (a new optional-diff mode wouldn't auto-pick the diff unless named `brainstorm`). Pre-existing; a `diff_policy`-driven refactor deserves its own PR.
- A missing/wedged git binary in a REAL repo is reported as `EXIT_NOT_A_REPO` ("cd into a repo") rather than a git-failure — still graceful (no traceback), just a slightly-off message. A tri-state probe would distinguish it.
- README `docs/mode-*.svg` diagrams + `dashboard/assets/app.js` empty-state still show the removed `--brainstorm`/`--quorum`/`--just-ask` flags (pre-existing doc/UI drift).

title: fix(cli): fail loud on removed --mcp / --ln flags with a structured error
body:
## What

`review --mcp` (and `--ln`) were removed in the subcommand refactor but still hit argparse's opaque `unrecognized arguments: --mcp`. This makes them fail LOUD with a structured **what / why / how-to-fix** error at the stable usage exit code (2).

```
$ review --mcp
review: `--mcp` was removed and is no longer accepted.
  why:  the `review --mcp` MCP entrypoint was removed in the subcommand refactor (agent-tools #32) — review is a CLI + skill, not an MCP server.
  fix:  remove the review MCP server registration: delete the `review` entry from ~/.claude/mcp/mcp.json (and any rig.yaml `mcp.review` / `mcp.items.review` block), then re-run `rig apply`. Use the `review` CLI or its skill directly instead.
```

## Why

ROADMAP §9: **"`review --mcp` is broken ecosystem-wide."** The `--mcp` flag was dropped in the subcommand refactor, but `~/.claude/mcp/mcp.json` (args `["--mcp"]`) and rig.yaml `mcp.review.command` still invoke `review --mcp` → a dead MCP server. argparse's bare `unrecognized arguments` gave a user zero migration guidance.

## Fix-or-remove decision

The ecosystem already decided **remove**, not reimplement: rig-cli's `riglib/errors.py` declares `review --mcp` a removed slot ("review is a CLI + skill, not an MCP server — the `review --mcp` entrypoint was dropped in the subcommand refactor", agent-tools #32). This PR is the **review-cli side**: keep the entrypoint removed, but make invoking it *diagnosable* — point the user at the exact stale registration to delete. Dropping the registration itself is rig-cli/global-config surface (`~/.claude/mcp/mcp.json` + rig templates), out of this repo.

## Implementation (smallest change, DRY)

- New `REMOVED_FLAGS` registry in `reviewlib/modes/registry.py` — for flags removed with **no replacement subcommand** (distinct from the existing `REMOVED_MODE_FLAGS`, which map to a verb). Each carries a `reason` + a concrete `fix`.
- `_reject_removed_flags` (the existing removed-mode-flag rejector) now also consults `REMOVED_FLAGS` and prints the 3-part error. One code path, reused.
- Scan still stops at `--` (end-of-options), so a literal `--mcp` positional value is untouched.

## Acceptance

- [x] `review --mcp`, `--mcp=stdio`, `--ln`, `--ln=5` exit **2** with a clear what/why/how-to-fix error — never argparse's `unrecognized arguments`.
- [x] `--mcp` fix line names the stale registration (`mcp.json`) + `rig apply`.
- [x] Caught after valid global args (`-C <dir> --mcp`) and before a subcommand (`--mcp brainstorm x`).
- [x] A `--mcp` positional after `--` is NOT intercepted (scan stops at `--`).

## Tests

`tests/test_mode_subcommands.py` — 9 new tests against real `cli.main` (no backend spawned): structured-error shape, `mcp.json`+`rig apply` in the fix line, equals-form, flag-position coverage, and the `--` escape hatch. `tests/smoke.sh` — added `--mcp`/`--ln` rejection assertions to the CI gate.

- `tests/test_mode_subcommands.py`: **29 pass / 0 fail**
- Full `bash tests/smoke.sh`: **green, 0 FAIL/ERROR**

Verified the double-dash test exercises the real path (`usage: review review` → `review` consumed as subcommand, `--mcp` after `--` not intercepted). Remaining nitpicks (`--ln` test parity for an identical code branch, `allow_abbrev` for `--mc` which the real registration never emits, positional false-positive — a pre-existing documented trade-off of the shared scan) justified-skip.

title: fix(brainstorm): fail loud on a dead panel instead of a hollow STOP
body:
## What

A brainstorm whose every panel seat returned empty (`(no output)`) used to run all its rounds, let the moderator rubber-stamp `DECISION: STOP` over a transcript of nothing, print an **empty synthesis**, and **exit 0 as if it worked** — wasting ~20 min of "it's still thinking" on dead/credential-less backends.

This detects a dead round and aborts LOUD with a clear error + a stable non-zero exit, never a hollow STOP.

## Why

ROADMAP §9 (CTO 2026-06-16): *"review brainstorm must FAIL LOUD when backends return empty (not silently 'converge')."* Pairs with the dead-provider cleanup (Fireworks suspended) and the `review sessions` resume work (a dead run must be resumable AND diagnosable).

## Behavior

```
$ review brainstorm "..." -m oc:nonexistent/dead-model
[review-cli] brainstorm aborted: round 1 produced no usable output (0/3 panel seats answered).
  most/all backends are dead or credential-less (empty output, an error, or an 'unavailable' notice) — continuing would only print a hollow synthesis.
  panel: oc:nonexistent/dead-model
  fix: check the backends are reachable (keys present, CLIs installed, provider not suspended), then re-run — or pass a working panel with `-m`.
$ echo $?
5
```

- **Dead round** = a strict majority of seats produced no usable verdict (`_round_is_dead`, reusing the same `result_is_usable` judgement the failover board uses, so the two can't drift).
- **Stable exit code** `EXIT_DEAD_PANEL=5` — scriptable, distinct from argparse-2 / not-a-repo-3 / git-4.
- **Guard scope**: fires ONLY before any productive round (`not transcript_blocks`). The target bug is "every seat dead from round 1". If an earlier round was productive and a later round flakes (transient rate-limit), the run **keeps its good rounds and still synthesizes** — not discard them (claude-opus review caught this regression risk). Mid-run transient resilience (retry/reserve-swap) is a separate ROADMAP item.
- **Resumable**: the dead round is logged for diagnosis WITHOUT a structural round sentinel → the session parser counts **0 completed rounds** → `review sessions --resume` re-runs the dead round instead of seeding its `(no output)`.
- **Honest run-stats**: a rc=0-but-empty seat is reclassified `ok->fail` (the total never inflated), so a dead run doesn't poison the ETA average.

## Acceptance (verified)

- [x] **Real CLI, end-to-end**: `review brainstorm -m oc:nonexistent/dead-model` exits **5**, prints the abort message, and emits **0** `# Final synthesis` blocks (proof attached).
- [x] all-dead-from-round-1 → `EXIT_DEAD_PANEL`, aborts on round 1 (3 seats, **no** moderator call), no hollow synthesis.
- [x] a dead round AFTER a productive round → exits 0, synthesizes the good round (no regression).
- [x] dead-panel discussion log parses as **0** completed rounds (real session parser); tally counts dead seats as **fail** (real begin/end_call_tally).

## Tests

`tests/test_brainstorm_dead_panel.py` — **18 tests** exercising the REAL `mode_brainstorm` loop, `_round_is_dead`/`result_is_usable`, the REAL session parser, and the REAL run-stats tally; only the backend boundary is stubbed (no network). Plus a `tests/smoke.sh` assertion. Full `bash tests/smoke.sh`: **green, 0 FAIL/ERROR**.

## Review

Two independent pre-commit reviews: `review --staged -m zai:glm-5.2` (diff-only) and `review --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8` (agentic, separate backend — the fast commandcode/zai gateways were saturated/rate-limited during the run). Substantive findings addressed: tally-inflation edge case (fail++ moved inside the ok-guard so a broken invariant can never lie upward, + regression test); the partial-success regression (guard now scoped to `not transcript_blocks`, + an end-to-end test proving round-1 content survives); a no-op-tally test. Verified the claimed `_disc`/`disc_path` crash concerns are non-issues (`_disc` no-ops on None; `disc_path` always assigned). Remaining nitpicks (threshold-as-named-constant, unused `capfd` harness param) justified-skip.

title: feat(board): make all repo-capable default seats agentic via opencode (closes #24)
body:
## What

Make ALL repo-capable default board seats **agentic via opencode** (closes alex-mextner/review-cli#24).

Before, the board's Kimi/GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek seats routed **diff-only** through the
`commandcode:`/`zai:` keyed-HTTP REST backends — they saw only the diff in the prompt.
Now they route through opencode (`oc:provider/model`), running read-only **inside** the
repo (`opencode run --agent read-only-reviewer --dir <cwd>`), so they can open any project
file — exactly like the codex and claude-CLI seats already did. Only **Gemini** stays
diff-only (it has no agentic transport).

`#24` asked to *re-investigate* commandcode + the GLM custom provider. Outcome: with
`commandcode` and `zai` registered as opencode **custom providers**
(`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`), the prior PR #15 blocker ("opencode's adapter
hangs/returns empty on the Command Code gateway") is **resolved** — a single
`oc:commandcode/...` call returns cleanly. (The flakiness seen under heavy parallel load is
SQLite/provider concurrency contention, which the board's reserve + failover absorbs.)

## How

- `_agentic()` derives each board seat from its diff-only constant (transport-only flip,
  idempotent + canonical: `opencode:` normalized to `oc:`), keeping one source of truth for
  every model id. The flat `DEFAULT_MODELS` panel keeps the diff-only commandcode Kimi seat
  on purpose — it has no reserve, so it must not silently shrink on an opencode-less host;
  the board can absorb that via its reserve.
- The raw `commandcode:`/`zai:` backends remain for explicit `-m cc`/`-m glm` and config
  boards on hosts without opencode.
- **Dashboard attribution:** the opencode sidecar header now records the
  `-m <provider/model>` selector (new `header_argv0` on `_run_streamed`, prompt/diff still
  redacted), and the parser maps an `opencode` backend call to `oc:<provider/model>` — so
  Kimi/GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek no longer collapse into a single `opencode` row / show `no_data` on

```

   #5  [reserve]  GLM       quality      oc:zai/glm-5.2  [available]  (agentic)

   #8  [reserve]  Gemini    contracts    gemini  [available]  (diff-only)
```

- `tests/test_reviewer_board.py`: board shape/priority/reserve with `oc:` ids, GLM agentic
  routing, an all-repo-capable-seats-are-agentic contract, `_agentic` rewrite/idempotency/
  canonicalization, and the opencode-vs-review-cli auth decoupling (availability keys on the
  opencode binary, not `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`).
- `tests/test_dashboard.py`: opencode `-m provider/model` → `oc:` attribution (round-trips
  every default `oc:` seat; bare opencode stays the backend name); health view covers the
  new `oc:` board ids.
- `tests/test_opencode_realrepo.py`: both opencode branches stamp the `header_argv0` model
  selector (no prompt/diff in the header).
- `tests/test_failover_pool.py` / `tests/test_run_stats.py`: failover + run-stats with the
  new `oc:` ids.
- `tests/smoke.sh`: `--show-board` agentic labels for Kimi/GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek, Gemini stays
  diff-only.
- **Full smoke suite green: 609 checks, exit 0.**

Pre-commit review: `review --staged -m gemini,codex` — both seats `[ok]` (non-degraded).
All codex/gemini findings addressed in-PR (key-resolution doc accuracy, stale README/CHANGELOG
notes reconciled to the agentic board, `_agentic` idempotency+canonicalization, SKILL_MD
agentic-board note, test env-var hygiene, and a smoke `--show-board` per-seat match that was
fragile against the unavailable-seat footer — now matched by unique `oc:` model id). One
pre-existing hardening item — validate/refuse a pre-existing permissive global
`read-only-reviewer` opencode agent — is tracked as a follow-up in #40, not in scope here.

Two further codex findings are accepted as in-scope trade-offs / doc precision: (1) on an
**opencode-less** host the four `oc:` reserve seats drop, so a default review can degrade if

"when `claude-p` is on PATH" (they fall back to the diff-only Anthropic API otherwise), which

title: fix(install): detect a PATH-shadowing stale console-script + smoke the shim bootstrap
body:
## Problem

`/opt/homebrew/bin/review` — a pip *editable*-install console-script whose `.pth`
finder pointed at a since-deleted worktree (`/private/tmp/w2-review-failloud`) — sat
EARLIER on `PATH` than the working `~/.files/bin/review` symlink and shadowed it. So
bare `review` died in every shell with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'reviewlib'
```

The repo's `bin/review` shim already bootstraps `sys.path` correctly (it realpath-
resolves the symlink back to the repo root and inserts it). The breakage was an
external stale install winning the `PATH` race — and nothing detected or surfaced it.

## Fix

- **`install.sh`** — after symlinking, probe `command -v review`. If it resolves to a
  DIFFERENT entry than the symlink we just created, warn loudly. When that entry is a
  stale pip/uv console-script (regular non-symlink file, `#!`-shebang, mentions
  `reviewlib`), diagnose it: extract the real interpreter from the shebang (handles
  `#!/abs/python`, `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, and `env -S`/`-C` flag forms), confirm it
  can't `import reviewlib`, and print copy-paste remediation (`<py> -m pip uninstall -y
  review-cli` and a single-quote-safe `rm '<path>'`). The interpreter is trusted only
  after an `import sys` python-ness probe, so a mis-parsed non-Python token (e.g.
  coreutils `dir` from `env -C dir python3` on Debian) never yields a garbage `<bin> -m
  pip` line. `install-skill` is now invoked via the absolute `$BIN/$TOOL` so a shadow
  can't run the broken script.

title: feat(retry): in-seat retry with retryable/seat-fatal classification before reserve-replace
body:
## What

The failover reviewer board had **reserve-replace** failover but no **in-seat retry** — it threw a seat away on the *first* failure, even a transient one a retry-a-second-later would have cleared. This adds the missing layer.

Closes the in-seat-retry work tracked against review-cli #13 / #14 / #15 / #17.

### Classification (retryable vs seat-fatal)
A non-usable seat result is classified as:
- **RETRYABLE** — a transient the same key recovers from in seconds: `429` rate-limit, `529`/5xx overload, an "overloaded"/"service unavailable" notice, or a process timeout (exit 124).
- **SEAT-FATAL** — no retry of the same key fixes it: auth (`401`/`403`/api-key), an unknown/invalid model, `501` not-implemented, a refusal, **or an exhausted quota/billing limit** (the same key won't replenish in the retry window — unlike the cross-harness chain, which can fall to a different provider's quota).

The transient regex is **mirrored from the agent-tools contract** (`lib/contracts/models.yaml` `fallback_chain:` + the `model-error-fallback` transient patterns) — agent-tools isn't importable from this single-dep repo, so the set is copied verbatim; a comment marks it to keep in sync. Classification reads the **error channel only** (stderr + the short rc=0 "unavailable" sentinel body), never the review body (a long review mentioning "503" isn't a throttle) or the command line (an argv `--timeout 503` isn't an error).

### Retry before reserve
`run_seat_with_retry` retries the same seat with **exponential backoff + jitter** under **three independent caps** so a slow-failing seat can't pin the run:
1. retry **count** (`--retry N` / `$REVIEW_RETRY_COUNT`, default 2, `0` disables, clamped to a ceiling);
2. a **timeout sub-cap** — a process timeout gets one extra attempt (each retry costs a whole per-call timeout);
3. a **wall-clock cap** (`$REVIEW_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS`, default 90s) — the backstop for a slow 503 returned just shy of the per-call timeout (rc != 124) the timeout sub-cap can't see.

Wired into **both** the failover board (`run_board_with_failover`) and the flat `-m` panel. A seat-fatal failure returns immediately so the reserve takes over without burning the budget.

### Durable logging
Every retry, seat-fatal short-circuit, timeout/time-exhausted cap, and reserve promotion is written **durably** to the run-log dir as a `*-retry.log` event (0600, each `kind=` distinct: `retry` / `seat-fatal` / `timeout-exhausted` / `retry-time-exhausted` / `promote`) — not stderr-only, so a post-mortem or the dashboard can reconstruct how a seat recovered or fell over. **Fail-loud-on-empty is preserved**: an unrecovered seat is handed back to the reserve/degrade path unchanged, never fabricated into a verdict.

## Tests

`tests/test_inseat_retry.py` (38 tests, all offline): the classification matrix (each transient/fatal shape, fail-closed default, fatal-first ordering), error-channel discipline (long body & command excluded, short sentinel included), transient-then-recovers, seat-fatal/quota zero-retries, the three caps (count / timeout / wall-clock), durable-log kinds, backoff growth + jitter bounds, suppression-aware tally (no cross-thread race), and the panel + flat-`-m` integrations (retry keeps the pool full without touching the reserve; fatal falls through; retry-then-reserve on an unrecoverable transient; one tally per logical seat across a reserve-replace round). Registered in `smoke.py`; full smoke green (22 checks).

Reviewed across multiple opus passes; every actionable finding addressed (cross-thread tally race, command-in-channel, quota-as-in-seat-fatal, timeout latency-multiplier, wall-clock cap for slow transients, distinct log kinds, flag-over-env precedence, flat-path retry).
