title: feat(backends): harden _ensure_opencode_readonly_agent — validate/rewrite a permissive global agent (#40)
body:
Closes #40.

## Problem
`_ensure_opencode_readonly_agent` trusted a pre-existing global
`~/.config/opencode/agents/read-only-reviewer.md` without validating it (early `return` if the file existed). A stale or tampered file granting `bash`/`edit`/`write` would silently give the "read-only" reviewer write/exec on the user's repo. With review-cli#24 making the agentic-opencode path the DEFAULT board route (Kimi/GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek seats), this runs on every `review`.

## Fix
The function now VALIDATES an existing agent and REWRITES the canonical deny-all definition (loudly, on stderr) when it is not strictly read-only:

- `_agent_is_strictly_readonly`: every known capability must be present and **fully denied**, and nothing present (extras included) may grant — accepts a scalar `deny` OR a granular per-pattern map **only if** it has an explicit catch-all `"*": deny`. opencode defaults unlisted patterns to ALLOW (verified against opencode's permission docs), so a granular map like `bash: {"git status": deny}` without a catch-all is a real privilege hole — it is rejected.
- A stricter user-hardened agent (extra `deny` keys) **passes untouched** (no downgrade of the user's hardening).
- Canonical markdown is **generated from the denied-permissions tuple** (single source of truth — validator and writer can't drift).
- **Atomic write** (`tempfile` + `os.replace`) so parallel board seats never read a truncated file and fall back to opencode's permissive defaults mid-rewrite.
- **Line-anchored** frontmatter split so a `---` inside a value can't tear the parse.

## Tests
`tests/test_readonly_agent.py` (20 hermetic cases, `$HOME` redirected to a temp dir — never touches the real global config), registered in `tests/smoke.py`. Acceptance criteria covered: (a) permissive pre-existing agent refused/rewritten, (b) canonical passes untouched, (c) missing one created correctly — plus granular-without-catch-all rejected, hidden-allow-leaf rejected, atomic-write cleanup, and parsing edge cases.

## CI
`python tests/smoke.py` -> `OK: 22 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped` (with `pip install -e '.[test]'`). Reviewed via `review diff --staged` (opus); the catch-all-deny hole was a review finding, verified independently against opencode's docs before fixing.

title: fix(config): guard DEFAULT_MODELS against silent provider rot (#25)
body:
Closes #25.

## Context — what was already done vs. what was missing

`DEFAULT_MODELS` no longer hard-codes the dead Fireworks/Kimi entry: PR #35 routed the default Kimi seat off the suspended `glide` account onto the live commandcode gateway (`KIMI_SEAT = "commandcode:moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code"`), and `test_reviewer_board.py` already bans the dead-route *tokens*. The issue's full manifest-resolution acceptance bullet depends on a `models.yaml` from other repos (rig-cli model-currency / agent-tools providers extraction) that **does not exist in this repo**, so that part is out of the "contained" scope.

What was missing — and what this PR adds — is the **anti-rot guard the issue's spirit asks for** ("the literal goes stale anyway... can't silently rot again"). The token ban stops the *specific* historical dead string from returning, but not a *new* stale default: `resolve_backend` has a catch-all that sends any unrecognized id to opencode, so a future stale/typo'd default degrades **silently at runtime** instead of erroring — exactly the #25 failure mode.

## Current default model list (verified live)

| Default | Routes to | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| `codex` | `review_codex` (codex CLI, `codex exec -s read-only`) | named branch; probe `_which("codex")` |
| `gemini` | `review_gemini` (REST) | named branch; probe `_gemini_key()` |
| `commandcode:moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` (`KIMI_SEAT`) | `review_commandcode` (keyed HTTP, `https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1`) | named branch; probe `_commandcode_key()` |

The dead route was `oc:fireworks/accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p6-turbo` on the suspended `glide` account → **gone from the defaults**. I independently verified (via git log + grep sweep) that commandcode is the codebase's most-used live gateway (3 board seats + the flat Kimi seat + the `cc` alias), with no deprecation/suspension/migration anywhere — not a swap of one dead provider for a soon-to-be-dead one.

## What changed

- `reviewlib/backends.py`: split `resolve_backend`'s named-route matching into `_match_named_backend` (behaviour-preserving — `resolve_backend` keeps its opencode catch-all, covered by existing `test_provider_keys.py` assertions). Add `effective_provider(model)` (peels the `oc:`/`opencode:` agentic transport to the real provider) and `default_routes_live(model)` (the provider under any transport must BOTH name a real backend AND not be in the `_DEAD_PROVIDERS` denylist).
- `tests/test_reviewer_board.py`: a CI guard pinning every `DEFAULT_MODELS` entry + `DEFAULT_BOARD` seat through `default_routes_live`, plus focused tests — dead default, typos across flat/`oc:`/`opencode:` spellings, a **load-bearing denylist** test (proves the denylist changes the verdict), and a **bare-token contract** over every named provider.

A typo'd default (`comandcode:...` or `oc:comandcode/...`) or a dead-provider default now **fails CI** instead of rotting at runtime.

## Design notes

- **Denylist, not allowlist** for dead providers: a live-allowlist would have to remember every new live provider; a denylist only needs the one that died. The "is it real?" half is the named-route check, which never goes stale.
- **CI-only enforcement** (a live network probe needs keys / can't run in CI) — documented in `default_routes_live`'s docstring as the single line of defense; defaults are constrained to named providers.

## Testing

`python tests/smoke.py` → **OK: 23 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped** (includes the dashboard `node --test` suite via `test_dashboard_js_unit` and all `tests/test_*.py` via `test_reviewlib_unit_files`). Reviewed 4 iterations via the opus review gate, all `[ok]`.

title: fix(spec-web): server-side ordering token + tombstone for draft autosave (#30)
body:
Closes #30.

## The race

Spec-web's draft autosave had a server-side ordering race. The store serializes writes under a per-slot lock, but applies them in **lock-acquisition order, which ≠ client send order** (the server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, one thread per request). So a non-empty autosave POST whose lock is acquired AFTER the trailing clear re-creates the draft, and a reload resurrects stale composer text. The client's abortable fetch + trailing `clearDraftOnServer` (from #29) is best-effort — it cannot recall a request already on the wire.

## The fix — server-authoritative ordering

**Monotonic token + tombstone.** Each `/api/drafts/<slot>` write carries a `token` (the client's monotonic per-session send sequence). The store records a per-slot **tombstone** (`draft_tokens: {slot -> last applied token}`) and REJECTS any write whose token is `<= last`. The tombstone **outlives the draft**, so a late write that arrives after the trailing clear is rejected (`token <= clear_token`) and can't resurrect it — regardless of lock-acquisition order. (`reviewlib/specweb/store.py`: `save_draft_result`, `_is_stale_token`, `_empty`/`load` schema.)

**Atomic staleness, no TOCTOU.** `save_draft_result` returns `(draft, applied)` decided INSIDE the store lock; the HTTP layer reports `stale = not applied` and returns the authoritative current slot state (`reviewlib/specweb/server.py: _save_draft`). The legacy `save_draft` is a thin back-compat wrapper.

**Reload seeding (the part that makes the feature keep working).** The tombstone is durable, but the client counter restarts at 0 on every page load — so a reloaded session's first autosaves would be `<= tombstone` and silently rejected, i.e. autosave would appear broken. Fix: the server sends `X-Draft-Token-Seed: <max token>` on the drafts GET **and on every write response**, and the client seeds its counter above it (`seedDraftToken`, only ever raises). This also self-heals a counter that fell behind (lost boot-seed, a second tab).

**Hardening.** `delete_comment` sweeps the gone edit-slot's tombstone (no unbounded growth); `_as_token` treats bool/str/float/negative/absurd values as token-less (legacy last-writer-wins preserved for older clients).

## Design note (no product decision needed)

The issue offered "client send-sequence OR server receive-time". Only the **client send-sequence** actually fixes *this* race: server-receive-time stamps a late arrival with a *newer* timestamp, so it would win — the bug. The trailing clear always carries the highest token (it fires after `cancelPendingDraftSave()`, which clears the debounce timer and aborts the in-flight autosave), so the server-side `delete_draft` in create/edit stays a simple sweep and the client's token-bearing clear is the ordering authority. No ambiguity, so this ships the full fix rather than stopping for a decision.

## Testing

`python tests/smoke.py` → **OK: 23 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped** (includes the dashboard `node --test` JS suite via `test_dashboard_js_unit`). **88 spec-web tests pass** (`tests/test_specweb.py`), including:
- out-of-order token rejection, delete-then-late-write tombstone, tombstone-survives-clear;
- a **concurrent-threads** test asserting the highest token always wins regardless of lock-acquisition order (the literal race);
- the reload seed path end-to-end (store + HTTP `X-Draft-Token-Seed`);
- malformed tokens (store + HTTP body parsing), legacy/token-mix semantics.

Reviewed 5 iterations via the opus review gate, all `[ok]`; no blocking findings on the core ordering correctness.

## Scope note

The client pieces (`nextDraftToken`/`seedDraftToken`/`postDraft`) have no dedicated JS unit tests: the spec-web `app.js` is a vanilla browser IIFE with no CommonJS export surface (unlike the dashboard app.js), and restructuring a working browser file purely for testability is out of scope here. The ordering invariant is enforced and exhaustively tested **server-side** (the authority); the client helpers are a monotonic counter + a `max`-seed, verified by inspection.

title: ci(lint): pinned ruff job + clear 13 latent errors + --retry as value-taking
body:
## Motivation

review-cli's CI ran tests but **no lint gate**, so 13 ruff errors accumulated
unnoticed. Separately, a genuine value-taking option (`--retry`) was missing from
the `-o` output pre-scan's allow-list (`_VALUE_TAKING_OPTS`), a latent correctness
gap the repo's own invariant test is meant to keep closed.

## What changed

**Lint gate (new).** A `lint` CI job pins `ruff==0.15.18` so an upstream ruff
release can't flip a green PR red on its own, and `[tool.ruff] target-version =
"py39"` pins intent to the project's Python floor. The default rule set is kept —
it is exactly what surfaced these errors.

**13 errors fixed.**

title: feat(qa): review-qa Phase 1 — mode skeleton + no-suites gate
body:
## What

Phase 1 (Increment 1) of the `review qa` "agent-as-tester" mode, per `docs/specs/review-qa.md` — the smallest independently-shippable, verifiable slice: the **mode skeleton + the no-suites gate**. NO executor, NO LLM-judge, NO env-harness (those are Phase 2+).

Closes #54.

### Shipped

- **`reviewlib/modes/qa.py`** — `MODE = ModeSpec(name="qa", subcommand="qa", diff_policy="none", stats_mode="qa", aliases=("test",), ...)`. Registered in `registry.py` (one import + one `MODES` entry). Dispatched table-driven by the existing `cli._dispatch` — no dispatch surgery.
- **Suite discovery** (`resolve_suites` / `count_cases`) — prose `*.md` suites in the conventional `docs/tests/suites/*.md` (relative to the SUT; `--suites` overrides with a glob, dir, or file). A suite's CASES tally = its `## Case:` blocks (the format §4 chose).
- **The NO-SUITES gate** — when `qa` runs but no suite resolves (or a file parses to zero `## Case:` blocks), it prints a 3-part WHAT/WHY/HOW message (mirroring `cli._fail_not_a_repo`) and exits `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES`. Runs BEFORE any agent/docker/browser. "A green qa run with zero authored cases is a lie."
- **No false-green on the suites-found path** — Phase 1 has no executor, so when suites DO resolve, the handler FAILS LOUDLY with a distinct `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (non-zero) rather than exiting 0. A 0 there would be the same lie the gate prevents — cases authored, zero executed, CI reads "qa passed." (Raised by the opus review-gate; fixed.)
- **CLI exit codes** (`reviewlib/cli.py`): `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES = 6` and `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED = 70`. `--suites` added to `_SUBCOMMAND_ONLY_FLAGS` (verb-less `review --suites …` gets the friendly pointer) and `_VALUE_TAKING_OPTS` (the `-o` pre-scan treats it as value-taking).

## Why

`review qa` makes an agent act as a tester. Without authored cases there is nothing to exercise and nothing to verify — a green run would be a lie. The mandatory no-suites gate is the load-bearing contract of the whole mode, and it ships + tests independently of the (large, security-sensitive) write/exec executor.

## Exit-code note

The spec's §6 first proposed `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES = 5`, but **5 is already taken at the process-exit level by brainstorm's `EXIT_DEAD_PANEL`** (`modes/brainstorm.py`). Structured exit codes must stay per-class distinct, so qa's codes start at the next free integer (**6**); the later qa env classes (NO_ENV/ENV_UNHEALTHY/SUT_BOOT_FAILED) continue from 7 in Phase 2/3. The transient Phase-1 `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is parked at 70, clear of that block (it disappears when the executor lands).

## Tests

`tests/test_qa_mode.py` (14 cases): qa + the `test` alias resolve via the registry; `qa --help` builds; the no-suites gate fires with `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES` + the 3-part message (incl. the distinct authored-but-empty variant); the suites-found path fails non-zero (`EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`); case counting; `--suites` dir/file/absolute-glob resolution; `-C`-vs-positional SUT resolution; the verb-less `--suites` friendly pointer; exit-code non-collision (both qa codes). Listed in `smoke.py`'s `_UNIT_FILES` (with a fresh log dir). `test_output_flag.py` extended to route `--suites` through the `qa` parser in the value-taking-opts guard.

## What

Adds a default reviewer-board seat `commandcode:zai-org/GLM-5.2` (display `GLM-cc`, role `performance`) at **priority 3 — directly under Opus (#2)**, per the CTO directive. A plain `review diff` now runs Fable, Opus, **GLM-5.2-via-commandcode**, Codex as its top-4 pool.

## Why this design

- **commandcode is an HTTP gateway, not a CLI.** In review-cli, `commandcode` is an OpenAI-compatible Provider API (`https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1`), keyed by `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` — there is no `commandcode` binary. The gateway serves `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (verified live: a chat-completion returns content, `finish_reason=stop`).
- **Diff-only / read-only by construction.** The seat routes through `review_commandcode` — a stateless keyed-HTTP POST of the diff, no repo/tools/exec. opencode's `commandcode` provider does NOT register this GLM id, so the agentic `oc:commandcode/zai-org/GLM-5.2` route errors (verified); the keyed-HTTP route is the only one that reaches it. So it's diff-only like Gemini, and needs no `-s read-only` cage.
- **Distinct from the existing `oc:zai/glm-5.2` seat** (#6, display `GLM`): same model family, different provider/transport (Command Code gateway vs the z.ai Coding-Plan subscription). Both kept.
- **Role `performance`, not a second `correctness`.** Inserting at #3 pushes Kimi (the old performance seat) to #5/reserve, so GLM-cc carries `performance` — the default top-4 pool keeps four distinct lenses (architect/correctness/performance/consistency). Degrades gracefully when `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` is absent (the pool backfills from the reserve). Board is now 9 seats.

- Seat registers at priority 3, directly under Opus (adjacency + index pinned).
- Resolves read-only through `review_commandcode`; passes the #25 default-routing guard.
- POSTs the **byte-exact** `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (embedded slash preserved).

## What

Phase 2 / Increment 2 of `review qa`: the **write/exec agentic EXECUTOR** — the piece that drives a System-Under-Test against authored prose `## Case:` suites and classifies pass/fail with evidence. Replaces the Phase-1 `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED=70` scaffold with the real executor.

Closes #56. Follow-ups tracked: #60 (model-suffix forwarding + trust-entry cleanup), #61 (Python bot detection + help-config row).

## Core (`reviewlib/qa/{__init__,executor,suites}.py`)
- `run_tester`: spawns ONE un-caged backend (claude `bypassPermissions` default; codex `exec -s workspace-write --full-auto --ephemeral` via `REVIEW_QA_TESTER` / `-m codex`) inside an isolated `git worktree` of the SUT (`--in-place` escape hatch), single-seat, streaming to `--report`, cleanup on every exit/signal + mid-run error + failed-`worktree add` + timeout paths. Subdir-SUT aware (runs in the matching worktree subdir).
- `build_tester_prompt` (§8) + the `## QA RESULTS` parser → verdict→exit mapping: PASS=0, FAIL=0 (report-only) / 10 (`--strict`), BLOCKED=8, UNKNOWN=1. Hardened: the contract header is required; PASS requires a consistent `run==passed` tally; a failed/blocked case or a non-zero backend exit downgrades; the unfilled `PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED` placeholder → UNKNOWN; a launch failure → BLOCKED (no traceback). claude output read via `--output-format json`. Suites embedded in a collision-safe fence (prompt-injection guard).
- `--kind auto` detection; `resolved_tester_backend` (claude default, `-m codex`/env honored, unsupported/suffixed testers rejected).

## Security (first un-caged agent in review-cli)
- The worktree sets the agent's **working directory**, bounding SUT mutations via cwd — it is **NOT an OS sandbox** (an un-caged shell with absolute paths can read/write anywhere + network). README + docstrings say this plainly; run qa only against trusted SUTs/suites.
- Prompt built at the ACTUAL run cwd (never the user's checkout); the `--in-place` prompt tells the agent its writes are NOT disposable. Default report written outside the SUT tree (0600). `--in-place` refused over a dirty/unknown-state git tree (fails closed) for both seats.
- Comment by `_READONLY_AGENT_DENIED_PERMISSIONS` records the deliberate write/exec exception.

## DoD (`tests/fixtures/qa/`)
A tiny shell SUT with a known off-by-one bug (`add 2 2 → 5`, must-FAIL) + a known-good variant (`→ 4`, must-PASS), each with a prose `## Case:` suite.

title: feat(qa): review-qa Phase 3 — SUT env bring-up (detect/reuse/health-gate/guaranteed-teardown)
body:
Phase 3 of `review qa`: the SUT ENVIRONMENT bring-up layer that stands the System-Under-Test up before the Phase-2 executor drives it, and GUARANTEES teardown of only what this run brought up.

## Lifecycle (`reviewlib/qa/env.py`)
`stage-detect` -> `reuse-if-reachable` (NEVER tear down a reused stage) -> else bring-up via a `qa/setup.sh` hook (lightweight default) or `docker compose -p <ns> up -d --wait` (heavier) -> `health-gate` (poll; fail `EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY`) -> seed -> hand the running env to the executor -> GUARANTEED teardown.

`reviewlib/qa/config.py` parses `docs/tests/qa.yaml` (stage / bringup / health / seed / teardown) into typed dataclasses with validation. Absent is fine; malformed is a clean `QaConfigError` (exit 2).

Wired into `modes/qa.py`: `_run_with_env` brings the env up before `run_tester` and tears it down in a `finally` on EVERY exit path. A SUT with no stage / hook / config skips bring-up gracefully (the agent does its own local bring-up).

## Teardown is REAL, not backstop-reaping (the spec adversarial must-fix)
`backstop.py` only SIGKILLs registered subprocess GROUPS; `docker compose up -d` daemonizes into the Docker daemon and is in no child group of `review`. So this layer registers a REAL `atexit` + SIGINT/SIGTERM teardown keyed by the `-p` project name (or the hook's `setup.sh down`), independent of subprocess reaping. **Ownership rule:** teardown only ever targets the namespaced `-p` project we created (never a bare `down`) or the hook we ran — a reused stage is NEVER touched, and qa never runs against the user's real infra. Reentrancy-safe (non-blocking lock acquire in the signal path).

## Exit codes
Already reserved in `cli.py`, +1-shifted from the spec because brainstorm took 5: `EXIT_QA_NO_ENV=7`, `EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY=9` (`EXIT_QA_SUT_BOOT_FAILED=8` is Phase 2's).

## Tests
`tests/test_qa_env.py` proves the DoD: (a) reachable stage reused & not torn down; (b) hook env brought up, health-gated, handed off, torn down; (c) never-healthy env fails `EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY` with teardown still run; (d) teardown guaranteed when the executor throws + via the atexit hook. Deterministic (stdlib HTTP server + shell `setup.sh` hooks, **no docker, no model**) for CI; the live `docker compose` bring-up + `-p`-namespaced teardown test is gated behind `REVIEW_QA_DOCKER=1` (verified passing locally against a real daemon). title: feat(board): resilience under concurrent load — memory cap + slow-seat deprioritize
body:
Closes #65.

## Problem
Under swarm load (~6 concurrent `review` invocations, each running a parallel pool, plus a `review quorum --pool 3`), the board became fragile: reviews slowed, and seats died mid-review (an Opus seat "died mid-review, exit 1" -> agents fell back to codex). Root causes:
- **Memory pressure**: `run_panel` uses `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs))` with NO global cap, so a high `--pool` (or a cascade of reserve backfills) fans out into as many concurrent heavy model subprocesses as there are seats -> OOM-kill.
- **A pathologically-slow reserve seat** (`oc:zai/glm-5.2`, was priority 6) that, when promoted, stalled the failover critical path.

## Fix
1. **Memory-aware concurrency cap** (`reviewlib/process.py`): a process-wide semaphore in `_run_streamed` bounds concurrent heavy backend subprocesses (default **4**, `$REVIEW_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `<=0` disables, clamped to 64). Acquired BEFORE `Popen`, released in `finally` AFTER the child is reaped. A queued seat **waits** for a slot (never dropped); the per-call timeout starts only after spawn, so queueing can't falsely time it out. The single-seat gate (`--pool 1`) and the default pool of 4 are unaffected.
2. **Deprioritize `oc:zai/glm-5.2`** to the bottom of the board (last-resort reserve): still available, but Qwen/DeepSeek/Gemini are promoted before it — off the critical path by default.
3. **Observability**: a seat parked in the cap queue logs a distinct `waiting for a concurrency slot` marker and writes its header only after acquiring the slot, so a queued seat isn't misread as hung/started.

Per-seat hard timeout + dying-seat-is-a-non-answer resilience already held (verified): `_run_streamed` enforces `proc.wait(timeout)` -> SIGKILL group -> rc 124, and the failover board treats any non-usable seat as a non-answer and backfills/proceeds. No board seat is ever dispatched with `timeout=None` (CLI floors it to `PANEL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`), so a hung seat always releases its slot.

## Tests
New `tests/test_concurrency_cap.py`: cap reader/clamp; the cap HOLDS (peak <=2 concurrent real children under a 6-seat fan-out); a disabled cap runs all concurrently; **a queued seat is NOT falsely timed out**; **a spawn failure releases the slot**; the single-seat path never blocks. Board-order tests + the dashboard fallback test + the README board table updated for the deprioritization.

Full smoke suite green (23 checks, 0 failures), ruff clean. Review-gate (`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1`) ran twice -> `[ok]`, no blocking findings (the first round's "untested correctness claims" were addressed by adding the queued-timeout and spawn-failure tests).

title: feat(qa): review-qa bot Tier-1 hermetic harness (fake Telegram + inject/capture)
body:
## What

The per-SUT-TYPE **bot Tier-1 hermetic harness** for `review qa` (Increment 5 of `docs/specs/review-qa.md` §7.3). review-qa shipped through Phase 3 (write/exec executor #62 + SUT env bring-up #64); this lands the deterministic, hermetic **BOT** harness — no real token, no live network, runs in normal CI.

Closes #67

## How it works (the hermetic mechanism)

- **`reviewlib/qa/bot_harness.py`** — an in-process **fake Telegram Bot-API server** (stdlib `http.server`, `127.0.0.1`-only). It answers `getUpdates` honoring the real **offset/ack long-poll contract** (retain-until-acked, with a short server-side hold so a real `timeout=30` poller doesn't busy-loop at 100% CPU), captures outbound `sendMessage`/`sendPhoto`/`answerCallbackQuery`/etc, and stubs `getMe`/`deleteWebhook` so a bot's startup handshake succeeds. `boot_bot` spawns the SUT bot in its **own process group** pointed at the fake via `TG_API_BASE`, with a continuous **stdout-drain thread** so a chatty bot can't deadlock on a full pipe. A **positive capability probe** turns an unwired sender (one that hardcodes `api.telegram.org`) into a LOUD `BLOCKED` with the `TG_API_BASE` pointer — never a false pass on zero captured sends. Fails closed on a real-looking `TG_CHAT_ID`.
- **`reviewlib/qa/bot_driver.py`** — the **deterministic driver**. Parses each prose `## Case:` block's `Send:`/`Send-callback:`/`Expect:`/`Expect-no:`/`Expect-silent` grammar, injects the synthetic update, waits **until the expectations are met** (so a delayed multi-message reply isn't false-failed) or the case timeout, classifies PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED, and emits the **same `## QA RESULTS` contract** the executor's parser reads. Distinguishes a crashed bot (output tail) from an unwired one. **Guaranteed teardown** of the fake + bot on every exit path.
- **`reviewlib/qa/config.py`** — a `sut.bot` block (`driver: mock`, `command`, `env`, `skip_probe`); `skip_probe` is strict-boolean parsed (`bool("false")` is `True` in Python — a safety flag must not misparse). **`reviewlib/modes/qa.py`** — `--kind bot` + a `sut.bot` mock config routes to the hermetic path (deterministic, off the un-caged-agent blast radius); a shared kind-resolution honors `sut.kind` from `qa.yaml` under `--kind auto` for both the hermetic routing and the executor fallback runbook.

Bot Tier-1 runs **deterministically — no un-caged agent**: "send update → assert reply" needs no write/exec agent, so it stays off the agent-cage blast radius entirely.

## Exit codes

Reuses the existing qa classes — a hermetic bring-up failure is `VERDICT: BLOCKED` → `EXIT_QA_SUT_BOOT_FAILED` (8); a found bug is **report-only** (exit 0), `--strict` flips it to 10. No new exit code needed.

## DoD (must-pass + must-fail fixtures)

- `tests/fixtures/qa/bot-good` — `/start` → "welcome" → **VERDICT: PASS** (4/4 cases), exit 0.
- `tests/fixtures/qa/bot-buggy` — wrong `/start` reply (missing "welcome") → **VERDICT: FAIL** with a P1 finding citing the captured reply as proof; exit 0 report-only, exit 10 under `--strict`.

Both driven end-to-end through the **real** hermetic harness (fake server + a real stdlib subprocess bot + inject/capture + parse). 35 deterministic bot tests in `tests/test_qa_bot.py`, full `tests/smoke.py` green, ruff clean. Three rounds of multi-model review (codex) addressed: long-poll busy-loop, stdout-pipe deadlock, capture-window false-fail, `skip_probe` bool misparse, and `sut.kind` auto-routing.

## Deferred (tracked)

- **Tier 2** (live MTProto/Telethon + agent-browser Telegram Web, `requires_live_telegram`) — needs provisioned test creds + test DC.
- The tg-cli `tg`-sender `TG_API_BASE` fix (so tg-cli itself is testable as a bot SUT) — the harness ships independent of it; any bot whose sender honors `TG_API_BASE` is testable today.

title: feat(qa): review-qa web Tier-1 deterministic harness (Playwright bring-up + DOM-driving driver)
body:
Closes #69.

## What

The **web (Playwright) Tier-1 harness** for `review qa --kind web` — a SUT-driver that tests a web-app project end-to-end by driving it in a real headless browser, **deterministically**, mirroring the merged bot Tier-1 hermetic harness (#68).

## How

- **`reviewlib/qa/web_harness.py`** — bring the app's dev server up (`sut.web.command`, in its own process group), health-gate it reachable at `base_url`, then drive it via Playwright (headless Chromium) behind a small `PageDriver` protocol (`goto`/`click`/`fill`/`text_content`/`current_url`/`screenshot`). The protocol decouples the driver from Playwright so the core logic is **browser-free and unit-testable**. Guaranteed server + browser teardown (try/finally + process-group reap). Playwright is **gated behind `REVIEW_QA_PLAYWRIGHT=1`** + an installed-browser check — off or missing is a clean `BLOCKED` with the install command, never a crash.
- **`reviewlib/qa/web_driver.py`** — the deterministic driver: parse the prose `## Case:` grammar into ordered actions + DOM assertions, run them, classify PASS/FAIL with evidence (failing selector/text/url + a screenshot), and emit the same `## QA RESULTS` contract the executor parser reads.
- **`reviewlib/qa/config.py`** — a `sut.web` block (`driver`/`base_url`/`command`/`ready_path`/`env`/`ready_timeout_s`) with validation.
- **`reviewlib/modes/qa.py`** — `--kind web` (or `sut.kind: web` under `--kind auto`) routes a `sut.web` SUT to the deterministic harness, off the un-caged executor — a clean self-contained fast path with worktree isolation + the same report-only verdict→exit mapping.

## The case grammar

```
## Case: home page greets the visitor
Goto: /
Expect-text: Welcome
Expect-no: error

## Case: login redirects
Goto: /login
Fill: #user = alice          # space-padded ' = ' so input[name=email] keeps its own '='
Click: button[type=submit]
Expect-url: /dashboard
```

`Goto`/`Click`/`Fill` are ordered actions; `Expect-text`/`Expect-no`/`Expect-url` are substring assertions checked after. Cases share one page (session continuity, documented). A prose-only case BLOCKS.

## DoD — must-pass / must-fail

`tests/fixtures/qa/web-{good,buggy}` + `tests/test_qa_web.py`: the good app (landing says "Welcome") verdicts **PASS**; the buggy app (wrong landing text) verdicts **FAIL** with a P1 finding — driven through the REAL driver against the fixtures' real HTML.

## How it gates in CI

The deterministic path needs **no browser**: the driver speaks only the `PageDriver` protocol, so an in-memory page (which mirrors `inner_text("body")`, not raw HTML) exercises the parser + action mapping + QA-RESULTS emission fully — green in normal CI. A **live-browser** variant of the DoD is gated on `REVIEW_QA_PLAYWRIGHT=1` and SKIPs without Chromium (verified locally against real Chromium: good→PASS, buggy→FAIL).

title: fix(diff): --staged -C <repo> honors the -C repo, strip leaked git env (#71)
body:
## The bug (review-cli#71)

`review diff --staged -C <repoB>` and `review just-ask --staged -C <repoB>` mis-resolved the diff to an **UNRELATED repo** when a parent process had `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported (a git hook spawning `review`, a stale shell export). Those vars pin git to a specific repo regardless of `cwd`/`-C`, so `git -C /repoB diff --cached` silently read the **env's** repo, not repoB.

This is the EXACT command every review-gate uses (`review diff --staged -m claude:... --pool 1 -C <worktree>`), so the gate had been reviewing the **wrong (or empty) diff** — a likely major cause of the 'review returns nothing / banner-only' degradation mis-attributed to the weekly cap.

## Root cause

Every git invocation (`_git_diff`, `_effective_cwd`'s `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `_is_git_repo`) inherited the parent environment via `subprocess.run(env=None)`. With the repo-pinning git vars set, the `cwd`/`-C` anchor is overridden by the env.

```
# proof (pre-fix): from cwd repoA, with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE=repoA, -C repoB
git -C /repoB diff --cached  ->  returns repoA's diff   # WRONG
```

## Fix

Add `reviewlib/process.py:git_repo_env()` — the environment with the repo-pinning git vars (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`) removed. Every repo-anchored git call now runs as `git -C <cwd>` **AND** `env=git_repo_env()`:

- `cli._git_diff` (the diff / staged-diff probe)
- `cli._effective_cwd` (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`)
- `cli._is_git_repo` (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`)
- `backends._opencode_runs_in_repo` (the agentic-seat repo gate)
- `install._write_review_stamp` (the stamp stays anchored to the SAME `-C` repo as the diff it stamps — keeps the #18 stamp/tool alignment)
- the isolated-sandbox `git init` in `backends.review_opencode` + `vision_client` (a leaked `GIT_DIR` can't divert the sandbox init to the leaked repo)

## Tests (RED-first)

`tests/test_staged_diff_honors_c_repo.py`: from cwd repoA with the git env leaked to repoA, `review diff --staged -C repoB` and `review just-ask --staged -C repoB` must review repoB's staged diff, not repoA's. **Failed pre-fix** (captured repoA's diff), **passes post-fix**. Registered in `smoke.py`. Full smoke green (23/0/0), ruff clean.

## Before / after (end-to-end)

| | CWD resolved | diff reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (env leak) | repoA | repoA (WRONG) |
| post-fix (env leak) | repoB | repoB (correct) |

## Review-gate note

Could not get a model stamp: every seat is degraded right now — codex seat-fatal/rate-limited (and roams to the wrong repo = this very bug), claude-opus 'malformed API response' (weekly cap), gemini empty, commandcode/kimi unconfigured. Verified independently (RED-first repro + before/after + smoke + ruff + no-regression check). Committed with `REVIEW_SKIP` (never `--no-verify`).

Closes #71

## What

The third and final per-SUT-type review-qa harness: the **VS Code extension Tier-1 deterministic harness** (`--kind ext`). Completes the bot (#68) / web (#70) / ext trio. Mirrors the web harness structure exactly: an `ext_harness.py` + `ext_driver.py` + `sut.ext` config + `--kind ext` deterministic routing in `modes/qa.py`.

Closes #73.

## How it works

- **`ext_harness.py`** — owns the heavy VS Code launch. It shells to a reference TS runner (`reviewlib/qa/ext_runner/ext_runner.mts`) that REUSES the proven `launchVSCode` pattern from `ext-test-projects/e2e/setup/electron-app.ts` (isolated `--user-data-dir` / fresh `--extensions-dir`, `--disable-workspace-trust` / `--skip-welcome`, `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, CDP connect, `window.screenshot` over CDP). The runner speaks a line-delimited JSON protocol over stdin/stdout (`run_command` / `open_file` / `notifications` / `editor_text` / `webview_text` / `screenshot`). The launch is gated behind `REVIEW_QA_VSCODE=1` + a node/tsx check (never bun — bun hangs Electron launch on macOS); off-by-default or no-runtime → a controlled BLOCKED with the enable command, never a crash.
- **`ext_driver.py`** — the deterministic driver. Parses the prose `## Case:` grammar into actions + assertions, drives them against an `ExtAutomation` protocol, classifies PASS/FAIL with evidence (+ a `window.screenshot` on FAIL), and emits the same `## QA RESULTS` contract the executor parser reads.
- **The `ExtAutomation` protocol seam** keeps the pure logic (parser, action mapping, QA-RESULTS emission) unit-testable with NO VS Code — exactly how the web harness decouples from Playwright behind `PageDriver`.

## Case grammar

```
## Case: hello command greets the user
Command: myext.hello              # run a VS Code command id
Open: src/file.ts                 # open a workspace file
Expect-notification: Hello        # a notification toast must contain this
Expect-editor-text: const x       # the active editor must contain this
Expect-webview: <h1>Panel         # the extension webview body must contain this
Expect-no: error                  # none of the surfaces may contain this
```

- `tests/fixtures/qa/ext-good` — a tiny extension whose `myext.hello` shows "Hello from myext" → the smoke suite verdicts **PASS** (2/2 cases).
- `tests/fixtures/qa/ext-buggy` — same suite, wrong notification ("Goodbye, cruel world") → verdicts **FAIL** with a P1 finding.

Both run through the REAL driver against a fake automation backed by each fixture's `behavior.json` (kept in sync with `src/extension.js`), so the DoD is deterministic in normal CI. A live-VS-Code leg is gated on `REVIEW_QA_VSCODE=1` and SKIPs without node + a VS Code binary.

title: fix(claude): run the opus review seat via claude --print, not the claude-p TUI-scraper
body:
Closes #76

## Root cause

The `claude:claude-opus-4-8` seat — the PRIMARY review-gate seat — routed through `claude-p`, whose own docstring admits it "does not invoke `claude -p`; it starts interactive `claude` under a PTY" (`pty.openpty()`) and **screen-scrapes** the result. That scrape is a lossy redraw surface. Reproduced live (`--raw-log`): the model produced a complete, correct review, but the fullscreen TUI redrew it dozens of times interleaved with the banner + spinner frames (`✶ Transmuting…`), smearing characters (`dd(a,b)` for `add(a,b)`, `neds-changes`), and `claude-p`'s scraper couldn't isolate the final answer → `assistant_output_timeout` → **empty stdout, exit 2**. That is the "output clobbered by an interactive fullscreen renderer bleeding into the TTY" agents reported. Distinct from the weekly-cap throttle — this is TUI-into-a-pipe corruption, and it's fixable.

## Fix

- **Invoke `claude --print --output-format text` directly** (genuine headless print mode — no PTY, no TUI, no scrape; clean UTF-8 stdout). Fall back to `claude-p` only when the `claude` binary is absent.
- **Read-only via an empty tool allowlist** (`--tools ""` = all built-in tools off) on the direct path — stronger and more future-proof than a denylist, and it stops real `claude` warning on claude-p-only tool names.
- **Decoration-hostile child env** (`TERM=dumb` / `NO_COLOR=1` / `CI=1`).
- **Belt-and-suspenders**: strip ANSI/OSC/control sequences (incl. carriage-return overwrite bytes) from the captured verdict via a single shared `strip_control_sequences` (now the one source for that and the `-o` output file).

Other seats and the API path are unchanged.

## Live proof (dogfood)

`review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` run against this PR's own staged diff, using the worktree's own `bin/review`:

```
## claude:claude-opus-4-8 [ok]

`claude --print --output-format text --permission-mode dontAsk --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --safe-mode --append-system-prompt <read-only-review>  (prompt via stdin)`
```

Clean, parseable verdict via the new direct path — no TUI bleed, no stderr tool warnings. The opus seat stamped its own PR `[ok]`.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_claude_seat_robust.py`: the strip helper parses interleaved ANSI/TUI/spinner/CR noise to the correct verdict; the direct-`claude` argv (print mode, `--tools ""`, no claude-p-only flags) and the claude-p fallback argv are asserted; binary resolution prefers `claude`; the decoration-hostile env is wired; the end-to-end strip+env wiring is pinned.
- `tests/test_streaming.py`: updated claude-backend argv assertions + a fallback test + a REAL-`_run_streamed` test proving `env` reaches the child.
- `tests/test_claude_api.py` / `test_workspace_trust.py`: CLI-presence mocks moved to a backends-local `_which_optional` indirection (no global stdlib monkeypatch).
- Full `python tests/smoke.py` green (23 checks, 0 failures); `ruff check .` clean.

Version bumped 0.6.0 -> 0.7.0; CHANGELOG updated.

body:
Consumer-side residual of rig-cli#8: the review board can now resolve a seat by **capability tag** or **role** from the shared `agent-tools/lib/contracts/models.yaml` manifest — additively, and with graceful degradation when the manifest isn't reachable.

## What
- **`reviewlib/manifest.py`** (new): loads `models.yaml` (via `$REVIEW_MODELS_MANIFEST` / `$AGENT_TOOLS_DIR` / conventional checkout paths, fail-soft), exposing `resolve_role`, `models_with_capability`, `resolve_capability`, `role_names`. - **`config.py`**: a config `board:` entry may name its seat by `capability: vision` (the strongest model carrying the tag) or `capability: role:reasoning` (the manifest's role map) instead of a literal `model:`. The resolved seat runs through the same `_expand_alias` normalization as a literal one.

## Backward-compat
Existing `-m <model>` and literal `model:` board entries are untouched. A host with no manifest reachable skips a `capability:` entry with a clear reason (a `role:<x>` hint for a pure role name, the canonical "no model carries the tag" message for a real-but-unmatched tag) and runs its literal seats / the hardcoded `DEFAULT_BOARD` — never a crash.

The manifest is another repo's source of truth. Hardened so a malformed one degrades, never crashes: non-string `roles:` keys are filtered (a `null`/numeric key can't crash a `.lower()` consumer), and a host with no resolvable home (a container under an arbitrary uid) no longer crashes the path probe.

title: feat(qa): harden the ext harness — queue-backed stdout reader + isolation warning
body:
## What (review-cli#75 — the bounded hardening)
- **Queue-backed stdout reader.** The ext runner's stdout was consumed via `select` + a text-mode `readline` in `_await_ready` / `_read_reply`. A text-mode pipe buffers ABOVE the OS fd, so `select` could report "nothing to read" while a full line sat decoded in the buffer (a false timeout), and `readline` issued anyway could block past the deadline. Replaced with a dedicated reader THREAD draining complete lines into a thread-safe queue (`_StdoutLineReader`, one per session, shared by `_await_ready` and the automation so a single thread owns the stream); each consumer polls with its own deadline, so a silent-but-alive or mid-reply-dying runner is bounded by the timeout, not the buffering.
- **Isolation-escape warning.** An ABSOLUTE `sut.ext` `extension_path`/`workspace` (or a `..` traversal) silently escaped the isolated worktree (`cwd / abs` drops `cwd`) while the docstring promised "relative to the run cwd" — VS Code would load the extension from the user's real checkout. `review qa` now WARNS that the ext run is not isolated under the default (worktree) run (silent under `--in-place`, where such a path is expected); `_path_escapes` catches both the absolute and traversal cases.

## Tests
The reader unit (line delivery / timeout / EOF), the `_read_reply` timeout / runner-death / noise-skip paths against a fake python runner, and the escape warning (absolute + traversal + the `_path_escapes` predicate). Full smoke green (23/0), ruff clean. Version bump -> 0.9.1.

## Deferred (tracked in #82)
The big follow-ups from the issue — Tier-2 window-screenshot visual diffing, more assertion types (status bar / quick-pick / diagnostics / terminal), the command-palette helper command, and the standalone `vscode-playwright` package — need real infra and are out of scope here. title: feat(qa): bot AGENT-SIDE tier — drive a bridge bot (tg-ctl) agent→card→tap→answer
body:
## What

Adds an **AGENT-SIDE tier** to the hermetic bot Tier-1 harness for **bridge** bots like `tg-ctl`. Their load-bearing flow is the opposite of the inbound `Send:`/`Expect:` path: the AGENT emits an AskUserQuestion/permission via a hook client → the daemon forwards ONE inline-button card to (the fake) Telegram → the user TAPS → the answer flows back to the hook client's stdout. The inbound inject/capture path has no seam to emit the question or read the answer; this adds exactly that, reusing the **UNCHANGED** `FakeTelegram`.

Closes #86.

## Pieces

- **config (`sut.bot`):** `ask_command` (selects the tier), `seed` (pre-boot precondition files via template tokens), `owner_id`, configurable `sender_id` (defaults to `owner_id` — a bridge gates a tap on the owner), `ready_file`. Rejects `driver: mtproto` + `ask_command` (the agent-side loop is mock-only; the live path would silently ignore `ask_command`).
- **harness seam:** `emit_question(payload)→AskHandle`, `AskHandle.await_answer()→str|None` (None/hang = tap-loss), `cards_captured()`, `tap(card,label)` (synthetic `callback_query`). Seed-path containment so a stray `../` from a reviewed repo's qa.yaml can't write outside the throwaway workdir.
- **grammar:** `Ask-question:`/`Ask-permission:` / `Expect-card: N` / `Tap: <label>` / `Expect-answer: <substr>`. A re-Ask with `Expect-card: 0` + `Expect-answer:` is the **tg-cli#98** duplicate-card regression assertion.
- **fixtures:** a faithful miniature bridge bot (`tgctl-agentside/sut.py`, an independent SUT-side impl) that verdicts PASS replaying an answered re-fire and FAILs under `SUT_DUP_BUG=1`; plus a `tgctl-real` suite for the RED→GREEN proof against a real `tg-ctl`.

## Proof (the whole point)

The SAME real-`tg-ctl` suite, run through the harness:

| tg-ctl | verdict | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| current (e41bb79, the #98 fix) | **PASS** | one card per question, tap reaches the agent, answered re-fire replays with NO second card |
| pre-#98 (271ff1d) | **FAIL** | the answered re-fire posts a duplicate, superseded card (cards before=1, after=2) — the #98 class |

That RED→GREEN is the proof the harness catches the real bug class. Both ends are pinned by the gated `test_real_tgctl_agent_side_proof` (`REVIEW_QA_TGCTL_DIR` + `REVIEW_QA_TGCTL_EXPECT`).

title: feat(backends): add OpenRouter backend (-m openrouter:<model>)
body:
## What

Adds **OpenRouter** as a review-cli backend so any seat can be `-m openrouter:<model>` — e.g. `openrouter:anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `openrouter:openai/gpt-4o`. OpenRouter is an OpenAI-compatible aggregator fronting 400+ models behind one key, so this **reuses the existing `_openai_compatible_request` transport** that z.ai/commandcode already use (no parallel mechanism).

Closes #88.

## How it's wired

- **`review_openrouter()`** (`reviewlib/backends.py`) — POSTs to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions`, auth `Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. API-only (no OpenRouter CLI; forced `REVIEW_OPENROUTER_MODE=cli` is a hard error, never a silent POST).
- **Parser**: `_match_named_backend` routes `openrouter` / `openrouter:<slug>` (no collision with opencode's `oc:`/`opencode:`).
- **Availability**: `backend_available("openrouter")` is `False` (loud skip) without the key, `True` with it — so the moderator/panel filter never picks a dead seat.
- **Default model**: bare `openrouter` → OpenRouter's own auto-router `openrouter/auto` (never-stale). Override via `openrouter:<slug>` suffix or `OPENROUTER_MODEL`; base via `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`. Suffix preserves the slug's `/` and any `:free`/`:beta`/`:nitro` variant; empty/whitespace suffix + env fall back to the default (never POST `model:""`).
- **Auth safety**: only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` resolves (a foreign `OPENAI_API_KEY` must not — cross-provider key-leak guard). No key committed or written to disk.
- **Optional headers**: `OPENROUTER_HTTP_REFERER` / `OPENROUTER_X_TITLE` (leaderboard attribution) via a new `extra_headers` hook; canonical `Authorization`/`Content-Type` written last + any stray case-insensitive auth/content-type in `extra_headers` dropped → a stray header can never shadow the real key. Header values validated (latin-1-encodable, no control chars) and dropped if unsafe → no CRLF injection, no crash on a non-latin-1 title.

## Tests

24 offline cases added to `tests/test_provider_keys.py` (no live API call — `urllib.request.urlopen` faked): routing, OpenAI request shape, slug/variant + env overrides, suffix-beats-env, optional + unsafe (CRLF/non-latin-1) headers, auth-shadow defense (3 cases), missing-key + forced-cli dead-backend, no-content/HTTP-error fail-closed, key-from-`.env`, and `mode_review` board integration. Full `python tests/smoke.py` suite + ruff green locally.

## Review

Multi-round `review diff -m claude:claude-opus-4-8` to `[ok]`; addressed each finding (empty-suffix/whitespace-env fallback, explicit reserved-header drop, header-value sanitization, missing-key test, docstrings).

title: feat(qa): real MTProto LiveBotDriver for review-qa Tier-2 live bot tier
body:
## What

Replaces the bot Tier-2 `LiveTierUnavailable` scaffold with a **real MTProto (Telethon) `LiveBotDriver`** for review-qa's LIVE tier. The driver connects as a dedicated test Telegram USER account and drives a prose suite against a real bot — `send` a message, `expect` a reply, `tap` an inline button — behind the same protocol seam the hermetic Tier-1 path speaks, emitting the identical `## QA RESULTS` contract.

## Key pieces

- **`reviewlib/qa/live_tier.py::LiveBotDriver`** — connect (auth check + chat resolve + high-water mark), idempotent disconnect (deletes our own sent messages), `send` (re-bases the high-water per `Send:` so a multi-message reply can't bleed into the next case), `expect` (polls for the next inbound reply; skips our outbound + Telegram service messages; bounded by the caller deadline **and** a fixed per-fetch op ceiling — a hung `get_messages` → controlled BLOCKED, a healthy-but-slow fetch near the deadline → clean no-reply), `tap` (callback query by label or index). Lazy-imports telethon; any failure is a controlled `LiveTierUnavailable`, never a traceback.
- **`reviewlib/qa/live_bot_runner.py`** — the live suite runner: parse the live grammar (`Send`/`Expect`/`Expect-no`/`Expect-silent`/`Tap`), drive each case with per-case error isolation, classify against the bot's real replies, label the transcript as the live backend.
- **`reviewlib/modes/qa.py`** — the gate-ok dispatch connects the real driver and drives the suite (loaded only on the gate-ok branch; `max_cases` forwarded). The creds-absent branch still SKIPs LOUD with the exact missing-creds BLOCKED, correctly labelled as the live backend.
- Availability gate + fail-closed safety preserved (opt-in flag + the 4 creds + a refusal when the test chat equals the real chat). `pyproject`: optional `[live]` extra (`telethon>=1.34,<2`), version `0.12.0 → 0.13.0`. web/ext live drivers remain #82 skeletons.

## Tests

29 driver/runner tests + the live-tier suite — all mock the MTProto client at the transport boundary (in-memory fake Telethon client + scripted fake driver): **no creds, no telethon, no network, no Telegram**. Covers connect/auth/resolve/timeout, the `expect` deadline + per-fetch bound (hung vs slow fetch), the multi-message re-base, the tap flow, per-case isolation, and the dispatch gate/label. CI installs no telethon and uses no live creds.

## Live-run status

End-to-end CLI was verified to the gate boundary (no-creds → BLOCKED naming the 4 creds; creds-present-but-telethon-absent → BLOCKED naming the dep; real Telethon 1.44 construction → controlled BLOCKED on a bad session, no traceback). A full live run against a real bot is **not** included: it needs a Telethon `StringSession` for a **dedicated throwaway** test account + a dedicated test chat, which require interactive auth (login code + 2FA) and must not reuse a production account — provisioning is a CTO step (the gate names exactly what to set).

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking)

- `expect` accepts any inbound message in a supergroup; for a multi-member test chat it should filter by the bot's sender id (the spec already mandates a dedicated 1:1-style test chat, which is the primary safety).
- Small test gaps: `connect()` re-entrancy, `flood_sleep_threshold` set path, `send(reply_to=)` passthrough.

title: fix(install): use `command git` in pre-commit hook template to bypass shell aliases
body:
## Summary

- Replace bare `git` with `command git` in all git calls in the `_PRECOMMIT` hook template
- `command` bypasses shell aliases and functions, ensuring the hook computes the same hash as review-cli's internal call
- Fixes false-blocking of legitimately-reviewed commits when a shell alias wraps `git`

## Problem

`review install-commit-hook` installs a pre-commit hook that computes:
```sh
h=$(git diff --no-ext-diff --cached | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1)
```

Tools like RTK (Rust Token Killer) can be wired as shell aliases that rewrite `git diff` output into a compact summary — completely different from git's unified diff format. This produces a different hash than what review-cli wrote to the stamp (review-cli uses `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` which bypasses aliases).

Result: the hook blocks commits even after a legitimate review.

## Fix

`command git` (POSIX built-in) bypasses shell aliases and functions while still walking PATH to find the git binary. Applied to all git calls in the template: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit`, `git diff --cached --name-only`, `git diff --no-ext-diff --cached`, and `git rev-parse --git-path review-stamp`.

Mirrors agent-tools#156 which fixed the same issue in the global `review-gate` hook.

Closes #101

## Test plan

- [x] Install-related tests pass (`tests/test_install_shadow_warning.py`, `tests/test_staged_diff_honors_c_repo.py`)
- [x] Review stamp hash verified: Python `hashlib.sha256(diff.encode()).hexdigest()` == shell `command git diff ... | shasum -a 256` (confirmed identical)
- [x] End-to-end: `rtk git commit` with correct stamp passes; without stamp blocks

title: feat(spec-web): single multi-spec daemon + --agent submit delivery (tg#5680, tg#5722)
body:
## What & why

Two CTO requests (tg#5680 + tg#5722):

1. **Single multi-spec daemon (tg#5680).** The old `review spec-web` spun up one
   foreground server per spec. This replaces that with **one persistent daemon** that
   serves every registered spec by name at `/spec/<name>` (a navigator at `/` lists them),
   so a single port / Tailscale mapping covers all specs. The daemon is a managed service
   via the shared `agenttools_service` lib (same pattern as `review dashboard`).

2. **`--agent` + submit delivery (tg#5722).** Submitted review comments used to sit in
   `~/.config/review-cli/spec-web/<hash>.json` with nobody reading them (the stdout watcher
   is only alive while an agent blocks on `serve`; the daemon outlives every launching
   agent). Now an owning `--agent <name>` is **required** to launch the daemon, and on every
   Submit the batch is **injected into that agent's live tmux session** — the same mechanism
   `tg-ctl` uses to inject inbound Telegram (`[TG from …]`) into a running session.

## How it works

**Daemon / navigator**
- `registry.py` — durable name→path map (`registry.json`), idempotent by resolved path,
  slug-deduped names, flock-guarded load-modify-write, reads corrupt/empty as empty.
- `service.py` — the daemon as an `agenttools_service.Service` (stable port `7920`), with
  the hidden `spec-web __serve` foreground entry so lifecycle actions never fork-bomb.
- `server.py` — `make_daemon_server` + `/spec/<name>` routing that reuses the SAME per-path
  comment stores as the single-spec server (full compat), a server-rendered navigator,
  SSE live-reload (`/api/events`, `spec-changed` on mtime change), and a cross-process
  `watch_submits` handoff (marker-framed JSON on stdout).

**Delivery**
- `deliver.py` — tg-ctl's live-proven tmux injection: `send-keys -l` for one line /
  `load-buffer`+`paste-buffer -p` for multi-line, then a paced separate `Enter` (Ink TUIs
  drop a combined/too-fast Enter); pane discovery under a forced UTF-8 locale (launchd
  inherits none); agent name matches a tmux **window** name first, then a **session** name.
  One line per comment: `[SPEC-WEB comment on <spec> §<section>] "<quote>" — <body>
  (question, id <id>)` + a `review spec-web reply <id> …` pointer. **Best-effort** — a
  missing tmux session never fails the Submit (the batch is already durable in the store).
- `--agent` is required by the daemon-launching actions (`start`/`run`/`enable`/`__serve`,
  `serve` and the legacy positional; and by `add` when it has to auto-start a stopped
  daemon). A per-spec `--agent` (on `add`/`serve`) overrides the daemon-wide default for
  that spec (`_owning_agent`). `status`/`stop`/`disable` don't need it.
- `app.js` surfaces a **failed** hand-off to the reviewer (a success stays quiet — the
  filter switch to Submitted is the signal).

## Activation

```sh
# start the daemon owned by the tmux window/session "ext"
review spec-web start --agent ext
# register specs (served immediately, no restart); open /spec/<name>
review spec-web add docs/specs/my-spec.md
review spec-web status            # running? + registered specs + their URLs
# one-shot: register + block until the reviewer submits, then hand back to the agent
review spec-web serve docs/specs/my-spec.md --agent ext
```

On Submit, the batch is injected into the `ext` session's pane. `--host 0.0.0.0` (default)
exposes it over Tailscale for phone review; writes are origin-guarded (loopback + the
discovered Tailscale host), reads are open (spec markdown, no secrets).

## Tests / evidence

- `tests/test_specweb_daemon.py` — 36 tests: registry (idempotent/dedupe/corrupt/missing),
  `/spec/<name>` routing + shared stores + add-while-running, SSE `spec-changed`,
  `watch_submits` baselining (fresh vs stale vs pinned), `--agent` ownership + priority,
  tmux pane matching, batch-scoped message formatting, submit delivery (spec agent vs
  daemon default vs none), and CLI wiring (agent-required, idempotent start, lib-absent
  fallbacks, backstop classification). Registered in `smoke.py`'s `_UNIT_FILES`.
- **Full CI smoke suite green** (`python tests/smoke.py`): `OK: 23 checks, 0 failures,
  0 skipped` (run in a venv with `pip install -e '.[test]'`, since this host's system
  python is PEP-668 externally-managed).
- **ruff clean** on all changed Python.
- Multi-model `review diff --staged` run; findings addressed: UI delivery feedback
  (app.js) and the `--agent`/delivery docs (README). See "Known / deferred" below.

## Known / deferred

- **Default bind host is `0.0.0.0`** — a reviewer seat flagged this. It is an intentional,
  documented choice: the feature exists for phone/Tailscale review, writes are origin-guarded
  and reads carry no secrets, and it matches the legacy per-spec servers. Flipping the
  default to loopback would regress the headline use case, so it's left as-is for @invntrm
  to decide rather than changed unilaterally.
- The review board ran **degraded** (2 of 4 model seats were out of API credits / timed
  out) — an environment limitation, not unreviewed code. The working seat (Gemini) reviewed
  every pass; a real single-model review wrote the commit-gate stamp.

title: feat(deploy): add scripts/deploy.sh — the rig-apply freshness hook
body:
Closes alex-mextner/review-cli#105.

## What

`scripts/deploy.sh`: the hook rig-cli 0.8.0+ runs on every `rig apply` to keep the installed `review` checkout fresh (a guarded ff-only pull — the install is a symlink to `bin/review`, pure Python, no build step, so a pull IS the deploy).

## Semantics

- **Default target**: the checkout the script itself lives in — rig invokes it no-arg with `cwd=<repo>` (`riglib/actions/runner.py _run_tool_deploy`) and the bin dir may not be on PATH (codex P1 in review). Outside a checkout: falls back to resolving the `review` symlink on PATH. `--checkout DIR` overrides; `--dry-run` reports without pulling.
- **Exit codes**: 0 up-to-date / ahead-only / deployed · 1 usage or environment refusal (dirty tracked tree, detached HEAD, non-repo, fetch failure, untracked-file ff collision) · 2 diverged from upstream (never merges/rebases for the user).
- Scrubs foreign `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` (the review-cli#72 hook-env hijack class); honors the configured `@{upstream}` (fork layouts); `daemon_changed` grep is pipe-free (pipefail/SIGPIPE false-negative found in review).
- Post-pull: bounded `install-skill` refresh (non-fatal) + a restart note when `reviewlib/` changed (a resident dashboard/spec-web daemon holds old code until restarted).

## Tests

17 cases in `tests/test_deploy_sh.py` drive the real script against throwaway origin+clone pairs (wired into `tests/smoke.py`). Full suite: 23/23 green. Review: multi-round, codex + gemini `[ok]` on the final diff (board partially degraded — commandcode seats out of credits, Opus timing out).

title: feat(review): checkpoint via review diff --staged --commit
body:
## Summary

An agent iterating a review → fix findings → re-review loop needs a safe way to undo a
bad attempt. Until now the only tool was `git reset --hard`, which can destroy unrelated
uncommitted work belonging to a DIFFERENT session/agent sharing the same checkout — this
happened in production today and motivated this change.

- New `--commit` flag on `review diff` (**requires `--staged`** — a hard usage error
  otherwise, distinct exit code `EXIT_COMMIT_REQUIRES_STAGED=11`; never a silent no-op,
  never an implicit `--staged`, never a `git commit -a` fallback). Creates a real `git
  commit` of the staged diff right after the review completes, so a bad next attempt can
  be undone with the safe `git reset --soft HEAD~1` (does not touch untracked/foreign
  files) instead of `reset --hard` (wipes everything).
- The checkpoint gate mirrors the existing `--staged` commit-hook stamp's three
  conditions exactly (`ok` / `staged` / not `diff_from_stdin`): it checkpoints the
  *reviewed* diff, not a *clean* one — a review reporting open findings still gets
  committed, since `ok` means the pool produced usable verdicts, not "zero findings".
- The commit runs the repo's own commit-msg/pre-commit hooks (never bypassed with
  `--no-verify`); a hook rejection fails `--commit` loudly with its own distinct exit
  code (`EXIT_COMMIT_FAILED=12`) rather than silently skipping the checkpoint.
- **TOCTOU guard:** a review is multi-minute, so right before committing, `--commit`
  re-reads the staged index and refuses (same exit code) if it drifted from what was
  actually reviewed — it never commits changes another process/session staged meanwhile.
- README.md / AGENTS.md / `review --help` now explicitly warn against `git reset --hard`
  mid-review-cycle and name the safe alternatives; the "read-only" claims in
  README/AGENTS.md/`cli.py` are updated to carve out this one narrow, opt-in exception.

Closes #119.

## Dogfooding

Both commits on this branch were created by running `review diff --staged --commit` on
this PR's own diff (a real, live exercise of the feature). That review surfaced two
genuine findings which are fixed in the second commit (a TOCTOU race in the checkpoint,
and a test-hygiene leak into the real `~/.cache/agent-tools/last-review`). Two further
findings from a second dogfood round were deliberately NOT fixed inline — documented with
rationale in [#119](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/119#issuecomment-4882508536)
(one is an inherent, accepted trade-off; the other's proposed fix was tested and found to
break the feature on a machine with the `require-review-before-commit` global hook
installed, so it was reverted).

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check reviewlib/ tests/` — clean
- [x] `python3 tests/smoke.py` — 24/24 checks pass (includes the new
      `test_commit_flag_requires_staged` E2E CLI check)
- [x] `python3 tests/test_review_commit_checkpoint.py` — 8/8 pass (usage error, real
      commit created, checkpoints-with-findings, failing review does not checkpoint,
      piped stdin does not checkpoint, commit-hook rejection is a distinct exit code,
      index-drift refuses to checkpoint, board-path checkpoint)
- [x] `python3 tests/test_review_marker.py` — 10/10 pass (regression check: the
      pre-existing stamp/marker gate is untouched)
- [x] Manual E2E: `review diff --help` renders the new `--commit` flag's help text
- [x] Dogfooded: `review diff --staged --commit` on this PR's own diff, twice

title: feat(cli): add --effort flag — per-run reasoning effort across backends
body:
Closes #126 (source: Alex tg#6964)

## What

All modes (`review diff` / `just-ask` / `quorum` / `brainstorm` / `visual`) accept a repeatable `--effort` flag that sets the reasoning effort for every backend that supports it.

## Usage

```bash
# heavy brainstorm: fable at max reasoning depth
review brainstorm "how should we restructure the preview bridge?" --task HYP-999 -m fable --effort xhigh

# deep diff review, whole pool lifted
review diff --task HYP-999 --effort xhigh

# global level + per-provider override (codex kept cheaper)
review quorum "X or Y?" --task HYP-999 --effort xhigh --effort codex=high

# env transport (flag wins within its scope)
REVIEW_EFFORT=xhigh review diff --task HYP-999
REVIEW_EFFORT_CLAUDE=max review diff --task HYP-999
```

Levels: `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`.

## Per-backend mapping (one shared argv builder each, used by text AND visual paths)

| backend | control |
|---|---|
| claude CLI (direct print) | `--effort <level>` |
| claude API | `output_config: {effort: <level>}` |
| codex | `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` (`max` → `xhigh` with a warning — codex has no max tier) |
| opencode | `--variant <level>` (verbatim provider-specific passthrough) |
| gemini / zai / commandcode / openrouter / legacy claude-p | **stderr warning once per process** — never a silent ignore |

Semantics: provider-scoped `$REVIEW_EFFORT_<PROVIDER>` beats global `$REVIEW_EFFORT`; a bare global flag clears stale scoped env vars ('the flag wins'); a scoped flag overrides only its own provider; unknown levels are rejected at the CLI (exit 2) and in env readback (warn + fall through to global).

## Verification

- 30 new unit tests (`tests/test_effort_flag.py`, runs under pytest AND as the standalone smoke subprocess) + 5 vision-client effort tests
- Full `tests/smoke.py` gate: green except the pre-existing local-env `test_dashboard_managed_surface_and_lib_absent_fallback` failure (identical on main — missing agenttools_service lib on this host, unrelated)
- Live end-to-end: `review just-ask ... -m fable --effort low` ran the real fable seat through `claude --print --effort` successfully
- `review diff --staged` iterated 3 rounds (opus+codex+gemini); all round-2 findings fixed (scoped-flag env semantics, invalid-scoped-env fallback, warn-dedup lock, effort threading into the visual vision client); round 3 clean

title: feat(task): add --quorum-check gate to review task (self-merge-authority PR1)
body:
## What

PR1 of the 5-PR self-merge-authority program. Adds a queryable quorum bar to the
`review task` command so `ship.sh` can decide whether a task's review activity is
sufficient before allowing an agent to self-merge.

```
review task CODE --quorum-check [--min-iter 3] [--min-models 3] [--json]
```

- Computes `iterations` = count of run-stats records for CODE, and `distinct_models`
  = size of the union of `models` across those records.
- Exits **0** iff `iterations >= min_iter AND distinct_models >= min_models`, else nonzero.
- Prints a one-line verdict naming which half is short and by how much:
  - `quorum met for RC-131: 3 iterations across 3 distinct models (codex, fable5, gemini)`
  - `quorum NOT met for HYP-742: 2/3 iterations, 3/3 distinct models`
- `--json` emits a fixed shape: `{task_code, iterations, distinct_models, models, min_iter, min_models, passed}`.
- **Fail-closed:** invalid code, missing/unreadable store, or zero records for CODE all
  exit nonzero with an `error` message and never pass.

## Semantics note (for the next dev)

The enforceable bar today is "N iterations RAN across M distinct models" — the run-stats
store records dispatched runs, not pass/fail verdicts. A "passed-verdict" quorum (e.g.
require every reviewer to have come back clean) would need a new verdict field threaded
through `record_run`; this is called out in a code comment on `quorum_check`.

## Tests

12 new tests (quorum met; short on iterations; short on models; zero records / missing /
unreadable / unexpandable store fail-closed; invalid code; CLI verdict + ratio + custom
thresholds; `--json` shape and exit codes; requires-code). Full `tests/test_run_stats.py`
suite: **51 pass, 0 fail** under the standalone runner. `ruff check` clean.

## Review

`review diff --staged` run clean (exit 0). Gemini's non-blocking suggestions folded:
clarified the CLI help text as a structural (not verdict) check, and added return-shape
type assertions. Codex/GLM/commandcode reviewers were unavailable (usage limits / timeout),
not blocking findings.

## Do not self-merge

Opened for a separate merger to ship, per the program's process.

Closes #131

title: fix(task): rename --quorum-check to --check to avoid quorum collision
body:
## Summary
- `review task CODE --quorum-check` (#131/#133) collided semantically with the unrelated `review quorum` multi-model consensus panel. Renamed the CLI-facing flag to `--check`; `--min-iter`/`--min-models`/`--json` unchanged. Help text and verdict output ("quorum met/NOT met" -> "review bar met/NOT met") neutralized. The internal `reviewlib.stats.quorum_check` function name is kept (diff stays focused, per the ticket).
- **Found and fixed a real collision the rename introduced**: `--check` already existed as a value-taking flag (`--check NAME`, visual module force-activation) on every other subcommand, sharing `_extract_output_path`'s `_VALUE_TAKING_OPTS` pre-scan. Reusing the spelling as a boolean on `task` broke `review task CODE --check -o FILE` (the pre-scan swallowed `-o` as `--check`'s value). Fixed by carving `task` out of the value-taking set for that pre-scan only — every other subcommand's `--check NAME` is untouched. Regression tests cover both shapes.
- No backward-compat alias (nothing consumes `--quorum-check` yet, per the ticket). Registered it in `REMOVED_FLAGS` instead, matching the repo's existing `--mcp`/`--ln` convention, so a stale caller gets a structured what/why/how-to-fix pointer to `--check` instead of argparse's opaque "unrecognized arguments".

## Known pre-existing limitation (not introduced here, out of scope)
`_reject_removed_flags` scans the whole argv, so a literal `--prompt`/positional value that equals `"--quorum-check"` also gets misdiagnosed as the removed flag — verified `--mcp` already has the identical limitation today (`review diff --task ABC-1 --prompt --mcp` also exits 2). Fixing this would mean redesigning the shared removed-flags mechanism for every entry (`--mcp`, `--ln`, `--brainstorm`, etc.), not just this one — flagging for a future ticket rather than expanding this rename's scope.

Fixes #134

title: fix(task): quorum gate counts only PASSED review iterations, not just ran
body:
## Summary

- `review task CODE --check` (self-merge-authority gate, #133/#135) counted review rounds that *ran*, not rounds that *passed* — `ok_count`/`fail_count` in `record_run()` are per-backend-call technical success, not the review's verdict. Gameable: 3 shallow/failing reviews could satisfy `--min-iter 3` the same as 3 genuine passes (CTO decision tg#7306 #1).
- `record_run()` now takes an optional `passed: bool | None` kwarg (omitted = verdict unknown, matching every pre-v3 record). `STATS_VERSION` bumps to 3.
- The verdict signal is each mode's own existing exit code (`review`/`quorum`/`just-ask`/`brainstorm` already return 0 iff their own success criterion held). `qa` is deliberately excluded — it is report-only (a FAIL verdict still exits 0 unless `--strict`), so its exit code is not a verdict.
- `quorum_check()` now counts only `passed_iterations` toward `--min-iter`, and `--min-models` is the distinct-model count among those same passed iterations. Legacy/verdictless records fail closed. `--min-iter`/`--min-models` below 1 are rejected (both in the CLI and in `quorum_check()` itself, so a direct library caller can't bypass the floor).
- `--check --json` now reports `passed_iterations`/`total_iterations`/`distinct_models_passed`; human output says "N passed iterations".

## Known limitation (documented inline + on #137)

`review` (diff review) mode's exit code means "every reviewer call completed technically", not "every reviewer approved with no findings" — there's no structured accept/reject grammar to parse for that mode (unlike `qa`'s PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED). This fix closes the literal gaming vector the CTO decision named (failed/degraded runs no longer count toward the bar); building a real content verdict for `review` mode is a separate, larger effort tracked in #137.

Fixes #136

## Test plan

- [x] `python tests/test_run_stats.py` — 61/61 pass, including new coverage: verdict recorded pass/fail, `--check` counts only passed iterations, legacy/verdictless records fail closed (both pre-v3 and current-but-verdictless e.g. `qa`), `--min-models` enforced among passed-only runs, zero/negative threshold rejection (CLI + library level)
- [x] `python tests/smoke.py` — 23/23 checks pass (full suite)
- [x] `ruff check .` — clean
- [x] `review diff --staged` (this repo's own dogfood gate) — iterated to clean across several rounds; two real findings fixed along the way (qa's report-only exit code was initially mis-threaded as a verdict; `--min-iter`/`--min-models` floor validation added to `quorum_check()` itself, not just the CLI)

Not self-merged deliberately — this PR changes the self-merge-authority gate itself.

title: fix(review): default gemini seat to current GA gemini-3.5-flash (#139)
body:
## Summary

Closes the config half of #139. The review pool's `gemini` seat defaulted to `gemini-2.5-flash`, which 404'd on live ship-gate runs (2026-07-09) and is retired-soon (Google shutdown **2026-10-16**). Google names [`gemini-3.5-flash`](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations) as its GA replacement (no shutdown date). This moves the default there for **both** call paths that carried the stale fallback:

- `reviewlib/backends.py` — `review_gemini` (text reviewer seat)
- `reviewlib/features/visual/vision_client.py` — the vision fallback

An explicit `$GEMINI_MODEL` env var or a `gemini:<model>` seat suffix still overrides the default (verified by test).

## Why this matters for the quorum bar

A stale/404 gemini seat could silently count toward the self-merge review-quorum's distinct-model bar (a dead seat that never actually reviewed). This PR removes the 404 at its source (correct model id). The **complementary count-side half** — a failed/404/degraded seat must not count as a *substantive* reviewer — is handled by **#138** (verdict recording: `record_run(passed=...)` + `quorum_check` counting only passed iterations). Deliberately not re-implemented here to avoid conflicting with #138; the two halves are orthogonal and land independently, exactly as #139 describes.

- **Kimi / commandcode out-of-credits** → the payment preflight + unpaid-provider skip landed in #140/#128 (`unpaid_provider_result`, `_PAYMENT_PREFLIGHT_MARKERS` catches `insufficient credits`). Confirmed live during this PR's own `review diff`: every commandcode seat returned `exit 400 insufficient credits` and was surfaced as a non-counting failure, not a silent pass.
- **z.ai GLM-5.2 timeout** → already deprioritized to the last-resort reserve (priority 9 in `DEFAULT_BOARD`, documented as pathologically slow); it never blocks a verdict. Reproduced live here: `GLM [quality] [exit 124] TIMEOUT after 1200s`, board degraded to "3 of 4 seats produced a usable verdict".

title: feat(review): run-scoped --effort flag over the per-seat effort path
body:
## What

Adds a run-scoped `--effort` CLI flag to review-cli, built **on top of** main's existing per-seat `effort` parameter path (config `board:` → `panel.py` → `call_backend` → backends). It overrides each seat's config effort for a single run — feeding the **same** parameter, never a second application.

**Supersedes #127** (the env-transport approach, which double-applied). #127 should be closed as superseded.

## Flag design

- `--effort <level>` — a bare level (`minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`) applies to every seat.
- `--effort <provider>=<level>` — e.g. `codex=high`, `opencode=max` — overrides one backend route; per-provider wins over the global level. Repeat or comma-separate.
- Provider tokens are validated + normalised to backend-route names (`oc=`/`opencode=` both hit the opencode route; a typo like `claud=` fails loudly instead of silently landing on the opencode catch-all).

## Resolution seam

`config.EffortOverride.resolve(model, seat_effort) = effort_for(provider) or seat_effort` — the run-scoped flag wins, the per-seat config value is the fallback. Applied **once**:
- diff/board path: `apply_effort_override` rewrites the board CLI-side (`cli.py`, in `validate_board`) so the failover board carries the effective effort — no double application.
- flat `-m` diff path + flat-panel modes (quorum/just-ask/brainstorm): threaded via `ModeContext.effort_override`.

## Coverage added beyond main

- **opencode** — `--variant` (both text `review_opencode` and the vision client).
- **vision client** — codex `-c model_reasoning_effort`, claude `--effort`, opencode `--variant`, via one shared `effort_for_model` helper.

## Tests

- `tests/test_effort_run_flag.py` — parse/override/per-provider/fallback, board + flat-`-m` threading, immutability, provider validation, and a backend-signature contract guard.
- `tests/test_vision_client.py` — effort reaches codex/claude/opencode vision; no double `--effort`/`--variant` in any argv.
- Full suite: **1623 passed, 6 skipped**; ruff clean; smoke green (one pre-existing, environment-only dashboard failure unrelated to this change).

Reviewed pre-commit via `review diff --staged` (findings addressed: strict provider validation, immutability, DRY vision helper, keyword args, forward-ref typing).
