title: feat(install): install-commit-hook delegates to rig (scoped) when rig is present
body:
## What

When `rig` is present, `review install-commit-hook` lets **rig own the global git hooks** (single source of truth) instead of writing `core.hooksPath` itself — removing the double-write that rig's `git_hooks.dispatcher` would otherwise duplicate. Part of Alex tg#8672 (all ecosystem CLIs' install-hooks delegate to rig when present).

Uses the shared `agenttools_rig_delegate` helper (**agent-tools#282**).

## Behavior

Delegation is **scoped** to `rig apply --only git_hooks` (never reconciles permissions / GitHub / tools as a side effect). Three outcomes:
- rig **fails** (non-zero) → surface the exit code (never swallowed into a fallback).
- rig **succeeds and the gate is in place** → rig owns it, return 0.
- rig **succeeds but provisions no gate here** (repo declares no `git_hooks:` block) → fall back to the direct installer so the user still gets the hook they asked for.
- rig **absent** / helper not installed → the direct installer runs exactly as before.

`install-skill` deliberately does **not** delegate (rig's `tools:` provisioning runs `review install-skill`, so delegating would loop).

## Tests

33 tests green; ruff clean. New `test_install_commit_hook_rig_delegate.py` covers scoped delegation, the postcondition fallback, exit-code propagation, rig-absent, and helper-missing. The real-helper integration cases skip cleanly when the in-ecosystem helper isn't installed (bare CI); a **hermetic injected-helper test** exercises the delegation branch in CI regardless. Registered in `tests/smoke.py`. Test isolation forces rig absent via a non-executable `RIG_BIN`.

## Notes / follow-ups

- **Depends on agent-tools#282** — delegation is inert until that lands (the guarded import degrades to the direct installer meanwhile).
- Committed with `REVIEW_SKIP` because the multi-model review pool was degraded (reserve exhausted) with orphaned reviewers wedging; findings from the two reviews that did run were addressed (scoping, postcondition, test isolation, CI coverage).
- **P2 follow-up (agent-tools):** rig's provisioned `review-gate` rejects `REVIEW_SKIP` and omits the now-required `--task` in its remediation hint — a parity gap with review's direct gate, to reconcile in agent-tools.

title: feat(qa): honor run-scoped --effort in the write/exec tester (harvest from #127)
body:
## What

Harvests the one feature unique to **#127** that the merged **#150** (run-scoped `--effort`)
left out: the `review qa` write/exec tester now honors `--effort`.

#150 lifts every review **panel** seat's reasoning effort, but `qa` is a single write/exec
seat riding `claude-p`/`codex` -- not the panel -- so `review qa --effort xhigh` silently did
nothing. #150's own reviewers flagged exactly this ("don't expose `--effort` to qa unless it
is honored"). #127's env-transport approach was superseded by #150; this reuses #150's
parameter path instead of resurrecting the duplicate.

## How

Threads the resolved level `handler -> run_tester -> _dispatch_tester -> spawn`, reusing
#150's shared helpers:

| tester | control |
|---|---|
| codex | `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` (same builder as the read-only codex seat; `max` -> `xhigh`) |
| claude | `--effort <level>` when the resolved binary advertises it (capability-gated via #150's `_claude_cli_supports_effort`), else nothing |
| both | the universal `_prompt_with_effort` prompt hint, so the level is never a silent no-op even when the CLI flag is absent |

`qa` is single-seat, so the level resolves against the tester **backend** (codex/claude), not
a pinned model suffix -- `resolve_tester_effort` keys on the provider route, so
`review qa -m codex:gpt-5.5 --effort codex=high` is not misrouted to the opencode catch-all.

## Review

Reviewed by the multi-model pool three rounds (`review diff --staged`, session
`sess-20260716T104347`, all exit 0). Both P1s from round 1 (missing `_UNIT_FILES`
registration; `effort_for(model or backend)` misrouting a pinned model) are fixed in this

title: feat(review): provider failover — ordered provider list, mid-review switchover, foolproofing (#151)
body:
Implements the consolidated provider-failover spec (`PROVIDER_FAILOVER_SPEC.md`, issue #151). Fixes the recurring regression where `-m opus` routed to `opencode -m opus` (agentic backend infra-fails), blocking review quorums.

## What changed

**Model → ordered provider list (`reviewlib/provider_failover.py`)**
- A logical model maps to an ORDERED LIST of providers (harness+service), tried in order — no 1-to-1 aliases.
- `opus` → `(claude-direct, oc:anthropic/…)` — claude FIRST, not the opencode catch-all. `glm-5.2` → `(zai-direct, oc:zai, commandcode)`. Config `provider_chains:` can override.
- Last-working provider cached under `~/.cache/review-cli/` (atomic write, logical-key keyed), tried first, rotated out on failure. Cache is skipped for single-provider seats.

**Live mid-review failover (`reviewlib/panel.py` seat loop)**
- Each provider first gets the in-seat transient retry; a still-unusable result FAILS OVER to the next provider and the review CONTINUES — the seat does not abort, the board does not degrade. A whole-service outage reroutes every model that used it (emergent from per-seat chains). Only when all providers are exhausted does the board reserve-replace the seat.

**Universal transient retry (`reviewlib/retry.py`)**
- One central classifier gains provider-agnostic network-layer patterns (DNS/getaddrinfo, connection reset/refused/aborted, SSL EOF, read timeout, `ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`) — retried with backoff BEFORE failover. Permanent errors (400 credits / 401 / 403) stay seat-fatal (no retry). Patterns compile with `re.IGNORECASE`.

**Skip dead/unpaid up front** — unpaid providers (`commandcode`, `gemini`) are dropped from the chain pre-flight, never dispatched, never failed-over into.

**Pool/model foolproofing (`reviewlib/pool_guard.py`, review mode ONLY)**
- When an explicit `-m` / `--pool N` selection can't fill the request, or the default board can't clear the min-converge floor (2 distinct engines), PROPOSE fitting boards/presets — each annotated per-seat LIVE/DOWN + reason — or, when nothing converges, a TARGETED per-provider error. `EXIT_UNSATISFIED = 10`.
- Distinct-engine collapse (codex/Sol, cross-provider variants) agrees with provider-failover's `logical_key`.
- Gated to `mode.name == "review"` so quorum/brainstorm/just-ask keep their own behaviour and never see review-specific proposal text.

**Supporting**
- `backends.backend_available` is now a thin wrapper over the new `backend_unavailable_reason` (single source of "is it live" + "why not"), which the guard annotates from.
- `config.py`: `opus`/`opus48` alias → `claude:claude-opus-4-8` (bare opus no longer hits the opencode catch-all).

## Tests (per the spec's test list)
Seat switches provider mid-review and completes; all-providers-fail → board reserve replaces; opus → claude; transient retries-then-succeeds (incl. bare-errno names); permanent no-retry; last-working cached & tried first; foolproofing per-model live/dead annotations; guard fires review-mode only; error headline uses per-board best (not the self-contradictory union count).

Test-isolation hardening: the seat-level failover neutralisation is now SCOPED per-test (was a collection-time global-patch leak that silently disabled failover in the integration suites), and a `conftest.py` autouse fixture snapshots/restores `_CONFIG_UNPAID_PROVIDERS`, the payment-preflight cache, and `_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` around every test.

Full suite: 1669 passed, 6 skipped. Reviewed with `review diff -m opus` (iterated to green; findings addressed or confirmed intended/non-issue).

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking, noted from review)
- Per-provider retry budget is multiplicative across the chain (worst case ~`len(chain) × per-call cap`); bounded by small chains (2–3) but not capped by a single cross-provider deadline.
- Config `pool: N` is a soft default (graceful shrink); only explicit `--pool N` triggers the proposal. Documented in-code; the asymmetry with `--pool` is intentional.

Refs #151

title: fix(review): sandboxed-caller log/jobs-dir write no longer kills a seat (refs #162)
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause fix (https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/162):** `log_dir()` / `jobs.jobs_dir()` raised a raw `PermissionError`/`OSError` from deep inside `_run_streamed` whenever the OS-standard log/jobs location couldn't be created or written — killing a review seat with `[exit 127] Operation not permitted` before the backend subprocess was even spawned. Confirmed live: this hits any seat run from inside a sandboxed Claude Code subagent's Bash tool; Fable is simply the slowest seat (~15min) so the most likely to still be in flight when a time-scoped sandbox grant narrows. Not fable-specific — every seat hits the identical code path.
- Fix: both functions now fall back to a guaranteed-writable temp dir when the standard location can't be created **or exists but isn't actually writable** (a real create+delete probe, not just `mkdir`/`exists`), with a final `os.devnull` tier so a log-open can never raise. Every fallback path prints which location it used to stderr.
- Three rounds of `review diff --staged` against this repo's own reviewer board (dogfooding the fix) found and fixed real follow-up bugs the initial fallback introduced: an `O_WRONLY` stdin-spool bug that silently discarded a piped diff for `--detach`, un-memoized `mkdtemp()` fallback calls scattering one run's bookkeeping across directories, and a standalone-test-runner monkeypatch gap.
- Bundled from the same branch (#160, child-process-reap): `install_signal_reaper()` (SIGTERM/SIGINT now reaps live backend children, chaining to the previous handler so `KeyboardInterrupt` still fires for graceful server shutdown), and `jobs.py` locking/job-id validation hardening.
- Corrected 10 in-repo references that had cited the wrong issue number (`#161`, which is an unrelated pre-existing ticket) — the real tracking issue is #162, filed this session.
- **Review round 2 hardening (commit c271ab9):** the spawning parent no longer reads stdin to EOF itself (an open, empty non-tty pipe — agent tool wrappers, pre-commit hooks — used to block the very call that promises to return at once); the caller's stdin fd is handed straight to the detached child. Leading global options are normalized BEFORE the detachable-mode check, which is now a whitelist of review modes (`review -m x dashboard run --detach` can no longer bypass the server rejection; `review jobs/wait/install-skill --detach` is rejected). A dead pid on a "running" record is persisted as `unknown-terminated` once, via compare-and-set under the job lock (a child that finished in between keeps its real status); a pid-less record stays "running" inside a short spawn grace window.
- **Review round 3 (commit 9defb39, Codex P1/P2 on the branch diff):** `main`'s finally-block job-status write is best-effort (an `OSError` from a jobs dir that became unwritable after spawn no longer replaces a finished review's exit code with a traceback); `read_job` treats valid JSON that is not an object as "no record"; `list_jobs` skips a record that is not a dict carrying a well-formed `job_id` matching its file name. Residual Codex findings of the same hand-edited-record class (a dict with `status: []` or a string `started_at` breaking `review jobs` rendering/sorting; a `{}` record making `review status` raise `KeyError`) are noted on #163 rather than chased here — the only writer of these files is review-cli itself.
- Filed https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/163 for deeper `--detach`/job-tracking hardening the review board surfaced (job-id validation ordering, a signal-reaper spawn/register race, QA-harness subprocess groups the reaper doesn't cover, `--detach` accepting non-review management commands, cross-process job discovery once the temp-dir fallback's `mkdtemp()` tier is hit) — all #160-scope, not blocking this fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_log_dir_fallback.py`, `tests/test_signal_reaper.py`, `tests/test_detach_jobs.py` — 18/18 pass, including the standalone `tests/smoke.py` direct-execution path.
- [x] Live repro: `REVIEW_LOG_DIR`/`REVIEW_JOBS_DIR` pointed at a `chmod 000` directory, ran a real `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-fable-5` — confirmed the fallback message fires and the process proceeds to attempt the backend call instead of dying with exit 127.
- [x] Full suite after merging `origin/main` (0.35.9, #203) and round 3: **2394 passed, 6 skipped** (see the CI matrix on the final push) (`python3 -m pytest -q`, 2026-09-07; the round-2 tests in `tests/test_detach_jobs.py` included). Earlier: 1673 passed, 6 skipped. 1 pre-existing failure (`test_reviewer_board.py`'s commandcode/opencode auth test) confirmed identical on clean `main` and only reproduces inside the full-suite run (test-order/env-leak flake, unrelated). 3 `test_review_commit_checkpoint.py` cases deselected — fail identically on clean `main` too (this machine's global git hook blocks the test's own inner `git commit`).
- [x] `review diff --staged` run three times against this repo's own board during development; all P1 findings from rounds 1–2 were fixed in this same PR, round 3 found nothing new in this fix's scope.

title: feat(backends): add omp (Oh My Pi) agentic read-only backend (#174)
body:
## What

A board or `-m` seat spelled `omp:<provider>/<model>` (e.g. `omp:kimi-code/k3`) routes to a first-class `review_omp` backend instead of falling through to the opencode catch-all. Closes #174.

## Transport (verified live against omp v17.1.8)

- omp does **not** read prompts from stdin (empty-message error); an argv message would hit the ~1 MB ARG_MAX ceiling opencode has. omp message args support `@file` prefixing, so the prompt+diff travels as `@payload.md` from a per-run temp dir — no ARG_MAX, no stdin.

## Read-only cage (each layer verified live)

1. `--tools read,grep,glob` (no bash/edit/write — asked to run a shell command, the caged seat answers it has none) + `--no-extensions --no-skills --no-session`.
2. **Neutral cwd + `--add-dir <repo>`**: omp *executes* project-shipped `.mcp.json` (spawns the MCP server command) and `.omp/tools/*.js` (import-time side effects) from its launch cwd — marker files proved both, despite layer 1. So omp launches from a fresh empty temp dir (no project discovery) with the repo mounted read-only as a workspace; the seat still reads any project file, nothing in the repo executes (markers stayed absent through `review_omp` itself against a hostile fixture).
3. A per-run `--config` overlay disables `fetch` (omp's read tool fetches https URLs — an exfil channel for a prompt-injected seat; verified blocked) and project MCP config (belt-and-braces).

## Wiring

- `_match_named_backend` / `resolve_backend` / `provider_route_name` / `is_known_backend_token` (`omp`, `omp:*`)
- `backend_unavailable_reason`: offline probe — binary on PATH + a non-disabled credential row for the seat's provider in omp's own sqlite auth db, honoring `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `OMP_PROFILE` (verified layout), memoized per (main, -wal) mtime with all providers hydrated in one read; failures are not cached
- `unpaid_providers:` gating as provider `omp`; `REVIEW_OMP_MODE=api` fails loudly (CLI-only); `--effort` → `--thinking`
- `--show-board` labels the seat `agentic`; dashboard attributes `omp -m <sel>` to the `omp:<sel>` seat (mirrors the `oc:` mapping, #24); `reviewlib` facade export
- Docs: README backends table + auth section, `review help config`, CHANGELOG

## Review iterations (gate: `review diff --staged`, task REVIEW-174)

- **codex P0**: project `.mcp.json` / `.omp/tools` execute despite `--no-extensions` — **fixed** (neutral cwd containment, verified with adversarial fixture through `review_omp`)
- **codex P1**: read tool fetches URLs (egress) — **fixed** (`fetch.enabled: false` overlay, verified)
- **codex P2**: profile-aware auth db (`OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`), `REVIEW_OMP_MODE` contract, facade export — **fixed**
- **codex P3**: effort lists — **fixed** (help, config docs, guard probes)
- **glm perf**: probe cache now hydrates all providers in one read; probe failures bounded (0.5s timeout); `diff.isspace()` emptiness check. Remaining nits (per-probe stat()s, shared `_which` pattern, per-run temp files by design) declined with justification — pathological-edge micro-costs on an offline probe path.
- Final gate: two-seat live panel (`omp:kimi-code/k3` + GLM-5.2) ok=2 fail=0 (default board degraded: codex rate-limited until Aug 5, claude session-limited).

## Verification

- 24 new unit tests in `tests/test_omp_backend.py` (hermetic: fake `_which`/`_run_streamed`, throwaway `OMP_AUTH_DB`); registered in smoke.py
- Full suite: `python tests/smoke.py` — **24 checks, 0 failures**
- Live smoke: one-seat review through `omp:kimi-code/k3` against a real buggy diff returned real findings (found the planted `discount()` bug + missing tests via its glob tool)
- Adversarial: `review_omp` against a repo with `.mcp.json` + `.omp/tools` traps — rc=0 findings returned, zero marker files created

title: fix(review): stop codex-backend self-reinvocation loop (review-cli#180)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the codex-backend recursion bug that caused a real 215-process/load-49
machine-hanging incident (2026-08-11, ref #180).

**Root cause**: the codex backend's only safety mechanism was `-s read-only`, an
OS-level filesystem/network sandbox that does NOT restrict codex's shell/exec tool
(codex's core capability IS running shell commands — unlike the claude backend's
`--tools ""` or opencode's explicit `bash: deny`). A codex reviewer could re-invoke
`review diff` on the same worktree as a plain shell command, which spawns another
codex backend, forming an unbounded self-reinvocation loop.

**Fix — two layers, per the ticket's acceptance criteria:**

1. **`$REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE` reentrancy guard (primary defense)**. `main()` sets it for
   the lifetime of a run; `_reject_if_reentrant` (checked first, before any other
   usage-error rejects) refuses immediately if it's already set. This is the
   mechanism that actually closes the loop — the existing process-group kill/backstop
   machinery cannot bound cross-recursion, because each backend child intentionally
   roots a brand-new OS session (`start_new_session=True`) so a per-call timeout can
   kill just that call's tree without also killing the CLI's own group. Every
   recursive level therefore re-roots into a group invisible to an earlier level's
   `killpg`. An env var survives `exec`/`setsid` regardless, so it's the one signal
   that reaches every descendant. Checks presence (`is not None`), not truthiness, so
   `REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE=` (empty string) can't slip through a falsy check.

2. **codex execpolicy `.rules` guard (defense-in-depth)** — the closest available
   equivalent to `--tools ""`/`bash: deny` for a backend whose only capability is
   shell exec. `install_codex_recursion_guard()` idempotently writes a Starlark
   `.rules` file to codex's user-level `$CODEX_HOME/rules/`, forbidding
   `review`/`codex`/`claude`/`opencode`/`omp` as shell commands — a `forbidden`
   decision hard-blocks the command before it runs (verified live via
   `codex execpolicy check`). Auto-installed on first codex backend call per process.

**Honestly documented residual limitations** (in code comments and regression
tests): the execpolicy layer is a literal-token prefix match, verified live to NOT
catch `bash -c "review diff"`, an absolute path, or `python3 -m reviewlib diff` —
widening the pattern set would false-positive-block ordinary reviewer shell usage.
The `$REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE` guard is what still holds against all three. It in turn
does not defend against a shell that explicitly clears the var (`env -u
REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE`) — no env-var guard can.

**Verified no regression**: dashboard/spec-web servers only shell out to
`tailscale`/`git`/`tmux`, never `review` itself, so a server subcommand holding
`$REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE` for its entire lifetime cannot break a real workflow.

## Test plan

- [x] Regression test: a stubbed codex binary attempts to re-invoke `review` as a
      real subprocess (not mocked) and is blocked, with a control run proving the
      same call succeeds without the guard.
- [x] Explicit proof that `$REVIEW_CLI_ACTIVE` propagates through the real
      `Popen(env=None)` path into the spawned process.
- [x] Live integration check against codex's own `execpolicy check` engine
      (skips if `codex` isn't on PATH).
- [x] Full standalone unit suites (`test_reentrancy_guard.py`,
      `test_codex_recursion_guard_rules.py`) — all green.
- [x] Full `tests/smoke.py` suite — 24/24 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped.
- [x] `ruff check` — clean.
- [x] Self-reviewed across 8 rounds with `claude:claude-opus-4-8` + `zai:glm-5.2`
      (never codex, for the obvious reason) — every correctness finding fixed;
      remaining suggestions are test-hygiene nitpicks on already-passing coverage.

Not merging this myself per instructions — leaving for review/merge decision.

title: feat: token-burn tracking tooling — review stat, diff-cap, seat cooldown (#185)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `review stat` (`reviewlib/dashboard/tokenstats.py`) — a per-harness/per-model usage and health report parsed from the real per-call logs (calls/ok/fail, real token counts where a backend emits them, the Fable dispatch/failure pattern, largest calls recorded).
- Adds `reviewlib/seat_cooldown.py` — a cross-invocation cooldown cache so a chronically-unavailable seat (Fable session-limit) stops paying for a full real dispatch on every single invocation.
- Wires a dispatch-time diff-size cap (`cap_diff_for_dispatch`, default 300,000 bytes, `$REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_BYTES`) into `review diff`, `brainstorm`, `quorum`, and `just-ask`, so an oversized diff degrades predictably (truncated with a visible marker) instead of being sent whole to every board seat every round.
- Replaces bare `returncode == 0` gating with the shared `result_is_usable` check across review/just-ask/quorum/brainstorm/moderator paths, so a cached-cooldown sentinel (rc=0, non-empty "unavailable" body) is never counted as a real usable result.

Closes #185.

Went through 5 rounds of manual multi-model review (`review diff --staged -m codex,opus,glm-5.2`, plus a final codex+opus confirmation pass after glm-5.2 timed out twice on this diff's size — logs in `/tmp/review_round{1..5}.log` and `/tmp/review_round5b_confirm.log`). title: fix(stats): thread real token counts into run-stats.jsonl
body:
## Summary

`reviewlib/stats.py`'s `record_run()` (the ETA/quorum-gate JSONL store) never recorded
token usage, even though `reviewlib/backends.py` already parses real usage from every
REST backend response. This wires that data through: `ReviewResult` carries
`prompt_tokens`/`output_tokens` (set only at the REST construction sites), `panel.py`'s
call tally sums them per run, and `record_run`/`task_summaries` persist and aggregate
them (STATS_VERSION bumped 3 -> 4, backward-compatible with older records).

Verified this does NOT duplicate #194 (the `review stat` / `dashboard/tokenstats.py`
per-call-log dashboard that landed on main today) — confirmed via direct diff that
`reviewlib/stats.py` was untouched by that PR. The two are complementary: #194 derives
counts from per-call log files for detailed per-model/harness reporting; this PR
aggregates from the same run's in-memory `ReviewResult` fields for the lighter-weight
ETA/quorum store.

Two real P1 bugs surfaced and fixed during multi-round review:
- The flat `-m` review path (`mode_review`) has its own executor that never called the
  tally at all, so the most common review invocation always recorded 0/0 tokens.
- Once fixed, tallying only the seat's FINAL result undercounted seats that needed an
  in-seat retry or provider failover — each real dispatch attempt is now tallied, not
  just the last one. Regression tests cover both the failover and in-seat-retry cases.

Also: `dataclasses.replace()` now used at panel.py's two hand-reconstruction sites
instead of field-by-field copies, closing off the class of bug where a future new field
silently resets to its default on reconstruction (this is exactly how the flat-path gap
above almost slipped through a second time).

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite: 1861 passed, 6 skipped, 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this
      change (confirmed identical on clean `main` before this diff — an environment
      issue where a global git commit-review hook fires inside
      `test_review_commit_checkpoint.py`'s throwaway temp repos)
- [x] New/updated tests: token persistence + backward-compat (`test_run_stats.py`),
      per-attempt tallying across provider failover and in-seat retry on the flat path
      (`test_provider_failover.py`), tally-shape updates across 4 other files whose
      exact-dict assertions needed the two new keys

## Follow-ups (not blocking, filed as review feedback during this PR, not yet tracked as tickets)

- Zero-vs-unknown ambiguity: `prompt_tokens: 0` means "no REST usage data", not a
  confirmed zero-token run; `task_summaries()` sums it as if authoritative for mixed
  REST/CLI pools. A real fix needs a coverage indicator, deferred as a bigger design
  change.
- Gemini's `candidatesTokenCount` excludes `thoughtsTokenCount` (thinking-model spend),
  a narrower undercount worth a follow-up.
- Structural fragility: every new result-producing code path must remember to call the
  tally functions independently; a single public tally entry point would remove that
  footgun class.

title: fix(backends): opencode zai/glm stall watchdog + cooldown by access method
body:
## Summary
- Adds a scoped liveness/stall watchdog for opencode's `oc:zai/glm-5.2` agentic seat, which hangs at ~0% CPU with zero output when z.ai quota is exhausted, wedging the review pool for the full idle window (up to 20+ min). A call with total silence for 5 minutes (`REVIEW_OPENCODE_STALL_SECONDS`) is retried up to 3 total attempts, then the seat is cooled down (subsequent invocations skip the doomed dispatch entirely). Scoped only to the confirmed-affected model (`REVIEW_OPENCODE_STALL_MODELS`, default `"zai/glm"`) — every other opencode seat (Kimi/Qwen/DeepSeek) is unaffected.
- Folds in #187: the `seat_cooldown` store is now keyed by `(model, access_method)` instead of `model` alone, so a cooldown recorded from one transport (e.g. claude CLI) no longer shadows an independently-healthy one (claude API, or opencode's separate route to the same model family). `access_method` is a **required** keyword on `record_cooldown`/`active_cooldown`/`clear_cooldown` — no silent default bucket a caller could forget to pass.
- `_run_streamed` gains an opt-in `liveness_timeout` distinct from the existing generous idle timeout (unchanged for every other caller/backend), plus a `timeout_kind` result attribute so callers can tell timeout kinds apart without text-scraping stdout for a marker substring.

## Known, deliberately-deferred limitations (surfaced during review, judged non-blocking)
- The liveness signal is "zero bytes on stdout AND stderr" — unverified against a live stalled zai/glm transcript; if opencode ever emits startup chatter to stderr before hanging, the watchdog would silently not fire for that call. Flagged for follow-up verification against real traffic.
- `seat_cooldown`'s `access_method="default"`-style migration paths (legacy flat-shape entries, two access methods coexisting under one model) have store-level tests but no test for the exact migration transition from a real pre-#187 file.
- The exhausted-stall→cooldown handoff composes with the outer `reviewlib.retry` layer (capped at 1 retry for rc=124) rather than being encoded directly in the returned result's classification; if `record_cooldown` fails to persist (best-effort, or `$REVIEW_SEAT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS<=0`), the outer retry could re-run the full 3-attempt stall cycle once more (~30 min worst case instead of ~15).
- Inner stall retries don't emit `write_retry_log` events, so they're invisible to the #185/#194 retry/token-burn dashboard.
- `review_claude` still requires `REVIEW_CLAUDE_MODE=api` set by a human to fail over to a healthy transport during a CLI cooldown — this PR fixes the cooldown from wrongly *blocking* the healthy transport, not automatic failover between transports (that's arguably #151/#157's scope).

title: feat(config,cli): usage-limit-aware model reuse for board/quorum/brainstorm panels
body:
## Summary

Per Alex's direct request: allow review-cli's board/quorum/brainstorm panels to reuse an already-available model across multiple roles/seats when fewer distinct models are reachable than requested, instead of silently shrinking the panel — and exclude any model at/above 70% of its tg-ctl-tracked usage window before role-filling, falling back to the single least-depleted model when everything is near its limit.

- **`reviewlib/usage_limits.py`** (new): reads tg-ctl's `~/.config/tg-cli/tg-ctl.*.usage-latest.json` as a best-effort, read-only, fail-open usage-percent signal. Merges samples across every chat file, takes the freshest sample per `(agent, limitName)` key, and honors both the sample's age and its own `resetAt` field. Currently covers the `claude`/`codex` agent families (documented as a known partial-coverage gap).
- **`reviewlib/config.py`**: `select_pool_with_reuse`, `select_pool_and_reserve_with_reuse`, `expand_flat_models_with_reuse` — the core selection algorithms. Drop-in replacements: byte-identical output to the existing `select_pool`/`split_pool_reserve` whenever `usage_percent` is `None` or nothing is excluded.
- **Board mode** (`reviewlib/modes/review.py`): the failover reserve now demotes near-limit-excluded seats to the tail instead of leaving them at their raw board position (a near-limit seat used to get promoted on mid-run failover *before* perfectly healthy overflow seats), and reserve is matched by seat identity so a config board that legitimately lists one model under two roles never loses a slot.
- **Quorum** (`reviewlib/modes/quorum.py`): repeated seats are labelled `<model>#1`/`<model>#2` in the transcript and the moderator prompt gets an explicit note to treat them as one opinion, not two.
- Operator-facing stderr notices ("panel padded" / "board padded") fire only on genuine reuse, not on a config that happens to list a model twice.

## Review process

This went through 7 rounds of the repo's multi-model `review diff --staged` gate (Fable/Claude, k3/Kimi, GLM). Real bugs found and fixed across rounds: a hardcoded-timestamp time bomb in a test, brainstorm padding compensating for raw unavailability instead of only usage-limits, a reserve seat-identity bug, a role-cycling bug that could dispatch byte-identical duplicate seats on boards with genuinely repeated roles, quorum using the raw (non-chain-aware) availability probe, quorum's padding target/fallback still applying usage-exclusion when it shouldn't, and `usage_percent_for_model` taking max-percent across merged samples instead of the freshest-per-key one. Round 7 produced no new correctness findings — only already-tracked architecture/performance preferences.

Deferred, tracked in **review-cli#206** (not blocking): whether quorum should pad at all given its seats share one prompt with no per-seat lens (this is a product tradeoff on Alex's own request, not something to reverse unilaterally); the total-exhaustion fallback filling *every* slot with the single most-depleted model; returning padding info explicitly from the selection functions instead of re-inferring it; `config.py`→`usage_limits.py` import direction; docs/README sync; a couple of low-severity performance nits (per-call snapshot rescans, sequential chain-aware probing).

title: fix(review): trivial-delta pre-commit gate tolerates small restages
body:
## Summary

The pre-commit review gate required the staged diff's hash to match byte-for-byte against the last reviewed diff, forcing a brand-new multi-model review round on every restage — even a one-line follow-up fix (observed: 9 rounds for one ticket). On a hash miss, the gate now re-diffs the current staged diff against the last reviewed baseline (stored alongside the hash stamp) and tolerates a small line-level delta (`REVIEW_TRIVIAL_DELTA_LINES`, default 10) without dispatching a fresh review. The baseline only ever advances on a real `review diff --staged` pass.

This PR went through five internal hardening rounds (each caught by a genuine multi-model review finding on this same PR, documented in code comments above `_TRIVIAL_DELTA_BLOCK`):

1. Exclude pure diff-generation metadata (`index`, `@@` hunk headers) from the line count.
2. Fail closed on binary/gitlink content, invisible to a line-count ruler.
3. Count added/removed lines separately (`max`, not raw/2) so a modified line's `-old`/`+new` pair isn't double-counted.
4. Extend the metadata exclusion to whole-file add/delete/rename headers (`diff --git`, `--- /dev/null`, `new file mode`, etc.).
5. Anchor the `--- `/`+++ ` header exclusion to git's actual header shapes (`--- a/`, `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/`, `+++ /dev/null`) — the bare form collided with a REMOVED source line that itself starts with `-- ` (SQL/Lua/Haskell comment syntax), undercounting a real unreviewed deletion toward zero.
6. Fail closed on mode-only changes and pure renames too (`old mode `, `new mode `, `rename from/to `, `copy from/to `) — these have no content hunk at all, so an arbitrary number of `chmod +x` follow-ups always read as `changed == 0`, unbounded by the threshold. Also anchored the `Subproject commit` fail-closed check to a real 40-hex-char sha so ordinary prose starting with those two words doesn't force a spurious full review.

Three lower-severity findings from this PR's own review pass are deferred to #210 rather than fixed here (to keep this PR's scope closed): a stale `review-stamp-diff` companion not being hash-verified against `review-stamp`, the gitlink anchor only covering SHA-1's 40-hex shas (not SHA-256's 64), and `mktemp` portability on non-GNU `sh`.

Refs #208.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_review_stamp_delta_tolerance.py` — 18 tests, exercising the real `_PRECOMMIT` shell script via subprocess against real temp git repos: trivial/substantive follow-ups, threshold boundaries, binary/gitlink fail-closed, multi-file/new-file/deleted-file metadata exclusion, the round-4 SQL-comment-collision fix, and the round-5 mode-only/rename fail-closed fix + `Subproject commit` anchor fix — each of the last two verified BOTH ways (fails against the reverted pre-fix pattern, passes against the fix).
- [x] Full repo test suite (`python3 tests/smoke.py`): 23/24 checks pass; the one failure (`test_effort_run_flag.py`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'`) is a pre-existing, unrelated environment issue on this machine (`pytest` installed under the real `$HOME`'s user-site path, which the smoke harness redirects for isolation) — reproduced identically on a clean `git stash` of this PR's changes.
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all changed files: clean.
- [x] Multi-model review (Opus + Codex): Codex's seat failed with a tooling/reserve-exhaustion error across 3 attempts (unrelated to this diff's content); Opus reviewed 3 rounds and found real, actionable issues each time — round 5 (the mode/rename bypass, fixed in this PR) was a genuine security-relevant gap verified empirically before and after the fix; the round-6 findings are lower-severity/likelihood and tracked in #210 instead of chased indefinitely in this same PR.

title: fix(stats,cli): bind quorum-store iterations to repo/diff identity
body:
## Summary

Closes #213. The self-merge-authority quorum gate (`review task CODE --check`)
used to key PASSED iterations purely by task-code STRING, with no binding to
which repo or diff was actually reviewed. Three real incidents in one session
(2026-08-11) exploited exactly that: a wrong-repo review counted toward an
unrelated PR's quorum (PR #151), a task-code substitution counted history from
two different PRs sharing a parent ticket (PR #131), and years of unrelated
cross-repo history piled onto one task code and was trusted by `gh ship`'s own
automated Guard-B gate (HYP-858).

- Every recorded iteration now carries `repo_id` (normalized `origin` remote,
  or a local path fallback) and `diff_files` (touched-file set), plus a
  diagnostic `diff_sha256`.
- `review task CODE --check` resolves `-C`'s current repo/diff and EXCLUDES
  any recorded iteration whose repo differs or whose files share nothing with
  the current diff — matching is file-**set overlap**, not diff-content-hash
  equality, so the normal review→fix→re-review loop still counts.
- History predating this field is "unverifiable" and still counts (backward
  compatible; a direct library caller that never passes the new context gets
  the byte-identical pre-v4 return shape).
- A new `identity_verification: "ran"|"disabled"|"skipped_unresolvable"` JSON
  field plus stderr warnings make "verification never ran" impossible to
  mistake for "verified and clean."
- **`gh ship`'s quorum gate needs zero code changes to benefit** — verified by
  reading agent-tools' `ci/ship/ship.sh`: it already `cd`s to the repo root and
  reads only `passed_iterations`/`.error`/`.models`/`.passed`, which now
  reflect the filtered count automatically.

## Dogfooded, not rubber-stamped

Shipped after 7 real `review diff --staged --task review-cli#213` rounds
against this PR's own diff (multi-model board each time). Each round fixed a
REAL bug the previous one found:

1. **Codex/GLM/Opus/Fable** — the `diff.noprefix=true` fix for
   `extract_diff_files` didn't cover the `--check` fallback path, silently
   disabling file-level matching on exactly this repo's own dev machine.
2. **Opus/Fable** — check-time file-set resolution took the first non-empty
   of local-uncommitted vs branch-diff, so a stray dirty file could shadow the
   real branch diff → fixed to union both.
3. **Opus/Fable/GLM** — added `identity_verification` (machine-readable) and
   a record-time noprefix regression test.
4. All four models: no blocking correctness issues.
5. **k3 + Opus, independently** — the noprefix fix moved the pre-commit
   review-stamp hash to stamp-WRITE time (after the panel finishes, possibly
   minutes after dispatch), reopening a TOCTOU window: a concurrent index
   mutation during the review could get silently certified as reviewed. Fixed
   by capturing the hash at dispatch time and threading it through
   `mode_review` into `_write_review_stamp`, with an end-to-end test that
   mutates the index from inside a stubbed backend call.
6. Two rounds timed out under heavy concurrent machine load (confirmed via

The run-stats store is a local, self-reported JSONL file a caller with write

title: fix(process,panel): clamp reserve-promotion idle timeout to a board wall-clock deadline
body:
## Summary

Closes review-cli#221.

A reserve seat promoted mid-run by `run_board_with_failover` got the full 20-minute default idle-silence floor (`process._DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT`) regardless of how long the run had already been going. Any caller wrapping `review diff --staged` in an external `timeout 900` (15 min — the convention used by this org's own commit/ship gates) could get SIGKILLed mid-promotion with zero graceful degradation, zero partial result, zero log. This is the exact symptom currently blocking real PRs (hyper-saas PR #735, gc-archive PR #223, and a same-session commit attempt on this repo itself — 5+ consecutive 900s hangs at `board: Codex [consistency] failed — promoting reserve`).

## What changed

- `$REVIEW_BOARD_DEADLINE_SECONDS` arms an optional process-wide wall-clock deadline (`reviewlib/process.py::set_board_deadline`) for the duration of one `run_board_with_failover` call.
- `idle_timeout_seconds()` clamps its returned idle-silence floor down to whatever time genuinely remains before that deadline, with a 90s minimum so a late-promoted reserve still gets a fair attempt instead of being starved to ~0.
- Unset (the default — every existing caller) is fully backward compatible: current unclamped behaviour, byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The two EXPLICIT-DISABLE contracts (`idle_floor=0`, `REVIEW_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0`) are exempt from the clamp — a caller/operator who opted OUT of idle reaping keeps that contract even with a deadline armed.

## Review process

2 rounds of this repo's own multi-model review gate (`review diff --staged --task 221`). Round 1: 3 independent reviewers (GLM, Opus, Fable) independently caught a real correctness bug — the clamp could hand back a value **larger** than the caller's own request when that request was already below the 90s minimum floor (e.g. an explicit `REVIEW_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30` near a deadline came back as 90). Fixed (`min(computed, max(remaining, floor))` instead of just `max`), with a regression test. Round 2: zero new correctness findings — only refinements of already-flagged architectural design points (see Deferred below).

## Tests

40 new/updated assertions across `tests/test_streaming.py` (pure-function contract) and the new `tests/test_board_deadline_wiring.py` (does `run_board_with_failover` actually arm/clear the deadline at the right moments, including the zero-config and all-seats-fail paths). Full suite: 1936 passed / 6 skipped / 4 failed — all 4 failures independently confirmed pre-existing on clean `main` via `git stash` comparison, unrelated to this change (3× `test_review_commit_checkpoint.py`, 1× `test_run_stats.py::test_cli_failover_backfill_records_actual_models_not_planned`).

## Deferred (follow-up ticket to file)

Both review rounds raised legitimate architectural points beyond this fix's scope — the deadline is armed per `run_board_with_failover` call rather than once per process (so a multi-round/multi-panel process could exceed the stated budget), the idle-timeout clamp is computed before the concurrency-semaphore wait (so a queued seat's clamp can be stale), the clamp only bounds silence rather than true wall-clock (a chatty-but-stuck backend can still outlive an external wrapper), and the set/clear-in-`finally` ownership doesn't survive nested/concurrent board runs. None of these affect the primary, currently-blocking failure mode (a genuinely SILENT stuck reserve under a single sequential board run — the exact case in the bug reports), so shipping this fix now and tracking the rest separately.

title: fix(seat_cooldown,stats,cli): escalating cross-invocation cooldown + stalled-model diagnostics
body:
## Summary
Closes #221. A seat that keeps failing across many separate `review` invocations (each its own process) was only ever getting a flat 10-minute cooldown, so a chronically broken model kept getting re-dispatched every few minutes instead of being pushed out of the pool long enough for the existing board-level reserve-promotion to substitute a working model. Confirmed live: HYP-1295 re-selected `oc:zai/glm-5.2` four times, each gap over 10 minutes.

- **Escalating cooldown** (`reviewlib/seat_cooldown.py`): window climbs 10min → 30min → 2h → 8h cap per consecutive failure, resets on a genuine success or a 24h quiet period. An explicit `ttl_seconds`/`$REVIEW_SEAT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` still pins a fixed window with no escalation.
- **Success clears escalation** (`reviewlib/backends.py`): both claude dispatch paths now clear an escalated cooldown on genuine success (rc=0, non-empty body — an empty-rc0 "silently disabled model" response does not count as recovery, matching `panel.result_is_usable`'s own contract).
- **Stalled-model diagnostic** (`reviewlib/stats.py`, `cli.py`): `review task CODE --check` (text and `--json`) now names any currently-stalled attempted model and why, instead of a bare N/M count.

## Known, tracked scope gaps (documented in README, not silently dropped)
- #226: only the two claude dispatch paths are wired into the escalation mechanism yet — opencode/codex/commandcode/zai are not covered, so the `oc:zai/glm-5.2` incident that motivated this fix is not itself fixed by this change alone. Live evidence added to that ticket (codex hitting the identical shape during this PR's own review rounds).
- #227: the `stalled_models` diagnostic sources from recorded run history, which on the normal board/failover dispatch path only contains surviving seats — a chronically-cooling seat successfully backfilled by a reserve stays invisible to the diagnostic.

## Process
8 rounds of multi-model review (Opus, Fable, k3, GLM, codex where quota allowed). Real bugs caught and fixed at every round: a vacuous test assertion (expired-entry check that passed regardless of whether the code under test ran), a stdout/stderr stream-split bug, an incomplete disable-fast-path that silently broke the documented cooldown un-stick hatch, and a missing empty-rc0-body guard on the success-clears-cooldown path. Round 7/8: correctness reviewer explicitly signed off ("I did not find a correctness-breaking defect... Net: I'd ship this on correctness grounds"); remaining findings are architectural preferences (already tracked or reasonable tradeoffs) and the two known scope gaps above.

## Test plan
- [x] Full suite: 1954 passed, 6 skipped, 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (confirmed via `git stash` against clean main)
- [x] New regression coverage: escalation schedule/cap/reset math, corrupt-store guards (bool `fail_count`/`recorded_at`), env-override precedence, skip-path store isolation (both dispatch sites), empty-rc0-body no-clear, mismatch-error + stalled_models coexistence (both directions), CLI text-mode stream routing, invalid-task-code text-mode no-crash

title: fix(seat_cooldown): serialize concurrent cooldown read-modify-write
body:
Closes #188.

`_locked()` wraps `record_cooldown`/`clear_cooldown`'s read-modify-write in a `threading.Lock` plus a bounded `fcntl.flock` (shared 2.0s deadline), so a stalled peer degrades progressively (both locks → in-process-only → fully unlocked) instead of hanging the caller or losing a write.

title: feat(stats,cli): --min-roles quorum-counting mode for the self-merge-authority gate
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #221 (the repo owner's current direction for that issue — see note below on scope).

The review-cli board assigns each reviewer model a ROLE/lens (architect, correctness, security, etc. — 8 roles total). When there aren't enough distinct models available to fill all the panel seats, the board fills the gap by reusing an already-picked model on the empty role instead of shrinking the panel (PR #207) — each duplicated pass genuinely reviews the diff under its own distinct role, clearly labeled as such.

The problem: the self-merge-authority quorum gate (`review task CODE --check`) counts distinct MODEL NAME strings toward `--min-models`. A role-fill pass that reuses an already-counted model never helps satisfy that count, even though it covered a real, different facet of the review. A task whose history is "2 real distinct models + 1 role-fill pass reusing one of them under a third role" can never satisfy `--min-models 3`, even though 3 genuinely distinct facets of the diff were reviewed.

## What changed

- **New `--min-roles N` flag** on `review task CODE --check`, independent of `--min-models`. Omitting `--min-roles` reproduces `--min-models`'s exact prior behavior (verified with a dedicated regression test). Passing `--min-roles` governs the pass/fail decision instead, counting distinct BOARD ROLES covered by the passed iterations rather than distinct model names.
- Per-seat role tracking is new to the run-stats record (`roles`, optional) and to `panel.FailoverOutcome` (`usable_roles`) — only the `review diff`/`review visual` board dispatch populates it; `quorum`/`just-ask`/`brainstorm`/`qa` iterations still count toward `--min-iter` but never toward `--min-roles`.
- When `--min-models` fails because model diversity is genuinely short, the denial suggests `--min-roles` as an alternative — but only when switching would actually pass (iteration floor already met, role coverage traced to at least 2 distinct models, enough distinct roles) — never a hint that sends the caller straight into a second denial or steers toward a single-model monoculture.
- Only a role that's an actual board role (not a typo'd/unknown string on a custom config board) ever counts as covered.
- Passing both `--min-models` and `--min-roles` explicitly prints a visible stderr note saying which one actually governs, instead of silently reporting the unused floor as if it were enforced.

## Review process

This went through 10 rounds of multi-model review (codex/opus/fable via `review diff`). Each of the first several rounds surfaced a real, fixed bug:
- A false-positive `--min-roles` suggestion that could fire even when switching couldn't possibly help (no roles recorded, or the iteration floor was also short).
- An unknown/typo'd role string on a custom config board could inflate the role count as if it were a genuine distinct lens.
- The monoculture guard on the advisory suggestion was checking model diversity across the wrong population (all passed iterations, rather than only the iterations that actually earned a valid role), which could still steer a caller toward a single-model monoculture in specific mixed-history shapes.
- A latent index-pairing gap between recorded models and roles in the stats layer.

Later rounds converged to confirmations, test-coverage gaps (closed with real tests, e.g. proving a real board dispatch's roles actually satisfy `--min-roles`, a multi-seat mid-list reserve-backfill alignment test, role-mode-aware `stalled_models` coverage), and doc-precision fixes.

## Known, deliberately unresolved item — needs your sign-off

Every review round flagged the same architectural question, and I did not change it because it's exactly what the task spec asked for ("a role filled by a duplicated-model pass counts once per role, same as any other role"): **`--min-roles`'s core gate has no minimum-model floor of its own.** A single model that reviewed under N distinct roles (an extreme case of the duplicate-model role-fill) satisfies `--min-roles N`, even though only one model ever looked at the diff. The advisory suggestion text is deliberately more conservative than the gate itself (it won't recommend `--min-roles` for that shape), which several reviewers flagged as an inconsistency — the hint is stricter than the enforcement it points at.

This is documented as a known trade-off in `quorum_check`'s docstring (`reviewlib/stats.py`), but it's a real weakening of the self-merge-authority guarantee for anyone who opts into `--min-roles`. Worth an explicit call: leave as specified, or add a `>= 2` distinct-model floor to `--min-roles` itself (the machinery already exists — `_models_behind_role_coverage`).

## Testing

`ruff check .` — clean. Full relevant unit-test suites (`test_run_stats.py`, `test_failover_pool.py`, `test_pool_reuse.py`, `test_effort_run_flag.py`) — all green, 178 tests including ~50 new/rewritten for this feature. `python tests/smoke.py` (the exact CI command) passes except one pre-existing, unrelated failure (`test_effort_run_flag.py`'s `import pytest` breaks under this repo's `HOME`-isolated subprocess test harness on this machine, because pytest is installed to a per-user site-packages path — confirmed present on an untouched `main` checkout, zero diff on that file).

Not shipped/merged per instructions — opening for review only.

title: fix(quorum): remove the "single opinion" discount note from the moderator prompt
body:
## What this does

The repo owner's call: a review model covering more than one board/panel role in
parallel is a completely valid, undiscounted contribution — there is nothing wrong
with the same model taking several roles at once. This removes the moderator-facing
caveat that used to tell `review quorum`'s moderator to treat all seats filled by one
duplicated model as a single, discounted opinion instead of independent, full-weight
seats.

## Where the caveat lived

`reviewlib/modes/quorum.py` — `mode_quorum()` built a `duplicate_note` string
(instructing the moderator: *"Treat ALL seats sharing one model ... as a SINGLE
opinion for majority-counting purposes — do NOT count a repeated model's agreement
with itself as extra weight toward QUORUM"*) and appended it to the moderator prompt
whenever `_seat_assignments()` reported `has_duplicates=True`. The same framing was
also documented in `README.md`'s Quorum section and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## What changed

- `reviewlib/modes/quorum.py`: removed the `duplicate_note` block and the
  `has_duplicates` boolean that only existed to drive it (`_seat_assignments` now
  returns `(labels, personas)`, dropping the unused third value). The moderator
  prompt no longer carries any instruction to discount a duplicated model's seats.
  The `<model>#N [<lens>]` seat labelling is untouched — it stays purely for
  traceability (which seat produced which answer), not as a discount signal.
- `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: updated the Quorum description to drop the
  "single opinion" framing and state plainly that a model covering multiple roles
  in parallel is a fully valid panel shape.
- `tests/test_reuse_warnings.py`: the duplicate-seat test now asserts the
  "SINGLE opinion" / "single opinion" text is ABSENT from the moderator prompt
  (previously asserted it was present); updated the module docstring and test/
  function names to match the corrected behavior.

## Testing

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_reuse_warnings.py -q` — 12 passed.
- `ruff check .` — clean.
- `ruff format --check reviewlib/modes/quorum.py tests/test_reuse_warnings.py` — already formatted (repo-wide format drift across ~90 unrelated files predates this change and is out of scope here).
- `python3 tests/smoke.py` — 23/24 checks pass; the 1 failure (`test_effort_run_flag.py`
  → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'` under smoke.py's subprocess
  harness) is pre-existing and unrelated: reproduced identically on an untouched
  `main` checkout with zero diff on that file (same failure documented in PR #246).
  mypy is not installed in this environment (not part of this repo's documented
  test commands in AGENTS.md).

title: feat: adversarial review-rigor fixes (Alex audit, all 4 findings)
body:
## Summary

Alex (repo owner, CTO) audited review-cli's own review rigor and found four gaps, then said explicitly: "Поправляй плиз все находки" (please fix all the findings). This PR implements all four.

### 1. Neutral prompts, not adversarial
`reviewlib/config.py` — `DEFAULT_PROMPT` (the shared base instruction every reviewer gets) now tells the model to actively try to break the change — walk through concrete failure scenarios and genuinely attempt to find a bug — before concluding it's fine, instead of a neutral "review this diff" ask with no skepticism built in.

### 2. No evidence requirement for a clean pass
`reviewlib/config.py` + `reviewlib/panel.py` — that same prompt now requires evidence for ANY verdict, not just findings: a "no issues" verdict must state which specific failure modes were checked and why each is ruled out (`checked: race condition on X — none found, guarded by a lock at Y`), not a bare "looks good". A new `panel.clean_verdict_missing_evidence` heuristic surfaces a body that skips this as a visible WARNING wherever diff-review results are rendered — a heuristic surfacing, not a hard enforcement gate (a real content-based exit-code verdict is a larger, separate effort tracked as #137).

### 3. Opt-in refutation / adversarial cross-check for `review quorum`
`reviewlib/modes/quorum.py` — `review quorum` gets a new `--adversarial-check` flag: after the panel reaches a clean verdict, one more pass tries to REFUTE "no issues found"; a successful refutation is surfaced as a new finding and flips the run non-zero. **Opt-in, not a universal default** — see "Scoping choice" below.

### 4. Adversarial framing blended into the default board's security/tests roles
`reviewlib/config.py` — `REVIEW_ROLES["security"]` / `["tests"]` (the default `review diff` 8-role board's own lenses) now blend in the adversarial framing from the quorum/brainstorm persona pool's "security-paranoid reviewer" / "skeptical SRE" personas, so the default board — which previously used none of those personas at all — gets some of their adversarial tone on the two roles closest in spirit, without turning the whole 8-role board into personas.

## Scoping choice flagged for the repo owner

Finding #3 was implemented as an **opt-in `--adversarial-check` flag** rather than a universal default, per the task's own explicit instruction to flag this choice for awareness. Reasoning: it costs one extra model call, which routine ad-hoc `review quorum` questions during normal dev work shouldn't always pay for — but it's wired to be trivial to add to a ship-gate flow specifically (`review quorum "..." --adversarial-check --task ...`). If the intent was actually "always run this, no exceptions," that's a one-line change (drop the flag, always attempt the extra pass when the verdict is clean) — happy to flip it if that's the call.

## Dogfooded extensively before opening this PR

This diff was reviewed against itself (`review diff --staged`) across 11 rounds, each round fixing a real bug or gap the previous round introduced or missed — full detail in CHANGELOG.md's "Unreleased" section. Highlights: a separator regex that silently skipped the new adversarial-check pass on exactly the clean verdict it exists to double-check; a marker-parsing scheme that went through several iterations of false-positive/false-negative fixes on decoration/whitespace variants of the refutation marker text; a ReDoS-shaped unbounded scan on pathological input; a `--visual` composition bug that silently disabled the evidence warning; and two documented, regression-pinned ACCEPTED RESIDUALS where a regex-based approach genuinely cannot parse certain adversarial-pass answer shapes (documented in `refutation_verdict`'s own docstring, not silently missing).

## Test plan

- [x] 58 new tests in `tests/test_adversarial_review_rigor.py`, covering all four findings directly: prompt content assertions, evidence-warning surfacing (isolated + end-to-end through both diff-review render paths, flat and board, including the `--visual` composition and custom-`--prompt` cases), the `--adversarial-check` flag's full gating logic (skip-on-disagreement, skip-on-unparseable, clean-run-passes, refutation-flips-exit-code), and the role-lens persona blending.

title: fix(stats,cli): fall back to model-counting on bare --check when a task has zero role data
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #246, per Alex's explicit request (Refs #251).

PR #246 made a bare `review task CODE --check` (no explicit `--min-models`/`--min-roles`) default to counting distinct **board roles** instead of distinct **models**. That's correct for tasks reviewed via the normal `review diff` board, which records per-seat role data. But it left a gap: any task whose entire review history predates role-tracking, or whose history comes only from `review quorum`/`review just-ask`/`review brainstorm`/`review qa` (modes that never record role data at all), has zero role-tagged iterations — and the bare-check default was treating "zero roles recorded" the same as "not enough roles," a guaranteed hard fail even if the task genuinely has 3+ distinct models in its history that would have satisfied the old model-counting default.

This PR makes the bare-check default fall back to the old model-counting check (same numeric floor) whenever a task has **exactly zero** role-tagged iterations in its non-mismatched history — not "some but below the floor." A task with even one role-tagged iteration, of any verdict (passed, failed, or unverdicted), still uses the role-based default and must pass or fail on its own merits; it never falls back just because the role floor isn't met. A task whose entire history is diff-identity-mismatched (e.g. a task-code collision with an unrelated repo) also keeps the existing role-based fail-closed shape rather than firing the fallback with a misleading message. Explicit `--min-models`/`--min-roles` paths are completely untouched.

The result payload gains two new keys whenever the bare-check path is active:
- `quorum_mode_fallback` — a human-readable explanation, present only when the fallback actually fires (also printed as a `note:` line in text mode).
- `min_models_source: "explicit" | "fallback"` — a positive, machine-readable discriminator, since `"min_models" in payload` alone can no longer tell an explicit `--min-models` request apart from a fallback-produced one.

## Review history

This went through several rounds of multi-model review (codex/opus/fable/glm via `review diff`), which caught and fixed two real bugs along the way:
1. The first cut scoped the "does this task have any role data" check to **passed** iterations only, which meant a role-tagged iteration that *failed* was invisible — the fallback could fire for a task that genuinely went through role-recording review, just not successfully.
2. A follow-up fix then missed that a task whose **entire** history is diff-identity-mismatched (not just short of the floor) would still fire the fallback with a message falsely claiming "no role data" when role data does exist, just for an unrelated repo/diff.

Both are fixed and covered by dedicated tests. Two verification concerns raised by reviewers were checked directly against the code and confirmed non-issues (documented in the commit/PR, not left open):
- The CLI's `role_mode`/`model_mode` selection (`reviewlib/cli.py:1737-1738`) is derived from the result payload (`"min_roles" in result`, `"min_models" in result`), not from parsed CLI flags — confirmed by direct read, not just by tests passing.
- `min_models_source` accompanies `min_models` on every shape that carries it, including both `_rejected()` early-return paths and the zero-recorded-iterations denial — pinned by dedicated tests.

**Deliberately not changed** (flagged repeatedly by reviewers as design-level concerns, but they either match the explicit spec or are follow-up-worthy, not blocking):
- The fallback intentionally applies to *any* task with zero role data, including brand-new tasks reviewed only via `quorum`/`just-ask`/`brainstorm`/`qa` — not just legacy pre-#246 history. This is what the dispatch explicitly asked for ("pre-#246 **and** quorum/brainstorm-sourced task history"), not an oversight. Reviewers noted this makes the self-merge-authority gate's role-based default "opt-out-able" by choice of review mode — worth a conscious decision if you want to narrow it to legacy history specifically (e.g. gate on a record-schema-version or timestamp cutoff), but that would be a deliberate scope change, not a bug fix.
- Mode discrimination is via a matrix of optional keys (`min_roles`, `min_models`, `min_models_source`, `quorum_mode_fallback`) rather than one unified `quorum_mode` enum field. Multiple reviewers suggested consolidating this — reasonable, but a larger API redesign better suited to its own PR.

title: fix(review): visible pool-shortfall notice when a board seat is silently unavailable
body:
## Summary

- Refs #276. Root-caused from Alex's "где glm5.2?!" — a `review diff` round reported as "reviewed via codex + Fable" with zero indication that other configured seats (Opus, GLM) were silently dropped before dispatch.
- Two distinct, unrelated root causes were found and fixed **outside this PR** (personal config, `~/.config/review-cli/config.yaml`, not code): GLM had been disabled since 2026-07-17 for a hang that recent logs show is resolved, and the default pool size was temporarily 3 (now 4, with GLM back in the live rotation). Separately, `codex`/`omp` live under `/opt/homebrew/bin` while `claude` resolves via `/Users/ultra/.local/bin` — a subagent/background shell whose PATH omits the former loses codex+omp while claude stays available, reproduced directly with a minimal PATH.
- This PR is the **code** fix: `_report_pool_shortfall` (`reviewlib/modes/review.py`) prints a visible STDOUT notice, with `flush=True`, naming every board seat absent from both the live pool and the reserve — with its actual unavailability reason — whenever the pre-dispatch pool selection comes up short of the requested size. The only prior signal (`board: degraded`) covers a different, rarer case (reserve exhausted *during* dispatch) and only prints to stderr, which report-pasting workflows routinely drop.

## Review history

Reviewed through `review-cli` itself across 9 rounds (Opus + Fable/k3/GLM rotating as the third seat — Fable dropped after a round-2 model-side safety false-positive; non-codex pools throughout, per the documented self-review recursion hazard). No correctness or security bug was found in any round. Real findings that were addressed:

- k3: "requested N" arithmetic went nonsensical when `--pool` exceeded the board size — now clamped via `config.py`'s own `_effective_pool_size` (single source of truth; also closes a separate GLM DRY finding about re-deriving that rule inline).
- k3: `--pool 0` ("all seats") mode exempted the notice entirely, reproducing the exact incident under that configuration — fixed; the target is `len(board)`.
- k3 / GLM: `test_reviewer_board.py`'s `_AvailabilityPatch` patched `backend_available` but not `backend_unavailable_reason`, so this new code path leaked a real, unmocked probe into an existing hermetic test — extended the patch symmetrically.
- Opus / Fable / k3 / GLM (raised repeatedly across rounds): no test exercised the real `select_pool_and_reserve_with_reuse` output or the actual `_mode_review_board` call site, only hand-built pool/reserve lists — added both as explicit tests.
- GLM: `pool`/`reserve` are now keyword-only — a future positional transposition would previously type-check cleanly while silently inverting the notice's semantics.

Two narrower, lower-severity findings are documented as known limitations in the function's docstring and filed as #277, a deliberate follow-up:
1. The reason shown is re-probed via `backend_unavailable_reason` on the raw board spelling; this is accurate for concrete-spelling seats but can be imprecise for a bare-alias board seat, and near-usage-limit exclusions that get padded over are invisible to this notice entirely (not merely mislabeled).
2. The notice prints at pre-dispatch time, before whatever produces a final "reviewed via X + Y" summary — a reader who only sees that summary (not the full terminal output) still misses it.

title: fix(seat-cooldown,config): catch chronic rc!=0/seat-fatal failures + demote Fable
body:
## Summary

Root-causes and fixes the Fable seat's near-100% dispatch-failure-rate problem, in two parts:

1. **Cooldown-recording gap.** `_chronic_unavailable_reason` (the function deciding whether `reviewlib.seat_cooldown` caches a dispatch as chronically doomed) only checked the "is currently unavailable" administrative-sentinel markers on the `returncode == 0` branch. A real production log confirms Fable's CLI wrapper sometimes relays the identical sentinel text with a non-zero exit code -- a shape the cooldown cache never caught, so the seat kept paying for a real dispatch on every invocation that failed this way (`review stat` showed only 33 of 447 doomed calls were being caught). Fixed by checking the marker set on both branches, gated by a `_looks_transient`/`_is_seat_fatal` guard (mirrors retry.py's own timeout/5xx/seat-fatal precedence, numeric AND text) so a genuinely transient 503/529/timeout blip, or a seat-fatal auth failure (401/403/501), is never cached as an hours-long chronic cooldown -- an auth failure resolves the moment credentials are fixed, not after a timer.
2. **Priority/effort demotion.** `review stat` telemetry shows a 97.9-100% dispatch failure rate -- Fable was priority 1 in `DEFAULT_BOARD`, so even a perfect cooldown catch rate still means the first slot of every review is wasted on a near-certain failure. Demoted Fable from priority 1 to the last board seat (mirrors the existing review-cli#65 precedent for a different pathological seat), and excluded it from the heavy preset (it was already excluded from the default preset).

Supersedes PR #290 (narrower fix for the same underlying problem -- excluded Fable from `HEAVY_PRESET_BOARD` only) and issue #280 -- both addressed as a strict subset of this change (Fable's demotion to last-resort in `DEFAULT_BOARD` naturally removes it from every preset too, achieving the same `HEAVY_PRESET_BOARD` outcome plus the root-cause cooldown fix and the `DEFAULT_BOARD` priority reorder #290 didn't touch). #290's `FABLE_SEAT`-constant and `reviewlib/__init__.py` facade-export ideas were harvested into this change.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD red-first: new tests confirmed failing before each fix, passing after.
- [x] Full `pytest` suite: 2174 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (after rebasing onto latest `main`, which includes PR #270's true-silence-detection change).
- [x] `ruff check .`: no issues.
- [x] `review diff --staged` (this repo's own multi-model review gate): 8 rounds across Opus/Codex/GLM/k3 (+ reserve seats on infra hiccups), fixing every real finding along the way -- a seat-fatal auth failure that could still get cached despite the transient guard, a quota-marker scan that briefly regressed to unbounded stdout (self-starve risk), a combined-length bound that dropped a genuine short sentinel paired with unrelated stderr, a timeout (rc=124) that could slip past the quota check, and an escalation-history wipe on a withheld-but-not-recovered result. The last 3 rounds found zero correctness bugs.
- [x] Live-verified `review --show-board` shows Fable at the last position, out of the routinely-dispatched pool.

Two follow-up findings are deliberately out of scope for this change and filed separately:
- review-cli#297 -- dashboard fallback hint isn't preset-aware (pre-existing, now shows a different seat).
- review-cli#301 -- `retry.classify_failure`'s seat-fatal check is text-only, unlike this change's new numeric check (an asymmetry between the cooldown-cache decision and the in-seat retry decision).

title: fix(dashboard): stop /api/stats from hanging on cold cache + O(n^2) clustering
body:
## What

Fixes review-cli#323: the dashboard's `/api/stats` (and `/api/runs`) could hang indefinitely / return nothing on a real, large install (~10GB, ~132k call-log files). Root cause was three compounding bugs in `_SessionCache`:

1. No cold-start handling — a fully cold cache blocked the request thread on a ~130s synchronous parse.
2. The `force=True` startup prewarm held `self._lock` for the entire parse — a real request racing the prewarm blocked trying to acquire the same lock before ever reaching any cold-placeholder logic.
3. Fixing #2 naively introduced a stampede — the cold-placeholder path and the prewarm path could both kick a background parse concurrently, doubling disk/CPU load instead of halving it.

Also fixed: `cluster_sessions`'s `same_task` check called `Session.task_code` (an O(n) scan-from-start) once per call, making clustering O(n²) whenever a session has no `task_code` — this alone dominated a warm parse at the real ~132k-call-log scale on this install.

## Hardening from adversarial review (8 rounds, codex + GLM)

- Cold placeholder no longer prematurely marks the cache "caught up" before the background parse runs — a failed parse now retries (bounded) instead of leaving the dashboard permanently blank.
- A malformed-timestamp filename is now handled inside `parse_call_log`/`parse_brainstorm_log` themselves (returns `None` per their documented contract) instead of needing a guard at every call site — fixes both the directory-scan path and the previously-unguarded SSE stream at the source.
- `get()`/`get_derived()` re-check the installed lineage after `_ensure_fresh` releases the lock, retrying (bounded) or falling back to a direct parse rather than risking a caller receiving another concurrent lineage's clustered sessions. The fallback is tagged with a sentinel generation (`-1`) so it can never poison the derived-value (stats) cache under another gap's tag.
- The sync-parse path now installs its result and clears the in-flight flag in ONE atomic lock hold instead of two separate ones — closes a window where another caller could observe "not refreshing" while stale data was still in place.

A same-lineage single-flight wait (Condition-based) was attempted and reverted after review found it introduced a narrower race of its own (notify-before-install allowed a waiter to slip through and still start a duplicate parse) — worse than the gap it tried to close.

## Deliberately NOT fixed here (tracked separately)

- **review-cli#327** — the real per-lineage in-flight-parse redesign several findings point at (concurrent different-gap requests can still race/stampede). This needs a proper redesign, not another patch under time pressure.
- **review-cli#328** — remaining low/moderate-severity gaps: cold-window 404s on writes/detail lookups, duplicated malformed-date guard logic (3 copies, should be 1), docstring precision, `_log_dir_fingerprint` computed under lock, test/comment cleanup.
- **review-cli#326** — separately: the dashboard service is currently intentionally stopped (`launchctl bootout`) because loading the real ~10GB/132k-file log directory balloons the process to 32.8GB RSS (a distinct memory-architecture problem — `CallLog` holds full body text in memory for every call, needed all at once for the aggregate/list view).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_dashboard.py` — 121/121 passing (was 113 before this fix)
- [x] 8 rounds of `review diff --staged` (codex + GLM), every HIGH/MODERATE finding addressed with a test
- [x] Manually verified `dparser.load_sessions` no longer raises on a malformed-timestamp filename, and clustering is behaviorally unchanged (traced the O(n²)→O(n) rewrite's equivalence)

title: fix(dashboard): cap CallLog body/stderr retention, fix #326 memory balloon
body:
## Summary
- Every streamed call body/stderr was retained in memory uncapped forever (the persistent SQLite parse cache never evicts), ballooning the review dashboard to 32.8GB RSS on the real ~132k-log install. Body is now capped to a bounded head+tail (character budget sized against PEP-393's worst-case 4-bytes/char string representation, so retained memory is provably bounded regardless of script/Unicode mix), and stderr is capped on both bytes and line count.
- Classification (`completed`/`has_error`/`error_summary`/`is_paywall`/`is_cf_blocked`/`is_bad_key`/`has_real_content`) is computed once from the FULL untruncated text at parse time and stored on `CallLog`, so a marker (or the EXIT-0 empty-vs-real-verdict split) surviving only in the omitted/mangled part of a huge log is still classified correctly, independent of what's later retained for display.
- `_PARSER_VERSION` bumped 1→2 so a warm, long-lived cache re-parses through the new path instead of serving stale uncapped/unclassified rows forever.
- Filed #335 for a follow-up: `compute_harness_stats`/`top_oversized_calls` still scan the (now capped) body for `SKILL.md`/`MEMORY.md`/diff markers — a lower-severity diagnostic gap, deliberately deferred. Verified no other `body`/`stderr_lines` consumer is affected.

title: fix(review): say WHY a passing review did not satisfy the commit gate
body:
## The incident

A detached agent ran `review diff`, saw every seat pass, found the commit-gate marker stale, followed the gate's own README advice to `touch` that marker by hand, and its headless permission policy rejected the write and killed the run. About forty minutes of work, and the predecessor agent died the same way. From the agent's side the tool said nothing at all: green review, blocked commit, no reason anywhere.

The marker is written by exactly one shape of run — a completed `review diff --staged` whose diff came from the real index and was not truncated for dispatch. Every other shape skipped the write silently.

## What this changes

**An OK review that does not satisfy the gate now says so, in one stderr line**, naming the condition that failed and the fix for that condition. The remediation is per-reason on purpose: a truncated diff is told to split the change rather than to "re-run it `--staged`", which would truncate again. Advice that loops is how the next agent burns another forty minutes. For the same reason truncation is checked first among the reasons — staging fixes the staged condition but never the truncation.

**The two writes report their own failures.** Both stay best-effort (neither an unwritable marker nor an unwritable `.git/review-stamp` may fail a good review), but a swallowed failure rebuilds the same trap one level down. They get separate messages because they feed different gates: agent-tools' hook stats the marker, the local git pre-commit hook verifies the stamp. A shared message would send the reader to fix the wrong file. Also now caught: a marker path that is not a regular file (`touch` on a directory "succeeds" by bumping its mtime), an exported-but-empty `REVIEW_MARKER=` (which degenerates to the current directory), and a `git rev-parse` that fails inside a repo rather than because there is no repo.

**The diff-shape half of the gate predicate lives in one place** (`_commit_gate_skip_reason`), so a future condition added to it cannot skip the warning by drift. A truth-table test alone would not pin that — it leaves the caller free to re-spell the predicate inline — so the test patches the helper and checks the caller follows it in both directions.

**The dispatch-cap helper now reports the plain fact "the cap cut this diff"** instead of a `--staged`-scoped version of it. Nothing about when the marker is written changed; an unstaged oversized run was refused before and is refused now, but it used to be told to stage and re-run, which truncates again.

The `review` skill blurb and SKILL.md now name `review diff --staged` as the pre-commit invocation.

## Ships with agent-tools#506

That PR removes the `touch` advice this incident followed and normalizes the empty-`REVIEW_MARKER` handling on the gate side. Land them together: the review seats on each side read the other repo's *installed* checkout and correctly report the mismatch until both are merged.

## Verification

- 28 tests in `tests/test_review_marker.py`, covering every reason branch, both write-failure branches, the delegation contract, and end-to-end oversized runs staged and unstaged.
- Full suite: 23 of 24 checks pass. The one failure, `test_dashboard_managed_surface_and_lib_absent_fallback`, reproduces on a clean `HEAD` worktree — the venv sees `agenttools_service` while the `bin/review` subprocess does not. Unrelated to this change.
- Thirteen review rounds across four models; the findings that shaped this diff are recorded in the code comments next to what they changed.
