title: feat(gate): single review-gate template (merge/rebase/cherry-pick skip, --print-gate) and review --version
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/396

## Problem

The pre-commit gate rig installs on every machine (`~/.config/git/hooks/review-gate`) was a hand-ported copy living in agent-tools. review-cli's own template got the trivial-delta tolerance (#211); the installed copy never did, and it has no exception for a commit that finishes a merge / rebase / cherry-pick. Result: agents ran 3-4 full reviews per PR and finished merges with `git commit --no-verify` (which also switches off the secret scan and the conventional-commit check).

## Change

- review-cli owns BOTH gate bodies from shared blocks: the self-contained `_PRECOMMIT` (no-rig machines) and the composer-stage `REVIEW_GATE` that rig installs. `review install-commit-hook --print-gate` prints the composer body for rig (rig-cli#382 consumes it; the agent-tools copy becomes its fallback).
- A commit that finishes an in-progress merge (`MERGE_HEAD`), rebase (`rebase-merge/` / `rebase-apply/` state dir) or cherry-pick (`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`) skips the staged-review requirement with a logged reason on stderr. Markers are resolved with `git rev-parse --git-path` so it also works in linked worktrees. The rebase case keys on the state DIRECTORY, not `REBASE_HEAD`: git 2.50 leaves that ref behind after the rebase completes, so keying on it would have exempted every later commit.
- `review --version` (pyproject `[project] version` first, installed metadata second).
- `TMPDIR=/` no longer collapses the temp-repo exemption to `/*`.

## Tests

`tests/test_review_gate_template.py` drives REAL `git commit` / `rebase --continue` / `cherry-pick --continue` through the installed gate in repos under `<repo>/.test-repos/` (outside the gate's temp exemption, so nothing passes vacuously): one-line restage after a stamped review passes, a substantive restage is blocked, merge/rebase/cherry-pick commits pass with the logged reason and the next unreviewed commit is blocked again, the linked-worktree case, `TMPDIR=/`, `--version`.

`python3 -m pytest -q`: 2425 passed, 6 skipped (before the round-1 review fixes; re-run in the follow-up commit).

## Review

Round 1: `review diff --staged --task GH-396` (Opus / Codex / Sonnet). Fixed from it: the lingering `REBASE_HEAD` bypass (confirmed live on git 2.50), `TMPDIR=/`, TOML layouts the version parser rejected, `install-commit-hook` flag dispatch, coverage for the version fallbacks. Deliberately kept: a `git merge --no-commit` followed by unrelated staged edits passes (same trust class as `--no-verify`, and it is logged).

title: fix(process): emit periodic heartbeats during silent backend waits
body:
## Summary

- A real incident (2026-09-07): an omp-harness session's `review diff` sat with zero visible output for 40+ minutes before being killed by hand. Forensics (see below) could not pin the exact hung call, but the underlying silent-wait code path is real and demonstrated by the fix's own tests: `_run_streamed`'s default idle timeout is 20 minutes, `retry.run_seat_with_retry` permits exactly one further timeout retry, and the plain `review diff` mode never sets `backends._ANNOUNCE_LOGS` (no "tail -f this log" pointer) — so any seat that goes idle can legitimately produce up to ~40 minutes of near-total caller-visible silence.
- Adds a periodic "still waiting" heartbeat to both wait loops in `_run_streamed` (idle-mode poll loop for review seats; wall-clock poll loop for bounded QA/vision callers), printed to stderr every `$REVIEW_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` (default 60s) regardless of `_ANNOUNCE_LOGS`.
- The heartbeat write runs on its own daemon thread (never inline on the timeout-enforcing poll thread — a write to a full-but-open pipe blocks, not raises) and is capped by a semaphore sized to the existing `$REVIEW_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, so a permanently stuck stderr costs a small bounded number of leaked threads, never unbounded, and never starves a different healthy seat's own heartbeat.

## Root-cause evidence (honest accounting)

- `~/.config/review-cli/seat-cooldown.json`: `claude:claude-opus-4-8`, `claude:claude-sonnet-5`, `claude:claude-fable-5` all recorded into an 8h cooldown within a 22-second window (08:19:27–08:19:49 UTC), reason `"session limit / usage credits"`.
- `~/.config/review-cli/run-stats.jsonl`: the reviewer pool collapsed from a healthy 3-seat mix (opus/codex/sonnet) throughout 07:05–08:19 UTC to a degraded single-seat (`codex` only, 1 ok / 5 fail) pattern for every run for hours afterward — including a concurrent `task-cli#130` session hitting the identical degradation at 10:28 UTC.
- **Correction made mid-investigation**: I initially hypothesized the three claude seats reached cooldown via two consecutive 20-minute idle-timeout hangs. Checking the actual per-call logs disproved this — claude session-limit failures are FAST (a one-line `"You've hit your session limit · resets 4pm"` message, exit 1, confirmed in `~/Library/Logs/review-cli/*-claude-r0.log`), not silent hangs. None of the retained per-call logs from the incident window span a continuous ~40-minute silence with a clean EXIT/TIMEOUT footer, so the exact call responsible for the reported hang could not be pinpointed. What's confirmed instead: hours of sustained multi-seat quota exhaustion, plausibly contributing to whichever call actually hung, plus a couple of per-call logs abandoned mid-write with no closing footer (consistent with an externally-killed process, though individually too short-lived to BE the 40-minute hang). The commit message and code comments reflect this corrected, hedged account rather than the disproven one.
- Independent of exact attribution, the silent-wait code path itself is real and reproducible — see the new tests in `tests/test_streaming.py`.

## Review process note

The gate for this PR (`review diff --staged`, review-cli's own pre-commit hook) required `-m codex:gpt-5.6-terra` (a single explicit seat) rather than the default board — the board is degraded by the very incident this PR fixes (all claude/opencode seats in cooldown for most of today), so a normal multi-seat run couldn't reach the "ok" verdict the commit-gate stamp requires. Ten review rounds against codex surfaced and fixed real issues along the way: a blocking-pipe timeout-loop stall, a per-call vs. process-wide thread-leak tradeoff (went through per-call → single global slot → the final bounded-semaphore design after the global slot was shown to starve concurrent healthy seats), non-finite/underflow env-var handling, and wording accuracy in the README/CLI help.

## Follow-up (not fixed here)

- review-cli#408 (filed by this review's own policy engine): a `Thread.start()` failure under host thread/resource exhaustion currently escapes the poll loop instead of degrading to "no heartbeat this tick, try again next tick".
- Documented-but-not-implemented scope: a seat still queued on the concurrency cap (before it spawns) gets no heartbeat; a handful of short, bounded, non-seat subprocess calls (e.g. `git worktree add` during QA isolation) use the plain, non-streamed runner and don't get one either.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_streaming.py` — 52 tests (11 new/changed for this feature), passing under both `pytest` and the file's own standalone `__main__` runner (used by `tests/smoke.py`/CI).
- [x] Broader targeted suite (`test_provider_failover`, `test_seat_cooldown`, `test_dashboard`, `test_concurrency_cap`, `test_reentrancy_guard`, `test_qa_bot`, `test_omp_backend`) — 398 passing, no regressions.
- [x] Confirmed 9 pre-existing `--help`/ANSI-color test failures (`test_help_defaults.py`, `test_no_git_repo.py`, `test_stat_subcommand.py`) reproduce identically on unmodified `main` — unrelated to this change.
- [x] `review diff --staged -m codex:gpt-5.6-terra` — passing verdict, commit-gate stamp verified to match the staged diff hash before committing.

title: fix(config): pad role-reuse pool against board size, not reachable count
body:
## Summary

`task-cli#139`: when a review board is down to a single live reviewer (a session-limit
cooldown, not merely a soft usage-limit warning), the quorum gate kept reading `0/3` or
`1/3` distinct roles instead of letting the one live seat cover the missing roles — even
though that exact role-reuse mechanism already existed in the codebase (built
2026-08-18) for a different, narrower case.

- **Root cause** (`reviewlib/config.py`, `select_pool_with_reuse`): the target pool size
  clamped to `len(reachable)`, which collapsed to 1 whenever only one seat was reachable
  — before the role-padding loop ever got a chance to run. Fixed by sizing the target
  against the full board (`min(pool, len(board))`) instead, when `usage_percent` is given
  and `pool` is a concrete positive request.
- **Unreachable from the real CLI** (`reviewlib/pool_guard.py` + `reviewlib/cli.py`): a
  separate pre-dispatch guard was bailing with exit 10 *before* dispatch ever reached the
  fixed selector — so the selector fix alone would not have resolved a real `review diff`
  run. Added a `reuse_eligible` gate, wired only for a non-`-m`, role-lensed board with a
  positive effective pool size.
- **Wrong ETA**: the planned-pool ETA computation used the non-reuse-aware
  `split_pool_reserve`; switched to `select_pool_and_reserve_with_reuse` so the announced
  pool size matches what actually dispatches.
- **Misleading notice**: the "board padded" stderr line hardcoded "usage limit" as the
  cause, which is false for a hard-cooldown pad; reworded generically.

Known follow-up, not fixed here: `--show-board`'s preview display still under-reports
this scenario (filed as `task-cli#147`).

## Test plan

- [x] New TDD red-first regression tests across `tests/test_pool_reuse.py`,
      `tests/test_pool_guard.py`, `tests/test_pool_guard_failover_wiring.py`,
      `tests/test_reuse_warnings.py` — each confirmed red against pre-fix code, green
      after.
- [x] Full suite: `python3 -m pytest -q` → 2415 passed, 9 pre-existing unrelated
      failures (ANSI-color leakage in `--help` capture, confirmed identical on
      unmodified `main`), 6 skipped.

title: fix(review): refuse to record a --task #<n> review from the wrong branch
body:
## Summary

Postmortem (conloca/landing): before `gh ship` could derive a review-quorum task code from a bare GitHub issue reference (agent-tools#566/#567), the documented workaround was to mint a throwaway ticket and run `review diff -C <shared primary checkout> --task <code>` — reviewing whatever happened to be uncommitted in a shared, actively-mutating checkout, not the PR's own worktree/branch. One resulting ticket (conloca/landing#135) reviewed a `package.json` claiming version "0.4.3", a version that never existed on any ref in that repo's history — direct evidence the diff being recorded had nothing to do with the task code it was credited to. This produced a string of near-duplicate "review the uncommitted diff" GitHub issues that could structurally never lead to a merge.

- When `review diff --task '#<n>'` names a bare same-repo GitHub issue with exactly one matching open PR, and the current branch isn't that PR's head branch, refuse (new `EXIT_TASK_BRANCH_MISMATCH` exit code) before dispatching any model calls, naming an existing worktree already on the right branch when one exists.
- Fail-open when the check can't be trusted: ambiguous/zero PR matches, `gh` missing/erroring, a non-`#<n>` code, a truncated PR page.
- Also refuses a piped diff for a `#<n>` code (bypasses the branch-derived diff entirely), excludes fork PRs and cross-repository closing references from the match set, treats a detached HEAD as "branch unknown" rather than a literal branch, scrubs `GH_REPO`/`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` from the `gh` lookup, and only applies once a diff review actually has a non-empty diff to record (so a diff-less `--visual` companion fallback is never falsely blocked).
- Escape hatch: `--no-verify-task-branch`.

Ref: conloca/landing#96, conloca/landing#135

## Known follow-ups (not blocking, found by this PR's own review rounds)

- `review visual IMAGE` (the standalone subcommand, not the `--visual` flag riding `review diff`) isn't yet covered by this guard.
- A concurrent index mutation during diff capture can still race the recorded review-stamp in a narrow window.
- The branch-change recheck doesn't yet scope itself strictly to bare issue codes only (cosmetic — it's a no-op for non-issue codes since the outer guard already gates on `_is_bare_issue_task_code`, but the recheck's own condition should say so explicitly).
- Repository-identity comparison (cross-repo closing-reference exclusion) compares owner/repo only, not host — a GitHub Enterprise remote could theoretically collide with a github.com repo of the same owner/name.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_task_branch_binding.py` — 22 new tests (unit-level against `_task_code_branch_mismatch_warning` with a fake `gh` on PATH, plus end-to-end CLI tests via both real subprocess and in-process stubbed-backend calls).
- [x] Full suite: 2271 passed, 6 skipped (pre-existing/unrelated), 0 new failures — verified against unmodified `main` that all pre-existing failures are ANSI-color/environment quirks on this machine, not introduced by this change.

body:
## Summary

- The dashboard's `/api/runs`/`/api/stats` invalidation check (`_log_dir_fingerprint`) and the SSE watcher's 1Hz poll (`_snapshot_logs`) both `os.scandir`+`.stat()`-ed the ENTIRE log directory on every call — measured ~3.9s cold / ~0.5-0.7s warm-cache against the real 147k-file, 18GB install (task-cli#151). `_log_dir_fingerprint` runs under `_SessionCache`'s lock on every request; `_snapshot_logs` runs continuously, independent of request volume — almost certainly the real explanation for "sustains 77% CPU continuously."
- Unifies all three duplicate scan sites (`_dir_signature`, `_log_dir_fingerprint`, `_snapshot_logs`) onto one shared `_scan_log_dir_entries`, which skips `.stat()` for any file whose filename-embedded stamp is older than a 6h safety-margined window (~18x the max per-call wall time) — safe because artifacts are write-once by their originating writer, and a file that old can never move the signature again. A stat-free `total_count` separately catches create/delete of files outside the window.
- The window's anchor is `min(newest valid filename stamp in the directory, now)` — directory-relative (works against test fixtures using fixed, non-"now" dates) but clamped to the real wall clock so a future-dated stray file can never push the cutoff forward and hide a genuinely-recent live file.

## Real-machine verification

Directly measured against the actual `~/Library/Logs/review-cli` directory (147k+ files):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `_dir_signature` / `_log_dir_fingerprint` / `_snapshot_logs` | ~3.9s cold, ~0.5-0.7s warm | ~0.35-0.4s, steady regardless of cache state |

The remaining ~0.35s is the `os.scandir` readdir itself — an irreducible floor this fix doesn't remove (filed as a follow-up, task-cli#156, alongside the log directory's total lack of retention/rotation).

A top-level-directory-mtime fast path was considered and rejected: verified directly on this machine's filesystem (APFS) that appending to an existing file does NOT bump its parent directory's mtime — that approach would have silently hidden a live-streaming review's growing `.log`.

## Review

Five rounds (Sonnet + Grok throughout; Codex/GLM quota-exhausted for the later rounds) found and fixed four real issues: a crash on a shape-matching-but-invalid filename date, a stale-cache gap where deleting an old out-of-window file never invalidated the signature, a future-anchor-poisoning gap (closed by clamping the anchor to `min(newest, now)` instead of trying to bound a rejection tolerance), and a semantic change to `total_size` that needed its own test. The last two rounds found no further correctness/security issues.

## Test plan

- [x] 144 dashboard tests pass (`python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q`), including 12 new regression tests
- [x] Full suite: 2414 passed, 9 pre-existing unrelated failures (confirmed identical on unmodified `main` — CLI `--help` ANSI-color formatting, unrelated to this change), 6 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean
- [x] Direct before/after measurement against the real 147k-file log directory (see table above)

Follow-ups filed: task-cli#155 (`review dashboard status` false "stopped" report — root-caused to a legacy launchd unit, lives in a different repo), task-cli#156 (log directory retention/rotation).

title: fix(process): opencode/omp backends never inherit review-cli's own stdin
body:
## What

`_run_streamed`'s Popen call (`reviewlib/process.py`) passed `stdin=None`
(inherit) whenever `input_text` was `None` -- the case for `review_opencode`
and `review_omp` in `reviewlib/backends.py`, both argv-only backends that
never pass `input_text`. A bare `None` means "don't redirect": the child
CLI inherits review-cli's own real stdin fd.

review-cli routinely runs as a subprocess of an orchestrating agent whose
own stdin is an open, non-EOF pipe/tty. If the opencode/omp CLI reads stdin
at all (a common non-TTY CLI pattern), the inherited fd let it block
indefinitely at 0% CPU with zero output -- observed live 2026-09-07: an
`opencode run` subprocess hung in a stdin-read syscall and had to be killed
and relaunched manually with stdin from `/dev/null`.

This is very likely the actual root cause behind some of the "opencode/oc:zai
stalls with zero output" cases previously band-aided only by the
true-silence stall watchdog + cooldown, which detects the *symptom* (zero
output) and cools the seat down as though the provider's quota were
exhausted -- when the real cause was review-cli's own subprocess wiring,
unrelated to the model/provider.

## Fix

`_run_streamed` now always passes `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` for the
`input_text is None` path -- never a bare/inherited `None` -- so an
argv-only backend call can never read the parent's stdin. The codex/claude
path (`input_text` provided) keeps `stdin=subprocess.PIPE` unchanged.

## Reproduction

Wrote a throwaway 3-process harness (outer harness holds an open,
never-written, never-closed pipe as the middle process's stdin; the middle
process calls `reviewlib.process._run_streamed` exactly like
`review_opencode`/`review_omp` do -- argv-only, no `input_text` -- spawning a
grandchild that blocks on `sys.stdin.read()`):

- **Before the fix**: harness times out after 6s with the grandchild still
  running (`HUNG after 6.01s (still running, poll=None)`), reading forever
  from the inherited pipe.
- **After the fix**: harness completes in ~0.14s
  (`COMPLETED in 0.14s, returncode=0`, grandchild sees 0 stdin bytes
  immediately -- DEVNULL is EOF-at-open).

## Tests

- New `tests/test_process.py`: spies on `subprocess.Popen` (no real
  opencode/omp process) and asserts `stdin is subprocess.DEVNULL` for the
  `input_text=None` path and `stdin is subprocess.PIPE` for the
  `input_text` provided path. Verified this test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes against the fix.
- Registered in `tests/smoke.py`'s `_UNIT_FILES` (required by
  `test_every_unit_file_is_run`).
- Ran `python3 tests/test_process.py` (2 passed) and the full
  `python3 tests/test_streaming.py` (40 passed) and
  `python3 tests/test_omp_backend.py` (26 passed) -- all green, no
  regressions in `_run_streamed`'s other timeout/liveness/true-silence
  behavior or the omp backend's dispatch.

## Changelog / version

Bumped `pyproject.toml` to 0.36.2 and added a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

Refs #428

title: fix(cli): surface near-miss task-code keys on a failed --check in text mode too
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #429 (review-cli#389): `quorum_check()` already sets `searched_key`/`near_miss_keys` diagnostic fields on a failed `--check` when a same-digits, different-`#` twin key exists in the store, but that diagnostic only ever reached `--json` output. A human running a bare `review task CODE --check` (no `--json`) never saw the near-miss note, even though issue #389's third acceptance criterion requires the mismatch be diagnosable from the refusal alone.

`_quorum_check_subcommand` now prints the same note to stderr in both text and `--json` modes, matching the existing excluded-mismatch warning's both-modes convention. The excluded-mismatch branch's wording was refined across two review rounds (an AI security reviewer on this diff's own PR caught first an overclaim — "already count above" can be false when diff-identity verification excluded that record — then a dangerous overcorrection recommending `--no-verify-identity` as a bypass, which the flag's own docstring forbids for a genuine mismatch; final wording just hedges and points at `mismatch_details`).

## Tests

- `test_cli_check_near_miss_key_note_text_mode_review_cli_389`: failed check on `#105` with iterations recorded under `105` prints the near-miss note to stderr in plain text mode.
- `test_cli_check_near_miss_key_absent_when_no_twin_review_cli_389`: no note when there's no twin key in the store.

title: fix(config): pad recorded review pool to ship min_roles floor (#309)
body:
Refs #309

A recorded `review diff --task CODE` (`--preset light` pool 2, or a single `-m` model) could never satisfy the default ship-gate floor (`review task CODE --check` / `gh ship`, `min_roles=3`) because the board is priority-ordered and dispatched the same top-N seats every time.

- Recorded reviews now take `max(resolved pool, 3)` unless `--pool N` is explicit (N<3 still wins but warns).
- `-m one-model --task` and a short (1-2 seat) config `models:`/`board:` roster get roles cloned onto unused board roles via `ensure_min_distinct_roles` so `select_pool_with_reuse` can pad to the floor.
- A multi-model explicit `-m` list always stays exact/unpadded — dispatch and `--show-board` agree.
- `ensure_min_distinct_roles` moves duplicate-role seats behind a distinct-role prefix and repairs role-less seats, so a positional pool-N slice actually carries N distinct lenses.
- Does not lower `_DEFAULT_QUORUM_FLOOR`, change `DEFAULT_PRESET`, or pad to the full 11-seat board.

Tests: `tests/test_pool_guard.py` (21), `tests/test_pool_reuse.py` (29), `tests/test_reviewer_board.py` (152), `tests/test_run_stats.py` (181) — all green.

title: fix(stats): waive min_iter when role coverage meets the floor
body:
## What
`review task CODE --check` now passes when one padded iteration covers the role floor, even if `min_iter` is the default 3.

A 1-model pad records **one** iteration with 3 board roles. `quorum_check` still ANDed `min_iter=3`, so `passed` was false and agents fired `ship-review-quorum` hatch even though role coverage (the ship predicate, agent-tools#644 / #645) was already met.

When `min_roles` is set (bare `--check` default or explicit), role coverage waives `min_iter`. Model-only mode still requires `min_iter`. Explicit `--min-models` still ANDs. Zero-iteration records still fail.

## Why
Hatch flood: agents saw `--check passed=false` on a valid 1-model 3-role pad and requested Telegram hatch.

## Test
`test_quorum_check_one_model_three_role_pad_waives_min_iter` plus existing `quorum_check` suite (90 passed).

Refs #433

title: perf(dashboard): stop hot path scaling with full log corpus
body:
Stop the dashboard hot path paying O(total historical file count).

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/447
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/151
(Not closing either: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/426 merged and was not enough.)

## What changed
- Directory-mtime-gated **name-list cache** in `_scan_log_dir_entries`: if `os.stat(log_dir).st_mtime` is unchanged, reuse the last candidate name list; still `.stat()` the windowed subset (live-streaming invariant). APFS: append does not bump parent dir mtime; create/delete does. Listing cache ≠ TTL debounce.
- Bound `load_sessions` default parse to last **7 days** via filename-stamp window, matching `review stat --days`. `days<=0` = all history. Directory-relative anchor `min(newest_valid_stamp, now)` so 2026-06 fixtures stay inside the window.
- Wire `?days=` on `/api/runs` and `/api/stats` (frontend may omit; default 7).

Out of scope: log retention (https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/156), false-stopped status (https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/155).

## Measured 2026-09-08 against `~/Library/Logs/review-cli`

| Probe | Before (main / PR 426 windowing only) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| corpus | 154810 entries (148100 `.log`, 6706 `.md`) | same |
| `os.scandir` only | 0.70–1.19s | 0.11s (warm) |
| `_scan_log_dir_entries` 6h window, 1st call | 0.75–1.85s (5085 windowed / ~154806 total) | 0.44s |
| `_scan_log_dir_entries` 2nd call (unchanged dir, in-window file may grow) | 0.55s (still full scandir) | **0.12s** (name list reused; still sees size/mtime) |
| `load_sessions` (default) | hung / never returned over full corpus (`GET /api/runs?gap=90`) | **4.3s** (7-day window: 2870 sessions / 10939 calls) |
| `/api/health` | 2.02s contended, then 0.16s/0.02s | not re-hit; live process still on old code until restart |

Assignment-day numbers (cold-ish): scandir 0.702s; `_scan_log_dir_entries` 1.849s / 4634 windowed / total_count 154333; `/api/runs?gap=90` HUNG.

## Tests
`python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q -k 'scan_log_dir or load_sessions or fingerprint or snapshot_logs'` — 13 passed including new name-list cache + 7-day window tests and existing #151 windowing tests.

title: fix(backends,dashboard): recognize weekly/monthly limit-exhausted quota phrase (#339)
body:
## What
`_CHRONIC_QUOTA_MARKERS` (reviewlib/backends.py) and its dashboard-side copy `_SESSION_LIMIT_MARKERS` (reviewlib/dashboard/tokenstats.py) were missing the "Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted. Your limit will reset at <timestamp>" phrase a real production log showed a backend returning. `_chronic_unavailable_reason` never recognised it, so the seat kept being retried on every call instead of cooling down, and the dashboard Fable report miscounted the retry event as "other" instead of "session_limit".

Fixes review-cli#339. Also fixes review-cli#342 (the two marker tuples had drifted out of sync).

## Why anchored on the longer phrase
Codex review (round 1, from the original stale worktree review-cli-wt-limit-exhausted-marker) found that a naive bare `"limit exhausted"` marker also matches ordinary transient throttle wording ("429 rate limit exhausted; retry after 5 seconds", "retry limit exhausted") that must NOT be cached as an escalating chronic cooldown. The marker is anchored on the full `"...exhausted. your limit will reset"` phrase, which is specific to the real weekly/monthly quota-reset notice shape. This directly addresses the "may be a no-op" / wrong-anchor concern raised in review-cli#370.

## Testing
- `tests/test_tokenstats.py` (30 tests) — all pass, including the two new tests covering the dashboard classification.
- `tests/test_seat_cooldown.py` — 15 pre-existing failures reproduce **identically** on a clean, unmodified `origin/main` checkout (verified via `git checkout origin/main --detach` and re-running in isolation, same failures with or without this diff) — the same pre-existing-local-failure pattern already documented in review-cli#285. The two new tests this PR adds fail for the identical pre-existing reason (`review_claude` takes a different path on this host before ever reaching the cooldown-recording code the assertions exercise), not because of anything in this diff. CI should be authoritative here.

## Origin
Recovered from the stale worktree `review-cli-wt-limit-exhausted-marker` (branch `fix/quota-limit-exhausted-marker`), rebased cleanly onto current `origin/main`.

title: WIP: dashboard Metrics tab real token usage + cost tracking (#344, unresolved finding #369)
body:
## What
Adds real token usage / cost computation to the dashboard Metrics tab (parser.py, tokenstats.py, app.js) instead of a permanent empty state. Addresses review-cli#344.

## ⚠️ KNOWN UNRESOLVED FINDING — DO NOT MERGE YET (review-cli#369)
4 review rounds around 2026-09-01 (on the original stale worktree `review-cli-wt-metrics-token-cost`) flagged a **high-risk finding that this fix may silently under-report token cost and usage specifically on real large reviews**. That finding was never reproduced or resolved before the branch went stale.

Per review-cli#369's acceptance criteria, before this can ship:
- [ ] Reproduce the under-reporting against a real large-review run (confirm or rule out)
- [ ] If confirmed, fix the underlying cause (not paper over it) and add a regression test that would have caught it
- [ ] Re-review until the finding closes clean

This PR is opened as **WIP** to preserve the work (recovered from a stale worktree) rather than let it rot further or discard it outright — not as a claim that it's ready to merge.

## Testing so far
`tests/test_tokenstats.py` + `tests/test_dashboard.py` — 182 passed (rebased cleanly onto current `origin/main`). This does NOT cover the flagged large-review under-reporting scenario, which is exactly why review-cli#369 remains open.

title: feat(stats): close token overspend visibility gaps + 0% feedback fill-rate (#355)
body:
## Summary
Closes review-cli#355 (token overspend visibility gaps + 0% feedback fill-rate).

### 1. `review feedback <run_id>` — closes the 0% overseer-feedback fill-rate gap
Real usage showed `~/.config/review-cli/dashboard.json` had never once been written — `feedback`/`conscious`/`links` existed only as a dashboard web-UI action with no CLI path and no reminder anywhere. Every recorded run now prints a one-line stderr reminder (`[review] run recorded (run_id=...). Rate it: review feedback <run_id> --useful yes|no [...]`), and `review feedback` writes into the same annotation store the web UI reads.

- New `run_id` field (deterministic 64-bit digest from `ts`/`mode`/`task_code`) on every new run-stats.jsonl record.
- New tri-state `useful` rating alongside the existing `conscious`/`links` fields.
- Auto-links a run's `task_code` as a ticket when it already looks like one.
- `REVIEW_NO_FEEDBACK_NUDGE=1` silences the reminder for scripted/CI callers.
- Annotation store gained a cross-process advisory lock (`review feedback` made it a multi-process writer for the first time) and a single-load-modify-write `apply_feedback` (was up to 4 separate round-trips — a partial write was possible under contention).
- `/api/stats` gains `useful_count`.
- Known gap, tracked separately: review-cli#357 (a `review feedback` annotation isn't yet visible in the dashboard's own per-session drill-down — still counts toward the aggregate fill-rate signal).

### 2. `review stat`: mode/repo attribution + fail-bytes column
- New `by_mode`/`by_repo_top` sections (busiest mode/repo first), joined from `reviewlib.stats`'s ground-truth run-stats.jsonl store on top of the existing call-log-only report.
- New `FAIL%B` column on the per-harness table (`bytes_fail`/`bytes_fail_pct` in `--json`) — share of a harness's bytes spent on calls that failed anyway (retry-inflation cost signal).

## Testing
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_dashboard.py tests/test_feedback_subcommand.py tests/test_run_stats.py tests/test_stat_subcommand.py tests/test_tokenstats.py -q` — **417 passed, 3 failed**
- The 3 remaining failures (`test_cli_task_flag_overrides_review_task_code_env`, `test_cli_standalone_visual_does_not_record_review_task_code_env`, `test_cli_failover_backfill_records_actual_models_not_planned`) are **pre-existing on a clean `origin/main` checkout with zero diff applied** — confirmed by running the same tests against an unmodified `origin/main` worktree. Two are DEFAULT_BOARD composition drift (unrelated `#450`/`#382` board reshuffle since these tests were written) and one is a missing `PIL`/Pillow dependency on this host (test-only extra, not installed). Not introduced by, or related to, this diff.
- During rebase, found and fixed a real bug in this branch's own new tests: 3 `by_mode`/`by_repo_top` tests were reading an empty `run-stats.jsonl` because an autouse conftest fixture (`_isolate_log_and_stats_paths`) sets `$REVIEW_STATS_FILE` globally for every test, and the tests only overrode `$HOME` (which `stats_path()` doesn't fall back to when `$REVIEW_STATS_FILE` is set) — fixed by pointing `$REVIEW_STATS_FILE` at the seeded file directly.

Rebased onto current `main` (post #458). Version bumped to 0.37.3 (0.37.2 already claimed by PR #470, open concurrently).

Refs review-cli#355, review-cli#368 (cross-worktree dashboard-file-overlap warning; this is one of six worktrees it flagged — this one touches `cli.py`/`dashboard/server.py`/`dashboard/store.py`/`tokenstats.py`/`stats.py`, not the dashboard frontend files PR #470 touches).

title: feat(capacity-check): report confirmed fleet-wide provider exhaustion for gh ship's auto-bypass
body:
## What
Adds `reviewlib/capacity_check.py` (`board_capacity_report` / `seat_exhaustion_evidence`) and wires a new `review capacity-check [--preset NAME] [--json]` CLI subcommand that reports whether **every** seat on the currently active reviewer board is confirmed exhausted right now.

Combines two independent, each-sufficient evidence sources per seat:
- **Proactive:** `reviewlib.usage_limits` (harness 5h/7d usage windows at 100%) — claude/codex only.
- **Reactive:** `reviewlib.seat_cooldown`'s `active_cooldown` — a real recent dispatch to that model/access-method failed and got cooldown-recorded. This gives every OTHER provider real coverage too.

`all_exhausted` is `true` only when the board is non-empty and every distinct model has confirmed exhaustion evidence. A missing/unmapped/errored seat always reads as "not confirmed" — fail-open toward today's existing behavior, never toward silently skipping review.

## Why
This is Slice A of a coordinated two-repo change (agent-tools is Slice B). `gh ship`'s review-quorum / external-review self-merge hatch gates currently always prompt a human for a manual one-time Telegram hatch whenever their bar isn't met, even when the root cause is a confirmed fleet-wide review-cli provider outage that no single PR controls. Every PR across the fleet has been independently hitting this same manual prompt for the identical root cause. agent-tools' `ci/ship/ship.sh` will consult `review capacity-check --json`'s `all_exhausted` field before ever prompting for a manual hatch.

## Testing
- `tests/test_capacity_check.py` — 7 new unit/CLI-wiring tests, all passing.
- Real CLI smoke test (`python3 bin/review capacity-check --json` / plain text) run against this checkout's real board — output matches the documented contract shape.

Closes #472

title: fix(backends): pass true_silence_timeout to codex/omp/claude_cli backends (#474)
body:
## Problem

4 backend functions in `reviewlib/backends.py` called `_run_streamed` without `true_silence_timeout=`, causing 13-30min silent 0%-CPU hangs on stall (#474) (https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/474). `review_opencode` already forwarded it correctly.

## Fix

Each of the 4 call sites now passes `true_silence_timeout=true_silence_timeout_seconds(model)`, keyed by the full model-identifier string (e.g. `oc:zai/glm-5.2`, `claude:claude-fable-5`), mirroring `review_opencode`:

- `review_codex` (backends.py:390)
- `review_omp` (backends.py:1260)
- `review_claude_cli` (backends.py:3518)
- `review_claude_cli_with_images` (backends.py:3586)

## Tests

- New `tests/test_true_silence_backend_wiring.py`: 4 wiring tests (one per backend) asserting the forwarded kwarg is present, non-None, and equal to the real `model_behavior.true_silence_timeout_seconds(<model>)` return — verified to **fail pre-fix** (stash-revert check) and pass post-fix.
- Existing `_run_streamed` capture stubs with fixed signatures (`test_opencode_realrepo`, `test_omp_backend`, `test_claude_seat_robust`) extended to accept the new kwarg.
- 319 passed across the new file + `test_opencode_realrepo` / `test_omp_backend` / `test_streaming` / `test_true_silence_cooldown_wiring` / `test_claude_seat_robust` / `test_reviewer_board`.

title: feat(config): add omp-hosted Claude seat + account-level fallback (#168)
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/479

## Summary

Adds an omp-hosted Claude board seat plus account-level fallback across Alex's multiple Claude accounts (the 2026-09-09 hatch-request incident: one account's outage/paywall took out every `claude:*` seat at once).

- **New `OMP_CLAUDE_SEAT`** (`omp:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, display "Sonnet-omp") joins `DEFAULT_BOARD` at priority 7.5 with the `quality` role, directly after the direct-CLI Sonnet seat — the SAME claude-sonnet-5 model dispatched through the omp harness, a genuinely different auth path (omp's own credentials/profile-scoped agent dir vs the Claude Code CLI's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/keychain), so it survives an outage hitting every `claude:*` seat's shared account. Raw board 14 → 15 seats (default/light 12 → 13, heavy 13 → 14); `ROLE_FALLBACK_MODELS["quality"]` gains `claude-sonnet-5-omp` as its third fallback.
- **Account rotation** (`reviewlib/claude_accounts.py`, new): discovers the registry `claude-rotate`/harness-cli already use (`~/.claude-accounts/account-*/`, `$CLAUDE_ROTATE_ROOT` override, `current` state file) and walks it in wrap-around rotation order, current account first. `review_claude`'s CLI transport rotates `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per dispatch via a fresh per-call env dict (never a global `os.environ` mutation — seats dispatch concurrently); the omp-hosted Claude seat rotates `--profile` across `$REVIEW_OMP_CLAUDE_PROFILES`. An account whose own harness 5h/7d window is exhausted is skipped pre-dispatch; a chronic-unavailable result falls through to the next account; only when EVERY configured account is exhausted does the run emit the synthetic usage-limit skip, now naming every account it tried. No registry → exactly one implicit candidate, byte-identical to before.
- **`usage_limits` `account=` scoping axis**: `usage_percent_for_model` / `allow_spawn_for_model` / `spawn_refuse_reason` accept keyword-only `account` (email, case/whitespace-normalized); only harness cards for THAT account gate the result. `account=None` keeps the old aggregate behavior for every existing caller.
- **Fix (pre-existing, surfaced by this work)**: `review_codex` passes `--skip-git-repo-check` only when `-C` isn't a git work tree (codex refused non-repo dirs outright, e.g. omp-cage sandboxes).

Internal tracker IDs #168/#169/#170 (the hatch-request incident family's own numbering) happen to collide with older, unrelated test-flake GitHub issues in this repo's issue namespace — the actual tracking issue for this feature is linked at the top of this description (issue 479).

## Rebase warning for #475 (ResumeReviewCliHangFix)

This branch makes substantial changes to `reviewlib/backends.py` functions `review_codex`, `review_omp`, `review_claude`, `review_claude_cli` — new helpers (`_cwd_is_git_repo`, `_review_omp_once`, `_review_omp_with_account_fallback`, `_review_claude_cli_with_account_fallback`, `_claude_account_candidates`, `_omp_model_hosts_claude`, `_review_omp_claude_profiles`) plus control-flow restructuring (the direct dispatch bodies moved into `_review_omp_once`; `review_claude`'s API/CLI split restructured around the account-fallback loop; `review_claude_cli` gained a `config_dir` kwarg). #475 wires `true_silence_timeout_seconds` into the same four functions' existing `_run_streamed` calls (no new functions, no control-flow restructuring), so whichever of the two merges second will likely need a rebase — reviewers, please check.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_claude_accounts.py` (16 tests): registry discovery, `current` state, oauth email extraction, rotation wrap order, `$CLAUDE_ROTATE_ROOT` override — hermetic temp-dir registries, no network/subprocess.
- New `tests/test_account_rotation.py` (15 tests): the rotation loops provably skip an exhausted/chronic account and try the next in rotation order — for both the direct `claude:*` CLI loop (incl. the end-to-end #170 incident shape through the real `review_claude`) and the omp `--profile` loop. Fake chronic results pinned against the real `_chronic_unavailable_reason` detector.
- Fixed branch-caused suite breakage the earlier workers hadn't caught: `tests/test_failover_pool.py` pre-#382 reconstruction sets + light-preset reserve pin updated for the 15th seat, and `tests/test_run_stats.py`'s board helpers now neutralize the live usage-limit signal (this incidentally also makes the machine-state flake in issue 352 deterministic).

title: fix(backends): wire true-silence timeout + cooldown into review_omp (review-cli#235)
body:
## Summary

Closes the omp half of review-cli#235: wires `true_silence_timeout_seconds(model)` and a seat cooldown into `review_omp` (`reviewlib/backends.py`), mirroring the wiring `review_opencode` already had.

Before this change, a hung omp seat (zero output, 0% CPU) ran to the full wall-clock timeout on *every single call*, with no true-silence reap and no escalating cooldown to bench a chronically-hanging seat.

## Why this matters -- two real-world hangs, one root cause

- `BlockOsascriptTcc` hit a 44-minute zero-output hang on an `omp:opencode-go` seat.
- `FixAcpTimeoutRecurrence` hit a 13-minute hang on `-m mimo` alone.

These look like two unrelated incidents, but `MIMO_SEAT = "omp:opencode-go/mimo-v2.5"` (`reviewlib/config.py:106`) **is itself an omp seat** -- both hangs went through the exact same `review_omp` code path that was missing this wiring. This one fix addresses both.

## Changes

- **`reviewlib/backends.py`**
  - Add `_OMP_ACCESS_METHOD = "omp"` (mirrors `_OPENCODE_ACCESS_METHOD`) -- omp's read-only agentic seat is a distinct failure domain from claude's `"cli"` transport, so it gets its own cooldown namespace.
  - Generalize `_record_true_silence_if_needed(model, proc, *, access_method)` (previously hardcoded to opencode's access method in three places) so any backend can share it.
  - Update `review_opencode`'s two existing call sites to pass `access_method=_OPENCODE_ACCESS_METHOD` explicitly.
  - `review_omp` now:
    - consults an active cooldown *before* `resolve_backend_mode`/`_which`/preflight (mirrors `review_opencode`'s own pre-check ordering, so a cooling-down seat skips all real work);
    - passes `true_silence_timeout=true_silence_timeout_seconds(model)` into `_run_streamed`;
    - records/clears the cooldown after the call via `_record_true_silence_if_needed(model, proc, access_method=_OMP_ACCESS_METHOD)`.
- **`reviewlib/model_behavior.py`**: corrected the module comment -- the mechanism is now wired into `review_opencode` **and** `review_omp` (2 of #235's backend call sites); `review_codex`, `review_claude`/`review_claude_api`/`review_claude_cli(+with_images)`, `review_gemini`, `review_zai`, `review_commandcode`, `review_openrouter` remain tracked, not done yet.
- **`tests/test_omp_backend.py`**: `_Captured.__call__` now accepts (and captures) `true_silence_timeout` -- every existing test using `_capture_omp()` would otherwise `TypeError` once `review_omp` passes that kwarg for real.
- **`tests/test_true_silence_cooldown_wiring.py`**: updated the 9 direct `_record_true_silence_if_needed(...)` test call sites for the new required `access_method` kwarg.
- **`tests/test_omp_true_silence_cooldown_wiring.py`** (new): mirrors the opencode wiring test file for `review_omp`:
  - a wiring test (true-silence reap records a cooldown, with the correct per-model timeout reaching `_run_streamed`);
  - the cooldown is actually consulted on the very next call (dispatch skipped entirely);
  - a negative control (an ordinary success records nothing);
  - **the acceptance-criterion test**: drives `review_omp` end-to-end against the REAL, unstubbed `reviewlib.process._run_streamed`, with a real subprocess that never writes a byte and a 1s true-silence budget. Proves termination fires well within budget (not a 60s hang), the result is a clean `rc=125` / `TRUE-SILENCE` failure (not an exception or an indefinite hang), and the omp cooldown is actually recorded.
  - Registered in `tests/smoke.py`'s `_UNIT_FILES` (required by `test_every_unit_file_is_run`).

## Verification

- `tests/test_omp_backend.py`, `tests/test_true_silence_cooldown_wiring.py`, `tests/test_opencode_realrepo.py`, and the new `tests/test_omp_true_silence_cooldown_wiring.py` all pass.
- Adversarially verified the new acceptance test is meaningful: temporarily reverting the `true_silence_timeout` wiring reproduces the OLD behavior exactly (runs to the ordinary wall-clock timeout, `rc=124`, no `TRUE-SILENCE` marker) -- confirming the test genuinely distinguishes "fix present" from "fix absent", not a vacuous pass.
- Full `python tests/smoke.py` is green except one pre-existing, unrelated flake (`test_dashboard_managed_surface_and_lib_absent_fallback`, a dashboard managed-service exit-code check unrelated to omp/true-silence) that reproduces **identically** on an untouched `main` checkout -- confirmed not caused by this change.

Refs review-cli#235

title: fix(stats): seat-granular role credit survives a sibling's hard failure (review-cli#137)
body:
## Summary

Fixes an adjacent, narrower gap in the same "what should count as a role credit" area as review-cli#137 (does **not** Refs #137's own two open acceptance criteria -- see below).

Alex hit this concretely: Opus review OK; Codex/GLM/Grok/Sonnet quota-exhausted -> could not record 3 review iterations. Root cause: an exact `-m modelA,modelB,modelC,...` board (no reserve to backfill a failed seat) records per-seat role data (`roles`), but `_run_mode_with_stats`'s `passed` is the WHOLE run's own all-or-nothing verdict, and `quorum_check` only ever read `roles` from a `passed is True` record -- so ONE hard-failed sibling seat (nonzero returncode from a quota-exhausted provider) zeroed out role credit for the ENTIRE iteration, including a seat (e.g. Opus) that genuinely produced a verdict.

## Fix

Role credit is now SEAT-granular while `passed`/`--min-iter`/`--min-models` stay exactly as they are today (still run-level, all-or-nothing):

- `record_run` gains a new `usable_roles` param -- the roles of seats that INDIVIDUALLY produced a usable verdict this run (`panel.FailoverOutcome.usable_roles`), written regardless of the run's own `passed`. No `models`-length-alignment requirement (unlike the existing `roles` field).
- `cli._run_mode_with_stats` threads a new `usable_roles_after` callable (mirroring `models_after`/`roles_after`), wired in `_dispatch` to `outcome_sink[0].usable_roles` for the review/visual board path -- the SAME source the existing non-exact (reserve-failover) `roles_after` already reads, with no exact-board special case needed.
- `stats.quorum_check`'s `--min-roles` gate credits from a new `_seat_credited_roles` helper: reads `usable_roles` when present (falling back to the legacy passed-only `roles` reading for pre-fix records), across every non-diff-identity-mismatched iteration regardless of that iteration's own `passed`.
- Regression tests: a 3-seat run (1 usable/correctness, 2 quota-exhausted) now credits "correctness" toward `--min-roles` despite `passed=False` for the whole run. Two pre-existing exact-board tests (`..._review_cli_221`) that pinned the old all-or-nothing behavior are rewritten to `..._review_cli_137` and now assert the fixed behavior, plus `min_models` staying unaffected.

## Not in scope (review-cli#137's own open questions)

This PR does **not** decide either of review-cli#137's own acceptance criteria, which remain open:
1. Whether non-review modes (brainstorm/quorum/just-ask) should count toward the self-merge-authority gate at all.
2. Review mode's free-text content-verdict gap (ran cleanly vs. approved-with-no-findings).

See review-cli#137 for that discussion and the plan comment posted there before this PR.

## Testing

`pytest tests/test_run_stats.py -q` -- 194 passed. 3 pre-existing failures (`test_cli_task_flag_overrides_review_task_code_env`, `test_cli_standalone_visual_does_not_record_review_task_code_env` [missing PIL], `test_cli_failover_backfill_records_actual_models_not_planned`) reproduce identically on an untouched `origin/main` checkout (verified via `git stash`) -- unrelated environment/config drift, not caused by this change.

Version bumped 0.37.3 -> 0.37.4 with a CHANGELOG entry.

title: feat(specweb): version history + compare view (review-cli#484 item 2)
body:
## What

Implements item 2 of review-cli#484 ("Version history & compare") — the only remaining
open item from that ticket; items 1/3/4/5 already shipped via #485 (separate, unrelated
branch).

Per the ticket's design sketch (git log/git show explicitly rejected — specs aren't
always in a git repo and reviewers often have uncommitted edits):

- **Snapshot mechanism** (store.py): `SpecStore.maybe_snapshot(text, mtime)` captures a
  version whenever the server detects the spec's on-disk text differs from the last
  recorded snapshot. Dedupe is on **text alone** — a byte-identical re-save (mtime bumped,
  body unchanged) is a no-op — and deliberately does **not** also gate on mtime: mtime-
  preserving tooling (`git checkout`/`cp -p`) or coarse filesystem mtime resolution can
  leave a real content change under an unchanged mtime, and gating on it would silently
  drop that revision from history (an earlier draft of this PR had that bug; caught by
  review, see "Review fixes" below). Capped at `MAX_SPEC_VERSIONS` (50) per spec, oldest
  dropped first. `list_versions()` returns lightweight summaries (no full text);
  `get_version(id)` returns one full record.
- **render.py**: extracted `render_markdown(text, ...)` from `render_spec` so a historical
  version's stored text can be rendered without touching disk (`render_spec` is now a thin
  wrapper: resolve path, read, delegate — same public behavior).
- **3 new read-only routes** (server.py):
  - `GET /api/spec/versions` — version list (summaries, newest-first)
  - `GET /api/spec/versions/<id>` — one snapshot's rendered HTML (`id="live"` reserved for
    the current on-disk text, so a snapshot can always be compared against "now")
  - `GET /api/spec/versions/compare?a=<id>&b=<id>` — stdlib `difflib` LINE-level diff (a
    whole-document word-level diff would be O(n·m) — too slow for a large spec)
  - Snapshot capture is wired into `_serve_spec_json` (hit on initial load AND every
    SSE-triggered live-reload re-fetch), with **stat-read-stat**: the mtime is read before
    and after the file read and the attempt is dropped if they disagree, so a snapshot
    never pairs mismatched text/mtime from a concurrent edit. The whole capture path is
    wrapped to never raise — a snapshot failure must not break `/api/spec` rendering.
    Existing live-reload/SSE behavior is unchanged.
- **UI** (static/): a "History" button in the topbar opens a modal (matching the existing
  `composer-backdrop` dialog pattern) listing versions with real dates/sizes, two selects
  (compare from/to, defaulting to the most recent SNAPSHOT vs "Live (current)" — i.e. "what
  changed since my last save") and a Compare button rendering the server-computed diff with
  `+`/`-` line styling reusing the existing `--danger`/`--answered` color vars. `app.js`
  matches the file's existing ES5-ish vanilla-JS style (`var`/`function`, no template
  literals).

## Review fixes

A multi-model review pass (`review diff --staged`) on the first draft caught two real bugs,
both fixed in this PR:

1. **Data-loss bug**: the original snapshot dedupe was `mtime == last.mtime OR text ==
   last.text -> skip`, requiring BOTH to differ to capture. That silently dropped a
   genuine content change whenever its mtime happened to equal the prior snapshot's (coarse
   mtime resolution, `git checkout`/`cp -p` preserving mtimes, two edits in the same
   second). Fixed to dedupe on text alone; the previously-passing test that pinned the old
   (wrong) behavior was inverted to assert the correct one.
2. **Wrong default compare pair**: `app.js` defaulted "compare from" to
   `opts[opts.length - 2]`, which — since the version list is newest-first — is the
   **oldest** stored snapshot, not the most recent one. A reviewer opening History on a
   spec with a long session would see a noisy full-history diff by default instead of
   "what changed since my last save". Fixed to default to the newest snapshot.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_specweb.py` → **105 passed** (added coverage: snapshot
  dedupe-on-text-alone semantics including the mtime-collision case, cap/eviction,
  `list_versions`/`get_version` shape, the 3 new HTTP routes including 400/404 paths, the
  `render_spec`/`render_markdown` round-trip, and an end-to-end `/api/spec` snapshot-capture
  test against a temp spec file).
- Manual smoke test against the **real** `review spec-web` CLI daemon (an isolated instance
  on a private port/store dir, started via `review spec-web __serve`, spec registered via
  the same `registry.register` `add` uses — the machine's shared production spec-web
  daemon at :7920 was left completely untouched throughout, including its own registered

title: feat(list): work outside a repo; group task list by project + session fallback
body:
## What

Make `task`'s read/list/global ops work **outside any git repo**, and turn `task list` into a cross-project, session-aware view. Implements two ROADMAP items:

- *Commands should work OUTSIDE a repo; task list groups by repo/project*
- *task list: fallback to all-tasks + session-vs-all messaging*

## Behavior

- **`task list` outside any repo** → ALL tasks across the registered projects, **grouped by project** (a heading per project, tickets beneath). A project whose backend errors is shown as a **degraded group**; it never aborts the aggregation.
- **`task list` inside a repo** → session scope, **falling back** to all of that repo's tickets (with a `showing all project tasks` line) when there's no agent session or the session has no tickets. **`--all`** gives the grouped cross-project view from anywhere.
- **`task read` / `status` / `find`** work outside a repo: an id is routed to a registered project (Linear `HYP-3` by team; `#123` when exactly one GitHub project is registered); an ambiguous id fails with a clear 3-part error.
- **Only `task create` is repo-bound** → a 3-part WHAT/WHY/HOW error outside a repo (honest HOW: `--repo owner/name` for GitHub, `linear.team` for Linear).

## Design (brainstormed, then reviewed)

A new pure `tasklib/projects.py` models the `projects:` registry (in the config cascade, usually the global `~/.config/task-cli/config.yaml`). Each entry becomes a config **overlay** that the existing `get_backend()` resolves unchanged — zero backend special-casing. Projects dedup by backend **coordinate** (repo/team), not display name. The multi-backend fan-out is an effect and lives in `cli.py`. `LoadedConfig.with_overlay()` is the new (immutable) seam.

`_current_project_overlay` returns `None` ONLY when genuinely outside a git work tree; a broken in-repo `origin` surfaces its real error instead of masquerading as "no projects". Linear `list`/`search` now scope to the backend's team (and project, if pinned) so the cross-project view doesn't double-count or leak workspace-wide hits.

## Acceptance evidence

`task list` outside any repo, registry of 3 projects (one Linear group degraded on auth):

```
$ task list   # OUTSIDE any git repo
showing all project tasks (`task list` defaults to tasks created in the agent session)
web-app · github-issues · 2
  #142 [in-progress] Fix login redirect
  #139 [todo] Upgrade Node 20

api · github-issues · 1
  #88 [todo] Rate-limit /search

HYP · linear · degraded
  ! linear: no team with key 'HYP' (run linear auth)
```

3-part errors outside a repo (no traceback, exit 2):

```
$ task list           → error: no projects to list. You are outside a git repo …  (why/fix)
$ task create …       → error: cannot create a ticket: no project context …  (why/fix: --repo owner/name)
$ task read #5        → error: cannot resolve which project ticket '#5' belongs to …
```

## Tests

`160 passed` (pytest) + `tests/smoke.sh` green (adds an outside-a-repo clean-degradation check). New/extended:

- `tests/test_projects.py` — registry parsing, coordinate dedup, hostile input.
- `tests/test_cli_non_repo.py` — grouped list, degraded groups, JSON shape, id routing (GitHub single / ambiguous / Linear-by-team / two-same-team), session fallback, current marker (incl. repo-in-registry), broken-remote-surfaces-error, 3-part errors (GitHub + Linear).
- `tests/test_cli.py` — `--label` filters the session view; a filter that excludes all session tickets does NOT fall back (no cross-session leak).
- `tests/test_backends.py` — Linear `list` team+project filter; `search` team scoping.

## Review

Reviewed across models via `review --staged` (3 rounds). All P1/P2 correctness findings addressed and regression-tested (filter-before-fallback leak, Linear same-team routing, current-marker-when-registered, swallowed remote error). Remaining findings are subjective style/refactor — declined per smallest-change.

title: feat(list): page list/find like git (interactive-only) + higher TTY limit
body:
## What

Adds the **pagination** half of two ROADMAP items:
- "Commands should work OUTSIDE a repo; task list groups by repo/project"
- "task list: fallback to all-tasks + pagination + session-vs-all messaging"
- (refinement) "task list pager: interactive-only + higher limit there"

The outside-repo / grouping / session-fallback / session-vs-all messaging shipped in #5. This PR fills the remaining gap: the **pager** and the **interactive-vs-piped result limit**.

## Behavior (git's pager model)

- Human (non-`--json`) `list`/`find` output pages through `less` **only when stdout is an interactive TTY**; piped/scripted output is plain text (scriptable). Short output that fits one screen prints directly (`less -F`).
- Result cap follows interactivity: **100** in a terminal (the pager scrolls), **30** when piped, unless an explicit `-n N` is given (which always wins).
- Opt out with `--no-pager`, `NO_PAGER` (any non-empty value), or an empty `$PAGER`/`$TASK_PAGER` (git's "cat, don't page"). Pager resolves `$TASK_PAGER` → `$PAGER` → `less` → `more`; `$LESS` defaults to `FRX` unless the user set it.
- `--json` is **never** paged (machine-readable stays un-paged, un-decorated).

## Implementation

- New `tasklib/pager.py`: a pure `should_page` decision and a defensive `page()` that pipes through the pager and falls back to a direct write on any failure. The pipe is forced **utf-8** (ticket titles can be non-ASCII; a locale-encoding crash would otherwise escape and kill the list). stdin is always closed in `finally` so the pager sees EOF.
- `cli._emit_list` is the single call site; `_format_tickets` / `_format_groups` now return strings (were direct prints) so output can be routed; JSON paths print straight to stdout.
- `_effective_limit` picks the cap by interactivity; the `-n` default is `None` so an explicit value is distinguishable.

## Tests

- `tests/test_pager.py` — decision + routing against a **real child-process pager** (`$TASK_PAGER`): utf-8 non-ASCII, broken-pipe / non-zero-exit / missing-binary fallbacks, `$LESS=FRX` seeding (and not overriding a user `$LESS`), empty / whitespace pager, closed-stream `isatty`.
- `tests/test_list_pager.py` + `tests/test_cli_non_repo.py` — `cmd_list`/`cmd_find` wiring: interactive paging, **piped-not-paged-even-with-pager-configured**, `--no-pager`, `NO_PAGER`, `--json` never paged, explicit `-n` flows into the backend, grouped (cross-project) paging on a TTY, no double-emit to stdout.
- 201 tests pass; smoke green.

Docs: README pagination section, AGENTS.md rule, install.py SKILL_MD.

Reviewed pre-commit via `review diff --staged` (glm). Two real bugs the review caught were fixed: utf-8 pipe encoding (was `text=True` → locale crash) and stdin-close-on-write-failure (FD/EOF).

title: feat(config): config-driven tracker backend via rig.yaml task: block
body:
## What

Wires task-cli's tracker backend selection to be **config-driven from the repo's `rig.yaml`** (CTO decision #4136.4: "for hyperide a LOCAL rig.yaml setting -> Linear, default -> GitHub Issues").

task-cli now reads its per-repo tracker backend from a flat `task:` block in the repo's committed `rig.yaml` — the single source of truth for the agent toolchain:

```yaml
# rig.yaml (repo root)
task:
  backend: linear      # or github-issues (the default for every other repo)
  team: HYP            # -> linear.team
  # project: ""        # -> linear.project
  # repo: owner/name   # -> github.repo
```

## Design

- **DEFAULT = GitHub Issues.** No `task:` block (or no `rig.yaml`) -> clean fall-through to `github-issues`.
- **Cascade** (later wins): defaults -> global -> `rig.yaml` task: -> `task.yaml` -> `--config`. A repo keeping a native `task.yaml` is untouched (it still wins over `rig.yaml`).
- **Flat block translated** to task-cli's own shape: `team`/`project`/`repo` are shorthands; full `github:`/`linear:`/`enforce:`/`classify:`/`session:`/`projects:` sections may be nested verbatim and **deep-merge** with the shorthands (order-independent; a true leaf collision is a hard error).
- **Forward-compatible with rig-cli** (rig.yaml is a foreign file rig owns/evolves):
  - a parse error or non-mapping root falls through to the github default (logged, never fatal);
  - an unknown sub-key under `task:` is warned-and-ignored, not a crash;
  - `version` is not passed through (rig.yaml has its own top-level version);
  - `validate()` type-guards a non-string `backend` into a clean `ConfigError` instead of an unhashable-type `TypeError` on foreign input.

## Tests

`tests/test_config.py`: default=github, rig.yaml override=linear, missing/inert/broken/non-mapping rig.yaml=github, flat+nested merge for both linear and github (both orders), leaf-conflict rejected, unknown-key and stray `version` tolerated, malformed `backend` -> clean error. `tests/smoke.sh` covers the end-to-end `rig.yaml -> linear/HYP` selection. Full suite: 223 passing.

Reviewed across models before commit (review-before-commit gate); GLM seat was throttled (429) throughout, so the diff was reviewed on the Opus correctness seat across three rounds — each round's findings fixed (data-loss on flat+nested mix, forward-compat for unknown keys, foreign-file tolerance, non-string backend guard).

## Problem

`task install-skill` writes `~/.agents/skills/task/SKILL.md` but never the

title: test(docker): real-agent integration harness — task-cli advertised + usable on a fresh machine
body:
## What

A hermetic, Docker-based integration test proving end-to-end that `task` works on a fresh machine. A container provisions `task` via the **real** install path (`install.sh` → `task install-skill`), lays down a special test repo with a trivial feature request, and asserts task-cli is:

- **ADVERTISED** — a fresh agent discovers `task`: the real `install-skill` wrote `SKILL.md` + the SessionStart blurb, and the SessionStart hook surfaces the `task` blurb into a new session.
- **USABLE** — `task new`/`task list`/`task read` round-trip through the **real** github-issues backend code path (stdlib `urllib` → REST) against a hermetic mock GitHub server.

> Scope (CTO, tg#4580): **no commit-gate assertion** — only *advertised* + *usable*.

Closes #15. Follow-up tracked in #16.

## Harness (`test/docker/`)

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `mock_github.py` | stdlib-only in-memory mock of the GitHub Issues REST endpoints the backend calls — `task new`/`list` exercise the REAL backend with no token/network. |
| `Dockerfile` | the "fresh machine": installs `task` the real way, wires the same SessionStart blurb hook a real Claude Code machine runs, builds the test repo + hermetic-backend env. |
| `assertions.sh` | the **deterministic (no-LLM)** leg — advertised + usable. |
| `agent_test.sh` | the **gated real-cheap-agent** leg (`claude -p`, `claude-haiku-4-5`). |
| `entrypoint.sh` | starts the mock, runs the deterministic leg always, the agent leg iff the key is present (else skips with a clear message). |

## Cheap agent + model

`claude -p` with **`claude-haiku-4-5`** (cheapest viable), gated behind the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` CI secret; the agent is un-caged **inside the throwaway container only** (`--allowedTools Bash`).

## CI (`test-cli` job)

- **Deterministic `smoke` leg** — runs on every PR **and** on push-to-main; the blocking gate.
- **`real-agent` leg** — runs on the **post-merge push to main** (the faithful "a PR merged" signal, since this repo squash-merges via `gh ship`; `merge_group` would need a queue this repo doesn't use). Gated behind the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret (skip-with-message when absent) and **`continue-on-error`** until hardened (see below).

## Deterministic vs credentialed-merge-gated

- **Deterministic (normal CI, no key):** SKILL.md + blurb written by the real install; the SessionStart hook surfaces `task`; `task new`/`list`/`read` succeed against the mock backend. **Verified locally** (`docker build` + the leg, exit 0).
- **Credentialed (merge):** the full real-haiku verification, gated behind the secret.

## Assertions

ADVERTISED: `SKILL.md` present w/ trigger frontmatter; blurb present; the SessionStart hook output advertises `task`. USABLE: `task new` creates a ticket via the real backend (id #1, mock URL); `task list` reads it back (session-scoped); `task read` returns the full body. Real-agent: did NOT use raw `gh issue create` (gh shimmed to record the attempt); created a task-shaped ticket in the backend; summary references `task`.

## Enabling backend seam

`github_issues.py`: `_api_root()` honors `GITHUB_API_URL` (the same env `gh`/octokit read — a real GHE need, not test-only), read per-call so an env set after import takes effect. **Security:** a non-loopback host must be `https` — the bearer token rides every request, so an ambient `GITHUB_API_URL` cannot exfiltrate the token over cleartext. Covered by new unit tests (250 pass).

## Deferred (tracked, #16)

The real-agent leg is the **tracked next increment**, not yet a proven gate: run against a live haiku, the agent correctly avoids raw `gh issue` and references `task`, but a cheap model tends to resolve the harness's own built-in to-do/task tool (`TodoWrite`/`TaskCreate`) over the advertised `task` CLI, so the ticket doesn't land in the backend. Hardening (precise built-in disablement + a collision-proof prompt + a live-key validation) + flipping `continue-on-error` off is #16.

title: fix(cli): validate transition legality on all three close paths (#10)
body:
## What

`task done <id>`, `task change <id> --done`, and `task status <id> done` all pushed a ticket to `State.DONE` without checking whether its CURRENT state legally permitted the move. So `task done` on an already-cancelled ticket silently re-closed it (re-ran `update()` + re-fired `_attach_screenshots`), and a double-close re-wrote a ticket already in `done`. The audit trail then lied about the lifecycle. (Issue #10, surfaced by the review-gate on the PR for #8.)

## How

- New `tasklib/transitions.py`: ONE explicit `LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` table + ONE shared `validate_transition(current, target, *, force)` helper that all three close paths (and the general `status` transition) consult — DRY, the legality lives in one place.
- `cancelled` is a deliberate dead-end (empty row): nothing leaves it without `--force`, so a deliberately-cancelled ticket is never silently revived. A same-state re-entry (`done -> done`) is absent from every row, so a double-close is rejected as a no-op re-write rather than re-firing side effects.
- An illegal move raises `TransitionError` -> the top-level handler renders a clean three-part `error:` line and returns the structured exit code (the shared `agenttools_errors` `EXIT_USAGE` class, `2`), never a traceback or a silent re-write.
- New `--force` flag on `done` / `change` / `status` — the explicit override the acceptance criteria require (e.g. deliberately reopen a cancelled ticket).
- In `cmd_change` the legality check runs immediately after `backend.get()`, **before any edit**, so an illegal `change --done` leaves the fetched ticket undirtied and fires no attachment.
- The exit code is hard-coded to the literal `2` (the `agenttools_errors` contract value) rather than imported, so `task --help` stays stdlib-only at import time; a test pins it to `agenttools_errors.EXIT_USAGE` when the lib is present, and the import-time smoke check now guards against an `agenttools_errors` leak.

## Tests (RED-first)

- Each illegal transition (`cancelled -> done`, `done -> done`) rejected via EACH of the three close paths, with the clear error + exit 2, and the ticket left unchanged.
- The legal `todo -> done` path still works on all three verbs.
- `--force` overrides on `done`, `change --done`, and `status`.
- The read-only `task status <id>` (no new-state) path never reaches the validator.
- An illegal `change --done --screenshot --title --label` fires no attachment and leaves the fetched ticket fully undirtied.
- Unit tests on the table + validator in isolation (exhaustive table, same-state for every state, force bypass, exit-code contract pin).

Full suite: 265 passed, 1 skipped (the `agenttools_errors` contract-pin test, lib not installed in CI's env). Ruff clean. Smoke green. Review-gate: claude-opus-4-8 `[ok]` (after two rounds addressing findings; codex fallback used once mid-throttle).

## Skipped gates

- screenshots: CLI/logic change, no UI surface.

Closes #10

title: test(docker): harden real-agent leg vs task-tool collision + assert require-ticket enforcement
body:
## What

Two improvements to the task-cli Docker `test-cli` harness (`test/docker/`), from #17.

### (1) Harden the gated real-agent leg — Closes #16

A cheap model (haiku) resolved its **built-in** `TodoWrite`/`TaskCreate`/`Task` tool over the advertised `task` CLI (the "task" name collision), so no ticket landed in the backend. Fixes:

- **Tool gating** extracted to `agent_tools_gating.sh` (single source of truth): canonical `--disallowedTools TodoWrite TaskCreate Task` (space-separated, per `claude --help`) + `--allowedTools Bash Read`; plus `--tools "Bash,Read"` (comma form — a different documented delimiter) added **only when `claude --help` advertises `--tools`** (anchored match, so a substring / `--tools-foo` can't falsely enable it and break the invocation).
- **Collision-proof prompt**: names the affordance concretely (run the `task` SHELL command via Bash) and forbids any built-in todo/task/scratchpad tool — without spelling out the subcommand (discovery still comes from the advertised skill/blurb).
- The **key-free gating config self-check** now runs in the **deterministic leg** (entrypoint step 2c, `agent_tools_gating.sh --check`), not hidden behind the credentialed + `continue-on-error` agent leg — so a regression that un-gates a built-in **fails a normal PR with no key**.

The leg stays **gated + `continue-on-error`** pending a recorded live-key run (the live flag-parse semantics and a reliable ticket-landing run remain on #16 — see the issue comment for the open items).

### (2) Require-ticket enforcement assertion in the deterministic leg — Closes #19

Now that `require-ticket-before-commit` is strict + rig-provisioned (agent-tools#95), `enforce_test.sh` vendors the canonical hook and proves end-to-end against a hermetic neutral-branch fixture (no LLM, runs on every PR):

- ticketless commit → **BLOCKED** (exit 10 + the stable `[require-ticket] BLOCKED: no ticket reference` marker)
- `Closes #1` / `task #1` commit → **ALLOWED** (exit 0, no marker)
- exempt `chore:` commit → **ALLOWED** without a ticket (no over-block)
- a ticketed commit is well-formed and **lands** in the fixture repo

## How disabled the built-in collision

title: feat(daemon): due-date reminder daemon + --due field
body:
## What

The minimal shippable core of the task-cli daemon epic (#2/#3): a `task daemon` subcommand group + a background watcher that polls the backend for open tickets whose due date is overdue or due-soon and pushes a reminder to the CTO's channel.

### Lifecycle (mirrors tg-ctl's shape, not its code)
- `task daemon start` — spawn the detached daemon (new session); idempotent via pid-file + `kill(0)` liveness, never double-starts; clears a stale pid-file and respawns; forwards `--backend`/`--repo`/`--config` to the child so it resolves the SAME coordinate.
- `task daemon stop` — SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL on timeout, clear the pid-file.
- `task daemon status` — running / stale / stopped + pid + config (`--json` too).
- `task daemon run` — the foreground loop `start` spawns; honors `daemon.enabled`.

### Due dates (backend-portable)
A `--due YYYY-MM-DD` flag on `new`/`create` and `change`, stored as an optional `## Due` body section that round-trips through render/parse for BOTH backends (kept OUT of the fixed `SECTIONS` so every pre-existing ticket still passes the formatting gate). Linear also mirrors it into the native `dueDate` (clearing sends `null`).

### Safety
Fail-soft end to end: a backend error / malformed ticket / down notifier in one tick is caught, logged, and the loop continues. De-dupe keyed on (ticket id → due date last notified); a changed due date re-fires; the state file is pruned each tick to currently-due ids and written atomically, so it can't grow unbounded. One daemon per repo coordinate.

### Config
A `daemon:` block: `interval_s`, `due_soon_days`, `query_limit`, `notifier`, `enabled` (normalizes a quoted `"false"`). README + `--help` updated.

## Tests
59 new tests (daemon selection/de-dupe/fail-soft/lifecycle, `--due` round-trip, Linear native dueDate, CLI dispatch). Full suite: **335 passed, 1 skipped**. Ruff clean. Version bumped 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 (minor, new feature).

- Purely a **view** — no mutation. Output paged like `list` (interactive); `--json` never paged.

## Design
- Pure, testable core in `tasklib/gantt.py`: window auto-fit, proportional column mapping, overdue derivation, the dated/undated split. The renderer takes a `color(code, s)` callback so a plain-text (identity) render is asserted deterministically — tests check **integer geometry**, not raw ANSI.
- CLI wiring in `cli.py` reuses the existing `list` scoping (`_known_projects` / `_aggregate_projects` / session fallback) so `gantt` and `list` never drift on what "this session" means.
- Control chars / ANSI in titles are flattened (`_truncate` + `isprintable()`) so a malicious/multiline title can't break the fixed-width grid or leak an escape.

title: fix(render): align columns by terminal display width, not code-point count (#29)
body:
## What
Fixes column alignment in task-cli's render paths: padding/truncation counted Unicode **code points** (`len`, `str.ljust`, slicing) instead of terminal **cells**. A CJK ideograph / wide emoji is 2 cells but 1 code point; a combining mark / ZWJ is 0 cells but 1 — so a wide-char ticket title over/under-fills its column and shears the `task gantt` grid (the one render path with padded columns; `list`/`read` are free-flow).

## How
- New stdlib-only helper `tasklib/textwidth.py`: `display_width`, cell-aware `pad` (ljust/rjust), `truncate` (never splits a wide char or strands a combining mark; ellipsis at the right cell width). No `wcwidth` dep — `unicodedata.east_asian_width` (W/F → 2) + a zero-width rule for combining / ZWJ / variation selectors.
- Routed the gantt label gutter (id right-pad + title pad + truncation) through it.
- Multi-code-point emoji ZWJ clusters are summed per code point (documented compromise, anchor-tested).

title: feat(daemon): PID-identity guard on stop + flock singleton (#25)
body:
## What
Daemon hardening deferred from the #26 daemon-core review (issue #25). Closes the two pid-file-daemon gaps the core left open.

### (a) PID-identity check before signalling in `stop()`
After a crash the OS can recycle the daemon's pid for an unrelated process; a bare `kill(pid,0)` probe reads it as "running" and `stop` would signal the innocent process. `stop` now classifies the pid (`identify_pid`, tri-state daemon/foreign/unknown):
- matches FIRST against the argv signature the daemon records in its own pid-file at startup — robust to ANY entrypoint (renamed console-script, frozen binary), and coordinate-bound so a different coordinate's daemon isn't mis-claimed;
- falls back to a positional `daemon run` shape match for legacy pid-files;
- refuses a positively-FOREIGN pid (`not-ours`), but on an UNREADABLE cmdline (busybox `ps` / no `/proc`) preserves pre-guard signalling so a real daemon is never orphaned in minimal Docker images;
- re-checks identity before SIGKILL; pid-file clears are guarded so a fresh same-coordinate start during the wait isn't orphaned.

### (b) flock singleton
The live daemon holds an exclusive flock for its lifetime. Two near-simultaneous starts both pass the liveness check, but only one child wins the flock; the loser exits without touching the winner's state — closing the check-then-spawn TOCTOU. Degrades safely on non-POSIX.

## Tests
67 daemon tests incl. an END-TO-END recorded-identity test on a real process (which caught + fixed an argv[0]-instability orphaning bug during review), the reused-pid refusal, the race-guarded pid clear, and the flock singleton. Full suite green, ruff clean.

Follow-up `pid_status`/`status` consistency tracked as #32.

Closes #25

title: fix(daemon): read full cmdline via `ps -ww` so a long-argv daemon isn't orphaned
body:
## Root cause (surfaced by Linux CI on the #25 follow-up)
`ps -o args=` TRUNCATES the command line to ~screen width by default. `process_cmdline` falls back to `ps` when `/proc` is unavailable, so a daemon whose identity is recorded from `/proc` (full argv) at startup would, on a `ps`-fallback read in `stop`, get a TRUNCATED argv → a different `argv_signature` → mis-classified FOREIGN → the real daemon ORPHANED (unmanageable via `task daemon stop`). Trigger: any daemon with a long argv (e.g. a long `-C <coordinate>`/config path).

## Fix
`ps -ww -p <pid> -o args=` (`-ww` disables truncation; procps-ng + BSD `ps`). A `ps` that rejects the flag exits non-zero → `_read_ps_cmdline` returns None; those platforms (busybox/Alpine) have `/proc` anyway, so the ps branch isn't taken — no regression.

## Tests
- /proc-gated regression test: spawn a process with a LONG spaced arg, assert the `ps` read is NOT truncated and `/proc` and `ps` paths yield the SAME signature.
- deterministic unit test pinning `argv_signature` invariance to `/proc`-vs-`ps` tokenization + argv[0].
- de-flaked the recorded-identity end-to-end test (short space-free `-c` body — the symptom that first exposed this).

Follow-up to #25.
