title: feat(replies): `tg replies` message recall subcommand
body:
## What

Adds `tg replies` so an agent (or you) can quickly recall what was sent over Telegram — with timestamps and `#message-ids` — without scrolling the pane.

```
tg replies [user|agent|all] [list | find <query>] [flags]
```

- **Direction** (1st positional, default `user`): `user` = inbound messages the user sent, `agent` = outbound messages the agent sent via `tg`, `all` = both (prefixed `←` user / `→` agent).
- **Action** (2nd positional, default `list`): `list`, or `find <query>` (case-insensitive substring; `--regex` for a regular expression).
- **Default scope = the current tmux session/pane** (`$TMUX_PANE`). `--all-sessions` drops the scope; `--session <paneId>` targets a specific pane.
- `-n/--limit N` (default 20), `--full` (no truncation), `--json` (array: `ts` ms, `id`, `direction`, `from`, `text`, `pane`), `--help`.
- Line format: `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] #<id> <text>` (local time; ~200-char truncation unless `--full`).

```
$ tg replies
[2026-06-15 10:42] #4821 deploy the canary and watch error rates
[2026-06-15 10:58] #4827 roll it back, latency spiked
```

## Persistence

A new append-only `~/.config/tg-cli/tg-ctl.<botid>.history.jsonl` (one JSON object per line, added to `CtlPaths` next to `routes`, created `0600`):

- The **tg-ctl daemon** writes every inbound message it processes, stamped with the pane the message actually routes to — a reply is stamped with its recognized origin pane (via the routes map), not the default target, so it never vanishes from that pane's scoped recall.
- **`tg`** writes one `agent` record per send (stamped `$TMUX_PANE`, first sent message id).
- Both writers are **best-effort** (a corrupt/unwritable log never breaks a send or an inject, like `routes`) and the file is trimmed to its last ~5000 lines on write.
- The transcript is **denylisted** from Telegram auto-attach / `--file` (it is a full conversation log).

## Architecture

Pure logic in `features/replies/` (arg parsing, JSONL parse/append/trim, direction + pane filters, substring/regex search, line + JSON formatters, inbound/outbound text extraction). The entrypoints (`tg`, `tg-ctl`) own the file I/O + tmux pane detection + stdout. `features/replies/cli.ts` is effectful-via-DI, mirroring `features/hooks/cli.ts`, so the orchestration is unit-tested without disk/tmux.

## Tests

89 new tests (`tests/replies-*.test.ts` + denylist + ctlPaths). Full suite **989 pass / 0 fail**. Both entrypoints bundle clean.

## Review

Ran multi-model `review --staged --pool 2`. Fixed the two High findings (inbound pane drift on replies → per-message origin-pane resolution; history transcript leak → denylist pattern + `0600`) and the config-dir/bot-id Medium (token now loaded from the same dir as the history). Deferred the concurrent-write-race Medium: both writers do read-modify-write exactly like the existing `routes` map, the daemon is a singleton inbound writer, and a full file lock is out of scope for a best-effort, bounded log.

title: feat(tg-ctl): harden defer-while-waiting (follow-up questions, wedges, stale resurface)
body:
## What

Hardens the tg-ctl **defer-while-waiting** path (ROADMAP §9 tg#30, alex-mextner/tg-cli#30). tg-ctl injects inbound Telegram text into the agent's tmux pane via `send-keys`; if a question/permission prompt is OPEN in that pane, injected text lands IN the prompt and is lost/corrupted. The daemon already queued inbound behind an open question and flushed on answer — but the flush had several real hazards. This PR closes them and adds the test coverage the feature lacked.

## Hazards fixed

- **Follow-up question** — the agent commonly re-prompts the instant its question is answered. The old flush drained the whole queue up front and pasted without re-checking, typing queued text straight into the new prompt. `driveFlush` now re-checks the pane before EVERY paste and re-defers the untouched tail.
- **Head-of-line block / indefinite wedge** — a transient inject failure (pane lost its agent) used to re-defer the whole tail behind a question that may never come, wedging every later message forever. Failures now log + drop + continue.
- **Out-of-order during a flush** — a message arriving in the 800ms settle window or between pastes could jump ahead of older queued items. A `flushingPanes` flag keeps new inbound deferring (strict FIFO) for the whole flush; the round-based drain loop delivers it.
- **Stale resurface** — a question removed WITHOUT a Telegram answer (timeout / hook-socket close / send failure) left its backlog to flush, stale and out of order, on a LATER unrelated question's answer. Those paths now dead-letter the pane's queue (only when the pane is otherwise idle — not when a flush is in flight or another question is still pending) and tell the user the messages did not land.
- **Throw safety** — `injectDeferredOne` can no longer reject `driveFlush`; the fire-and-forget `flushDeferred` call is `.catch`-guarded.

## Design

`features/tg-ctl/defer.ts` is a pure, fully unit-tested module (`DeferQueues` + `driveFlush`); the daemon owns all tmux I/O and the `pendingButtons` map. The button-reply channel (inline buttons → routed hook answer) already existed; this PR is the daemon/inbound side.

## Tests
- Unit: `tests/ctl-defer.test.ts` — queue FIFO/redefer/drop, and `driveFlush` (inject-all, mid-flush re-defer, failure-continues, whole-queue re-defer).
- Integration (real daemon + fake Telegram + fake tmux/ps): deferred → FIFO flush on answer; and **question abandoned without an answer does not wedge or resurface** (Q1 expiry then Q2 answer must not flush Q1's backlog).
- Full suite green: 1011 pass / 0 fail.

## Quality gate
Multi-model `review --staged` run across several rounds; every real finding fixed (head-of-line block, stale resurface, whole-pane over-drop, throw safety, FIFO-during-flush).

## Known pre-existing limitation (not introduced here)
When a Telegram question EXPIRES but the agent's TERMINAL prompt stays open, the daemon loses its only "busy" signal and the next inbound can inject into that open prompt. Solving it needs prompt-state the bridge cannot observe (no event signals an in-terminal answer). Same behavior as before this PR; called out for follow-up.

title: feat(tag,help): lowercase-english-only --tag + colorized help
body:
Implements two ROADMAP items (CTO 2026-06-16): **"tg --tag: lowercase-english only"** and the tg side of **"ONE shared help-formatter"** (match the ecosystem color scheme until the Python migration lands the real shared lib).

## 1. `--tag` is lowercase-english ONLY

Accepted values: `answer` / `decision` / `problem` / `report`. Russian aliases (`ОТВЕТ`/`РЕШЕНИЕ`/`ПРОБЛЕМА`/`ОТЧЁТ`) and uppercase / mixed-case / unknown words are now **rejected at parse time** with a 3-part error and a **non-zero exit**, replacing the old soft-render-and-warn:

```
$ tg --tag ANSWER --reply-to 1 "x"
Error: invalid --tag 'ANSWER': tags must be lowercase english. Use one of: answer, decision, problem, report
$ echo $?
1
```

- `validateTag()` (`features/render/tag.ts`) is the gate, called in `parseArgs` so **every** send path fails before touching Telegram. The validated tag is stored **trimmed**, so the `answer`→`--reply-to` gate (a literal compare) can't be bypassed by a padded value like `--tag " answer "`.
- `TAG_ALIASES` (Cyrillic) removed; `resolveTag` uses a canonical `Set` and stays total for the renderer. The now-unreachable unknown-tag stderr warning + its `resolveTag` import were dropped from the entrypoint.
- Docs updated to lowercase-english only: `tg --help` / `--format-help`, the install-skill `SKILL.md` + always-on blurb, `AGENTS.md`, and the `prefix.ts` tag contract. The skill badge table now matches the real `TAG_PILL_FALLBACK` (`🔵 ANSWER`, …).

## 2. Colorized `--help`

`tg --help` and `tg --format-help` were the only ecosystem CLI helps printed flat. New `features/render/help-color.ts` colorizes **section headers** (bold cyan) and **option names** (green) to match review/rig/draw — dependency-free ANSI, the same `\033[CODEm` scheme as rig's `_c`. Auto-disabled when stdout/stderr is not a TTY or `NO_COLOR` is set, so piped/redirected help stays plain. Only color codes are injected: strip the escapes and the text is byte-identical.

## Tests

`bun test` — **1014 pass / 0 fail**. New coverage:
- `validateTag` accepts the four lowercase tags; rejects uppercase / mixed-case / Cyrillic / unknown with the 3-part error (unit + `parseArgs` + subprocess, asserting non-zero exit).
- the padded-`answer`-without-`--reply-to` gate (regression guard).
- `colorizeHelp` headers + option flags get the right escapes; piped `--help` is plain (no `\x1b[`); strip-ANSI == input.

title: fix(test): unlink throwaway tmux socket in tmux-integration teardown (stop leaking tgctl-test-* sockets)
body:
## Problem

`tests/ctl-tmux-integration.test.ts` runs every test against a private `-L tgctl-test-<pid>` server and tears it down in `afterAll` with `tmux kill-server`. **On macOS, `kill-server` ends the server *process* but does NOT unlink the socket file** under `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/`. The socket inode leaked every run.

This is the same bug as rig-cli's e2e fixture (alex-mextner/rig-cli#31). Together they leaked ~185 `tgctl-test-*`/`rigtest-*` sockets into `/private/tmp/tmux-501/` on the dev machine, which once starved/killed the live tmux server.

## Fix

- `afterAll` now kills the server **AND `rmSync`s its socket file**.
- The path is computed by a small `socketPathFor()` helper that mirrors tmux's `server_create_socket` (`TMUX_TMPDIR` honored only when absolute, else `/tmp`) and is reused by the new regression test.

## Test

Adds `teardown leaves no leaked tmux socket file`: boots a real server, asserts the socket file exists, runs the same kill+unlink, asserts the file is gone.

Verified: full `bun test` suite green (1015 pass), and the tmux integration suite leaves **zero** `tgctl-test-*` sockets behind in both the default and `TMUX_TMPDIR`-set environments.

title: feat(deploy): scripted, idempotent deploy step for installed tg checkouts (tg-cli #36 deploy follow-up)
body:
## What & why

`tg` is a committed Bun script run via a symlink (`tg` → `<checkout>/tg`), so the checked-out file **is** the running binary — there is no build step. "Deploying" a merged change is just a guarded fast-forward `git pull` in the checkout the symlink points at. Until now that step was undocumented and unscripted, which is how the ROADMAP item **"tg-cli #36 merged but NOT deployed"** happened: a merged `--tag`/help change sat un-deployed because the live `~/.files/repos/tg-cli` checkout was never pulled.

This adds `scripts/deploy.sh` — the documented, scripted, safe, idempotent deploy step — plus a README section and a `CHANGELOG`/VERSION bump to 1.14.0.

## What the script does

- **Resolves the checkout** from the `tg` on PATH (follows the symlink chain hop-by-hop; `--checkout DIR` to override).
- **Refuses** a dirty *tracked* tree (untracked files like a stray `node_modules` do **not** block it), a detached HEAD, and a non-fast-forward divergence (exit `2`). Idempotent no-op when up to date.
- **`--dry-run`** reports what would land without touching anything.
- **tg-ctl-aware**: the resident `tg-ctl run` daemon loads its code at start, so a deploy that changes the `tg-ctl` entry or anything under `features/` (which the daemon imports) only takes effect after a restart — which **drops the daemon's pane/cwd/session registration**. The script warns by default (prints exactly what to restart) and only restarts with `--restart-ctl`. Daemon calls are `timeout`-bounded; a `stop` failure is surfaced on its own rather than being misattributed to `start`.
- Post-deploy `tg --version` + `install-skill` run the **deployed checkout's own** `tg` (not whatever is first on PATH), bounded by `timeout`, and never abort the deploy on failure.

## Acceptance evidence

**Dry-run against the real live checkout** (`~/.files/repos/tg-cli`), correctly detecting the 3 pending commits and flagging the tg-ctl restart need:
```
deploy: checkout = /Users/ultra/.files/repos/tg-cli
deploy: branch  = main
deploy: 708bac7 -> ff1d44f, commits to land:
  ff1d44f feat(autolink): tg#<id> message refs + GitHub-anchor line specs (#34)
  3dedfea docs(agents): correct stale test count (#38)
  6de3f93 docs(readme): fix stale agent-tools ecosystem description (drop agenttools_log lib claim) (#33)
deploy: --dry-run — not pulling.
deploy: (dry-run) would require a tg-ctl restart (daemon code changed).
```

**Tests** — 25 hermetic tests drive the *real* `scripts/deploy.sh` against throwaway git repos + stub `tg`/`tg-ctl` binaries (zero host mutation; tests run on a hermetic PATH so they can never resolve/pull the live checkout). Cover: up-to-date no-op, fast-forward, dirty-tree/non-FF/detached refusal, untracked-file tolerance, symlink-chain resolution, the daemon warn / `--restart-ctl` restart / stop-failure / start-failure / no-daemon branches, and the `--version` + `install-skill` paths (incl. failure warning).

```
bun test tests/deploy.test.ts   ->  25 pass, 0 fail
bun test (full suite)           ->  1091 pass, 0 fail
shellcheck scripts/deploy.sh    ->  clean
tsc --noEmit tests/deploy.test.ts -> clean
ci/leftover-grep + ci/secret-scan -> PASS
```

## Review

Pre-commit multi-model review (GLM / Gemini + fast board) run on the exact staged diff across 5 rounds; substantive findings fixed each round (notably: `--checkout` running hooks against the wrong PATH `tg`, single-hop symlink resolution, `set -e`/`pipefail` aborting the deploy on an empty version probe, swallowed `tg-ctl stop` failure, untracked-files blocking, `tg-ctl` change-detection too narrow). Remaining suggestions (arbitrary-remote-name support, exit-code taxonomy for "deployed-but-post-step-failed", RCE threat-model note) consciously declined as YAGNI for a single-machine `git pull` wrapper.

## NOT done here (deploy = HOLD)

This PR adds the deploy *tooling*; it does not itself mutate the live machine. See the PR thread for the live-checkout state + the owed `tg-ctl` restart.

title: feat(tg-ctl): align service lifecycle to agenttools_service + OS autostart (enable/disable)
body:
## What

Refit `tg-ctl` (the tg-cli inbound control daemon) toward the shared agent-tools
service-management contract defined by the merged `agenttools_service` lib
(agent-tools#54), per ROADMAP **"tg-ctl must self-register for system autostart on
first run"**.

`tg-ctl` is Bun/TS so it cannot import the Python lib directly yet — this **aligns its
subcommands and autostart behavior to the lib's CONTRACT** (same subcommand names, same
launchd LaunchAgent / systemd-user **semantics**, idempotent install/remove), **not its
code**.

## Lifecycle (matches `agenttools_service`)

| Subcommand | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `run` | foreground / blocking — the daemon process itself |
| `start` | background detached daemon, returns immediately |
| `status` | running? / pid / bot / target pane / **autostart** |
| `stop` | stop the background daemon |
| `enable [--dry-run]` | install OS autostart **AND** start now (new) |
| `disable` | remove OS autostart **AND** stop (new) |
| *(bare)* | prints **HELP**, never launches (was an error before) |

## OS-autostart matrix (mirrors the lib's semantics)

- **macOS** → launchd LaunchAgent: label `com.agenttools.tg-ctl.tg-ctl`, `RunAtLoad` +
  `KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false}` (restart only on a non-clean exit — the mirror of
  systemd `Restart=on-failure`), legacy `launchctl load`/`unload` verbs (pinned to the
  lib, which defers the `bootstrap`/`bootout` migration).
- **Linux** + `systemctl --user` → systemd `--user` unit
  `agenttools-tg-ctl-tg-ctl.service`: `Restart=on-failure` + `RestartSec=2`, ordered
  after `network-online.target`, `WantedBy=default.target`, `daemon-reload` +
  `enable --now`.
- **No supported autostart** (Linux without `systemctl --user`, or any other OS) → a
  **no-op fallback** that background-starts now and reports it will **NOT** survive
  reboot — exactly the lib's `NoopAutostartBackend` (no crontab).

Idempotent install/remove (re-enable overwrites in place; disable on a missing unit is
a no-op), single-owner / no-double-start (enable stops any background instance before
the OS takes over), and **exit 4** when OS autostart install/remove fails (the daemon
is still started; autostart is just not live).

## Design

The autostart **policy** lives in `features/tg-ctl/autostart.ts` as a **pure module**
(unit / label / command *plans*) — no I/O, no spawns — so the whole thing is
unit-testable with no real launchd/systemd. The `tg-ctl` entrypoint executes the plan.

## Tests (`bun test`)

- Pure plan/label/unit-rendering matrix (`tests/ctl-autostart.test.ts`): launchd/systemd
  unit shape pinned against the contract; `none` fallback; systemd `%`/space quoting.
- E2E CLI (`tests/ctl-service-cli.test.ts`): bare = HELP (never launches), `enable
  --dry-run` (writes nothing), OS-command-failure → exit 4 + fallback start, idempotent
  enable→disable round-trip, disable-failure leaves the unit file in place. Every path
  is driven through `launchctl`/`systemctl` **shims** — no real autostart is ever loaded.
- Full suite green: **1107 pass, 1 skip (Linux-only), 0 fail**.
- launchd plist validated with `plutil -lint`.

Reviewed with the multi-model `review` tool before commit; findings addressed (named
exit-code constant, `autostartUnitPath` helper instead of rebuilding the plan,
guarded fallback messages, added disable-failure coverage, removed an unused import).

## Follow-up

Full **code-share** with `agenttools_service` (importing the Python lib instead of
reproducing its contract) when tg-cli grows a Python seam — noted in `AGENTS.md` and the
`autostart.ts` header.

title: feat(tg-ctl): forward Claude Code plan-approval (ExitPlanMode) to TG as Proceed/Keep-planning buttons
body:
## ⛔ HOLD — do NOT merge until LIVE button round-trip is verified by the CTO

This is an **interactive** feature. The tests prove the wire/round-trip logic, but the real value — tapping **Proceed / Keep planning** on your phone and having Claude Code actually proceed or stay in plan mode — needs a **live** verification with a real Claude Code session in tmux + the bot. Please verify the round-trip before merging. **Do not auto-ship.**

## What this does

Extends the q-buttons / permission-forwarding work (tg-cli#30, ROADMAP "Forward harness confirmation / permission prompts to TG as inline buttons").

Claude Code's plan-mode **plan-approval** is a BLOCKING prompt gated as the `ExitPlanMode` tool. Before this it fell into the generic permission branch and rendered as a content-less "Allow ExitPlanMode?" with Approve/Reject — losing the plan text and mis-wording the choice. Now it forwards as a permission carrying the **plan text** (clamped to Telegram's 4096-char limit) with relabeled buttons: **Proceed** (allow) / **Keep planning** (deny).

## Key design points

- **Event-correct reply shape.** PreToolUse → `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (+ `permissionDecisionReason` on a relabeled deny). PermissionRequest (the installed `*` catch-all, the production path) → `hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior`; `hookEventName` is required. A bare allow is sufficient — `updatedInput` is optional and omitted. All confirmed against the live hooks docs.
- **No double-forward.** ExitPlanMode gets NO dedicated PreToolUse matcher: per the live docs both `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest` fire for the same call, so a second matcher would forward the plan twice and strand the losing `tg-ctl ask` until timeout. The existing `PermissionRequest *` catch-all delivers it exactly once.
- `decisionLabels` + `permissionEvent` survive both the raw-payload normalize AND the daemon wire hop (`normalizeButtonRequest`).

## Known limitation (documented in code, phased follow-up)

The live hooks docs document **no model-facing reason channel** for a `PermissionRequest` deny (unlike PreToolUse's `permissionDecisionReason`). The keep-planning intent therefore rides the documented top-level `systemMessage`, which surfaces to the **user**, not the model. On the production path Claude sees the bare deny; the user sees the intent. Conveying it to the model means injecting into the pane (the existing defer/inject infra) — a deliberate phased follow-up, not in this PR.

The pre-existing `AskUserQuestion` output shape (an undocumented internal) is left unchanged — out of scope, working in production.

## Review notes

Ran multi-model `review diff`. The codex seat flagged the `decision.message` vs `systemMessage` choice as High. Investigated against the live hooks docs (multiple verbatim fetches): the `PermissionRequest` `decision` object documents **only** `behavior` + `updatedInput` — there is **no** model-facing `message`/`reason` field. `systemMessage` is the documented (user-facing) channel; `decision.message` would be an undocumented field that the harness ignores. Kept the documented `systemMessage` and documented the model-visibility limitation honestly in code rather than emitting an undocumented field. The "ExitPlanMode allow needs updatedInput" finding only affects the non-installed hypothetical PreToolUse path; docs say allow alone is sufficient.

## Tests

- `tests/ctl-plan-approval.test.ts` — pure helpers: normalize, button rendering, both reply shapes (PreToolUse / PermissionRequest), plan truncation, malformed-labels fallback, already-normalized pass-through.
- `tests/ctl-plan-approval-integration.test.ts` — full round-trip: raw ExitPlanMode payload → live `tg-ctl` daemon → Telegram Proceed/Keep-planning buttons → tap → hook output.

`bun test` green: **1136 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail**.

title: fix(tg-ctl): retry a transient empty tmux pane query before reporting "no agent"
body:
## The bug

The daemon's launchd runtime was idle-exiting every 30 min (`no agent pane for 30 min — idle exit`) and replying the misleading **"Claude Code not in tmux → …"** to every inbound message — while live `claude` panes existed the whole time. The discovery CODE and ENV both test correct (`pickTargetPane` finds the agent in every manual run); the failure is an INTERMITTENT one in the long-running launchd process: `tmux list-panes -a` occasionally exits 0 with an EMPTY pane list (a momentary connect to the wrong/empty server). `snapshot()` read that single result and silently degraded to the no-agent path.

## Fix

`panesWithRetry` re-runs the pane query ONLY on that targeted flake (exit 0 + empty), accepting empty after a few attempts. It does **not** retry a non-zero exit — a non-zero `tmux list-panes` means the client couldn't reach a server (no server / socket gone / connect failed), the STEADY STATE when tmux is unused; retrying it would block the daemon's single thread (and the Telegram long-poll) ~240ms per message in the whole "no agent right now" population. Breaking on any non-zero is also robust to tmux's varying no-server stderr wording (no fragile message match).

PURE (caller injects `run`/`sleep`) → 8 unit tests: happy-path single call, exit-0-empty retry-then-succeed, exit-0-empty give-up (sleeps attempts-1), non-zero breaks immediately (no retry/sleep), null break, delayMs honored, sleep optional. Full suite green (1146 pass).

## Deploy note

The live daemon runs `~/.files/repos/tg-cli` (origin/main). After merge it needs `git pull` there + a daemon restart to take effect.

Refs #25.

## What & why

CTO (2026-06-19): **each background agent lives in its own Telegram forum topic** —
creating a topic spins up an agent that asks PATH + MODEL (like `/new`), and the topic
*is* the address (no more flat `/agent` phonetic disambiguation).

This is **increment 1 of 4**: the design spec + the pure, fully-tested core. The
live-daemon executor (tmux spawn + per-topic routing + outbound threading) is
increment 2. **Nothing changes for current users**: the topic path is gated behind
`topicsEnabled` (default OFF) and the entrypoint does not pass it yet, so the flat
behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (pinned by a "topics OFF → unchanged" test).

## Contents

- **`docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md`** — full design: topic lifecycle state machine,
  the per-topic `/new` flow, the `tmux new-window -c <path> -- claude --model <m>`

title: fix(tg-ctl): force a UTF-8 locale for discovery — the REAL 'not in tmux' root cause
body:
**The actual root cause** behind the whole "Claude Code not in tmux" saga (#44/#46 treated symptoms).

Under launchd the daemon inherits NO locale. tmux then escapes the TAB field-separator in `PANE_FORMAT` to `_` in its `-F` output (`2<TAB>1` → `2_1`). `parsePaneList` splits on a real tab, so every row collapses to one field (<6), all are dropped, `snapshot()` returns ZERO panes, and the daemon says "not in tmux" for every message despite live agents. A retry never helped — the output was non-empty, just mis-separated.

Caught by the #46 no-agent logging: `exit=0 lines=5 parsed=0 firstLineCodes=[...95...]` (95=`_`, not 9=tab). Bisected to the missing UTF-8 locale.

**Fix:** pass a guaranteed-UTF-8 env explicitly to the tmux+ps spawns (Bun.spawnSync ignores runtime `process.env` mutation). `LC_ALL` set unconditionally (overrides the `LC_ALL=C`+`LANG=*.UTF-8` trap), platform-appropriate (en_US.UTF-8 on macOS, C.UTF-8 else).

Verified in the daemon's no-locale env AND the LC_ALL=C trap → 5 panes / 3 agents / routes correctly. Confirmed in prod by the user's own test message reaching an agent. Suite 1175 green.

Refs #25.

title: feat(tg-ctl): forum-topics routing half — topic→pane map + inbound route + outbound message_thread_id
body:
Closes #52. ROADMAP #31. Spec: `docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` (§9).

## What this does

The forum-topics **pure core** (increment 1, merged in 2157f09) recognised forum-topic updates and emitted `topic-*` Actions, but was **dead-wired** — the daemon never consumed them, never allocated a topics store, and had no `control.topics` flag. In a real forum supergroup nothing routed per-topic.

This wires the **routing half** (spec §9.3 minus spawn) behind a **default-OFF** flag:

- `control.topics` config flag (default `false`) + parse; `CtlPaths.topics` state file.
- The poll loop passes `topicsEnabled` + `topicStatusOf` (reads the binding store) into `stepUpdates`. With the flag **OFF** this is byte-identical to before — flat 1:1 routing is untouched.
- `executeAction`:
  - `topic-route` → map `threadId → paneId`, inject the wrapped text into THAT pane. Safety: re-verify the pane still hosts an agent AND (when the binding recorded a path) the live pane path still matches it — the same pane-id-reuse guard `handleReplyRoute` uses — so a stranger agent that inherited the old `%N` never receives the message. A genuinely **dead** pane is marked closed; a path **mismatch** is non-terminal (skip + notice, no close) so a transient empty-path read or a legit `cd` can't irreversibly kill a live topic.
  - `topic-close`/`topic-reopen` → persist the status transition.
  - `topic-new`/`topic-answer` → **logged no-op = the clean seam for increment-2 spawn**. No binding is created from the daemon yet, so a topic only routes if a binding already exists.
- All topic-originated daemon output carries `message_thread_id`.

## Safety (tg-ctl is the CTO's daily 1:1 lifeline)

Flag default OFF → `topicsEnabled: false` → `stepUpdates` is byte-identical to today. Topic cases run ONLY when opted in AND a binding exists. Two mutation checks back the guarantees:
- disabling `topicsEnabled` → the topic→pane routing test FAILS (message leaks to flat %1);
- removing the path-match guard → the REUSED-pane test FAILS (message leaks into the stranger pane).

## Tests

New `tests/ctl-topics-integration.test.ts` (mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`, mirrors `ctl-defer-integration.test.ts`), 8 cases:
- 1:1 routing unchanged with flag **off** AND **on** (General / no thread id → flat pane);
- a bound-topic message routes into THAT pane (`%2`), not the flat target (`%1`);
- a **dead** bound pane → no leak, error threaded into the topic, binding closed;
- a **reused** pane (path mismatch) → no leak, notice threaded, binding **left bound** (recoverable);
- an **untracked** topic message → ACK-only, never reaches a flat agent;
- `forum_topic_closed`/`forum_topic_reopened` lifecycle persistence.

Plus `parseControlConfig`/`resolveControlConfig` units for the `topics` flag. **Full `bun test` suite green: 1187 pass, 0 fail.**

## Known limitations (documented in README + spec, increment-2/4)

- Creating a topic does **not** spawn an agent yet (the `/new` path+model flow + `tmux new-window`).
- The agent's own `tg` replies still post to **General** (needs `tg --topic`); only the daemon's own messages thread today.
- The shared deferred-flush drain re-checks agent presence but not project path (a property shared with the flat 1:1 path).
- Reopen leaves the old agent untracked until the spawn executor lands.

Increment-2 follow-up findings (defer-path test, service-message 👀 suppression, reopen-orphan cleanup, additional edge tests) are captured in the review trail; I was blocked from filing a second tracking issue by the auto-mode classifier — they should be tracked under the spec §9.2/§9.4 work.

title: fix(tg-ctl): recognized reply route never loses to the global registration (#53)
body:
Closes #53.

## The bug

With two agents running (`[3d]` at `%5`, `[rig]` at `%2`), a Telegram reply to a message that **originated from `[3d]` (%5)** was mis-delivered to `[rig]` (%2). Daily multi-agent workflow breaker.

**Root cause.** `handleReplyRoute` recognizes the origin pane from `routes.json`, but only injects there if the CURRENT `snapshot()` confirms the pane hosts a same-project agent. Under launchd, `tmux list-panes -a` intermittently returns an empty/partial pane list (the no-locale tab-mangle flake, `no-agent reply: panes=0`). The recognized reply then **fell through** and, when the partial snapshot left exactly one agent visible — deterministically the registration's last writer, `%2` — silently injected into THAT wrong agent. A second contributor: `recordRoute`'s unlocked read-modify-write let concurrent agents clobber each other's route entries (last-writer-wins), another way the replied-to id went missing.

## The fix

**Part A — recognized-route guard (`tg-ctl`).** When the replied-to id IS recognized but the snapshot can't confirm the origin pane (`!pane`), do NOT fall through to the single-candidate auto-inject. A fresh candidate snapshot (`listAgentCandidates` — the retry) is taken and the reply goes to the existing agent **picker** so the human disambiguates; it is never injected into the registration's last-writer pane. Happy path (snapshot confirms the same-project origin → inject there) unchanged; an UNRECOGNIZED reply with a single visible agent still injects directly. The duplicated history-stamp `resolvePane` path gets the mirror guard (stamps the origin pane for scoped recall, never the wrong default) — attribution only, never an inject target.

**Part B — locked routes write (`tg` + `features/tg-ctl/routes.ts`).** `recordRoute` now runs under `withRoutesLock`: an O_EXCL lockfile whose owner is a PID. A held lock is broken ONLY when its owner process is **dead** (liveness, not mtime-age — a live writer is never clobbered), and a SIGKILL-window empty/unparseable lockfile is also breakable so the mutex can't permanently wedge. Ownership-checked removals, fd-leak-safe, non-EEXIST open errors fail fast. `tg` `recordRoute` is the sole writer of `routes.json` (the daemon only reads), so every concurrent send's route survives.

## How the guard works

`recognized && !pane` (origin known, snapshot can't see it) → fresh candidate snapshot + **picker**, never the registration default. Retry = the second independent snapshot via `listAgentCandidates`; picker = the disambiguation when still unconfirmable.

## Tests

- **`ctl-reply-misroute-integration.test.ts` (new)** — real daemon vs fake Telegram + switchable fake tmux/ps: the exact misroute (origin `%5` recognized, only `%2` visible → picker, never injects into `%2`), the empty-snapshot no-misroute case, the happy path (routes to `%5`), the single-agent direct-inject regression. **Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix code** (it injected `%2`).

title: fix(tg-ctl): a SCOPED forwarded question waits indefinitely for its Telegram answer
body:
## What

A forwarded `tg-ctl` question (Claude `AskUserQuestion` / `ExitPlanMode` / permission prompt mirrored to a Telegram inline-button message) used to auto-expire **110s** after posting, rewriting the prompt to "expired — answer in terminal" and closing the hook socket. The CTO must be able to answer from Telegram with no deadline — this is the daily-critical lifeline.

This makes a **SCOPED** forwarded question (its pane is known) wait **indefinitely** for its Telegram answer or a socket close, while keeping the abandon bound for the **UNSCOPED** case only.

Closes #57.

## How the no-wedge guarantee is preserved

The 110s timer was the mechanism bounding the inbound defer-while-waiting so an open question couldn't wedge routing (`paneHasPendingQuestion`'s fail-closed `if (!pb.req.paneId) return true`). The danger is asymmetric:

- **SCOPED** question (`paneId` known) defers inbound for **only its own pane**. That pane's agent is itself blocked on this very question, so deferring its inbound starves nothing; the queue flushes on the answer. ⇒ **safe to wait forever — no timer.**
- **UNSCOPED** question (`paneId` undefined — hook ran without `TMUX_PANE`) defers **ALL** panes. Waiting forever would wedge every pane. The `#55` reply-route picker resolves where a *reply* goes, not a question's own `paneId` (set once in `hook-normalize.ts`, never reassigned), so an unscoped question is never re-scoped. ⇒ **keeps the bound.**

Net: a scoped question waits forever; the only kind that could wedge all-pane routing (unscoped) still self-clears at the bound. Socket-close cleanup is preserved unchanged for both kinds (a dead agent's question is removed and its pane's backlog dead-lettered), so nothing leaks on a dead socket.

## Changes

- `tg-ctl`: arm the abandon timer only for `!req.paneId` (unscoped). Scoped → no timer. `PendingButton.timer` is now optional; every `clearTimeout(timer)` site is a safe no-op when undefined. The bound is `UNSCOPED_ABANDON_MS` (default 110s, overridable via `TG_CTL_UNSCOPED_TIMEOUT_MS` for tests only, clamped to `TIMEOUT_MAX` so a huge value can't flip to instant-expiry).
- Tests (`tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts`, mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`):
  - a scoped question stays open past the (test-shortened) bound — no "expired" edit, the callback still answers it later, deferred inbound flushes on the answer;
  - a scoped question still cleans up on socket close (agent dies) — backlog dead-lettered, pane freed;
  - NO-WEDGE guard: an unscoped question never answered still self-clears at the bound and frees all-pane routing (a regression dropping the unscoped bound hangs this test).
  - Mutation-verified: arming the timer for scoped too makes the wait-forever test fail.

## Review (gate: `[ok]`)

Review gate passed `[ok]`. Advisory findings addressed:
- `UNSCOPED_ABANDON_MS` clamped to `TIMEOUT_MAX` (a huge value can't flip to instant-expiry); `0`/absent ⇒ 110s default, documented.
- Verified the socket `'close'` listener is registered synchronously **before any `await`**, so an early close (even before `messageId` is set) still frees a scoped entry — the only non-answer release once the timer is gone.
- Verified every `clearTimeout(entry.timer)` / `clearTimeout(pending.timer)` site is a safe no-op on the now-optional timer; no code assumes the timer is always armed.

Pre-existing gap surfaced and tracked separately (#58): an **unscoped** question expiring unanswered silently loses its deferred backlog (no `onAbandon`, no dead-letter notice). The old 110s timer behaved identically; this PR reworks the expiry path but does not fix that gap. It is asserted as deliberate current behavior in the NO-WEDGE test so a future change can't silently regress it.

Noted follow-up (not done here): a two-pane discovery fixture proving a scoped %1 question does not defer a %2 inbound — the single-pane harness can't express it without a larger fixture; the invariant is the readable `pb.req.paneId === paneId` line and the scoped-skip is mutation-verified.

## Tests

Full `bun test` green: 1207 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail (1208 tests, 82 files). Review gate: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` → ok.

title: feat(tg): forum-topics incr2 — `tg --topic` / `TG_TOPIC` outbound threading
body:
## What

Forum-topics **increment 2** (spec `docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` §8). Increment 1 (#54) wired the inbound routing half and threaded the *daemon's* own output; this adds the missing **outbound side** so an agent's own `tg` replies thread INTO a forum topic instead of scattering to General — making a bound topic finally end-to-end useful.

Closes #56.

## Scope (chosen from §9 deferred list)

Picked **`tg --topic <id>` / `TG_TOPIC`** (the §9 RECOMMENDED-first item) — the highest-value piece that is **fully safe**: it touches only the outbound `tg` send path, zero daemon routing code, so it cannot regress #54's topic-route guard or #55's reply-misroute fix or the 1:1 lifeline.

- `--topic <id>` flag + `TG_TOPIC` env fallback (flag wins; env trimmed before validation), validated like `--reply-to`.
- `message_thread_id` is stamped on **every** outbound primitive (sendMessage, sendRich, sendPhoto, sendDocument, sendMediaGroup) and is **NOT consumed** after the first message — a >4096 split and album items all stay in the topic.
- With **neither** flag nor env the wire payload is **byte-identical** to before (the daily-critical 1:1 path is untouched).
- `TG_TOPIC` is **ADVISORY**: an agent shell can inherit a stale/closed/foreign id, so a malformed value is logged + ignored, and a well-formed but server-REJECTED value (`message thread not found` / `TOPIC_CLOSED` / non-forum) makes a **text/rich** send retry ONCE to General (dropping the thread AND the reply anchor so Telegram can't re-bind it) rather than hard-fail. An explicit `--topic` stays strict. Media sends keep the strict path (documented limitation).

## Tests

- **Transport-level** (`tests/transport-topic.test.ts`): every primitive stamps the thread id; it rides every message (mutation-verified — a consume-once mutant fails exactly the "rides EVERY message" test); advisory fallback on BOTH HTTP-400 and 200/`{ok:false}`; advisory still **fails loud** on a non-thread error (rate-limit/blocked) — mutation-verified; explicit-topic fails loud; reply-anchor dropped on the General retry (sendMessage + sendRich); direct `readErrorDescription` / `isThreadRejection` unit cases.
- **End-to-end through the real binary** vs a `TG_API_BASE` mock (`tests/cli-topic-send.test.ts`): `--topic`, `TG_TOPIC`, flag-wins, malformed-env-non-fatal, multipart `--photo` carries the thread, stale-env General fallback, and the documented media hard-fail.
- **Parse/validation** (`tests/ergonomics.test.ts`, `tests/cli-subprocess.test.ts`) + a **flag-OFF 1:1 byte-identical regression**.

- **Daemon auto-stamp** of a bound pane's `TG_TOPIC` (so the agent threads without `--topic`) — touches the spawn/inject path; lands with the spawn executor (the advisory fallback here is what keeps that future auto-stamp safe against a since-closed topic).

title: fix(tg-ctl): /agent inline-keyboard picker with distinct cwd labels (closes #59)
body:
## The bug (CTO-reported)

Bare `/agent` printed a useless TEXT list — three indistinguishable `4 · claude` rows (panes in a window with no name fall back to the session name, here "4") and **no tappable buttons**. CTO: "где кнопки?".

```
agents (address with /agent <window> <message>):
▸ 4
   4 · claude
   4 · claude
   4 · claude
```

## The fix

Bare `/agent` now reuses the #55 inline-keyboard picker machinery (`buildAgentSelectMessage` + `pendingAgent` + `tga:` callbacks): **one tappable button per agent with a DISTINCT, human-meaningful label.**

- `AgentCandidate` carries `panePath` (cwd). `distinctLabels` leads with the cwd **project dir** (`rig` / `3d-cli` / `hyperide`) when window names are bare/numeric or collide, falling back to the pane id as the always-unique last resort. `dedupeCandidates` guards a flaky snapshot that repeats a pane id.
- A tap confirms the choice and hands back the exact `/agent <selector> <message>` command (`suggestSelector`), verified against the **full live fleet** at tap time so it never points outside the picker (no silent misroute) and never hands back a whitespace/misrouting token.
- For the suggestion to actually route, `matchWindows` now consults each pane's cwd — but in two strict tiers that never change existing behaviour:
  - **tier 1**: window NAMES only (fuzzy) — a real `deploy` window still routes directly, never tied by a pane merely sitting in a `…/deploy` cwd;
  - **tier 2** (only when tier 1 is empty): the cwd, matched **EXACT-only**, so a window-name typo / short token can't resonate into another project's cwd. This is what makes the common multi-`claude` shape work — tmux auto-renames several panes to the same `node`/`claude` name, useless for picking, but their cwds differ.

The daemon sends these labels as **plain text** (no `parse_mode`), so special chars in cwd basenames are safe.

## Tests

- Unit coverage: distinct labels / dedupe / the two-tier + EXACT-only cwd match / the anti-typo guard / the round-trip routing guarantee / the misroute guard / the empty-lead label edge.
- A daemon **integration test** (fake tmux+ps, mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`) drives bare `/agent` → inline keyboard with distinct cwd labels → tap → the suggested `/agent rig …` injects into the right pane (`-t %5001` on the same log line) and **not** its siblings.

title: fix(tg-ctl): log every ask-forward attempt + outcome (no silent non-forward)
body:
Closes #65

## The bug

A Claude Code **AskUserQuestion** raised in one session (the `ext-test-projects` session) was **never forwarded to Telegram** — the CTO answered it in the local Claude harness UI (the 3-option picker is the *harness* AskUserQuestion UI, not a Telegram message). Nothing reached Telegram and **nothing was logged**.

Root cause: tg-ctl keeps a **single** registration file naming the one pane/cwd that owns the inline keyboard. It was registered to a *different* session (`%2` / `/Users/ultra/xp/tg-cli`). When the ext session's `tg-ctl ask` hook fired, `registrationAllowsHook` returned false and `handleHookSocketLine` did a bare `socket.end("null")` at tg-ctl:1133 — **no log line at all**. So the drop was invisible.

## The fix (primarily logging)

Every ask-forward outcome is now a distinct, greppable `ask-forward …` line in the daemon log:

- `ask-forward arrived: agent=… kind=… req=… pane=… cwd=… session=…`
- `ask-forward posted: … messageId=…` on success
- `ask-forward dropped: reason=<not-registered|not-forwardable|duplicate-in-flight|send-failed|unparsable-payload> …` — the not-registered line also names the registration it failed to match (`reg=pane=… cwd=… session=…`)
- client-side (hook process stderr): `reason=unsupported-payload` and `ask-forward not-posted: … daemon declined or unreachable`

No more silent `socket.end("null")`. The not-registered path now reads the registration once (was re-read just for the log).

## Tests

`tests/ctl-ask-forward-logging.test.ts` (mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`): not-registered / not-forwardable / duplicate-in-flight / send-failed each assert their distinct diagnostic; the happy path still logs arrived+posted and posts buttons. Full `bun test` green (1268 pass, 0 fail).

## Underlying provisioning note

The deeper cause is that only one session is registered at a time. If the ext session's Claude Code didn't run `tg start` (or another session re-registered after it), its questions can't forward by design — this PR makes that **visible** in the log so it's diagnosable. The registration/provisioning model is a separate concern.

title: feat(tg-ctl): per-pane registration SET — every live session's questions forward (#67)
body:
## Problem

tg-ctl kept ONE global registration naming a single pane/cwd. Every `tg` send from an agent session auto-runs `tg-ctl start --pane --cwd`, which **overwrote** that file, so the registration migrated to whichever session sent last. A question (AskUserQuestion / permission prompt) from any OTHER live session then failed the forward gate (`registrationAllowsHook`) and never reached Telegram — logged since #66 as `ask-forward dropped: reason=not-registered`. The CTO runs several sessions at once ([rig], [3d], ext-test-projects, hyperide), so this dropped real questions daily.

## Fix — per-pane registration SET

- **`features/tg-ctl/registration-store.ts`** (new, PURE): parse (array form **+ LEGACY single-object back-compat** so an in-place daemon upgrade keeps its live registration), upsert (per-pane key — a session's `tg start` updates only its own entry), prune (dead-pane entries by tmux liveness; **never** on an empty/flaky snapshot), serialize.
- **`registrationSetAllowsHook`** (questions.ts): a hook forwards when ITS pane matches **ANY** entry — every registered session forwards, each scoped to its own pane. The per-entry rule is unchanged (paneId authoritative), so a same-cwd-different-pane session is still rejected. Empty set fails closed.
- **`pickTargetPaneFromSet`** (discover.ts): the §10 chain with tier-1/tier-3 matching the SET. One registered live agent pane → pick; SEVERAL → ambiguous (a fresh non-reply inbound to multiple agents is genuinely ambiguous — never silently pick; disambiguation is forum-topics #31's job). Byte-identical to the single-reg path for one entry.
- **`tg-ctl` entrypoint**: `startLauncher` UPSERTS under the registration lock (O_EXCL + PID-liveness, like routes) instead of overwriting — concurrent `tg start`s no longer clobber each other. `discoverTarget` / `composeStatus` / the forward gate all read the set. `discoverTarget` **durably prunes** dead entries on disk (re-read + re-prune under the lock) so they can't accumulate to the cap and evict a live session.

## Guarantees preserved

- **#55** (recognized-reply-beats-registration) and **#49** (unscoped-question fail-closed) live in `handleReplyRoute` / the defer logic, which key off `req.paneId` and the routes map — **not** the registration. Neither path was modified (verified: the diff touches no reply-route/defer line).
- **Single-session happy path is byte-identical.**

## Tests

- Per-pane store unit tests (parse/legacy-migrate/upsert/prune/cap/round-trip + the set-gate rule + paneId-authoritative reject).
- `pickTargetPaneFromSet` tier coverage (one/several/fall-through, fixedSession, cwd-fallback, sole-agent).
- **Multi-session forward integration** (mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`): TWO sessions registered concurrently — a question from EITHER forwards (posts buttons, scoped to the right pane); an unregistered pane still fails closed; a re-register keeps the other; two concurrent `tg start`s both land.

title: feat(tg-ctl): self-provision the bot command menu via setMyCommands on startup
body:
Closes #68

## What

The tg-ctl bot handled `/agent`, `/stop`, `/kill`, `/status` but never registered them with Telegram, so they did NOT appear in the client's command menu / "/" autocomplete. The daemon now publishes its own command list on startup via `setMyCommands` — the bot self-provisions its commands.

## How

- **`features/tg-ctl/bot-commands.ts`** — single source of truth for the published menu (`BOT_COMMANDS`) plus `validateBotCommands` enforcing Telegram's constraints (command `[a-z0-9_]`, 1-32 chars; description 1-256 code points; <=100 commands; no duplicates).
- **`tg-ctl`** — `runDaemon` calls `publishBotCommands(ctx)` once on startup, before entering the poll loop, POSTing `setMyCommands` through the existing resilient `botPost` transport. The whole publish path is `try/catch`'d: a failed, rejected, or unreachable `setMyCommands` is logged and ignored — it never crashes or blocks routing (the daemon's core job).

## Commands registered

| command | description |
|---|---|
| `/agent` | Route a message to a specific agent (or pick from buttons) |
| `/stop` | Interrupt the current agent turn — session survives |
| `/kill` | End the agent session (SIGINT) |
| `/status` | Report daemon state |

Pass-through slashes (`/compact`, `/clear`, …) that go verbatim to the harness are deliberately NOT published — they aren't the bot's own commands.

## Tests

- Startup POSTs `setMyCommands` exactly once, with the expected payload (asserts `/agent` etc. with valid names/descriptions).
- A **rejected** (HTTP 400) AND an **unreachable-transport** (connection refused) `setMyCommands` both leave startup alive and the poll loop running — resilience.
- A **drift guard** scrapes the commands `textAction` actually handles and asserts the menu only publishes handled commands and every handled (non-hidden) command is published — so a new command can't silently miss the menu.
- Full `bun test` green: 1276 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.

title: fix(tg-ctl): no-reply auto-bind to last-active agent + /agent picker uses tmux window names
body:
Two tg-ctl routing/picker fixes the CTO reported with screenshots (Closes #75). tg-ctl is the CTO's daily-critical lifeline.

## (B) No-reply auto-bind to the most-recently-active agent
A plain (non-reply) message to a multi-agent fleet fell to `ambiguous target`. It now binds to the **most-recently-active agent** — the pane whose last outbound `tg` send is newest (the `aggregateUsage` LRU/MRU signal the reply picker already ranks by). New pure `resolveAmbiguousByActivity` (`features/tg-ctl/discover.ts`), layered on top of `pickTargetPaneFromSet`. It fires only on a genuinely ambiguous base result with a **unique** most-recent candidate; a tie or no history stays ambiguous → the button picker (#76) still fires (the #49 unscoped fail-closed).

Precedence (keep-both with #76):
1. recognized reply route (#55) wins first — the auto-bind lives ONLY on the inject path (`discoverForInject`), never on `handleReplyRoute`;
2. the no-reply auto-bind resolves an otherwise-ambiguous non-reply CONTENT inject (text/photo/voice);
3. #76's button picker fires only when auto-bind can't resolve (no recent agent / tie).

`/kill` (SIGINT) and `/stop` (Escape) deliberately do **NOT** auto-bind — a destructive/interrupting verb on an ambiguous fleet asks (the select-picker), never guesses.

## (C) /agent picker labels by the tmux WINDOW NAME, not the cwd
The picker showed `hyperide · claude` (cwd basename) instead of the CTO's window name `ext`. **Root cause:** window names were fetched in a SEPARATE `tmux list-panes` call that skipped the UTF-8 locale env — so under launchd the tab-mangle (the same root cause as the "not in tmux" saga) blanked every name and the label fell back to the cwd. `#{window_name}` is now a fixed field in the core, locale-safe `PANE_FORMAT` (`PaneInfo.windowName`, carried through `parsePaneList`). A bare default — a number, a shell/launcher command (`zsh`/`node`), or a cc version string (`2.1.181`) — is treated as non-distinguishing and the label leans on the cwd. `formatCandidates` (the `status` diagnostic) applies the same `isBareWindowName`.

## Tests
- `resolveAmbiguousByActivity` unit cases (unique-recent / partial-history / tie / no-history / passthrough);
- window-name vs cwd-fallback `distinctLabels` cases (incl. the CTO's `ext`/`rig`/`3d` setup and `node`/version-string fallbacks);
- integration (mock Telegram + fake tmux fleet): a non-reply text auto-binds to the most-recent agent (no picker), recency flips the bind, no-history stays ambiguous → picker, and an UNRECOGNIZED reply with activity STILL posts the picker (the auto-bind never leaks onto the reply path).

Full `bun test` green (1327 pass / 0 fail). Rebased onto #76; keep-both verified.

title: fix(tg-ctl): no-reply inbound binds to the last-message agent (simplify the MRU machinery)
body:
Closes #78.

## The regression

A non-reply Telegram message used to land on the last-active agent. The recent stack broke it:

- **#69** swapped the single-registration `pickTargetPane` for `pickTargetPaneFromSet`. Per-pane registration puts EVERY live agent in the registration SET, so Tier 1 now matches several panes → `ambiguous`. The simple single-target resolution was lost.
- **#76** turned `ambiguous` into a tappable picker.
- **#77** bolted `resolveAmbiguousByActivity` (a per-pane LRU/MRU map from `aggregateUsage` over routes.json) on top to recover — but it only fires when the base result is `ambiguous` AND routes.json has history AND there is a UNIQUE most-recent pane. In practice it pops the picker instead of binding, and the machinery is heavier than the problem.

## The fix (the simple semantics the CTO asked for)

- `routes.lastMessagePane()` — the origin pane of the LAST recorded outbound `tg` send: a single \"who posted last\" value (the chronological tail entry by position, robust to a backward clock step between two sends), NOT a per-pane aggregate.
- `discover.resolveByLastMessage()` — an ambiguous non-reply result binds to that pane when it is still a live candidate; otherwise stays ambiguous → the #76 picker.
- The daemon's `discoverForInject()` now calls `resolveByLastMessage(lastMessagePane())` instead of `resolveAmbiguousByActivity(aggregateUsage-derived map)`. The old per-pane machinery is removed.

Precedence: (1) a recognized reply route (#55) wins; (2) else bind to the last-message agent; (3) only with NO last-message agent (no history / gone) → the #76 picker.

## Safety preserved

- `/kill` and `/stop` (destructive) still use the base `discover()` with NO auto-bind — they ASK on an ambiguous fleet (tested even with a populated routes file).
- Reply-routing (#55) and the unscoped fail-closed (#49) are untouched.
- `aggregateUsage`/`orderByLruMru` stay — the reply picker still ranks its buttons by them.

## Tests

- Unit: `resolveByLastMessage` (binds / flips / no-last-message / gone-pane / no-agent / already-ok) and `lastMessagePane` (tail by position, clock-step robustness, empty).
- Integration (real daemon + fake tmux + fake Telegram): a non-reply inbound binds to the last-message agent (no picker), flips when the other agent posts last, never injects into a gone pane, and `/kill` never auto-binds even with a populated routes file.
- Full `bun test`: 1334 pass, 0 fail.

title: test(ctl-integration): guarantee + scope daemon teardown to stop process leaks
body:
## Problem

The `tests/ctl-*-integration.test.ts` suite spawns real `tg-ctl run` daemons (and, via `tg-ctl start`, detached `run` grandchildren) against a mock Telegram + temp-dir socket. Two leak vectors left stray daemons holding a temp socket and competing for the singleton flock — exactly the kind of thing that surfaces as flaky `no agent` / intermittent routing failures. Multiple agents this session had to `pkill` leaked test daemons by hand.

### Leak vectors fixed

1. **spawn-before-track gap (every `startDaemon` helper).** The helper did `Bun.spawn([... 'run'])` and THEN `expect(socketExists).toBe(true)`. When that assert throws (socket never appeared), the spawned daemon was not yet pushed to `procs[]` → never killed.
2. **detached grandchild (`ctl-multi-session-forward`, = #70).** `tg-ctl start` always spawns an unref'd detached `tg-ctl run`. Its flock+pid-write is async and can come up AFTER `afterAll` killed the main daemon (freeing the flock); the late grandchild then acquires it and survives. `procs[]` only ever held the `start` launcher.
3. **timing flake (`ctl-buttons-failure`).** Two tests asserted `Date.now() - t0 < 1500` while a mock op blocked 3000ms — too tight under full-suite parallel load (cold `bun` subprocess spawn + IPC), giving 1 pass / 2 fail across identical runs.

## Fix

New shared **`tests/helpers/daemon-lifecycle.ts`**:
- a registry that tracks the daemon + its temp cfgDir **before** the socket wait (closes vector 1);
- `reapDaemons`: kills tracked procs + **awaits** exit, then a **scoped backstop** that reaps any daemon recorded in `<cfgDir>/tg-ctl.<botId>.pid`. Keyed on the temp cfgDir's own pid file → can **never** touch the real daemon (a non-temp config dir), and never matches by process name;
- `awaitDetachedStartsSettled` + an opt-in settle-reap (`detachedStarts`) for the one file that runs `tg-ctl start`: every grandchild reaches (and loses) the flock while the main daemon still holds it, before teardown (closes vector 2). Non-`start` cfgDirs get a single-pass reap, so the common teardown stays fast.

De-flake the two timing tests deterministically: assert a flag that flips only after the slow 3s mock op completes is still false at ask-exit, instead of a wall-clock budget.

All 11 daemon integration files migrated to the shared lifecycle.

## Verification

- Full `bun test` green: **1342 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**.
- `pgrep -f tg-ctl` returns to baseline after the suite — **zero** temp-dir strays across repeated runs (multi-session loop x4, full suite x3).
- Self-tests in `helpers-daemon-lifecycle.test.ts` cover: the scoped backstop reaping an **untracked** daemon, the settle-reap catching a **late flock-grabber** (the #70 path), a stale-pid no-op, and `awaitDetachedStartsSettled` timing.
- A deliberately-**failing** test still gets its daemon reaped (proven with a throwaway throwing test → `PROOF OK: daemon … was reaped`).

The real daemon (`~/.files/bin/tg-ctl run`) is never touched — the backstop is scoped strictly to `mkdtempSync` temp config dirs.

Closes #82
Closes #70

title: feat(tg-ctl): spawn an agent on forum_topic_created (the /new flow trigger)
body:
## What

The **spawn-on-topic-create** half of forum-topics mode (`docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` §5, increment 2). When a Telegram **forum topic is created**, the daemon runs the interactive `/new` flow and spins up a fresh agent bound to that topic — one topic = one agent.

The routing half (#56/#61, `tg --topic`/`TG_TOPIC`) and the pure foundation (state machine + model catalog + slugifier) already landed; the entrypoint `topic-new`/`topic-answer` actions were logged no-ops behind the `control.topics` flag. This PR wires them to real `tmux new-window` spawn + persistence, and adds the model-pick button callback.

## Design

**Convention — interactive flow, NOT path-in-topic-name.** Per the spec (authoritative), the topic NAME is only the tmux-window slug (`slugifyTopicName`, already shipped, transliterates Cyrillic). Path + model come from an interactive button flow, reusing the `/new` machinery:

```
forum_topic_created  -> awaiting-path  : post "which directory?" into the topic
path message (text)  -> awaiting-model : validate dir (exists + isDirectory), post model buttons
model button tap     -> spawn + bind   : tmux new-window -> bind returned pane -> bound + confirmation
```

- **Spawn reuse:** `MODEL_CATALOG.argv()` (single source of truth for both the buttons and the argv) + `tmux new-window -c <path> -n <slug> -P -F '#{pane_id}' -- <argv>`. `-P -F '#{pane_id}'` returns the new pane id -> bound immediately (no discovery race). Path + argv are discrete argv elements (a spaced dir is safe, never shell-split).
- **Model buttons:** a new `tgm:<threadId>:<modelId>` callback (`buildModelKeyboard` / `parseTopicModelCallback`), routed in `stepUpdates` BEFORE the question/agent parsers and only when `topics` is on. The sender allow-list still gates it (an unauthorized user can't spawn).
- **Session target:** the configured `control.session`, else the session a live agent already runs in, else the current/only session.

## Safety (this is the CTO's daily-critical lifeline daemon)

- **Never throws into the poll loop.** Every spawn step (`sessionForSpawn`->`snapshot`, `statSync`, `Bun.spawnSync`) is exception-guarded; a bad path / missing tmux / spawn error posts a human-readable error INTO the topic and leaves the binding mid-flow for a retry. (Review catch: `sessionForSpawn()` was lifted INSIDE the try so its `snapshot()` can't escape the guard.)
- **Idempotent / no double-spawn.** A duplicate `forum_topic_created` for an in-flight/bound topic is filtered in `stepUpdates`; `handleTopicModel` refuses a second spawn for an already-`bound` topic; the model id is validated ONCE up front (before persist + before the "starting..." toast) so a forged id can't strand the binding.
- **Gated behind `control.topics` (default OFF).** With the flag off `stepUpdates` never emits `topic-model`/`topic-new`, and the 1:1 path is byte-identical (proven by the flag-off tests).

## Tests (mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE` + fake tmux/ps)

`tests/ctl-topic-spawn-integration.test.ts` — valid create->path->model-tap spawns one agent (asserts the model argv + `-c <path>` + `-n <slug>` + the bound pane); malformed path errors + no spawn + daemon survives; spawn FAILURE caught (binding stays awaiting-model, daemon keeps polling); duplicate `forum_topic_created` no double-spawn; duplicate model tap -> "already running", one new-window; spawn->bind->route end-to-end (a follow-up message reaches the spawned pane); forged/unknown modelId -> "unknown model" no spawn; no-binding tap -> "not in setup"; awaiting-path tap -> "send a directory first"; `topics:false` -> no binding, no spawn. Plus pure parser/keyboard/callback-emission units in `tests/ctl-topics.test.ts`. Full `bun test` green (1356 pass).

## Deferred to increment 4 (review-flagged, low-risk, documented in the spec)

- **crash-window orphan:** a daemon crash between a successful `new-window` and the `bound` write leaves a live orphan pane + `awaiting-model`; a re-tap then spawns a second agent (the "restart can't double-spawn" guarantee covers `bound` topics, not this sliver). Close by detecting the topic-slug window before re-spawning.
- **dangling model buttons:** the keyboard isn't removed (`editMessageReplyMarkup`) on bind — harmless (the bound-guard answers "already running"), `messageId` is already carried for the fix.
- Recent-repo path BUTTONS (today the path is free-text only) and re-spawn on a dead pane.

Refs #27. Closes #84.

Reviewed: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` -> [ok] (claude-opus-4-8 seat; opus not near-cap).

title: feat(tg-ctl): forum-topics increment-4 lifecycle polish
body:
## What

Increment-4 lifecycle polish for forum-topics spawn (deferred items from #85). Closes #86, refs #31/#85. Builds on the #85 spawn executor; all gated behind `control.topics` (default OFF → 1:1 byte-identical when off).

## Items shipped

- **Recent-repo path buttons** on the awaiting-path step (`tgp:<thread>:<index>:<nonce>`): the prompt offers recent project cwds (routes + per-pane registrations, merged newest-first by timestamp, deduped to absolute existing dirs) as one-tap buttons; free-text fallback remains. A per-prompt nonce rejects a stale button from a superseded prompt.
- **Model keyboard cleared on bind / restart** (`editMessageReplyMarkup`).
- **Re-spawn on a dead/closed pane**: a one-tap *Re-spawn* button (`tgr:<thread>`) re-launches with the retained path + model (or restarts the `/new` flow if path/model is missing/the dir vanished). Throttled (`respawnOffered`), only stamped on a successful send, restored to `closed` on a re-spawn failure, gated on a live offer so a manual `forum_topic_closed` never re-launches.
- **Daemon auto-stamps `TG_TOPIC`** into the spawned window env (`new-window -e`) so a topic agent's plain `tg "reply"` threads back into the topic without `--topic`.
- **Crash-orphan reconcile** on startup re-binds a crash-orphaned agent instead of double-spawning, proven by a per-spawn `@tg_spawn_token` **window user option** (queryable via `#{@tg_spawn_token}` in the pane format — `new-window -e` process env is NOT queryable later; **verified against real tmux**) plus a recorded-paneId fallback. Adoption requires same slug + same cwd + (unambiguous token OR paneId) + `awaiting-model`+path+model+`spawnPending`, so a same-slug/cwd stranger / failed-spawn / pre-model state is never adopted. A model re-tap re-probes (just-in-time adoption) with the same flake/claim/ambiguity guards.

## Safety / correctness

- Flake guards (empty `panes`/`procs` signature) are consistent across startup reconcile, the JIT probe, AND route-time.
- Lifecycle-vs-callback ordering: a same-batch close/reopen wins over a spawn tap; an order-aware message guard routes a *pre*-transition message but suppresses a *post*-transition one.
- Persist-before-cosmetics on every restart branch (durable state before async Telegram I/O).
- Fail-soft throughout; nothing throws into the poll loop.

## Tests / review

80+ new tests across `ctl-topic-spawn-integration`, `ctl-topics`, `ctl-discover`; full `bun test` green (1428 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail). Token mechanism verified end-to-end against real tmux. Hardened across 31 codex review rounds + a final gemini `[ok]` (the codex seat hung mid-run, so the final gate fell back to gemini).

Docs (spec §9.4, README, CHANGELOG) updated; version bumped to 1.18.0.

title: fix(tg-ctl): status detects external launchd autostart supervision (Closes #88)
body:
## Problem

`tg-ctl status` reported `autostart: NOT enabled` even though the daemon IS autostarted on boot — supervised by an external launchd job `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl` (a LaunchAgent with `KeepAlive`/`RunAtLoad`) whose `ProgramArguments` is `bun /Users/ultra/.files/bin/tg-ctl run`, i.e. the exact same daemon. The autostart check only recognized tg-ctl's OWN `enable` unit (`com.agenttools.tg-ctl.tg-ctl`), which is absent here — so status lied while launchd kept the daemon alive across reboots. (`Closes #88`)

## Fix

`status` now ALSO probes launchd for an external supervisor before declaring "NOT enabled":

- `launchctl list` → loaded labels; `launchctl print <domain>/<label>` per job → its `ProgramArguments`.
- Match any job (other than tg-ctl's own label) whose argv runs THIS tg-ctl binary with the `run` subcommand. Discovered by **what the job runs**, not by hardcoding `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl`.
- Reports `autostart: enabled (via launchd: <label>)`.
- Own-mechanism detection is unchanged and **takes precedence** (a daemon enabled via `tg-ctl enable` keeps its precise kind/label).

### Robustness
- The pure policy (matcher, `launchctl list`/`print` parsers, precedence formatter) lives in `features/tg-ctl/autostart.ts` — fully unit-testable with mocked launchctl output. Only the spawn is impure (in the entrypoint).
- Non-macOS / launchctl unavailable / any hiccup → wrapped, falls back to existing logic, **never crashes** status.
- Root (uid 0) uses the `system` launchd domain, not `gui/0`.
- binPath match is basename-aware so a **symlink-vs-realpath** mismatch (rig writing the target while we resolve the `~/.files/bin/tg-ctl` symlink) still matches — the exact scenario this fix exists for.
- Consolidated the duplicated unit-label helper to one source of truth.

## Tests

`tests/ctl-autostart.test.ts` (+17 cases): external-supervisor detection (enabled/not), own-label exclusion, `run`-requirement, basename symlink/target match, `launchctl list`/`print` parsers incl. a **real captured `launchctl print` fixture** (guards against macOS format drift), and `autostartStatusLine` precedence (own-unit > external > NOT enabled) + non-macOS graceful. Full `bun test` green (1448 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail).

## Live verification (read-only, no restart)

Before: `autostart: NOT enabled — run `tg-ctl enable` to start at login`
After:  `autostart: enabled (via launchd: ai.hyperide.tg-ctl)` (pid matches the launchd-supervised daemon)

## Review

`review diff --staged`: `## gemini [ok]` (the `claude` seat spun an interactive TUI that corrupted machine output, so I fell to `gemini` for a clean verdict, per the dispatch note). Earlier `claude`/`codex` passes surfaced the symlink-fragility, root-domain, and testability findings — all addressed in this PR.

title: fix(tg-ctl): dead-letter the backlog stranded by an unscoped-question expiry (Closes #58)
body:
## What

An **unscoped** forwarded question (the hook ran without `TMUX_PANE`) that expires unanswered no longer silently strands the inbound messages deferred behind it (#58).

An unscoped question defers inbound for **any** pane (`paneHasPendingQuestion`'s fail-closed `if (!pb.req.paneId) return true`), so its backlog can sit on several panes at once and there was no single pane key to dead-letter — the expiry timer dropped the queue without telling anyone. The equivalent **scoped** socket-close path already dead-lettered via `onAbandon` + the user notice; the unscoped expiry was the gap.

## How

On the unscoped abandon (timeout / hook socket close / send failure), the daemon now **sweeps every pane that still holds a backlog** and dead-letters the idle ones, emitting the same `⚠️ … were NOT delivered. Resend them.` notice.

- `DeferQueues.panesWithBacklog()` enumerates panes with a non-empty queue.
- `onUnscopedAbandon()` sweeps them through the **existing per-pane abandon guard** (`onQuestionAbandoned`), so a pane that still has **another** live question (its answer flushes the queue legitimately) or an in-flight flush (it owns the queue) is left untouched — no other handler's messages are dropped.
- The unscoped entry is removed from `pending` **before** the sweep, so the guard sees the real post-removal state.
- Threaded through `startHookServer` + `handleHookSocketLine` into all three unscoped removal paths.

The **no-wedge guarantee is unchanged**: the stale text is never pasted into the freed pane (the agent moved on), and routing un-wedges immediately.

## Tests

- The NO-WEDGE integration test now asserts the dead-letter notice fires (was pinned to the silent-loss behavior).
- A **guard** test proves a still-live scoped question's backlog is **not** dropped by an unscoped expiry on the same pane (the dangerous failure mode).
- A **socket-close** test covers that removal path distinctly from the timeout path.
- A `panesWithBacklog` unit test.
- Full `bun test ./tests` suite green (1460 pass).

## Deferred (test-hardening, follow-up)

A true **multi-pane** end-to-end sweep test and the **send-failure** removal-path test need a multi-pane fake-tmux harness / a forced-send-failure hook the current single-`%1` harness doesn't support. The sweep logic over the unit-tested `panesWithBacklog` is the same loop; reviewer (opus) confirmed no functionality-breaking bugs across two passes.

Closes #58

title: feat(tg-ctl): /new flat-chat command — spawn an agent via inline buttons (Closes #27)
body:
Closes #27.

## What

A flat-chat `/new [<model>] [<dir>] <name> [<task>]` slash command that spawns a fresh agent session straight from Telegram. Omitted model/dir are chosen interactively via inline buttons — a recent-project picker for `<dir>` (the in-use project dirs **and their `..` parents**, normalized, deduped, LRU/MRU-ranked) and a model picker for `<model>`. A `<name>` colliding with a live tmux window is a non-blocking warning. With name+dir+model all supplied, the agent spawns immediately, passing the optional `<task>` as its initial prompt (after a `--` so a dash-prefixed task isn't parsed as a flag); otherwise the daemon walks the interactive flow.

This is the **non-topic sibling** of the forum-topics `/new` flow: it carries its own in-memory pending-state machine (`NewSession`) and its own callback prefixes (`tnm:`/`tnp:`) that never collide with the topic flow's `tgm:`/`tgp:`/`tgr:`, and it works regardless of `control.topics`. The whole feature is fail-soft (no path may throw into the poll loop) and 1:1 routing stays byte-identical when no `/new` is in flight.

## Key design points

- New PURE module `features/tg-ctl/new-command.ts`: arg parser (order-tolerant model/dir prefix; a lone model alias is reclaimed as the name), parents-aware LRU/MRU dir ranker (capped parents per cwd so a deep path can't starve the menu), name-uniqueness, button keyboards + callback parsers, the `NewSession` state shape.
- `updates.ts`: parses `/new` and the `tnm:`/`tnp:` taps. A typed **absolute-path** answer while a `/new` awaits its dir routes to `new-answer` (positive path-form gate, not `!isLikelySlashCommand`) — so ordinary prose and harness passthrough commands (`/compact`, `/clear`) still reach the live agent, and single-component paths (`/tmp`) are accepted. Topic messages are routed earlier and never reach this gate.
- `DAEMON_SLASH_COMMANDS` is **derived from `botCommandNames()`** (the set the bot-commands test pins to `textAction`'s handled verbs) so it can't drift as new commands are added.
- `tg-ctl`: the handlers + a non-topic spawn-into-named-window (reusing the topic spawn plumbing without `TG_TOPIC`); typed root `/` rejected; file-not-dir rejected; spawn failure re-offers the model keyboard.

title: fix(tg-ctl): cleanExit removes the pidfile only when it owns it (Closes #93)
body:
## Bug (daily-critical)

The tg-ctl daemon's `cleanExit()` unlinked `ctx.paths.pid` **unconditionally**. On a launchd relaunch a departing daemon — or one whose ownership a newer instance already took over by rewriting `tg-ctl.<bot>.pid` with its own pid — would delete the **live successor's** pidfile. `tg-ctl status` (which reads the pidfile) then falsely reports **"not running"** while the real daemon is alive and long-polling. The flock (the true singleton) is unaffected, so routing keeps working — but the operator sees a false negative.

## Fix

New pure helper `ownsPidFile(content, ownPid)` in `features/tg-ctl/lock.ts`. `cleanExit` now removes the pidfile **only when its content is still our own pid**.

- The flock LOSER is unaffected — it `process.exit(0)`s at the flock check (line ~1646) **before** the pidfile write (~1649), so it never writes a pidfile and its `cleanExit` (defined later) is never reached.
- The WINNER's graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT/idle-exit still removes its OWN pidfile (the existing singleton test covers this).
- `stopDaemon`'s two unlinks are unchanged — they are operator-driven removals of a specific known-pid daemon (stale-clean / post-SIGTERM), not the owner-blind unlink the bug was about.

Read-then-unlink is not atomic, so this **narrows** rather than fully closes the race; the flock — not the pidfile — is the real singleton (spec §6), so the pidfile is informational and this keeps `status` honest in practice. Documented in the helper.

## RED-first test

`tests/ctl-singleton-integration.test.ts` adds a test that parks a FOREIGN live pid in the pidfile (simulating a successor taking ownership), SIGTERMs the daemon, and asserts the foreign pidfile **SURVIVES**. Confirmed RED before the fix (the blind unlink deleted it), GREEN after. Unit tests in `tests/ctl-lock.test.ts` pin `ownsPidFile`'s boundaries (own / foreign / absent / garbage).

## Verification

- Full `bun test ./tests`: **1531 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail** (1532 tests, 96 files).
- Review gate: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` → **[ok]**, no blockers (two rounds; reviewer's correctness asks re flock→pidfile ordering and other unlink sites independently re-verified in-code).
- Version bumped 1.19.0 → 1.19.1 (patch, per the `fix` convention).

Closes #93

title: fix(tg-ctl): stop AskUserQuestion forwarding a duplicate Telegram card (Closes #97)
body:
## Problem (tg-cli#97)

An agent's `AskUserQuestion` is forwarded to Telegram as an inline-button card. After the CTO taps an answer (which DOES reach the harness), a SECOND identical card appears; tapping it yields an "expired" toast — reading as "answer not accepted" though the first already landed. The answer path also logged nothing.

Root cause: the `requestId` is a stable hash of (session, question text), and the in-flight dedup (`activeButtonKeys`) only guards CONCURRENT duplicates — it's released the instant the question is answered. Two compounding causes:
1. **Double coverage** — Claude installs both `PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion` and a `PermissionRequest:*` catch-all; both fire for an `AskUserQuestion`, normalize to the same requestId, and forward.
2. **No idempotency across the answer boundary** — once the first card is answered the dedup key is freed, so the same question re-firing posts a second card (proven from logs: same requestId forwarded twice, 37s apart).

## Fix

- **A — answered-replay cache (`tg-ctl`).** A re-forward of an already-answered requestId replays the stored answer down the hook socket and posts NO new card. Scoped to `kind === 'question'` (a permission's stable requestId is never silently re-replayed — a behavioral/security boundary), bounded by a 5-minute window (env-overridable for tests) after which the entry is pruned so a genuinely new question reusing the hash gets a fresh card. Swept on each record → bounded.
- **B — drop the double-cover (`hook-normalize.ts`).** An `AskUserQuestion` delivered via the `PermissionRequest` matcher normalizes to `null`; only the dedicated `PreToolUse` matcher forwards it. Verified safe: the `PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion` matcher has shipped in every `hook-install` version, so this never strips the only delivery path.
- **C — ack + observability.** The answer path now logs `ask-answered:` (was silent); the tap toast reads "✓ sent to the agent"; a tap on an already-answered card (within the window) reads "already answered" instead of the misleading "expired".

## Tests

`tests/ctl-hook-normalize.test.ts`: PermissionRequest-delivered AskUserQuestion → null; PreToolUse + no-event back-compat still forward.

`tests/ctl-answered-replay-integration.test.ts` (new, daemon-level): replay-in-window posts no second card; "already answered" toast; past-window prune → fresh card; aged-out tap → "expired"; answered permission is never replayed; both matchers firing → exactly one card.

Full tg-cli suite green locally (1534 pass). One unrelated topic-spawn integration test is flaky under full-suite load (passes 55/55 in isolation).

Closes #97
