title: fix(tg-ctl): durable forwarded-question state — late-deliver + lossless reconnect (Closes #99)
body:
## Problem

The `tg-ctl` daemon held all forwarded-question state ONLY in memory, so two failures hurt the CTO's question channel:

1. **Tap-loss** — a Telegram tap that arrived AFTER a question's hook socket closed (the agent's 120s hook budget elapsed, or the agent process died) hit the `!pending` branch and was **DROPPED**. You pressed a button and nothing reached the harness.
2. **Restart-loss** — a daemon restart (crash-relaunch / stop+start) wiped every pending and recently-answered question.

Closes #99.

## Fix (one mechanism: persist scoped questions + answered-replay on every mutation, restore on bootstrap)

- **Persist** to a new durable file (`tg-ctl.<bot>.questions.json`, atomic temp+rename) on every mutation; restore before the poll loop starts. New PURE module `features/tg-ctl/question-store.ts` owns the on-disk format (versioned envelope, separate age windows for questions vs answered, recency cap at both serialize and parse, corrupt-file tolerance). The entrypoint owns I/O + authoritative `req` normalization.
- **Late-deliver** — a tap with no live pending socket injects the chosen option into the asking pane (the established text-reply inject path). A socket-closed scoped question moves into `abandonedButtons` (never defers its pane's inbound), retained for `TG_CTL_ABANDONED_RETAIN_MS` (default 30 min) **enforced at delivery time** (not only on restore), so a quiet daemon can't inject a long-stale answer. The retained card keeps its keyboard.
- **Reconnect** — the `tg-ctl ask` client for a SCOPED question reconnect-and-resends the same requestId across a mid-block socket drop; the restored daemon re-attaches the pending entry (no duplicate card) or replays the stored answer.
- **Single-delivery** — the claim (`abandoned`→`answered:pane`) is taken **before** the inject await, so a reconnect racing the inject hits `already-pane-delivered` and the agent gets the answer exactly once; rolled back on inject failure for a re-tap.
- **Dead-card UX** — a genuinely-dead card (unscoped, or send-failed) has its keyboard cleared on expiry; a successfully late-delivered card is cleared too (no misleading "expired" on a re-tap in the answered/retention gap).

Permissions + unscoped questions keep the single-attempt path (resending would duplicate the card); unscoped questions are **never persisted/resurrected** (they defer ALL panes). The #98 answered-replay is extended (a persisted `delivery` channel: `socket` re-fire replays vs `pane` late-delivered → no double-deliver), not changed.

## Tests

**11 unit** (`question-store` round-trip, separate age windows, forward-compat version guard, recency cap at write+read, corrupt/malformed-input tolerance) + **16 integration** (persist; late-deliver + failure-retry + busy-pane; single-delivery; reconnect-during-inject race; pane-delivery survives restart; restore→tap→late-deliver headline; mid-send scoped backfill; mid-send unscoped keyboard-clear; retention enforced at delivery time; unscoped not-resurrected safety; reconnect re-attach; reconnect replay; expiry keyboard-clear).

Full suite green: **1599 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**.

## Notes / accepted bounds (documented in code)

- A SIGKILL in the sub-ms window between a card posting and its persist (or the sub-inject window during late-delivery) can lose a record / duplicate a card — strictly better than the pre-PR drop; full closure needs a write-ahead marker, not worth it.
- In-memory maps are bounded by **age** (the file is count-bounded); a count-bound in memory is omitted deliberately for a trusted single-human channel.
- The LIVE socket answer-path still leaves its keyboard (pre-existing #98 behavior, out of this PR's scope) — a candidate one-line consistency follow-up.

title: fix(md-pdf): network-blackhole + drop --embed-resources for md→PDF (Closes #102)
body: ## What Brings `convertMdToPdf` (the `tg --file report.md` → PDF render) to security parity with the surfaces `convertHtmlToPdf` closed in #96. Closes #102. The markdown→PDF render (pandoc → headless Chrome `--print-to-pdf`, result uploaded to Telegram) had two open surfaces: - **No network blackhole.** Chrome printed without `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND`, so a markdown doc with a remote resource (`![x](http://host/p.png)`, a remote font/iframe) made Chrome **fetch** it at print time — tracking pixel / SSRF / network egress. - **pandoc-stage local-file inlining.** pandoc was invoked with `--embed-resources --resource-path`, which base64-inlines **any** local file the markdown references (`![x](/etc/passwd)`, `![x](../secret)`) into the produced HTML — zero attacker effort, every referenced path — and fetched remote `src=`s at the pandoc stage. ## How - Extract a single hardened `printToPdf` helper into `features/md-pdf/convert.ts` carrying the **DNS blackhole** + the empty-PDF check. Both `convertMdToPdf` and the two `code-pdf` paths route through it, so the print sandbox flags live in ONE place and can never drift again (the exact gap #96 left). `code-pdf` now imports `printToPdf` instead of carrying its own copy. - Drop `--embed-resources` / `--resource-path` from the md pandoc invocation (matching #96's `.html` decision). The stylesheet becomes an external `file://` `` Chrome resolves at print time. Cost: a relative LOCAL image shows broken in the PDF; remote images were blackholed regardless. ## Proof A real-render integration test plants a unique secret in local files referenced by an ``, renders the real pandoc→Chrome chain, and asserts the secret bytes are **never** inlined into pandoc's HTML (no `data:…;base64`, no plaintext, no base64), the refs survive only as relative references, and the output is a valid PDF without the secret. Argv tests pin the blackhole flag present and `--embed-resources`/`--resource-path` absent. Independently verified: the OLD `--embed-resources` invocation **does** inline the secret as a `data:…;base64` URI; the shipped invocation produces **zero** leaks — the test is not vacuous. `bun test`: **1601 pass / 0 fail** (pandoc + Chrome present locally, so the integration exfil proof actually executed; the md-pdf file alone: 6 pass / 0 skip). ## Scope / honesty This closes #102's two surfaces. It is **NOT** full parity with the `.html` path and does not claim to be — two residuals remain, both tracked and documented in the spec + CHANGELOG: - **#103** (shared with `.html`): Chrome still loads an absolute-path / `file:`-scheme `` from the `file://` document into the PDF (the blackhole doesn't apply to `file://`). - **#104** (md only): no `sanitizeReportHtml` / `stripEventHandlerAttrs`, so a hostile `.md` with raw `

title: feat(tg-ctl): private-chat forum topics (Bot API 9.4)
body:
## Summary

- New config flag `control.private_topics: true` — when set, each `/new` agent spawn calls Bot API 9.4 `createForumTopic` against the user's private chat, creating a per-agent thread in Telegram
- The returned `message_thread_id` is stamped into the spawned tmux window as `TG_TOPIC=<id>` so the agent's outbound `tg` replies automatically thread back into the right topic
- A `bound` `TopicBinding` is written to the existing topics store; inbound routing (`topicsEnabled: cfg.topics || cfg.privateTopics`) then routes replies back to the agent pane automatically
- The `forum_topic_created` Telegram echo is silently absorbed (the binding is already `bound` by the time the echo arrives in the next poll cycle)
- **Graceful fallback**: `createForumTopic` failure (Threaded Mode not enabled in BotFather) → logs once, falls back to current flat-chat behaviour without any user-visible disruption

- [ ] `bun test` — 1669+ tests pass; 6 new tests in `tests/ctl-private-topics-integration.test.ts`

- [ ] Scenario 3: `forum_topic_created` echo does NOT trigger a second spawn or re-enter the `/new` flow
- [ ] Unit: `parseControlConfig` + `resolveControlConfig` correctly handle `private_topics:` key

## Manual activation

1. Enable "Threaded Mode" for your bot in BotFather
2. Add to your `~/.config/tg-ctl/config.yaml` (or wherever your config lives):
   ```yaml
   control:
     private_topics: true
   ```

title: fix(tg-ctl): /agent no-match guard — error reply, never deliver to wrong agent
body:
## Problem

When `/agent ext hello` finds no tmux pane matching "ext", the handler was falling through to `postAgentPicker(all, message)`. With only one other agent visible (rig), `subset.length === 1` triggered auto-inject — silently delivering the message to rig.

Root cause: the trailing comment `// selector matched nothing → the whole text is the message, ask over all` was not an else branch — it was a plain fallthrough. `subset` stayed `= candidates` and the full `action.all` message was treated as if it were a normal unaddressed message.

## Fix

Convert the fallthrough to an explicit `else` branch. On no-match:
1. Log `[routing] /agent <selector>: NO MATCH — candidates: <list>`
2. Reply to the user: `No agent matching "ext" found.\nRunning: rig · claude`
3. `return false` — never delivers to any agent

## Also

- Add structured `[routing]` log lines at every dispatch decision point (`/agent` confident/ambiguous/no-match, reply recognized/gone/unrecognized, topic thread)
- Update `docs/specs/agent-addressing.md` and `features/tg-ctl/agent-match.ts` comment to match new no-match contract
- New integration test `ctl-agent-nomatch-integration.test.ts`: 1 pass, asserts exactly 1 plain-text error message, no inject into %5001

## Test

1674 pass, 0 fail (full suite)

## Ext agent status

The ext agent IS running (`claude --resume ext`, pane %0, pid 28924, window name "ext"). It should be detected by `listAgentCandidates()`. The misroute to rig happened when ext wasn't running at the time the message was sent. This fix prevents any such fallthrough regardless of which agents are running.

title: fix(tg-ctl): question buttons — answer never sent + extra Enter on multi-question (tg#5741)
body:
Fixes #118. Reported by Alex in tg#5741: «answered: Да — подними argocd-server и выкати #602 … Пишется и никогда не отправляется на самом деле, и ещё если вопросов несколько, то надо в конце ещё раз enter нажать».

## Bug 1 — the tapped answer is never actually delivered

**Root cause.** `formatAgentHookOutput` (claude+question branch) emitted
`{hookSpecificOutput:{permissionDecision:"allow",updatedInput:{…}}}` **without `hookEventName:"PreToolUse"`**. Claude Code ≥2.1.198 (the installed version) validates hook JSON output and rejects the ENTIRE output when `hookSpecificOutput` lacks `hookEventName` — its parser carries a dedicated error string for exactly this case (`hookSpecificOutput is missing required field "hookEventName"`, extracted from the 2.1.198 binary). Result: the daemon logs `ask-answered`, the card edits to "answered: …", the toast says "✓ sent to the agent" — and the agent opens the local question dialog anyway. The answer is dropped on the harness side.

**Incident proof** (daemon log + durable question store):
```
[2026-07-02T08:30:06.115Z] ask-forward posted: … req=[REDACTED scanner match 73c9969a2fa2] … messageId=5740
[2026-07-02T08:31:23.893Z] ask-answered: … key=[REDACTED scanner match 73c9969a2fa2] label=Да — подними argocd-server и выкати #602 messageId=5740
questions.json: {"key":"[REDACTED scanner match 73c9969a2fa2]", …, "delivery":"socket"}
```
The tap went down the LIVE hook socket one minute before the complaint — the daemon side worked; the emitted envelope was rejected by CC.

**Why it used to work:** the spec's live spike passed on CC 2.1.170 (spec §8 "Verification status") and its own caveat predicted this exact contract drift ("the contract is an UNDOCUMENTED internal … add a canary that fails loudly on contract drift"); the canary was deferred.

**Fix.**
- The envelope now stamps `hookEventName:"PreToolUse"` (`buildClaudeQuestionAnswerOutput`).
- `updatedInput` echoes the **original `tool_input`** (carried on the ButtonRequest by hook-normalize AND preserved across the daemon socket boundary — `normalizeButtonRequest` used to drop it, which also silently downgraded an ExitPlanMode "Proceed" to a bare allow) with the collected `answers` merged in. 2.1.198 schema-validates `updatedInput` wholesale against the tool's input schema (option `description` is REQUIRED there, `preview` must survive), which the lossy rebuilt shape could violate; the rebuild stays only as a fallback for manual callers.
- **Stale-daemon repair:** the ask client rebuilds a single-question reply coming from a RUNNING daemon that predates `hookEventName` (live-symlink deploys update the hook client immediately, the daemon only on restart), so the fix takes effect on merge; `tg-ctl restart` completes the daemon side.

## Bug 2 — multi-question needs an extra Enter at the end

**Root cause.** `hook-normalize.ts` bailed to the local UI for `questions.length !== 1`, so a 2-4-question AskUserQuestion never reached Telegram and had to be finished in the local dialog, whose multi-question flow ends on an extra final Enter.

**Fix.** The 2.1.198 input schema supports 1-4 questions plus an `answers` record ("User answers collected by the permission component"), and the tool's `call()` returns `input.answers` directly — a complete record finishes the tool with zero local keypresses. A multi-question call now forwards as one **sequential card per question** (`(i/N)` title suffix; per-question stable requestIds so replay/reconnect dedup is unchanged; the next card posts only after the previous answer), and the ask client composes ONE combined PreToolUse reply from the collected answers. **ALL-OR-NOTHING:** any multiSelect/free-form/duplicate-text question, or any declined/timed-out card, bails the whole call to the local UI — a partial answers record is never emitted (CC would silently record unanswered questions as "(no option selected)"). For the same reason a set member is **never late-delivered**: once the local dialog takes over it owns ALL the questions, so a late tap on an abandoned member answers "expired" and retires the card instead of injecting a lone answer into a possibly-different prompt (reconnect re-attach across a daemon bounce still works).

## Review iterations (review-cli, 3 rounds)

- Round 1 (pool 2): codex found (a) the daemon-side `normalizeButtonRequest` drops `toolInput` at the socket boundary — fixed + round-trip integration test (proven to fail with the fix reverted); (b) duplicate question texts would collide requestIds / collapse the answers record — now bail to the local UI + test.
- Round 2 (pool 2, partially timed out; gemini seat completed): documentation-clarity advice only, already covered by the module comments.
- Round 3 (single codex seat, long timeout): (P1) late-tap on an abandoned multi-question member could inject a lone answer into the wrong local prompt — fixed with a `multiQuestion` marker + refusal + integration test (kills the client mid-collection; proven to fail with the guard disabled); (P2) a stale bare-allow assertion in `ctl-answered-replay-integration` — updated to expect the now-correct `updatedInput` echo.

## Scope

title: feat(tg-ctl): harness-limit notify + auto-continue, /tasks board, reaction lifecycle (#113, #114, #115)
body:
Implements Alex's tg#5698 / tg#5699 requests as three coherent features, and
fixes the three bugs a prior (lost) WIP leaked live. Closes #113, #114, #115.

## Features

### 1. Harness limit/error notify + auto-continue (#113)
- `tg-ctl harness-event` — a **StopFailure**-hook subcommand. Reads the hook
  payload on stdin (+ transcript tail), extracts the reason + reset time, and
  messages the operator that a session hit its limit / errored.
- When the reset time is parseable the notification carries an inline
  **auto-continue** button; tapping it arms a timer that injects `continue`
  into the originating tmux pane at reset time (immediately if already past).
- Schedules persist to `*.schedules.json` and **re-arm on daemon restart**.
- `tg-ctl install-hooks` now also provisions the StopFailure hook (idempotent).

### 2. `/tasks [<agent>] [<status>]` board (#115)
- New bot command: composes `task list --json` + `gh pr list --json` into a
  rich-HTML table (id linked, title, state, due, PR, CI), sent via
  `sendRichMessage`. Filterable by normalized task-cli status, scoped to a
  fuzzy-matched agent's project. **Missing PR/CI renders as an em dash, never
  fabricated.** Published in the bot menu (invariant test passes).

### 3. Reaction lifecycle (#114)
- 👀 working → 😴 stalled (limit-stop) → 👌 done. Alex's literal ⏳/✅ are
  `REACTION_INVALID` for a bot (verified live); 😴/👌 are the allowed proxies
  (Alex allowed "или что-то подобное"). `harness-event` sets 😴 on the source
  message; `tg --tag answer --reply-to <id>` flips `<id>` to 👌.

## Bug fixes (the live leak)
A prior WIP's smoke test leaked a real, **stale** "session limit" alert to
Alex's chat with an unrendered `%0` placeholder. This branch is a from-scratch
rebuild that fixes all three by construction:
- **(a) Test isolation** — the automated suite already runs against a local
  `Bun.serve` fake with a fake token/chat (never a real chat); additionally
  `harness-event --dry-run` renders WITHOUT sending, so any dev smoke is safe.
- **(b) Staleness guard** — `buildLimitNotification` returns null (suppresses
  the whole alert) when the reset time is already in the past. Proven by unit
  + integration tests.
- **(c) `%0` template** — every string is a template literal + `escapeHtml`;
  tests assert the rendered text carries no `%\d`/`%s`/`{token}` placeholder.

## Architecture
Logic lives in PURE, DI-testable modules (repo convention); the daemon/CLI is
thin glue: `features/tg-ctl/limits.ts`, `reactions.ts`, `tasks-command.ts`,
`schedule-store.ts`, plus wiring in `tg-ctl`, `tg`, `updates.ts`, `hook-install.ts`.

## Test evidence (all isolated from any real chat)
- Unit: `ctl-limits` (18), `ctl-reactions` (5), `ctl-tasks-command` (8),
  `ctl-schedule-store` (6), `ctl-hook-install` (+4).
- Integration (fake Bot API): `ctl-harness-event-integration` (notify + button
  + staleness + `--dry-run` + 😴), `ctl-tasks-integration` (rich table via
  `sendRichMessage`), `ctl-auto-continue-integration` (tap→arm→persist→ack;
  restart→re-arm→fire), `cli-answer-reaction` (👌 flip).
- Full suite: **1730 pass / 0 fail** (a pre-existing flaky
  `ctl-topic-spawn-integration` timing test intermittently fails on `main` too —
  unrelated to this change).

title: feat(replies): --session accepts a tmux window name, not only a pane id
body:
## What

`tg replies --session <arg>` now scopes recall by a tmux **window name** (`--session ext`), not only a pane id.

- **`%`-prefixed arg → pane id** (unchanged, backward compatible).
- **Otherwise → window name**, resolved to the pane-id set of every window whose `#{window_name}` **exactly** equals `<arg>` (exact match, not prefix — `ext` never matches `ext: diagram`), **unioned** across sessions when the name repeats.
- **Unknown window name → structured error**: non-zero exit + `no tmux window named '<name>'` (never a silent empty recall).
- Default (no `--session`) and `--all-sessions` scope are unchanged.

Resolution shells out to `tmux list-panes -a -F "#{pane_id}\t#{window_name}"` — pane id first, TAB-delimited, so window names containing spaces survive intact.

## Why

Pane ids (`%7`) are un-typeable from memory; the CTO wants to scope by human window name like `ext`. Closes alex-mextner/tg-cli#121.

## How

- `features/replies/window.ts` (new): `parseWindowPanes` (pure) + `resolveWindowPanes` (tmux shell-out, injectable runner).
- `select.ts`: `filterByPane` → `filterByPanes` (pane-SET membership); `selectHistory` takes `string[] | null`.
- `cli.ts`: `resolveScope`/`scopeSuffix` helpers, `resolveWindow` DI dep, USAGE + example.
- `args.ts`: `--session` error wording; `tg`: wired `resolveWindow`.
- Docs: README, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG; version `1.24.0 → 1.25.0`.

## Tests

TDD (red → green). New `tests/replies-window.test.ts` + updates to `replies-{args,select,cli,roundtrip}`. Full suite: **1720 pass, 0 fail** (`bun test`).

## Review

`review diff --staged` — Gemini `[ok]`; the rest of the board died on exhausted API credits (infra, not this diff). The one advisory finding (are `features/replies/*` exports a "public API" needing a major bump?) is a non-issue: the CLI is the public surface, these exports are internal/DI-only, and the CLI stays backward-compatible.

title: fix(tg-ctl): flush deferred backlog on unscoped blocker answer
body:
## What

Fixes #127: answering an **unscoped** blocker (a permission/question hook that ran without `TMUX_PANE` — the common Claude Code case) never flushed the deferred inbound backlog, so the reply never reached the agent, and the ✍️ "queued" reaction on the original message never flipped to 👀.

## Why

Deferred inbound items only carried wrapped text, with no link back to the source Telegram message. The unscoped-answer path had no way to know which reaction to update, and (per Alex's report, tg#5855) the flush itself could be dropped for the unscoped case, silently losing the message.

## Fix

- `DeferQueues<T>` is now generic (`DeferredItem = { text, messageId }` in production; existing unit tests still drive it with bare strings).
- Every queued item carries its source Telegram `messageId` end-to-end through enqueue/flush/redefer/drop.
- `flushDeferred` reacts correctly per outcome: delivered → 👀, failed/dead-lettered → ✍️ cleared (never leaves a "queued" mark on a message that's gone), re-deferred → keeps ✍️ (still genuinely waiting).
- Two races found while building this are also closed:
  - a flush-rerun request that could otherwise strand a backlog when a second answer landed inside the first flush's re-entrancy window
  - a previously-silent paste-failure path (pane gone mid-flush) that now clears the reaction and warns the user instead of dropping the message with no trace

## Test plan

- `tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts` (+370 lines), including:
  - `tg#5855: answering an UNSCOPED permission flushes the deferred backlog and flips its ✍️ to 👀` — the core repro/fix
  - two-unscoped-blockers hardening (answering one must not flush while the other is still open)
  - the unscoped-abandon sweep actually clearing ✍️ on dead-letter (not just inferred from sharing code with the scoped case — added after review flagged the gap)
  - a real paste-failure (pane vanishes mid-flush) clearing ✍️ and warning the user instead of silently dropping (added after review flagged the gap)
- Full suite: `bun test` — 1790 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail (verified locally, twice, on the final commit)
- Reviewed via `review diff --pool 1` — clean `[ok]`, no actionable findings on the final diff

Refs: #127, tg#5855, tg#5922

title: fix(hooks): remove pre-send-photo full-window-screenshot block
body:
## Summary
- **Commit 1** — Removes `looks_like_vscode_window()` from `features/hooks/review-descriptor/pre_send_photo.py` — the pixel heuristic that unconditionally BLOCKED every full VS Code window screenshot (dark, uniform left activity-bar strip), regardless of whether the content inside was actually broken. Added 2026-07-01 (`87b4522`) to force cropped preview-pane proofs. Superseded by Alex's 2026-07-03 standard (tg#6041): full-window screenshots with Explorer/Inspector/Logs panels ARE the desired HyperIDE diagnostic proof format now. False-positived on legitimate full-window proofs at least twice in one day (HYP-891). Removed at Alex's explicit direction (tg#6063/6064).
- **Commit 2** — Adds `looks_like_empty_vscode_watermark()`: Alex's follow-up idea (tg#6071) for a narrower, more precise successor signal — VS Code's own central "watermark" (the keybinding-hint rows shown ONLY when the active editor group has ZERO open tabs), instead of matching any full window. A real content-full window (code, a rendered preview, busy panels) cannot produce a small compact glyph cluster on an overwhelmingly flat central pane.
- **Deliberate choice: WARN-only, not a block.** The thresholds are reasoned from VS Code's known watermark layout, not calibrated against a captured reference screenshot (none was available at implementation time). Blocking on an unvalidated pixel heuristic is exactly the HYP-891 failure mode this same PR already fixed once. It surfaces a stderr warning in the audit trail without bricking the send; promoting to a block is a follow-up once real field data exists.
- `review visual --strict` (vision-model verdict on the actual image content) remains the only gate that can block a send — noted in-code as an accepted, unproven tradeoff.
- Bump 1.25.0 → 1.26.2 (renumbered after rebasing/merging onto main's own 1.26.0, from tg-cli#113/#114/#115).

## Implementation notes (commit 2)
Iterated through ~14 rounds of `review diff` against the watermark heuristic; every threshold/box/tolerance choice and the reasoning behind it is recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`. Highlights of what review caught and what got fixed:
- Background-color estimate is quantized-bucket based (not exact-tuple) to survive PNG/JPEG re-compression and font-AA noise.
- Compactness (span) check is outlier-robust (trims coordinates, not raw min/max) so a single stray non-bg pixel can't hide the real cluster — and the trim itself was fixed to never collapse to a degenerate 0-span core.
- Sample box widened + shifted right (was symmetric around the window center) because VS Code's watermark centers on the EDITOR PART, which is offset right by the Activity Bar + Explorer sidebar on the common "Explorer open, nothing docked right" layout.
- Density floor lowered (with test evidence) so a realistically SPARSE watermark (thin icon+text strokes, not a bulky filled block) still clears it.
- Compactness caps tightened from 70-80% of the box (effectively disabled) to 35-40%, with a dedicated "moderate spread, still low density" test locking in the boundary.
- Decode latency bounded: a cropped-box size cap (with Pillow <9.1 fallback), a file-size guard, AND a decoded-pixel-count guard (a small, highly-compressible file can still decode to tens of megapixels) — all checked before the expensive `Image.convert("RGB")` call, all still fail-open.
- Several test-fixture bugs found and fixed along the way (draw-step vs. sample-step aliasing that made two different negative fixtures pass for the wrong reason; a misleading no-PIL test that never actually exercised the PIL-absent code path).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test tests/hooks-watermark-detector.test.ts tests/hooks-review-descriptor.test.ts tests/hooks-photo-integration.test.ts tests/hooks-runner.test.ts tests/hooks-cli.test.ts tests/hooks-non-breaking.test.ts` — 111 pass / 0 fail.
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile features/hooks/review-descriptor/pre_send_photo.py` — compiles clean.
- [x] `review diff --pool 1 --staged` iterated to a clean pass on the full watermark-heuristic diff (~14 rounds; see CHANGELOG.md for the full trail of findings addressed).
- [x] Merged origin/main (which had advanced to 1.26.0 via tg-cli#113/#114/#115 while this PR was open); resolved the package.json/CHANGELOG version conflict by renumbering to 1.26.1/1.26.2. Full suite (120 tests) green post-merge.
- [x] `review diff --staged` re-run on the full merged diff (this PR's watermark work + all of main's pulled-in content) — no actionable findings.
- [x] GitHub Actions CI green: CodeQL (both gates), dependency-review, gitleaks (both runs), leftover-grep, review-threads, and the `test` job — all pass.
- [x] Alex to confirm the WARN-vs-block decision and threshold reasoning are acceptable (this PR is unmerged pending his sign-off per team policy: no self-merge). **Confirmed directly by Alex via Telegram, tg#6276: "Давай warn."**

title: fix(tg-ctl): unscoped blocker answer never flushed the deferred backlog; flip writing-hand to eyes on delivery (Fixes #127, tg#5855)
body:
Rebase of PR #129 onto current main. #129's branch was cut before PR #120
independently merged the same bundled feature set (/tasks command,
harness-limit notify, reaction lifecycle, schedule-store) that #129's
single commit also happened to carry — so #129 became unmergeable
(CONFLICTING) once #120 landed. This commit carries ONLY the actual
defer-flush fix: the 25 files that duplicated #120 are dropped entirely
(main already has them); nothing from #120 is touched or reverted.
Verified byte-for-byte: every file below now matches #129's original
fix commit (f07ac8b) exactly, confirming nothing was lost or altered
in the process, and that no file outside this list differs between the
original commit and current main.

Deferred inbound messages (queued while a pane has an open blocking
question) carried only their wrapped text, with no link back to the
Telegram message they came from. When an unscoped blocker (a question
with no TMUX_PANE) was answered, the daemon had no way to tell the
deferred queue which reaction to update, so the ✍️ "queued" mark on the
original message never flipped to 👀 on delivery — and in the unscoped
path specifically, the answer's flush could be dropped entirely, so the
agent never saw the reply at all.

Fix: DeferQueues<T> is now generic (DeferredItem = { text, messageId }
in production, bare strings still work for existing unit tests) so every
queued item carries its source Telegram message id end-to-end through
enqueue/flush/redefer/drop. flushDeferred uses that id to react
correctly on every outcome: delivered items get 👀, failed/dead-lettered
items get their ✍️ cleared (never leave a reaction claiming a message is
still queued when it's gone), and re-deferred items keep ✍️ since
they're still genuinely waiting. Also fixes two races surfaced while
building this: a flush-rerun request that could otherwise strand a
backlog when a second answer landed inside the first flush's re-entrancy
window, and a silent paste-failure path that now notifies the user
instead of dropping the message with no trace.

Tests: tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts (+370 lines) covers the
unscoped-blocker flush path, the reaction transitions on each outcome
(delivered/failed/abandoned/re-deferred), the flush-rerun race, the
unscoped-abandon sweep actually clearing ✍️ (not just inferred from
sharing code with the scoped case), and a real paste-failure (pane gone
mid-flush) clearing ✍️ and warning the user instead of silently dropping.

Known gaps (pre-existing in the original fix, not introduced by this
rebase — confirmed via byte-exact diff against f07ac8b), flagged by
review for a possible follow-up:
- /agent-route and picker-route deferred sends don't set the ✍️ "queued"
  mark before enqueueing (only plain-text/reply-route paths do), so the
  ✍️→👀 lifecycle this fix adds isn't visible on those two paths — they
  still deliver correctly, just without the interim ✍️ indicator.
- No test for the mixed case where an unscoped-blocker sweep hits a pane
  that ALSO has its own still-open scoped question (should re-defer, not
  inject) — the existing "two unscoped blockers" test only covers two
  unscoped questions, not one unscoped + one scoped on the same pane.
- The paste-failure warning message doesn't name the pane/agent.

Fixes #127, tg#5855

title: fix(hooks): forward outgoing photo caption as --intent to review visual
body:
## Summary

Closes #140

- The pre-send-photo hook receives the outgoing caption in the event args but never
  used it — `review visual` was always called without `--intent`, so review-cli's
  intent-gated checks (e.g. `selection-highlight`'s hard CV veto) were inert for every
  tg-sent photo, in any language. This was the other half of tg#6188 (companion fix:
  alex-mextner/review-cli#110, Russian synonym matching in the intent gate itself).
- Now forwards the caption as `--intent=<value>` (single argv token — a caption
  starting with `-` would otherwise misparse as an option).
- Three security-relevant issues were found and fixed during review, each closing a way
  a crafted caption could disable verification outright (not just fail to add
  `--intent`): a lone UTF-16 surrogate raising `UnicodeEncodeError` at argv-encode time,
  an oversized caption hitting the OS exec() argv-size limit, and the NUL-byte case.
  All three now degrade to "drop `--intent`, keep running the check" via a new
  `_safe_intent()` sanitizer, instead of crashing the whole `review visual` call into
  fail-open.

title: feat(tg-ctl): git-state-check banner - warn before a message lands in an occupied pane
body:
## Summary

Root-cause fix for a real incident: an agent working ticket HYP-915 (a
separate, hyperide-repo ticket) appeared to silently drop that task for 6
hours. Cause: `tg-ctl` routes an inbound Telegram message to a tmux pane,
not to "the agent's current task" — a fresh, unrelated message landed in the
pane mid-flight on HYP-915, and the pane (human or AI, Claude or Codex) had
no signal that this was a new, different thread rather than a continuation.

This implements the harness-agnostic fix ("Вариант В"): `tg-ctl` now checks
the destination pane's git state (uncommitted changes / a branch other than
main/master) right before a silent auto-bind delivery, and prepends a
warning banner when the pane looks mid-flight — so whoever/whatever receives
the message gets an explicit signal instead of silence.

```
This pane currently has uncommitted work on branch feat/foo (3 files changed).
If this new message is about a DIFFERENT task, consider: (a) finish/commit
current work first, or (b) this should go to a NEW agent, not this pane.
```

- Ticket: #152
- Full design/scope writeup: `docs/specs/git-state-banner.md`

## Deviation from the original ask worth flagging

The task as handed to me said to implement this in `features/tg-ctl/updates.ts`.
That module is pure, and for the flat auto-bind path the destination pane
isn't resolved until `injectViaTarget` runs in the entrypoint - after
`stepUpdates` has already built the wrapped `Action`. Doing the check inside
`updates.ts` would mean re-`discover()`-ing the pane a second time via an
injected closure, which can race against (and disagree with) the pane the
message actually lands in. So `updates.ts` is untouched - the pure logic
lives in a new `features/tg-ctl/git-state.ts` (mirroring `discover.ts`'s
raw-stdout-in/structured-data-out shape), wired in at the entrypoint's
actual delivery point instead.

## Scope - deliberately narrow

Applied only to the three silent auto-bind deliveries in `injectViaTarget`
(a fresh, non-reply message landing on a discovered pane with nothing else
choosing it for it):
- plain inbound text (`inject-text` - the exact HYP-915 shape)
- a non-reply photo/document notice
- a standalone (non-reply) voice transcript

Deliberately NOT applied to: `reply-route` (anchored to a specific prior
message - on-topic by construction), `topic-route` (forum-topics mode - a
different, per-topic targeting model), a `/new` spawn (a brand-new pane has
no prior work to protect), a picker tap (the human already chose that pane),
a harness control-command passthrough (`/compact` mid-`/new`-flow), or a
message deferred behind an open question (a separate flush path).

## Honest tradeoff (surfaced, not hidden)

This detects "this pane's cwd is mid-flight", not "this message is
off-topic" - those are not the same thing. An agent that always works on a
feature branch will see the banner on every delivery to that pane. New
`control.git_state_banner` config flag (default true, same `control:` block
pattern as `topics`/`private_topics`) opts out per machine if that noise
is not worth it.

## Test plan

- [x] Pure module tests (`tests/ctl-git-state.test.ts`) - 17 cases: banner
      appears for uncommitted changes, a clean-but-non-main branch, and a
      dirty detached HEAD (fixed a malformed "on branch  (1 file changed)"
      rendering a review pass caught); no banner for clean main/master or an
      undeterminable state.
- [x] Config parse tests (`tests/ctl-config.test.ts`) - `git_state_banner`
      token parsing + default-true resolution.
- [x] End-to-end integration test
      (`tests/ctl-git-state-banner-integration.test.ts`) - a real
      `tg-ctl run` subprocess against a real git fixture (dirty feature
      branch / clean main / not-a-repo) with tmux/ps shimmed to one live
      agent pane: confirms the banner is actually prepended to the injected
      text exactly when expected, and absent otherwise.
- [x] Full suite: 2026 pass, 1 skip (pre-existing), 0 fail.
- [x] Multi-model `review diff` pass (Codex + Gemini); addressed both
      findings - the detached-HEAD rendering bug above, and made sure the
      new files are actually staged/committed (this PR).

Not merging this myself - it changes the behavior of an important
inter-agent communication tool, so it needs review first.

## Summary

- `looks_like_empty_vscode_watermark()` (`features/hooks/review-descriptor/pre_send_photo.py`) never actually fired on a real empty VS Code window screenshot, despite being designed exactly to catch that case — every prior test fixture was synthetic and far higher contrast than reality (tg#6651, tg#6672 investigation).

- Recalibrated `WATERMARK_BOX` / `WATERMARK_BG_TOL` / `WATERMARK_NONBG_RATIO_RANGE` / `WATERMARK_MAX_SPAN_RATIO` together against the real screenshots.

title: fix(hooks): downgrade selection-highlight-only veto to WARN, not BLOCK (tg-cli#163)
body:
Closes #163.

## Problem
The `pre-send-photo` review-visual gate (`features/hooks/review-descriptor/pre_send_photo.py`) hard-blocks (exit 10) any `review visual --strict` rollback. One rollback source is review-cli's `selection-highlight` module, which activates purely on a caption/`--intent` keyword (`selected`/`выбран`/`выделен`/`highlight`) and vetoes when it can't find a 2px `rgb(59,130,246)` HyperCanvas selection outline. That activation is caption-text-only — it can't tell whether the "selected" thing is a canvas element (which *should* carry the outline) or something else (an Explorer file, editor text, a non-canvas control). In the non-canvas case there's nothing to highlight, so the block was a false positive with no escape except rewording the caption (Alex, tg#6691 / tg#7133).

## Change
`decide_from_review_result` now downgrades a rollback whose **sole** blocking module is `selection-highlight` to a warn-and-allow (exit 0). The stderr WARN spells out the one legitimate-bypass condition Alex asked for: the outline is expected when a canvas element **is** selected (a real defect if absent — go verify the render), and proceeding without it is legitimate **only** when the selected thing is **not** a canvas element.

Every other rollback shape still hard-blocks unchanged:
- another module vetoing (alone or alongside selection-highlight),
- an unstyled/broken/blank render (arrives as a rollback with an empty `modules` array from the core cvGate, before any module runs).

`_sole_blocking_module` is structural (mirrors review-cli's own `decision == "block"` predicate; counts every blocking entry; refuses to reason about a malformed `modules` array) so a second genuine veto with a corrupted module name can never be silently dropped into an unsafe allow.

## Scope
review-cli's core `policy_engine` module-veto semantics ("any module block is a hard veto") are **deliberately untouched** — other consumers (PR screenshot gates) depend on that, and loosening it there is a much larger, out-of-repo change. This carve-out lives entirely in the tg-cli hook layer, downstream of review-cli's verdict, the same pattern `warn_empty_watermark_if_detected()` already uses. Two accepted HONEST LIMITS are documented in-file: the partial-`modules`-array short-circuit and the exit-10 vs verdict coupling.

## Tests
6 new cases in `tests/hooks-review-descriptor.test.ts`: sole-veto → allow; urgent WARN text actually surfaces on stderr (with the "NOT a canvas element" clause); selection-highlight + another module → still block; non-selection module alone → still block; empty modules → still block; malformed second-module name → still block; non-`block` decision → still block. Full suite green (2069 tests, 0 fail). ruff clean.

Not a version-affecting change (hook ships via `git pull` / `review install-hook tg`, not the `tg` binary), so no `tg` VERSION/CHANGELOG bump.

## Coordination
Distinct from the in-flight `visual-proof-gate` `ALLOW_NO_VISUAL_PROOF` → `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` conversion in agent-tools — that's a separate pre-bash agent-hook. No overlap.

title: feat(hooks): escalation-format gate — question tag + pre-send-text hook (tg#164)
body:
Closes #164. Core **tg-cli-only** parts of the CTO-approved escalation-format design (the agent-tools skill/marker writer and the rig-cli stats reader are separate PRs; this PR does NOT touch them).

**Warn-mode default, non-breaking.** The escalation-format check is ADVISORY by default — nothing that worked before hard-fails. The hard block is behind an off-by-default `ESCALATION_GATE_ENFORCE` flag, so the later "flip to block" PR just changes that default once the skill lands + a warn week passes (skill-first → warn → flip).

## What shipped

- **`question` canonical `--tag`** — renders like `decision` (orange dot) but deliberately stays on the unicode fallback for every viewer (a placeholder pill, not DECISION's real ids, to avoid a premium-vs-non-premium mismatch). A real QUESTION pill is a follow-up.
- **`pre-send-text` hook point** (`features/hooks/run-text-hooks.ts`) — the agents-hooks/v1 sibling of `pre-send-photo`, fired at the `tg` seam over every plan text message before `transmit()`. Same trust-by-default / fail-open framework.
- **Tier-1 parse-time gate** (`TAG_GATES` registry in `args.ts`, built from a shared `ESCALATION_TAGS` list). Each gate carries a **severity**: the `answer`-gate is `block` (hard exit 1, unchanged); the `decision`/`question` escalation-format check is **`advisory`** — `parseArgs` attaches copy-pasteable guidance as `escalationWarning` and still returns a `send`. The entrypoint prints it and **only** hard-blocks (exit 1) when **`ESCALATION_GATE_ENFORCE`** (default OFF) is set. Mode-specific framing lives in the entrypoint so warn-mode ("sending anyway") never contradicts enforce-mode ("blocked").
- **Tier-2 reference hook** (`features/hooks/escalation-format-descriptor/`) — WARN-ONLY (never blocks), checks the *final* body for a table. Ships as a template + runnable script; **nothing installs it yet** (separate PR).
- **`detectTableKind`** — HTML `<table>` / boxed `<pre>` / markdown pipe (incl. borderless 2-column), rejecting `a || b` code prose and bare `---` as false positives.
- **Generic `gate_*` / `body_sha256` audit extension** — optional top-level fields any hook can report; non-gate hooks' lines stay byte-identical.
- **`audit.jsonl` rotation** (`MAX_AUDIT_LINES`) — fixes the pre-existing unbounded-growth bug, under `routes.ts`'s already-tested cross-process lock, with a below-cap append fast path + atomic temp-file+rename at the cap.
- **v1.34.0** minor bump + CHANGELOG (non-breaking — advisory by default).

## Tests
Full suite **2123 pass / 0 fail**. New: `escalation-gate-args` (warn-default + `escalationGateEnforced` flag parse), `cli-subprocess` (warn vs enforce, both decision & question, through the real `tg` binary), `run-text-hooks`, `hooks-escalation-format-gate`, `hooks-audit-lock` (incl. a real N-process concurrency test), plus `hooks-runner`/`table`/`tag`/`render` additions.

## Reviewed
Many `review diff` rounds (Opus/Codex/Gemini/GLM). Fixed: lost-update race in the first hand-rolled lock, non-atomic audit write-back, two `detectTableKind` false-positive/false-block heuristics, an unguarded `writeFileSync` that could throw out of `appendAudit`, a Tier-1 error naming the wrong tag, and a warn/enforce message contradiction.

## TODO (follow-ups — tracked in #168 + separate PRs)
- Flip `ESCALATION_GATE_ENFORCE` default ON (after skill lands + warn week).
- `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST`-style bypass wiring for the enforced gate.
- Install the Tier-2 descriptor (agent-tools skill/marker, rig-cli reader).

title: fix(tg-ctl): make flat /new robust — session target, arg order, inline dir, no failure loop
body:
Closes #186.

Fixes three separately-reported `/new` bugs in the tg-ctl Telegram control bot.

## BUG 1 — `tmux: create window failed: index 1 in use` + a re-ask loop
The spawn built `tmux new-window -t <session>` with a **bare** session name. When the session is named numerically (Alex's daily setup has a session literally named `1`, base-index 1), tmux parses `-t 1` as **window index 1** — already occupied — so every `/new` in that session aborted. New pure helper `sessionTargetArgs` targets the session unambiguously (`-a -t =<session>:`): trailing `:` forces session interpretation, `=` exact-name match, `-a` appends at the next free index. Shared by both the flat and forum-topic spawns.

On a spawn failure the flow previously fell back to **re-asking the model** — looping the user through the questionnaire while the real error scrolled away. Now `offerNewRetry` reports the error once and offers a single **Retry spawn** button (`tnr:<token>`) that re-spawns with the preserved name/dir/harness/model; the session moves to a new `awaiting-retry` state and never re-asks. New `handleNewRetry` guards forged/expired/wrong-state taps.

## BUG 2 — inline directory argument ignored
`/new hyperos /Users/ultra/work/foo` dropped the path into the task and still prompted for a dir. `parseNewCommand` now recognizes an absolute path as the dir in **any** position and skips the prompt.

## BUG 3 — arbitrary argument order
`/new` now parses name / dir / harness / model by **shape** in any order; selectors fill their empty slot wherever they appear, the first leftover bareword is the name, the rest is the task. Only genuinely-missing pieces are asked interactively.

## Tests
`sessionTargetArgs` unit + a numeric-session integration test that reproduces the exact `-t 1` collision (verified RED without the fix); parser order/inline-dir/reclaim/contiguous-selector cases; retry-button integration + refusal-branch + dir-vanished-on-retry tests. Full suite: **2249 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail**.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
#185 — private-topic spawn leaks an orphan topic/binding on each retry (pre-existing, amplified by the new Retry button).

title: feat(tg): hard-block stray CJK stuck mid-word into Latin/Cyrillic text
body:
## What

Adds a **stray-CJK guard** (feature `cjk-guard`, ON by default) to `tg`. An LLM occasionally emits an isolated CJK/ideographic codepoint stuck into an otherwise Latin/Cyrillic message (e.g. `ка<CJK>eat`, `<CJK>ляет`), so a report arrives with a hieroglyph jammed into a normal word. The guard hard-errors such a send before it leaves, naming each offending character, its `U+XXXX` codepoint and position so the sender re-sends clean.

Closes #188.

## Detection heuristic (precision over recall)

Flag a **lone** ideograph (a CJK run of exactly one codepoint) only when a Latin/Cyrillic **letter immediately follows** it — the ideograph splits or prefixes a word. Both required examples have a letter after the hieroglyph (`ка日|eat`, `注|ляет`).

Passes untouched:
- a CJK suffix/particle that **ends** a token: `iOS版`, `React를 배포`, `APIを 更新`
- a multi-character bilingual word: `Deploy到生产`, `3D打印`, `Word文書`
- a genuinely CJK message (dominant script: >= 3 ideographs **and** >= 50% of script-bearing chars)
- space-delimited CJK quotes, emoji, accented Latin

Accepted/documented tradeoffs (escape: `--no-feature cjk-guard`):
- Latin-dominant **CJK-language prose** that glues a lone ideograph to a Latin word (`用Python写代码`) is structurally identical to the target garble and is flagged. No heuristic distinguishes it from `注ляет` without language detection; irrelevant for Latin/Cyrillic senders.
- quoted/inline-code content is not exempt (no Markdown parsing).

## Where

- `features/cli/cjk-guard.ts` — pure detector (`findStrayCjk` / `formatStrayCjkError`), Unicode-script based (`\p{sc=Han|Hiragana|Katakana|Hangul}`), codepoint-accurate (handles the supplementary plane).
- `tg` — runs the guard on the final decoded caption + `--title` right before send; exits 1 on a hit. Feature default in `features/auto-attach/feature-flags.ts`.
- `--title` is scanned as-is (buildPrefix renders it verbatim); the guard runs on the agent-authored text, intentionally before autolink/line-spec append externally-sourced excerpts.

## Tests (`bun test`, full suite 2268 pass / 0 fail)

- `tests/cjk-guard.test.ts` — unit tests: block `ка日eat` / `注ляет` / Katakana / Hangul; pass English / Russian / emoji / accented / Japanese / bilingual words / suffixes / particles / digit+punct neighbours; short-garble floor (`日a` caught, `日本語a` passes); supplementary-plane indexing + `U+20000` formatting; pinned tradeoffs (`난React`, quoted-code flagged; heavy garble across the dominance line passes).
- `tests/cjk-guard-cli.test.ts` — subprocess CLI tests: block plain / `--table` cell / `--title` / clean-title+stray-body (exit 1, names char + position); pass-through (genuine CJK, Korean particle, `--no-feature`) via an offline `TG_API_BASE` so they never hit the real Bot API.
- `tests/feature-flags.test.ts` — `cjk-guard` default-ON assertion.

## Default-on + escape

ON by default (hard ban, as requested). Escape: `--no-feature cjk-guard` or `features.cjk-guard: false` in `~/.config/tg-cli/config.yaml`.

## Overlap with other in-flight branches

Independent feature touching only `tg` (one import + one guard block right after caption assembly), `features/cli/cjk-guard.ts` (new), `features/auto-attach/feature-flags.ts` (one append-only entry), plus docs/tests. No overlap with the tg-ctl / topics / replies branches.

## Review

Reviewed across Opus / Codex / Gemini / GLM (`review diff`, 5 rounds); all returned `[ok]`. Findings addressed: false-positive class on bilingual/suffix CJK (right-follows rule), title decode mismatch (scan raw title), short-garble dominance floor, `--table`/escape-decode seam, test integrity (exit-code + position assertions).

title: feat(tg-ctl): inject `!shell` messages verbatim for harness passthrough
body:
Closes #190

## What
An inbound **owner** Telegram message starting with `!` (column 0) is injected into the harness pane **verbatim** — no `[TG from …]` wrapper, no git-state banner, no reply quote-anchor — so the harness runs the rest as an in-session `!` shell command. Any prefix would knock the `!` off column 0 and defeat the harness `!` convention.

Alex's ask: "добавь в tg-cli возможность отправки !команд без префиксов и постфиксов как есть в харнесы".

## Where the branch happens
- `features/tg-ctl/updates.ts` `textAction`: `!`-prefixed text → raw `inject-text` (no wrap). Reply branches exclude `!` (no quote-anchor). Topic routing: `!` in a bound topic injects verbatim (plain + reply); closed-topic carried text treats `!` as verbatim.
- `tg-ctl` `withGitStateBanner`: skips the banner for `!` as well as `/` (a dirty pane must not push the `!` off column 0).
- `tg-ctl` inbound-history `resolvePane`: a `!` text reply is not a routed reply → its `tg replies` history stamps under the default pane, not the origin.

## Owner-gating
The existing `senderAllowed` allowlist gates every inbound message *before* `textAction`. A non-owner `!…` message is rejected outright (no action emitted), so the raw shell passthrough can only be triggered by the owner. Test: `non-owner '!cmd' gets NO raw passthrough`.

## Tests
`ctl-updates` (verbatim, multi-line, `!` reply, leading-space-not-passthrough, non-owner-rejected), `ctl-topics` (bound `!` plain + reply), `ctl-git-state-banner-integration` (`!` never bannered on a dirty pane), `replies-inbound` (`!` reply → default pane). title: feat(replies): agent-scoped tg replies (attribution + default/--agent/--all/--untagged) (#191)
body:
Closes #191 (Alex tg#8346).

## What
`tg replies` was mixing every agent's messages with no attribution. This makes it AGENT-SCOPED and adds the missing write-side attribution.

## Schema (write side)
- `HistoryRecord.targetAgent?: string` (`features/replies/history.ts`) — the routed-to / sent-from agent name. Absent = legacy/untagged (back-compat).
- Derived by a single shared helper `agentNameForPane(windowName, panePath)` (`features/tg-ctl/agent-name.ts`): the tmux window name, or the cwd project basename when the window name is a bare/auto-rename default — the same tier the `/agent` picker uses.
- **Inbound** (`tg-ctl` poll loop): stamps the routed target pane's agent name via a new `resolveAgent` hook on `inboundHistoryRecords`.
- **Outbound** (`tg`): stamps the sending session's own agent name (same namespace, so a session's inbound and outbound share one label).

## Read side (`tg replies`)
- **Default**: only the CURRENT agent's messages (resolved from the current pane's window/project). When it can't be resolved (e.g. outside tmux) it degrades to untagged only + a stderr note.
- `--agent <name>` filters to one agent (case-insensitive); `--all` shows every agent; `--untagged` shows only legacy/no-target rows. Mutually exclusive. An explicit one drops the current-pane default so the agent filter is the real axis.
- Every line is marked `[→ <agent>]` / `[→ ?]`; `--json` carries `targetAgent`.

## Tests
`bun test` — new `tests/agent-name.test.ts` (5) + `tests/replies-agent-scope.test.ts` (14) cover: targetAgent stamping (in/out), default=current, case-insensitivity, unresolved→untagged+note, `--agent`/`--all`/`--untagged`, mutual-exclusion, blob round-trip, marking. Existing replies/roundtrip/select tests updated for the mark. Full suite green except one PRE-EXISTING unrelated failure (`ctl-tasks-integration.test.ts`, fails identically on clean `origin/main`).

Real-binary E2E verified `--all` / `--agent ext` / `--untagged` against a crafted history file.

title: feat(tg-ctl): graceful reload preserves the defer-while-waiting backlog (#194)
body:
Closes #194.

## What
Makes a `tg-ctl` reload/restart lossless for inbound Telegram messages. The
daemon held the **defer-while-waiting** queue — messages a person sends while
an agent is blocked on its own open question (spec tg#30), which are queued
rather than typed into the prompt — **only in memory**. Any daemon exit (a
deliberate `tg-ctl restart`, a launchd bootout/bootstrap reload, or a
crash-relaunch) silently dropped those already-sent messages; the human had to
resend them.

## How
- **`features/tg-ctl/deferred-store.ts`** (new): pure, versioned
  (de)serialization of the backlog + per-pane/per-item validation + a per-pane
  cap. Fail-safe by construction — a corrupt or unknown-version file degrades
  to "no restored backlog" and never throws; empty backlogs are omitted so a
  restore never resurrects one.
- **`DeferQueues.snapshot()/restore()`**: copy-on-snapshot round-trip of the
  per-pane queues (arrays are copied so a later mutation can't alias the
  snapshot).
- **`tg-ctl`**: persist the backlog to `CtlPaths.deferred` on every queue
  mutation (best-effort; a persist failure never breaks the hot enqueue/flush
  path), and restore it on bootstrap so each pane's restored question flushes
  its restored backlog on answer. The update-offset was already persisted
  before acting, so together a reload is lossless.

## Tests
Full `bun test` suite green: **2252 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip** (`Ran 2253 tests
across 136 files`). New/extended coverage: `tests/ctl-deferred-store.test.ts`
(round-trip, fail-closed parse, pane cap), plus additions to
`tests/ctl-defer.test.ts` (snapshot/restore), `tests/ctl-lock.test.ts`, and
`tests/ctl-service-cli.test.ts`.

Multi-model review was intentionally skipped for this landing (review harness
is flaky this session; a separate re-review effort owns review quality) — this
relies on the green suite.

title: fix(tg): label main session by project window/cwd, not version/subagent
body:
## Problem

A flagless `tg` from the MAIN/orchestrator session rendered `✳️ [2.1.207] [subagent]` instead of `✳️ [rig-cli]`. Alex: *"Почему у тебя 2.1.207 и subagent? Должно быть rig-cli и без subagent же!"*

Two independent bugs, each in a separate header bracket.

## Root cause

**Field 1 — `[2.1.207]` (the `[window]` bracket).** `getTmuxWindow()` used the raw `#{window_name}`. Verified live: a Claude Code pane runs with `automatic-rename=1`, and the cc process reports its **version as `pane_current_command`**, so tmux auto-sets `window_name=2.1.207`. The version string leaked straight into the header.

```
rig:1 name=[2.1.207] cmd=[2.1.207] auto_rename=1 path=[/Users/ultra/xp/rig-cli]
```

**Field 2 — `[subagent]`.** `detectAgentLabel(env)` (`features/agent-detect/detect.ts`) assumed `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is present **only** in a subagent. It is not a reliable main-vs-subagent signal (the main session's own subprocesses carry it too), so the orchestrator was classified as a subagent and, unable to match a single sidechain-metadata record, fell to the generic `subagent` label.

## Fix

- **`resolveWindowAgentLabel(windowName, panePath)`** (new, in `features/tg-ctl/agent-match.ts`): a real user-chosen window name leads; a bare auto-rename default (version string / numeric index / shell name / empty — via the existing `isBareWindowName`) falls back to the pane's **cwd project basename**. `getTmuxWindow` now reads window name + cwd and runs both through it → `[rig-cli]`.
- **Removed the env-based auto-detection** from the outbound label path. The second bracket is explicit-only now: **`--subagent <name>`** (renamed from `--agent`; the deprecated `--agent` alias still parses) or `TG_AGENT`. The main agent needs no flag.
- `--detect-agent` now prints the resolved `[window]` label (computed lazily so the emoji/model info flags don't spawn a tmux subprocess).

## Proof (before → after)

Real `tg` in a tmux window named `2.1.207` at cwd `xp/rig-cli`, no flag, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` set:

```
✳️ [𝗿𝗶𝗴-𝗰𝗹𝗶]
has [rig-cli]: true   has [subagent]: false   has literal [2.1.207]: false
```

`tg --detect-agent` in the same window → `rig-cli`.

## Tests

- New `tests/window-agent-label.test.ts` — the resolver (version/numeric/shell/empty → cwd basename).
- `tests/agent-flag-args.test.ts`, `tests/cli-agent-send.test.ts`, `tests/ergonomics.test.ts` — rewritten for `--subagent` + deprecated `--agent` alias + no env auto-detection (incl. the exact regression: `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` present, no flag → no `[subagent]`).
- Full `bun test`: **2238 pass, 0 fail** locally after the fix.

## Coordination with open PRs

- **#195 (`fix/ctl-routing-name-qa`)** only edits `features/agent-detect/detect.ts`. This PR keeps that module (doesn't delete it) and merely unwires its call site in `tg`, so #195 rebases cleanly. Note: the auto-detection it evolves is no longer used for the outbound label; converge intent when it lands.
- **#193 (`feat/replies-agent-scope`)** adds `features/tg-ctl/agent-name.ts::agentNameForPane`, which does the same window→cwd fallback as this PR's `resolveWindowAgentLabel`. Conceptual duplication — converge the two helpers when #193 merges (noted in the code comment).

title: feat(tg-ctl): delegate codex hooks to rig (scoped) + gate codex hook-trust bypass
body:
## What

Alex tg#8672 (install-hook → rig delegation) + tg#8708 (codex hook-trust option a). Part of consolidating ecosystem CLIs onto **rig as the single source of truth** for agent-harness hooks, killing codex's `loading hooks from both …/hooks.json and …/config.toml` warning.

Uses the shared `agenttools_rig_delegate` helper (**agent-tools#282**).

## `install-hooks` (codex part)

- When rig is present, delegate to **`rig apply --only harness`** (scoped — never a full 226-action apply) instead of writing `~/.codex/hooks.json` directly.
- A present-but-**failing** rig surfaces its exit code (propagated out of `installHooks`) — no silent fallback (the shared contract: fallback is for *absent* rig only).
- **Telemetry never lost**: after delegating, re-read the authoritative artifact rig owns (`~/.codex/config.toml`, fresh from disk — not a stale pre-delegation snapshot) and only skip the direct write when rig actually provisions the usage-telemetry Stop hook.
- rig absent / helper not installed → the direct `hooks.json` write runs exactly as before.

## `/new` codex spawns

- Add `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` **only when codex hooks are rig-managed** (`~/.codex/config.toml` carries rig's bridge marker) — so rig-vouched hooks fire in autonomous runs, while a user's own untrusted hooks on a machine without rig keep facing codex's trust gate. `models.ts` stays pure; the flag is applied at spawn (`codexHooksRigManaged` / `applyCodexHookTrustBypass`).

## Tests

Full suite green: **2251 pass, 0 fail** (the one `ctl-tasks-integration` ordering flake is pre-existing, passes in isolation, untouched by this diff). title: feat(escalation): enforce decision-request format + render markdown pipe tables
body:
## What & why

Fixes the escalation framework, per CTO direction (tg#8940 "таблица сломана / tg должен требовать особый формат / провижениться через rig", tg#8970 "8-point message was still a wall of text").

### 1. Markdown pipe tables now render ("таблица сломана")
Telegram renders no markdown tables, so an escalation typed as `| a | b |` arrived as literal plain text. `pipeTableToHtml` (`features/render/table.ts`) rewrites a markdown pipe grid to a real `<table>`, routed as a Rich Message via the existing `isRichHtml` path; the `tg` entrypoint applies it and forces `--format html`. Surrounding prose is preserved (and HTML-escaped for a plain-text send). The block is anchored at the GFM header+separator so a pipe-bearing prose line above the grid is not absorbed as the header.

### 2. `--tag decision|question` REQUIRE the decision-request format (deny-by-default)
New pure validator `features/cli/escalation-format.ts` checks the body for:
- **Options** as a real `<table>` (or a `<ul>`/`<ol>` with ≥2 items) with **pros/cons**,
- a **Recommendation**,
- **Context**,
- a concrete **file reference** ("where to look"),
- **Readability structure**: ≥2 `<h3>`/`<h4>` headings, bullet lists, `<hr>` dividers, no wall-of-text run-ons or inline comma-runs — sent with `--format html`.

The parse-time gate (`args.ts`) runs it; the entrypoint hard-blocks (exit 1) with a checklist of what's missing. A `--table` decision/question (rows arrive on stdin, unseen at parse time) is validated on the **final rendered body** so it can't bypass the gate. Bilingual (ru/en) heuristics.

`ESCALATION_GATE_ENFORCE` now defaults to **ON**; `=0` is the one documented escape (downgrade to advisory). `report`/`answer`/`problem` are unaffected.

### Provisioning
Enforcement is a `tg` **code default** (ships with the binary, kept current by `rig`) so it can't silently regress to unenforced. The companion agent-tools PR updates the rig-provisioned `decision-request-discipline` skill to document it.

## Docs
`tg --help`, `tg help format`, and the installed `tg` skill get the good-vs-bad structured shape + the auto-conversion note.

## Tests / verification
- New unit tests: `pipeTableToHtml` (incl. prose-header anchoring, no-double-wrap), `validateEscalationFormat` (compliant passes, each missing section, ru keywords, wall-of-text, options rigor, where-to-look).
- Updated `escalation-gate-args` / `cli-subprocess` for deny-by-default + the `--table` bypass-closure regression.
- Full suite green for the changed areas; the only intermittent red (`ctl-tasks-integration.test.ts`) is a pre-existing flaky tg-ctl/Linear test, unrelated (passes on re-run).
- End-to-end against a mock Bot API: markdown pipe → `<table>` → `sendRichMessage`; compliant decision sends; malformed decision blocked (no API call); plain report unaffected (`sendMessage`).

## Follow-ups (deferred, out of scope)
- The optional Tier-2 pre-send-text reference hook (`features/hooks/escalation-format-descriptor/`) still uses the table-only `detectTableKind` and stays warn-only (not installed anywhere; not the enforcement path). Aligning it to the shared validator is a follow-up.

#150 lifts every review **panel** seat's reasoning effort, but `qa` is a single write/exec

nothing. #150's own reviewers flagged exactly this ("don't expose `--effort` to qa unless it

Threads the resolved level `handler -> run_tester -> _dispatch_tester -> spawn`, reusing

title: feat(tg): block mixed-script "garbage word" tokens (homoglyph/mojibake)
body:
## What

Extends the `cjk-guard` feature (from #189) to catch a **second garbled-token shape** besides stray CJK: a **homoglyph/mojibake "garbage word"** — a single contiguous run of letters where a foreign alphabet (Latin, Greek, …) is *sandwiched inside* Cyrillic. This is the shape an LLM occasionally emits, e.g. the reported **`почčesна`** (Cyrillic `по` + Latin `čes` + Cyrillic `на`) where it meant **`починена`**.

A message (or `--title`) carrying such a token is now a hard error (exit 1) before send, naming the offending token and its position so the sender re-sends clean.

Closes #205.

> Stacked on #189 (`feat/cjk-stray-guard`) — that PR adds the `cjk-guard` this one extends, so this PR targets that branch. Retarget to `main` once #189 merges.

## The detection rule (before → after)

The naive rule "a whitespace token containing both Cyrillic and Latin letters" over-fires on legitimate Russian tech writing (`PR-ревью`, `IDшник`). The implemented rule is precise:

- Scan **maximal runs of letters** (digits, punctuation, hyphens, whitespace, emoji all break a run).
- Within a run, classify each letter as **Cyrillic** or **foreign** (non-Cyrillic, non-CJK). Combining marks, modifier letters, and **CJK letters are ignored** — they neither vote nor create a transition, so this guard stays *structurally* orthogonal to the stray-CJK guard (it reuses `cjk-guard`'s `isCjk`).
- Flag the run only when it contains **both** a Cyrillic and a foreign letter **with ≥ 2 script transitions** — i.e. the foreign fragment is *sandwiched* (`…Cyr → Lat → Cyr…`), the true mojibake signature.

The `≥ 2 transitions` threshold is what lets legitimate one-boundary compounds through.

| Input | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `почčesна` | **blocked** | Cyr→Lat→Cyr = 2 transitions |
| `починeна` (Latin `e` mid-word) | **blocked** | 2 transitions |
| `дельτа` (Greek τ) | **blocked** | 2 transitions |
| `починена` (pure Cyrillic) | passes | no foreign letter |
| `влил PR gh ship` | passes | separate words, each one script |
| `PR-ревью`, `MCP-сервер` | passes | hyphen breaks the run |
| `IDшник`, `APIшка`, `PRы` | passes | glued suffix = **1** transition |
| CJK hieroglyph (`ка<CJK>eat`) | blocked by the **stray-CJK** guard | (regression preserved) |

Accepted recall gap (same precision/recall tradeoff as the CJK guard): a garble with the foreign fragment at a run **edge** (one transition) is indistinguishable from a glued compound and is left alone. Escape hatch for any false positive: `--no-feature cjk-guard`.

## Wiring / gating

- New module `features/cli/mixed-script-guard.ts` (`findMixedScriptTokens` / `formatMixedScriptError`), style-matched to `cjk-guard.ts`.
- Called in the `tg` entrypoint's existing `if (cjkGuardOn)` pre-send block, right after the stray-CJK check, on the final caption and `--title`. The stray-CJK check runs first, so when a message has both, the CJK error wins.
- **Same toggle** as the CJK guard: `--no-feature cjk-guard` (or `features.cjk-guard: false`) disables both checks. `feature-flags.ts` default-ON comment updated to cover both.

## Tests

TDD, red-first. New `tests/mixed-script-guard.test.ts` (detection heuristic incl. the reported word, glued-compound allows, edge-fragment recall gap pinned by codepoint, CJK-legit regressions, multi-token error format) and `tests/mixed-script-guard-cli.test.ts` (CLI block/pass-through incl. `--title`, `--table`, `--no-feature`, both-guards ordering).

Full suite green: **2294 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail** (`bun test`, exit 0). Reviewed with `review diff --staged` (Opus, correctness) — `[ok]`, no hard bug; the two Medium/Low findings raised on the first pass (over-blocking glued compounds; hand-duplicated CJK predicate) were folded into this diff.

title: fix(auto-attach): skip bad disk attachments and cap message flooding

## Summary
- A disk attachment (auto-detected path mention, or explicit `--photo`/`--file`) that goes missing, gets truncated to empty, or loses read permission between detection and send is now skipped with a stderr warning naming the path and reason — the primary text still delivers. - 1.41.1 introduced `TG_CTL_QUEUED_DECISION_DELIVERY_MS`, a 10-minute window past which a queued Telegram tap on a disconnected permission was silently demoted back to plain "hook disconnected" text -- violating the standing rule that a pending question must stay pending in Telegram until 100% confirmed resolved (Alex tg#9982: "Опять тайм-аут. Нельзя!").

## What

Adds **omp (Oh My Pi)** as a recognized harness kind at the tmux-floor level, in both directions:

- **Inbound**: `matchAgentCommand` gains one row — argv0 basename `omp` (omp is a compiled Bun binary, e.g. `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp`). Every inbound gate keys off this matcher, so this single row fixes pane discovery (`findAgentInPane` BFS), the inject verify-pane checks, reply-route liveness, and candidate discovery — an omp pane is now injectable via tmux send-keys, exactly like `pi`/`aider`.
- **Outbound**: `detectAgentViaAncestry` labels a session launched under omp as `omp`; the emoji maps carry `omp` (custom ID shares Claude's ✳️ per the existing aider/continue/devin pattern, Unicode fallback 🥧), so sends get the agent emoji and `:omp:` works as an emoji helper.

Fixes #243.

## Deliberate scope decisions

- `omp` is in `AgentKind` but **not** `SpawnHarness` — `/new` does not spawn it (same as pi/aider).
- `questionCapability` is now an **exhaustive switch** with omp explicitly `'unsupported'` (honest tmux floor, no native question buttons) plus a runtime fail-safe default for out-of-union values crossing the hook-socket JSON boundary.
- `tg-ctl ask --agent` now validates against **`HOOK_AGENT_KINDS`** — a Record-derived, compile-exhaustive single source (`Object.hasOwn`, so prototype keys like `toString` are rejected). `--agent omp` classifies as omp instead of silently inheriting claude semantics; a present-but-unrecognized value now **warns on hook stderr** before the claude fallback (kept for back-compat: a typo'd claude hook install still gets working claude semantics; garbage payloads drop cleanly — verified live).
- No hook/permission integration for omp this round; `harness-event --agent` stays a separate free-form telemetry label (verified: it uses `parseHarnessEventFlags`, not the closed selector).

## Evidence

- **Live inbound**: a real tmux pane running `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp` → `findAgentInPane` = `{agent:"omp", pid:43292}`; `pickTargetPaneFromSet` = `ok agent=omp pane=%13`. Pasted probe text appeared in the omp TUI input (tmux floor confirmed), cleared after.

New coverage: `matchAgentCommand` omp rows (incl. `ompi-info` non-match), pane BFS + ancestry omp cases, `questionCapability('omp')` pin, `HOOK_AGENT_KINDS`/`isHookAgentKind` pins (typo + prototype keys), end-to-end `--detect-model` branding, end-to-end omp ask-forward drop, `--agent` warning path.

title: fix(tg): brand omp sessions as omp — lineage-first model detection
body:
## What

`tg --detect-model` misbranded **omp sessions as claude**: omp exports `CLAUDECODE=1` (pi heritage, verified live in the session env), and `detectAiModel` checked that env marker **before** walking the ancestor process tree — so the omp detection shipped in #245 never fired for outbound branding. Every send from an omp session went out branded `claude ✳️`.

Detection is now **lineage-first**: `TG_AI_MODEL` override → ancestor process walk → env-marker fallbacks → pgrep. Env vars are *inheritable* (an agent inside another agent's pane carries the outer agent's markers), so the nearest recognizable ancestor is the truth in nested topologies; the env markers become fallbacks for detached spawns whose launcher isn't in the tree.

Fixes #246.

## Behavior matrix (all pinned by tests)

| Topology | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| omp ancestor + `CLAUDECODE=1` (the bug) | `claude ✳️` | `omp 🥧` |
| claude ancestor + `CLAUDECODE=1` | `claude` | `claude` (unchanged) |
| **two agents in one tree** (opencode → claude → tg) | — | nearest wins → `claude` |
| opencode ancestor | config model name | config model name (unchanged) |
| inherited `OPENCODE` + codex ancestor | opencode model | `codex` (lineage over stale env) |
| detached nested (OPENCODE+CLAUDECODE, no ancestry) | `claude` | `claude` (pre-existing fallback order kept) |
| `OPENCODE` + unreadable config | fall-through to pgrep (ollama hazard) | `opencode` generic (never pgrep) |
| **detached omp spawn** | `claude` | `claude` — **known limitation** (omp exports no marker of its own — verified live: zero `OMP_*` in the process env); documented in CHANGELOG |

## Hardening riding along (review findings, each pinned)

- `opencode debug config` is now timeout-guarded (2s + SIGKILL) — a wedged opencode binary could previously block a send indefinitely on the env path, and the lineage-first order puts this spawn on the hot path.
- `process.env.OPENCODE/CODEX` unified onto the `env` closure (`env = {...configEnv, ...process.env}`, tg:579 — identical inputs).
- `writeFakePs` gains a chain form (nearest-first) with synthetic pids anchored above `pid_max` — multi-agent trees testable without format duplication, no pid-cycle/collision windows.

## Evidence

- **Live repro of the reported scenario**: `CLAUDECODE=1` + fake omp ancestry → `omp 🥧` (was `claude ✳️` pre-fix).
- 65/65 tests in `tests/emoji_map.test.ts` green (13 new/updated tests); full suite green except the two known load-sensitive integration flakes (`ctl-tasks-integration`, `ctl-new-spawn-integration` — pass standalone, pass with `--timeout 30000`, untouched by this diff; same class documented on #245).
- Review gate: 5 rounds of `review diff --staged`; the naive reorder's nested claude-inside-opencode regression (round 1) is what produced the lineage-first design; later rounds added the timeout, CODEX fallthrough, chain-helper, and cycle fixes. `env`-vs-`process.env` equivalence verified at tg:579.

## Checklist

- [x] Regression tests: bug pin, no-change pins, two-agent tree, fallback ordering, broken-config symmetry
- [x] `VERSION` 1.43.1 + matching `## 1.43.1` CHANGELOG section (incl. the detached-omp known limitation)
- [x] Review-gate stamps recorded under task HYP-246
- [x] Scope: `tg`, `tests/emoji_map.test.ts`, `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md` only
- [x] No merge, no deploy, live checkout untouched

title: fix(escalation-format): stop wall-of-text check from newline-formatting hazing
body:
## Summary Fixes #261. A subagent reported (relayed by Alex via Telegram) that `--tag question|decision`'s escalation-format gate rejects realistic decision-request content — a real file path, a multi-row options table, a multi-item recommendation list — while only the tool's own toy template passed. **Root cause**: `hasWallOfText` split the body on literal `\n` only. A fully structured Rich Message (`

`/`

`/``/`
    `/`
    `) assembled as one continuous source string, with no literal newline between sections, still renders as separate visual lines in Telegram — but the raw source string was one giant "line" whose character count blows past the 350-char `WALL_LINE_CHARS` threshold the moment the content is realistic. The toy template joined into one line is 345 chars (just under the threshold); the same shape with one real filename swapped in is 538. This reproduces every reported symptom exactly. **Fix**: `hasWallOfText` now scans "visual lines" — a virtual break inserted before each opening block tag and after each closing/void one — instead of literal-`\n`-split lines, so the same content gets the same verdict regardless of the caller's newline formatting. `INLINE_ENUM_RE` moved inside the per-line loop (still ahead of the skip-list) so it can no longer match across unrelated sections of a one-line body. I also independently re-verified several other claims from the same report that did **not** reproduce (real file paths, 3-row tables, 2-item recommendation lists, Context prose length — all already passed on main with real literal newlines) and pinned those with regression tests rather than touching code that wasn't broken. ## Review trail Reviewed via `review diff` across 4 rounds (Opus + Fable; Codex hit its usage cap each time). Two real regressions were caught and fixed before this PR: the first-draft fix broke the `
  • ` skip-list (splitting `
  • ` from its content defeated the exclusion for long list items) and let `INLINE_ENUM_RE` match across unrelated sections of a one-line body. Also closed a `blockquote`/`pre` skip-list asymmetry. **Deferred, not fixed here** (architectural, not a reported bug — noted in the ticket): the three tag lists (`OPEN_BLOCK_RE` / `CLOSE_BLOCK_RE` / skip-list) are hand-maintained and could drift from each other or from the actual renderer; a shared "visual lines" normalization could be applied validator-wide instead of only in `hasWallOfText`; `WALL_LINE_CHARS` counts raw markup rather than tag-stripped text. ## Test plan - [x] `bun test tests/escalation-format.test.ts` — 17 tests, including the exact one-line reproduction (verified to fail pre-fix, pass post-fix, by reverting the fix locally and re-running) - [x] `bun test tests/dry-run.test.ts tests/hooks-escalation-format-gate.test.ts tests/message-structure.test.ts tests/render.test.ts` — all green (87 total across the 5 targeted files) - [x] Live `tg --tag question --dry-run` with the exact reported repro shape (real `.github/workflows/...` path, one continuous line, no literal `\n`) — now passes - [x] Confirmed a genuine run-on paragraph (400 chars, no tags) is still caught as a wall of text, both via unit test and live `--dry-run` - [ ] Full `bun test` suite (2000+ tests) — not run to completion locally (exceeds this session's time budget); CI runs it on this PR 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ds5NW835SF5hJxkyYA5HVw
