title: feat(tg-ctl): late-deliver a permission tap by injecting the digit into the still-showing terminal menu (#267)
body:
## Summary

A Telegram Approve/Reject tap that lands after a permission's hook socket already closed (Claude Code's ~120s hook budget elapsed, harness fell back to its own terminal "Do you want to proceed?" prompt) now re-checks the pane via `tmux capture-pane` and, if the menu is still live for this same request, injects the matching digit directly — no waiting process, no dependency on a hook reconnect that may never come. Previously the tap was only ever QUEUED for delivery on a hook reconnect, which meant a terminal-fallback permission could wait forever despite the human having already answered.

This is the CTO's spec, verbatim: "no waiting process — check via tmux whether the permission request is still showing, and send the keypresses."

## What's in this PR

- New pure module `features/tg-ctl/permission-menu.ts`: parses a captured pane for Claude Code's numbered permission menu, picks the matching digit for allow/deny, and binds a captured menu to a specific request via line-exact identity matching (never a substring — `git push` must not match a live `git push --force` menu).
- `tg-ctl`: on a late tap for a permission, queues first (durable before any tmux touch — a crash mid-inject can never lose the tap), then attempts pane-injection for `claude` specifically, confirming delivery via the menu's cursor glyph rather than assuming Claude Code erases a resolved menu from the pane (unconfirmed either way).
- `features/tg-ctl/inject.ts`: `buildDigitInjectPlan` — a bare digit keypress, no Enter (verified live: Claude Code's menu submits instantly on a bare digit).

## Live verification

Claude Code's permission-menu submit-key behavior (bare digit vs digit+Enter) was tested on an isolated throwaway tmux + Claude Code session, not any real/shared session — confirmed a bare digit resolves the prompt in well under a second with no Enter needed.

## Review process

3 rounds of this repo's own multi-model review gate (`review diff --staged --task 267`). Real findings caught and fixed across rounds, not just style:
- Round 1: bounded-context identity matching (whole-pane matching would let a stale tap match unrelated scrollback), single-digit injection safety, exact Yes/No label matching (not a prefix, to avoid silently granting a broader standing decision like "don't ask again").
- Round 2: the post-inject "menu is gone" confirmation was gated on marker/option TEXT disappearing — but there's no confirmed evidence Claude Code erases a resolved menu rather than leaving it in scrollback. Fixed: gate on the menu's cursor glyph (`hasLiveCursor`) instead, which is correct whether or not the surrounding text sticks around. Added regression tests for both possible real-world behaviors.
- Round 3: verified (not a bug) a hypothesized reentrancy race during the 400ms confirm window — the daemon's action dispatch is explicitly documented and coded as strictly sequential, so a second tap cannot interleave with an in-flight confirm.

## Tests

Full suite: 2557 passed / 1 skipped / 1 failed / 1 error — the 1 fail + 1 error are pre-existing flaky integration tests (`ctl-voice-integration.test.ts`, `ctl-tasks-integration.test.ts`), confirmed reproducing identically on a clean `git stash` against unmodified main, unrelated to this change.

47 tests specific to this change (`ctl-permission-menu.test.ts`, `ctl-permission-pane-late-deliver-integration.test.ts`, plus updates to `ctl-inject.test.ts`), including regression coverage for both the "text vanishes" and "text retained, cursor stripped" resolve behaviors.

## Deferred (tracked, not blocking)

tg-cli#268 tracks: live-verification of the deny label / edit-write/plan-approval prompt shapes, making `capturePane` async instead of blocking the event loop on `spawnSync`, two missing unit/integration tests (plan-approval null-parse, defer-guard on the pane-inject path specifically), and a dead truncated-identity code path. All non-blocking and fail-safe on the approval axis — worst case is a missed speed-up, never a wrong action.

title: fix(tg-ctl): non-reply routing anchors on the CTO's own last message, not any agent's
body:
## Summary
- An unrelated agent proactively messaging the CTO could hijack the CTO's very next non-reply message: routing bound to `routes.json`'s "last outbound sender" (`lastMessagePane`), which conflated "who spoke last" with "who the CTO was addressing" (live incident, 2026-08-19/20).
- Adds a dedicated `last-alex-target.json` anchor recording ONLY the CTO's own last CONFIRMED inbound delivery (auto-bind, picker tap, reply, named `/agent`) — never an agent's outbound send, never a failed inject.
- Guards against tmux pane-id reuse via `routeMatchesPane`, including a fix for an empty-live-path bypass (`resolve('')` was resolving to the daemon's own cwd, which could falsely match). The same class of bug is also fixed in `withGitStateBanner` (was silently checking the daemon's own git state instead of skipping the banner).
- `/tasks`'s ambiguous-fleet default scoping now shares the SAME anchor the inbound-routing path uses, instead of the two surfaces silently disagreeing.
- Widens the attach denylist to cover the anchor file's `.tmp.<pid>` staging form (a crash/failed rename could otherwise leak it).
- Removes the now-fully-superseded `lastMessagePane`/`resolveByLastMessage` mechanism and its unit tests.

Went through 7 rounds of multi-model review (codex + Opus + GLM + Fable). Fixed: 2 P1s + 1 P2 (round 1), an empty-path pane-reuse bypass + dead-code cleanup (round 2), 3 more P1s including an untested denylist gap (round 3), a `withGitStateBanner` empty-path bug + comment-accuracy fixes (round 4), a genuine `/tasks` test regression + 2 missing anchor-recording call sites + a stale spec doc (round 5), 2 cheap doc/test-coverage fixes (round 6). Rounds 6-7 found no more blocking issues.

Remaining architectural follow-ups (deliberately out of scope for this bug-fix PR, tracked in #272): centralizing anchor recording at one delivery chokepoint instead of ~8 scattered call sites, scoping the anchor by sender identity for the (currently unused, empty-by-default) `allowed_senders` config, and a registration-cwd fallback for pathless-tmux panes.

Closes #271.

title: fix(tg-ctl): permission prompts gave up too early, falsely reporting "never delivered"
body:
fix(tg-ctl): permission prompts gave up too early, falsely reporting "never delivered"

A permission-kind abandoned entry (approve/reject request whose hook socket
closed) now uses its own, much longer retention window
(TG_CTL_ABANDONED_PERMISSION_RETAIN_MS, default 12h) before the daemon gives
up and reports "this was never delivered over Telegram" -- previously it
shared the 30-minute question window, so a permission left unanswered for as
little as half an hour (easily overnight, or a few hours away from the
phone) was falsely reported as unrecoverable even though the harness might
still be sitting on its own terminal fallback prompt, fully answerable.

Threaded through all retention-check sites via two pure, exported helpers
(retainMsFor/isAbandonedExpired) and a new decideQueuedPermissionReconnect
that extracts the reconnect-time delivery decision into one deterministic,
directly-unit-testable function -- closing a real race where a reconnect
landing between an entry's expiry and the next periodic sweep could still
auto-deliver a stale queued decision, and a bug where an expired decision
also logged a false "payload mismatch".

A related fix (multi-line command matching for the late-delivery
pane-injection path, tg-cli#267) was attempted but reverted after a 3-round
review surfaced an unresolved escalation risk and an unverified rendering
assumption -- tracked as tg-cli#283 for a live-verified redesign.

Went through 11 rounds of the mandatory multi-model review gate; real
findings fixed along the way included a genuine escalation bug in an
earlier draft of the multi-line matcher (already reverted before this
commit), a reconnect-time race allowing stale decision delivery, and a
double-log bug from two unconnected if-chains.

Closes #182

title: feat(tg-ctl): add /spend bot command and scheduled weekly/monthly usage push
body:
## Summary

Recovers previously-implemented-and-tested work for this ticket that had been left in a git stash instead of committed. Adds two things a user can do:

- **`/spend [day|week|month]`** — reply with a token/cost usage report for you or your team (via `rig usage`), on demand in Telegram, in both flat chats and bound topics.
- **Automatic weekly/monthly push** — `tg-ctl usage-schedule enable` installs a background job (macOS only) that checks once a day and sends the same report to the chat automatically at the end of each week and each month, so you don't have to remember to ask.
- Also adds **`/daily`** — a "what shipped" report of merged pull requests since the last time you asked, and documents both new commands in the README's command table.

Refs #290.

## Follow-up (sweep, 2026-09-05)

The post-review work that had been left uncommitted in the sibling `tg-cli-wt-290-usage` worktree is harvested here, plus the two Codex threads:

- **Scheduled push is watermark-based now.** The daily launchd check compares a persisted per-bot "last reported completed week/month" watermark against the current completed period instead of asking "is today the boundary?" — launchd runs a firing missed during sleep at wake, so the old same-day check silently dropped the report whenever the machine slept through 23:50 on the boundary day. A failed send keeps the period due (retried next day); dry-run never advances it.
- The scheduled push escapes the body at the HTML boundary (`rig usage` really emits a `<synthetic>` model name); `rig usage --json` periods are shape-validated before formatting; an all-unpriced period renders as "unpriced", not "~$0.00"; `usage-schedule disable` tolerates a never-loaded plist.
- `/daily` and `/spend` replies are split into ≤4096-char chunks (shared `splitMessage`); a `/daily` report whose send fails part-way is persisted and prepended to the next `/daily` (`rig daily` advances its watermark while generating, so it would otherwise be lost).
- Version 1.45.0 + CHANGELOG.

## Why it's not named `/usage` (as originally specced)

While recovering and re-reviewing this work, I found that `/usage` collides with a command that already exists inside the coding-agent sessions this bot forwards messages to: Codex has its own native `/usage` (used to redeem a banked usage-limit reset), and Claude Code's `/cost` and `/stats` are documented aliases for its own `/usage`. A bot-level `/usage` (or `/cost`, or `/stats`) would have silently swallowed that text before it ever reached the agent, breaking a real, already-working feature for anyone using those commands. I verified this directly against the installed Claude Code, Codex, opencode, and pi binaries before settling on `/spend`, which doesn't collide with any of them. New tests assert the whole reserved set (`/usage`, `/cost`, `/stats`) still reaches the agent untouched, in both routing modes.

## What I found and fixed along the way

- The scheduled background job wouldn't have been able to find the `tg`/`rig` commands it needs (the OS starts it with a very limited search path) — fixed by capturing the right path when the job is installed.
- The same job wouldn't have picked up a non-default configuration directory — fixed to match how the main bot already handles this.
- Documented the new `tg-ctl usage-schedule enable|disable` commands in the built-in help text.

## Test plan

- [x] Full test suite re-run fresh multiple times (not the original stash-era numbers) — consistently green aside from confirmed machine-load flakiness in different unrelated files each run (each one 0-fail when re-run alone; none touched by this change).
- [x] All new/changed test files green in isolation: `ctl-updates`, `ctl-topics`, `ctl-usage-schedule`, `ctl-limits`, `ctl-harness-event-integration`, `ctl-new-updates`.
- [x] `review diff --staged` (multi-model review) run six times across the recovery/rename process; all real findings either fixed or explicitly ruled out/deferred below.

## Ruled out (not regressions — pre-existing behavior, verified)

- A pending `/new` flow can treat `/usage` as a directory answer — true before and after this change (`/usage` was never a recognized bot command either way).
- `/usage@your_bot_name` (the `@botname` form Telegram appends in group chats) doesn't pass through verbatim in a bound topic — verified this is a pre-existing bug affecting other already-working commands too (`/stop@your_bot_name`, `/compact@your_bot_name` have the identical problem), unrelated to this change. Filing separately.

## Deferred to follow-up tickets (robustness gaps, not blockers for this PR)

- The scheduled report is silently skipped if the computer is asleep or off right at the weekly/monthly boundary.
- An unexpected shape in the underlying usage data could crash the report instead of showing a friendly error.
- A very long `/daily` report could be dropped by Telegram's message-length limit with no way to retry it.
- `/spend` can show a misleading `$0.00` for models with no published price, instead of saying the cost is unknown.
- The scheduled report doesn't escape special characters before sending as formatted text.

title: feat(tag): drop --tag question — an open question is a decision request
body:
Refs #301

## What

Alex (2026-09-05): agents use only the standard message tags — `answer`, `decision`, `problem`, `report`. There is no separate "question" message type: an open question for him IS a decision he has to make, so it goes out as `--tag decision` in the decision-request format (options with pros/cons, a recommendation, where to look). Two names for the same escalation split the format rules and let agents pick the softer one.

- **`--tag question` is refused** at parse time (non-zero exit, nothing sent) with a one-line redirect instead of the generic off-list error:
  ```
  --tag question was removed: an open question is a decision request — use --tag decision in the decision-request format
  ```
  It is refused even when the body is a fully compliant decision request (the vocabulary is the problem, not the format); `--dry-run` refuses it the same way.
- `--help`, `tg help format`, and the installed `tg` skill / blurb list exactly `answer` / `decision` / `problem` / `report`. `ESCALATION_TAGS` is now `['decision']`, so both the parse-time `TAG_GATES` and the pre-send-text hook derive the single escalation tag from one list.
- The QUESTION wordmark/emoji branding (`TAG_PILL_IDS` / `TAG_PILL_DOT` / `TAG_PILL_FALLBACK` entries, the orange `🟠 QUESTION` fallback badge) is deleted. The header renderer's placeholder-id guard stays — it is generic and still protects against a broken `<tg-emoji>`.
- Version `1.44.5` → `1.45.0` (minor, same class as the 1.12.0 Cyrillic-alias removal), CHANGELOG entry added.

## Tests

- `bun test`: 2618 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.

title: feat(tg-ctl): agents outside tmux — unreachable status + Stop-hook inbox delivery (#306)
body:
Refs #306. Companion: agent-tools#526 (the Stop-hook reader) and a `claude-rotate` change in the dotfiles.

## What changed

**Agents running outside tmux are now visible and reachable.** tg-ctl used to discover agents only via `tmux list-panes` and deliver only via `tmux send-keys`, so an interactive `claude`/`codex`/`opencode` started from a plain terminal tab (no `$TMUX`) did not exist for it — silently (incident 2026-09-05, agents `landing` and `rig-fable`).

1. **Discovery scans the process table too** (`ps -axo pid=,tty=` + `lsof` for the cwd; pure logic in `features/tg-ctl/unreachable.ts`). An interactive agent process with a controlling tty and no tmux pane is listed by `tg-ctl status`, `/status` and the bare `/agent` picker as `unreachable: not in tmux (tty …, cwd …, name …, pid …)` with the hint how to reach it. Headless shapes (`-p`/`--print`, `codex exec`, Claude's `daemon`/`bg-*` helpers) are ignored; a launcher wrapper + its binary count once; a session nested under another agent's shell tool stays a distinct agent (caught live in the first proof run).
2. **A second delivery channel — the Stop-hook inbox.** `/agent <name> <text>` to such an agent appends the already-wrapped text to `~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/<key>/pending.jsonl` and replies "`<name>` is running outside tmux (tty, cwd) — queued to its Stop-hook inbox; delivered when the agent next ends a turn". The agent-tools Stop hook consumes it and hands the text to the agent as its next instruction; the daemon reacts 👌 on the Telegram message once `delivered.jsonl` shows up and archives it to `acked.jsonl`. The no-agent reply lists unreachable agents instead of the bare "not in tmux" text. The daemon no longer idle-exits while such an agent is up.
3. **Inbox key contract shared with agent-tools byte-for-byte**: sanitized `--name`, else `cwd-<sha256(cwd)[:16]>`; documented in both READMEs, test vectors mirrored in `tests/ctl-unreachable.test.ts` and agent-tools' `tests/test_tg_inbox.py`.
4. `tg-ctl inbox` / `tg-ctl inbox queue <name|dir> <text>` — the CLI view of the channel. Version 1.46.0 + CHANGELOG; README, AGENTS.md and the `tg` skill explain the two channels and the idle-agent limitation.

## Live proof (2026-09-06, final SHAs: tg-cli `9cec44f` + agent-tools `094da16`)

A REAL interactive `claude --name tgtest` under a pty (`script -q`, prompts piped in), started with `TMUX` unset — deliberately NOT `claude -p`: a `-p` run is headless and is filtered out of the unreachable list on purpose. The session's Stop hook is the agent-tools branch (`--settings` → `PYTHONPATH=…/.worktrees/526-stop-inbox/lib python3 -m cc_hook_bridge Stop`, stderr to a file); the `tg-ctl` binary is the tg-cli branch. Everything below was captured from inside that run (driver: `scratchpad/tgtest-driver3.sh`).

**1. The agent is outside tmux, and this branch's `tg-ctl` sees it + queues to it:**

```
$ ps -axo pid=,ppid=,tty=,command= | grep "bin/claude --name tgtest"
34250 34097 ??       script -q /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-typesc
34253 34250 ttys019  /Users/ultra/.local/bin/claude --name tgtest --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions --permission-mode bypassPermissions -

$ echo "TMUX=$TMUX" (in the shell that started the agent)
TMUX=

$ tg-ctl inbox queue tgtest "LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED"
queued to tgtest (tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 1 queued)

$ tg-ctl inbox queue tgtest "second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line"
queued to tgtest (tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 2 queued)

$ tg-ctl status
…
unreachable (not in tmux): 4
  - tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253), 2 queued
  Not in tmux → no direct injection; a message sent with `/agent <name> <text>` is queued to its Stop-hook inbox and delivered when the agent next ends a turn (an idle agent gets it only at its next turn). To make it fully reachable, restart it inside tmux: `claude-rotate --tmux <name>`.
…

$ ls -la ~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/tgtest (before the Stop)
total 8
drwx------@ 3 ultra  staff   96 Sep  6 21:38 .
drwx------@ 3 ultra  staff   96 Sep  6 21:38 ..
-rw-------@ 1 ultra  staff  484 Sep  6 21:38 pending.jsonl
```

**2. The agent finishes a turn → the Stop hook (agent-tools branch) consumes the inbox — hook stderr:**

```

```

**3. On disk after the Stop: `pending.jsonl` is gone, ONE complete `delivered-*` batch, `tg-ctl inbox` shows nothing queued:**

```
$ ls -la ~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/tgtest (after the Stop)
total 8
drwx------@ 3 ultra  staff   96 Sep  6 21:38 .
drwx------@ 3 ultra  staff   96 Sep  6 21:38 ..
-rw-------@ 1 ultra  staff  700 Sep  6 21:38 delivered-43009-1788716338055394000-631ea499.jsonl

$ cat ~/.config/tg-cli/inbox/tgtest/delivered-*.jsonl
{"id": null, "ts": "2026-09-06T17:38:53.104Z", "from": "tg-ctl", "text": "LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED", "wrapped": "[TG from tg-ctl] LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED", "delivered_ts": "2026-09-06T17:38:58+00:00", "session_id": "3e8c9178-de50-474d-a099-629edf95b30d"}
{"id": null, "ts": "2026-09-06T17:38:53.273Z", "from": "tg-ctl", "text": "second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line", "wrapped": "[TG from tg-ctl] second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line", "delivered_ts": "2026-09-06T17:38:58+00:00", "session_id": "3e8c9178-de50-474d-a099-629edf95b30d"}

$ tg-ctl inbox
  - tgtest · claude — unreachable: not in tmux (tty ttys019, cwd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/tgtest-proj, name tgtest, pid 34253)
```

**4. The agent's transcript (`~/.claude-accounts/…/tgtest-proj/3e8c9178-….jsonl`) — both messages AND the regular stop gate's reason arrive in ONE `Stop hook feedback` block (the v1 stop hooks ran first, the inbox was consumed last):**

```
[user] Reply with exactly the word READY and nothing else.
[assistant] READY
[user] Stop hook feedback:
[TG from tg-ctl] LIVE PROOF tg-cli#306 / agent-tools#526 (final SHAs): reply with exactly the word DELIVERED

[TG from tg-ctl] second entry — reply DELIVERED-2 on the next line

Before finishing, one check (this turn made no tool calls, …) — the regular stop-completion-selfcheck gate, in the SAME block
[assistant] DELIVERED
DELIVERED-2
```

**Caveat from a second run against the MACHINE'S installed hook (agent-tools main `7964f9a`, no `--settings`):** nothing was delivered — the pty typescript shows no "Ran 1 stop hook" at all and `pending.jsonl` stayed at 2 queued. Cause: the session runs under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-accounts/account-0` (claude-rotate), and none of the `~/.claude-accounts/account-*/settings.json` files carries a `hooks` key — Claude Code reads settings from the config dir only, so the rig-provisioned hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` never fire for a claude-rotate session (that includes every session of the 2026-09-05 incident). Not a defect of this PR (the hook code is proven above with the identical lib loaded via `--settings`), but until the hooks reach the account dirs the inbox channel is dead on this machine — tracked as a rig-cli ticket (linked in the ship report).

Not exercised here: the daemon's `👌` reaction on the Telegram message — the launchd daemon on this machine still runs the pre-#315 code (needs a restart after the merge to pick this up), and a `tg-ctl inbox queue` entry has no Telegram message id anyway.

## Tests

`bun test`: new `tests/ctl-unreachable.test.ts`, `tests/ctl-inbox.test.ts`, `tests/ctl-unreachable-route-integration.test.ts` (fake tmux/ps/lsof; `/agent landing …` queues + replies, plain no-agent lists). `tests/ctl-daemon-integration.test.ts` gained a `ps` shim so its byte-exact guard-text assert stays hermetic on a developer machine with real agents outside tmux.

## Known limits

An idle agent (already at its prompt) receives an inbox message only when it next finishes a turn — nothing can wake a tty-less Claude Code. opencode has no Stop hook, so an opencode session outside tmux is listed but has no fallback channel. The daemon's `👌` acknowledgement needs the real Telegram message id (a `tg-ctl inbox queue` entry has none).

title: fix(tg-ctl): report running when launchd owns the daemon
body:
## Summary

`tg-ctl status` treated a missing pidfile as "not running" while launchd `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl` pid 11062 was alive and holding the flock. Hatches then treated Telegram as unreachable.

Status now consults, in order: live pidfile, flock holder (`lsof` on `tg-ctl.<bot>.lock`), then a launchd job that supervises this binary *for that proven pid*. A launchd-owned process is `running (launchd, pid N) (job <label>)`.

Live check with this branch binary:

```
tg-ctl: running (launchd, pid 11062) — bot 8574086668 (job ai.hyperide.tg-ctl)
```

`tg-ctl ask` still talks to the unix socket and does not consult status.

## Tests

- `tests/ctl-daemon-run-state.test.ts` — pidfile live/stale/absent, launchd running, lock-holder-without-socket
- `tests/ctl-status-liveness-integration.test.ts` — delete pidfile; delete pidfile+socket; ask still posts

## Notes

This is the status-lie that made hatches think Telegram was down. Hooks.json / config.toml telemetry is out of scope here. Do not use magic-close keywords.

Refs #334

title: feat(tg-ctl): control live omp via ACP, not tmux send-keys
body:
## Summary

tg-ctl talks to live omp through **ACP JSON-RPC**, not tmux `send-keys` and not `omp --resume --print` (PR 322 forks history).

**ACP methods (proven on omp 18.1.14):**
- `initialize` → agentInfo `oh-my-pi`
- `session/new` `{cwd, mcpServers:[]}` → `sessionId`
- `session/prompt` `{sessionId, prompt:[{type:"text", text}]}`
- `session/update` / `session_info_update.title` — name from omp
- `session/request_permission` → Telegram buttons; tap replies with `{outcome:{outcome:"selected", optionId}}`

**Also:**
- Process-table discovery (pid, primary session jsonl, title) with or without tmux
- Tmux still classifies `kind=omp` (issue 243 recognition already shipped), including version-string `pane_current_command`
- When a pane AND ACP both exist, ACP only — never send-keys
- Session label is omp's own title, not cwd basename

Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/323

## Test plan

```
cd .worktrees/omp-live-acp
bun test ./tests/ctl-omp-acp.test.ts
bun test ./tests/ctl-omp-acp-integration.test.ts
```

Integration: fake `omp acp` child, `TMUX` unset, `/agent ReviewFix deploy now` → ACP `session/prompt` with `[TG from Alex tg#10]`; fake tmux log has no `send-keys`.

title: feat(cli): block screenshot mention without an attached photo
body:
Refs https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/337

## What

Outbound `tg` now hard-blocks a send whose caption or `--title` mentions screenshot / скриншот (any case) when no real on-disk photo is attached.

- `tg "see screenshot foo.png"` (no `--photo`) → exit 1 before transmit. The error tells the sender to attach with `tg --photo`, and not to dodge by deleting the word.
- `tg --photo x.png "screenshot of …"` is allowed.
- A `--photo` whose path is missing or empty does not count (that file is later skipped and the caption would otherwise go out as text-only).

## Tests

Red then green on the real `tg` entrypoint:

- `blocks a plain message that mentions screenshot without --photo`
- `blocks Cyrillic скриншот without --photo`
- `allows screenshot mention when --photo is attached`
- `error tells to attach the image, not to omit the word`

## Review

Astra (consistency) P1 on a missing `--photo` path was folded in. Residual: an unreadable file or a TOCTOU delete after the gate can still skip the photo at transmit time — same class as other pre-send guards; not the agent failure mode this ticket targets.

title: fix(tg-ctl): retain and auto-deliver RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* approvals past process exit (#349)
body:
Refs #349

## Bug
A `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_*` approval (agent-tools' `agenttools_hatch_escalation.request_hatch_approval`) pipes a manually-built `ButtonRequest` of kind `permission` into `tg-ctl ask` -- a headless, one-shot request with no `paneId` and no `promptTurnId`. `retainAbandonedQuestion` previously did `if (!req.paneId) return false` unconditionally, so the moment the requesting process exited (its own timeout, or the harness killing it) -- which routinely happens before a human taps Telegram -- the entry was expired outright and dropped. A tap landing even a moment later hit nothing: the approval was silently lost. This was the *only* delivery path any hatch approval had.

## Fix
- `features/tg-ctl/questions.ts`: `parseHatchHookId`/`isHatchRequest`/`hatchEnvVarName` helpers, plus three hatch-specific card texts (`hatchAbandonedPermissionText`, `hatchApprovalRecordedText`, `hatchAbandonedLongOutageText`) that name the concrete `RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_<HOOK_ID>` retry instead of the impossible "tap again once it reconnects" / "answer in the terminal" promises a headless one-shot request can never keep.
- `tg-ctl`:
  - `retainAbandonedQuestion` now retains a paneless hatch permission instead of falling through to expiry.
  - `armPendingSocketClose`'s abandon branch picks the hatch text and releases correctly with no real paneId.
  - `handleHookSocketLine` gets a hookId-keyed short-circuit (`findQueuedHatchDecision`) so a RETRY -- a fresh `ask` with a new requestId but the same hookId, exactly what agent-tools' documented retry produces -- is answered automatically with no new Telegram prompt and no second card.
  - The permission tap handler and `notifyAbandonedLongOutage` branch on hookId to show the hatch-specific text/toast.
  - The durable-state restore filter no longer drops a hatch permission on daemon restart just because it has no paneId.
  - `lateDeliverAbandonedQuestion`'s early `if (!retained.req.omp && !retained.req.paneId) return false` gate is widened -- without this a hatch tap would have been rejected before ever reaching the new permission-branch logic above.

## Test
`tests/ctl-hatch-approval-retry-integration.test.ts` reproduces the exact race end-to-end against a real daemon + mock Telegram: the requesting process exits before any tap, a late tap is durably recorded (verified on disk), and a retry on a brand-new connection with a new requestId but the same hookId is answered automatically with no second card. Verified this test **fails** against the pre-fix code at the exact point the bug manifests (`git stash` the fix, rerun -- both tests fail), then passes with the fix.

```
✓ HATCH RETRY (tg-cli#349): a tap after the requesting process exited is recorded, and a retry with the same hookId is answered automatically with no new card [6009.92ms]
✓ HATCH ABANDONED (no tap): the card names the concrete retry command instead of the impossible "tap again"/"answer in the terminal" promises [2224.91ms]

 2 pass
 0 fail
 15 expect() calls
```

Per fleet-wide notice: not running `gh ship`/review-cli (model board exhausted) -- opening this for CI + human/later-agent merge once the review-cli fix lands.


---

**Update (tg-cli#349 review finding):** the original fix above only made `retainAbandonedQuestion`/`expireDeadCard` retention reachable from `armPendingSocketClose`'s socket `'close'` handler. A separate raw `UNSCOPED_ABANDON_MS` (110s) `setTimeout` in `forwardAndPostQuestion` also retires the same pending entry and called `expireDeadCard` directly, bypassing retention entirely. Since a hatch requesting process stays connected ~120s (its own hook budget) -- longer than the 110s default abandon window -- the raw timer fired FIRST in the default, dominant production case, destroying the card before the socket ever closed. Only the edge case where the process exits/gets killed early went through the already-fixed path.

Fixed by extracting the retain-or-expire decision into a shared `retireAbandonedEntry`, called from both the socket-close handler and the raw abandon timer. New regression test reproduces the exact default scenario (process never killed, socket never closes, only the raw backstop timer retires the entry) and fails against the pre-fix code.

title: fix(tg-ctl): detect stale registrations across tmux server restarts via a server-epoch marker
body:
Fixes #354

## Root cause

tg-ctl's per-pane registration store (`features/tg-ctl/registration-store.ts`) tracks "which tmux pane hosts which agent session" keyed **only** by tmux's `%N` pane_id string. `pruneRegistrations()` treats an entry as still-live purely by checking "is this paneId a member of the current `tmux list-panes -a` snapshot".

tmux's pane_id counter is monotonic **only for one continuous tmux server process lifetime**. Across a tmux server restart (reboot, `tmux kill-server`, a crashed/relaunched server) the counter resets to zero, so a brand-new, unrelated pane can be assigned the exact same low `%N` a long-dead pane from a *prior* server lifetime once held. `pruneRegistrations` cannot tell these apart — a registration entry survives forever, silently, as long as *some* pane in each subsequent server lifetime happens to reuse that same low number (very likely for `%0`-`%9` on a machine that always has several panes open).

### Live evidence (captured on the reporting machine)

`~/.config/tg-cli/tg-ctl.8574086668.registration.json` (the real, currently-running production daemon) contained, among current entries, two clearly stale ones:

```json
{"paneId":"%5","cwd":"/Users/ultra/xp/hyperos","registeredAt":1784290247}
{"paneId":"%1","cwd":"/Users/ultra","registeredAt":1784306797}
```

(~2 months old). Live `tmux list-panes -a` on the same machine showed pane `%1` is *actually* the hyperos omp pane, and pane `%5` is *actually* an unrelated tmux "main" session's status pane (zsh, not an agent at all) — proof tmux reused `%1`/`%5` for entirely different panes since the registrations were written, and the store never detected or dropped the old entries because their bare paneId strings still happened to exist in the current snapshot.

`discover.ts`'s `pickTargetPaneFromSet()` tier 1 (`registeredPaneIds.has(...)` against live candidates) is the exact routing consumer that misfires on this: if tmux ever reassigns a registered-but-stale paneId to a new, unrelated agent pane, a fresh inbound Telegram message with no explicit `/agent` selector silently routes to that wrong session — the "old sessions/titles" symptom, even though every session now genuinely runs inside tmux (the prior tmux-migration fix is unrelated and unaffected).

## Fix

Add a tmux-**server-lifetime** marker ("epoch") to registrations, independent of pane_id reuse. tmux resets all of a server's option state on every restart, so a server-scoped tmux user option (`@tg_server_epoch`) is a clean, self-resetting nonce:

- `Registration` gains an optional `serverEpoch` field.
- `pruneRegistrations(existing, livePaneIds, currentEpoch = null)` drops an entry whose stamped `serverEpoch` no longer matches `currentEpoch`, **in addition to** (not instead of) the existing pane-liveness check. The epoch check fires **only** when both the entry and the caller know an epoch — a legacy entry with no `serverEpoch`, or a caller that couldn't resolve the live epoch, falls through unchanged to pane-liveness-only pruning. Fully additive/backward-compatible: every pre-existing on-disk entry and every hand-written fixture across the `tests/ctl-*integration.test.ts` files has no `serverEpoch` and is completely unaffected.
- `tg-ctl` gains `tmuxServerEpoch()`: reads-or-creates `@tg_server_epoch` via `tmux display-message`/`set-option -s`, cached in-process with a **60s TTL** (not forever — see below), and wired into `discoverTarget`, `composeStatus`, and `startLauncher` (which now stamps `serverEpoch` on every fresh registration).

### Why a TTL, not cache-forever

An earlier draft cached the resolved epoch for the whole process lifetime. Multi-model review (`review diff`) caught a real blocker in that: the tg-ctl **daemon** is long-lived and outlives any single tmux server by design, so a `tmux kill-server` (or reboot) with the daemon still running would leave it comparing every registration against a permanently stale cached epoch — pruning every fresh, correctly-stamped entry forever (a full, permanent registration blackout, worse than the bug this PR fixes). A bounded 60s TTL still avoids a tmux round-trip on every single poll (the original perf goal) and keeps test-stub safety (a test run comfortably fits inside one TTL window), while bounding real-world staleness to well under a minute after a genuine server restart.

## Tests

`bun test tests/ctl-registration-store.test.ts`: **19 pass**, 0 fail (15 pre-existing behaviors unchanged + 4 new regression tests, including the exact captured `%5`/old-epoch production scenario as a fixture, its before/after behavior, a legacy-entry back-compat guard, and the epoch-only-prune-with-null-livePaneIds path).

`bun test tests/ctl-daemon-integration.test.ts` (full daemon subprocess round-trip, exercises the TS compile of the touched root `tg-ctl` script + `/status` reply path): **1 pass**, 0 fail.

title: fix(tg-ctl): evict wedged omp ACP client after a failed session/prompt
body:
Refs #353

## What

`promptOmpAcp` now evicts + kills the cached ACP client when a session/prompt call fails, and the prompt timeout is overridable via `TG_CTL_ACP_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS` for tests.

## Why

The NDJSON framing fix (#346) made ACP `initialize`/`session/load` succeed, but a `session/prompt` call that never gets a reply (e.g. the target omp session is already owned by another live process) left the ACP child cached in `ompAcpClients` forever with `exitCode===null`. Every later reply into that same session reused the dead pipe and repeated the identical "ACP session/prompt timed out" failure -- forever, with no way to recover short of a daemon restart.

**Live evidence** (2026-09-09, `launchd.tg-ctl.err.log` on the CTO's machine, full detail in #353): the same session id (cwd=`.../state-lib/site`) timed out 3x over 30 minutes under a daemon that had already picked up the merged NDJSON fix (initialize/session-load logged as succeeding each time) -- confirming this is a *distinct* bug from #346, not a stale-deploy symptom. The wedged child (pid 61725) stayed alive 35+ minutes holding 90+ open sockets before this fix, since `promptOmpAcp` never killed or evicted it on timeout.

## Testing

- `tests/ctl-omp-acp-prompt-evict.test.ts` (new): a fake `omp acp` that answers `initialize`/`session/load` but never answers `session/prompt`. Asserts a second reply after the first one wedges spawns a **second** `omp acp` process rather than reusing the dead one. Red-checked against the pre-fix code (fails: only 1 spawn); green against the fix (2 spawns).
- Existing `tests/ctl-omp-acp.test.ts`, `tests/ctl-omp-acp-integration.test.ts`, `tests/ctl-omp-reply-no-tmux-integration.test.ts` all still pass (35/35 across the 4 files).
- Version bumped 1.49.1 -> 1.49.2 (package.json; repo has no pyproject.toml) + CHANGELOG entry.

title: fix(tg-ctl): fire-and-forget omp delivery, persist batch before offset advance (tg-cli#322, task-cli#138)
body:
## Summary

- **Fire-and-forget omp delivery:** `promptOmpAcp` no longer awaits `acpCall(..., 120_000)` for the agent's real reply. It writes the NDJSON `session/prompt` frame via `writeAcp` and returns immediately — matching the original ask (task-cli#138: get the message to the agent, not wait for and surface the reply). The prior synchronous wait (up to two minutes) was the root cause that a rejected PR #322 then papered over with a shutdown-drain timer instead of removing the wait.
- **Persist-before-ack:** `runDaemon` now durably journals each `getUpdates` batch to `ctx.paths.pendingBatch` (atomic temp+rename) **before** advancing the offset. On startup, a leftover journal is replayed through the same `stepUpdates` + dispatch path. Net semantics shift from at-most-once (crash mid-action = silent loss) to at-least-once with idempotent downstream handling.
- **`GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_MS` retained** (8s) for in-flight side effects (e.g. Telegram API calls) but is no longer message-loss-critical — durability comes from journal-before-offset ordering.

## Proof

`tests/ctl-persist-before-ack.test.ts`:
- **SIGKILL durability:** daemon SIGKILL'd as soon as `pending-batch.json` is written; respawned daemon recovers and `sendMessage` fires again; journal is unlinked after full processing.
- **Unit:** `serializePendingBatch` / `parsePendingBatch` round-trip and edge cases.
- **Fire-and-forget:** fake `omp` logs `session/prompt` but never responds; routing confirm lands within 2s of the prompt write (not ~120s).

## Supersedes PR #322

This is a **from-scratch reimplementation against current `main`**, not a rebase of #322 (stale, ~53 files diverged). Recommend retiring #322 in favor of this PR once merged.

Not merging/shipping this myself — leaving it for review.

Refs #322

title: fix(tg-ctl): dispatch action delivery concurrently per target to fix head-of-line blocking
body:
Refs #357

## Root cause
tg-ctl's single daemon serialized ACP session/prompt delivery via a 120s-timeout sequential
action loop, causing head-of-line blocking across the whole agent fleet: one slow/stuck
target delayed delivery to every other target queued behind it.

## Fix
- Added a per-target concurrent dispatch queue (features/tg-ctl/concurrent-dispatch.ts) so
each target's actions are delivered independently instead of through one shared sequential
loop.
- Reduced the per-action delivery timeout from 120s to 15s so a stuck target fails fast
instead of blocking the queue.

## Tests
- New tests/ctl-concurrent-dispatch.test.ts: 8/8 passing.
- Scoped regression check on the existing ACP test files (tests/ctl-omp-acp.test.ts +
  tests/ctl-omp-acp-integration.test.ts): 31 pass, 0 fail, no regressions.
- Full test suite / lint / format intentionally not re-run for this push (already scoped-tested
per prior verification); only the above targeted files were run.

Refs #357

title: tg-ctl: active-silence nudge for tg-unaware agent sessions
body:
Refs #363

## What changed

**1. New pure module `features/tg-ctl/tg-awareness-nudge.ts`** — the daemon's
decision logic for when to proactively remind a live omp ACP session it hasn't
used `tg` in over an hour: `parseAwarenessNudgeStore`/`serializeAwarenessNudgeStore`
(durable per-key state), `planAwarenessNudges` (who's due this sweep — one nudge
per silence *episode*, never a repeat storm), and `lastTgSentAtByKey` (derives
each key's last-outbound-send time from the shared `history.jsonl` log). Fully
unit tested in `tests/tg-awareness-nudge.test.ts` (9 tests).

**2. `tg-ctl` daemon wiring** — `CtlPaths.awarenessNudge` (new state file,
`tg-ctl.<botid>.awareness-nudge.json`, same convention as `schedules`/
`questions`). `runDaemon` loads/persists the store next to `scheduleStore`,
and the poll loop sweeps `listLiveOmpAgents()` every iteration (cheap no-op
when nothing is live and the store is empty), delivering any due nudge via
the existing `promptOmpAcp`/ACP channel.

**3. Fix: `tg`'s outbound history writer only recorded tmux sends.**
`recordOutboundHistory` gated `HISTORY_PATH`/the write on `TMUX_PANE` alone,
so an omp session with **no tmux pane** (headless, ACP-controlled — exactly
the population the nudge targets) never got an outbound `history.jsonl`
record at all, only a `routes.json` entry. Now gated on `originPaneId`
instead (tmux pane if present, else the synthetic `omp:<pid>` origin already
used for `ROUTES_PATH`), matching `outboundOriginPaneId`'s own precedence.
Without this fix the nudge sweep would have had zero last-tg-sent signal for
its main target population. Extends the existing
`cli-omp-route-notmux.test.ts` integration test to assert the history record
too.

**4. `~/.agents/skills/tg/SKILL.md`** (not part of this repo/PR diff — a
separate, non-git-tracked skill file on this machine) updated with a short
note: don't wait for a natural stopping point, and the `tg --help` fallback.

## Why

Alex has repeatedly asked agents to reliably use tg-cli. The `tg` skill is
already discoverable via the SessionStart blurb, but its own triggers
(finish a task, hit a question/blocker) only fire at a natural decision
point — a long, heads-down working stretch never produces one, so passive
discovery alone can't close the gap. This is the active side: the daemon
itself reminds a session that's gone quiet.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/tg-awareness-nudge.test.ts` — 9/9 pass.
- `bun test ./tests` (full suite) — 2920 pass, 1 pre-existing skip
  (Linux-only autostart test), 0 fail.
- Manually ran `tg --help` from the built binary — exit 0, confirms the
  skill's `tg --help` fallback text is accurate.
- Confirmed the sweep's reachability by reading through `runDaemon`'s poll
  loop: `listLiveOmpAgents()` is called every iteration right where the
  existing `abandonedButtons` sweep sits, `promptOmpAcp` is the same
  function every other inject-to-omp path already uses.

## Scope note

Scoped to live omp agents only (`listLiveOmpAgents()`) — `promptOmpAcp` is
the only channel the daemon can push into out-of-band. A tmux-only
Claude/Codex pane has no equivalent live-control channel; extending this is
a real follow-up, not silently promised here.

title: fix(tg-ctl): let hatch permission asks skip the pane/cwd registration gate
body:
## What
Hatch permission asks (`requestId` like `hatch-no-long-inline-process-...`) come from non-tmux omp sessions — pane=`-`, cwd outside the tmux registration set. `handleHookSocketLine`'s not-registered gate dropped them before Telegram ever saw the card, per the launchd log evidence in #333 (regs only tmux panes %5/%1/%56, hatch req had pane=- cwd=/Users/ultra/xp/rig-cli).

Added `isHatchPermissionRequest(req)` (kind === 'permission' AND requestId.startsWith('hatch-')) and used it in `handleHookSocketLine` to bypass `hookMatchesRegistration` for hatch permissions only; `canForwardButtonRequest` still gates them downstream, so this doesn't broaden what's forwardable — only which asks reach that gate.

## Why
Hook hatch is the documented exception to no-long-inline-process. If a hatch ask can't reach Telegram, an omp session outside tmux has no way to get human approval and is stuck.

## Test evidence
- New unit test `isHatchPermissionRequest: permission whose requestId starts with hatch- only` in `tests/ctl-questions.test.ts` covers the true/false matrix (hatch permission, bare "hatch-" prefix, normal permission, question kind reusing the prefix, requestId with hatch- not as a prefix).
- New integration test `hatch permission with unmatched pane/cwd is not dropped not-registered` in `tests/ctl-ask-forward-logging.test.ts` drives `ask` with pane=`-`/unregistered cwd and asserts the log line switches from `reason=not-registered` to `ask-forward posted`, and that the Telegram send actually happens.
- Ran `bun test tests/ctl-questions.test.ts tests/ctl-ask-forward-logging.test.ts`: 50 pass, 0 fail, 161 expect() calls.

Refs #333

title: fix(tg-ctl): ask once before falling back from private topics (#181)
body:
## What
tg-ctl asks once before falling back from private topics to a flat `/new` spawn, instead of
degrading unilaterally with a repeated fallback warning.

## Why (motivation)
Alex corrected the previous behavior: if private topic capability is unavailable, the daemon
should not unilaterally degrade with a confusing warning; it should ask once whether to move
forward without topics.

## User impact
Alex sees one clear choice in Telegram when topic support is unavailable, instead of repeated
confusing warnings while trying to start agents.

## Cost of inaction
The bot keeps emitting confusing fallback copy and may start agents without the expected topic
decision.

## Changes
- `features/tg-ctl/new-command.ts`: new `awaiting-private-topic-fallback` session status, the
  `tnf:<token>:continue|cancel` callback parse/build pair, and the Continue/Cancel keyboard.
- `features/tg-ctl/updates.ts`: routes the new callback prefix to the fallback handler.
- `features/tg-ctl/types.ts`: shared shapes for the fallback decision.
- `tg-ctl`: wires `getMe.has_topics_enabled=false` to ask once (threaded to the originating
  topic when present) instead of a repeated fallback warning; the answer/once-only notice is
  recorded so later `/new` attempts in the same daemon run do not repeat the question.
- `CHANGELOG.md` / `package.json`: 1.50.0.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] When `getMe.has_topics_enabled` is false, tg-ctl asks the user once whether to continue
  without topic routing instead of repeatedly printing a fallback warning.
- [x] The prompt is threaded to the originating topic when present and subsequent `/new`
  attempts do not repeat the same question after the user answers or the once-only notice is
  recorded.
- [x] Existing private topic success, `createForumTopic` failure, and fallback spawning
  behavior remain covered by tests.
- [x] Proof: 99 tests pass, 223 `expect()` calls across `tests/ctl-new-command.test.ts`,
  `tests/ctl-new-updates.test.ts`, `tests/ctl-private-topics-integration.test.ts`.

## Test plan
```
bun test tests/ctl-new-command.test.ts tests/ctl-new-updates.test.ts tests/ctl-private-topics-integration.test.ts
99 pass, 0 fail, 223 expect() calls
```

Refs #181



## Follow-up fix (review-cli finding)
An independent review-cli pass (Opus, correctness role) found that a stale/replayed
`tnf:` fallback tap could reset the global `privateTopicFallbackState` even while a
*different* session had a legitimate live pending decision, letting a later `/new`
silently discard it. Fixed in `handleNewPrivateTopicFallback` (only resets state when
no session is actually `awaiting-private-topic-fallback`) and covered by a new
regression test that reproduces the exact failure (verified to fail pre-fix, pass
post-fix).

Updated test plan: 100 pass, 0 fail, 234 `expect()` calls across the same three files.

title: feat(tg-ctl): generic `tg-ctl ask` approval primitive (#149)
body:
## Summary

Adds a synchronous, unforgeable **"ask a question and block for a real Telegram reply"** primitive: `tg-ctl ask "<question>" [--timeout <seconds>]`. A *third-party* caller (a pre-bash hook, a CI step, any script) can invoke this to get a genuine human yes/no verdict routed through the trusted daemon that already owns the bot's `getUpdates` long-poll.

Fixes #149.

Motivating context: Alex tg#6554 and agent-tools PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/189, which replaced self-service escape hatches in two safety hooks (`pin-primary-worktree`, `block-reset-hard`) with a deny-by-default external-approval extension point.

## Design

- **Deny-by-default, no silent ALLOW.** Generic mode is detected by a non-flag positional arg after `ask`, resolved *before* the bare-`ask` no-creds shortcut. That shortcut's `exit(0)` means "no opinion, hook harness UI takes over" for the existing Claude-Code hook client — correct there, but a landmine for a security gate's approval primitive. Every failure path in generic mode (no creds, daemon unreachable, socket drop, timeout, malformed response, explicit reject) is an explicit `exit(1)`; only a genuine verified Approve tap exits 0.
- **Same trusted transport, no new state.** Built as an ordinary unscoped `ButtonRequest` (`kind: 'permission'`, `agent: 'claude'`) sent through the same `oneAskAttempt`/daemon transport every other permission request uses — no new callback namespace or daemon-side state.
- **Genuinely one-time.** `crypto.randomUUID()` per call means a verdict can never replay a cached answer from a past, unrelated request.
- **Timeout override survives the socket boundary.** Adds `ButtonRequest.unscopedAbandonMs` so a generic `tg-ctl ask --timeout <seconds>` override reaches the daemon's own abandon backstop instead of silently falling back to the default 110s and getting killed before the caller's own wait elapses.
- Distinct, actionable stderr per failure mode (`daemon unreachable`, `timeout after Ns`, `no bot credentials configured`, an explicit reject reason) instead of one generic decline.

## Testing

`tests/ctl-generic-ask.test.ts` — 21 tests / 73 `expect()` calls, covering:
- argv parsing (question position, `--timeout` position, multi-word questions, malformed flags)
- timeout clamping/defaults (300s default, 900s max, sub-1s floor)
- verdict resolution (allow / deny / malformed / no-answer)
- every deny path (no creds, daemon unreachable, socket drop mid-wait, timeout, malformed response, explicit reject)
- concurrent calls never share a `requestId`
- two end-to-end round trips against a real daemon (Approve and Reject taps)

```
bun test tests/ctl-generic-ask.test.ts
 21 pass
 0 fail
 73 expect() calls
```

Rebased onto current `main` (was 53 commits behind); resolved 4 merge conflicts in `tg-ctl` (all additive — new `install-hooks` doc line alongside an unrelated Claude/Codex telemetry doc update, a new `unscopedAbandonMs` field alongside an unrelated `promptTurnId` field, a new `runGenericAsk` function alongside an unrelated `codexConfigDir` function, and the no-creds guard combined so `codex-usage-hook`'s existing silent-exit-0 shortcut and generic-ask's explicit deny-on-missing-creds both hold). Scoped test re-run green after the rebase.

title: fix(tg-ctl): report ask-forward outcomes truthfully (tg-cli#372)
body:
## What
Refs #372: the asking side no longer conflates a card the daemon actually
posted to Telegram with one dropped at the door.

This is the truthful-reporting slice of tg-cli#317. Filed #372 as the scoped ticket this
PR actually satisfies, since #317 also asked for a longer answerable window (already
tracked separately as tg-cli#303) and for codex-session requests to carry real routing
detail (now tracked as tg-cli#373) — neither of those is touched by this diff. #317, #303,
and #373 stay open and linked from #372.

## Why
Incident 2026-09-05: an agent asked Alex for a one-time exception; the daemon posted
the card (`ask-forward posted ... messageId=14880`), nobody tapped within the
110-second unscoped window, and the daemon closed the hook socket with the same bare
`null` it uses for a request refused at the door. The client logged
"ask-forward not-posted ... daemon declined or unreachable" and the agent was told a
card visible in Telegram had never been sent.

## What changed
- The daemon writes an interim status line on the hook socket before its final reply:
  `posted` (messageId), `dropped` (reason), or `expired` (messageId + age). The final
  reply is unchanged.
- `tg-ctl ask` reads those lines and logs the real outcome instead of one generic
  "not-posted ... declined or unreachable" for every non-response.
- 3 rounds of independent review (omp:claude-opus-4-8 + omp:claude-sonnet-5) also
  surfaced and fixed:
  - the reconnect re-attach path wrote no `posted` status, so a live card could still
    report `unreachable` after a daemon restart
  - the reconnect loop discarded an earlier `posted` status once a later attempt
    couldn't even connect (found independently by both reviewers)
  - a resend landing after the human already answered via pane injection reported
    "no decision" instead of the real `answered-via-pane` outcome
  - the `expired` message asserted "posted to Telegram" even when the send hadn't
    completed yet

## Tests
`bun test tests/ctl-ask-forward-truth.test.ts tests/ctl-buttons-integration.test.ts` — 4/4 pass.
Rebased onto latest `main` (which merged tg-cli#333's hatch-permission registration-gate
skip); updated the `not-registered` test fixture to use a non-`hatch-` requestId so it
still exercises the registration gate rather than being exempted by #333.

Note: `tests/ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration.test.ts`'s "a late tap on an abandoned
multi-question member is REFUSED, never injected" test fails on this branch after the
rebase; verified it also fails the same way against plain `origin/main` (pre-existing,
timing-flaky — not introduced by this diff, which does not touch that code path, only the
pre-existing `.then(a => a.raw)` adapter, unchanged in shape). Flagging for visibility, not
fixed here to keep this PR scoped to #372.

title: fix(tg-ctl): apply tg-cli#78 anchor to no-tmux-pane multi-candidate omp fallback
body:
## What

`injectViaTarget`'s no-tmux-pane fallback branch never consulted the tg-cli#78
last-user-target anchor, so a non-reply message into 2+ live out-of-tmux omp
agents always re-posted the agent picker instead of routing to the anchor's
last-resolved agent.

## Why

`resolveLastUserTarget()` only ever sees `TargetPane[]` (tmux-pane-only)
candidates. The out-of-tmux omp support added in #306/#339/#342 reaches a
separate `found.reason === "no-agent"` branch inside `injectViaTarget` that
picks purely by `listAgentCandidates().length` — 2+ candidates always call
`postRoutePicker`, never consulting the anchor. This silently regressed the
#78 guarantee for the out-of-tmux-omp case.

## Fix

Adds `resolveLastUserTargetCandidate` — the same anchor lookup as
`resolveLastUserTarget`, against the merged tmux+omp `AgentCandidate[]` view
— and consults it in `injectViaTarget`'s no-agent branch (when `autoBind` is
set) before falling back to the picker.

## Testing

title: fix(ci): stop dependency-review SBOM probe aborting under runner's default set -e
body:
## What

The `dependency-review` workflow's "Preflight — is the Dependency Graph enabled?" step
intermittently fails CI on unrelated PRs (confirmed on this PR's own predecessor, #371,
and on `main` itself — see e.g. run 34434999987 / a similar shape).

## Why

GitHub Actions' default Linux runner shell is `bash -e {0}`. Combined with the workflow's
own `set -uo pipefail`, the preflight step's
`code="$(gh api ... | awk ...)"` assignment aborts the whole step whenever `gh api` returns
a non-2xx status. That includes the *intentional* "dependency graph disabled -> 404" path
this probe exists to detect — not just transient network blips. Any `gh api` hiccup (rate
limit, transient 5xx, or the expected 404) kills the step under `-e` before it ever reaches
its own `if/else` that is supposed to handle exactly that case gracefully.

## Fix

Append ` || true` to the one `code="$(...)"` assignment so a non-zero exit from the pipeline
never aborts the script under `-e`; `code` falls through empty/unset and the existing
`if [ "${code:-}" = "200" ]` branch already handles that case (treated as "not enabled",
gate skipped with a clear notice — same as today's non-abort 404 case). No other line
touched.

## Testing

Pure CI-workflow change; verified by this PR's own `dependency-review` check running clean
against a real (dependency-graph-enabled) repo. No app code touched — no unit tests apply.

Refs #369 (the root-cause analysis + retry workaround for this same flake originated while
shipping #371, referencing that issue's context; this PR is the follow-up permanent fix, not
part of #369's own scope).

title: feat: SD 3.5 APIs and local inference with native Apple Silicon/GGUF backend
body:
## Summary

Adds Stable Diffusion 3.5 **Large** (`stabilityai/stable-diffusion-3.5-large`) through hosted APIs, local Diffusers, and an explicit native Apple Silicon path. Current version: **0.4.0**. Existing HF/FLUX defaults, stdin input, console/symlink entry points and agent-skill installation remain compatible. Nothing has been merged into `main`.

## Backends

- `--backend hf` / `api`: Hugging Face Inference Providers, model aliases, optional `--provider` and generation controls.
- `--backend stability`: direct Stability AI API using `STABILITY_API_KEY`, aspect ratio, negative prompt and seed. No automatic retry or credential-bearing redirects.
- `--backend local`: original optional `[local]` Diffusers stack, full three-encoder SD3.5 Large pipeline, CUDA/MPS/explicit CPU, precision and CUDA offload controls.
- **`--backend sdcpp` (Apple Silicon follow-up):** external `stable-diffusion.cpp` CLI with Metal and Q4_0/Q5_0/Q8_0 GGUF presets. The lightweight `[sdcpp]` extra adds psutil, **not PyTorch**. Supports Metal on native Apple Silicon and explicitly requested CPU.

## Native Apple Silicon implementation

- Inspect the installed executable's actual help and `--list-devices`; reject missing options, CPU-only builds and Rosetta Python before weights download. Select the returned Metal device explicitly; do not rely on silent engine fallback.
- Download exactly four selected files from `second-state/stable-diffusion-3.5-large-GGUF`: full-model GGUF, matching T5 GGUF and both CLIP encoders. This is a **community quantization**; no encoder is silently omitted and no implicit requantization is performed.
- Use exact Hub file sizes, immutable revisions, completed-cache accounting and 2 GiB/5% disk reserve. Offline manifests reject missing/truncated files without remote metadata or token lookup.
- Count Apple unified RAM **once**. Estimate memory from the selected weights, allocator overhead, resolution-sensitive workspace and system headroom; no fixed 32 GiB minimum on this new backend. Smaller dimensions genuinely lower its estimate. The existing Diffusers MPS implementation/checks remain unchanged.
- `--sdcpp-memory disk` explicitly uses upstream disk parameter residency, trading repeated reads for lower estimated memory use.
- Tiled VAE decoding; diffusion Flash Attention enabled by default, with `--no-flash-attention` for comparison and a larger unfused-attention workspace estimate.
- Recheck available RAM after downloading, before launch. The native Metal allocation limit is **not measured**; no OS/GPU limits or safety thresholds are changed.
- Launch without a shell or inference API credentials. Native timeout includes model loading; cancellation/timeout cleans up the process group on macOS. Validate output existence, decoding and dimensions before atomic final replacement. No paid-API fallback.
- Emit load+generation wall time excluding model downloads. Each invocation remains a fresh process; this is not a persistent model server.

These are **planning heuristics**, not measured memory peaks or guarantees against OOM, swap, or slow generation.

## Research and documentation

Added [docs/apple-silicon.md](https://github.com/alex-mextner/draw-cli/blob/9cd1eff831f7617a3ac556ba0913c15dd836d808/docs/apple-silicon.md): verified CLI/build options, source-pinned Metal build recipe, extras, presets, memory/offline behavior and reproducible benchmark procedure.

- `stable-diffusion.cpp` is the closest llama.cpp-style option, with SD3.5, Metal and GGUF. Its own [build notes](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp/blob/6b3edaaf32cc19e5bb2d819c788bd557eddc8eba/docs/build.md) still warn about slow large-matrix Metal operations. Flash Attention is not a guaranteed speed improvement on Metal.
- [Draw Things CLI](https://releases.drawthings.ai/p/draw-things-cli-local-media-generation) is a genuine native command-line alternative; the current [Homebrew formula](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/draw-things-cli) is `brew install draw-things-cli`. Documented as a separate candidate for matched Mac benchmarks, **not integrated into draw-cli** in this change.
- DiffusionKit was archived on March 21, 2026 and was not chosen as a new dependency. Exact SD3.5 Large compatibility for MFLUX was not established from the reviewed docs, so it was not silently substituted.

## Verification

Latest implementation commit: `9cd1eff831f7617a3ac556ba0913c15dd836d808`.

- Added **59 native-backend test cases** on top of the previous SD3.5 coverage.
- **Full GitHub CI test jobs passed on Python 3.9 and 3.12.** The [Python 3.12 log](https://github.com/alex-mextner/draw-cli/actions/runs/33959327570/job/101288302579) reports **188 passed**; [workflow run](https://github.com/alex-mextner/draw-cli/actions/runs/33959327570).
- Before publication, 48 non-CLI native tests ran locally, including actual small child-process timeout, failure and shell-interpolation checks. Source compilation and Python 3.9 grammar checks passed. Published source blob hashes match the tested files.
- Tests mock model downloads, hardware discovery and inference; they do not make paid calls or download model weights.
- **Not performed:** compiling sd-cli on a Mac, real SD3.5 Metal/MPS/CPU image generation, quality evaluation, or target-Mac speed/RAM benchmarks. Native support and lower estimated residency do not establish that this is faster than Draw Things or Diffusers.

## Examples

```bash
# Hosted paths:
draw "a tiny robot" --model sd3.5 -o robot.png
draw "a tiny robot" --backend stability --aspect-ratio 16:9 -o robot.png

# After installing the lightweight extra and a compatible Metal sd-cli:
draw --backend sdcpp --quantization q4_0 --check-resources --json
draw "a tiny robot" --backend sdcpp --quantization q4_0 --seed 42 -o robot.png
draw "a tiny robot" --backend sdcpp --sdcpp-memory disk \
  --width 768 --height 768 --seed 42 -o robot-small.png
```
